How to set email up and its test email: Email. The messages LibreFolio sends: Email: Links and Messages.

docs.title: 🛠️ When It Does Not Work
docs.text:
Two kinds of problem:

What you see Why Where to look State Not working as soon as you open the Email tab A variable LibreFolio cannot use Configuration Problems The error shows only when you send an email The SMTP server refuses the email or does not answer Sending Errors

A configuration that cannot be used turns only email off: the server starts as usual and everything else works.

Where you act, in the tables of this page:

Where What Afterwards .env — LibreFolio's .env file (where it lives) The LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_… variables and LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL Restart LibreFolio. With Docker Compose, run docker compose up -d. SMTP server — the server or the provider Login, allowed senders, certificate, relay Try the test email again. Interface — Settings › Administration › Email, Profile, Users & Invitations State, test email, your address, the accounts No restart. Log The server's exact reply and the code What the Log Says: where to read it.

docs.title: ⚙️ Configuration Problems
docs.text:
Where: LibreFolio's .env file. The Email tab names the variable; the code is in the log, right after Starting LibreFolio. After every fix: restart LibreFolio. With Docker Compose, run docker compose up -d.

What you see (tab) Code Why What to do LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_HOST is not a valid server name… SMTP_HOST_INVALID Not just a name or an IP address smtp.example.com, not smtp://smtp.example.com, smtp.example.com:587 or user@smtp.example.com. The port goes in LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PORT; an IPv6 address without square brackets. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_TLS must be starttls, tls or none. SMTP_TLS_INVALID Word not allowed One of the three. Encryption from the first byte, port 465: tls. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PORT must be a whole number from 1 to 65535. SMTP_PORT_INVALID Out of range or not numeric Digits only, or remove the line: the port of the mode applies. The password file named by LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE cannot be read. SMTP_PASSWORD_UNREADABLE The file does not exist at that path (with Docker, the path inside the container), the user that runs LibreFolio cannot read it, it is empty or blank, not UTF-8, or larger than 64 KiB The log says which: file system or path. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_USER is set alone… (or LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD) SMTP_CREDENTIALS_INCOMPLETE User without password or the other way round. A password from LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE counts as LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD Both, or neither. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_FROM is missing… SMTP_FROM_MISSING Required as soon as you set a server Add the sender. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_FROM must be one address… SMTP_FROM_INVALID List or line break One address, with or without a name: LibreFolio <noreply@example.com>. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_REPLY_TO must be one address. SMTP_REPLY_TO_INVALID Same rule as the sender One address, or remove the line. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_MAX_PER_HOUR must be a whole number of at least 1. SMTP_MAX_PER_HOUR_INVALID Not a whole number ≥ 1 Digits only, at least 1. To stop sending, remove LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_HOST instead. LIBREFOLIO_SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS must be a whole number of at least 1. SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS_INVALID Not a whole number ≥ 1. Like the others, it turns email off until you fix it; the server starts anyway Digits only, at least 1, or remove the line: default 20.

docs.title: 📤 Sending Errors
docs.text:
The test email, in Settings › Administration › Email, says why it did not go out. The server's exact reply is in the log (What the Log Says).

What you see (test email) Code Why What to do — where LibreFolio cannot reach the SMTP server… CONNECTION_FAILED Server name, port or firewall. The name counts from where LibreFolio runs: in a container, localhost is the container itself .env: LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_HOST, LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PORT. Network: a firewall that refuses the connection. The secure connection failed… TLS_FAILED Mode and port do not go together; with starttls the server does not offer encryption; certificate not valid or not issued for the name in LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_HOST (self-signed, or an IP instead of the name, fails) .env: starttls with 587, tls with 465; in LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_HOST the name of the certificate. SMTP server: a valid certificate. The SMTP server refused the login… AUTH_FAILED Wrong user or password. A server without login refuses the login .env: user and password; with a provider, an app password. Server without login: remove both. The SMTP server refused the sender address… SENDER_REFUSED The server accepts only the addresses your account may send with. Without a user, it may still require a login .env: in LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_FROM one of those addresses, or add the login. The SMTP server refused your address. RECIPIENT_REFUSED The email of your account. Without a login, a server may refuse to relay to other domains: the reply in the log says so Interface: your address in Profile. SMTP server: the relay. The SMTP server did not answer in time. TIMEOUT Beyond the 20 seconds LibreFolio waits for each step: a firewall that drops the connection without refusing it, or starttls on port 465 .env: the mode/port pair. Network: the firewall. The SMTP server did not take the message. SEND_FAILED The server refused the message itself. Non-ASCII letters before the @, such as zoë@example.com, need SMTPUTF8: without it, the email never leaves LibreFolio and the log reports SMTPNotSupportedError Log: the server's reply says why. SMTP server: SMTPUTF8, or an ASCII address. The hourly limit of … emails is reached… (state), or The hourly email limit is reached: try again in … min. (test) EMAIL_RATE_LIMITED Maximum of the hour reached Wait the minutes shown. For more, .env: raise LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_MAX_PER_HOUR and restart. Email is off or not working on this instance. EMAIL_UNAVAILABLE Configuration changed since you loaded the tab, for example after a restart Interface: the tab now shows the state and its problem. The address of your account is not a valid email address. EMAIL_RECIPIENT_INVALID The email of your account Interface: correct it in Profile. The test email could not be sent. — No known answer, for example a network error Reload the page and look at the log. Test email sent to your address…, but nothing arrives — The server accepted: from there, delivery is its job. A sender on a domain that does not authorize that server may be rejected or end up in spam along the way Spam folder, then the logs of the server or of the provider.

The state of email could not be read.: the tab did not reach the server. Reload; if it persists, look at the log.

Send by email, in the invitation and reset dialogs, says why a link did not go out:

What you see (dialog) Code Why What to do — where Email is off or not working on this instance. EMAIL_UNAVAILABLE Configuration changed since you opened the dialog, for example after a restart Interface: Settings › Administration › Email. Emails cannot carry links: LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL is not set, or cannot start a link. EMAIL_LINKS_UNAVAILABLE The start of the links is missing .env: set LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL, then restart (Emails with a Link). This link no longer works: create a new one. EMAIL_LINK_INVALID Link expired, used or revoked Interface: create a new link and send that one. The account is not active: activate it before sending it a reset link. EMAIL_ACCOUNT_INACTIVE Deactivated account Interface: Reactivate in Users & Invitations; or command line: user activate (CLI). Then send the link again. Enter the address to send the invitation to. EMAIL_RECIPIENT_REQUIRED The invitation holds no address Interface: type one in Send to. This is not one valid email address. EMAIL_RECIPIENT_INVALID Invalid address. For a reset, it is the account's own Interface: correct Send to. For the reset, copy the link instead. The hourly email limit is reached: try again in … min. EMAIL_RATE_LIMITED Maximum of the hour reached Wait the minutes shown. For more, .env: raise LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_MAX_PER_HOUR and restart. The SMTP server refused the recipient's address. RECIPIENT_REFUSED The address of the link: Send to for an invitation, the account's email for a reset. Without a login, a server may refuse to relay to other domains Interface: the address. Log: the server's reply. SMTP server: the relay. The other messages of the test email CONNECTION_FAILED, TLS_FAILED, AUTH_FAILED, … As in the table above As in the table above. The email could not be sent. — No known answer, for example a network error Reload the page and look at the log.

EMAIL_RECIPIENT_NOT_ALLOWED (another address for a reset link) comes only from the API: the dialog never returns it.

docs.title: 📜 What the Log Says
docs.text:
Where to read it:

Installation Command or file Docker docker compose logs librefolio On the host logs/librefolio.log in the data folder (Filesystem Structure); the server also prints it to the console

At every start, right after Starting LibreFolio, the server checks the configuration, email included (Startup Checks): a configuration that cannot be used (the first two lines below), none towards a server outside your local network (one line), LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL missing or invalid (one line). None of them stops the start. The same three checks are in Settings › Administration › Security, read again when you ask; a finding links to the Email tab (see «Security» in Global Settings).

Start and sending

The log says Level When Email configuration cannot be used: email stays off error A variable cannot be used. Once per server process, at startup, with variable, problem (the code) and reason: the rule it breaks, or why the password file cannot be read. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_… cannot be used (SMTP_…): email stays off until it is fixed error At startup, after the line above, with check set to email.smtp: the startup checks report the same problem. LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_TLS=none with …: emails, their links and the SMTP password travel unencrypted; use starttls or tls warning At startup, with check set to email.smtp_encryption: none towards a server outside your local network, which the line names (Security Notes). LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL is not set: emails work, but none with a link (forgotten password, invitation, reset) can go out info At startup, with check set to email.links: email works, but LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL is not set (Emails with a Link). LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL cannot start a link (it needs http:// or https:// and a host, with no user name, password, ? or #): no email with a link (forgotten password, invitation, reset) can go out warning At startup, with check set to email.links: email works, but the variable cannot start a link (Emails with a Link). Email sent info The server accepted an email; kind says which: test, invite, password_reset, email_verification, email_changed or email_change_confirmation. Email not sent warning The server refused the email or did not answer: code, as in Sending Errors, and detail, the server's own reply, the most precise clue. Email not sent: the hourly limit of the instance is reached warning The hourly limit stopped an email; retry_after is in seconds. Test email sent by an administrator info A test email went out, with admin_id and language. Link emailed by an administrator info An administrator sent a link by email: admin_id, purpose (invite or password_reset), token_id, the account's user_id for a reset link, and language.

Forgotten passwords

The log says Level When Forgotten password: reset link emailed info A reset link went out: user_id, token_id and language. Forgotten password: no active account matches, nothing sent info No active account has that username or email address. What was typed is never logged. Forgotten password: the account had a reset link moments ago, nothing sent info The account's limits: a reset link less than 5 minutes ago, or 3 in the last hour; with user_id. Forgotten password: an administrator's reset link is still live, nothing sent info A request never cancels a link given by an administrator; with user_id. Forgotten password: the hourly limit of the instance is reached, nothing sent warning The hourly limit was reached after the answer; with user_id. Forgotten password: the mailbox had reset emails moments ago, nothing sent info That mailbox already had 3 reset emails in the last hour, those that did not go out included; with user_id. Forgotten password: another request won the race, nothing sent info Two requests for the account at the same moment: the other one sends the email; with user_id. Forgotten password: no email sent warning Email or LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL stopped working after the answer, or the email was refused: reason and code say which. The link created is revoked. Forgotten password: the request failed error An unexpected error, with its type in error and nothing more: no detail of the request reaches the log.

Every reset link also leaves a Password reset link created line, with user_id, token_id and, if an administrator created it, created_by_user_id.

Email verification

The log says Level When Registration waits for email verification info A new account waits for its link; with user_id. The User registered line of the same registration has waits_for_email set to true. Verification email held: address limit or instance budget reached info The address had already received its LIBREFOLIO_SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS emails (20 by default) in the hour, or the hourly limit of the instance is spent: the account waits without its email, and the login page tells its owner so; with user_id. Verification link emailed info A verification link went out: user_id, token_id and language. Verification email: not sent warning The email of a registration did not go out: reason and code say why. The page had said that the email was on its way: only this line says that it did not go out. The account still waits; the owner can ask for the link again. Verification email: the account no longer waits, nothing sent info An administrator activated, deactivated or deleted the account before the email went out; with user_id. Verification email: the request failed error An unexpected error, with its type in error and the user_id, nothing more. Login refused: email not verified info A waiting account logged in with the right password; with user_id. Verification resend refused: wrong credentials warning Request for a new verification link with a wrong password, or for an account that does not exist. Neither what was typed nor the address is logged. Email verified info The owner confirmed on the page of the link: the account is active; user_id and token_id. Email verification refused: the link's email did not go out info Confirmation with a link whose email LibreFolio counted as not sent: the account still waits, and Send the link again works. Email verification refused: the link was sent to another address info The account's address changed after the link was sent: that link stops working.

Email address change

The log says Level When Email change notice sent to the previous address info The notice went to the old address. The line has user_id and language, neither address. Email change notice sent to the new address info The confirmation went to the new address. The line has user_id and language, neither address. Email change notice: email is off, nothing sent info Email is off: nothing to send, nothing wrong. Email change notice: past its limits, nothing sent info The account already had 3 changes with emails in the hour: the change went through, its two emails did not. With user_id. Email change notice: the previous mailbox is past its limit, not sent there info The old mailbox already had 3 of these emails in the hour: the notice did not go, the confirmation to the new address still can. With user_id. Email change notice: the new mailbox is past its limit, not sent there info The same, for the new mailbox and its confirmation. With user_id. Email change notice: the account no longer exists, nothing sent info The account was deleted before the email went out. Email change notice: not sent warning Email is configured but cannot be used now, the hourly limit is reached, an address is not one plain address, or sending failed: reason and code say which, and recipient (previous or new) which of the two emails, when it is one of them. Email change notice: the request failed error An unexpected error, with its type in error and the user_id, nothing more.

None of these lines holds the SMTP password, the content of an email, a link or its secret part, what someone typed to ask for a reset or verification link, or the recipient's full address: only its domain, in recipient_domain. The server's reply is masked too, because it often quotes the refused address: 550 5.1.1 <***@example.com>: Recipient address rejected. The lines of an email change name neither the old address nor the new one.

docs.title: 🔒 Security Notes
docs.text:
• starttls never falls back to plain text. A server that does not offer encryption gets neither the password nor the message: the test email fails with TLS_FAILED.
  • The certificate is always checked, with starttls and with tls: no option skips it.
  • none sends everything in clear: messages, links and the SMTP password. Use it only for a relay on your own machine or network. Towards any other server, Settings › Administration › Email shows a warning: Emails, their links and the SMTP password travel unencrypted to a server outside the local network; the start log has one too (What the Log Says).
  • Keep the password in a secret file (LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE) that only the user running LibreFolio can read, out of .env and out of the data folder. Use an app password, or an account just for LibreFolio, that you can revoke on its own.
  • Links come only from LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL, never from a request: nobody can make LibreFolio send one of your users a link to a third-party site (Emails with a Link).
  • A verification link goes only to the account's own address, and nobody sees it, administrator included. Send the link again asks for the account's password, like the login, and a new link disables the previous ones.
  • Names stay on one line. Username, inviter's name and instance name go into an email on one line: control characters and line breaks become spaces, bidirectional controls are removed. A crafted username can neither add lines to an email nor disguise its text.
  • No stranger's words in an email. Password reset, email verification and the two emails of an address change can be sent, by someone who is not an administrator, to an address of their choice. These emails open with a plain «Hello,», without the username, the notice shows no part of the new address and the confirmation to the new address none of the old one: LibreFolio does not resolve domains, so even the end of an address is chosen freely. A reset link you send by email is written the same way; the username appears once the link is opened. Only the test email and the setup link of the initial administrator greet by name: you, or whoever runs the server, send them.
  • Forgotten passwords tell nobody which accounts exist: the same answer for everyone, the search after the answer, and limits per address, per username or email address, per mailbox and per account (Forgotten Passwords).
  • Changing an account's email address requires its current password. Without it, a moment inside someone's session (a stolen session cookie, a computer left unlocked) would be enough to put one's own address on the account and then reset its password: reset by email exists only together with this rule. When email works, the old address also gets a notice, and the new one a confirmation (Email Address Changes).
  • The hourly limit caps what the instance can send, whatever happens: raise it only as far as you need.
🏠 What counts as your local network — when the warning appears

LibreFolio judges LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_HOST as written, without resolving the name. Local means:

  • localhost, or a name without a dot, such as a Docker Compose service (smtp-relay) or a machine of your LAN;
  • a name ending in .local, .lan, .home.arpa, .internal or .localhost;
  • a loopback, private or link-local address, such as 127.0.0.1, 192.168.1.10 or fd00::25, or a Tailscale address (100.64.0.0/10, fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48).

Any other server gets the warning, even one on your network known by a full name such as relay.example.com. A Tailscale name such as relay.tailnet.ts.net gets it too, while its 100.x address does not.

docs.text:

  • 📄 Email: Links and Messages — Emails with a Link, Links Sent by an Administrator, Forgotten Passwords, …

docs.title: 📂 Filesystem Structure
docs.text:
Everything LibreFolio stores lives in one data directory: database, uploaded files, broker reports, logs and the instance key. Knowing it is all you need for backups and maintenance.

Where it is. In the rest of the page, <data> is this folder:

Installation <data> on the host <data> inside the container Host (Pipenv) backend/data/prod/ in the project folder, or the path in LIBREFOLIO_DATA_DIR — Docker Compose LibreFolio-data/ next to docker-compose.yml /app/backend/data/prod-docker

docs.title: 🗂️ Directory Layout
docs.text:
backend/data/
├── 📂 prod/                          # Production data (default)
│   ├── 🗃️ sqlite/
│   │   └── 📄 app.db                 # Main SQLite database (WAL mode)
│   ├── 🖼️ custom-uploads/            # Files uploaded in the app
│   ├── 📊 broker_reports/
│   │   ├── 📥 uploaded/              # Reports waiting to be read
│   │   ├── ✅ parsed/                # Reports read successfully
│   │   └── ❌ failed/                # Reports that could not be read
│   ├── 📝 logs/                      # Application log files
│   ├── 💾 backups/                   # Backups kept by LibreFolio, one folder each
│   ├── 🎭 scenario_catalog/          # Optional: your own stress scenarios
│   ├── 🗄️ cache/                     # Safe to delete: PDF preview fonts, fetched again
│   ├── 🔐 secrets/                   # Created when LibreFolio first needs the key
│   │   └── 🔑 instance.key           # The instance key: back it up, never change it
│   └── 📋 scheduler_state.json       # Scheduled syncs: last run, pending retry
│
└── 🧪 test/                          # Test data (completely isolated)
    ├── 🗃️ sqlite/app.db
    ├── 🖼️ custom-uploads/
    ├── 📊 broker_reports/
    └── 📝 logs/
Folder What it holds Who writes or reads it 🗃️ sqlite/ app.db: users, brokers, transactions, assets, prices, FX rates, settings The server 🖼️ custom-uploads/ Files uploaded in the app (such as those of the Files page) and default avatars The app 📊 broker_reports/ The uploaded broker reports, one broker_<id>/ folder per broker The import 📝 logs/ librefolio.log and its weekly archives The server writes, you read 💾 backups/ The backups kept on the server, one folder each Backup and restore 🎭 scenario_catalog/ Your own stress scenarios, if you added any You 🗄️ cache/ Copies that can be downloaded again (pdf-fonts/) The PDF preview 🔐 secrets/ instance.key, the instance key LibreFolio, the first time it needs the key 📋 scheduler_state.json Last run and pending retry of the scheduled syncs The scheduled syncs

docs.title: 🗃️ sqlite/
docs.text:
• 📎 app.db-wal and app.db-shm: SQLite's working files (WAL mode), present while the server runs. Never copy app.db alone while the server is up.
  • 🔒 app.db.post-migration.lock: empty file used at startup, leave it in place.
  • 🗑️ app.db.pre-<fix>-<UTC time>.bak: copy kept after a failed post-migration fix. Delete it once you no longer need it.

docs.title: 🖼️ custom-uploads/
docs.text: Each file has a random name and a .json next to it that describes it: keep the pairs together.

docs.title: 📊 broker_reports/
docs.text:
Inside broker_<id>/, a report moves from uploaded/ to parsed/ or failed/: the original is always in one of the three.

  • 📥 uploaded/ — waiting to be read
  • ✅ parsed/ — read successfully
  • ❌ failed/ — could not be read, kept so you can check why

docs.title: 📝 logs/
docs.text:
• 📄 librefolio.log: one JSON record per line; the server also prints the log to the console.
  • 🗓️ Every Monday (UTC) the file is archived and compressed (.gz); the last 52 archives, one year, are kept.

How much to write. In LibreFolio's .env (default INFO):

LOG_LEVEL=INFO
📶 Log levels — what each one records

Each level also records all the more serious ones.

Level What it captures 🔬 TRACE High-frequency granular data: individual FX rates parsed, per-asset price points 🐛 DEBUG Operational internals: which provider was used, intermediate results, algorithmic decisions ℹ️ INFO (default) Significant user operations: sync completed, import, login, resource created/deleted ⚠️ WARNING Recoverable anomalies: fallback activated, missing optional data, degraded mode ❌ ERROR Handled errors: failed operations, data corruption, provider unreachable 💀 CRITICAL Fatal errors that stop the process
  • Production: LOG_LEVEL=INFO — clean signal, no noise
  • Troubleshooting: LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG — see what the system is deciding
  • Deep FX/price debugging: LOG_LEVEL=TRACE — see every individual data point

Reading the log. Each line is a JSON object: message in event, level in level, time (UTC) in timestamp, traceback in exception. A line written during a request carries its request_id; when something fails, the same id reaches the browser: X-Request-Id header of the response, body of the server error, [API] line in the browser's console (developer tools, Console).

  1. Ask for the id from the user who reports the error.

  2. In the <data>/logs/ folder, read its lines with jq:

    # Every line of one request
jq -cR 'fromjson? | select(.request_id == "3f2a9c0d41b7e865")' librefolio.log

# The errors, each followed by its traceback
jq -rR 'fromjson? | select(.level == "ERROR" or .level == "CRITICAL") | "\(.timestamp) \(.request_id // "-") \(.event)", (.exception // empty)' librefolio.log

    A failed-request line names method and path, never query string, headers or body.

  3. fromjson? skips the lines that are not JSON, such as those of the libraries LibreFolio uses.

  4. Archived week: gzip -dc librefolio.log.2026-10-12.gz | jq -cR ….

docs.title: 🗄️ cache/
docs.text: pdf-fonts/: the Chinese, Japanese and Korean fonts the PDF preview downloads at first use when the PDF uses them, see The Content-Security-Policy. Deleting it loses nothing; it is not part of a backup.

docs.title: 🔐 secrets/
docs.text:
• 🔑 instance.key is the instance key, from which LibreFolio derives its encryption keys. If it is missing, LibreFolio treats it as a first use: it creates a new key and what was encrypted with the old one can no longer be read.
  • 🔒 Folder 0700, file 0600, owned by the user that runs LibreFolio. Otherwise the start log has a warning, or an error if LibreFolio itself cannot open them.
  • ⛔ Never edit, replace or delete the instance.key in use. If it is damaged, or if LibreFolio has already replaced a lost key with a new one: stop LibreFolio and put your copy back before anyone enters a plugin secret again, see The Instance Key.
  • ♻️ When you restore the data directory, put secrets/ back with it before you start LibreFolio. Never start LibreFolio on restored data without its secrets/.
  • ⚙️ With the key in LIBREFOLIO_INSTANCE_KEY or LIBREFOLIO_INSTANCE_KEY_FILE, LibreFolio does not use this folder.

🔗 For developers: Data directory on disk — every file, its format and the code that writes it, scenario_catalog/ included.

docs.title: 🌍 Environment Variables
docs.text:
Host, in LibreFolio's .env. A relative path starts from the project folder:

LIBREFOLIO_DATA_DIR=/path/to/data        # production data directory
LIBREFOLIO_TEST_DATA_DIR=/path/to/test   # test data directory

Docker Compose, in docker-compose.yml. The path inside the container is fixed: to keep the data elsewhere on the host, change the left side of the volume.

- ./LibreFolio-data:/app/backend/data/prod-docker

The other variables and the .env file: Configuration.

docs.title: 💾 Backup
docs.text:
The recommended way is a backup archive, made while LibreFolio keeps running: Backup, Restore and Moving Your Instance.

  • From the command line, ./dev.py backup create: one zip of database, uploaded files, broker reports and stress scenarios, by default in a folder of its own inside <data>/backups/. See Back Up the Instance and, for the command in the container, Back Up with Docker.
  • The archive leaves out secrets/, which you back up separately (What to Back Up), unless you make it secure with --encrypt: a secure archive holds the instance key LibreFolio generated.
  • The alternative is to copy the data directory by hand, as below.

docs.title: 📦 Simple Backup
docs.text:
1. Stop the server, for the consistency of the database.

  2. From the project folder, copy the whole data directory:

    # Stop the server first (to ensure database consistency)
cp -r backend/data/prod/ /path/to/backup/librefolio-$(date +%Y%m%d)/

    Result: a complete, dated copy of <data>.

This copy, like the Docker one below, also includes backups/, with every backup LibreFolio keeps there (Backups Kept on the Server): delete the ones you no longer need first, set the automatic clean-up, or leave the folder out.

docs.title: 🐳 Docker Backup
docs.text:
The data directory is the LibreFolio-data/ folder on the host: no Docker copy command.

  1. From the folder of docker-compose.yml, stop the container, copy, restart:

    docker compose stop librefolio
cp -r ./LibreFolio-data/ /path/to/backup/librefolio-$(date +%Y%m%d)/
docker compose start librefolio

    Result: a consistent copy; the server stays stopped only for the duration of the copy.

🔄 Back up the database without stopping the server

SQLite's online backup makes a consistent copy while the server runs. It needs the sqlite3 tool:

sqlite3 backend/data/prod/sqlite/app.db ".backup '/path/to/backup/app.db'"

With Docker, the database is ./LibreFolio-data/sqlite/app.db. This command copies the database only: copy the folders listed below as usual.

docs.title: ✅ What to Back Up
docs.text:
At minimum, back up:

  1. sqlite/app.db — All your data (users, transactions, settings, FX rates)
  2. custom-uploads/ — User-uploaded files (avatars, documents)
  3. broker_reports/ — The original broker reports, in case you need to import them again
  4. scenario_catalog/ — Your own stress scenarios, if you added any
  5. secrets/ — The instance key, if LibreFolio has created it

🔑 Keep secrets/ with the data, and keep it private

Save secrets/ together with the database and keep the copies as private as the database. Never change or delete the instance key in use: what is encrypted with it can no longer be read. When you restore, put secrets/ back with the data before you start LibreFolio.

Only the user that runs LibreFolio can open secrets/. The same goes for backups/, created at the first backup, and .restore/, created the first time an archive is checked for a restore: LibreFolio creates both as 0700, and the archives in backups/ as 0600. If cp reports Permission denied in one of them, for example with Docker when your host user is not the container's, copy as root and keep the permissions: sudo cp -a. Deleting an old archive from backups/ fails the same way: use sudo rm.

If storage is limited, keep at least sqlite/app.db, which holds all the structured data, and the small secrets/ folder: files and reports can be uploaded again if you still have them.

docs.title: 📦 Host Installation (Pipenv)
docs.text:
Install LibreFolio on your machine without Docker, with Python, Node.js and Pipenv: handy with few resources, and the first step towards a development environment.

For Docker, see the User Manual Installation or the Advanced Docker Guide.

docs.title: ✅ Prerequisites
docs.text:
Install these three tools first.

🐍 Python 3.13

The version set in the project's Pipfile.

  • macOS, with Homebrew: 
    brew install python@3.13
  • Windows: download the installer from python.org and check "Add Python to PATH".
  • Linux (Ubuntu/Debian): 
    sudo apt update
sudo apt install python3.13 python3.13-venv python3.13-dev
📦 Node.js 24+

Builds the web interface.

  • macOS, with Homebrew: 
    brew install node@24
  • Windows/Linux: with nvm (Linux/macOS) or nvm-windows (Windows), or download from nodejs.org.
📋 Pipenv

Manages the Python virtual environment and its packages.

  • All platforms: 
    pip install --user pipenv
    Add the user binaries folder (~/.local/bin on Linux/macOS, %APPDATA%\Python on Windows) to the shell's PATH.

docs.title: 📋 Setup Instructions
docs.text:
Commands run in the Pipenv environment

The dev.py commands start with pipenv run, which runs them in the project's virtual environment. Or enter it once with pipenv shell, then type ./dev.py … without the prefix.

docs.title: 📥 1. Download the Project
docs.text:
Where: terminal, in the folder where you want the project.

git clone https://github.com/Librefolio/LibreFolio.git
cd LibreFolio

Result: the LibreFolio/ folder. Or download and unzip the latest release from GitHub Releases.

docs.title: 🐍 2. Create the Python Environment
docs.text:
Where: terminal, LibreFolio/ folder.

pipenv install --dev

Result: the virtual environment with the Python packages. Do this before any dev.py command: without it, it stops with ModuleNotFoundError.

docs.title: 📦 3. Install the Other Dependencies
docs.text:
Where: terminal, LibreFolio/ folder.

pipenv run ./dev.py install

Result, in order:

  1. the Python packages again (pipenv install --dev);
  2. the project tools (npm ci);
  3. the web interface dependencies (npm ci in frontend/);
  4. the Chromium browser of Playwright, for the end-to-end tests and the documentation screenshots. If only this download fails, the installation still completes.

docs.title: ⚙️ 4. Configure the Environment
docs.text:
Where: terminal, LibreFolio/ folder; then the .env file just created.

cp .env.example .env

Result: the .env file with defaults that work as they are. The main variables:

Variable Default Description PORT 6040 Server bind port. LIBREFOLIO_DATA_DIR ./backend/data/prod Directory of the database, uploaded files and logs (see Filesystem Structure). LOG_LEVEL INFO Logging verbosity.

The other variables: Environment Variables Guide.

docs.title: 🚀 5. Start the Server
docs.text:
Where: terminal, LibreFolio/ folder.

pipenv run ./dev.py server

Result: LibreFolio answers on http://localhost:6040. The first start builds the web interface and the documentation: a few minutes. Workers, another port, the other options: Command-Line Tools.

docs.title: 👤 6. Create Your Account
docs.text:
Where: browser, http://localhost:6040, link Register here below the login form.

Result: the first account registered becomes the administrator. To manage users from the terminal, see Command-Line Tools. To have LibreFolio create the administrator at its first start, see The Initial Administrator.

docs.title: 🗃️ Database Initialization & Reset
docs.text:
There is nothing to initialise: at every start the server creates the database if it is missing and applies the pending migrations.

To start again from an empty database, use one of the two ways below.

All data is lost

Both ways delete the database for good: users, brokers, transactions and settings. Make a backup first (see Backup).

docs.title: 🧹 With dev.py
docs.text:
Where: terminal, LibreFolio/ folder, with the server stopped (the command refuses to run while the server is up).

pipenv run ./dev.py db create-clean

Result: a new, empty database.

docs.title: 🗑️ By Hand
docs.text:
Where: the data directory, by default backend/data/prod/.

  1. Stop the server if it is running.
  2. Delete the SQLite database file, by default backend/data/prod/sqlite/app.db.
  3. Start the server: it creates a new one.

Both ways replace only the database: uploaded files, broker reports and logs stay in the data directory. For a completely fresh start, stop the server and delete the whole data directory: the next start recreates it.

docs.title: 🛡️ Admin Manual
docs.text: For the people who install and run LibreFolio. Almost everything is done in one of three places: from the command line, in the .env file (environment variables) or in the app's Settings › Administration tabs.

docs.title: 🐳 Deployment & Exposure
docs.text:
• 📦 Host Installation: Python, Node.js and Pipenv directly on the host machine.
  • 🐳 Advanced Docker: Docker Compose, volumes and file ownership through GID/UID.
  • 🌐 Expose Securely: your private instance with Tailscale, no router port opened: a VPN for your own devices or a subnet router for your whole home network.
    • 🌍 Expose Securely: Public Access with Funnel: a public HTTPS address with Tailscale Funnel, one for LibreFolio or one for each service with Docker.
  • 🔍 Check Connection Security: the checklist, the indicator, the server's view and the session cookie; what to do when a check fails.
    • 🧰 Check Connection Security: Behind a Reverse Proxy: Nginx, Caddy, Traefik or Tailscale: the headers to send, the trusted proxy and the visitor's address.

docs.title: ⚙️ System Configuration
docs.text:
• 📝 Environment Variables: the .env file and the main variables (PORT, JWT_SECRET, LIBREFOLIO_DATA_DIR, etc.), with the precedence between the values.
    • 🔐 Configuration: Secrets and Plugin Settings: secrets read from files (such as Docker secrets), the instance key, the settings and API keys of the plugins.
    • 🛡️ Configuration: Checks and Protections: the checks at startup, the Content-Security-Policy, the frame protection and how the server stops.
    • 👥 Configuration: Accounts and Asset Search: who can sign up, limits on accounts and failed sign-ins, the initial administrator, the order of the price providers.
  • 📧 Email: optional SMTP: the variables, examples for the most common servers, the Email tab of Settings › Administration and the test email.
    • 📬 Email: Links and Messages: invitations and password resets, forgotten passwords and their limits, email verification, the notice of an email change.
    • 🛠️ Email: When It Does Not Work: the errors, what the log says, SMTP security notes.
  • ⚙️ Global Settings: the runtime settings (session TTL, upload limits, market data sync intervals), the Administration tabs and the Security checks of the instance.
  • 👥 Users & Invitations: the app's Users tab: invitations, password-reset links, administrator rights, deactivation and deletion.

docs.title: 🧹 Maintenance & Operations
docs.text:
• 🛠️ CLI Admin Tools: the dev.py script for user management, database upgrades and instance backups.
  • 💾 Backup, Restore & Moving: one archive with the whole instance, from Settings › Administration › Backup or from the command line: make it, check it, restore it, move LibreFolio between two installations.
  • 📂 Filesystem Structure: where databases, logs, uploads and temporary folders live, and how to perform backups.

docs.title: 🔔 Update Notifications
docs.text:
When an administrator signs in, LibreFolio checks GitHub for a newer stable release. If there is one, the New version available window shows your version and the latest side by side, with the How to update (updating guide) and Release notes on GitHub links.

Button Effect Remind me later Closes the window until a later sign-in. Skip this version No automatic prompt for that version; an even newer one will be announced.
  • A release is announced only when its Docker image can be downloaded; the window waits until no other window or guide is open.
  • Without internet access the check fails silently: no error, no banner.
  • To check right away: Check for updates in the changelog. It reports errors, and skipped versions too.
👥 Other users — when someone who is not an administrator checks

For users who are not administrators, no check runs at sign-in. If one of them runs Check for updates and a newer release exists, the Update available — contact an administrator window lists the administrators, with their email addresses when available.

docs.title: 🔐 Keep Users Signed In After a Restart
docs.text:
JWT_SECRET is the key that signs every login session.

  • Not set (the default): a new random key at every start, so everyone signs in again after a restart or an update.
  • Set: sessions survive restarts. Set it also when several LibreFolio servers share the same users behind a load balancer.

To set it:

  1. Generate a key. From a terminal, on the host:

    python3 -c "import secrets; k = secrets.token_urlsafe(64); print(f'JWT_SECRET={k}'); print(k)"

    You get two lines: the first, JWT_SECRET=…, is ready to paste into .env; the second is the key alone, for when you keep it in a file (JWT_SECRET_FILE, below). Without Python on the host, run the command in the container:

    docker exec librefolio python -c "import secrets; k = secrets.token_urlsafe(64); print(f'JWT_SECRET={k}'); print(k)"

  2. Paste the first line into LibreFolio's .env file:

    JWT_SECRET=paste-the-generated-value-here

  3. Restart LibreFolio. With Docker Compose, run docker compose up -d.

    From then on, a restart signs nobody out.

🔒 Keep the key secret

Whoever knows it can forge a session.

🐳 Keep the key out of .env — JWT_SECRET_FILE

Save the key in a file, such as a Docker secret, and set JWT_SECRET_FILE to its path instead of JWT_SECRET: for example JWT_SECRET_FILE=/run/secrets/jwt_secret. The rules and a Docker Compose example are in Secrets.

  • The workers of a single ./dev.py server --workers … share one key on their own.
  • How long a session lasts is the Session Duration in Global Settings.
  • Details for developers: Security Architecture.

docs.title: 🌐 Exposing Securely
docs.text:
Reach LibreFolio away from home without opening any port on your router, with Tailscale, a mesh VPN that is free for home use. The same steps work for any other service on your local network.

Do Step 0, then only the level you need. Levels 1 and 2, private, on this page; Levels 3 and 4, public, in Exposing Securely: Public Access with Funnel, after the one-time Funnel setup on the console.

Level Best for Tailscale on your phone/PC Public HTTPS address Where it is set up 🏃 1. Private VPN Just you, with the quickest setup Needed No Step 0 only 🥉 2. Subnet router Every device of your home LAN, not only LibreFolio Needed No Server terminal + Tailscale console 🥈 3. Funnel A public address for LibreFolio, and installing it as an app Not needed Yes Tailscale console + server terminal 🥇 4. Multi-Funnel with Docker One public address per service, each in its own container Not needed Yes Tailscale console + docker-compose.yml

⭐ Our recommendation: Level 4

Little more setup than Level 3; every service stays isolated in its own container, with a public address of its own. Levels 1–3 are simpler alternatives and stages on the way to it.

6040 is LibreFolio's default port: if you set a different PORT in your .env, use that number. Web app, API and built-in documentation all go through this port: it is the only one to expose.

📚 This guide is in several pages

Here: why Tailscale, Step 0, Levels 1 and 2, MagicDNS. Levels 3 and 4 and the Funnel setup: Exposing Securely: Public Access with Funnel.

docs.title: 🔒 Why not plain port forwarding?
docs.text:
Opening a port on the router and pointing a dynamic DNS name (such as DuckDNS) at it works, but:

  • The open port is visible to anyone on the internet, who can scan it and attack it.
  • HTTPS is your job: a reverse proxy (Nginx, Caddy…) and its SSL certificates to renew.
  • Without HTTPS, data travels in clear: password and financial data can be intercepted.
graph LR
    User["👤 External User<br>(Away from Home)"] --- Cloud["☁️ Internet / Router (Public IP / DDNS?)"]
    Cloud --- Server["🖥️ Local Server<br>(Port 6040)"]

With Tailscale no router port is opened, the traffic between your devices is encrypted, and Funnel (Levels 3 and 4) adds HTTPS with certificates that Tailscale manages.

docs.title: 🏁 Step 0: Install Tailscale on your devices
docs.text:
Tailscale (WireGuard protocol) links your devices in an encrypted private network, your tailnet. It runs on Linux, macOS, Windows, iOS and Android, on a NAS or in Docker; the free Personal plan is enough for home use (Tailscale pricing for the current limits).

Install it and log in on at least two devices: LibreFolio's server and a client, phone or laptop.

LinuxmacOSWindowsAndroidiOS (iPhone/iPad)

On the server, in a terminal:

curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh
sudo tailscale up

The server joins your tailnet. Details: Generic Installation Guide.

On the server: official app from the Mac App Store, or from a terminal with Homebrew:

brew install --cask tailscale
sudo tailscale up

Details: Generic Installation Guide.

On the server: download the official installer from the Tailscale portal and follow the login wizard. Details: Windows Installation Guide.

On the phone: official app from the Google Play Store.

On the device: official app from the Apple App Store.

🔑 Keep the server connected — disable key expiry

Tailscale asks every device to log in again after 180 days. A server must not drop off the tailnet for that. In the Tailscale admin console, Machines page:

  1. Locate your server.
  2. Click the three dots (...) icon on the right of its row.
  3. Select Disable Key Expiry.

docs.title: 🏃 Level 1: Private point-to-point VPN
docs.text:
Best if you are on your own, with the quickest setup. The client reaches LibreFolio through the tailnet; nothing is exposed to the internet.

graph LR
    Client["👤 Client (VPN active)<br>(100.x.y.z)"] -->|Direct VPN Connection| Server["🖥️ Server (VPN active)<br>(100.a.b.c:6040)"]
    subgraph LAN ["Local LAN Network"]
        Server -->|Local access| LibreFolio["📊 LibreFolio (Local)"]
    end
    style LibreFolio fill:#d4edda,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#28a745,stroke-width:2px;

docs.title: ▶️ Step 1: Check that LibreFolio answers on its port
docs.text:
Nothing to configure: with Tailscale on on the server, port 6040 is already reachable from the tailnet at the server's Tailscale IP.

Prefer an HTTPS address inside your tailnet?

On the server, in a terminal:

tailscale serve --bg 6040

Open https://<server-name>.your-tailnet.ts.net instead of the IP; it stays private, only the devices of your tailnet open it. --bg keeps it on after you close the terminal; tailscale serve reset removes it. The first time, Tailscale may ask you to enable HTTPS certificates for the tailnet.

docs.title: 📱 Step 2: Open LibreFolio from your device
docs.text:
On the phone or PC, with Tailscale on, type the server's Tailscale IP (or its MagicDNS name) and the port in the browser:

http://100.a.b.c:6040

LibreFolio opens. To check its security: Checking Connection Security.

⚠️ Limits: every device you connect from must have Tailscale on; you reach only the server, not the rest of the LAN (Level 2 adds that).

docs.title: 🥉 Level 2: Subnet router for your whole home LAN
docs.text:
Best for reaching every device at home, not only LibreFolio. The server becomes a subnet router: the client, with Tailscale on, opens any local IP as if at home, for example http://192.168.1.2:6040 for LibreFolio.

graph LR
    Client["👤 Client (VPN active)<br>(100.x.y.z)"] -->|WireGuard Tunneling| Server["🖥️ Server (Subnet Router)<br>(100.a.b.c)"]
    subgraph LAN ["Local LAN Network (192.168.1.0/24)"]
        Server -->|Local forwarding| LibreFolio["📊 LibreFolio<br>(e.g. 192.168.1.2:6040)"]
        Server -->|Local forwarding| OtherDevice["🖨️ Other Devices/Services<br>(e.g. 192.168.1.100)"]
    end
    style LibreFolio fill:#d4edda,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#28a745,stroke-width:2px;

docs.title: 🔀 Step 1: Enable subnet routing on the server
docs.text:
Replace 192.168.1.0/24 with your local network.

LinuxmacOSWindows

  1. On the server, in a terminal, enable IP forwarding in the kernel:

    echo 'net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1' | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.d/99-tailscale.conf
echo 'net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding = 1' | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.d/99-tailscale.conf
sudo sysctl -p /etc/sysctl.d/99-tailscale.conf

  2. Advertise the subnet:

    sudo tailscale up --advertise-routes=192.168.1.0/24

    The route appears in the console, waiting for approval.

On the server, in a terminal, with the path of the Tailscale executable:

/Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/Tailscale up --advertise-routes=192.168.1.0/24

The route appears in the console, waiting for approval.

On the server, in Command Prompt (cmd.exe) or PowerShell as Administrator:

tailscale up --advertise-routes=192.168.1.0/24

The route appears in the console, waiting for approval.

docs.title: ✅ Step 2: Approve the route in the admin console
docs.text:
In the Tailscale admin console, Machines page:

  1. Click the three dots next to your server -> Edit route settings.
  2. Enable the advertised subnet.

From the client you now reach every IP of the LAN. The server is now network infrastructure: if you have not yet, disable its key expiry (tip at the end of Step 0).

⚠️ Limits: the client must have Tailscale on, you must know the local IPs of your devices and, inside the LAN, the traffic travels as plain HTTP.

docs.title: 🔮 MagicDNS and custom domains
docs.text:
MagicDNS gives each device of the tailnet a name: instead of an IP like 100.110.x.x, you type http://your-server. Public Funnel addresses end in .ts.net (for example https://librefolio.your-tailnet.ts.net, where librefolio is the TS_HOSTNAME of Level 4).

A domain of your own, such as librefolio.mydomain.com, for private access through the VPN: two methods.

🌍 Method 1 — A public DNS record pointing to the Tailscale IP (simplest)

In the console of your domain registrar (e.g. Cloudflare, GoDaddy, Namecheap):

  1. Create a type A (or AAAA for IPv6) DNS record for the chosen subdomain (e.g. librefolio.mydomain.com).
  2. Point it at the server's private Tailscale IP (e.g. 100.77.x.x).

The name works only while you are connected to the tailnet: the 100.64.0.0/10 network is not routable on the internet, no outsider can reach or scan the service. Details: official documentation on DNS settings.

🧭 Method 2 — Split DNS with your own DNS server

For internal records that you manage, never published on the internet:

  1. In your LAN: set up a private DNS server (Pi-hole, AdGuard Home or CoreDNS).
  2. In your DNS server: add the records of your domain, pointing them at your Tailscale IPs.
  3. In the Tailscale admin console, DNS -> Nameservers -> Add Nameserver: add the Tailscale IP of your private DNS, as a global nameserver or restricted to your domain. Details: official documentation on Split DNS.

For public access, keep the *.ts.net address: Funnel's certificate is signed for that name, so a CNAME from your domain gives SSL/TLS errors in browsers, unless you add a reverse proxy of your own (Caddy or Nginx) with certificates for your domain.

docs.title: 🔗 Useful links
docs.text:
• 🖥️ Tailscale admin console (Machines)
  • 🔐 Access controls management (ACLs)
  • 📖 Official guide to Tailscale Funnel (documentation in English)
  • 🐳 Running Tailscale in Docker

docs.title: 🔗 Related
docs.text: • 📄 Exposing Securely: Public Access with Funnel — Enabling Funnel and ACLs on the console, Level 3: Public HTTPS address with Tailscale Funnel, Level 4: Multi-Funnel with Docker sidecars

docs.title: 🌍 Exposing Securely: Public Access with Funnel
docs.text:
LibreFolio on the internet with Tailscale Funnel, at a public HTTPS address, with no port opened on your router:

  • the one-time setup of Funnel and the ACLs in the Tailscale console;
  • Level 3: one address for LibreFolio, with one command on the server;
  • Level 4: one address per service, each with its own Docker container.

Tailscale must already be installed on the server: why Tailscale, Step 0 (the installation) and the private Levels 1 and 2 are in Exposing Securely. 6040 is LibreFolio's default port: if you set a different PORT in your .env, use that number.

docs.title: 🔑 Enabling Funnel and ACLs on the console
docs.text:
One-time setup, needed by Levels 3 and 4. It allows Funnel in the access control rules (ACLs) of your whole tailnet.

🔐 Before you make the service public

With Funnel, anyone on the internet can open LibreFolio's login page. Create your own account first: until one exists, anyone can register, and the first account registered becomes the administrator. After that, a new instance lets people in only with an invitation link (Registration is By invitation by default): send one to each person. An instance upgraded from an earlier version keeps its mode: if Registration in Global Settings is Open, switch it to By invitation, or to Closed if nobody else should join (Who Can Sign Up).

Where: in the Tailscale admin console, Access Controls page.

  1. Click Add node attribute.

  2. Fill in the form:

    Field Value Targets The nodes allowed to use Funnel. We suggest tag:external_access (you will give it to the Level 4 containers) or autogroup:member (all the devices of your account). Attributes funnel Note A few words on why the rule exists. IP Pools, App, Capability, etc. Leave them empty or at their default values.

Result: the nodes listed can turn Funnel on. This rule is not an auth key: auth keys (Level 4) only register a new device or container in the tailnet.

📄 View the complete ACL JSON configuration to enable Funnel

Where: in the tailnet policy file, if you prefer to edit it directly. It enables Funnel for your own devices and for the containers tagged tag:external_access:

{
  // Declaration of authorized tags
  "tagOwners": {
    "tag:external_access": ["autogroup:admin"]
  },

  // Standard access rules
  "acls": [
    // Allows all nodes in your private network to communicate
    {"action": "accept", "src": ["*"], "dst": ["*:*"]}
  ],

  "ssh": [
    {
      "action": "check",
      "src":    ["autogroup:member"],
      "dst":    ["autogroup:self"],
      "users":  ["autogroup:nonroot", "root"]
    }
  ],

  // Enabling Funnel on specific nodes or tags
  "nodeAttrs": [
    {
      "target": ["autogroup:member"],
      "attr":   ["funnel"]
    },
    {
      "target": ["tag:external_access"],
      "attr":   ["funnel"]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: 🥈 Level 3: Public HTTPS address with Tailscale Funnel
docs.text:
Best for a public address, with no VPN on the client. Funnel publishes LibreFolio at https://<server-name>.your-tailnet.ts.net, which anyone opens without installing Tailscale. HTTPS is also what lets you install LibreFolio as an app (PWA) on your phone.

Before you start: complete Funnel and ACLs on the console.

graph LR
    User["👤 User (No VPN)"] -->|HTTPS Request| Funnel["☁️ Tailscale Funnel Ingress<br>(Tailscale Public Server)"]
    Funnel -->|WireGuard Tunneling| Server["🖥️ Local Server (tailscaled)<br>(100.a.b.c)"]
    subgraph LAN ["Local LAN Network"]
        Server -->|Local forwarding| LibreFolio["📊 LibreFolio (Port 6040)"]
        Server -.->|"<font color='red'><b>Cannot expose</b></font>"| Other["🔌 Other Local Services (Different ports)"]
    end
    style LibreFolio fill:#d4edda,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#28a745,stroke-width:2px;
    style Other fill:#f8d7da,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#dc3545,stroke-width:2px;
    linkStyle 3 stroke:#dc3545,stroke-width:2px;

docs.title: ▶️ Step 1: Start the Funnel on the server
docs.text:
Where: on the server, in a terminal. Publish LibreFolio's local port:

tailscale funnel --bg 6040

Result: LibreFolio is served at https://<server-name>.your-tailnet.ts.net on port 443. --bg keeps it running after you close the terminal; tailscale funnel reset stops it.

  • No auth key: the server already joined the tailnet in Step 0.
  • Nothing to configure in LibreFolio: Funnel sends X-Forwarded-Proto: https, so with the default SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=auto the session cookie is marked Secure. never is only for a proxy that claims HTTPS to a browser on plain, unencrypted HTTP.

docs.title: ✅ Step 2: Approve and wait for propagation
docs.text:
The first time, the terminal warns that Funnel is not yet allowed for this node:

Funnel is enabled, but the list of allowed nodes in the tailnet policy file does not include the one you are using.
To give access to this node you can edit the tailnet policy file, or visit:

         https://login.tailscale.com/f/funnel?node=xxxxxx
  1. In the browser: open the link, log in to Tailscale and approve Funnel for this node.
  2. In the server's terminal: your public URL appears.
  3. From an outside network: wait a few minutes for the MagicDNS records to propagate, then open the URL.

To check the result: Checking Connection Security.

⚠️ Limits: one machine has one public name, shared by every service it publishes. Level 4 gives each service its own.

docs.title: 🥇 Level 4: Multi-Funnel with Docker sidecars
docs.text:
Best for Docker users who want one public address per service. Each service gets a small Tailscale container (a sidecar), a node of the tailnet in its own right with its own https://<name>.your-tailnet.ts.net. A startup script installs socat in the sidecar, which forwards the Funnel traffic to the static LAN IP of the service.

Before you start: complete Funnel and ACLs on the console.

🧰 What is socat?

socat (SOcket CAT) relays data between two connections: it listens on a port inside the Tailscale container and passes everything to the real port of the service on your LAN.

One sidecar for every service you want to publish, on one host or several; the only limit is the number of tagged devices of your Tailscale plan. Here two hosts run two sidecars each:

graph LR
    User["👤 External User"] -->|HTTPS| Funnel1["☁️ Funnel 1<br>(librefolio.yourtailnet.ts.net)"]
    User -->|HTTPS| Funnel2["☁️ Funnel 2<br>(service1.yourtailnet.ts.net)"]
    User -->|HTTPS| Funnel3["☁️ Funnel 3<br>(service3.yourtailnet.ts.net)"]

docs.title: 📁 Step 1: Prepare the folder and the script
docs.text:
Where: on the server, in a terminal. Create a folder, for example where you keep your Docker persistent volumes:

# Create a folder for the Tailscale nodes and enter it
mkdir -p <path_chosen>/tailscale-nodes
cd <path_chosen>/tailscale-nodes

Download the startup script custom_startup.sh into it:

# Download the script from the official repository
wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Librefolio/LibreFolio/main/mkdocs_src/docs/static/tailscale-guide/custom_startup.sh
# Make the script executable
chmod +x custom_startup.sh

Result: the folder <path_chosen>/tailscale-nodes holds an executable custom_startup.sh; in Step 2 you mount it in the container.

🔄 Set up the sidecar before? Update your copy of the script

The current script also works as a watchdog and has a Docker health check (Step 2). If your sidecar runs an older copy:

  1. On the server, in the script's folder: download the script again. -O custom_startup.sh overwrites the old file (without it, wget saves the download as custom_startup.sh.1).

    cd <path_chosen>/tailscale-nodes
wget -O custom_startup.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Librefolio/LibreFolio/main/mkdocs_src/docs/static/tailscale-guide/custom_startup.sh
chmod +x custom_startup.sh

  2. In your docker-compose.yml: add TS_ENABLE_HEALTH_CHECK, TS_LOCAL_ADDR_PORT and, optionally, STARTUP_TIMEOUT to the Tailscale service, together with the healthcheck block, exactly as in Step 2.

  3. In the folder of the docker-compose.yml: recreate the container, a restart does not apply compose changes.

    docker compose up -d

    It recreates the services whose configuration changed. Alternatively, the Recreate / re-deploy action of Portainer or CasaOS.

  4. In the container log: docker logs -f tailscale-librefolio shows Tailscale is running., then Starting the funnel on port 6040... and Available on the internet: with your public URL. Within the 2-minute start_period of the health check, Docker shows the container as healthy (docker ps, Portainer, CasaOS). If it keeps restarting: troubleshooting panel in Step 3.

docs.title: 🐳 Step 2: Configure Docker Compose
docs.text:
Where: in the docker-compose.yml of the exposed service (for example LibreFolio), so the two stay together. Add the Tailscale service:

services:
  tailscale-librefolio:
    image: tailscale/tailscale:latest
    container_name: tailscale-librefolio
    hostname: tailscale-librefolio
    restart: unless-stopped
    privileged: false
    network_mode: bridge
    cap_add:
      - NET_ADMIN
      - NET_RAW
    devices:
      - /dev/net/tun:/dev/net/tun
    command:
      - /custom_startup.sh
    environment:
      - HOST_IP=192.168.1.20                # Local IP of the service to expose (e.g. Server 1)
      - HOST_PORT=6040                      # Real port of the service to expose
      - TAILSCALE_FUNNEL_PORT=6040          # Internal Funnel port
      - TS_HOSTNAME=librefolio              # Custom public hostname (e.g. librefolio)
      - TS_AUTHKEY=tskey-auth-...           # Authentication key generated by Tailscale
      - TS_ACCEPT_DNS=true
      - TS_STATE_DIR=/var/lib/tailscale
      - TS_USERSPACE=false
      - TS_ENABLE_HEALTH_CHECK=true         # Expose /healthz for the healthcheck below (Tailscale ≥ 1.78)
      - TS_LOCAL_ADDR_PORT=127.0.0.1:9002   # Where /healthz listens: inside the container only
      - STARTUP_TIMEOUT=180                 # Optional: seconds to reach the Running state (default 180)
    volumes:
      - <path_chosen>/tailscale-nodes/tailscale-librefolio/state:/var/lib/tailscale
      - <path_chosen>/tailscale-nodes/custom_startup.sh:/custom_startup.sh
      - /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro
      - /etc/timezone:/etc/timezone:ro
    # Shows healthy/unhealthy in Docker, Portainer or CasaOS; the restart itself comes from custom_startup.sh exiting
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-q", "-O", "/dev/null", "http://127.0.0.1:9002/healthz"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 120s

Set these values for your network:

Value What to put <path_chosen> The absolute path of Step 1, where the script and the state data live (for example /home/user/docker). HOST_IP The static LAN IP of the machine that runs the service. HOST_PORT The real port of the service on that machine: for LibreFolio, the PORT of your .env (6040 by default). TAILSCALE_FUNNEL_PORT The port the container listens on and publishes through Funnel. Same value as HOST_PORT. TS_HOSTNAME The name of the node: the public address becomes https://TS_HOSTNAME.your-tailnet.ts.net. TS_AUTHKEY The key that registers the container in the tailnet (below).

Where to get TS_AUTHKEY: in the Tailscale console, Keys page.

  1. In the Auth keys section (not in the API access tokens section), click Generate auth key....
  2. Turn on the Tags toggle and select your tag (for example tag:external_access). Add a description you will recognize, such as docker-librefolio-funnel.
  3. Click Generate and copy the key (tskey-auth-...) into TS_AUTHKEY.

Result: on the container's first start the one-time key is used up, it disappears from Keys and the new device appears in Machines.

🩺 Watchdog and health check — what the extra settings do
  • Watchdog (automatic restart), in the script: if Tailscale does not start (no internet at boot, a wrong flag), does not reach the Running state within STARTUP_TIMEOUT seconds, or Tailscale, socat or the Funnel stop later on, the script exits with an error and Docker restarts the container (restart: unless-stopped). The container never stays "running" with nothing behind it; docker stop still shuts everything down cleanly.
  • Health check (status only), in the compose: TS_ENABLE_HEALTH_CHECK=true turns on Tailscale's /healthz endpoint (Tailscale 1.78 or later): 200 while the node has a Tailscale IP, 503 otherwise. Docker, Portainer and CasaOS show healthy or unhealthy.

Plain Docker (outside Swarm) does not restart an unhealthy container: the restart comes from the script exiting. No "autoheal" container is needed: it would also require the Docker socket, that is full control of the host.

Optional setting What it does TS_LOCAL_ADDR_PORT Where /healthz listens. The endpoint needs no authentication, and Tailscale's default, [::]:9002, listens on all interfaces: 127.0.0.1:9002 keeps it inside the container. If you change it, update the URL of the healthcheck test too. STARTUP_TIMEOUT Seconds to wait for the Running state (default 180) before exiting and having the container restarted. Raise it only on a very slow server. DEBUG Not in the example above. DEBUG=1 prints every command the script runs to the container log. Off by default to keep the log readable. 📈 Watching LibreFolio with a monitor (Uptime Kuma)

The librefolio service has a health check of its own, on GET /api/v1/system/health (see the compose file below): it tells Docker that the server answers. To watch it from another device, for example with Uptime Kuma, point the monitor at /api/v1/system/ready on the address you open LibreFolio with, such as https://librefolio.your-tailnet.ts.net/api/v1/system/ready. It needs no sign-in and answers:

  • 200 when LibreFolio is ready to serve requests;
  • 503 when it is not, with the check at fault in the answer: database (unreachable) or migrations (behind, ahead, unknown).

The codes: Advanced Docker Guide, section «Service: librefolio».

📄 View the complete production Docker Compose file (LibreFolio + Tailscale)

The librefolio service of the official docker-compose.prod.yml file, with the Tailscale sidecar next to it:

# =============================================================================
# LibreFolio — Production Docker Compose
# =============================================================================
# Optimized for end-users running the official pre-built image from GHCR.
# =============================================================================

services:
  librefolio:
    image: ${LIBREFOLIO_IMAGE:-ghcr.io/librefolio/librefolio:latest}
    container_name: librefolio
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${PORT:-6040}:6040"
    volumes:
      - ./LibreFolio-data:/app/backend/data/prod-docker
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      - LIBREFOLIO_DATA_DIR=/app/backend/data/prod-docker
      - HOST=0.0.0.0
      - PORT=6040
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:6040/api/v1/system/health')"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      start_period: 15s
      retries: 3

  tailscale-librefolio:
    image: tailscale/tailscale:latest
    container_name: tailscale-librefolio
    hostname: tailscale-librefolio
    restart: unless-stopped
    privileged: false
    network_mode: bridge
    cap_add:
      - NET_ADMIN
      - NET_RAW
    devices:
      - /dev/net/tun:/dev/net/tun
    command:
      - /custom_startup.sh
    environment:
      - HOST_IP=192.168.1.20                # Local IP of the service to expose (e.g. Server 1)
      - HOST_PORT=6040                      # Real port of the service to expose
      - TAILSCALE_FUNNEL_PORT=6040          # Internal Funnel port
      - TS_HOSTNAME=librefolio              # Custom public hostname (e.g. librefolio)
      - TS_AUTHKEY=tskey-auth-...           # Replace with your generated key
      - TS_ACCEPT_DNS=true
      - TS_STATE_DIR=/var/lib/tailscale
      - TS_USERSPACE=false
      - TS_ENABLE_HEALTH_CHECK=true         # Expose /healthz for the healthcheck below (Tailscale ≥ 1.78)
      - TS_LOCAL_ADDR_PORT=127.0.0.1:9002   # Where /healthz listens: inside the container only
      - STARTUP_TIMEOUT=180                 # Optional: seconds to reach the Running state (default 180)
    volumes:
      - /DATA/AppData/tailscale-nodes/tailscale-librefolio/state:/var/lib/tailscale
      - /DATA/AppData/tailscale-nodes/custom_startup.sh:/custom_startup.sh
      - /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro
      - /etc/timezone:/etc/timezone:ro
    # Shows healthy/unhealthy in Docker, Portainer or CasaOS; the restart itself comes from custom_startup.sh exiting
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-q", "-O", "/dev/null", "http://127.0.0.1:9002/healthz"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 120s

docs.title: 🚀 Step 3: Start and approve the Funnel
docs.text:
1. On the server, in the folder of the docker-compose.yml: start the stack, service and sidecar together.

    docker compose up -d

  2. In the Tailscale container log: on the first start, the approval link for the new node appears.

    docker logs -f tailscale-librefolio

    Funnel is enabled, but the list of allowed nodes in the tailnet policy file does not include the one you are using.
To give access to this node you can edit the tailnet policy file, or visit:

         https://login.tailscale.com/f/funnel?node=nsKGo6k9ZF11CNTRL

  3. In the browser: open the link, log in to Tailscale and approve the Funnel activation. Right after, the log confirms the public URL and the local proxy:

    Available on the internet:

https://librefolio.yourtailnet.ts.net/
|-- proxy http://127.0.0.1:6040

Press Ctrl+C to exit.

  4. From an outside network: wait a few minutes for the MagicDNS records to propagate, then open the URL.

Result: the service is online. Nothing to configure in LibreFolio: Funnel sends X-Forwarded-Proto: https and socat passes it on, so the session cookie is Secure with the default SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=auto (see Level 3, Step 1).

To check the result: Checking Connection Security.

🛠️ The container restarts in a loop or is marked unhealthy

A persistent problem is a container that keeps restarting (Docker, Portainer or CasaOS may also mark it unhealthy), not one that looks "running" but does not work. In the log, docker logs tailscale-librefolio: before each restart, the script prints what went wrong, usually followed by Exiting so Docker restarts the container. The most common causes:

  • A flag in TS_EXTRA_ARGS has no value. This optional variable (not in the compose above) passes extra flags to tailscale up, split on spaces. A flag without a value makes tailscale up fail: the reason is on the line right after Running 'tailscale up', above the help text that starts with USAGE (for example flag needs an argument: -advertise-tags), followed by failed to auth tailscale: … tailscale up failed: exit status 2 and containerboot exited before Tailscale was running. Write each value as --flag=value or --flag value: --advertise-tags=tag:container and --advertise-tags tag:container both work.
  • A management panel truncated the value. The environment-variable editor of CasaOS (and of similar panels) truncates a value at its second =: TS_EXTRA_ARGS=--advertise-tags=tag:container becomes --advertise-tags, which fails as above. In these panels, write the flags with a space: --advertise-tags tag:container.
  • A required variable is missing: the script stops at once with HOST_IP is not set (or the same message for HOST_PORT or TAILSCALE_FUNNEL_PORT).
  • No internet at boot: the container restarts until Tailscale starts, then works normally. This is expected.
  • Very slow start: the log shows Tailscale is not running after 180s.; raise STARTUP_TIMEOUT.
  • Unhealthy, but not restarting: no successful answer from /healthz. If you have just added it, check that TS_ENABLE_HEALTH_CHECK=true is set and that the URL of the healthcheck test matches TS_LOCAL_ADDR_PORT; otherwise, the node has no Tailscale IP at the moment.

To trace every command of the script: in the docker-compose.yml, add DEBUG=1 to the environment section, recreate the container and read the log again.

Because its auth key carries a tag, Tailscale disables key expiry for the container by default. With an untagged key, disable it as for the server (tip at the end of Step 0).

⚠️ Limits: it takes a terminal and some editing of Docker Compose files.
