  • GET /users/over-limit lists the active accounts (who is protected, how many brokers each owns alone); POST /users/over-limit/resolve {keep_user_ids} deactivates the others in one transaction under SQLite's write lock, as update_user_status(is_active=False) does (sessions end, links retired), never delete_user. Refusals: 409 NOT_OVER_LIMIT; 422 UNKNOWN_USER, TOO_MANY_KEPT, PROTECTED_MISSING, NO_ADMIN_KEPT.
  • Protected: the managed owner (account_protection); with none, the administrator who chooses. At least one administrator stays. Live invitations are revoked newest first only as far as the kept accounts need their places; accounts waiting for a verification keep theirs.
  • The web app shows UserLimitPage instead of the app on the first 423 user_limit_exceeded (features/instance/userLimit*.ts, the same shape as the instance block).
Request When used >= max_users POST /auth/register without an invitation The account is inserted, then counted in the same transaction: over the limit, rollback and 409 USER_LIMIT_REACHED, with no numbers and no link, as the caller is anonymous. The first writer holds SQLite's write lock until it commits, so two registrations racing for the last place cannot both take it POST /auth/register with a valid invitation, or for the first account Not checked POST /users/invites 409 USER_LIMIT_REACHED with limit, used and billing_url, counted under SQLite's write lock (lot A-56: Decided under the write lock) PATCH /users/{user_id} reactivating an account The same 409, counted under the write lock too (lot A-56), except for an account waiting for its email verification whose link is live: holds_place() says that its place is already counted. Once the link has expired, the account needs a free place like any other. Promotions, demotions and deactivations are not checked ./dev.py user create, ./dev.py user invite, ./dev.py user activate of an inactive account The warning The instance is at its limit (LIBREFOLIO_MAX_USERS: <used> of <max> places taken): the command line <action> anyway, <action> being creates the account, creates the invitation or reactivates the account; then the command goes ahead. user activate prints none for an account that already holds its place: one waiting for its email verification whose link is live (holds_place()), or, since lot A-40, the initial administrator waiting for its setup (registration_service.is_pending_admin(), the filter user_usage() counts it with; IMG-030f of ./dev.py test utils dev-cli-image)

billing_link() returns LIBREFOLIO_BILLING_URL to administrators only: in usage.billing_url of GET /users, in the 409 USER_LIMIT_REACHED of the administrator routes, and in billing_url of GET /system/block, the block page of a blocked instance (Security → Instance Block). An invalid LIBREFOLIO_BILLING_URL or LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL is treated as unset and logged like an invalid mode, with its own consequence: the billing link stays hidden until it is fixed, or links show the bare path until it is fixed.

docs.title: 🛠️ Administrator API
docs.text:
backend/app/api/v1/users.py, every route behind require_admin (401 without a valid session, 403 Admin access required for a regular account); the last row, the public half of the address probe, is in auth.py. The static paths are declared before /users/{user_id}, so /users/invites, /users/account-links and /users/address-probe are never read as a user id.

Route Body Does Answers GET /users — Every account, oldest first (id, username, email, is_active, is_superuser, created_at, protected: see Protected Accounts, holds_place: inactive and waiting for its email verification with a live link, so its place is already counted, from place_holders() in one query — see Email Verification —, pending_verification: inactive and waiting for its email verification, a link neither used nor revoked, live or expired, so that the Users tab badges it — holds_place says whether it still holds a place —, from email_verification.waiting_ids() in one query (lot E-7), pending_setup: the initial administrator waiting for its setup, from registration_service.pending_admin_ids() in one query, and avatar_url: the account's avatar as its user settings store it, an image uploaded to the app or an address, null without one or without a settings row, from user_service.avatar_urls() in one query, lot N69-4), with usage: {used, max_users, billing_url} 200 PATCH /users/{user_id} {is_active?, is_superuser?, cancel_setup?} update_user_status(), all or nothing: an omitted field, or a value equal to the current one, changes nothing, with two exceptions for is_active: false on an account inactive already: one waiting for its email verification ends the wait as user deactivate does — its links revoked, its place free —, and the initial administrator waiting for its setup has its setup links revoked, the cancellation of its link (any other account has the setup links it never consumed retired). cancel_setup: true (default false, lot A-51) makes the request that cancellation and nothing else: an account that does not wait for its setup is left as it is. The service reads the account again under SQLite's write lock before its own decisions — a deactivation or a demotion, the last active administrator, «waiting» —, so a change committed since the route's first read, a setup completed for one, is seen (Decided under the write lock). A deactivation or a demotion ends every session of the account. A change of is_active revokes the account's email-verification links and retires its setup links (The Initial Administrator) 200 with the account, holds_place, pending_verification, pending_setup and avatar_url included (holds_place and pending_verification false once a wait has ended, pending_verification from awaiting_verification(); pending_setup still true after a cancellation); 404, also for an account deleted since the route's first read (lot A-54); 422 for cancel_setup: true without is_active: false; 409 ACCOUNT_PROTECTED for a deactivation, a demotion or a cancellation of a protected account, checked first; 409 PENDING_SETUP for is_superuser: false or is_active: true on the initial administrator waiting for its setup (is_pending_admin()), checked before the user limit, nothing changed; 409 LAST_ADMIN for the last active administrator; 409 SETUP_COMPLETED for cancel_setup: true on an account that does not wait for its setup, its setup completed since the caller looked (A setup completed meanwhile), nothing changed; 409 USER_LIMIT_REACHED for a reactivation over the limit, counted under the write lock (lot A-56), unless the account holds_place GET /users/{user_id}/deletion-preview — preview_user_deletion(): what deleting the account would take with it. Writes nothing 200 AccountDeletionPreviewRead; 404 DELETE /users/{user_id} — delete_account(): the account, and the brokers it is the only OWNER of, all or nothing. Cannot be undone: see Deleting an Account 204 with an empty body; 404, also for an account deleted since the route's first read; 409 SELF_DELETION, ACCOUNT_PROTECTED or DEMOTE_FIRST (never for the initial administrator waiting for its setup, deleted directly; whether the account is an administrator, and whether it still waits, is read under SQLite's write lock, so one set up or promoted since the route's first read answers DEMOTE_FIRST, lots A-51 and A-55: Decided under the write lock); 500 when the deletion fails, nothing deleted POST /users/{user_id}/password-reset-link — A reset link, shown once 201 {token, path, url, expires_at}; 404, also for an account deleted since the route's first read (under the write lock, lot A-54) POST /users/{user_id}/sessions/revoke — end_sessions(): every device of the account is signed out at its next request 204; 404, as above POST /users/{user_id}/onboarding/reset optional {flow} reset_onboarding_progress(): that flow, or every flow, back to pending, steps included, with completed_at and skipped_at cleared (backlog item 21-5) 204; 404, as above; 422 for a flow that does not exist GET /users/account-links — account_links.list_links(): every account token, of every purpose, newest first (lot UA3): id, purpose, state (revoked, used, expired or open, read in that order, as inspect_token() does: a retired link reads revoked), revocable, user_id and username, email, grants_admin, created_by_user_id and created_by_username, created_at, expires_at, used_at with used_by_user_id and used_by_username (the account that spent it: consumed_by_user_id, or the link's own account for a purpose other than invite), revoked_at. Never the token nor its hash 200 POST /users/invites {grants_admin=false, email?} create_invite(); the link is shown once 201 {invite, token, path, url}; 409 REGISTRATION_DISABLED; 409 USER_LIMIT_REACHED DELETE /users/account-links/{link_id} — account_links.revoke_link(): an open link of a purpose in REVOCABLE_PURPOSES (invite, password_reset, email_verification) stops working at once; an invitation frees its place. One conditional UPDATE: a link spent meanwhile is not revoked 204; 404 when no such link is open; 409 LINK_NOT_REVOCABLE for an open admin_setup link (cancelled from its account) or email_change link (the host's address drives it, and the next start issues it again) POST /users/address-probe — issue_probe_nonce(): a signed nonce for the address probe, valid 120 s and stored nowhere; a new one at every call 200 {nonce, expires_at}; 503 INSTANCE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE when the instance key cannot be used GET /auth/address-probe?nonce=… — Public, the same answer with or without a session: verify_probe_nonce(), whether this instance issued the nonce. Readable from any origin (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *) 200 {match}: false for anything not issued here or expired, never 422
  • path is token_path(): the page, with the token in the fragment (#token=…, see Links in Use). url is LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL followed by the path (public_link()), null when the variable is unset or invalid.
  • Each change writes a structured log event with the id of the account or of the invitation, and the administrator's (admin_id, or created_by_user_id for an invitation or a reset link): Invitation created, Invitation revoked by an administrator, Account updated by an administrator, Account deleted by an administrator, Password reset link created, Sessions ended by an administrator, Onboarding reset by an administrator. None carries the token or its hash.

Decided under the write lock (lots A-51 to A-56). A path that changes an account reads it, then takes SQLite's write lock and reads it again before its first write: user_service.refreshed_under_lock(session, user) calls backend.app.db.session.begin_writes(), then selects the id. When the account was deleted in between, it rolls back and answers False, and the caller answers as for an account that does not exist: 404 User not found, the bare string of _user_or_404(), or User '<username>' not found on the command line (lot A-54; before, the API answered a 500, or a success for nothing done, and the command line printed a traceback). Otherwise it refreshes the account, and the decisions listed below read it as it is under the lock: a setup completed or a promotion committed by another request since the first read is seen. The refusals a route makes on its first read (SELF_DELETION, ACCOUNT_PROTECTED, PENDING_SETUP) write nothing.

  • PATCH /users/{user_id} (update_user_status(), "NOT_FOUND" for an account gone): the last-administrator rule, «waiting» for a cancellation, and the change;
  • DELETE /users/{user_id}: whether the account is an administrator and whether it still waits for its setup, so one set up (A-51) or promoted (A-55) since the first read answers 409 DEMOTE_FIRST;
  • POST /users/{user_id}/password-reset-link, /sessions/revoke and /onboarding/reset (A-54);
  • DELETE /api/v1/auth/users/me (A-52): the other active administrators are counted under the lock, so of the last two active administrators deleting their own accounts at once, the second gets 400 LAST_ADMIN;
  • ./dev.py user activate, deactivate, promote and demote (set_user_active(), set_user_admin()): the last-administrator guard, then «waiting».

The user limit is counted under the lock too (A-56): the PATCH reactivating an account takes it before user_usage(), and create_invite() (POST /users/invites) before its count, so of two requests that saw the last free place, the second sees the first and answers 409 USER_LIMIT_REACHED, the PATCH's with the counts read under the lock. A refusal rolls back, and lets the lock go. Tests: TestDecidedUnderTheWriteLock of ./dev.py test api users-admin (UADM-LOCK-01 to UADM-LOCK-15) and of ./dev.py test api account-deletion (ACCDEL-LOCK-01 to ACCDEL-LOCK-03), and LOCK-CLI-01 and LOCK-CLI-02 of ./dev.py test services admin-bootstrap: without threads, a rival commits on another connection right before the code's first write.

docs.title: 🗑️ Deleting an Account
docs.text:
DELETE /api/v1/users/{user_id} deletes another account by the rule of deleting one's own: broker by broker, the last-owner rule of BrokerService.leave_broker(). A broker the account is the only OWNER of goes, with its transactions and its report files; on the others only the account's access goes. An inactive co-owner's OWNER row counts as another owner. The rule, the shared helper and the preview are in Deleting an Account.

GET /api/v1/users/{user_id}/deletion-preview tells the administrator beforehand what the deletion would take, by the same rule, writing nothing: brokers_deleted, brokers_left and transfers_unpaired. GET /api/v1/auth/users/me/deletion-preview gives any signed-in user the same for their own account.

After require_admin, the deletion refuses, in this order:

  1. 404 User not found: no such account;
  2. 409 SELF_DELETION: the caller's own account, which is deleted from the profile (DELETE /api/v1/auth/users/me);
  3. 409 ACCOUNT_PROTECTED, with the reason of the protection hook. It comes before DEMOTE_FIRST because demoting a protected account is refused too;
  4. 409 DEMOTE_FIRST: an administrator, active or not. It must be demoted first, so the last administrator can never be deleted from here. Not the initial administrator waiting for its setup (is_pending_admin(), lot A-43): it cannot be demoted (409 PENDING_SETUP) and never was an active administrator, so it is deleted directly, the hard cancellation of its setup: its setup links go with it (account_tokens.user_id cascades), its place is freed, and nobody waits any more: ./dev.py user setup-link finds nobody, and a next start with the variables still set answers ignored, since the instance has accounts (The Initial Administrator). Whether the account is an administrator, and whether it still waits, is read under SQLite's write lock, on the account read again (Decided under the write lock): one set up (lot A-51) or promoted (lot A-55) since the route's first read answers DEMOTE_FIRST, rolled back, nothing deleted; one deleted meanwhile answers the 404 of point 1 (lot A-54).

Each 409 carries detail {error_code, message}, plus reason for ACCOUNT_PROTECTED. Otherwise the route calls user_service.delete_account(), the helper of DELETE /auth/users/me too, and answers 204 with an empty body. All or nothing: a technical failure rolls everything back and answers 500 Account deletion failed: nothing was deleted. The deleted account's sessions get 401 at their next request.

  • Log: one structured event, Account deleted by an administrator, with user_id, username, admin_id, brokers_deleted (the ids of the deleted brokers) and files_removed. A failure logs Account deletion by an administrator failed: nothing was deleted, with user_id, admin_id and the traceback.
  • Blocked instance: both previews and the administrator's deletion are outside ALLOWED_WHEN_BLOCKED (Instance Block): 423 for a signed-in caller, 401 for anyone else. Of the deletion routes, only DELETE /api/v1/auth/users/me is on the list.

docs.title: 🛡️ Protected Accounts
docs.text:
user_service.account_protection(user) -> Optional[str] gives the reason why nobody may delete, deactivate or demote an account, or None. It is the hook for the owner of a managed instance, the administrator who pays for it (PAYING_ADMINISTRATOR). On any other profile it returns None for every account. On a managed instance (LIBREFOLIO_PROFILE=managed):

  • the account recorded as the instance owner (users.is_instance_owner) is protected by that mark alone, whatever its address and whatever the variable says;
  • once the startup step owner-sync has read the owner (user_service.note_recorded_owner()), the mark decides alone when an owner is recorded: an account that holds the address of a variable changed in conflict is a stranger and never receives the owner's protection;
  • when the step recorded nobody, the account with the address of LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL (A–Z case aside) is protected by its address only while it is an active administrator (the criterion by which the step records an owner);

  • before the step has run (a command, a test) the A5-1 address rule is the fallback: the address alone protects.

  • GET /users reflects it in protected (AdminUserRead), as do the accounts PATCH returns.

  • DELETE /users/{user_id}, and a PATCH /users/{user_id} that deactivates or demotes the account, or cancels the setup link of the initial administrator waiting for its setup (is_active: false on that inactive account, lot A-43, The Initial Administrator), answer 409 ACCOUNT_PROTECTED with that reason. The PATCH checks it first, before PENDING_SETUP, the user limit and the last-administrator rule.
  • Promoting or reactivating a protected account is not refused.
  • The command line stays above protection: ./dev.py user deactivate, user demote and the other user commands never read the hook, as the operator of the server may do what the administrator API refuses.

docs.title: 📬 The Owner's Address
docs.text:
The protected owner cannot change its address from the app (PUT /auth/profile answers 409 ACCOUNT_PROTECTED). The real change starts at the host, and services/accounts/instance_owner.py runs it:

  • startup_owner_sync(), the startup step owner-sync (right after restore-commit, which revokes every live one-time link after a restore and would kill a link issued before it; skipped while the instance serves no data): managed only, with a usable variable. A waiting initial administrator (pending_admin): nothing, bootstrap_admin_service follows the variable as before. No owner recorded: the account with the variable's address is recorded (heal) only if it is an active administrator, else an error is logged and nobody is recorded. The owner has the variable's address: nothing, stale links revoked. Otherwise: another account holds the address → blocked, an error line, no change; a live email_change link already carries it → waiting, nothing resent; else the owner's older links are revoked, a new one is issued (7 days, email = the new address) under SQLite's write lock (two workers issue one) and emailed to the NEW address in a background task (build_email_change_confirmation()). The link is logged at warning only when the email did not go.
  • owner_change_status(session) answers "pending", "blocked" or None for the security checks and the hosting panel. It reads only and never returns an address.
  • POST /email/email-change/confirm (confirm_owner_email_change, no session): confirm_email_change() spends the link and, in the same transaction, checks that the instance is managed, that the token's account is the recorded owner, that the token's address is still the variable's and that no other account holds it; then sets the address (verified), ends the owner's sessions, and revokes its other change links and its reset links. A link that no longer matches is revoked and answers TOKEN_INVALID revoked. The notice to the old address is flows.email_changed_work, as for the profile.

Tests: ./dev.py test services owner-email-change, ./dev.py test api owner-email-change, ./dev.py test db migration-005.

docs.title: 🔑 Password-Reset Links
docs.text:
A reset link is a password_reset account token: 30 minutes, single use, link /reset-password#token=…, bound to its account (user_id). Unlike ./dev.py user reset, the administrator does not choose the new password: whoever spends the link does.

  • Issued by user_service.create_password_reset(), from POST /api/v1/users/{user_id}/password-reset-link or ./dev.py user reset-link <username>, and, when email works, from Forgot Password? on the login page (POST /api/v1/email/password-reset, workstream E): that link is never shown, only emailed to the account's own address, within its limits, and never while an administrator's reset link is still live (A Forgotten Password). It first revokes the account's live reset links, so only the newest one works. Issuing a link ends no session.
  • Spent by POST /api/v1/auth/password-reset {token, new_password}, which is public. new_password must meet the password rules, checked before the token is read: a weak one is 400 PASSWORD_TOO_WEAK, and the link is neither spent nor inspected, so a valid link stays valid. complete_password_reset() consumes the token, hashes the new password with bcrypt in a worker thread, ends every session of the account, revokes its other live reset links and retires its setup links (The Initial Administrator), in one commit; the answer is 200. A link that is not valid (used, expired, revoked, unknown or of another purpose) changes nothing: 400 TOKEN_INVALID.
  • Revoked with the account's password or address: a password change, an email change (the same address in another A–Z case is none) and ./dev.py user reset revoke its live reset links, whoever issued them, in the commit of the change (lot A-27, Session Revocation).

Tests: ./dev.py test services registration (backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_registration_service.py: the variables, the effective mode, the usage, invitations, every branch of register_user(), the limit under a race), ./dev.py test api registration (backend/test_scripts/test_api/test_registration_api.py: registration by mode, inspection, the password reset, the password rules on both, the accounts block, the locked setting) and ./dev.py test api users-admin (backend/test_scripts/test_api/test_users_admin_api.py: the administrator API with its guards and its logs; the deletion and its preview on the lane's server, and in process the protection hook replaced, the log event and an injected failure; each account's avatar_url, lot N69-4, UADM-AV-01 to UADM-AV-04: in GET /users and in the answer of a PATCH on the lane's server, in process with the settings rows given the ids of other accounts, and the schema; each account's pending_verification, lot E-7, UADM-VER-01 to UADM-VER-05: in process, on a private database, in GET /users and in the answer of a PATCH, a live link and an expired one alike). The address probe has its own tests, listed in Address Probe.

The web pages of the links, /invite and /reset-password, are in Authentication Components.

The administrator's side is in Global Settings, section «Who Can Sign Up»; Configuration, section «Accounts and Sign-ups»; and Command-Line Tools, section «Manage Users».

docs.title: 👑 The Initial Administrator (F02)
docs.text:
Feature F02 of the release 1.3 plan (lot A7a): an operator, such as a hosting provider or a scripted install, names the administrator of a new instance in the environment. The startup creates it, inactive, with a single-use setup link; whoever spends the link chooses the password, activates the account and is signed in. The variables are read in backend/app/config/accounts.py, the rest is in backend/app/services/accounts/bootstrap_admin_service.py. Administrator side: «The Initial Administrator» in Configuration.

The variables. admin_bootstrap_config() returns an AdminBootstrapConfig(email, username, token), read at every call from the process environment only, or None while LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL is unset or blank: without the variables, an install is unchanged.

Variable Rule Refused with (AdminBootstrapConfigError.code) LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL An email address (pydantic EmailStr), surrounding spaces ignored. Turns F02 on ADMIN_EMAIL_INVALID LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_USERNAME admin when unset (DEFAULT_ADMIN_USERNAME); 3 to 50 characters and no @, the rules of every new username (USERNAME_MIN_LENGTH, USERNAME_MAX_LENGTH, which user_service applies too since lot A-46; USERNAME_RESERVED_CHARACTER since lot A-21a, see Which Account an Identifier Names); surrounding spaces ignored ADMIN_USERNAME_INVALID, for the length and for the @; the message of the @ names it and says that the administrator signs in with LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL anyway. ADMIN_USERNAME_WITHOUT_EMAIL without the email LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN, or its _FILE (env_secret()) Optional: the token of the setup link, given by a hosting panel; None for a generated one. 32 to 200 characters (ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_MIN_LENGTH; ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_MAX_LENGTH, the longest token the link's requests accept), each one in ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_CHARACTERS, the unreserved characters of a URL (A–Z a–z 0–9 - . _ ~): it travels in /setup#token=… as written. Not trimmed: like every secret env_secret() reads, it is used as written ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_INVALID_CHARACTERS (a space included), ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_TOO_SHORT, ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_TOO_LONG; ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_WITHOUT_EMAIL without the email. A _FILE that cannot give it raises SecretFileError

AdminBootstrapConfigError(variable, code, message), a ValueError, names the variable in variable and in its message, never the token. log_configuration_audit() calls admin_bootstrap_config() (Configuration Checks), so an unusable value stops the startup, on an instance with accounts too, as an unreadable LIBREFOLIO_BLOCKED does.

At startup. The admin-bootstrap step, right after global-settings (Server Startup), runs startup_admin_bootstrap(), which returns at once with F02 off. Otherwise run_admin_bootstrap(session, config) applies the variables, commits what it writes, and returns a BootstrapResult whose action (BootstrapAction) says what it did:

action When What it does off F02 off Nothing ignored Accounts exist and none is waiting, the setup done included, through the link or another way (below); or a re-arm that finds the setup completed in the meantime (rearmed) Logs LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_* ignored: this instance already has accounts (INFO); after a re-arm cut short, the INFO line of rearmed instead created No account at all In one transaction: the registration_mode row set to invite (inserted when missing, updated_by_user_id NULL); the administrator, superuser and inactive (create_user(..., is_superuser=True, is_active=False, commit=False)), whose password is the bcrypt hash of secrets.token_urlsafe(32), a secret nobody ever sees, so no password signs in and a login attempt costs what it costs for any account; an admin_setup token for it, the variable's or a generated one, 72 hours. A variable's token already stored once (an instance emptied after an earlier setup) is not stored again: a token is generated instead, with a warning naming the variable. link_token holds the plaintext of a generated token, and only of that rearmed An administrator waits, and the variable's token was never stored (_token_known(): no row has its hash, whatever its account or purpose) Revokes the administrator's setup links, then reads «waiting» again under the write lock that revocation took (lot A-42, The Setup Link's Lifecycle): an account set up in the meantime rolls everything back, and the start is ignored, with the INFO line LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN not re-armed: the initial administrator was set up meanwhile. Otherwise stores the new token, 72 hours. The token is neither logged nor emailed pending An administrator waits, with a live setup link Nothing new: no link issued, none logged expired An administrator waits, with no live setup link: the link expired, or was revoked — by a cancellation, for one — and no token of the variable re-arms it, as one already stored never does Logs one WARNING, which ends with the remedy run ./dev.py user setup-link, followed by , or set a new LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN when the variable is set. Which one (lot A-50): at the start that writes a new address, the WARNING of the address change (below); otherwise, when the account's latest setup link (by created_at, then id) was revoked and never consumed (_latest_setup_withdrawn()), a cancellation or an address change at an earlier start, The initial administrator's setup link was withdrawn (cancelled, or its address changed): …; otherwise The initial administrator's setup link has expired: …
  • The waiting administrator is pending_admin(session), built on registration_service.pending_admin_filter(): an inactive account with at least one admin_setup token, none of them consumed. An expired or revoked link keeps it waiting, a cancelled one included; a spent one ends the wait, and so does a retired one, the account set up another way (below). Before rearmed, pending or expired, the account follows the variables (_follow_variables()): a different username or email is written, unless another account holds it, which logs an ERROR and keeps the account's own.
  • A new address (lot A7b-2, A-33) — not the same one in another A–Z case, whose spelling the account simply takes (decision P18) — revokes the account's setup links in the transaction that writes it: they went to the earlier address. Revoked, not retired: the account still waits. A token of the variable never stored re-arms it at that start (rearmed); otherwise no live link is left and the start is expired, with the WARNING The initial administrator's address changed: the setup link handed over before no longer works; run ./dev.py user setup-link (and , or set a new LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN when the variable is set), once: the next starts log the WARNING of a withdrawn link, since the latest setup link is revoked (lot A-50, expired above), until a new link is given. A new username alone, or an address another account holds, revokes nothing. user_service.update_profile() revokes them the same way on a real change of the address (./dev.py user set-email): the account then waits for a link of ./dev.py user setup-link, and a next start whose LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_EMAIL names another address, the earlier one for instance, writes it, which revokes them again.
  • Registration. The waiting administrator is a users row, so first_account_open() is false from the first start, and nobody registers as the first account: register_user() applies the mode, invite unless LIBREFOLIO_REGISTRATION pins another. The step writes registration_mode only when it creates the administrator.
  • Delivery, only after created with a generated token. deliver_setup_link(result, engine=…) writes the link once in the log, at WARNING: Setup link of the initial administrator, single use: open it to choose the password, with link (public_link(): the full address with LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL, otherwise the path, and a note asking to put the server's address in front of it) and expires_at. Then, when require_email() and require_links() allow it, it emails the link to the account's address with build_admin_setup() (Email Service), in the instance's language (instance_language()). The startup runs it in a background task (asyncio.create_task()), with a session of its own, so a slow SMTP server never delays the start. It never raises: an email that cannot go logs Setup link of the initial administrator not emailed (INFO), with the exception's class in reason, and the link in the log still works. A token from the variable is neither logged nor emailed: the panel that chose it delivers it.
  • Several workers. Each worker runs the step, and only one creates the administrator. SQLite runs in WAL with a 30 s busy_timeout: a transaction whose first statement writes waits for the write lock, while one that reads first and writes later can fail at once with database is locked if another connection wrote in between. So _create_pending_admin() commits, which ends its reads, and starts with a write, the registration_mode row: it holds the write lock before it counts the accounts. The worker that comes second finds the account, goes on as pending, and delivers nothing. On a restart, a worker that finds the lock taken while another re-arms or renames answers pending, and lets that one apply the change.

The setup's status, for a hosting panel (lot H-61). admin_setup_status(session, *, now=None) tells the status route of a hosting panel where the setup of the initial administrator stands. It answers an AdminSetupStatus, a frozen dataclass: state, an AdminSetupState (a StrEnum, so it formats and serialises as its value: none, pending, done or expired), and setup_expires_at, in UTC, for pending only, None otherwise. It reads the admin_setup links of every account, though only the F02 administrator ever gets one; the links of the other purposes (invitations, password resets, email verifications) never count. The status is not «waiting» (pending_admin(), above): an administrator whose link ran out or was cancelled still waits, and its setup reads expired. The rule, in this order («done wins»):

  1. No admin_setup link stored: none. None was ever issued, or the account that held them was deleted: account_tokens.user_id is ON DELETE CASCADE, and its links went with it (Deleting an Account).
  2. Any admin_setup link consumed: done. Spent by the setup (complete_admin_setup(), below), or retired because the account was activated or given a password another way (A-32, below). A consumption is final: no link is issued after one (pending_admin() wants none consumed), so a stray newer link, which a setup through an older one leaves revoked, never makes a set-up instance read expired.
  3. Otherwise the latest link, by created_at then id, decides. Revoked without use — the setup cancelled (A-43), the address changed (A-33, above) — or past its expiry (expires_at <= now): expired. Otherwise pending, with that link's expires_at as setup_expires_at. A link replaced by a newer one (issue_setup_link(), a re-arm) is revoked too, but the newer one is then the latest, and decides.

now, the moment the expiry is compared with, is the clock (utcnow()) when left out. The function only reads: it writes and commits nothing, leaves nothing in the session for its caller to commit, and never takes SQLite's write lock.

The setup. POST /api/v1/auth/setup {token, new_password} (AdminSetupRequest, token of at most 200 characters) is public:

  1. The password rules come first: 400 PASSWORD_TOO_WEAK with rules, as for registration, a reset and a password change. Nothing is read or written, and a valid link stays valid.
  2. complete_admin_setup(session, token, new_password) spends the token first, with consume_token(), as a reset link does: of two requests racing for one link, only one gets it. A link that is not a live setup link (used, expired, revoked, unknown, of another purpose) changes nothing: 400 TOKEN_INVALID. The link of an account that is already active is refused the same way: the spending is rolled back, and every setup link of the account is retired (token_service.retire_tokens(), lot A7b-2), with the WARNING Setup link refused and retired: the account is already active. Since lot A-42, so is the link of an account another of whose setup links was already consumed (_setup_spent_before()): the setup done through it, or the links retired. That is a link left live by a race with a new link, or by an earlier 1.3 build, and its WARNING reads Setup link refused and retired: the account was set up before. Once the account is set up, by any way, none of its links may set its password, nor make it wait for its setup again once deactivated. Both refusals come before bcrypt (The Setup Link's Lifecycle).
  3. Otherwise, in one commit: the bcrypt hash of the new password, computed in a worker thread; the account active; its sessions ended (end_sessions(): session_version + 1); the link's consumed_by_user_id set to the account; its other setup links revoked.
  4. The answer is the login's: 200 AuthLoginResponse, show_donation_popup and user.whats_new (What's new) included, and the session cookie of _issue_session_cookie(). The administrator is signed in.

The route is not in ALLOWED_WHEN_BLOCKED (developer's decision P16: a blocked instance stays blocked until the subscription is paid): on a blocked instance it answers 401, like registration, and the link keeps running out its 72 hours. The pinned list of test_instance_block.py refuses any addition.

POST /api/v1/auth/tokens/inspect takes purpose: "admin_setup": a valid setup link answers username and expires_at, as a reset link does (Invitations).

The command line. ./dev.py user setup-link, with no argument (cmd_setup_link() in scripts/user_cli.py): issue_setup_link() revokes the waiting administrator's setup links, then, under the write lock that revocation took, reads «waiting» again (lot A-42, The Setup Link's Lifecycle): an account set up in the meantime gets no link. Otherwise it issues a generated one, 72 hours, which the command prints as reset-link prints its link: the full address with LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL, otherwise the path and a note. It sends no email. Without a waiting administrator, or once it was set up in the meantime, it prints ❌ No administrator account is waiting for its setup link and exits with 1.

Set up another way (lot A7b-2, A-32). The setup link is not the only way in, and the command line stays permissive on purpose: ./dev.py user activate and ./dev.py user reset on the waiting administrator are how an operator sets it up without its link (activate alone leaves an active account whose password nobody knows, until user reset or a reset link gives it one). Whatever the way, the account's setup links are retired in the transaction of the change, with token_service.retire_tokens(…, purpose=AccountTokenPurpose.ADMIN_SETUP): revoked and consumed at once (Revocation). The callers:

  • an activation: user_service.set_user_active(), behind user activate, and user_service.update_user_status(), behind PATCH /users/{user_id}, which refuses the waiting administrator itself first (409 PENDING_SETUP);
  • a new password: user_service.reset_password() (user reset), user_service.complete_password_reset() (a reset link spent, one an administrator issued for the waiting account included) and POST /auth/change-password;
  • complete_admin_setup(), when it refuses the link of an account already active, or, since lot A-42, of an account another of whose setup links was consumed (above).

This applies to every account with a setup link, not only the waiting one. Afterwards the old link inspects revoked (the setup page's withdrawn card) and sets nothing (400 TOKEN_INVALID), and the account is out of pending_admin_filter(), inactive or not: pending_setup is false, PATCH /users/{user_id} reactivates it as any inactive account (no 409 PENDING_SETUP), issue_setup_link() returns None (user setup-link prints its error), and the startup answers ignored. A reset link issued and never spent retires nothing: the account keeps waiting, and its link still works. Since lot A-43, a demotion of the waiting administrator is refused, and its deactivation revokes its setup links: the account keeps waiting, but the link handed over stops working (below).

The user limit. user_usage() counts the waiting administrator (pending_admin_filter()) beside the active accounts and the live invitations, its link live or not: it holds a place from its creation, and keeps it once active. Set up another way but still inactive, it waits no more and holds no place, as any inactive account.

The administrator API and the Users tab (lot A7b). The account waiting for its setup is marked:

  • GET /users and the answer of PATCH /users/{user_id} carry pending_setup (AdminUserRead, default false), true for an account of pending_admin_filter(): inactive, with at least one admin_setup token and none of them consumed — live, expired or revoked alike, an administrator or not; a retired token is consumed, so an account set up another way is false. registration_service.pending_admin_ids() reads it for the list, is_pending_admin() for one account. An expired link keeps the account waiting, and so does a cancelled one: ./dev.py user setup-link gives it a new one.
  • PATCH /users/{user_id} with is_active: true on that account, alone or with is_superuser, answers 409 with detail: {error_code: "PENDING_SETUP", message} and changes nothing: nobody knows its password, and an activation would retire its setup links (above). The check comes before the user limit. Since lot A-43 a demotion is refused with the same detail, word for word: is_superuser: false, alone or with is_active: false, changes nothing either, checked right after the protection hook. The account keeps its role until its setup: its link is cancelled, or the account deleted, instead (below).
  • The Users tab draws the account with the badge Waiting for setup; Cancel setup link in place of Reactivate, Remove administrator turned off with the reason pending-setup, Delete enabled (on a protected account, all three are off with the reason protected); and a hint that names dev.py user setup-link (UserRow).
  • No route issues a new setup link: in release 1.3 the command line does (backlog).

Cancelling the setup link (lot A-43). Deactivating the waiting administrator cancels the link handed over: PATCH /users/{user_id} with is_active: false (the Users tab's Cancel setup link, after a confirmation, sends {is_active: false, cancel_setup: true}, lot A-51) and ./dev.py user deactivate <username> revoke its setup links, live or expired (user_service._end_setup_links()). Whoever holds the link can no longer set the account up: inspected, it answers revoked, and POST /auth/setup with it 400 TOKEN_INVALID. The account keeps waiting: pending_setup stays true, in the 200 of the PATCH too, it keeps its place, and its reactivation stays 409 PENDING_SETUP. A new link comes from ./dev.py user setup-link, or from a new LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN at the next start; the same token re-arms nothing, being stored already, and that start is expired, with the WARNING of a withdrawn link rather than of an expiry (lot A-50: the latest setup link is revoked and never consumed), its remedy unchanged: The initial administrator's setup link was withdrawn (cancelled, or its address changed): …. The cancellation itself logs the WARNING of The Setup Link's Lifecycle; a second PATCH finds no link left to revoke and changes nothing. A protected account refuses it on the API, 409 ACCOUNT_PROTECTED, nothing changed and the link still working: update_account() asks the hook about the cancellation (cancel) as about a deactivation or a demotion. The command line stays above protection. The hard cancellation is the deletion, which needs no demotion first for this account (Deleting an Account). Deactivating any other account retires the setup links it never consumed instead, so that a stray one can never make it wait for its setup.

A setup completed meanwhile (lot A-51). The Users tab's row can be stale: the administrator may have spent its link since the list was loaded, or in the same millisecond. Sent with {is_active: false} alone, the same body as a deactivation, a cancellation from a row loaded before the setup would have deactivated the new owner. So the tab adds cancel_setup: true, which makes the request the cancellation and nothing else: update_user_status() reads «waiting» under SQLite's write lock, on the account read again, and an account that no longer waits answers 409 SETUP_COMPLETED (This account does not wait for its setup: nothing was changed, a sentence that also fits a direct API call on an account that never waited; the tab, which sends the field only from a waiting row, says the administrator completed its setup in the meantime), rolled back, with the INFO line Setup cancellation refused: the account does not wait for its setup (user_id). The tab reloads, and the row shows the account active. Without the field, {is_active: false} keeps its meaning, a deactivation, decided on the account as the lock finds it: in the same-millisecond race it deactivates the administrator just set up, and its answer is what the database holds (before lot A-51, a 200 read from the stale account, nothing deactivated). The deletion and the command line read the account again under the lock as well (Deleting an Account, Superusers and the User CLI).

The web page. The link opens /setup, an anonymous page that reads the token from the fragment, inspects it with the purpose admin_setup, then spends it with POST /auth/setup from SetupCard, and enters the app signed in: Account Link Pages.

How the setup link is protected (stored by its hash, single use, logged once by design) is in Links in Use.

Tests: ./dev.py test services admin-bootstrap (backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_admin_bootstrap.py, PURE, every database a private file: the variables and their codes, issue_token(token=), every action, two engines racing for the creation, the expiry to the microsecond, the delivery and the logs, complete_admin_setup(), the usage, user setup-link, the startup step) and ./dev.py test api admin-setup (backend/test_scripts/test_api/test_admin_setup_api.py: POST /auth/setup and tokens/inspect with admin_setup; in process on private databases for every case that needs a waiting administrator, and on the lane's server only refusals that write nothing). The administrator API's side is UADM-060 to UADM-067 of ./dev.py test api users-admin (backend/test_scripts/test_api/test_users_admin_api.py), in process, on a private database where the bootstrap itself creates the waiting administrator: pending_setup on each state of a setup link, the 409 PENDING_SETUP, and what that refusal must not reach. Lot A7b-2 adds A32-001 to A32-007 and A33-001 to A33-003 to admin-bootstrap (set up another way, the refused link of an active account, a new address in the variables), SETUP-014 and SETUP-015 to admin-setup, UADM-068 to UADM-071 to users-admin, UPROF-003 to UPROF-005 of ./dev.py test services user-profile (a new address through update_profile()), and contract 9 of ./dev.py test services account-tokens (retire_tokens()). Lots A-42 and A-43 add A42-001 to A42-006 and A43-001 to A43-005 to admin-bootstrap (the issue and the re-arm under the write lock, a stray link refused at its spending; the cancellation revoking, another account's deactivation retiring, user demote refused), SETUP-016 to SETUP-018 to admin-setup (what leaves the account waiting, user deactivate cancelling its link, the stray link of an account set up before) and UADM-072 to UADM-079 to users-admin (the demotion refused, the cancellation through the PATCH, another administrator's stray link retired, the direct deletion and the protection hook before it, the cancellation of a protected waiting administrator refused, its link still working). Lot A-50 adds A50-001 to A50-004 to admin-bootstrap: the start after a cancellation, from the Users tab or from user deactivate, and the starts after the one that wrote a new address, log the WARNING of a withdrawn link; a link that ran out still logs the expiry, even when an earlier one was revoked by a re-arm, as the latest link decides. Lot A-51 adds A51-001 to A51-006 to users-admin (TestTheSetupCompletedWhileTheUsersTabActs: a cancellation from a stale list or in the setup's window answers SETUP_COMPLETED and changes nothing, a cancellation of an account still waiting works as before, cancel_setup without is_active: false is 422, a plain deactivation in that window deactivates the administrator just set up and says so, a deletion in it answers DEMOTE_FIRST) and A51-007 and A51-008 to admin-bootstrap (user deactivate and user demote of the only administrator of a new instance while its setup completes, both refused as the last active administrator). Lot H-61 adds H61-001 to H61-018 to admin-bootstrap, for admin_setup_status(): the two types and the signature; none without any setup link, the tokens of the other purposes counting for nothing, and once the administrator was deleted; pending after the creation, until the expiry to the microsecond; done through the link, another way, and through the older of two links; expired once the link was withdrawn; the link that replaced another; of two links, a consumed one first, otherwise the newer; the order by created_at then id; the links of every account; nothing written in any state; the clock without now. Every test name holds setup_status, so ./dev.py test services admin-bootstrap setup_status runs them alone.

docs.title: 🏗️ System Architecture Overview
docs.text: LibreFolio is designed as a modern web application with a clear separation between the backend API and the frontend user interface.

docs.title: 🗺️ High-Level Diagram
docs.text:
The architecture can be visualized as three main components:

graph TD
    subgraph User's Browser
        Frontend[SvelteKit Frontend]
    end

    subgraph Server
        Backend[FastAPI Backend]
        Database[(SQLite Database)]
    end

    subgraph External Services
        direction TB
        BrokerAPIs[Broker APIs / CSVs]
        PricingAPIs[Pricing APIs]
        FXAPIs[FX Rate APIs]
        WebSearch[Web Search Engine<br/>ddgs metasearch]
    end

    subgraph Plugins
        direction TB
        B_Plugins[BRIM Plugins]
        A_Plugins[Asset Plugins]
        F_Plugins[FX Plugins]
        R_Plugins[Risk Analytics]
        T_Plugins[Tool Plugins]
    end

    Frontend -- HTTP API Calls --> Backend
    Backend -- SQLAlchemy ORM --> Database

    Backend -- Uses --> Plugins

    B_Plugins -- Parses --> BrokerAPIs
    A_Plugins -- Fetches --> PricingAPIs
    F_Plugins -- Fetches --> FXAPIs

    A_Plugins -. Last-resort URL resolve .-> WebSearch

docs.title: 🧱 Components
docs.text:
1. 🖥️ Frontend (SvelteKit): A single-page application (SPA) that runs in the user's browser. It communicates with the backend via a RESTful API to fetch and display data.

  2. ⚙️ Backend (FastAPI): A Python-based API server that handles all business logic, including:

    • 🔐 User authentication and authorization.
    • 🗃️ Database operations (CRUD).
    • 📥 Data import from brokers (BRIM).
    • 📈 Fetching asset prices and FX rates from external sources.

  3. 🗄️ Database (SQLite): A single-file database that stores all user data, including transactions, assets, user settings, and cached data.

  4. 🔌 Provider Plugins: A system of pluggable modules that abstract the interaction with external data sources. This makes it easy to add support for new brokers, pricing APIs, or FX rate providers without modifying the core application logic. The same registry mechanism also discovers plugins that call no external service: the risk analytics and the Tools.

docs.title: 🔑 Key Subsystems
docs.text:
For detailed architectural documentation of specific subsystems, see:

  • 🗃️ Database Schema: Data models and relationships.
  • 👤 Users & Brokers: Authentication and multi-user access control.
  • 🔐 Access Control (RBAC): Role-based broker access (Owner/Editor/Viewer).
  • ⚙️ Settings System: User preferences and global settings.
  • 📥 BRIM Architecture: Broker Report Import Manager.
  • 📈 Asset Pricing: Asset data fetching and metadata.
    • 🔎 See also: Asset Search & Link-Finder for the three-layer interactive search (on-site → ddgs web link-finder → resolve_url); best-effort, last-resort, and never used on automated price fetches.
  • 💱 FX Architecture: Foreign Exchange system.
    • 🔀 See also: FX Configuration & Routing for multi-provider setup.
  • 🧮 Financial Math Layer: backend/app/services/financial_math/, the one home of financial calculations — package map, layer rules, guards.
  • 📉 Risk Engine: Bulk risk analytics over a portfolio, a broker, an asset or a selection of assets — plugin catalogue, eligibility verdicts, and simulation and optimization in spawned worker pools.
  • 🧰 Tool Plugins: Atomic, typed calculations behind a versioned catalogue (first tool: the PAC allocator), each computed in a spawned process the executor owns.
  • 🧭 Onboarding Guides: Welcome setup, intro tour and contextual guides, with versioned per-user progress kept by the backend.
  • 📁 File Upload System: Custom uploads stored with a JSON metadata sidecar, and the default avatars seeded at startup (backend/app/services/files/static_uploads.py); image previews go through an in-memory cache (PreviewCache in backend/app/api/v1/uploads.py: 50 MB by default, PREVIEW_CACHE_MAX_MB, entries expire after 1 hour). Broker report files belong to BRIM. Where all these files live: Data Directory on Disk.

docs.title: 🔄 Request Flow Example: Displaying Portfolio
docs.text:
1. User logs in and navigates to the dashboard.
  2. The Frontend makes an API request to GET /api/v1/portfolio.
  3. The Backend receives the request, authenticates the user, and queries the Database for the user's transactions.
  4. For each asset, the backend may need to fetch the latest price. It calls the appropriate Asset Provider Plugin (e.g., Yahoo Finance).
  5. If currency conversion is needed, the backend calls the FX Provider Plugin to get the latest exchange rate.
  6. The backend processes the data, calculates portfolio metrics, and returns a JSON response to the frontend.
  7. The Frontend receives the JSON data and renders the portfolio dashboard.

docs.title: 🚀 Server Startup
docs.text:
backend/app/main.py sets up the test mode and the logging, then builds the app: FastAPI(..., lifespan=lifespan), install_middleware(app), install_validation_error_handler(app) (backend/app/api/validation_errors.py: a 422 that never sends the request's input back, see Validation Errors Without the Input), install_response_validation_handler(app) (backend/app/api/response_validation.py: a response that breaks its model is logged without its content, see Request Logs), install_server_error_handler(app) (backend/app/api/server_errors.py: a 5xx answers with the request id and the type of its failure, and its cause reaches the log once, see Error Answers), the API v1 router under API_V1_PREFIX, and install_static_site(app) (backend/app/services/platform/static_site.py). The latter registers the documentation (/mkdocs), /, the /_app chunks when the frontend build has them and, last, the SPA catch-all GET /{path:path}: a GET route added after it would never be reached. The catch-all serves the file of frontend/build/ that the path names, once its .. segments are resolved (/assets/../favicon.png is served); a path that would leave the build (confined_path()), or whose resolved location inside the build has a name starting with . (_hidden_in_build(): the build's markers .build-debug, .build-version and .tool-contract-inputs, the emoji font's .cache_manifest.json), gets the SPA fallback instead, 200.html, else index.html (tests: ./dev.py test utils static-route-confinement). The /_app mount and /mkdocs/{path} refuse a path with a name starting with . too (/mkdocs/{path} through _hidden_below(), which _hidden_in_build() uses; the mount checks the names of the path Starlette hands it; same tests), each with its own 404: the mount answers as for a missing file, once Starlette has resolved the .. segments (/_app/immutable/../.DS_Store names the build's _app/.DS_Store), and /mkdocs/{path} answers the documentation's 404, as for a path leaving mkdocs_src/site/. backend.app.main:app stays uvicorn's entry point.

Browser caching. The static site gives each kind of file its own Cache-Control (static_site.py; tests: ./dev.py test services static-cache-policy):

  • Revalidated, no-cache, must-revalidate (REVALIDATE_HTML): every HTML document, of the web app's build (index.html, the SPA fallback 200.html, offline.html) or of /mkdocs, and every file of /_app outside /_app/immutable/ (today env.js and version.json), whose name does not change with its content. The browser checks with the server before it reuses its copy, so it picks up a new build at its next load.
  • Kept for a year, public, max-age=31536000, immutable (IMMUTABLE_CACHE_CONTROL): the chunks under /_app/immutable/, whose names change with their content.
  • No Cache-Control: any other file of the build or of the documentation (icons, fonts, the manifest, the documentation's style sheets, scripts and images); the browser may keep it by heuristic freshness, from its Last-Modified.
  • Private, private, max-age=3600, outside the static site: the image previews of uploads (GET /api/v1/uploads/file/{id}?img_preview=WxH), which the browser may reuse for an hour and a shared cache must not store; see Uploaded Files: Common and Personal.

In the static site, only the /_app mount (ImmutableStaticFiles, a StaticFiles) answers 304 Not Modified when the browser's copy is current, and its 304 keeps the file's Cache-Control. The other files come from a route's FileResponse, which answers no 304, so an HTML document is sent whole each time. All these responses also carry the security headers, and install_static_site() first calls register_served_types(), so that every file served goes out with its right MIME type, which nosniff requires.

The lifespan (lifespan() in backend/app/services/platform/app_lifespan.py) prepares everything before the first request by running STARTUP_STEPS, in this order:

  1. shutdown-watchdog: installs the shutdown watchdog (install_shutdown_watchdog(), in shutdown_budget.py), only where uvicorn serves from the main thread with its own signal handlers and the budget is not 0. The first SIGTERM or SIGINT arms it: when the budget runs out, it logs Shutdown budget exhausted: ending the process, ends the child processes and exits with status 1, whatever still holds the server.
  2. announce: logs Starting LibreFolio with the version, the database path and the test mode.
  3. configuration-checks: runs the configuration checks (log_configuration_audit(), in a thread): a configured secret that cannot be used stops the server, every other finding is logged.
  4. signal-plugins: checks the signal-plugin runtime (validate_signal_runtime()) and discovers the signal plugins.
  5. tool-catalog: loads the Tool catalogue (ToolPluginRegistry.get_snapshot(), in a thread).
  6. pending-restore: applies a restore confirmed for the next start (apply_pending_restore(), in backend/app/services/platform/instance_backup/apply.py, in a thread), before any step reads the data: it swaps the folders with the checked copy (The Swap), leaves the restore waiting with its reason, or undoes a swap a start that was killed left half done.
  7. restore-state: asks whether the state of the restore can be read (probe_restore_state(), in backend/app/services/platform/restore_guard.py, in a thread; lot B-33). When it cannot, a restore may have stopped half way: the step logs one error and never stops the start, but from here on the process serves no data (restore_interrupted()): the eight later steps that repair, write or warm up the data are skipped (post-migration-fixes, lone-transfer-legs, admin-bootstrap, stored-currencies, provider-prewarm, market-holidays, brim-parse-pool and scheduler, each with a Startup step skipped line), and every API route but a few answers 423 instance_restore_interrupted (A Restore Stopped Half Way).
  8. data-directories: creates the data directories (ensure_data_dirs()).
  9. serving-lock: takes the shared serving lock on the data directory (hold_serving_lock(), in a thread), held until the process exits: from here on no restore swaps or undoes the data under this process.
  10. risk-scenarios: loads the risk scenario catalogue (initialize_risk_scenario_catalog()).
  11. default-avatars: seeds the default avatars (seed_default_avatars()).
  12. database: creates or migrates the database (ensure_database_exists() in database_bootstrap.py); a failed alembic upgrade head stops the server (sys.exit(1)).
  13. post-migration-fixes: runs the post-migration fixes in a thread; they never stop the startup.
  14. lone-transfer-legs: turns the lone giving legs of TRANSFERs that older broker deletions left into ADJUSTMENTs taking the units out, without a value (decision 47, N78-1; convert_lone_giving_legs_at_startup()). With something to convert, it first runs PRAGMA quick_check and leaves a damaged database as it is; it never stops the startup.
  15. global-settings: seeds the missing global settings (_initialize_global_settings()).
  16. admin-bootstrap: applies the variables of the initial administrator (startup_admin_bootstrap(), in backend/app/services/accounts/bootstrap_admin_service.py): on an instance without accounts it creates the administrator, inactive, with its setup link; a generated link goes out by email in a background task, so the step never waits for the mail server.
  17. restore-commit: completes a restore this start applied (finish_pending_restore(), in a thread): every session ends, the backup's one-time links are revoked, and the restore is recorded as committed. A step before it that raises rolls the restore back at the next start; one after it no longer does (decision N57).
  18. restore-owner: after a restore from the app on a managed instance, gives the owner the account the administrator chose (assign_restored_owner(), in backend/app/services/platform/instance_backup/owner.py), then asks whether anything still keeps the owner from it (probe_owner_assignment(), in restore_guard.py; lot H5-3). It never raises. While the owner has no account (pending, or the code of a refusal) the process serves no data, as for an unreadable restore state, and the steps after it that warm up the data or run jobs are skipped (A Restore Stopped Half Way).
  19. backup-leftovers: removes what runs of the backup killed outright left in clear (sweep_backup_leftovers(), in backend/app/services/platform/instance_backup/leftovers.py, in a thread; decision N66): the checks a stopped server left running and the decrypted archives in the copies, the folders of a dev.py backup inspect older than an hour, the work files of the backups that died with their process, and the backups past their hour (What a Run Killed Outright Leaves). It never touches what a running process holds, nor anything through a link. It never raises, since after restore-commit a step that raises would stop every start: a part that fails is logged as an error, and the others still run.
  20. plugin-secrets-check: runs the plugin secrets check (log_plugin_secrets_check()): stored system secrets of the plugin settings that the instance key cannot read are one error in the log, with their count; it never stops the startup.
  21. stored-currencies: once the repairs are done and the restore is settled, starts the audit of the stored currency codes in the background, in a worker thread, and goes on at once (log_stored_currency_audit() in backend/app/services/platform/stored_currencies.py): its scans take about 0.6 s at a million price rows. Read-only, on a connection with trusted_schema off, it logs one warning when the database holds currency codes that are not ISO 4217 codes (admin guide, Command-Line Tools, «Currency Codes That Are Not ISO Codes»), names or numbers an earlier version saved as written. It reports on the data, so it starts after restore-commit (decision N57); it never stops the startup.
  22. provider-prewarm: starts the provider cache pre-warm in the background (_prewarm_provider_caches()).
  23. market-holidays: starts building the market-holiday table in the background, in its own process (start_market_holiday_prewarm()).
  24. brim-parse-pool: with the warm-up on (brim_prewarm_enabled() in backend/app/config/brim.py, from LIBREFOLIO_BRIM_PREWARM: off by default, on in test mode), starts the BRIM parse pool's forkserver in the background, in a worker thread (prewarm() in backend/app/services/brim/brim_parse_pool.py), preloaded with the BRIM module and its plugins: the first parse after a start then forks a ready worker. Off, the step does nothing; a value it cannot use is logged as a warning and starts nothing either. It never stops the startup: a failed warm-up is logged, and the first parse starts the forkserver, as with the warm-up off.
  25. scheduler: starts the scheduler task (scheduler_loop()).
  26. idle-monitor: only with LIBREFOLIO_IDLE_SUSPEND_MODE=fly, registers the busy checks tools and backup on the activity record and starts the idle monitor task (start_idle_monitor(), in sleep_wake/idle_monitor.py), which asks Fly.io to suspend the machine when nothing is busy and no user's request has come for LIBREFOLIO_IDLE_SUSPEND_MINUTES.

On shutdown, the lifespan's finally runs FINALLY_STEPS: tool-executor stops the Tool executor, also when serving ended with an error. Then, only after a normal end, it logs Shutting down LibreFolio and runs SHUTDOWN_STEPS: idle-monitor (sets the idle monitor's stop event and awaits its task, when it runs), scheduler (sets the scheduler's stop event and awaits its task), providers (the asset, FX and BRIM providers), brim-parse-pool, quant-pools, market-holidays (ends any holiday build at once), caches (closes the TTL caches) and child-processes (terminates the child processes still alive, such as parse, risk and Tool workers, so that none outlives the server; only where the watchdog is installed).

docs.title: 🧩 Steps and Middleware: the Contract
docs.text:
backend/app/services/platform/lifecycle.py runs the steps; it imports nothing of the app.

  • Adding a step takes one line at its place in STARTUP_STEPS, SHUTDOWN_STEPS or FINALLY_STEPS: Step("my-step", lambda: my_function()). run returns None or an awaitable (a coroutine, a Task), which the runner awaits; a blocking startup call goes through asyncio.to_thread(), as post-migration-fixes does. The lambda finds my_function in app_lifespan when the step runs, so a test replaces it with monkeypatch.setattr(app_lifespan, "my_function", ...).
  • Startup (run_startup_steps()): each step runs to its end, in order. An exception stops the startup, and no shutdown step runs.
  • Shutdown order is declared, not derived: SHUTDOWN_STEPS is not the reverse of STARTUP_STEPS, and a step that must also run after a serving error belongs in FINALLY_STEPS.
  • Shutdown (run_shutdown_steps(steps, deadline)): a step that raises is logged as an error (Shutdown step failed) and the next step runs anyway. deadline is an instant on time.monotonic(): the lifespan's finally gets it once from shutdown_deadline() (backend/app/services/platform/shutdown_budget.py) and gives it to both FINALLY_STEPS and SHUTDOWN_STEPS. After a SIGTERM or a SIGINT in a process where the shutdown watchdog is installed, it is the watchdog's deadline (the signal plus the budget) less CLEANUP_MARGIN_SECONDS (0.75 s), kept for the last step. Without a signal, or without a watchdog, it is the current time plus the budget less uvicorn's drain share (shutdown_drain_seconds(): 3/8 of the budget, at least 1 s), worked out at each call. The budget is LIBREFOLIO_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, 8 s by default: 0 means no limit, and then shutdown_deadline() returns None and no step is ever cut; a value that cannot be used is logged once and the 8 s apply (see Stopping the Server in Configuration). Under a deadline, each step gets the time left, never less than MIN_STEP_SECONDS (0.2 s), so the short steps still run after an overrun; a step past its time is cut (the coroutine or task it awaits is cancelled) and logged as a warning (Shutdown step cut by the deadline). The runner returns one StepOutcome per step.
  • blocking=True marks a synchronous call that may block (brim-parse-pool): under a deadline run() is called in a worker thread, so the deadline holds; the thread cannot be stopped, and the sequence moves on without it. What run() returns is awaited as for any step. Without a deadline, and at startup, the flag changes nothing. A synchronous step without it runs on the event loop, where a deadline cannot cut it.
  • current_step() names the step in progress, startup:<name> or shutdown:<name>, and is None between steps and while the app serves: a watchdog thread can read it to name a step that hangs.
  • Adding a middleware takes one MiddlewareEntry(name, cls, options) at its place in MIDDLEWARE_STACK (backend/app/services/platform/middleware.py). The first entry is the outermost, the first to see a request and the last to see its response: activity (ActivityMiddleware, backend/app/services/platform/sleep_wake/activity.py: the user's presence and the requests in flight; outermost, so that it sees every request first and counts the compression of a response as in flight, while the probes are not counted, and the scheduled wake-up, /system/wake-sync (WAKE_PATHS), is counted as in flight but never as the user's presence, as are the hosting panel's routes under /backup/panel/ and /panel/ (PANEL_PATH_PREFIXES, lot H-61)), then request_id (RequestIdMiddleware, backend/app/services/platform/request_id.py: an id for every request, in every log line of the request and in the X-Request-Id of its response, the 500 of an exception nobody handled included; see Request Logs), then security_headers (SecurityHeadersMiddleware, backend/app/services/platform/security_headers.py: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Referrer-Policy on every response, plus frame protection and, on the web app's pages, a report-only Content-Security-Policy when LIBREFOLIO_FRAME_PROTECTION and LIBREFOLIO_CSP_REPORT_ONLY are on, as in the managed profile, each unless the route set its own; see Response Headers), then gzip, then cors. activity also adds to every /api/ answer but a probe's the response headers that a feature registers on the activity record (register_response_header()), unless the route set that header itself: today the scheduler's X-LibreFolio-Price-Refresh, present while prices catch up (see Catch-up Progress). install_middleware(app) adds the entries from the last, because Starlette puts each middleware outside the ones added before it.

docs.title: 🐳 Docker Image
docs.text:
The production image is runtime-only: the frontend (SvelteKit) and the documentation (MkDocs) are built on the host and copied in, so the image carries neither Node.js nor the documentation toolchain. ./dev.py docker build prepares those builds first (see Developer Workflow → Docker Integration); the release workflow builds and tags the published images (see Release & CI/CD Pipeline).

graph LR
    subgraph "Host (build)"
        FE["frontend/src"]
        MK["mkdocs_src/"]
        BE["backend/"]
        PF["Pipfile*"]
    end
    subgraph "Docker Image (runtime)"
        FB["frontend/build/"]
        MS["mkdocs_src/site/"]
        BC["backend/"]
        PP["Python packages"]
    end
    FE -- "npm run build" --> FB
    MK -- "mkdocs build" --> MS
    BE -- "copy" --> BC
    PF -- "pipenv requirements" --> PP
  • Build stages (Dockerfile): docs-full and docs-light take the pre-built mkdocs_src/site/, and docs-light deletes the gallery images before they reach the final image (the DOCS_VARIANT build argument picks one). frontend runs scripts/docker/check_frontend_build.sh, which refuses a debug, coverage-instrumented or sourcemapped frontend/build/. pybuilder installs requirements.txt with the compiler toolchain, and only the installed packages reach the final python:3.13-slim stage, which adds gosu, sqlite3, tzdata and tzdata-legacy. zoneinfo reads the system's time zone database (the PyPI tzdata package is not a dependency), and Debian keeps old names such as Asia/Calcutta and US/Eastern in tzdata-legacy: without it, a scheduler time zone saved under such a name would fall back to UTC.
  • Contents: backend/, scripts/, dev.py, the checked frontend build, the documentation site, VERSION (the git version frozen at build time, since the image has no .git/) and .env.example copied as /app/.env. .dockerignore keeps out, among others, backend/data/, backend/test_scripts/, the documentation sources and the developer journal. dev.py registers a command group only when the directories it needs exist, so in the image test, i18n, mkdocs translate and mkdocs translate-validate stay listed but answer not available in this installation and exit with 2 (see Test Mode in the Container).
  • Startup: entrypoint.sh starts as root, creates the data directory and hands it to the numeric LIBREFOLIO_UID:LIBREFOLIO_GID (the UID/GID build arguments, default 1000:1000), then exec gosu replaces itself with the command. The default command is uvicorn backend.app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 6040: one worker, PID 1 of the container, always on port 6040, the only port the image EXPOSEs. PORT only changes the host side of the Compose port mapping: both Compose files set PORT=6040 in environment:, so the dev.py commands run in the container read the port the server listens on. The image's HEALTHCHECK probes /api/v1/system/health on 6040 too. ./dev.py docker exec runs its command through gosu with the same numeric ids, so what it creates in the data directory belongs to the server's user.
  • Database: the container runs the same startup sequence as any server, so pending migrations and the post-migration fixes are applied before the first request: a container never needs a manual db upgrade.

docs.title: ⚙️ Backend
docs.text:
• 🚀 FastAPI: A high-performance web framework for building APIs with Python (LibreFolio requires Python 3.13), based on standard Python type hints. It generates the OpenAPI schema and can serve interactive documentation (Swagger UI and ReDoc); LibreFolio serves them on debug and test instances only (API Reference).
  • 🗃️ SQLAlchemy: The SQL toolkit and Object-Relational Mapper (ORM) used for all database interactions. LibreFolio uses SQLAlchemy's asyncio support for non-blocking database queries.
  • 📋 Pydantic: A data validation and settings management library. Used extensively for defining data schemas, validating API requests, and managing application settings.
  • 🔄 Alembic: A lightweight database migration tool for SQLAlchemy. See Database Migrations.
  • 🗄️ SQLite: The default database engine. Simple, serverless, and perfect for a self-hosted application. Configured in WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) mode for better concurrency.

docs.title: 🎨 Frontend
docs.text:
• 🖥️ SvelteKit: A web application framework for building fast, modern user interfaces with server-side rendering, routing, and great developer experience.
  • 📝 TypeScript: A statically typed superset of JavaScript that adds type safety to the frontend codebase.
  • 🎨 TailwindCSS: A utility-first CSS framework for rapidly building custom designs.
  • ⚡ Vite: The build tool and development server. Provides extremely fast Hot Module Replacement (HMR).

docs.title: 🧪 Testing
docs.text:
• 🐍 Pytest: The framework used for writing and running backend tests.
  • 🎭 Playwright: A framework for end-to-end testing of the web application.
  • 📊 Coverage.py: A tool for measuring code coverage of Python programs.

docs.title: 🔒 Security Architecture
docs.text: This document outlines the security model, authentication system, and deployment recommendations for LibreFolio.

docs.title: 🎯 Threat Model and Scope
docs.text: LibreFolio is a self-hosted application. The primary security assumption is that the host system is secure.

docs.title: ✅ In Scope
docs.text:
• 🔐 Authentication: Stateless JWT-based authentication via HTTP-only session cookies with configurable expiration, session revocation per account, a limit on failed sign-ins, and an identifier that names one account only: no username can stand in front of another account's email address.
  • 🛡️ Data Segregation: Strict isolation between users via Role-Based Access Control (RBAC).
  • ✏️ Input Validation: Preventing injection attacks via strict Pydantic schemas; a request that fails them gets a 422 that never sends its input back (Validation Errors Without the Input).
  • 🧼 Output Escaping: User- and provider-supplied text is escaped or sanitized before the browser can render it as HTML.
  • 📁 File Upload Security: MIME type validation, executable blocking, size limits, and a scope per file: common, or personal to its uploader and the administrators.
  • 🚫 Endpoint Protection: All data and file endpoints require a valid session cookie — including uploaded files and plugin assets.

docs.title: ⚠️ Out of Scope
docs.text:
• 💻 Host System Compromise: If an attacker gains shell access to the server, the database file is accessible. Encryption at rest is currently not implemented.
  • 🔗 SSL/TLS Termination: The application server (Uvicorn) speaks HTTP. HTTPS is the responsibility of the deployment environment (Reverse Proxy).

docs.title: 🔑 Authentication — JWT Cookies
docs.text: LibreFolio uses stateless JWT (JSON Web Token) authentication stored in HTTP-only session cookies.

docs.title: 🔄 How Login Works
docs.text:
1. User sends credentials to POST /api/v1/auth/login
  2. Server validates credentials and sets an HTTP-only cookie containing the JWT, whose payload is sub (the user id), sv (the account's session version, see Session Revocation), iat and exp
  3. The browser automatically includes this cookie on all subsequent requests
  4. <img> tags, fetch() calls, and page navigations all send the cookie seamlessly

Before the account is even looked up, the sign-in asks the failed sign-in limit: past it, the answer is 429 TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS, and no password is checked.

A refused sign-in is logged without what was typed, because the field takes an email address too and no address goes in a log (workstream E's rule, lot A-22): Login failed: user not found carries nothing about the identifier, Login failed: wrong password and Login failed: user inactive carry the account's user_id. Tests: ./dev.py test api auth, TestSignInLogsNoTypedIdentifier (LOGIN-027 to LOGIN-033, in-process).

Why cookies over Bearer headers?

HTTP-only cookies are automatically sent by the browser for all same-origin requests — including <img src>, <link href>, and AJAX calls. This means uploaded files and plugin assets are served securely without any special frontend handling.

docs.title: 🪪 Which Account an Identifier Names
docs.text:
The sign-in's field takes a username or an email address, and so do «forgot password» and «send the link again» (Email): all three find the account with user_service.get_user_by_username_or_email(). Until lot A-21a (release 1.3), a username could be any 3 to 50 characters, @ included, and that lookup was one query, username = X OR lower(email) = lower(X), keeping the first row. So account A could take account B's email address as its username, at registration or with a rename in the Profile, which asks for no password, and SQLite then returned A for B's address. B could no longer sign in with its address: each try was checked against A's password and counted as a failure, up to the failed sign-in limit, which then refused B's address altogether; and B's «forgot password» or «send the link again» could find A (workstream E's review, rated medium, 8/10). Three rules close it:

  1. No @ in a new username (USERNAME_RESERVED_CHARACTER in backend/app/config/accounts.py). Refused by user_service.create_user() (registration, open or by invitation, the first account included, and ./dev.py user create), by user_service.update_profile() for a username that changes (the name an account already has is not checked again), both through _new_username_refusal(), and by admin_bootstrap_config() for LIBREFOLIO_ADMIN_USERNAME. Nothing else changes: spaces, accents, ., _, - and + are still taken.
