The upload limit bounds the archive as it travels, compressed. The check unpacks what the manifest declares: those sizes equal the zip's headers and the reads stop at them, so nothing unpacks past its declared size, but a small archive can declare far more than the disk holds, deflate reaching about 1000:1. LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_RESTORE_MB caps the declared total (lot B-35).

  • The reader. backup_max_restore_mb() (config/backup.py, beside the upload limit's), in megabytes, 0 for no limit. A value set wins, 0 included; anything but a whole number of ASCII digits raises BackupConfigError BACKUP_MAX_RESTORE_MB_INVALID. Unset or blank: 0 in the selfhosted profile; in any other, RESTORE_TO_UPLOAD_RATIO (8) times backup_max_upload_mb(), 0 when that is 0, raising what it raises (BackupConfigError, ProfileDefaultError): it fails closed through the upload limit's own entry. It has no entry of its own in ENVIRONMENT_PROFILE_DEFAULTS (Settings): a multiple, it follows a provider's own upload limit. In managed, 500 MB gives 4000 MB.
  • Why 8. SQLite databases deflate about 4:1 (measured: the test database 4.1×, a 52 MB synthetic price history 3.9×), uploads (images, PDF, XLSX) about 1:1. An archive heavy with its database sits near 4×: a ratio of 4 would refuse it at the upload limit; 8 leaves it twice its room, and still cuts deflate's worst case by more than 100.
  • The check. stage_archive(..., max_unpacked=), in bytes, None for no limit: _stage adds up the sizes of manifest.files after _checked_entries(), which holds each entry to the manifest, and before _check_space(), so a total above it is refused first, StagingError unpacked_too_large, «Unpacked, the archive is larger than this LibreFolio accepts for a restore»: nothing unpacked, and the stage removed, as for any refusal. A secure archive is decrypted first, about its own size, which the upload limit bounds, then measured the same way. unpacked_too_large is one of RestoreErrorCode (schemas/backup.py).
  • Its callers. POST /backup/restore/stage reads it with _restore_limit(), as _upload_limit() reads the upload limit, turns megabytes into bytes (× 1024²) and 0 into None, and passes it through restore_jobs.start_check(..., max_unpacked=) and _run_check(); a limit it cannot read is logged as an error and answered 503 backup_restore_unavailable (The Routes). backup restore reads the same variable in _check_on_a_copy(): ❌ <message> (backup_restore_unavailable) and exit 1 before the check, the usual ❌ … (unpacked_too_large) when it refuses; LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_RESTORE_MB=0 lifts it for one command. The startup checks report a limit that cannot be read (backup.restore_limit, Configuration Checks of the Backup).

Tests: ./dev.py test services backup-staging (under, at and over the limit, refused before any byte is written, a secure archive, None as before) and ./dev.py test services backup-checks (the reader in each profile, and its check).

docs.title: 🔐 The Routes
docs.text:
Every route under /backup/restore requires an administrator (require_admin), but GET /backup/restore/outcome, which takes the one-time ticket of a restart instead (The Outcome Ticket); it is also the only one in ALLOWED_WHEN_BLOCKED (Instance Block). An error answers {"detail": {"code": …, "message": …}} (backup_error), never with a path of the server in it.

Route What it does PUT /backup/restore/upload, POST /backup/restore/stage, GET /backup/restore/stage/{stage_id} The upload of an archive and its check on a copy (lot B2); the password of a secure backup comes with POST /backup/restore/stage, tried in the request (Secure Backups). At its start (its folders, its first state), POST /backup/restore/stage answers 507 no_space, the check's own code, on a full disk or quota, logged as a warning, A check of a backup archive could not start: not enough free space, and 500 stage_failed on any other failure of the file system (permissions, a read-only disk, EIO), logged as an error, A check of a backup archive could not start, with the error's type and the system's reason; either way the upload stays, for another try (lot B-30). When the restore limit cannot be read (_restore_limit(), The Restore Limit), it answers 503 backup_restore_unavailable, «The restore limit of this instance cannot be read», logged as an error: no check starts, and the upload stays (lot B-35) DELETE /backup/restore/stage/{stage_id} Drops an ended check and its copy; 409 restore_pending for the copy of a restore not finished yet POST /backup/restore/stage/{stage_id}/confirm Confirms the restore of a finished check: 202 RestoreStatus, with the administrator's username in confirmed_by. Refused with 404 restore_stage_not_found; 409 restore_stage_running, restore_not_restorable, restore_stage_outdated (LibreFolio was updated since the check) or restore_already_pending; 410 restore_stage_expired; 500 restore_folder_unusable. A full disk or quota anywhere in the confirmation (the .restore folder, the lock, the state's write) is 507 backup_no_space, logged as a warning, A restore could not be confirmed: not enough free space; any other failure of the file system is 500 restore_confirm_failed, logged as an error, A restore could not be confirmed, with the error's type and the system's reason. Either way nothing is confirmed, as the state is written last and atomically, and the check and its copy stay: the same confirmation answers 202 once the failure is gone (lot B-31). A state the file system cannot read, met under the lock, is 500 restore_state_unreadable, and nothing is written: the restore it holds may be half applied, and its journal must not be overwritten (lot B-32) GET /backup/restore/status RestoreStatus: its state is none, pending, in_progress (applying, applied or rolling_back), committed or rolled_back, with reason, and waiting (backup_running, other_data_directory, server_running or instance_blocked) on a restore a start left waiting. 500 restore_state_unreadable, «The state of the restore cannot be read: the server's log has the cause», when the file system cannot read the state: it never answers none then (lot B-32) DELETE /backup/restore/pending Drops the restore waiting (204) with its checked copy and its check record, as backup pending --cancel does (B-17): confirming that check again answers 404 restore_stage_not_found. 404 restore_not_pending. A failure of the file system before the restore is dropped (its lock, or removing its state) is 500 restore_cancel_failed, logged as an error, A pending restore could not be cancelled: the restore still waits. Once the state is dropped, apply.cancel_restore(drop_copy=True), behind the route and the command alike, logs a copy it cannot remove as a warning, The copy of a cancelled restore could not be removed: it goes when its check expires, with stage_id and the error, and never raises: the route answers 204, and prune removes the copy at its age (lot B-31). A state the file system cannot read is 500 restore_state_unreadable, with the state, the copy and the ticket untouched: cancel_restore reads it strictly before its lock, as prepare_restart does; before, a .restore/ the server could not search read as no state, 404 restore_not_pending (lot B-32) POST /backup/restore/restart Stops the server so that it applies the restore waiting: see The Restart. 202 RestoreRestartAccepted: the RestoreStatus and outcome_ticket, with Cache-Control: no-store. 409 restore_not_pending; 500 restore_restart_failed when the ticket cannot be written, a full disk included, logged as an error, The ticket of the restore's outcome could not be written: no restart, with the error's type and the system's reason, or restore_folder_unusable: no restart then, no ticket, and the restore still waits. Lot B-31 pins it, and gives restore_restart_failed its sentence on the card. A state the file system cannot read is 500 restore_state_unreadable, with no ticket and no restart; before, it answered 409 restore_not_pending (lot B-32) GET /backup/restore/outcome No session: the ticket of the restart in the X-Restore-Ticket header. 200 RestoreOutcome, state (pending, in_progress, committed or rolled_back), reason and waiting only, with Cache-Control: no-store, as often as asked until the ticket expires, a final outcome included; the same 404 restore_outcome_not_found for every ticket that does not give it. See The Outcome Ticket

A full disk or quota that a backup route meets before it answers is a 507 (lot B-30), recognised by jobs.out_of_space(): ENOSPC or EDQUOT in the error or one of its causes, or SQLite's SQLITE_FULL. Its code is backup_no_space for an upload, at the start of a backup and at the confirmation of a restore (lot B-31), and no_space at the start of a check, the code of a check that runs out of space. For the upload, UploadWriter (restore_jobs.py) maps one met anywhere from the creation of its folder, .restore/upload/, to the end of the file, its fsync and close included (a network file system or a quota may report it only there), to UploadNoSpaceError, and takes its descriptor before closing it, so that abort() never closes it twice: nothing of the upload is left.

Every RestoreStatus carries upload_limit_mb, the largest archive PUT /backup/restore/upload accepts at the time of the answer, in megabytes: 0 for no limit, null when the limit cannot be read (the upload then answers 503 backup_upload_unavailable, and an error naming the variable is logged). It cannot be read when LIBREFOLIO_BACKUP_MAX_UPLOAD_MB is not a whole number (BackupConfigError), or when ENVIRONMENT_PROFILE_DEFAULTS gives the active profile no value for it (any profile but selfhosted, H-37) or a value of the wrong type (ProfileDefaultError, Settings; B-21): _upload_limit() and _readable_limit_mb() in restore.py treat the two alike, so the status still answers 200. The startup checks report it too (backup.upload_limit, Configuration Checks of the Backup).

On the server, ./dev.py backup restore ARCHIVE confirms as cli, once the word restore is typed at a terminal or with --yes, and ./dev.py backup pending [--cancel] shows the restore, or drops it with its copy. The command prints what it reads from an archive or from the restore's state (versions, revision, table and administrator names, who confirmed, the data directory's path) through _safe() in scripts/backup_cli.py: every character that is not printable, control characters and escape sequences included, becomes ?, so an archive cannot drive the operator's terminal.

docs.title: 📄 The Restore State
docs.text:
One file holds the restore of a data directory, .restore/restore.json (RestoreState): pending, then applying, applied and committed, or rolling_back and rolled_back; with the stage, who confirmed it and when, the date and version of the backup, the journal of the swap, the boot that applied it, the reason of a rollback, why a start left it waiting (waiting), and the session version given at the commit.

  • Written atomically. A .part beside it, fsynced, then os.replace and an fsync of the folder: a reader, or the next start, finds the old state or the new one, never half of one. Mode 0600.
  • Never through a link. The file is opened with O_NOFOLLOW, and .restore must be a plain folder: a confirmation that finds a link or a file there is refused (BackupPathError, 500 restore_folder_unusable), and a startup step logs an error and ignores the restore. .restore/ and the folders the restore makes in it are created 0700 (paths.ensure_private_dir).
  • Checked strictly. A state is used only in the shape this LibreFolio writes: the journal may name only the four swapped folders, and the stage id must be 32 lowercase hexadecimal digits, so nothing read from a file of the data directory becomes a path outside the swap. Any other state is ignored, with an error logged.
  • What cannot be read is not none (lot B-32). A state the file system cannot read (EACCES or EPERM on the file or on the search of .restore/, EIO, a link swapped in as it is opened) is reported, never read as none: _read_state logs the error and raises RestoreStateUnreadableError, restore_state_unreadable, whose reason is the system's words, never a path, through read_restore, cancel_restore, prepare_restart and confirm_restore (a 500 on the routes, exit 1 in backup pending and backup restore); a link or a folder in its place, or a content that does not validate, still reads as none, as above; the startup steps (apply_pending_restore, finish_pending_restore), the outcome (GET /backup/restore/outcome, which reads the state only for the ticket of a restart not expired, so no other caller makes LibreFolio read it nor log the error, lot B-41) and the pruning (protected_stage) keep reading it as none, the error logged, so a start applies nothing and goes on with the data as it is.
  • One at a time. While a restore is not finished (pending, applying, applied, rolling_back), another one is refused (restore_already_pending), and its checked copy is never dropped nor pruned, however old (restore_jobs.remove_check, prune).
  • The steps take turns on an exclusive flock of .restore/apply.lock: the workers of one server run them one after the other. An ordinary start, with no restore, only finds that the state file does not exist: it creates no folder and no lock file.

docs.title: 🔄 The Swap, the Journal and the Rollback
docs.text:
The startup step pending-restore (app_lifespan.STARTUP_STEPS, after tool-catalog, before data-directories and database) applies a pending restore:

  1. It leaves it waiting, with waiting recorded, when the data directory's real path is not the one the restore was confirmed for (other_data_directory: a copy of the data directory), when the hosting provider blocks the instance (instance_blocked: LIBREFOLIO_BLOCKED, read at each start; a value that cannot be read counts as blocked), when another server process serves the data directory (server_running, see below), or when a backup holds its lock (backup_running), in this order. The undo of a swap and the commit still run on a blocked instance: the first repairs the data directory, and the block cannot change during one start. A restore can so wait as long as the block lasts: its copy keeps its disk space (an active restore's copy is never pruned; backup pending --cancel frees it), and if LibreFolio was updated meanwhile, the step database of the first start after the unblock migrates the restored database, checked at the revision of then, with the data of before still in .restore/previous/ until the commit (a failure rolls back, first_start_failed).
  2. It records it rolled_back without moving anything when the checked copy is gone or changed (stage_missing), or when one of the four folders of the data directory is a link or a file (swap_failed).
  3. It writes the journal, fsynced, before the first move: applying, the boot, and for each folder of SWAPPED_FOLDERS (sqlite, custom-uploads, broker_reports, scenario_catalog) whether the live one and the copy's existed.
  4. It moves, by renames inside the data directory: each live folder to .restore/previous/, then the copy's in its place, with the mode the live one had. Then applied.

secrets/, logs/, scheduler_state.json, backups/ and anything else in the data directory are never touched.

The step restore-commit (after global-settings) completes a restore applied by this boot. In one transaction of the restored database it ends every session (Session Revocation) and revokes the live one-time links (Revocation); then it records committed, and removes .restore/previous/ (decision 41: the data of before only served to go back), the copy and its check state. What a finished restore, committed or rolled_back, leaves behind, a later start removes too.

The boot. A start is known by the server's root process — restart.server_pid(): the parent that started this process through multiprocessing while it is alive, uvicorn's master with --workers N or its reloader, otherwise this process — and by that process's creation time, read with psutil once per process, so that a reused pid is never taken for it and a clock step during a start does not make it another boot (apply.current_boot(), boot_alive()). The workers of one server share the boot: the first swaps, the others find the restore applied by their own boot.

Never under a running server. The step serving-lock, right after data-directories and before any step reads the data, gives every server process a shared flock on the data directory itself (hold_serving_lock(); no file is created), which the system releases when the process exits, however it ends. pending-restore runs before it, and before it moves anything it takes the same lock exclusively, without waiting, until its last move (_exclusive_serving_lock()). It cannot get it while another process serves, and a process reaching serving-lock meanwhile waits until the folders have moved, so nobody reads them half moved. The processes it finds serving are others: a worker that uvicorn starts again beside its running siblings (after a crash, or with SIGHUP or SIGTTIN), or a second server on the same data directory. A pending restore then waits (server_running), and a restore that a dead start applied is not undone under such a process. Where flock cannot be used (no fcntl, a file system without it), the lock finds nobody and a warning says so: the restore works as if there were no lock.

The rollback is driven by what the files say, in the reverse order of the journal, and can be cut and run again: whatever stands in the data directory goes to .restore/failed/, and the folder in .restore/previous/ comes back. A start runs it when it finds:

  • applying or rolling_back: a start died during the swap, or during a rollback (swap_interrupted, or the reason already recorded); only the rollback makes such a data directory whole again, so it runs whoever serves, with the lock held exclusively when it can be;
  • applied by a boot that no longer runs, while no server process serves the data directory: the first start on the restored data died before restore-commit, on a migration that fails or a damaged file (first_start_failed);
  • an OSError during its own moves: at once (swap_failed), and the start goes on with the data as it was.

Fail closed. RestoreInUseError (restore_in_use) stops the start rather than serve data whose restore is not committed: in pending-restore, when the restore was applied by another boot that still runs, or by a dead one while a server process serves the data directory; in restore-commit, when it was applied by another boot. A rollback that fails raises RestoreApplyError (restore_apply_failed): the data directory is half restored, so the start stops, the state stays rolling_back, and every later start tries again.

docs.title: 🔌 The Restart
docs.text:
A restore is applied at a start, never while the server serves. POST /backup/restore/restart answers 202 with the restore waiting and the ticket of its outcome (The Outcome Ticket); once the answer is sent, a BackgroundTask calls restart.request_restart(), which logs a warning and sends SIGTERM to the server's root process (restart.server_pid(), as for the boot): uvicorn's master stops its workers, and the shutdown budget bounds the stop («Stopping the Server» in Configuration). The route answers 409 restore_not_pending unless a restore waits, so an administrator stops the server only to apply one; on a blocked instance it is refused like the others. The signal goes through restart.send_signal, os.kill by default, read at each call: the tests replace it and never stop a real server. Since the signal goes to the root process, the next start is one of the whole server, which finds no sibling holding the serving lock. uvicorn's SIGHUP is not one: it replaces the workers one at a time, each new one started before the old one ends, so the restore keeps waiting (server_running).

Nothing in LibreFolio starts the server again: whatever supervises it does, after a stop that is not a failure.

Supervisor Starts it again Does not Docker restart: unless-stopped (both compose files of the repository) or always on-failure, no systemd Restart=always Restart=on-failure Fly.io Machine The always restart policy on-fail, the default of fly launch and fly deploy

In the Docker image, uvicorn is the container's first process and ends with status 0, or 1 when the shutdown budget runs out. A Fly.io Machine stopped under on-fail waits for the Fly Proxy to wake it on a request, when its service lets it. Without a supervisor the server stays stopped until someone starts it, and the restore is applied then.

docs.title: 🎫 The Outcome Ticket
docs.text:
A restore ends every session, and without JWT_SECRET every start does too: once the server is back, the page that asked the restart cannot tell from its session what became of the restore. So the restart request hands it a one-time ticket (lot B5c, instance_backup/outcome.py), and GET /backup/restore/outcome tells the holder of that ticket, without a session, the state of that restore and nothing else.

  • Issued by POST /backup/restore/restart, before the stop is scheduled, under the restore's lock (apply.prepare_restart), so that two restart requests take turns and no cancel or confirmation comes in between: secrets.token_urlsafe(32), 256 random bits, returned once in outcome_ticket. When it cannot be written, the route answers 500 and the server keeps running.
  • Kept as a hash. Only its SHA-256 is stored, in .restore/outcome-ticket.json (OutcomeTicket), with the stage of its restore, issued_at and expires_at: 0600, written atomically, never through a link, and read only in the shape this LibreFolio writes. Any well-formed ticket reaches that file without a session, so a file that cannot be read (a link included) or is not in that shape is logged as an error once per data directory in each server process, then at debug while the same failure lasts. A failure of another kind, or one after the file was written, removed or read successfully, is logged as an error again (lot B-42). .restore is never swapped, so the ticket outlives the restart, the swap, the commit and a rollback.
  • In a header. The page sends it in X-Restore-Ticket, never in the URL, which the access log records (Request Logs): the route ignores the query string, and a ?ticket=… typed by hand is written there as ***. LibreFolio never logs it, and the page keeps it in memory only.
  • One restore, one hour. It answers only for the restore of its stage, until one hour after the restart request (OUTCOME_TICKET_TTL), room for a first start that migrates a large database: as often as it is asked, a final outcome (committed, rolled_back) included (decision N53). Were a final answer read only once, losing it, to a connection reset while LibreFolio starts, would leave the retry a 404, and the page would fall back on its session, which reads «restored» after a rollback without JWT_SECRET. One-time means one ticket per restart: a new restart request replaces it; a new confirmation and a cancel, from the API or the command line, remove it, and so does its holder presenting it expired.
  • One answer for every miss. No ticket, a malformed one, an unknown one (never issued, replaced or removed), an expired one (then removed) or one of another restore: the same 404 restore_outcome_not_found. The hashes are compared in constant time (hmac.compare_digest), and a wrong ticket changes nothing: the route removes a ticket only when its own holder presents it expired. The ticket is checked before the state of the restore, so a caller without the ticket of a restart not expired never makes LibreFolio read that state, nor log that it cannot (lot B-41).
  • Nothing more. RestoreOutcome holds state, reason and waiting: no name, date, version or path.

When the route answers 404, 401 or 423 (a ticket expired, replaced or removed, a server without the route, a proxy in between), the page falls back on GET /backup/restore/status with its session, where a 401 means that the session ended (restoreOutcome(), frontend/src/lib/features/backup/backupApi.ts).

Tests: ./dev.py test services backup-apply (backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_backup_apply.py: the state, the swap, every rollback, the commit, the sessions and the links), ./dev.py test services backup-outcome (backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_backup_outcome.py: the ticket), ./dev.py test api backup-restore-apply (the routes, the ticket, the signal recorded and never sent), ./dev.py test utils backup-cli-restore (the command line) and ./dev.py test e2e backup-roundtrip (a populated instance backed up, restored on an empty one, then started in a fresh process).

docs.title: 📡 Address Probe
docs.text:
Developer decision D-A3 has the Invite dialog prefill the server's address and let the administrator edit it. When the address is edited, the browser checks that this instance answers there, not merely something. backend/app/services/accounts/address_probe.py does it with a signed nonce and two routes:

  1. the browser asks its own instance for a nonce: POST /api/v1/users/address-probe, administrators only (require_admin), 200 {nonce, expires_at} (AddressProbeIssued), a new nonce at every call;
  2. it sends the nonce, without credentials, to GET <address>/api/v1/auth/address-probe.png?nonce=… (H-55 v2: an image, see The Address Check Is an Image): public, a PNG of 1×1 only when the instance there issued the nonce, of 2×1 otherwise. The older JSON route, GET <address>/api/v1/auth/address-probe?nonce=…, answers 200 {"match": true} or {"match": false} (AddressProbeResult), and nothing else; it stays for curl and older clients, and the paragraphs below about CORS and fetch describe it.

In the app. LinkShare, the panel of the Users tab's invitation and password-reset dialogs, runs the check through checkAddress() (frontend/src/lib/features/settings/users/addressProbe.ts), and only for an address the administrator changed, 500 ms after the last keystroke. The nonce comes through the Zodios client; the check loads an Image of the address (referrerPolicy = 'no-referrer', no crossOrigin), abandoned after 8 s, and reads its naturalWidth: 1×1 reads match, 2×1 mismatch; any other size, a failed load or the timeout reads unverifiable, never no. (Until H-55 v2 it was a bare fetch of the JSON route, a CORS simple request: see the warning below; an enforced connect-src blocks it for another origin.) No verdict stops the administrator from copying the link. Component side: LinkShare.

docs.title: 🎯 Why a Signed Nonce
docs.text:
A stable instance id readable from any origin would have been simpler, and was set aside: any page visited by someone on the instance's network could read it from a LibreFolio on the LAN, and recognise the same instance at two addresses, a fingerprint. With the nonce, the public answer is one bit about a value only an administrator of this instance can obtain:

  • issuing needs an administrator's session, and its answer carries no Access-Control-Allow-Origin: no other origin can read a nonce;
  • the check answers match and nothing else: no id, no version, no configuration;
  • any page can still tell that a LibreFolio answers at an address, since the check answers {"match": false} to anyone, but not which one.

Unlike an account token, the nonce rides in the query string, so it reaches the request log: the request-log filter masks credential-like parameters, and nonce is not one. There it is worth the same bit, for at most two minutes.

docs.title: 🧾 The Nonce
docs.text:
issue_probe_nonce() returns the nonce and expires_at:

base64url( rand16 ‖ expiry_be8 ‖ HMAC-SHA256(derive_key("accounts.address-probe.v1"), rand16 ‖ expiry_be8) )
Part Bytes Content rand16 16 secrets.token_bytes(16) expiry_be8 8 The expiry in Unix seconds, big-endian: the second of the issue plus 120 (PROBE_TTL_SECONDS) MAC 32 HMAC-SHA256 of the first 24 bytes, under the key derive_key() gives the purpose accounts.address-probe.v1 (PROBE_PURPOSE): see Instance Key

The 56 bytes are written in base64url without padding: 75 characters. Nothing is stored: the nonce carries everything its check needs, so any worker verifies a nonce any worker issued, and a check consumes nothing: a nonce matches as often as it is asked until it expires. This instance means this instance key: a copy running with the same key, such as a restored backup, matches too. Without a configured key, issuing a nonce, or checking a well-formed one, can be the first use that generates the key file.

docs.title: 🔍 Verification
docs.text:
verify_probe_nonce(nonce) is True only for a nonce this instance issued that has not expired, False for anything else, and never raises:

  1. Shape: a text over 256 characters (MAX_NONCE_LENGTH) is refused at once; otherwise it must be exactly 75 characters of the base64url alphabet (A–Z, a–z, 0–9, -, _). The alphabet is checked before decoding because Python's base64 decoder is lenient: it skips the characters outside its alphabet, and its URL-safe variant also reads + and /.
  2. One spelling per nonce: the text must decode to 56 bytes that encode back to the very same text. The last character carries two bits the decoder ignores, so four texts would otherwise pass for one nonce.
  3. The MAC is recomputed and compared with hmac.compare_digest, the only judge of the signature.
  4. The expiry is read only once the MAC holds: the nonce matches up to expires_at, included.

An instance key that cannot be used makes every check False, with one warning per process (Address probe: the instance key cannot be used, every probe answers no match); the configuration checks give the reason at startup. Issuing has no such fallback: POST /users/address-probe then answers 503 INSTANCE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE, with no nonce, and logs one warning per refused call, Address probe: the instance key cannot be used, no nonce issued, with admin_id (H-19).

GET /auth/address-probe reads nonce from the query string, "" when it is absent, with no length constraint, so no value gets a 422: an empty, malformed, oversized, non-canonical, forged, expired or foreign nonce is 200 {"match": false}. A session cookie, valid or not, changes nothing.

docs.title: 🌐 One Route Readable from Any Origin
docs.text:
The check is cross-origin by nature: the page runs at the address the administrator is using, the check goes to the edited one. answer_address_probe() (backend/app/api/v1/auth.py) sets two headers on every answer, true or false:

  • Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, once: no other route of the backend sets this header;
  • Cache-Control: no-store.

The global CORSMiddleware (the cors entry of MIDDLEWARE_STACK, backend/app/services/platform/middleware.py: allow_credentials=True, no allowed origin) leaves that header in place on a simple GET and only adds Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, which the browser ignores for a request without credentials. Every other route answers a request from another origin without Access-Control-Allow-Origin.

The check must be a CORS simple request

GET, no custom header, no Content-Type: application/json, and credentials: 'omit': a bare fetch, not the Zodios client, whose Axios instance sends cookies (withCredentials: true); the browser does not let a request with credentials read an answer with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. Anything else makes the browser send an OPTIONS preflight first, which the middleware refuses with 400 Disallowed CORS origin (CORSMiddleware.preflight_response() in Starlette).

Limits. Only a readable 200 {"match": …} is an answer: false means that a LibreFolio answers there but did not issue the nonce, or that the nonce has expired. Anything else must be read as «cannot verify», not as «no»; among the cases:

  • a network error: nothing answers, the connection is refused, DNS or TLS fails;
  • an HTTPS page checking an http:// address: mixed content, which the browser blocks;
  • a page on a public origin checking a LAN address, which Chrome guards: a Private Network Access preflight is refused by the middleware like any other, and Local Network Access, its successor, lets the request through only once the user grants a permission;
  • anything at that address but a LibreFolio with this route, an earlier version included: no readable {match};
  • a blocked instance: the check is a public route outside ALLOWED_WHEN_BLOCKED, so, without a session as it always is, it gets the guard's 401, which carries no Access-Control-Allow-Origin. There, issuing a nonce answers 423, like every route outside the list for a signed-in caller.

Key changes and threads. A change of the instance key invalidates the nonces issued before it: harmless, for a value that lives two minutes. derive_key() reads the instance key at every call, from a file unless LIBREFOLIO_INSTANCE_KEY holds it, so both routes are plain def functions, which FastAPI runs in a worker thread, off the event loop.

Tests: ./dev.py test services address-probe (backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_address_probe.py: the layout under the derived key, the expiry, every altered, malformed, oversized, non-canonical or foreign nonce refused, hmac.compare_digest, never raises) and ./dev.py test api address-probe (backend/test_scripts/test_api/test_address_probe_api.py: 401, 403 and 200 for the nonce; the exact {match} with both headers; a GET from another origin through the CORSMiddleware of the lane's server; cookies ignored; another instance, in process; an unusable instance key, in process too, with the probe module's derive_key replaced by one that raises InstanceKeyError: 503 INSTANCE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE for the nonce, its warning logged exactly once and nothing at error level, while the public check still answers {"match": false}, even for a nonce this instance issued). No test sends a preflight: its refusal is the middleware's.

docs.title: 🧼 Output Escaping
docs.text:
User- and provider-supplied text — asset, broker, and file names, notes, currency codes, icon URLs — is rendered as text in tables, chart tooltips, notifications, and validation messages. It never reaches {@html}, innerHTML, or a hand-built HTML string unescaped.

Svelte already escapes a plain {expression}. The risk lies wherever the frontend renders a string as markup, and each of those places has one rule:

Where markup is rendered Rule Helper Hand-built HTML strings: html table cells (rendered by DataTable with {@html}), ECharts tooltip formatters, validation-message parameters Escape every user or provider value at the point where it is interpolated escapeHtml (frontend/src/lib/utils/core/escapeHtml.ts) {@html} sinks fed from many places: toasts (ToastContainer.svelte), Tooltip.svelte, the transaction modals and result banner Sanitize the whole string at the sink. DOMPurify keeps the markup those strings are made of and drops event-handler attributes, <script>, and javascript: URLs sanitizeHtml (frontend/src/lib/utils/core/sanitizeHtml.ts) PAC planner explanations shown as tooltip HTML Escape the text first, then add only the line breaks and bullet lists the helper itself produces tipHtml (frontend/src/lib/features/tools/pac-allocator/planner/shared/tipHtml.ts)

escapeHtml escapes &, <, >, ", and ', so its output is safe both as text and inside a single- or double-quoted attribute. The escapeHtml exported by $lib/utils/inlineMath deliberately leaves the apostrophe alone because its output feeds KaTeX, where f'(x) is prime notation: do not use it for attribute values.

Three source gates keep the rule in force; the first two run in ./dev.py test front-utility core-unit, the third in ./dev.py test front-portfolio chart-safety-unit:

  • frontend/src/htmlInterpolation.gate.test.ts parses every non-test .svelte and .ts file under frontend/src and fails when a user or provider text field reaches an HTML template without passing through escapeHtml(…). Local escapers such as esc(…) are not accepted, because they leave " unescaped.
  • frontend/src/htmlSink.gate.test.ts requires every {@html X} in a non-test .svelte file to be a sanitizeHtml(…) call or an entry of its reviewed list, which records a reason for each sink. An entry that no longer matches a sink fails the gate.
  • frontend/src/lib/utils/core/escapeHtml.single.test.ts fails when a non-test .svelte or .ts file under frontend/src holds an HTML escaper of its own (& mapped to &) outside escapeHtml.ts. One file is exempt: inlineMath.ts, the KaTeX variant above. An exempt file that no longer holds a copy fails the gate (see Tooltip HTML).

No gate sees a raw innerHTML assignment that involves no template: do not write one. ./dev.py test front-asset asset-name-xss (frontend/e2e/assets/asset-name-xss.spec.ts) creates an asset whose name and icon URL carry markup, through the API, and checks in a real browser that the table and card views of /assets show it as text and run nothing.

A file opened in a spreadsheet is an output too. The CSV series exports of /api/v1/backup (GET /backup/asset/{asset_id}/prices and …/events, GET /backup/fx/{base}/{quote}/rates), written by series_export.stream_rows_as_csv, put one more leading apostrophe (') in front of a text cell that starts, after any apostrophes, with =, +, -, @, a tab or a carriage return, so that Excel, LibreOffice or Google Sheets show it as text and never run it as a formula (OWASP «CSV injection», lot B-39). A plain number (-1.5, +2, -1E+2) is never touched, and the JSON exports are unchanged. Counting the apostrophes already there keeps the round trip exact: the events import drops exactly one from notes (unescapeFormulaText, Data Editor), so a note =SUM(A1) exports as '=SUM(A1) and imports back as =SUM(A1). Tests: backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_series_export_csv.py.

Fixed in 1.2: a stored XSS present since v1.1.0

In v1.1.0 the Name column of the Assets table interpolated the asset name raw into an html cell, which DataTable renders with {@html}. The backend stores any string as an asset name and assets are global, so a name containing markup ran as script in the browser of every user who opened the asset list — the administrator included. The same flaw sat in other html cells, chart tooltips, toasts, and validation messages. The 1.2 fix escapes user text where it enters an HTML string, sanitizes the sinks that receive mixed markup, and adds the first two gates above.

docs.title: 🐳 Container Image Check
docs.text:
The automatic update check runs only for superusers, after login (frontend/src/routes/(app)/+layout.svelte), and only on a self-hosted instance (F05): checkForNewerRelease() awaits instanceConfig.load() and asks nothing of GitHub or of the registry, and writes nothing to its cache, unless GET /system/instance answered profile: selfhosted. A managed instance is updated by its hosting provider, and a failed configuration request skips the check too. Its release lookup is cached in localStorage (librefolio-update-check) for one hour (CHECK_INTERVAL_MS), and Skip this version is stored in the same entry. A manual Check for updates in the changelog modal bypasses both the cache and the dismissal, and reports errors. ChangelogModal shows that button only once GET /system/instance has answered profile: selfhosted: not on a managed instance, not before the answer, and not when the configuration request failed.

The update check reports a new release only once its Docker image can be pulled from GHCR. GHCR's anonymous token handshake is not available to browsers through CORS, so the frontend calls GET /api/v1/system/container-image-status?tag=X.Y.Z (authenticated) and the backend performs it (backend/app/services/platform/container_registry.py):

  1. Accept only a stable X.Y.Z tag; both the route's query pattern and the service check it.
  2. Send an anonymous HEAD for the tag's manifest on ghcr.io/librefolio/librefolio. Any answer other than 401 is final: success is published, 404 is pending, anything else is an error.
  3. On 401, parse the WWW-Authenticate Bearer challenge strictly (quoted parameters only, no duplicate keys). It is trusted only when realm is exactly https://ghcr.io/token — HTTPS, default port, no credentials, query, or fragment — service is ghcr.io, and scope is repository:librefolio/librefolio:pull.
  4. Request an anonymous pull token from that realm; accept it only if it has bearer-token syntax (when both token and access_token are present, they must match).
  5. Repeat the HEAD with that token in the Authorization header.

Every deviation fails closed with an error status (image-auth-request-failed for the challenge and token steps, image-request-failed for the manifest requests). An untrusted challenge is never followed, so the token request can only go to https://ghcr.io/token. The HTTP client uses a 5 s timeout and does not follow redirects. The frontend keeps the gate fail-closed as well (frontend/src/lib/features/update-check/updateCheck.ts): an error is never shown as "up to date".

docs.title: 📜 Request Logs
docs.text:
uvicorn writes one line per request, with its path and query string: HTTP requests on the uvicorn.access logger, WebSocket handshakes on uvicorn.error. A credential in a query string would reach that line in clear, so configure_logging() (backend/app/logging_config.py) adds a filter to both loggers. It replaces with *** the value of every credential-like query parameter: one named exactly code, or whose name holds token, ticket, secret, password, passwd, api_key/apikey/api-key or signature, in any case, judged on the name percent-decoded as the app reads it. The filter masks every string argument of the record where it stands, so the line keeps its shape, and the log stays on everywhere. A value is not decoded: a URL encoded inside another parameter's value is not read.

The links the app writes carry their tokens in the URL fragment, which the browser never sends, and the app's redirects (?redirect=, ?returnTo=) carry a path and query, never a fragment: the filter covers a token typed by hand into a query string. mask_query_credentials() holds the rule. One mode is outside it: uvicorn's own --log-level trace, which LibreFolio never passes, logs every ASGI message on uvicorn.asgi, headers included. It is a debugging mode, not meant for a server with real users.

The lines LibreFolio writes itself are JSON, one object per line, the message in event (H-60, decision D1); since lot H-60 each one names its request, and a failure is written once:

  • The request id. RequestIdMiddleware (backend/app/services/platform/request_id.py), the request_id entry of MIDDLEWARE_STACK, right inside activity and outside security_headers, draws an id for every HTTP request: secrets.token_hex(8), 16 lowercase hexadecimal characters, nothing derived from the request. It stores the id in scope["state"], where request.state.request_id and request_id_of() read it, and binds it in structlog's context variables while the request runs: merge_contextvars is the first processor of configure_logging(), so every line LibreFolio's loggers write for the request carries request_id. Every response gets it back in X-Request-Id, the 500 of an exception nobody handled included (Response Headers), and every 5xx in its body too (Error Answers). An X-Request-Id sent by the client is ignored, so the ids in the log are always the server's own. The middleware writes no line itself.
  • logger.exception() writes one line. structlog's wrapper is LibreFolioBoundLogger (backend/app/logging_config.py), and its exception() logs at ERROR with exc_info: the traceback is rendered once, inside the JSON line, under exception. Before, the standard library's Logger.exception added it a second time, in plain text after the line, and the level read EXCEPTION.
  • A failure is written once. A warning or a higher line written with an exception, or while one is handled, marks that exception as reported, when its logger writes that level (LibreFolioBoundLogger, mark_reported() in backend/app/utils/runtime/errors.py). The mark is per request (lot H-60r): one exception object can reach several requests, such as the failure of a build they all waited on. It keeps the request_id of each request whose log has a line about the exception, None for a line outside any request, and whether such a line carried its traceback. A line names the request_id it carries: the call's keyword, else the logger's bound context, else structlog's context variables, where RequestIdMiddleware binds it. A line with exc_info, exception() included, marks every exception its traceback shows: __cause__, else a __context__ that is not suppressed (mark_traceback_reported()). The platform's safety net, the 5xx handler and the 500 of an exception nobody handled, reads the mark. It writes nothing when the request's own log has the failure, and only the short Request failed with an error already logged, pointing to the first request's line, when another request's log has it (Error Answers). So every request id a client sees is in the log, and a traceback is written once. uvicorn logs an exception that leaves the app once more, as Exception in ASGI application on uvicorn.error, a plain-text traceback without the request id: configure_logging() adds to that logger a filter, _ReportedExceptionFilter, which drops such a record when its exception is marked, in any request, and lets every other record through. Any request will do: SecurityHeadersMiddleware writes the line of the request it answers, unless that request's log has it already, before it raises the exception again, so uvicorn's record is always a second copy.

Nor does the log keep a response that breaks its model (lot H-33, from workstream E's security review R13-SEC4). When an endpoint returns what its response_model refuses, FastAPI raises ResponseValidationError, for which it registers no handler: the exception used to go on to uvicorn, which logged it on uvicorn.error (Exception in ASGI application) with its traceback, whose message, str(exc), lists every error with its input: the response itself, the data of the user who asked. Now install_response_validation_handler(app) (backend/app/api/response_validation.py) handles it, for every route, and logs one ERROR, A response does not match its model, with the method, the route (its path template), the endpoint and, for each error, its type and loc only: never the input, never the msg (a validator may build it from the value), never the traceback (its message is str(exc)). Like every line of the request, it carries the request_id. The answer is the 500 of every platform failure since H-60, in JSON: {"detail": "Internal Server Error", "request_id": …, "error_type": "ResponseValidationError"} (Error Answers), with the security headers and X-Request-Id. It is the handler's own answer, which crosses the middleware stack like any other, and the exception stops there. Tests: ./dev.py test services response-validation (backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_response_validation.py) and, for the answer's request_id behind the request-id middleware, ./dev.py test services server-errors.

docs.title: 🖥️ The Browser Console
docs.text:
The web app writes one line to the browser console for each API call that fails unexpectedly, in a production build too (lot H-60): reportApiFailure() (frontend/src/lib/api/apiErrorConsole.ts), which the API client (frontend/src/lib/api/zodios-client.ts) calls from two places. The error branch of the Axios response interceptor reports an HTTP error, a network failure or a timeout. The zod-validation plugin of zodiosApi, Zodios's own response check replaced under its name so that it keeps its place in the plugin chain, validates the answer as before and reports a ZodiosError, an answer that breaks its schema, before throwing it again. A 5xx is reported once, by the interceptor.

[API] 503 POST /api/v1/ai-export/snapshot {code: 'snapshot_source_failure', component_id: '…', request_id: '3f2a9c0d41b7e865', error_type: 'ValueError'}
  • The line. console.error('[API]', '<status> <METHOD> <path>', fields). The status is network when nothing answered, with Axios's code in network (such as ERR_NETWORK or ECONNABORTED), and schema when an answer breaks its schema, with its issues in schema_issues: <path>:<issue code>, ten at most, a path segment that is neither an identifier nor an index printed as *. An HTTP failure's fields come from its answer: code (the code, else the error_code, of a detail that is an object, such as a coded refusal or an AI Export problem), reason_code and component_id from the same detail, request_id (the X-Request-Id header, else the body's) and error_type. A value is kept only when it has the shape of a code, an id or a class name.
  • How much. At error, the server errors (5xx), the network failures and the schema mismatches; at debug, every 4xx too: client_log_level decides (below). A request its AbortController canceled (ERR_CANCELED) is not a failure, and is never printed. reportApiFailure() never throws: the line is a help, never a new failure.
  • Never printed (the developer's question: does what we print expose sensitive data?): the request body; the request headers, so no token, cookie or password; the response headers but X-Request-Id; the query string, which can carry a token; a detail sentence; a 422 input; error.message, since a ZodiosError's message quotes the whole answer it refused; a value Zod received. The line says enough to find the request in the server log, and nothing a user typed or the server sent.
  • The id for a message. requestIdOf(error) gives the request id of a failed call, the X-Request-Id of its answer, else the request_id of its body, or null. A message shows it to the user through withRequestId(), for a server error only (The Error Code in a Message).
  • No other raw error. BrokerImportFilesModal.svelte no longer prints the error object of a failed load, and the request interceptor's own line, written in a debug build only (debug.log(), $lib/debug), names the path without its query string.

client_log_level (H-60, decision D4). GET /system/instance publishes how much the console gets (Public instance configuration): "debug" when the backend's LOG_LEVEL, or LIBREFOLIO_LOG_LEVEL which replaces it, is DEBUG or TRACE, in any case, and "error" otherwise (client_log_level(), backend/app/logging_config.py). Two states only: the level itself is not published. instanceConfig.load() hands each answer's value to setApiConsoleLevel() (Instance configuration): the level is error until an answer sets it, and a failed or superseded request changes nothing.

Every test lane runs at DEBUG. dev.py server --test always sets LIBREFOLIO_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG (cmd_server() in dev.py: test mode turns its debug mode on), and every lane's backend is started that way, the runner's shared one and Playwright's own webServer alike. A lane thus publishes client_log_level: "debug", and the browser console of the E2E suites gets a line for every failed call, a 4xx included. No spec fails on a console line: watchPageErrors() in frontend/e2e/fx/fx-detail.spec.ts, the only spec helper that collects them, writes them into a failed assertion's message as a diagnosis, and the specs that fail on a page error listen to pageerror, an uncaught exception, which a console line is not.

Tests: ./dev.py test front-utility core-unit runs src/lib/api/apiErrorConsole.test.ts (the level, the summary of each kind of failure, one line or none at each level, a canceled request, the request id, junk that must not make it throw, and a leak sweep: every value the console must never show carries a canary, looked for in every argument of every console call, through the real client too) and src/lib/features/instance/instanceConfig.test.ts (the level a successful load sets, and that a failed or superseded one leaves alone); ./dev.py test services server-errors covers client_log_level on the backend side.

docs.title: The Error Code in a Message
docs.text:
A user who meets a generic failure can quote its code, and the administrator finds the request in the server log with it (H-60's decision D3, lot H-60r). withRequestId(t, message, error) (frontend/src/lib/api/requestIdMessage.ts) is the one helper for every surface. It keeps the surface's message whole and puts the code after it, in parentheses, at the end, on the same line, through the key common.errorWithRequestId (REQUEST_ID_MESSAGE_KEY, in frontend/src/lib/i18n/base/): «… (code: 0123456789abcdef)», in Italian «… (codice: …)», in French «… (code : …)», with the space the French catalogue puts before a colon, in Spanish «… (código: …)».

  • A server error only. The code is the request id of the failed call, shown only for a 5xx that carries a LibreFolio id: that is the failure whose id the server log always holds (Error Answers). The platform writes no line for a 4xx, so its id would lead nowhere. A network failure has no answer, so no id, and a 5xx from a proxy carries no LibreFolio id. Otherwise withRequestId() returns the message unchanged, without calling t.
  • The answer behind a wrapper. serverErrorRequestId(error) looks for the failed answer, the response, on error, then on what it wraps: originalError (the AI Export client errors), else cause (the standard Error cause), eight links at most, never the same object twice. The id is requestIdOf()'s, above, kept only when it has the shape of an id. It never throws: an error it cannot read, null included, gives the message as it is.
  • Where to use it. Where the interface shows a generic failure (the server failed, the answer was not the expected one), never instead of a message that tells the user what to do. Pass the caught error as it is: an Axios or Zodios error, or a wrapper that keeps it in cause or originalError. RequestIdTranslate, the type of t, accepts svelte-i18n's $_ and get(_), AiExportTranslate and the Translate aliases of frontend/src/lib/api/ as they are.

Tests: ./dev.py test front-utility core-unit runs src/lib/api/requestIdMessage.test.ts (a 5xx with its id, from the header before the body; a 4xx, a network failure, a canceled request and a 5xx without an id keep the message, and t is never called; the answer up to eight links behind cause or originalError, and not further; cycles; hostile objects that must not make it throw; the key in the four generated catalogues; the translators the surfaces hold, taken with no cast).

docs.title: 🤐 Validation Errors Without the Input
docs.text:
FastAPI answers a request that fails validation (RequestValidationError) with 422 and one error per problem, each with the input that caused it: the value of a field that breaks its constraint and, for a missing field, the whole object it is missing from, a password or a token of the body included. Since lot A7b-2 of release 1.3 (A-35), no 422 of the app sends the request's input back.

  • Where. install_validation_error_handler(app) (backend/app/api/validation_errors.py) registers a handler for RequestValidationError; backend/app/main.py calls it once, so it answers for every route.
  • The answer. The handler builds a new RequestValidationError from the errors without their input and hands it to FastAPI's own request_validation_exception_handler(): the answer is FastAPI's, 422 with {"detail": [...]}, each error keeping type, loc, msg and, when the constraint has one, ctx. A client still knows which field is wrong and why; nothing of the request's body is kept.
  • What it leaves alone. A 422 a route raises itself, an HTTPException with its own detail such as a coded refusal, is not a validation error and goes out as before. The OpenAPI schema does not change: FastAPI's ValidationError still declares input, optional, so the generated client stays as it is.
  • Why every route. The login, the registration, the password change and reset, the setup link, tokens/inspect, the profile and the resend of an email verification take a password or a token in their body: a malformed request to any of them would get it back in the answer. The plugin-settings routes already kept the input out of their 422, for their secrets (_NoInputEchoRoute, see Plugin Settings); the rule now holds for every route.
  • Non-finite numbers (a follow-up of A-35, found by workstream X). Python's json reads 1E+400 and -1E+400 as infinities and takes NaN, Infinity and -Infinity, which RFC 8259 does not have. A Decimal field refuses each with finite_number, and FastAPI's default 422 carried the value as input (inf), which Starlette's JSON renderer (allow_nan=False) cannot write: the answer was a 500, on any route with a Decimal in its body. Without the input, the handler's answer is a readable 422: one error, finite_number, whose msg does not hold the value, without ctx.
  • What it does not remove, and the rule (A-38). The handler drops input only: msg and ctx stay as Pydantic wrote them. A validator that formats the value into its message (raise ValueError(f"… {value}")) puts part of it in msg, while the ValueError itself, in ctx.error, serializes to {}. So the rule: the validator of a secret field (a password, a token, a secret, a key, a credential) says what is wrong, never with what: no value in the message. The validator of a public field may show it, as the currency validators of schemas/common.py do with the code they refuse. None of the routes that take a credential breaks the rule, their tests look for the secret in the whole answer, and backend/test_scripts/test_schemas/test_secret_validator_messages.py (./dev.py test schemas secret-validator-messages) reads the source of backend/app/schemas and fails for any field_validator of a field named like a secret that formats its value into what it raises.

Tests: ./dev.py test api validation-errors (backend/test_scripts/test_api/test_validation_errors_api.py): in process, a small app with and without the handler — a password too short, a missing field, two errors at once, a query parameter, a body that is not JSON, then a valid request and a route's own 422, answered as before —; on the lane's server, every route with a secret in its body, the secret field invalid and another field missing, the secret nowhere in the answer; the shape a plain 422 keeps, and the OpenAPI schema. Its section 4, the non-finite numbers: in process, 1E+400, -1E+400, NaN, Infinity and -Infinity on a plain and on a constrained Decimal, a 500 without the handler (the premise) and a 422 that a strict JSON parser reads with it, 20 cases; on the lane, 1E+400 and NaN as the amount of POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/convert, a Decimal, refused before the route runs, signed in as an account of the test's own.

A 422 never sends the request's input back; a 500 from a response that breaks its model never writes the response to the log: see Request Logs.

docs.title: 🏷️ Response Headers
docs.text:
SecurityHeadersMiddleware (backend/app/services/platform/security_headers.py), the security_headers entry of MIDDLEWARE_STACK (see Steps and Middleware: the Contract), adds the security headers of decision D5. Two of them, ALWAYS_HEADERS, go on every HTTP response of the app: API answers, the web app, the documentation and the files, compressed or not, errors included. A Content-Security-Policy is enforced on every document too, in every profile, and two switches add more, off on a self-hosted install and on in the managed profile: see The Content-Security-Policy and Frame Protection.

Header Value Effect X-Content-Type-Options nosniff The browser uses the type the server sends and never guesses another, so no file, an upload included, is sniffed into a script or a page Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin Another site learns at most the origin of a page, never its path or query
  • A header the route set is kept. The middleware adds a header only when the response has none of that name, in any case: a route's Referrer-Policy: no-referrer stays, and the nosniff that the file routes of the uploads (backend/app/api/v1/uploads.py: the text preview and serve_file()) and the download of a broker report (backend/app/api/v1/brokers.py) set themselves is not repeated. Names are compared whole, never by prefix: content-security-policy is a prefix of content-security-policy-report-only, so a prefix check would let a route's report-only policy suppress the enforced one, or the reverse. A route that sets its own X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy or Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only keeps it alone, and the middleware still adds the others. WebSocket and lifespan scopes pass untouched.
  • The 500 of an exception. Starlette answers an unhandled exception from ServerErrorMiddleware, which it puts outside every middleware of the stack, so its 500 would go out without the headers. When a request raises before its response has started, the middleware sends the 500 itself with the headers of every response: since H-60 in JSON, {"detail": "Internal Server Error", "request_id": …, "error_type": …}, plain text before (Error Answers). The exception reaches the request's log once, as Unhandled error unless that log has it already, or as a short line when another request's log has it, and the middleware re-raises it: ServerErrorMiddleware finds the response started and sends nothing, and uvicorn's own line for the exception is dropped (Request Logs).
  • X-Request-Id is not a security header, but it is on every HTTP response too: RequestIdMiddleware, the request_id entry right outside this one, adds the request's id, so the 500 this middleware sends carries it as well. An X-Request-Id the app set itself is kept, and never repeated. See Request Logs.
  • A type for every file served. With nosniff, a script or a style sheet sent with a type that is not its own is refused, so every file the app serves must carry its right type. FileResponse (the /_app mount, the SPA catch-all, /mkdocs) and the plugin-asset route (/uploads/plugin/…) take it from mimetypes, with application/octet-stream for a name it does not know. mimetypes reads Python's own table, which has no type for the fonts or .map, then the system's mime.types files, which a slim image such as the runtime python:3.13-slim does not have. register_served_types(), which install_static_site() calls, adds SERVED_TYPES (JavaScript, CSS, JSON and source maps, the web manifest, WebAssembly, SVG, the fonts) to mimetypes for the whole process, so these extensions get the same type on every machine.

docs.title: 🛡️ The Content-Security-Policy and Frame Protection
docs.text:
Decision D5 for the managed profile, and, since H-55 v2, the Content-Security-Policy always enforced (developer decision of 19/10: on by default in every profile, no switch, a mesh widened only where it is truly needed). Two bool switches of Settings, False in the code and True in PROFILE_DEFAULTS["managed"] (see Settings System), still add to it: LIBREFOLIO_FRAME_PROTECTION and LIBREFOLIO_CSP_REPORT_ONLY. Each can be set on its own, in either profile, and a value set in the environment or in .env wins over the profile. In the managed profile, a switch that is off shows in the configuration checks: platform.frame_protection, a warning, and platform.csp_report_only, an info (H-39). The enforced policy has no check: it cannot be off. For administrators: «The Content-Security-Policy» in Configuration.

One Content-Security-Policy field per response (never two), and the module's docstring (backend/app/services/platform/security_headers.py) is the reference:

Response Enforced directives Constant A document, any path: HTML (the web app's pages, the documentation, Swagger UI and ReDoc), XHTML, SVG, XML, any type ending with +xml (H-45); not a PDF object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self' DOCUMENT_DIRECTIVES The API's documentation pages, /api/v1/docs and /api/v1/redoc (text/html; only where LIBREFOLIO_API_DOCS or test mode is on, R5), in addition script-src 'self' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net; worker-src 'self' blob:; connect-src 'self' API_DOCS_PAGES, api_docs_policy(), WEB_APP_WORKER_SRC A page of the web app (text/html exactly, outside /mkdocs and /api), in addition script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval' 'report-sample' and the sorted hashes of the build's inline scripts; worker-src 'self' blob:; connect-src 'self', then the origin of LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL, then https://api.github.com in the selfhosted profile only WEB_APP_SCRIPT_SRC, WEB_APP_WORKER_SRC, web_app_policy(), connect_sources() A script of the web app's build (R4, H-55 wave 4): a response of type text/javascript or application/javascript (parameters ignored) on a path starting with /_app/ script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' and the same extra sources as the pages; worker-src 'self' blob:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self' SCRIPT_MEDIA_TYPES, APP_ASSETS_PREFIX, worker_policy() Every response, with LIBREFOLIO_FRAME_PROTECTION on frame-ancestors 'self' (first), and the X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN header FRAME_ANCESTORS, PAGE_POLICY A non-document with frame protection off no policy

Never in the enforced header: default-src, style-src, img-src, font-src, frame-src. Styles, images (asset and broker icons are set by URL), fonts and frames stay free, and framing the app (a Home Assistant panel) stays a legitimate self-hosted use, controlled by frame protection alone. What each directive is for:

  • The trio on every document (H-42, H-45, now always): no plugin content (<object>, <embed>), no injected <base> sending relative URLs elsewhere, no form sending its data to another site. LibreFolio uses none of them. Not a PDF: Chromium shows an inline PDF with a viewer it treats as a plugin, which object-src 'none' on the PDF's own answer could stop. A user's SVG or XML never comes inline as a document (an upload of a type outside INLINE_SAFE_MEDIA_TYPES is an attachment, its text preview is text/plain), so the document types are defence in depth.
  • script-src is the point of the lot: only the app's own scripts, and an inline script only by its hash. 'wasm-unsafe-eval' lets WebAssembly compile, for the PDF viewer (EmbedPDF's PDFium). 'report-sample' puts the first 40 characters of a blocked script or eval in the page's own securitypolicyviolation event; there is no report endpoint, so they never leave the browser (if one is ever added, they would).
  • worker-src 'self' blob:: without it workers follow script-src, which has no blob:, and the PDF viewer's workers are blocked.
  • The policy of a worker script (R4, worker_policy()): a browser applies the Content-Security-Policy of a script response only to a worker it starts from that URL, and ignores it on any other script. So every JavaScript file of the build (/_app/…) carries one: script-src 'self' (the worker loads the build's own modules and nothing else), the same connect-src as the pages, worker-src 'self' blob: (a worker may start workers from the build or a blob), object-src 'none' and base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self' first when frame protection is on. No default-src, no 'unsafe-inline', no 'unsafe-eval' and no 'wasm-unsafe-eval': the only worker started from a URL today, priceProcessing.worker, compiles no WebAssembly. The PDF engine's worker starts from a blob: URL and keeps the policy of the page that started it. Not on a 304 (below), not on JavaScript outside /_app/ (plugin assets, /mkdocs), and a header the route set is kept.
  • connect-src: the app's origin, the canonical origin of LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL (canonical_origin(), backend/app/utils/runtime/origins.py: scheme://host[:port], lower case, no default port, the same form as the hosting panel's audience), and GitHub's API for the update check, which runs in the administrator's browser (frontend/src/lib/features/update-check/updateCheck.ts; the managed profile never makes it, and gets no GitHub source). A LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL that cannot be used (env_url() raises) adds nothing, logs one warning when the middleware is built, and the server keeps serving.
  • Frame protection (LIBREFOLIO_FRAME_PROTECTION): X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN on every response (a 304 included) and frame-ancestors 'self' in its policy; only the app's own pages may frame it, so a hosting panel or a dashboard on another origin is refused by the browser. The policy of a response follows its type, read at http.response.start: _media_type() takes the first content-type, the part before ;, stripped and lower case ("" when there is none); _is_document() holds when that type is in DOCUMENT_MEDIA_TYPES (text/html, application/xhtml+xml, image/svg+xml, application/xml, text/xml) or ends with +xml; _is_web_app_page() requires exactly text/html and a path outside /mkdocs (bare or /mkdocs/…) and /api (bare or /api/…). The middleware is outside GZip, so a compressed page still says text/html. The pages of the documentation (/mkdocs), the HTML 404 for an unknown API path and any non-HTML document get the trio (and frame-ancestors) but no script-src: the documentation is a separate site this policy does not describe. Swagger UI and ReDoc, where they are on, are the exception: they get api_docs_policy(), described below. The check is by path (API_DOCS_PAGES, the two page paths, whole) and by type (text/html exactly), after the web-app and /_app/ checks; the start scripts (text/javascript, outside /_app/) and openapi.json keep the plain headers, with no policy.
  • The API's documentation pages (R5, api_docs_policy(), backend/app/api/api_docs.py): off everywhere except where config.api_docs_enabled() holds, that is LIBREFOLIO_API_DOCS (which ./dev.py server --debug sets) or test mode; anywhere else the routes are not registered and answer 404, openapi.json included, so an instance in use publishes no map of its API. FastAPI's own pages are never used (main.py passes docs_url=None and redoc_url=None): they load swagger-ui-dist@5 and redoc@2 from jsDelivr at a moving version, with no integrity, and start them with an inline script. Ours: the page is a fixed HTML string; the libraries come from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net at an exact version, each <script> and <link> with its Subresource Integrity hash (integrity="sha384-…") and crossorigin="anonymous", so the browser refuses a file whose bytes changed; the start script is a separate response of the instance (/api/v1/docs/swagger-init.js, /api/v1/redoc/redoc-init.js) reading the schema's address from a data-openapi-url attribute, so there is no inline script and no inline handler; no Google Fonts, no third-party favicon, no validator badge. The policy follows: script-src 'self' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net (the origin, not the hashes: the browser checks the integrity of each tag), worker-src 'self' blob: (ReDoc's search worker) and connect-src 'self' (the schema), with the trio and, with frame protection on, frame-ancestors 'self'. No 'unsafe-inline', no 'unsafe-eval'. The routes sit outside the instance-block guard, as before. The libraries and how to bump one: The Pinned Libraries of the API Docs.
  • No policy on a 304 (H-45). self.not_modified_headers has no content-security-policy: a browser freshens the response it cached with the header fields of a 304 (RFC 9111 §4.3.4), and Starlette's NotModifiedResponse (StaticFiles, the /_app mount) has no Content-Type, so a policy on it would replace the cached document's (checked in Chromium 149). X-Frame-Options, nosniff and Referrer-Policy still go on it. FileResponse (the pages, the documentation) never answers 304, so the guard is latent.
  • A header the route set is kept, names compared whole: a route's own Content-Security-Policy leaves the middleware's out, and the report-only one is its own field.

docs.title: 📌 The Pinned Libraries of the API Docs
docs.text:
api_docs.LIBRARIES holds the three files the pages load: SWAGGER_JS and SWAGGER_CSS (swagger-ui-dist@5.33.1) and REDOC_JS (redoc@2.5.4, the standalone bundle). Each is a Library(url, integrity); the pages are built from the same constants, and LIBRARY_ORIGIN (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net) is the only host the policy names. To bump a version:

  1. Change the version in the url: an exact one, never a range or a tag such as @5.

  2. Compute the hash of the file jsDelivr publishes at that URL, never of a copy or of the previous version's:

    curl -s https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/swagger-ui-dist@<version>/swagger-ui-bundle.js | openssl dgst -sha384 -binary | base64

  3. Write it as sha384-<that output> in the integrity of the same Library.

  4. Check both pages on a ./dev.py server --debug server, then run ./dev.py test api api-docs (backend/test_scripts/test_api/test_api_docs.py), which pins the contract of the pages: an exact version, an integrity and crossorigin on every external tag, the only external host, no inline script, the routes out of the schema and 404 when off.

A wrong hash is not silent: the browser refuses the file, and the page does not load that library (the console names the integrity failure).

docs.title: 🔤 The PDF Viewer's CJK Fonts
docs.text:
The PDF preview asks nothing of a third party, and connect-src stays 'self' (H-55 wave 4, decision (c) of the developer). The viewer's engine is always the instance's own copy: when it does not answer, pdfViewerAssets() (frontend/src/lib/utils/files/pdfViewerAssets.ts) throws, and the preview shows the browser's own PDF viewer (file-preview-pdf-fallback) instead of falling back to a CDN. The Chinese, Japanese and Korean fallback fonts (@embedpdf/fonts-jp, -kr, -sc, -tc) are tens of megabytes each, too heavy for the image, so the viewer asks the instance for one only when a PDF needs it, and the server gets it.

  • The route: GET /api/v1/files/pdf-fonts/{package}/{file} (backend/app/api/v1/pdf_fonts.py), out of the OpenAPI schema (the viewer's worker reads it, never the generated client) and for signed-in users only (get_current_user: an anonymous caller must not make the instance fetch tens of megabytes; 401 without a session). A name that is not exactly an entry of the list is a 404. 200 is the file as font/otf, Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable. The blocking work runs through asyncio.to_thread.
  • The list: backend/app/services/files/pdf_font_hashes.json, the version of the packages and, for each of the 26 files, its package, name, size and sha256. Only these files are ever fetched, from one fixed host (PDF_FONT_SOURCE, https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@embedpdf, at <package>@<version>): no name from a request reaches the network.
  • The fetch (cached_font() in backend/app/services/files/pdf_fonts.py): the file is <data dir>/cache/pdf-fonts/<package>/<file> when it exists with the entry's size. Otherwise fetch_font_bytes() (the one network call, httpx, no redirects, at most the entry's size) gets it, the sha256 is checked before anything is written, and the file is written under a temporary name in the same folder, then renamed. One fetch at a time per file: two concurrent requests fetch once. cache/ is a managed path of validate_test_data_dir() and is not in the backup (ARCHIVED_FOLDERS); deleting it only means the fonts are fetched again.
  • The failures: the source cannot be reached, answers other than 200, or sends more than the entry's size: PdfFontUnavailable, a 503 with detail.code pdf_font_unavailable, and the PDF shows without those glyphs. A file whose hash or size is not the entry's: PdfFontMismatch, a 502 with pdf_font_mismatch, never written, one warning naming package and file.
  • Regenerating the list: it is not written by hand but read from the copies the lock installed in frontend/node_modules/@embedpdf/fonts-{jp,kr,sc,tc} (the same files, byte for byte). After updating those packages, run node frontend/scripts/pdf-font-hashes.mjs; node frontend/scripts/pdf-font-hashes.mjs --check exits 1 when the file differs from what it would write, without writing. The Vitest guard frontend/src/lib/utils/files/pdfFontHashes.test.ts does the same in the unit lane (the list equals the script's output for the installed packages, holds the 26 files of the four packages and no other, and carries their package.json version): a package updated without regenerating the list turns it red, instead of production refusing every font with a hash mismatch.

Tests: ./dev.py test services pdf-fonts (backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_pdf_fonts.py: the list, the cache, a wrong hash thrown away and logged, the source unreachable, one fetch per file under concurrency, the route's session, type, cache header and absence from the schema), and in the browser frontend/e2e/files.spec.ts and frontend/e2e/files-pdf-offline.spec.ts (no request to cdn.jsdelivr.net).

docs.title: 🔄 The Hashes Follow the Build
docs.text:
spa_inline_script_hashes(build_dir) (backend/app/services/platform/static_site.py) reads every top-level *.html of frontend/build/ (today index.html, 200.html, offline.html; never a hidden one) and gives the source expression 'sha256-<base64>' of every <script> without src, whatever its type: its text with the line ends the HTML parser leaves (CR LF and a lone CR become LF), UTF-8, each once, sorted. SvelteKit has no csp option here and adds no nonce, and its start script names the build's own chunks, so its hash changes with every build.

Before H-55 v2 the hashes were read once, when the middleware was built, and a build made while the server ran left a blank page under an enforced policy. Now _BuildScriptHashes (a cache of the middleware) keeps the hashes of the build as it is:

  • the signature of the build is, for every *.html directly in static_site.FRONTEND_BUILD_DIR whose name does not start with ., (name, st_mtime_ns, st_size), sorted: one stat per page, paid by web-app HTML responses only (never an asset, an API answer or /mkdocs);
  • the same signature as last time: no page is read again (static_site.spa_inline_script_hashes is looked up as a module attribute at each miss, so a test can count its calls); a changed one: the hashes are recomputed and used from that response on, in the enforced header and in the report-only one;
  • a page of the last good signature missing now (the build being written): the last good hashes stay and the next web-app response checks again; no build, ever: no hash, just 'self'.

So a new frontend build needs no restart. What is read once, when the middleware is built, are the settings: frame protection, report-only, the profile and LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL; Starlette builds the stack lazily at the app's first ASGI call. A change of any of them takes a restart.

docs.title: 🕵️ A Script Nobody Sent
docs.text:
A proxy that injects a script (Cloudflare's Rocket Loader or automatic Web Analytics, an Nginx sub_filter), a CDN or a browser extension is blocked: a script-src-elem violation. It is made visible where an administrator looks, and nowhere else (frontend/src/lib/features/security/cspNotice.ts):

  • frontend/src/app.html has, after the anti-FOUC script, a second block in its own try: it fills window.__lfCspViolations from securitypolicyviolation events with disposition === 'enforce', before any bundle loads. startCspNotice() drains it, listens for the next ones and, where the browser has one, a ReportingObserver with {types: ['csp-violation'], buffered: true};
  • KNOWN_CSP_VIOLATIONS are never reported: cheetah-grid's probe of the global object, script-src, eval, sample (function anonymous( ) { return this }) (the same entry as the E2E baseline's cheetah-grid-global-probe);
  • anything else enforced: one console.error per page load, LibreFolio blocked a script it did not send (<origin, inline or eval>): a proxy, a CDN or a browser extension adds it. Guide: <origin>/mkdocs/admin/configuration_security/#csp, and its source added once to sessionStorage['librefolio-csp-blocked'], a JSON array of distinct strings; storage failures are swallowed;
