docs.title: ⚡ Asynchronous Architecture
docs.text: LibreFolio is built from the ground up using an asynchronous architecture to ensure high performance and efficiency, especially when dealing with I/O-bound operations like database queries and external API calls.

docs.title: 🤔 Why Async?
docs.text:
A traditional synchronous web server handles one request at a time per worker process. If a request involves waiting for a database query or an external API call, the entire worker process is blocked, unable to handle other requests.

An asynchronous server, on the other hand, can handle multiple requests concurrently within a single process. When a task needs to wait for I/O, the server can switch to another task instead of blocking. This leads to:

  • Higher Throughput: The server can handle many more concurrent connections with fewer resources.
  • Better Responsiveness: The application remains responsive even when performing long-running I/O operations.
  • Efficient Resource Usage: Less time is spent waiting, and more time is spent doing actual work.

docs.title: 🚀 FastAPI
docs.text:
FastAPI is an asynchronous web framework by default. All API endpoint functions in LibreFolio are defined with async def, allowing them to be run concurrently by the ASGI server (Uvicorn).

@router.get("/assets", response_model=List[AssetRead])
async def get_assets(session: AsyncSession = Depends(get_session)):
    # This is an async function
    assets = await AssetCRUDService.get_all(session)
    return assets

docs.title: 🗃️ SQLAlchemy with asyncio
docs.text:
All database interactions are performed using SQLAlchemy's asyncio extension.

  • AsyncSession: Instead of a regular Session, the application uses an AsyncSession which provides an awaitable interface for all database operations.
  • asyncpg / aiosqlite: Asynchronous database drivers are used to communicate with the database in a non-blocking way.
# Example of an async database query
async def get_all(session: AsyncSession) -> List[Asset]:
    result = await session.execute(select(Asset))
    return result.scalars().all()

docs.title: 🌐 Asynchronous Provider Contracts
docs.text:
Asset provider methods such as get_current_value(), get_history_value(), fetch_asset_metadata(), search(), and resolve_url() have asynchronous contracts. The service layer can therefore fan out work with asyncio.gather() and limit provider concurrency with semaphores.

The contract does not require every third-party SDK to be async-native. For example, YahooFinanceProvider calls the synchronous yfinance API directly inside its async def methods. This is safe because the caller moves the entire provider coroutine away from the main event loop before it starts.

docs.title: 🧵 Canonical Provider Thread Boundary
docs.text:
The single provider isolation helper is backend/app/services/assets/core.py::_run_provider_in_thread(). Manager operation modules and AssetSearchService route provider I/O through it. For every call, the helper:

  1. starts a worker with asyncio.to_thread();
  2. creates a new event loop inside that worker thread;
  3. runs the provider coroutine to completion on that loop;
  4. closes the loop and applies the caller's timeout with asyncio.wait_for().

The implementation is equivalent to this shortened excerpt:

async def _run_provider_in_thread(coro_factory, *, timeout=60.0):
    def _sync_runner():
        loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
        asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)
        try:
            return loop.run_until_complete(coro_factory())
        finally:
            loop.close()

    return await asyncio.wait_for(
        asyncio.to_thread(_sync_runner),
        timeout=timeout,
    )

Provider implementations must therefore leave synchronous I/O direct:

class YahooFinanceProvider(AssetSourceProvider):
    async def get_current_value(
        self,
        identifier: str,
        identifier_type: IdentifierType,
        provider_params: dict | None,
    ) -> FACurrentValue:
        info = yf.Ticker(identifier).info  # Direct sync call in the provider thread
        ...

Do not add asyncio.to_thread() or run_in_executor() inside an asset provider. A nested offload is redundant and makes timeout and exception behavior harder to reason about. Async-native provider clients remain valid; they simply run on the worker thread's event loop.

Event Loop Blocking Rule

Outside the asset-provider boundary, never call synchronous I/O (HTTP requests, file reads, time.sleep()) directly inside an async def endpoint or service method. Use an async-native library or an explicit service-level offload.

Long CPU-bound work holds the loop as well: the portfolio engine's daily replay runs on a dedicated executor, not on the default one every asyncio.to_thread() call shares, so its own two workers bound how many replays run at once (Off the Event Loop).

Symptoms of event loop blocking:

  • Other API calls hang until the blocking call completes
  • E2E tests time out intermittently
  • Health checks fail during provider sync operations

docs.title: 📦 BRIM Plugin Guide
docs.text:
How to create a new Broker Report Import Manager plugin to support a new broker's CSV/Excel export format.

Base class: BRIMProvider (in backend/app/services/brim/brim_provider.py) Plugin folder: backend/app/services/brim_providers/<code>/ — the code in plugin.py, beside an __init__.py holding only its docstring (see Auto-Discovery) Registry: BRIMProviderRegistry

docs.title: 🤖 Tip: Let an LLM write the plugin for you
docs.text:
Paste this entire page plus the Generic CSV Provider page into an LLM and use this prompt:

Suggested prompt

Here is the LibreFolio BRIM plugin specification: [paste this page]
Here is the Generic CSV reference implementation: [paste generic_csv page]

I have a broker called [BROKER_NAME]. Here is a sample of their CSV export: [paste header + 3–5 rows]

Write a complete Python BRIMProvider plugin for this broker. Follow the conventions
exactly (BRIMParseOutput, BRIMExtractedAssetInfo, sign conventions, @register_provider).

The LLM will produce a complete, working plugin skeleton. Test it with the probe endpoint, then save it as brim_providers/<code>/plugin.py, beside an __init__.py holding only a docstring, and restart — it will be auto-discovered.

docs.title: 🔄 Flow
docs.text:
The system calls plugin methods in two distinct phases:

graph TD
    subgraph "Phase 1 — Detection (upload, and first read after an update)"
        D1["File uploaded"] --> D2["can_parse(file_path)<br/><small>Quick header/extension check</small>"]
        D0["Original read after an update<br/><small>plugins_signature ≠ app version</small>"] --> D2
        D2 -->|true| D3["Plugin listed as<br/>compatible option"]
        D2 -->|false| D4["Skip"]
    end

    subgraph "Phase 2 — Parsing (user selects plugin)"
        P1["parse(file_path, broker_id)<br/><small>Full parsing</small>"] --> P2["Returns:<br/>• BRIMParseOutput"]
        P2 --> P3["User reviews<br/>in preview UI"]
        P3 --> P4["POST /transactions<br/><small>Core handles persist</small>"]
    end

    D3 ~~~ P1

    style D0 fill:#e3f2fd,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#1565c0
    style D1 fill:#e3f2fd,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#1565c0
    style D2 fill:#e3f2fd,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#1565c0
    style D3 fill:#e3f2fd,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#1565c0
    style P1 fill:#e8f5e9,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#2e7d32
    style P2 fill:#fff3e0,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#e65100
    style P3 fill:#fff3e0,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#e65100
    style P4 fill:#f3e5f5,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#7b1fa2

Phase 1 runs automatically when a file is uploaded — every registered plugin is asked if it can parse the file. Compatible plugins are listed for the user. It runs again, once per app version, when an original detected by another version is read: see The lifecycle of compatible_plugins.

A file's compatible_plugins are what the import wizard offers for it, so can_parse must not claim a file that parse would refuse, fallback plugins included: the Generic CSV (broker_generic_csv, detection_priority 0) says True only for a .csv whose header row names both required columns, date and type, directly or through its multilingual aliases (HEADER_MAPPINGS: data, fecha, datum…; tipo, operazione, action…) — it used to claim any CSV with a header, then fail at parse. A file no plugin recognises is offered every plugin; parsing it with a single-file plugin whose can_parse says no answers 400 Plugin '<name>' cannot parse file '<file name>' — the plugin's provider_name and the name the file was uploaded with —, followed by : <reason> when the plugin says why (cannot_parse_reason), and moves the file to failed with that message as its error.

The rule has one extension: a plugin may claim a file it recognises as its own broker's even when it cannot import it, provided parse explains what is wrong — no transactions and one BRIMNotice in the file's language saying what to upload instead. The plugin does not fail to read such a file: it knows the file is its broker's, so cannot_parse_reason stays None, and parse succeeds instead of refusing it — the file moves to parsed with the notice. Reference: DEGIRO's Transactions export, the list of orders, which has no dividends, deposits, withdrawals or currency conversions. broker_degiro claims it next to the Account Statement (_layout tells the two apart), and its parse returns no transactions and the degiro_orders_list warning, which asks for the Account Statement.

Phase 2 runs when the user selects a specific plugin — the plugin parses the file, the user reviews the results, and confirms the import.

Plugin responsibility: Read the broker-specific file format and convert to standard TXCreateItem DTOs. Core responsibility: File storage, asset matching, duplicate detection, database persistence.

A bank that splits one account across several exports (Danske Bank: a custody XLSX and a cash CSV) adds a step between the two phases: the exports uploaded together form a report set, the plugin combines them, and phase 2 parses the combined file. See Multi-report plugins (report sets).

docs.title: ♻️ The lifecycle of compatible_plugins
docs.text:
A file's compatible_plugins is detected once per app version, not once for the file's whole life (brim_provider.py):

  1. At upload, save_uploaded_file asks every plugin (BRIMProviderRegistry.get_compatible_plugins) and stores the list in the file's sidecar with plugins_signature, the signature of the plugin catalogue that detected it: detection_signature(), which is the app version (get_version()).
  2. On read — get_file_info and list_files, so also the wizard's Plugin column, its set grouping (setPluginFor) and collect_members — an original whose stored signature is missing (a file uploaded before 1.2) or differs from the running version's is detected again, on the data file beside its sidecar, whatever its status. The read returns the new list and saves it with the current signature, once per version; under the current signature the stored list is trusted as it is.
  3. Kept as stored: a combined file is never detected again — its list is the plugin that built it. An original whose data file is gone, or whose detection fails, keeps its stored list and nothing is saved: the next read tries again.

The effect: after an update, a plugin added or changed since a file's upload is offered for it, and one that no longer reads it drops out — the Generic CSV, stricter since 1.2, drops from the CSVs that lack its date or type column, which 1.1.0 offered it for. Files uploaded together (one batch_id) before a report-set plugin could read them form their set after the update, without a new upload. Files uploaded with 1.1.0 or earlier are the exception: those versions recorded no batch_id, so the files belong to no set — each is offered the set plugin, whose parse answers 422 set_required — and must be uploaded again, together.

For a plugin author there is nothing to implement, but can_parse answers are cached per app version and evaluated again after an update:

  • a change to can_parse reaches the files already uploaded with the next app version, and needs no plugin_version bump: that version covers what parse and combine output, not detection;
  • a can_parse that raises counts as False (get_compatible_plugins skips the plugin), and that answer is cached like any other until the next version — never raise;
  • in a development checkout the version is git describe --tags --always --dirty, unless LF_APP_VERSION is set (Version Stamps), read once per process: an edited can_parse reaches the files already uploaded only once that string changes (a commit) and the server restarts — or upload the file again.

The detection itself takes no lock, because it reads the file. The save takes the broker metadata lock, reads the sidecar again under it and writes only if the sidecar is still where it was read and still lacks the current signature, changing only compatible_plugins and plugins_signature: a move, a deletion or another write made meanwhile is never undone. Because a read may now open the file, the API calls list_files and get_file_info (in _get_brim_file_with_access) through asyncio.to_thread.

docs.title: 🔒 The broker metadata lock
docs.text:
Every write of a broker's sidecars holds that broker's lock, broker_metadata_lock(broker_id) (_broker_metadata_lock inside brim_provider.py). A plugin never takes it: the core does, around its own writes.

  • Two layers. In the process, a re-entrant threading.RLock per broker; across processes, an advisory fcntl.flock on broker_reports/.locks/broker_<id>.lock (broker_none.lock for the legacy files at the root of a status folder). The file lock is taken once, by the outermost block of a thread, and released when that block ends, on an exception too. It must hold across processes because a server may run several uvicorn workers (./dev.py server --workers N); the Docker image runs one.
  • Holders: the upload (save_uploaded_file, around its sidecar write), _update_metadata, save_combined_file, save_parse_result, _move_file (move_to_parsed, move_to_failed), delete_file, and the save of a re-detection. The key is the broker of the sidecar's folder, <status>/broker_<id>/; a move changes only the status folder, so every writer of a file takes the same lock.
  • Reads take no lock: every write is an atomic rename (_write_metadata_atomic), so a reader sees the old sidecar or the new one.
  • Never across an await: re-entrant within a thread, the lock would let two coroutines of the event loop in together. combine_set holds it in a worker thread, from the reuse check to the save (POST /sets/combine).

docs.title: 🧭 Import philosophy & currency rules
docs.text:
A BRIM plugin is a faithful transcriber, not a re-calculator. These rules are mandatory for every new plugin:

  • Verbatim / copy-paste import. Import the numbers exactly as they appear in the broker's report. Do not recompute totals, prices or amounts; transcribe them.
  • No forex system. A BRIM plugin must never invoke the FX subsystem and must never convert amounts using the report's own exchange-rate column. If the export has a rate column (e.g. Fineco's Cambio), ignore it.
  • Currency from the source. Derive each transaction's currency from the broker's own currency column (per row) and tag every monetary figure in that row with it. A single file may legitimately contain multiple currencies — that's expected, keep them as reported.
  • Delimiter detection. Always resolve the separator with self.detect_csv_delimiter(file_path) — never hardcode , or ;.
  • Encoding fallback. Never open an export with a fixed encoding such as open(file_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") — banks and Excel on Windows often write Windows-1252 or Latin-1, and a UTF-8 read fails on the first accented byte. Read text with self._open_text(file_path) (add newline="" when the stream feeds csv and line endings must be kept) or through _brim_io.read_rows. The test suite enforces it (class TestWindows1252Invariance): test_no_plugin_opens_files_with_a_fixed_encoding fails on any open(..., encoding=...) in a module of a broker_*/ plugin folder, and test_sample_parses_identically_when_saved_as_windows_1252 requires every non-ASCII CSV sample, re-saved as Windows-1252, to be detected and parsed identically by each plugin that accepts the original.
  • Multiple export layouts. When a broker ships more than one report layout (e.g. with and without commission columns), detect the variant dynamically — locate the header row and branch on the actual column set rather than assuming a fixed line offset.
  • Sign conventions. Set signs per TransactionType (BUY: qty > 0, cash < 0; SELL: qty < 0, cash > 0; DIVIDEND/INTEREST: qty = 0, cash > 0; FEE/TAX: qty = 0, cash < 0; ADJUSTMENT: qty ≠ 0, no cash), but take the magnitudes verbatim from the report.
  • One source row may emit several transactions. Keep economic legs explicit: securities-only buys can be DEPOSIT + BUY, sells can be SELL + WITHDRAWAL, maturities can be SELL at par + INTEREST, and snapshots can be DEPOSIT + ADJUSTMENT seeds.
  • Fake asset IDs. Emit high positive fake asset IDs (keyed by ISIN/ticker) plus BRIMExtractedAssetInfo so the core can drive the asset-matching UI.
  • The operation date, and only settled rows. Record every transaction on its operation date, the day the operation was made (the trade date), never on the settlement or value date (the developer's principle, 19/10/2026): a purchase made on the 27th is a BUY dated the 27th, whenever its cash moves. Why: the movement is recorded when it happens, not when the systems process it: in between the money is already gone and cannot be used, so hiding it would be wrong (the developer, 28/10/2026). No exception for a subscription during a placement or an IPO: the order of 17/02 is dated 17/02 even when the issue and the cash debit come on 25/02; LibreFolio shows the position at cost and the cash already gone in between, which is what happened. The report's other dates only tell whether the row is stable and booked, read from the columns the report has:
    • a status column, when there is one, decides; what it says follows the next rule (reserved, cancelled or pending are known; a word the plugin does not know is unknown);
    • otherwise a value or settlement date after the server's today (server_today() in backend/app/utils/datetime_utils.py, never the browser's date) marks a provisional row: Fineco, notice fineco_not_yet_settled (Fineco notes);
    • a report that covers a known period compares with its end instead: Danske Bank, notice excluded_not_yet_settled, for the custody trades valued after the cash statement's last day (Finnish notices);
    • with neither, the operation date itself must not be after today.
    • A provisional row is left out whole, with every transaction it would have produced (its fee, its premium), and arrives with the next import. Say so with one severity="info" notice per reason (a code, context.count, the rows as evidence), never a warning: nothing is wrong, the rows are simply not final yet.
    • A report set that compares balances with the bank's, as Danske Bank does, compares them in operation-date terms. A truth on a day adds what is still in flight then: the cash and the quantities of the trades the set imports with an operation date up to that day and a value date after it (_Analysis.in_flight). The set opens on the eve of the oldest operation date of the export, even when the cash statement starts later: the statement's first balance then stands for the opening (Danske Bank → Truth points).
    • The one exception is the Generic CSV: its files are the user's own, so the date column the user maps is the transaction date, whatever it means (trade_date, value_date and settlement_date are all aliases of its date column, Generic CSV).
    • Which date each plugin records (inventory W-B88, 23/10/2026; a column that only the plugin's own tests read is not a date the plugin uses). Every plugin that has both dates in its report records the operation date: Directa (Data operazione), DEGIRO (Datum / Date), InvestEngine (Trade Date/Time), Saxo (Trade Date), Crédit Agricole (Data operazione for securities, Data Op. for cash), Schwab (Date: of 03/01/2025 as of 02/28/2025 the first date counts), Fineco and Danske Bank. Disnat records Date de transaction and falls back to Date de règlement only for a row whose trade date is - (a dividend has no other date). Avanza, Intesa and Rabobank only have a currency column called Valuta, never a value date. The test test_brim_operation_date.py (./dev.py test external brim-operation-date) fixes this per plugin, on rows whose two dates differ: a plugin that switches to the value date fails it.
  • Known rows quietly, unknown rows loudly. Leave a row out only for a reason the plugin can name (lot W-B85, the developer's principle of 19/10/2026):
    • Known and safe to leave out — a blank, header or total row, a reservation, a row the broker marks as cancelled, a duplicate of another row: no notice, at most one backend log line per reason (logger.info(…, reason=…, count=…)). In a report set the row keeps its place in the set's accounting: an excluded outcome with its reason, counted in the summary's reasons and labelled in the wizard by importWizard.reportSet.reason.<reason>. Example: Danske Bank's reservation, a cash row labelled Varaus (reserved, not booked).
    • Unknown or unreadable — a type, status or description the plugin does not recognise; a date, amount or required field it cannot read: leave it out, and say so with one severity="warning" notice per reason (a code, context.count, the rows as evidence) that carries context.report_issue = True. The helper RowSkips builds that notice for you (Rows left out): a plugin collects the rows and returns two shared notices, instead of writing a string warning for each row. The wizard then shows the link open an issue on GitHub under the warning, on every instance, self-hosted or hosted (context keys): the users become the canaries of a broker whose export changes. Example: Danske Bank's excluded_status, the rows whose Tila is neither executed nor booked.
    • Never silently leave out a row that may carry an economic effect (a split, a fee, a tax, a currency conversion) unless the plugin knows that is safe: a row it cannot import is unknown. A row the plugin reads but only in part (Trade Republic's fee and tax columns, not imported) is unknown too: list it.
    • A stable plugin follows the rule: it uses RowSkips, or its own codes with context.report_issue.
    • A plugin in beta may not yet. The plugins the lot W-B86 did not reach (the pending set of its contract test: the beta plugins, Intesa, the Generic CSV) may still write one plain string per skipped row (a legacy warning, no link): with no reliable reports there is no way yet to tell the safe rows from the unknown ones (decision of 19/10/2026, confirmed 22/10). It is a rule, not a lot: leaving the beta means adopting RowSkips (or own codes with report_issue), in the same change that removes the Beta label. The contract test says what to do: take the plugin out of ROW_SKIPS_PENDING, list it in ROW_SKIPS_BY_PLUGIN with an unknown and an unreadable row, bump plugin_version. Fineco did it when it left the beta (W-B92, version 1.5.0); the plugins that already use the helper are in Rows left out.
    • The provisional rows of The operation date, and only settled rows are neither: they keep their info note.
    • report_issue also serves a plugin in beta that imports a row but doubts its own reading, on an info note: Fineco's fineco_incomplete_rows imports the rows missing a required number and asks the user to open an issue if the file is right.

docs.title: 🔢 Decimal places
docs.text:
Every figure a plugin emits must fit its transactions column (C-97; the types are in Decimal Columns): a quantity keeps 10 decimal places, a cash amount 6, a per-unit cost_basis_override 12 — the scale of the prices — and any of them at most 15 significant digits. A cost_basis_override is also never negative (0 for a gift or the new shares of a split): below 0, the batch refuses its row when the user saves it (costBasisNegative, J-60, see Cost basis sign).

  • Read from the file: never rounded. A figure the report states goes in as written, under the verbatim rule above. Over a limit, neither the plugin nor the import rounds it: the batch refuses its row when the user saves it (decimalPlacesExceeded or significantDigitsExceeded, with the maximum; decision D2, see Decimal limits).
  • Computed by the plugin: rounded, explicitly. A figure the plugin derives can have any number of decimals: a per-unit cost as a total divided by the quantity (1000 / 3), a bond price divided by 100. Round it to its column where it is computed, with the one helper round_computed_value(value, model, column_name) (backend/app/db/precision.py): ROUND_HALF_EVEN to the scale of the model's column, then to 15 significant digits on a RealDecimal column (decision D6). On such a column the rounding always brings the result within the decimal places and the significant digits, but not within the third limit, the digits before the decimal point (15 for a quantity and a cash amount, decision N63; 12 for a per-unit cost), which no rounding brings back: the confirmation refuses a value past them with integerDigitsExceeded. broker_intesa/plugin.py calls it on the patrimonio seed's per-unit cost, broker_credit_agricole/plugin.py on the per-unit cost of a bond received by succession, its price divided by 100.
  • An exponent past ±100: refused while parsing. Currency itself refuses an amount whose exponent (Decimal.adjusted()) is outside ±100, whoever builds it (check_decimal_exponent() in backend/app/schemas/common.py, R13-SEC7-3): a plugin that builds such a Currency fails while it parses the file (pydantic's ValidationError, a ValueError), not at confirmation. No real report comes near it: no column takes more than 24 digits before the decimal point, or 12 after.

docs.title: ✅ Required (Abstract)
docs.text:
Method Signature Description provider_code @property → str Unique identifier, and the name of the plugin's folder (e.g., "broker_directa"). Must return a string literal — see below provider_name @property → str Display name, in English (e.g., "Directa CSV"); the UI shows the value of brimPlugins.<code>.name, in the user's language — see Register the name and description description @property → str Brief description for the UI, in English; the UI shows the value of brimPlugins.<code>.description can_parse(file_path) → bool Quick check if this plugin can parse the file (check extension, header row) parse(file_path, broker_id) → BRIMParseOutput Full parsing — returns structured BRIMParseOutput object containing transactions, warnings, and extracted asset info

provider_code must return a string literal

Write return "broker_my_bank" — never a module constant (return PROVIDER_CODE) or an expression. Two tools read the code from the source, without importing the module:

  • the R13 test in frontend/src/lib/components/ui/select/optionFilter.test.ts (run by ./dev.py test front-utility core-unit) scrapes every broker_*/plugin.py for what provider_code, provider_name and description return, and fails on anything but string literals (adjacent literals and a parenthesised run of literals are accepted; an f-string, a name, a call or a + are not);
  • the test runner's _PROVIDER_CODE_RE in scripts/test_runner/_backend_external.py builds the list of BRIM codes shown in the --providers / --exclude-providers help: a plugin it cannot read is missing from that list (the filter itself still works, because the option has no fixed choices).

Danske Bank once returned a constant: the R13 suite failed as a whole, and the runner's help listed one BRIM plugin too few. provider_name and description follow the same rule, because the R13 test reads them the same way.

docs.title: 🔧 Optional (Override)
docs.text: Method Default Description supported_extensions ['.csv'] Accepted file extensions detection_priority 100 Auto-detection priority (higher = checked first). Use 0-49 for generic plugins. cannot_parse_reason(file_path) None Why can_parse refuses a file, in one short sentence the user can act on — appended to the parse guard's 400. See Saying why a file is refused cannot_parse_detail(file_path) wraps cannot_parse_reason, no code The same refusal as a BRIMRefusal, with a stable code the frontend translates and its context — asked by the import wizard right after an upload. See Saying why with a code icon_url None Broker favicon URL for the UI (see Favicons) docs_url None Link to a user-facing MkDocs page. Leave None if no page exists (avoids dead links). plugin_version "1.0.0" Semver of the parsing logic — bump it whenever output for the same input changes test_file_pattern None Single filename substring used by the test suite to map a sample → this plugin test_file_patterns derived from test_file_pattern List of filename substrings when one plugin owns several export formats (e.g. ["revolut-invest", "revolut-crypto"]) report_roles (and the rest of the report-set contract) [] Non-empty turns the plugin into a report-set plugin: see Multi-report plugins generate_static_url(path) — Helper to build /api/v1/uploads/plugin/brim/{path}

docs.title: 🗣️ Saying why a file is refused
docs.text:
cannot_parse_reason(file_path) -> Optional[str] is a concrete method of BRIMProvider, not an abstract one: it returns None by default, so a plugin written without it stays valid. Override it when your can_parse refuses a file for a cause the user can fix in the file — a missing column, say.

  • When the core asks. In the guard of parse_file (brim_provider.py), after can_parse answered False for the file the parse runs your plugin on. The guard asks about the path it checked last: the relocated one, when a concurrent parse moved the file in the meantime. The default cannot_parse_detail asks it too, when the import wizard checks an upload against the broker's default plugin.
  • What it returns. One short English sentence saying why can_parse refuses the file, with a lowercase start and no final period, because it completes the guard's message; None when there is nothing to add.

  • What the user reads. The guard's Plugin '<name>' cannot parse file '<file name>' gains : <reason>. It names the plugin by its provider_name and the file by the name the user uploaded it with, never by the plugin code or the <file_id><ext> LibreFolio stores it under; a duck-typed plugin without provider_name is named by its code. The API answers 400 with that text, the file goes to failed with it as its error_message, and the wizard's parse-error box shows it after the user's file name:

    export.csv — Plugin 'Generic CSV' cannot parse file 'export.csv': required column 'date' not found in the CSV header

  • Cost and failure. Keep it as cheap as can_parse and never raise. Without a reason — the default None, or no such method at all, since the guard reads it with getattr — the message stays plain. If the method raises anyway, the guard logs the exception and keeps the plain message: still a 400, never a 500.

The Generic CSV is the reference implementation. It checks, in this order, and gives each refusal a code too:

The file cannot_parse_reason answers code and context has an extension other than .csv the Generic CSV reads only .csv files csv_only, with its own plugin_code cannot be read the file could not be read file_unreadable is empty, or starts with an empty row the file has no header row no_header_row has a header row without date, type or both — no alias of HEADER_MAPPINGS matches required column 'date' not found in the CSV header, the same with 'type', or required columns 'date' and 'type' not found in the CSV header missing_columns, with columns (date, type or date, type) and count (1 or 2) has a header row naming both None —

Its can_parse is return self.cannot_parse_reason(file_path) is None, and the sentence is the message of its cannot_parse_detail, so the three can never disagree: build yours the same way when your refusals have causes worth naming. The suite holds every registered plugin to the contract: test_every_plugin_answers_nothing_or_one_sentence, in backend/test_scripts/test_external/test_brim_providers.py (./dev.py test external brim-providers), asks the method about every file of sample_reports/ and about paths with nothing to read, and fails on an exception or on an answer that is neither None nor one sentence (a non-empty single line, lowercase start, no final period).

docs.title: 🏷️ Saying why with a code
docs.text:
cannot_parse_detail(file_path) -> Optional[BRIMRefusal] gives the same refusal as cannot_parse_reason, with a stable code the frontend translates. It is a concrete method of BRIMProvider too: the default wraps cannot_parse_reason without a code (BRIMRefusal(message=reason), or None when there is no reason), so every plugin answers it unchanged. Override it when the user should read your reason in their own language.

BRIMRefusal (backend/app/schemas/brim.py):

Field Type Content code Optional[str] Stable snake_case code (^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$), translated by the frontend as importWizard.parseRefusal.<code>; None when the plugin gives only a sentence message str, not empty The cannot_parse_reason sentence — one short English sentence, lowercase start, no final period: the fallback text context Dict[str, Any] The parameters of the translation, e.g. the plugin that reads the file
  • Same rules as cannot_parse_reason: as cheap as can_parse, None when there is nothing to add, and never raise.

  • One sentence, two methods: message must be what cannot_parse_reason returns. Write the detail and derive the sentence from it, as the Scalable plugins do — the parse guard keeps reading cannot_parse_reason, the plugin check below reads cannot_parse_detail:

    def cannot_parse_detail(self, file_path: Path) -> Optional[BRIMRefusal]:
    return _scalable.refusal(self, file_path, _scalable.BROKER)

def cannot_parse_reason(self, file_path: Path) -> Optional[str]:
    detail = self.cannot_parse_detail(file_path)
    return detail.message if detail else None

The endpoint. GET /api/v1/brokers/import/files/{file_id}/plugin-check?plugin_code=<code> (check_file_plugin in api/v1/brokers.py) asks one plugin about one uploaded file and answers a BRIMPluginCheck: plugin_code, can_parse and refusal.

{
  "plugin_code": "broker_scalable",
  "can_parse": false,
  "refusal": {
    "code": "scalable_deposit_file",
    "message": "this is the export of the Scalable overnight account: read it with the Scalable Capital overnight account plugin",
    "context": {"plugin_code": "broker_scalable_deposit", "plugin_name": "Scalable Capital overnight account"}
  }
}
  • Nothing is parsed, and the file keeps its status. The work is check_file_with_plugin (brim_provider.py), run off the event loop (asyncio.to_thread) because the plugin reads the file.
  • refusal comes only with can_parse: false, and stays null when the plugin has nothing to add. A can_parse that raises counts as false, and a cannot_parse_detail that raises leaves refusal empty: both are logged, never a 500. As in the parse guard, a refusal on a path that a concurrent parse has just moved is asked again on the new path.
  • Access: any user with a role on the file's broker (VIEWER+), the uploader of a file with no broker, and the administrator; 403 otherwise (Who reaches a report file). 404 for an id that is not a UUID, an unknown file, an unknown plugin, or a file whose content is gone.

In the import wizard. Right after an upload, the wizard asks the endpoint about the broker's default import plugin. When that plugin refuses the file, the wizard shows the reason under Notes from the plugin in its wrong-broker prompt, translated as importWizard.parseRefusal.<code>, with context as its parameters, and falls back to the English message when the refusal has no code or the code no translation. A plugin that context names by plugin_code gets its name in the UI language as plugin_name, from its catalogue key: the plugin_name the refusal carries — the named plugin's English provider_name — is only the fallback.

Example: Scalable Capital. One plugin per account, each account in its own LibreFolio broker: broker_scalable reads the broker account, broker_scalable_deposit the overnight account, and both import the shared reader _scalable.py. Each refuses the other account's file and names the plugin that reads it (_scalable.refusal):

code Given by For context scalable_deposit_file broker_scalable the exporter's overnight account file broker_scalable_deposit, Scalable Capital overnight account scalable_broker_file broker_scalable_deposit the exporter's broker account file broker_scalable, Scalable Capital broker scalable_prime_file broker_scalable_deposit Scalable's own CSV (PRIME) broker_scalable, Scalable Capital broker scalable_mixed_file both an exporter file mixing the two accounts empty: the message asks to export the two accounts separately

context names the other plugin, as plugin_code and plugin_name. Any other file gets None: the two plugins give a reason only for Scalable's own exports.

Shared codes. Some causes belong to no broker: the extension, a file that cannot be read, no header row, missing required columns, no movement rows. Their codes are shared: a plugin that refuses a file for one of these causes reuses the code, and its translation, instead of adding its own.

code Given today by context English text csv_only Generic CSV plugin_code of the refusing plugin The {plugin_name} plugin reads only .csv files. file_unreadable Generic CSV, DEGIRO empty The file could not be read. no_header_row Generic CSV empty The file has no header row. missing_columns Generic CSV columns, the names joined by ,; count, an integer that picks the plural Required column(s) {columns} not found in the CSV header. no_movement_rows DEGIRO empty The file has no movement rows.

Example: DEGIRO. broker_degiro reads only the Account Statement exported as CSV. Besides the shared file_unreadable and no_movement_rows, it has two codes of its own, with an empty context: degiro_csv_only, for a file that is not a .csv (the message asks to download the Account Statement as CSV), and degiro_not_account_statement, for a CSV of another layout (12 columns with the ISIN fifth, unnamed amount columns ninth and eleventh, dates as DD-MM-YYYY). Unlike its notices, which keep the language of the file (the tip Warning language follows the input format, below), a refusal is shown in the UI language: a file the plugin refuses has no language it recognised.

Where the translations live. Every code is a key of importWizard.parseRefusal, in the import wizard's sources (frontend/src/lib/i18n/importWizard/{en,it,fr,es}.json), whether it is shared or a plugin's own: a plugin's fragment holds only its brimPlugins.<code> keys (The Ownership Gate). Add one with the i18n tool, which finds the source from the prefix:

./dev.py i18n add "importWizard.parseRefusal.mybroker_xlsx_only" --en "…" --it "…" --fr "…" --es "…"

A message with a count is an ICU plural, and its text must differ between languages (Locale-Sensitive ICU Messages, in the frontend i18n guide). TestGenericCSVRefusesWithACode (test_brim_providers.py) and TestRefusalCodes (test_brim_degiro.py) pin the codes and contexts of the two plugins file by file; defaultPluginCheck.test.ts (./dev.py test front-transaction tx-unit) checks that every code has its key in the four languages.

docs.title: 📮 How a failed parse reaches the wizard
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/brokers/import/files/{file_id}/parse answers a failed parse with 400 and a detail object, never an English sentence the wizard would show as it is (lot W5-5, C-70b):

{"code": "parse_failed", "message": "Parse error: …", "plugin_code": "broker_x", "plugin_name": "Broker X",
 "reason": {"code": "missing_columns", "message": "…", "context": {"columns": "date", "count": 1}}}
  • A BRIMParseError(message, details={"code": …, "context": …}) gives reason from its details (code and context are null and {} when the plugin gave none) and message as the diagnostic Parse error: <message>.
  • The parse guard (can_parse false, BRIMCannotParseError, a ValueError) gives reason from the plugin's cannot_parse_detail; message is the guard's own sentence.
  • Any other ValueError (an unknown plugin) keeps a plain string detail; a missing file is still 404.
  • The file goes to failed with the English text as its stored error_message, as before: it is the diagnostic, not what the user reads.
flowchart LR
    A["Plugin raises<br/>BRIMParseError(message, details={code, context})"] --> B["API: 400 detail<br/>parse_failed {reason: code, context}"]
    A -. "English message" .-> L["logs and error_message<br/>of the failed file"]
    B --> C["Wizard: resolveParseFailureMessage<br/>(parseFailure.ts)"]
    C --> D["frame importWizard.parseFailed"]
    C --> E["reason importWizard.parseRefusal.<code><br/>with context as values"]

The wizard (resolveParseFailureMessage, parseFailure.ts) shows importWizard.parseFailed with the plugin's name and the reason, translated as importWizard.parseRefusal.<code> with the context (the keys of the refusals, and the ones of every BRIMParseError code), else the plugin's own sentence (resolveParseRefusalMessage, defaultPluginCheck.ts). A failure with no reason at all shows importWizard.parseFailedNoReason. The same helper reads the 400 of the two file previews (GET …/files/{file_id}/preview and GET /api/v1/uploads/file/{file_id}/preview): {"code": "preview_unsupported" | "preview_unreadable", "message": "…"}, translated as importWizard.previewFailed.<code>.

docs.title: 📏 The rule: every BRIMParseError carries a code
docs.text:
Since lot W5-6 (backlog E-21) this is mandatory, for every raise BRIMParseError(...) in a plugin (backend/app/services/brim_providers/, shared readers such as _scalable.py included):

  • A code. details={"code": "<code>", ...}: a string constant, or a refusal's code (refused.code, as _scalable.py does for scalable_not_export). A raise without one would show the user an English sentence.
  • A context when the text has placeholders. A dict literal whose keys are exactly the placeholders of the user text ({"file": file_path.name}, {"columns": "date", "count": 1}). plugin_name is the one placeholder you never supply: the wizard adds it.
  • The English message stays the diagnostic. It goes to the logs and to the error_message of the failed file; the user never needs to read it. Write it for the developer who reads the log.

  • The user text lives in importWizard.parseRefusal.<code>, in the four languages. Add it with the i18n tool (the placeholders must be the same names in all four):

    ./dev.py i18n add "importWizard.parseRefusal.<code>" --en "…" --it "…" --fr "…" --es "…"

  • Other details keys stay. Keys such as "file" or "headers" keep sitting beside code and context; they are for diagnostics and are not sent to the wizard.

  • Do not lose the code on the way out. A coded raise inside a try needs except BRIMParseError: raise before any broad except Exception, otherwise the broad handler catches it and re-wraps it in a new BRIMParseError that has the code of the wrapper, not yours (or none).
try:
    rows = self._read_rows(file_path)  # may raise BRIMParseError(…, details={"code": "header_row_not_found", …})
    ...
except BRIMParseError:
    raise
except Exception as e:
    raise BRIMParseError(f"Error parsing file: {e}", details={"code": "file_unreadable", "context": {"error": str(e)}}) from e

Shared codes plugins reuse. Reuse these, with their translations, before adding a code of your own:

code context Cause file_not_found file the path to parse does not exist (the plugin raises it in its except FileNotFoundError) file_unreadable error the file could not be read or decoded header_mismatch none the header row is not the one of this export header_row_not_found layout, expected (both optional) the table's header row was not found in the file missing_columns columns, count required columns are not in the header (count picks the plural) no_valid_transactions none the file holds no valid transactions file_empty none the file is empty no_movement_rows none the file has no movement rows no_header_row none the file has no header row

Plugin-specific codes are prefixed with the plugin's name, so they never collide: danske_* (Danske Bank: the cash, custody and combined layouts), degiro_* (degiro_csv_only, degiro_not_account_statement), intesa_layout_unknown and scalable_* (the Scalable refusals, plus scalable_not_export). The catalogue frontend/src/lib/i18n/importWizard/en.json, under parseRefusal, is the list that is always current.

The tests that guard it. ./dev.py test services brim-parse-error-codes (backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_brim_parse_error_codes.py) reads every plugin file statically (ast), so a new plugin or a new raise is caught without anybody remembering it, and names each offender by file:line:

  • every BRIMParseError has a code (and a context literal has string-constant keys);
  • a coded raise is not swallowed: a broad except Exception after it in the same try must be preceded by an except BRIMParseError that re-raises;
  • every code has a text in the four languages, with the same placeholders, and the placeholders are all supplied by the context of the raise sites of that code.

docs.title: 🧮 The gap-fix 409 is translated the same way
docs.text: POST /brokers/import/gap-fix (below) refuses with 409 {code: "ledger_unreadable", message, reason: "values" | "currency_codes", params} when LibreFolio's side of the comparison cannot be computed (BRIMLedgerUnreadable, _set_error_detail in api/v1/brokers.py). The wizard shows it through resolveGapFixFailureMessage (parseFailure.ts) as importWizard.reportSet.gapFix.ledgerUnreadable.<reason> with params (values: count; currency_codes: codes and more). message stays English, the fallback when the key or the reason is missing; every other set error still shows its message.

docs.title: 🧰 Base-class helpers you should use
docs.text:
Defined on BRIMProvider — call these instead of re-implementing:

Helper Use it in What it does self._read_file_head(file_path, num_lines=15) can_parse Reads the first N lines trying TEXT_ENCODINGS (module constant in brim_provider.py) in order: UTF-8 (with or without BOM), then Windows-1252, then Latin-1, which always decodes self.detect_csv_delimiter(file_path) parse Sniffs the delimiter (, ; \t) via csv.Sniffer with a char-count fallback; reads the head with the same TEXT_ENCODINGS fallback self._open_text(file_path, newline=None) parse (and can_parse when you must read the header with csv) Drop-in replacement for open(...): an in-memory text stream decoded with TEXT_ENCODINGS; newline="" keeps line endings for csv self._create_transaction(row_num, transactions, validation_issues, context, **tx_fields) parse Builds a TXCreateItem, appends on success, or records structured BRIMValidationIssues on ValidationError: each with the error's code and message, the field of a field's error (a packed business rule's sub-errors name none), and params by the batch's rule, shared in backend/app/utils/pydantic_errors.py (error_params(), loc_to_field(); Per-type rules): every error's plain context, a business rule's {type} as a field's {max_length: 500}, and null when the context is not plain data (a value_error) or there is none (W-B70). Never call TXCreateItem(...) directly.

docs.title: 💻 Implementation Example
docs.text:
# backend/app/services/brim_providers/broker_mybroker/plugin.py

from pathlib import Path
from backend.app.services.brim.registry import BRIMProviderRegistry
from backend.app.services.brim.brim_provider import BRIMProvider
from backend.app.services.provider_registry import register_provider
from backend.app.schemas.brim import BRIMExtractedAssetInfo, BRIMParseOutput
from backend.app.schemas.transactions.transactions import TXCreateItem

@register_provider(BRIMProviderRegistry)
class MyBrokerProvider(BRIMProvider):

    @property
    def provider_code(self) -> str:
        return "broker_mybroker"

    @property
    def provider_name(self) -> str:
        return "My Broker (CSV)"

    @property
    def description(self) -> str:
        return "Import transactions from My Broker CSV exports"

    def can_parse(self, file_path: Path) -> bool:
        """Quick check: read first lines and look for known header."""
        content = self._read_file_head(file_path, num_lines=5)
        return "Date;Operation;ISIN;Amount" in content

    def parse(self, file_path: Path, broker_id: int) -> BRIMParseOutput:
        """Parse the CSV and return transactions in a BRIMParseOutput envelope."""
        transactions = []
        warnings = []
        extracted_assets = {}

        # ... your parsing logic ...

        return BRIMParseOutput(
            transactions=transactions,
            warnings=warnings,
            extracted_assets={
                fake_id: BRIMExtractedAssetInfo(
                    extracted_symbol=info["extracted_symbol"],
                    extracted_isin=info["extracted_isin"],
                    extracted_name=info["extracted_name"],
                )
                for fake_id, info in extracted_assets.items()
            }
        )

docs.title: 🔍 Auto-Discovery
docs.text:
A plugin is a folder named after its provider_code — here brim_providers/broker_mybroker/:

backend/app/services/brim_providers/
├── _brim_io.py, _brim_output.py, _scalable.py   ← helpers shared by the plugins
├── static/                                      ← icons, served under /api/v1/uploads/plugin/brim/…
├── sample_reports/                              ← every plugin's sample exports (see below)
└── broker_mybroker/
    ├── __init__.py   ← its docstring and nothing else: """BRIM import plugin ``broker_mybroker``: …"""
    ├── plugin.py     ← the code above
    └── i18n/         ← en.json, it.json, fr.json, es.json: its name and description (see below)

Restart the app: the BRIMProviderRegistry finds the folder, loads plugin.py as backend.app.services.brim_providers.broker_mybroker.plugin, and registers the class. The plugin will appear in the ImportPluginSelect dropdown, under its English provider_name until it has its catalogue keys. How discovery reads a folder, and the gate that keeps every plugin in one, are in Plugin Folder Layout.

  • The folder is the code. Name the folder exactly as provider_code returns: the UI reads the plugin's texts under brimPlugins.<code>, the fragment that holds them is the folder's, and ./dev.py test utils gate-plugin-i18n-ownership fails on a BRIM plugin whose code is not its folder's name. Keep the broker_ prefix: the encoding test above and the R13 test read only broker_*/ folders.
  • A name that starts with an underscore is not a plugin: auto_discover skips it (provider_registry.py). That is where code shared by several plugins lives, at the family root — _brim_io.py and _brim_output.py for any plugin, _scalable.py for the two Scalable Capital plugins, whose plugin.py files hold only their properties (the string literals R13 reads among them) and calls to it. A helper only your plugin uses goes in its folder, as _*.py beside plugin.py.
  • Importing the plugin starts nothing: no thread, no process and no connection at module level, in plugin.py or in a helper it imports. Discovery also runs inside the BRIM parse pool's forkserver, and every parse worker is a fork of it (Preload and warm-up): a thread there is how deadlocks start, and the single-thread guard of ./dev.py test services brim-parse-pool fails when it finds one; a process or a connection would be inherited by every worker.
  • Import and patch the plugin's names from its plugin module, backend.app.services.brim_providers.broker_mybroker.plugin: the package re-exports nothing, so a test that patches the package fails (Importing and Patching a Plugin).

docs.title: 🧭 Real-world reference plugins
docs.text:
Copy the structure of an existing, well-tested plugin rather than starting from scratch:

File Best example of backend/app/services/brim_providers/broker_directa/plugin.py Equity/ETF, index-based columns, Italian types, ISIN grouping, tax/fee linking backend/app/services/brim_providers/broker_generic_csv/plugin.py Column auto-detection, locale-aware number parsing backend/app/services/brim_providers/broker_coinbase/plugin.py Crypto assets (symbol, no ISIN), staking as ADJUSTMENT, separate fee tx backend/app/services/brim_providers/broker_revolut/plugin.py One plugin, two formats (invest + crypto) via header detection backend/app/services/brim_providers/broker_intesa/plugin.py CSV/XLSX, two layouts in one plugin; patrimonio snapshot → liquidity DEPOSIT when present + per-holding ADJUSTMENT seed with per-unit cost_basis_override backend/app/services/brim_providers/broker_credit_agricole/plugin.py Richest wizard integration and the second report set (securities + account exports, each in CSV or XLSX): 4-tier causale registry, evidence tables, info notices, blocking and splitting field todos — read it before designing any field_todos. Also: rule M with most_rows, pairing on the value date, balances that open the cash and turn a hole into a correction, par-100 bond maturity split, succession rows as cashless ADJUSTMENT — see Multi-report plugins backend/app/services/brim_providers/broker_saxo/plugin.py Mixed trade/cash rows, verb-in-text events, localized verbs backend/app/services/brim_providers/broker_danske_bank/plugin.py Report set (custody XLSX + cash CSV): roles, a pure combine with pairing, zones and truth points on segments, the parse of its combined file, Finnish notices — see Multi-report plugins backend/app/services/brim_providers/broker_degiro/plugin.py One layout in many languages: the Account Statement read by column position, the notice language picked from the header (_detect_language), linked FX_CONVERSION pairs (see Linked pairs), and its orders list (the Transactions export) claimed and answered with one notice instead of transactions (the rule's extension in Flow)

docs.title: ➕➖ Sign conventions (enforced by the test suite)
docs.text:
TransactionType (in backend/app/db/models.py) fixes the sign of quantity and cash amount. test_all_transactions_are_schema_valid fails the plugin if any emitted transaction breaks these rules, so flip source signs as needed:

Type quantity cash amount asset BUY > 0 < 0 required SELL < 0 > 0 required DIVIDEND = 0 > 0 required INTEREST = 0 > 0 optional DEPOSIT = 0 > 0 none WITHDRAWAL = 0 < 0 none FEE = 0 < 0 optional TAX = 0 < 0 optional ADJUSTMENT / TRANSFER +/- must be None optional
  • DIVIDEND/INTEREST carry no quantity — set quantity=0 and discard any token amount with a warning (see coinbase).
  • Crypto — the fiat leg decides the type. If a row settles in fiat (your account currency) use a cash type: buy crypto with fiat → BUY, sell for fiat → SELL, a reward paid out in fiat → INTEREST, a stock payout → DIVIDEND, plain cash in/out → DEPOSIT/WITHDRAWAL. If a row has no fiat leg — staking/airdrop paid in coins, a crypto↔crypto trade, an on-chain transfer in/out, or a crypto-denominated fee — model it as a cashless ADJUSTMENT (quantity +/-, cash=None) so the position still updates. This is what keeps every crypto row schema-valid, because ADJUSTMENT forbids a cash amount. Reference: broker_bitvavo/plugin.py, broker_cointracking/plugin.py, broker_delta/plugin.py, broker_cryptocom/plugin.py (note cryptocom emits INTEREST for fiat-valued rewards but a cashless ADJUSTMENT for coin-only rewards).
  • Prefer skipping a row with a notice (RowSkips, Rows left out) over emitting a schema-invalid transaction.

Warning language follows the input format

A plugin's user-facing warnings (and any BRIMAssetNotice.reason) should be written in the language of the export it parses. For a single-nation broker whose report is published in only one language — e.g. Crédit Agricole, Directa and Intesa Sanpaolo (Italian), Danske Bank (Finnish) — emit the warnings in that language so they match the report the user is reading. Fineco is still an exception: it reads only the Italian export, but its one plain warning (No valid transactions found in file) is in English; its rows left out go to the two shared notices of RowSkips (below), and its two info notes, fineco_not_yet_settled and fineco_incomplete_rows, are in Italian. The two shared notices of RowSkips are the exception to the rule: the wizard words them in the user's language, and only the Reason column of their evidence is the plugin's text. When a broker ships differently localized export layouts (a UK vs. IT Fineco file, a non-Italian Crédit Agricole entity), detect the format and emit each variant's warnings in its own language. Code, comments and docstrings stay in English.

A broker can also ship one layout in many languages: DEGIRO's Account Statement has the same twelve columns in every language, so the layout cannot tell the language, but the header can. broker_degiro/plugin.py (_detect_language) counts, for each language, how many of the file's named columns are among that language's header names (_HEADER_WORDS; ISIN and FX, the same everywhere, do not count) and picks the best language only with at least three matches and no tie (_MIN_LANGUAGE_MATCHES). A word two languages share decides nothing on its own — Datum is Dutch and German — and any other header gets English. The language chooses the messages only (_MESSAGES: English, Dutch, German, French, Spanish): rows are classified with the words of every language, because one DEGIRO file can mix them.

The user reads the file's language only if the notice code has no importWizard.brimNotice.<code> key. The wizard resolves a notice with resolveBrimNoticeMessage (frontend/src/lib/features/transactions/resolveBrimNotice.ts): a key, when it exists, replaces the plugin's message with the text in the UI language; without one, the plugin's message is shown as written. The degiro_* codes have no key on purpose, and test_no_i18n_key_overrides_the_language_of_the_file (test_brim_degiro.py) fails if one is added.

Field todos follow the same rule, keyed by their reason_code under the same namespace and resolved by resolveBrimTodoMessage (same file), wherever the wizard and the bulk editor list them. A todo is worth a key only when its message has no file language to honour, like the Generic CSV's corporate_action; every other todo keeps the file's language on purpose.

The comment under a notice's evidence table follows the notices' contract too, in its own namespace: importWizard.brimEvidence.<code> — the notice's code, with its context as values — replaces the evidence's comment when the key exists (resolveBrimEvidenceComment, in resolveBrimNotice.ts too, called by BrimNoticeList.svelte). There is one key per notice, so a notice with several commented tables shows the same text under each; and a key only replaces: a table without a comment stays without. The caption needs no key: an empty title gets the wizard's own, importWizard.evidenceRowsTitle (Source rows, Righe del file), where the table folds behind its caption — the confirmation modal; the parse-detail modal shows such a table without a caption. The Scalable plugins write in English, so they leave title empty and give each of their twelve notice codes both keys: the user reads the whole notice — message, caption and comment — in the UI language. TestWhatTheWizardWords (test_brim_scalable.py, ./dev.py test external brim-scalable) holds them to it: both keys for every code in the four catalogues, and no title on the samples' evidence tables. A plugin that writes in its file's language gives its evidence no key either.

cost_basis_override is PER-UNIT, never a total

When a plugin freezes an inherited cost basis (WAC) on a TRANSFER/ADJUSTMENT seed — e.g. an opening patrimonio snapshot, or a TRANSFER_IN — the value you put in cost_basis_override (and its cost_basis_currency) must be the cost per single unit, not the position's total countervalue. The portfolio engine and the lot analysis both multiply it by quantity to reconstruct the total cost basis, so a total slipped in here is silently multiplied again and blows the cost basis up by a factor of quantity.

If your source only reports a total (e.g. Intesa's "Controvalore di carico fiscale €"), divide it by the quantity first, and round the quotient to the column (see Decimal places):

unit_cost = round_computed_value(total_cost / qty, Transaction, "cost_basis_override")
cost_basis_override = Currency(code="EUR", amount=unit_cost)

Bond nominal note: for bonds quantity is the face value (e.g. 50000) and the seed per-unit cost lands near 1.0 — that is correct, the engine handles the /100 quote scaling elsewhere. Canonical example: broker_intesa/plugin.py (patrimonio seed).

A plugin sets a cost basis on these incoming seeds only: on any other row — a BUY, a cash row, a TRANSFER's giving leg — _create_transaction() refuses the row, a costBasisNotAllowed validation issue instead of a transaction (rule 12b, W-B72, or rule 12's costBasisModeIncompatible when the row names a cost_basis_mode; an ADJUSTMENT taking units out is refused the same way, since it has no value: see Per-type rules).

Matured-bond redemption: close at par, surplus → INTEREST

A bond is redeemed at par (100) at maturity. When the bank credits more than par (e.g. a BTP Italia premio fedeltà or a FOI inflation revaluation), that surplus is reddito di capitale — the same nature as a coupon — and must be booked as a separate INTEREST leg, not folded into the sale price. Folding it in would inflate the realised gain and leave a residual position when ctv/price ≠ the true nominal.

Working assumption (document it on the plugin's own page): a maturity/redemption row is a bond quoted at par 100, so anything above 100 is interest. A plugin whose maturity causale is bond-specific (e.g. Crédit Agricole's TITOLI SCADUTI) can apply this unconditionally; a plugin whose causale is generic (e.g. Fineco's Rimborso, which also covers equities) must still gate on io.looks_like_bond(name). Generalise only when a real counter-example appears.

The nominal to redeem comes from the held position (the BUY / succession / seed rows), never from the maturity row itself (whose quantity is often 0). Use the shared helper:

from backend.app.services.brim_providers import _brim_io as io

if ctv is not None:                       # (+ io.looks_like_bond(name) if the causale is generic)
    model = io.model_bond_maturity(ctv=ctv, price=price, held_qty=held or None)
    sell_qty  = -model.nominal            # SELL closes the nominal at par, e.g. -30000
    sell_cash = model.principal_cash      # e.g. 30000.00 (nominal × par/100)
    if model.surplus_cash > 0:            # surplus over par → INTEREST income
        emit_interest(cash=model.surplus_cash)   # e.g. 105.00
  • held_qty > 0 → source == "position": exact close, no verify flag. This is the normal case — the nominal lives in the position, so there is nothing for the user to check. If the file is not chronologically ordered, pre-compute the position in a first pass (see broker_credit_agricole/plugin.py).
  • no position → source == "derived": the nominal is inferred from ctv/price (a best effort, imprecise because the quoted price embeds the premium — e.g. 30105/100.40 = 29985 vs a true 30000). This happens on a partial download (a "last 3 months" export where the buy legs are missing). Attach a warning BRIMFieldTodo (reason_code="derived_quantity") so the user verifies the nominal — the plugin sees only the file, so it cannot confirm the close against the position already stored in LibreFolio (that reconciliation happens in the portfolio engine at compute time).
  • Cash-only maturity in a bank/account export → nominal from a same-day companion row (still in-file). Some exports carry the redemption only as a cash row with no securities position and no reliable price (e.g. Crédit Agricole's account TITOLI SCADUTI O ESTRATTI, whose truncated securities export had already dropped the opening BUY). Such a row has just the total cash, so it cannot split par vs premium on its own. Recover the nominal from another row in the same file: the final coupon paid on the same date states the security's ISIN + NOMINALE. Match the two by security code in a first pass, then feed that nominal as held_qty to model_bond_maturity (source == "position"). This never touches the database — a plugin only ever reads its own file. If no same-day companion row identifies the security, book the whole redemption as a SELL for the full cash (everything as sold, no premium split) plus a warning — never a plain cash DEPOSIT, so the proceeds reduce a position instead of inflating paid-in capital (consistent with the securities-export fallback). With no held position and no reported price, assume a par (100) redemption so the derived nominal equals the cash (SELL with quantity < 0, flagged for the user to verify). See broker_credit_agricole/plugin.py (_parse_account_movements, income_identity_by_date, _ACCT_MATURITY_CAUSALI).
  • A price at or below par yields surplus_cash == 0 → emit a single plain SELL (pass-through); don't invent negative income.
  • Keep the plugin's usual cash model: if BUYs get a balancing DEPOSIT and SELLs a WITHDRAWAL, the par principal nets to zero and only the INTEREST surplus adds cash.

Reference plugins: broker_credit_agricole/plugin.py (TITOLI SCADUTI in the securities export with the position pre-computed from succession legs, and the account cash-only TITOLI SCADUTI O ESTRATTI with the nominal recovered from the same-day coupon) and broker_fineco/plugin.py (Rimborso above par, nominal from the row).

docs.title: 🔗 Linked pairs from a plugin
docs.text:
A currency conversion is two transactions that only exist together: the cash that leaves one currency and the cash that arrives in another. A plugin emits both legs as FX_CONVERSION and gives them the same link_uuid; the batch turns the shared id into reciprocal related_transaction_ids and never stores the id itself (see Transaction Service → Linked Pairs). broker_degiro/plugin.py is the first plugin to emit pairs (_pair_fx_legs, _fx_pair): Swissquote lists its conversion legs in the shared notice rows_not_recognized (it does not import them yet), and the Generic CSV refuses the paired types.

What the batch accepts — resolve_create_links in batch_creates.py, with _validate_linked_pair and _validate_pair_description_tags in validation.py (all in backend/app/services/transactions/):

  • exactly two creates per link_uuid: a leg alone, or a third one, is linkUuidPairCount;
  • the same type on both legs (pairTypeMismatch);
  • two distinct brokers for a TRANSFER or a CASH_TRANSFER (pairSameBroker); an FX_CONVERSION must stay on one (pairBrokerMismatch). Every row a plugin emits carries the one target broker_id that parse() receives, so a transfer pair saved as the plugin emitted it is refused at this check, while an FX_CONVERSION pair saved the same way passes it;
  • for a TRANSFER, one asset on both legs (pairAssetMismatch) and exactly opposite quantities (pairQuantityMismatch, compared as Decimal, with no tolerance): what leaves one broker arrives at the other, so both legs carry the same quantity, rounded alike, with opposite signs;
  • an identical description (pairDescriptionMismatch) and identical tags (pairTagsMismatch). Brokers word the two legs differently, so build one description for both: DEGIRO keeps the text when both legs read the same, and joins the two otherwise (FX Credit / FX Debit);
  • each leg valid on its own: an FX_CONVERSION has quantity = 0, a non-zero cash amount in its own currency, and no asset.

The link_uuid is deterministic. test_parse_is_idempotent compares two parses of each sample, and test_sample_parses_identically_when_saved_as_windows_1252 compares a non-ASCII sample with its Windows-1252 copy: a uuid4() fails the first, an id hashed from the file's bytes fails the second. DEGIRO derives it with uuid5 from a SHA-256 of the decoded rows of the whole file and the line numbers of the two legs, so the same statement always gives the same ids, whatever its encoding, and two statements that differ give different ones.

Recognise the legs without the rate. No forex system still holds: the report's exchange rate neither converts nor matches anything. DEGIRO only asks whether a row's FX cell is filled — that makes the row a leg — and finds its partner by structure: the same order (same Order Id, or the same date and time when there is none), another currency, the opposite sign, and the adjacent row when several qualify. A leg whose partner is missing or ambiguous is listed in a notice (degiro_unpaired_fx) and not imported: never a guessed pair, and never a lone leg, which the batch would reject.

In the import wizard a pair is one row of the review step: the leg that pays (the negative amount; the first one the plugin emitted when both legs have the same sign), with the leg that receives shown as its To and the rate the two amounts imply — computed from the amounts, not read from the report. The receiving leg is not a row of its own (pairs.hidden, step4Rows): the row's cash cell (data-testid="import-tx-pair-cash") holds a From line and a To line in the bulk editor's markup (renderFromToHtml mirrors renderDualHtml of TransactionBulkModal.svelte), then a chip such as USD → EUR @ 0.8554 (renderImpliedRateHtml: |to| / |from| through computeFxConversionInfo). Selecting the row selects both legs (setPairSelected: its tick shows the pair as selected only when both legs are, and select all, deselect all and select visible move both legs too), only complete pairs reach the bulk editor, and each pair reaches it with a fresh link_uuid, the same for both legs (frontend/src/lib/features/transactions/import/importPairs.ts, and pairCellHtml.ts beside it for the cell): the plugin's ids repeat whenever the same statement is parsed again, so two uploads of one statement would share them. The counters and the Import {n} transactions button count transactions, not rows, so a pair counts as two (step4SelectedCount and step4TotalCount, over step4LegRows): the English sample shows 17 transactions in 15 rows.

docs.title: 📡 Talking to the import wizard
docs.text:
A plugin does not only produce transactions. It produces what it could not do, and that is what drives the wizard's UI. There are four output channels, and picking the right one is the single most important design decision in a plugin:

Channel Field on BRIMParseOutput The plugin is saying Where it shows Transactions transactions "I read this row" Review table Validation issues validation_issues "I read this row and the schema refused it" Parse-detail modal, red Notices warnings "Something about the file you should know", the rows it left out included Parse-detail modal + confirmation modal Field todos field_todos "I booked this row but a specific field is a guess" Correction step, before the duplicate check

A notice is not a todo

The line is not severity, it is actionability. If the user can fix it on one row, it is a BRIMFieldTodo; if it is a statement about the file as a whole, it is a BRIMNotice. Putting a fixable problem in warnings sends the user to a modal that offers no way to fix it, and showing the same finding in both channels teaches them to skip both. Crédit Agricole has a test asserting a given finding appears in exactly one.

docs.title: 🔔 BRIMNotice — something about the file
docs.text:
warnings.append(
    BRIMNotice(
        severity="info",                       # "info" (blue) | "warning" (amber)
        code="ca_unknown_causale",             # machine-readable, i18n-stable
        message="12 righe con 3 causali non previste …",   # report's language
        context={"causali": [...], "row_count": 12},
        evidence=[...],                        # see below
    )
)
  • severity="info" — the plugin did something correct and non-obvious: explain it. An unknown transaction code booked by sign, a succession row turned into a cashless ADJUSTMENT, rows left for the next import because they have not settled yet (the rule The operation date, and only settled rows, under Import philosophy). Blue, still surfaced in the confirmation modal.
  • severity="warning" — the plugin had to fall back or guess: look at it. Also a row left out because the plugin does not know it, with context.report_issue (the rule Known rows quietly, unknown rows loudly, under Import philosophy; the helper RowSkips writes these notices, see Rows left out). A row the plugin knows it may leave out gets no notice at all.
  • A bare str still works (coerced to severity="warning", code="legacy"), but new code should never use it: the code is what lets the frontend and the tests address the notice.

docs.title: 🔎 BRIMEvidence — show the row, do not just describe it
docs.text:
Every notice and every todo can carry evidence tables. This is what turns "row 282 looks bundled" into something the user can check without opening the file:

BRIMEvidence(
    title="Riga di acquisto",                 # short caption
    headers=["Data Op.", "Causale", "Descrizione", "Importo"],
    rows=[["28/07/2025", "COMPRAVENDITA …", "NOTA INF. ACQ. TIT:BTP …", "-46603.73"]],
    row_numbers=[282],                        # 1-based source line, per row
    comment="L'importo di questa riga è un totale: comprende …",
)
  • row_numbers is not decoration. It renders a "row N in the file" button that opens the file preview scrolled to that line, so the user sees the neighbours too. Omit it and the evidence becomes an unverifiable claim.
  • Attach evidence at the moment the plugin gives up — that is the only moment the source row is still in hand. Re-reading the preview later costs a fetch and misaligns indexes if the preview paginates.
  • comment is the reasoning, the message is the headline. The collapsed row in the correction list is read while scrolling twenty others: keep it to one line. Everything the plugin looked at, found and concluded belongs in comment, which is read only by someone who opened the row.
  • Several tables are allowed: Crédit Agricole shows the purchase row and the coupon row that supplied the nominal, each with its own comment.
  • title may be empty. The field is required, but title="" lets the wizard show its own caption, translated (Source rows), where the table folds behind it: the Scalable plugins, whose notices are translated, leave it empty rather than write an English caption. The comment of a notice's table can be translated by code too — both are explained in the tip Warning language follows the input format, under Sign conventions.

docs.title: 🚮 Rows left out: RowSkips
docs.text:
The helper of the rule Known rows quietly, unknown rows loudly (lot W-B86), in the section ROWS LEFT OUT of backend/app/services/brim_providers/_brim_io.py (the plugins import that module as io). A plugin collects the rows it cannot import as they come, and returns the notices once at the end:

from backend.app.services.brim_providers import _brim_io as io

skips = io.RowSkips(header_cells)          # or io.RowSkips() and skips.set_headers(reader.fieldnames) later

for line, row in enumerate(rows, start=2):
    if not row_date:
        skips.unreadable(line, row, "invalid date")                    # cannot read it
        continue
    if tx_type is None:
        skips.unknown(line, row, f"unknown type: '{raw_type}'")        # does not recognise it, or does not import it yet
        continue
    if raw_type in KNOWN_NO_EFFECT:                                     # known and safe: nothing is collected
        quiet += 1
        continue
    ...

return BRIMParseOutput(transactions=transactions, warnings=[*warnings, *skips.notices()], ...)
Method The row is Notice code unknown(line, row, reason) a type, status or description the plugin does not recognise, or recognises but does not import yet (a split, a currency conversion, a fee column) rows_not_recognized unreadable(line, row, reason) one whose date, amount, currency or required field cannot be read rows_unreadable
  • row is a list of cells or a csv.DictReader row (read in the order of the headers); line is its 1-based line in the file; reason is the short text of the last column.
  • notices() returns at most two notices, rows_not_recognized first: each is a warning, with context {"count": n, "report_issue": True} and one BRIMEvidence (the file's header, a last column Reason, the rows, their line numbers). A row shorter than the header is padded; a longer one gets numbered headers.
  • The wizard words them once for every plugin: importWizard.brimNotice.<code> and importWizard.brimEvidence.<code>, in the four catalogues (frontend/src/lib/i18n/importWizard/), with {count} as an ICU variable. The message in RowSkips is the English fallback.
  • A known row that is safe to drop is not collected: count it and write one log line at the end (logger.info(…, count=…)), as Revolut and Trading 212 do for Transfer, and Scalable for a cancelled order.
  • A plugin that already has a notice of its own for a case keeps it, with context.report_issue = True (DEGIRO's six degiro_* notices, Crédit Agricole's ca_securities_unknown_causale, ca_unknown_causale and ca_account_invalid_amount, Scalable's scalable_unreadable_rows and scalable_not_imported).
  • Contract test: ./dev.py test external brim-row-skips (backend/test_scripts/test_external/test_brim_row_skips.py). Every registered plugin must be in exactly one of two sets: the plugins that follow the rule (and obey it), or the pending ones, which W-B86 does not cover yet. A new plugin lands in one of them, or the test fails.

docs.title: 🧩 BRIMFieldTodo — one field, one question, one screen
docs.text:
BRIMFieldTodo(
    tx_index=len(transactions) - 1,     # index into transactions[]
    field="asset_id",                   # TXCreateItem field that needs input
    severity="blocker",                 # "blocker" | "warning"
    reason_code="ca_account_trade_unresolved",
    message="Riga 282: acquisto di BTP … — l'importo potrebbe raggruppare più voci.",
    context={...},                      # see the contract below
    evidence=[source_row_evidence(row, offset, comment="…")],
)

field and severity together decide where the row lands, so they are not free-form:

severity field Wizard behaviour blocker one of type, date, quantity, asset_id, cash, cash.amount, cash.code Correction step, "trades" panel. The step cannot be passed until every such row is settled. blocker anything else (e.g. cost_basis_override) Carried on the transaction, but not shown in the correction step — that screen cannot fix it. warning asset_id Correction step, "charges" panel — a fee or an income with no instrument. warning any, with context.split_hint Correction step, "split" panel — see below. warning asset_event_id, reason_code="possible_split" Not in the correction step: it is carried to the Bulk editor, which marks the row «may be a split» and answers it with a SPLIT event (_brim_io.possible_split_todo, Revolut and Trading 212: Possible splits).

A row is filed by its worst todo: a blocker that also carries split_hint lands in the trades panel, and its split zone appears there as soon as the user types the row into a BUY/SELL. That is deliberate — an unresolved trade is a trade too, only a less complete one, and its total is bundled for exactly the same reason.

Why blockers must be duplicate-relevant fields
