Before queueing an item, the executor compares its contract_version, implementation_version, and schema_fingerprint with the live definition: a stale pin returns a per-item version_mismatch without starting a worker, which is a compatibility error rather than a result for the submitted scenario. The child rechecks all four Tool identity fields against its own discovered definition.

success_count and failed_count count platform outcomes, not domain readiness. A valid domain response such as invalid or needs_input can be a platform success. Likewise, a domain's initial-valuation ready status must not be presented as proof of trade feasibility or an optimized plan.

docs.title: 🧯 Error boundaries
docs.text:
Area Platform error codes Lookup and availability unknown_tool, tool_unavailable, version_mismatch, service_unavailable Parameters invalid_parameters, input_limit_exceeded Admission and waiting queue_full, queue_timeout Execution execution_limit, execution_timeout, memory_limit, worker_crashed, execution_failed Output invalid_output, output_limit_exceeded Termination cleanup_failed

A crash, hard timeout, memory-limit breach, invalid output, or failed cleanup is a platform failure. Do not turn it into a domain answer such as “infeasible” or “needs more input.”

Transport failures are distinct from per-item results. The route rejects malformed JSON, duplicate object keys, and nonfinite numbers as invalid requests. It bounds received bytes, sanitizes envelope validation failures, and applies request deadlines. Whole-request errors include HTTP 400 for invalid JSON, 413 for oversized input, and 422 for an invalid envelope. Admission is decided once per batch, before any item task exists (ToolExecutor._admit): a batch that would exceed the batch, process, or per-principal capacity — including a second concurrent batch from the same principal — is refused whole with queue_full, and a closed, non-POSIX, or fully quarantined pool refuses it with service_unavailable. A top-level queue_full execution error is mapped to 429; other raised execution errors and request deadline failures use 503.

Per-item ToolError exposes a code, retryable, and bounded validation issues. The sanitizer omits input values, validator context, URLs, and raw messages. It returns at most 32 issues, each with at most 16 safe path segments; issue_count retains the total issue count.

The platform sets retryable=True only on queue_full, queue_timeout, execution_limit, execution_timeout, version_mismatch, and a service_unavailable raised by the supervisor. Every other platform code — and the service_unavailable of the child's non-POSIX guard, and that of a Tool whose required setting has no value — carries retryable=False; a plugin's own ToolExecutionError keeps the flag it was raised with. Renderers read this flag to decide whether to offer a retry: the PAC planner's ToolErrorPanel.svelte shows Retry only when it is set.

The handler watches for client disconnection and cancels the awaited computation task. The executor propagates cancellation to item tasks and signals owned jobs; tickets and cleanup callbacks govern capacity release. Cancellation alone is not evidence that physical cleanup has completed.

docs.title: 🔬 Process-local diagnostics
docs.text:
ToolDiagnosticsResponse has scope="api_process", an opaque runtime identifier, the effective policy, loaded descriptors, sanitized registration failures, the memory-enforcement capability (capabilities.memory), and a pool snapshot.

Pool fields report availability, active, queued, pending, degraded lanes, completed, and failed counts, plus resources: the memory capacity (workers × memory_limit_bytes) and the memory limits reserved by the jobs the executor still tracks. They describe one API process, not global deployment capacity. The catalogue exposes only coarse unavailable summaries; diagnostics adds safe filenames (<name>/plugin.py for a plugin folder) and bounded failure reasons.

_item_finished increments completed for every tracked item task that reaches a terminal state, including cancellation or an exception. failed is the subset without a platform-success result, not an additional disjoint total. These counters can advance while physical cleanup remains outstanding; completed does not certify process termination or released capacity. Both start at zero when get_tool_executor() lazily creates the process-local executor, on the first Tool request the process serves, and they count the items of every principal: they are neither installation-wide totals nor a per-user history.

Diagnostics must not expose submitted scenarios, results, cookies, raw traces, or logs. It is not a probe, reset, repair, or other mutation interface.

docs.title: 🔤 JSON and generation boundary
docs.text:
wire.py validates values before encoding: string keys, JSON-compatible values, finite numbers, valid Unicode scalars, and bounded nesting. Surrogate code points are rejected rather than replaced.

Encoding produces compact UTF-8 JSON with sorted keys, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False, and compact separators. Limits are measured in encoded bytes during encoding, not characters. Parsing rejects duplicate keys and nonfinite values; decode_json additionally validates the decoded value.

The API's envelope check deliberately excludes heterogeneous parameter contents from its early string validation. This allows per-item parameter validation to retain its own error boundary rather than promoting every invalid parameter string into an envelope error.

Before dispatch, validation must be a gate, not a scenario rewrite. Preserve the original parameter values, text, and explicit choices rather than replacing them with a validator's transformed or default-populated output. Canonical encoding can change whitespace and key order; it must not change the scenario. Inside the child, _validated_input builds the typed model and checks that its operation still matches the original JSON operation.

docs.title: ⚙️ Generation requirements
docs.text:
schema_export.py roots the real registry adapters in a build-only OpenAPI 3.1 document with paths: {}. It emits one manifest entry per (tool_code, contract_version) service identity with the schema fingerprint, componentKey, uiVersion, operation names, and separate validation/serialization schema roots. This is a build artifact, not a runtime schema endpoint.

frontend/scripts/generate-tools-client.mjs validates that manifest, generates strict Zod transport and service codecs, and publishes generated-tools.ts with tool-contract-map.generated.ts as one generation. The literal map is keyed by service code and contract version and points to that service's input/output codecs. implementation_version is intentionally not a renderer or codec key; the client reads it from the live descriptor and pins it separately in every compute request.

Cross-language acceptance must match for valid inputs, valid outputs, and error envelopes:

  • Reject unknown fields in nested models, not only at the envelope boundary.
  • Validate Unicode scalar content before canonical JSON or dispatch.
  • Apply string bounds in Unicode code points, not JavaScript UTF-16 length.
  • Do not send transformed/defaulted validation output in place of the caller's original scenario.
  • Preserve discriminators, correlation identifiers, versions, fingerprints, and exclusive success/error shapes.

Do not maintain a second handwritten I/O contract beside the Pydantic models. Canonical encoding is not evidence of request deduplication: deduplication remains disabled.

docs.title: 🧵 Worker primitives
docs.text:
ToolWorkerJob carries bounded parameter bytes and server-owned identity, deadlines, and limits. It has no principal, database session, or provider handle. Its optional settings field holds the BoundSettings the parent resolved for the user who asks (None for a Tool without fields): plain values only, picklable to the spawn child.

execute_tool_job is a child-only entry point run in an owned spawn process. It rejects invocation outside a multiprocessing child. On POSIX, it creates a fresh session with setsid and sends a ready frame containing execution and process identity. The executor checks the execution identifier, PID, process group, and creation time before sending the start ACK (b"\x00"). Plugin discovery and computation wait for that ACK. On non-POSIX systems, this entry point reports service_unavailable; it is not a portable process-containment implementation.

Once started, the child:

  1. Resolves the definition and verifies the requested versions and fingerprint.
  2. Bounds and decodes input, validates it with the input adapter in strict mode, and verifies the operation.
  3. Constructs the plugin once, binds the job's settings on it when it carries any (bind_settings), and calls synchronous compute, with checkpoints around the execution phases.
  4. Requires a model result, serializes through the output adapter, encodes bounded JSON, and validates the emitted bytes with the output adapter in strict mode.
  5. Checks the hard deadline and cancellation before returning a result frame. Exceptions become sanitized platform failures.

The worker closes its pipe endpoints on exit. A result frame is not a cleanup acknowledgement.

docs.title: 🧹 Descendant cleanup
docs.text:
OwnedProcessTree tracks the multiprocessing root, its fresh process group, and captured descendants. Process identities include PID and creation time; session adoption verifies that the group belongs to the worker and is not the supervisor's own group.

Cleanup observes recursive descendants and group members, requests termination, escalates to a kill if needed, and checks for observed termination within its deadline. Only then does it join and close the root process handle. A False cleanup result retains the handles instead of pretending the job is gone. These methods perform blocking I/O and must run off the event loop.

Plugin-created processes and threads are allowed only within the job's lifetime. No detached or daemonized work may outlive the job. The supervisor must clean up the entire owned subtree after success, error, timeout, abort, and shutdown.

Ownership is not a security sandbox

These POSIX primitives manage the lifetime of packaged plugin work. They do not establish an OS sandbox, filesystem isolation, or permission to run arbitrary untrusted plugins; the per-job memory limit described below caps consumption, it does not isolate memory. Descendant tracking does not make detaching work a supported escape from job ownership.

docs.title: 📏 Supervisor and budgets
docs.text:
ToolExecutor coordinates admission, queueing, absolute deadlines, cancellation, and cleanup for one API process. Its constructor starts no workers. Each physical job has one I/O owner, _run_owned_job, dispatched through asyncio.to_thread; its finally path attempts cleanup even after a successful result.

The executor creates an independent task per batch item and gates execution through a bounded queue of lane tokens. Every item that reaches execution gets a distinct non-daemon spawn process, even for identical inputs; there is no coalescing or cross-user cache. Queue deadlines use the batch's shared admission time, effective operation limits, and the request deadline. The hard job budget includes cold process startup. _job_finished returns a lane and its admission credit only after confirmed cleanup; an unconfirmed outcome quarantines the job instead of silently recycling capacity.

Each item task has an _ItemTicket and a registered done callback. If cancellation occurs before the coroutine starts, or before it owns a physical job, _item_finished still releases its admission credit. Once a job is attached to the ticket, physical cleanup owns that release, preventing a premature or double refund. Queue bookkeeping also returns an acquired lane when no job was started.

Shutdown closes admission, cancels tracked item tasks, signals owned jobs, and waits within the cleanup budget. Jobs with unconfirmed termination remain quarantined. The process-local executor reference is cleared only when its pending count reaches zero. These source paths do not replace runtime verification of cancellation races or descendant cleanup.

The following are the ToolPlatformPolicy defaults declared in backend/app/schemas/tools.py. The process-local executor runs with them: get_tool_executor() builds ToolExecutor() without a policy override. They are limits, not measured throughput or latency guarantees:

Limit or budget Platform default Items per batch 1–4 Worker lanes per API process 2 Pending items per API process 8 Concurrent batches / pending items per principal 1 / 4 Request body / response body 1 MiB / 1,088 KiB (four 256 KiB results plus a 64 KiB envelope reserve) Parameters per item / result per item 128 KiB / 256 KiB JSON nesting depth 32 Compute ingress / shared queue budget 2 s / 5 s Engine budget (one claimed engine window) 30 s Hard job budget, including startup 45 s Cooperative soft budget / output reserve 44 s / 1 s Cleanup / response reserve 5 s / 2 s Server request / client budget 59 s / 65 s Memory limit per job 1 GiB

ToolPlatformPolicy validates its own coherence: the engine budget must fit within the soft deadline, the soft deadline plus the output reserve within the hard deadline, and ingress + queue + hard job + cleanup + response reserve within the request deadline; the client timeout must exceed the request deadline, and a full batch of maximum-size items plus the envelope reserve must fit both the request and the response caps. At the defaults the server bound equals the request deadline exactly (2 + 5 + 45 + 5 + 2 = 59 s).

A ToolOperationPolicy declares its own values. A field the plugin omits takes the model's default — 4 s engine and soft, 5 s hard, 5 s queue, 2 s cleanup, 20 s request, 25 s client, 128 KiB / 256 KiB, and 1 GiB — so an operation that needs longer budgets must declare them. effective_operation (backend/app/services/tools/catalog.py) then clamps each operation to the platform. Every limit becomes the smaller of the two values, the soft deadline is also capped at the hard deadline minus the output reserve, and the engine budget at the soft deadline. A clamped soft deadline that is not positive, or a server bound that no longer fits the clamped request deadline, rejects the definition with invalid_operation_policy, and the whole service leaves the catalogue. The catalogue publishes, and the executor enforces, only the clamped values.

For example, the plan operation of PacAllocatorTool (backend/app/services/tool_plugins/pac_allocator/plugin.py) declares 256 KiB of parameters and 512 KiB of results. The clamp caps them at the platform's 128 KiB and 256 KiB (max_parameter_bytes and max_result_bytes in effective_operation). Its time budgets equal the platform defaults (30 s engine, 44 s soft, 45 s hard, 5 s queue and cleanup, 59 s request, 65 s client), so its server bound has no slack: a request budget one millisecond lower would make the service unavailable.

The catalogue and diagnostics routes declare no request body, so they have no ingress phase (ToolRoute in backend/app/api/v1/tools.py): their 20 s request budget, capped by the platform request_timeout_ms, starts with the request and covers authentication. A compute request opens under the 2 s ingress window, which bounds receiving, decoding, and validating its envelope together with the dependencies resolved with it, authentication included. Its deadline then moves to the batch's request budget: the largest effective request_timeout_ms among its resolvable items (ToolExecutor.batch_request_timeout_ms), or 20 s when none resolves. The frontend Tool client applies the catalogue policy's client_timeout_ms to the compute request (prepareToolRun in frontend/src/lib/features/tools/contracts.ts); it remains a client transport budget, not a throughput or completion guarantee.

Each job also runs under its memory_limit_bytes. On Linux, when the API process's own cgroup-v2 directory is writable and enables the memory controller for its children, every job gets a private child cgroup holding that hard limit (cgroup_v2_hard). Otherwise the supervisor sums the resident memory of the owned process tree while it waits for the worker, at most 50 ms apart (process_tree_observed); a non-POSIX host reports unavailable. A breach ends the item with memory_limit. The mode in use appears in diagnostics under capabilities.memory (backend/app/services/tools/resources.py).

docs.title: 📊 Timing metrics
docs.text:
Per-item metrics are queue_wait_ms, startup_ms, input_validation_ms, compute_ms, output_validation_ms, serialization_ms, execution_ms, cleanup_ms, and total_ms. They are measured monotonic durations in milliseconds, not estimates derived from the requested budgets. An unobserved phase is null, not an invented zero. Once a started job has gone through cleanup, resources.memory adds its enforcement mode, its limit, and the peak observed bytes (null when nothing was observed). An item that ends with worker_crashed also carries worker_exit_code: the worker's own exit status, read before the cleanup that may signal it — an exit code, or the negative number of the signal that ended it (-9 for SIGKILL, as the kernel's out-of-memory killer sends) — and null when the crash was seen while the worker still ran; every other outcome leaves it null. The executor also logs one warning, Tool worker crashed, with the execution id, the tool code, that exit status and the memory figures, never the item's input or output (J-19).

The child measures its validation, computation, and serialization phases. The executor records queue wait from admission, startup through the accepted ready frame, execution from lane allocation until cleanup begins (so execution_ms already contains startup_ms and the child's phases), and cleanup duration. total_ms measures elapsed time from item admission to its recorded outcome, not from HTTP request arrival. For API calls, batch server_processing_ms runs from the start that ToolRoute's bounded handler records, before the request body is read, until every item of the batch has an outcome; response encoding and network transport are outside it. Neither these timings nor result counts are a benchmark or SLA.

Do not sum parallel item durations and label the sum as request latency: their execution windows can overlap. Phase measurements and aggregate fields can overlap too. Browser network round-trip time is a distinct observation, not another name for compute_ms or the batch's server_processing_ms.

The shared ToolExecutionMetrics.svelte (frontend/src/lib/features/tools/components/) renders these fields under Backend timings: batch server_processing_ms and item total_ms first, then queue wait, worker startup, compute, worker execution, and cleanup, with the two validation phases and serialization behind a Detail disclosure. A null renders as the localized No data available label, never as 0 ms, and the caption states that the values are backend measurements excluding network time, that phases can overlap, and that parallel items are not added together. The PAC planner shows it in its result proof panel (ProofPanel.svelte).

docs.title: 🖥️ Frontend and documentation
docs.text:
Frontend compatibility first resolves the exact service code and contract version in the generated contract map, then compares the schema fingerprint, descriptor.ui.component_key, string SemVer descriptor.ui.version, and operation set. The request separately pins the live descriptor.implementation_version; UI version is never inferred from it.

registry.ts accepts only source-owned literal component imports. A registration repeats the service code, contract version, component key, and UI SemVer and must agree with the generated contract before it can bind a catalogue descriptor. Duplicate code/version registrations, cross-tool component-key collisions, missing registrations, and mismatches stay unavailable. A server descriptor never becomes an arbitrary module URL, and incompatibility never falls back to a generic generated financial form.

The compiled registry currently holds one registration: the pac_allocator service at contract version 1.0.0, with component key pac-allocator, UI version 1.0.0, and a lazy import of frontend/src/lib/features/tools/pac-allocator/planner/PacPlannerTool.svelte. A compatible catalogue descriptor without a registration resolves as unavailable with renderer_missing, while its backend service stays listed in the catalogue. When a custom component exists, it owns domain-specific input and result presentation while the backend owns the calculation. A descriptor and schema still do not make a service usable until its generated contract and compiled renderer registration are present and compatible.

resolveToolRenderer returns either a ready binding or one unavailable reason. The hub card (ToolsHub.svelte) and the Tool host (ToolHost.svelte) then show that reason's unavailableMessage (presentation.ts, keys under tools.availability.*) instead of a link or a mounted renderer, so no calculation can start:

Reason Source Cause Message key tool_not_installed inspectToolCompatibility The code is neither in items nor in the unavailable summaries, for example a stale /tools/<tool_code> URL. notInstalled tool_unavailable inspectToolCompatibility The backend lists the code only as an unavailable summary. backendUnavailable contract_not_compiled inspectToolCompatibility No generated contract exists for that code and contract_version. incompatible schema_mismatch inspectToolCompatibility The live schema fingerprint differs from the generated one. incompatible ui_mismatch inspectToolCompatibility ui.kind, ui.component_key, or ui.version differs from the generated contract. incompatible operation_mismatch inspectToolCompatibility The descriptor's operation set differs from the generated one. incompatible renderer_missing Renderer registry The contract is compatible, but no compiled registration exists. rendererMissing renderer_registration_invalid, renderer_collision Renderer registry A registration disagrees with its generated contract, repeats a code/version, or shares a component key with another tool. rendererInvalid

The hub counts the two failure families separately in one banner — backend unavailable summaries, and descriptors whose interface is unavailable or whose compiled module failed to load — and points to Settings → About → Plugin diagnostics, where ToolAboutPanel.svelte resolves the same reasons per service. An empty items list renders the No tools available state.

A renderer that shows money, holdings, or rates must follow the privacy masking contract: money only through the D8 currency formatters with an explicit sensitivity, held quantities through maskableQuantity, rates and percentages explicitly public, and — for a missing value. See Contract for Tool renderers.

The Tools hub card (ToolsHub.svelte) and the opened Tool header (ToolHost.svelte) show the compatibility pair Backend/API <contract_version> · UI <ui.version>. The Tool panel under Settings → About → Plugin diagnostics (ToolAboutPanel.svelte, with its nested ToolDiagnosticsPanel.svelte) lists each service as Version: <contract_version>. No screen renders implementation_version: it exists only in API payloads — the catalogue and diagnostics descriptors, the pin of every compute item, and the identity of every result — where the client pins it per request and checks it on each result (client.ts). It identifies the deployed implementation, not the frontend contract users need to match.

Use DocsLink for documentation destinations. It builds /mkdocs/ URLs from the current language and a relative path rather than forcing English. For an EN-only destination, a caller can supply an existing localized destination through localizedFallbackPath; the helper selects that fallback for non-English languages. It does not discover missing pages automatically.

Tool documentation follows this path. The hub card, the Tool header, and both About panels pass descriptor.documentation.path through toolDocumentationPath (presentation.ts), which accepts only /-separated segments of letters, digits, -, and _, with an optional trailing slash, and refuses a mkdocs/ or language prefix (en/, it/, fr/, es/). A refused path shows Documentation link unavailable instead of a link; the diagnostics list simply omits it. DocsLink then opens /mkdocs/<path> in English or /mkdocs/<lang>/<path> in another language, in a new tab and without a localizedFallbackPath, so a Tool guide opens in the app's current language.

Keep submitted financial data out of documentation URLs, logs, and HTML attributes. Documentation metadata identifies a page and its version, not a scenario transport channel.

docs.title: ✅ Addition and integration checklist
docs.text:
The following work must be completed and verified before presenting a new Tool as available:

  • [ ] Define the atomic boundary and pack every required input before dispatch. Exclude ambient authority and side effects.
  • [ ] Declare package-wide contract/implementation versions and a nonempty service tuple; give every service complete metadata, policies, models, UI SemVer, and documentation.
  • [ ] Define strict nested models, operation discriminators without defaults, and matching operation policies.
  • [ ] Register the packaged class and verify service expansion, healthy siblings, failed imports, duplicate-code quarantine, invalid definitions, and closed registration.
  • [ ] Place the package in its folder, tool_plugins/<name>/plugin.py beside a docstring-only __init__.py, and add each service's name_i18n_key and description_i18n_key texts to its i18n/ fragment in the four languages (./dev.py i18n add … --into tool_plugins/<name>); ./dev.py test utils gate-plugin-layout and gate-plugin-i18n-ownership hold both.
  • [ ] Implement a zero-argument constructor and synchronous code-based dispatch with bounded checkpoints and job-scoped child work.
  • [ ] If the Tool declares settings_fields: personal or instance fields only, no secret; defaults that keep the behaviour before the field; read in compute(), never __init__; tests copied from tool-settings-contract, tool-settings-runtime and tool-settings-lifecycle (A Field in a Tool Plugin).
  • [ ] Verify input/output adapters, schema references, fingerprints, Unicode and byte limits, safe errors, and unchanged caller scenarios.
  • [ ] Integrate generated codecs and the compiled renderer map; verify acceptance parity, unsupported renderer/version handling, and language-aware documentation links.
  • [ ] Verify authenticated route mounting, response order/cardinality/pins, platform-versus-domain outcomes, and process-local diagnostic privacy.
  • [ ] Verify genuine parallel execution, distinct workers for identical items, admission limits, cold startup deadlines, cancellation, crashes, invalid output, and subtree cleanup on every exit path.
  • [ ] Integrate documentation navigation and cross-boundary targets, then run the project's established tests and documentation checks when runtime verification is authorized.

Treat passing those checks as evidence to gather during integration, not as a consequence of adding a descriptor or writing a guide.

docs.title: 📧 Email Service (SMTP)
docs.text:
The email service sends LibreFolio's transactional emails through an SMTP server that the administrator names in environment variables. It can write six kinds — a password-reset link, an invitation, an address to confirm, the activation link of the first administrator, a test message, and the notice that an account's email address changed. The service lives in backend/app/services/email/, its configuration in backend/app/config/email.py, and its hourly budget counts with the sliding-window limiter of backend/app/utils/runtime/rate_window.py. Its routes (backend/app/api/v1/email.py) give administrators the state of email, a test email and the emailing of the links they create; one more lets anyone ask for a reset link for a forgotten password; two more spend the link of a verification email and send it again. The Email tab of the settings (frontend/src/lib/features/email/) shows the state and sends the test email; the same folder holds the page of a verification link and the sign-in's notice, «Send by email» and the «forgot password» form. The administrator's guide is Email.

Status: lots E1 to E5 of release 1.3

Every email has a caller: the test email (POST /api/v1/email/test), the links an administrator emails (POST /api/v1/email/links), a reset link for a forgotten password (POST /api/v1/email/password-reset), the verification email of a new account (Email Verification), the notice of an email change, and the setup link of the initial administrator: workstream A's deliver_setup_link() (backend/app/services/accounts/bootstrap_admin_service.py, lot A7a) sends build_admin_setup() for a link the instance generated itself.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose and Rules
docs.text:
Email is optional (feature F04 of the release 1.3 plan). Four rules shape the whole package:

  1. Optional. With LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_HOST unset or blank, email is off and nothing changes for a self-hosted install: nothing is sent, the other LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_* variables are not even validated, and the configuration check reports ok. "Email off" is the default state, so a caller handles EmailUnavailableError as a normal outcome, not as a fault.
  2. Environment only. The configuration comes only from the LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_* variables, and the password also from a secret file (LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE). It is never written anywhere, so it is never in the database and never in a backup; it is never shown in the interface either. GET /api/v1/email/status answers with the state, the problem and the variable at fault, the checks' i18n keys and detail, the hourly budget and the state of the links: never the host, the port, the user, the sender, the Reply-To or the password. The detail of a check, the part meant for the interface, never holds the host, the user or the sender either. The public GET /api/v1/system/instance says only whether email is usable and whether emails can carry links.
  3. Read at every call. The accessors read the process environment each time, nothing is cached, and they are the only readers of these variables, as the config package rule requires. The variables are documented, commented, in the «Email» section of .env.example.
  4. Links from LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL alone (developer decision 45). Every link an email carries, the ones an administrator sends included, is that variable followed by the path of the page that takes the token, never anything taken from a request (Links). Without the variable, no email with a link goes out.
Module Role backend/app/config/email.py The LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_* accessors and EmailConfigError services/email/smtp.py The transport: deliver(), SmtpServer, SmtpErrorCode, SmtpDeliveryError services/email/delivery.py email_config_state(), the hourly budget (INSTANCE_BUDGET, budget_status()), send_email(), the EmailError family, and mailbox_budget_key(), the key of the per-mailbox limits (The Key of a Mailbox) services/email/messages.py and templates/ EmailKind, email_language(), the six builders and compose_message(); the texts in four languages and the HTML layout. Nothing here sends, reads the configuration or logs services/email/checks.py check_smtp_configuration(), check_smtp_encryption(), check_email_links(), EMAIL_CONFIG_CHECKS, which closes the platform's CONFIG_CHECKS services/email/links.py links_state(), require_links(), email_link(), email_instance_config() and EmailLinksUnavailableError: every emailed link from LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL (Links) services/email/flows.py What an action of the application sends, to whom and in which language: the test email, a link an administrator emails, a forgotten password and its limits, the notice of an email change (Flows); require_email() and link_ttl(), which verification.py reuses services/email/verification.py Email verification at sign-up (developer decision 44): the wait, the emailed link, its confirmation, «send the link again», and the place a waiting account holds (Email Verification) backend/app/api/v1/email.py and backend/app/schemas/email.py GET /email/status, POST /email/test and POST /email/links for administrators, POST /email/password-reset, POST /email/verification/confirm and POST /email/verification/resend for anyone, and their models (The API); EmailInstanceConfig, the email field of GET /system/instance backend/app/utils/runtime/rate_window.py SlidingWindowLimiter and RateDecision, the sliding-window limiter frontend/src/lib/features/email/ and frontend/src/lib/i18n/email/ The Email tab of the settings, its seam over the API client, the check of the links' base from the browser, and its texts (The Email Tab); the frontend of email verification (In the Frontend); «Send by email» and the «forgot password» form (Links by Email in the Interface) frontend/src/routes/verify-email/+page.svelte The page of a verification link (In the Frontend)

services/email/__init__.py holds only the package docstring.

docs.title: 📋 The Variables
docs.text:
Variable Unset or blank Accepted Code when unusable LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_HOST Email off A host name or an IP address, IPv6 without brackets: letters, digits, ., -, _ and :; no scheme, user, port, path, bracket or space SMTP_HOST_INVALID LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_TLS starttls starttls, tls or none, in any case SMTP_TLS_INVALID LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PORT The port of the mode: 587 (starttls), 465 (tls), 25 (none) ASCII digits, 1–65535 SMTP_PORT_INVALID LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_USER No authentication Any text, stripped SMTP_CREDENTIALS_INCOMPLETE without a password LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD, or LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE No password env_secret("LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD"): the value as written, otherwise the content of the file SMTP_PASSWORD_UNREADABLE (a _FILE that cannot give it); SMTP_CREDENTIALS_INCOMPLETE without a user LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_FROM Required with a host One mailbox: Name <address> or address SMTP_FROM_MISSING, SMTP_FROM_INVALID LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_REPLY_TO Replies go to the sender One mailbox SMTP_REPLY_TO_INVALID LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_MAX_PER_HOUR 50 ASCII digits, at least 1 SMTP_MAX_PER_HOUR_INVALID LIBREFOLIO_SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS 20 ASCII digits, at least 1 SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS_INVALID
  • One variable is not an SMTP one. LIBREFOLIO_SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS (signup_emails_per_address(), the limit of the registration emails per client address) does not start with SMTP_ENV_PREFIX. email_config_state() validates it with the others, so a bad value makes email unusable (email.smtp is an error naming it, the server starts anyway), and only while a host is set; delivery.address_budget_limit() reads it again at every request.
  • Blank is unset, and values are stripped — except the password, which env_secret() takes as written, spaces included (Secrets from Files).
  • The modes: starttls upgrades a plain connection before anything else is sent and refuses to go on without the upgrade; tls is TLS from the first byte (SMTPS); none sends in clear, meant for a relay on the same machine or the local network (the encryption check warns otherwise).
  • ASCII digits is literal: a sign, a decimal, 2_525 or fullwidth digits, all of which int() would take, are refused.
  • A mailbox is exactly one address, with a non-empty local part and domain and no whitespace inside; a comma inside a quoted display name belongs to the name. A CR or LF anywhere in the raw value is refused, even where stripping would remove it: no header injection reaches a message.
  • The : of the host is there for IPv6 literals, written without brackets (::1, fd00::25); [::1] is refused. A value with exactly one colon, such as smtp.example.com:587, is a name with its port and is refused too, with a message saying that the port goes in LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PORT: an IPv6 address always has at least two colons.

docs.title: 🧾 EmailConfigError
docs.text: EmailConfigError is a ValueError with two attributes, variable and code. Its message is <VARIABLE>: <rule>, for example LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PORT: expected a whole number from 1 to 65535: it never holds the value of a variable, so never a secret. The accessors raise it for the six *_INVALID codes. The other three codes combine several variables, so email_config_state() decides them: SMTP_PASSWORD_UNREADABLE, SMTP_CREDENTIALS_INCOMPLETE and SMTP_FROM_MISSING.

docs.title: 🔌 Email Off, Usable or Unusable
docs.text:
email_config_state() (in delivery.py) reads every variable through its accessor and never raises. It returns a frozen EmailConfigState:

State configured problem, variable server, sender, reply_to, max_per_hour usable Off: no host False None Unset; max_per_hour 50 False Unusable True The code and the variable at fault Unset; max_per_hour 50 False Usable True None The SmtpServer, the two mailboxes as (display name, address), the hourly limit True

The first fault wins, in this order: the host; then the TLS mode, the port, the user, the password, the sender, the Reply-To and the hourly limit (an EmailConfigError, or a SecretFileError reported as SMTP_PASSWORD_UNREADABLE on LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE); then the credentials, which come in pairs (SMTP_CREDENTIALS_INCOMPLETE on whichever of LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_USER and LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD is set without the other); then the sender (SMTP_FROM_MISSING).

An unusable value turns email off: send_email() raises EmailUnavailableError with the problem code, and the check email.smtp reports an error. The fault is logged once per process: _report_invalid() is a functools.cache keyed by variable, problem and reason, so the event Email configuration cannot be used: email stays off, with those three fields, appears the first time a fault is read, not at every send. A different reason is new information and is logged again, such as a password file that was missing and is now empty. The reason is the accessor's message or the SecretFileError message, which names the variable and the path of the file, never its content: no secret reaches the log.

The server starts either way. The startup audit reads the configuration at every start of every process, through the configuration checks: an unusable value is logged there, first by _report_invalid(), then as the email.smtp error of the audit. Later reads in the process log it again only for a new reason. log_configuration_audit() never stops a start for email, only for the platform's own secrets and settings (Configuration Checks).

docs.title: 📡 Transport (smtp.py)
docs.text:
deliver(server, message) sends one EmailMessage through one SmtpServer with the standard library's smtplib: no third-party SMTP client. It blocks, so it runs in a worker thread: send_email() calls it through asyncio.to_thread(), as the Event Loop Blocking Rule requires, and a test checks that the connection is opened on a thread without a running event loop.

SmtpServer is a frozen dataclass: host, port, tls (starttls, tls or none), user, password (kept out of repr) and timeout. email_config_state() builds it with SMTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, 20 s, read at call time. It is the socket timeout to connect and for each exchange with the server, not a deadline for the whole conversation.

The conversation:

  1. Connect: smtplib.SMTP_SSL in tls mode, smtplib.SMTP otherwise; then EHLO.
  2. starttls mode: STARTTLS, then EHLO again. A server that does not offer STARTTLS is refused with TLS_FAILED before the password or the message is sent: the mode never falls back to plain text.
  3. Authentication, only with a user: login().
  4. The message: send_message(); the envelope sender is the From address, the recipient the To address.
  5. QUIT. Once the server has accepted the message, a failure here — a QUIT answered badly, a dropped connection — is not a failure of the delivery: the email counts as sent.

Both TLS modes use ssl.create_default_context(), which verifies the certificate and the host name. smtplib's own default for starttls() and SMTP_SSL is an unverified context (ssl._create_stdlib_context()), which is why deliver() always passes its own.

A failure raises SmtpDeliveryError with a code from SmtpErrorCode, a StrEnum whose values are the names:

Code When CONNECTION_FAILED The connection could not be opened or was lost: nothing listening, a name that does not resolve, a refused greeting, a network error outside the TLS step TLS_FAILED STARTTLS not offered or refused, a failed handshake, a certificate that does not verify (ssl.SSLError at any step) AUTH_FAILED The credentials were refused, or another SMTP error ended the login step (a server without AUTH, for one) SENDER_REFUSED MAIL FROM refused RECIPIENT_REFUSED RCPT TO refused TIMEOUT A TimeoutError anywhere in the exception chain: smtplib turns a read that timed out into SMTPServerDisconnected SEND_FAILED DATA refused, or another protocol error while sending; also an address with letters outside ASCII towards a server that does not advertise SMTPUTF8, which smtplib refuses on the client side (SMTPNotSupportedError, before MAIL). With SMTPUTF8 advertised, smtplib sends MAIL FROM:<…> SMTPUTF8 BODY=8BITMIME and the message in UTF-8; for ASCII addresses it adds neither

str() of the error is the code alone, for the interface. detail holds what the server said (such as 550 5.1.1 <alice@example.com>: Recipient address rejected), or the exception's text, raw: the transport adds no password and masks nothing. It leaves the process only through the Email not sent log, which masks it (What Is Logged). The original exception is dropped (raise … from None).

docs.title: ⏳ The Hourly Budget
docs.text:
INSTANCE_BUDGET is a SlidingWindowLimiter over 3600 s (BUDGET_WINDOW_SECONDS) with a single key, shared by every send of the process. send_email() hits it with limit= the configured LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_MAX_PER_HOUR, read at call time; budget_status(max_per_hour=None) peeks it with the limit it is given (the status passes the one of the state it has just read) or else the configured one, and returns its RateDecision (allowed, remaining, retry_after) without spending anything, for GET /api/v1/email/status.

  • One unit per attempt. An attempt that passes the configuration and recipient checks spends one unit before any connection, whether the server then accepts the message or not.
  • Refusal before any connection. With the budget spent, send_email() raises EmailRateLimitedError without opening a connection; its retry_after is the number of seconds until the oldest send of the hour leaves the window. A refused attempt is not recorded, so it never pushes that moment further.

Per process, not per instance

The budget lives in the memory of each process: with N worker processes the instance may send N times LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_MAX_PER_HOUR emails an hour, and a restart starts from zero. .env.example says so: the limit is per server process. GET /api/v1/email/status shows the budget of the process that answers it.

docs.title: 📨 send_email()
docs.text:
async def send_email(content, *, to, user_id=None) sends one EmailContent to one address. A blocked instance sends nothing (decision D-E13): sending_blocked() is true while the hosting provider sets LIBREFOLIO_BLOCKED, and also when that variable cannot be read, which the startup checks stop the server on. The /api/v1 guard already refuses the email routes on a blocked instance (Instance Block); the check here holds for any other caller. Then send_email() reads the configuration with asyncio.to_thread(email_config_state): with LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE that read opens a file, and no file is read on the event loop.

flowchart TD
    Call["send_email(content, to, user_id)"] --> Blocked{"sending_blocked()?"}
    Blocked -->|yes| Held["EmailUnavailableError<br/>INSTANCE_BLOCKED"]
    Blocked -->|no| State{"email_config_state()<br/>in a worker thread: usable?"}
    State -->|"no host"| Off["EmailUnavailableError<br/>EMAIL_NOT_CONFIGURED"]
    State -->|"unusable value"| Bad["EmailUnavailableError<br/>the SMTP_* problem code"]
    State -->|yes| Compose["compose_message()"]
    Compose -->|"not exactly one address"| Value["EmailRecipientError<br/>a ValueError"]
    Compose --> Budget{"INSTANCE_BUDGET.hit()"}
    Budget -->|refused| Limited["EmailRateLimitedError<br/>retry_after"]
    Budget -->|"allowed: one unit spent"| Thread["asyncio.to_thread(smtp.deliver)"]
    Thread -->|"SmtpDeliveryError"| Failed["EmailDeliveryError<br/>the SmtpErrorCode"]
    Thread -->|accepted| Sent["Email sent"]
Raised code When Budget EmailUnavailableError INSTANCE_BLOCKED, EMAIL_NOT_CONFIGURED, or the problem code of the configuration A blocked instance, no host, or an unusable value Not spent EmailRecipientError (a ValueError) — to is not exactly one address Not spent EmailRateLimitedError EMAIL_RATE_LIMITED; retry_after in seconds The hourly budget is spent Not spent; no connection EmailDeliveryError A SmtpErrorCode value The server did not take the message Spent

The three Email*Error classes derive from EmailError, which carries code: a caller needs a single except EmailError. EmailRecipientError, from messages.py, is not part of the family: it subclasses ValueError, and a caller that maps it to an answer catches it by name, never as any ValueError.

docs.title: 📝 What Is Logged
docs.text:
Event Level Fields Email sent info kind, language, user_id, recipient_domain Email not sent warning kind, code, detail (masked), user_id, recipient_domain Email not sent: the hourly limit of the instance is reached warning kind, user_id, recipient_domain, retry_after (rounded) Email configuration cannot be used: email stays off error variable, problem, reason; once per process for each combination of the three Test email sent by an administrator info admin_id, language: logged by POST /email/test after Email sent Link emailed by an administrator info admin_id, purpose, token_id, user_id (a reset link's account, None for an invitation), language: logged by send_link_email() after Email sent Forgotten password: reset link emailed info user_id, token_id, language: logged by forgotten_password_work() after Email sent Forgotten password: no active account matches, nothing sent info None: the identifier is never logged Forgotten password: the account had a reset link moments ago, nothing sent info user_id: past a per-account limit Forgotten password: an administrator's reset link is still live, nothing sent info user_id: a request never cancels an administrator's link Forgotten password: the hourly limit of the instance is reached, nothing sent warning user_id: the budget, peeked again in the work Forgotten password: the mailbox had reset emails moments ago, nothing sent info user_id: past the per-mailbox limit Forgotten password: another request won the race, nothing sent info user_id: the recount inside the write transaction Forgotten password: no email sent warning reason (the exception's class) and code: the configuration changed after the answer, or a refusal; a link created for it is revoked Forgotten password: the request failed error error, the exception's class, and no traceback: a database error would print its SQL parameters, the identifier among them Email change notice sent to the previous address info user_id, language: logged by email_changed_work() after Email sent Email change notice: email is off, nothing sent info user_id: no host is set, the default of a self-hosted instance, so never a warning Email change notice: past its limits, nothing sent info user_id: the account, or the old mailbox, had 3 notices in the hour (EMAIL_CHANGE_NOTICES_BY_ACCOUNT, EMAIL_CHANGE_NOTICES_BY_MAILBOX) Email change notice: the account no longer exists, nothing sent info user_id Email change notice: not sent warning user_id, reason (the exception's class) and code: email set but unusable, a blocked instance, the hourly budget spent, an old address that is not exactly one address, a message the server did not take Email change notice: the request failed error user_id, error, the exception's class, and no traceback

Each reset link also leaves workstream A's Password reset link created event (create_password_reset()), with user_id, token_id and created_by_user_id, None for a forgotten password. The events of email verification have a table of their own: What Is Logged.

Never logged by these events: the body (text and HTML), the link it carries and its token, the SMTP password, the recipient's full address, the new address of an email change (not even its domain), the identifier of a «forgot password» request or of a «send the link again». The recipient appears as the domain of its address and as the user_id the caller passes; a link, as the token_id of its row. Outside this module, workstream A's deliver_setup_link() writes the setup link of the initial administrator to the log once, on purpose: without email, the log is how it reaches whoever runs the server.

That holds for the server's own words too. Servers quote the address they refuse, so before detail reaches the Email not sent event, _redacted() replaces the SMTP password with *** and the recipient's address with ***@<domain>, both matched case-insensitively: 550 5.1.1 <alice@example.com>: Recipient address rejected is logged as 550 5.1.1 <***@example.com>: Recipient address rejected.

An unavailable email or a malformed recipient raises without an event of its own, beyond the one-time configuration error.

docs.title: 🏷️ The Key of a Mailbox
docs.text:
mailbox_budget_key(address) is the key of the three per-mailbox limiters, each still 3 emails an hour: FORGOT_BY_MAILBOX (A Forgotten Password), EMAIL_CHANGE_NOTICES_BY_MAILBOX (An Email Address Changes) and VERIFICATION_BY_MAILBOX (Sending the Link Again). The aliases of one mailbox give one key, so they share its budget (backlog E-9):

  1. The address stripped and case-folded. A value without @ stops here.
  2. Split at the last @, the local part cut at its first +, on every domain, unless nothing would be left before it.
  3. For Gmail, googlemail.com becomes gmail.com, and every dot of the local part goes.
Address Key Victim.Name+News@GoogleMail.com victimname@gmail.com first.last+x@example.org first.last@example.org first.last@outlook.com first.last@outlook.com: outside Gmail a dot is part of the mailbox a.b@mail.gmail.com a.b@mail.gmail.com: a subdomain of Gmail is not Gmail +tag@example.org +tag@example.org: nothing before the +
  • Only a key. It is never stored, logged or shown, and the email still goes to the address as stored, tag and dots included.
  • No IDNA. A domain beyond ASCII is case-folded, never encoded.
  • The other limits are unchanged: per account, per client address and per identifier. FORGOT_BY_IDENTIFIER still counts the identifier as typed, stripped and case-folded: it limits whoever asks, while the mailbox's key protects whoever receives.
  • What it cannot see: a catch-all domain, or Fastmail-style subdomain addresses (anything@user.fastmail.com), give a new key for each local part. Only the hourly budget of the instance bounds them (Coming Next).

docs.title: 🗂️ The Six Kinds
docs.text:
Each kind of email has a keyword-only builder that returns an EmailContent, a frozen dataclass with kind, language, subject, text (the plain-text part) and html:

EmailKind Builder Arguments Greeting Link password_reset build_password_reset() language, link, ttl, instance Anonymous Yes password_reset build_password_reset_after_restore() language, link, ttl, instance Anonymous Yes invite build_invite() language, link, ttl, instance, inviter=None, grants_admin=False Anonymous Yes email_verification build_verification() language, link, ttl, instance Anonymous Yes admin_setup build_admin_setup() language, username, link, ttl, instance By username Yes email_change_confirmation build_email_change_confirmation() language, username, link, ttl, instance By username Yes test build_test_message() language, username, instance By username No email_changed build_email_changed() language, instance Anonymous No
  • build_password_reset_after_restore() is the same kind with other words (the restore_* keys of the password_reset section): it tells the owner of an instance restored from a backup that the password was revoked after the restore and points to «Forgot Password?» for when the link expires. Only instance_owner.assign_owner_and_send_reset() uses it; it does not say who restored the backup, and shows no address and no name.
  • The greeting is the catalogue's common.greeting_anonymous, «Hello,», or common.greeting, «Hello $username,», for the two kinds whose sender is trusted (No Stranger's Text).
  • The four link kinds share their values with the purposes of the single-use account tokens, but the builders issue no token: the caller passes the finished link and its lifetime (ttl).
  • A link must start with http:// or https:// and hold no whitespace; anything else (javascript:, data:, mailto:, a relative path) is a ValueError. Plain http:// is accepted for an instance on a home network.
  • An invitation opens without a name (the account does not exist yet), names the inviter only when inviter is given, and adds one sentence when grants_admin is true.
  • The notice of an email change says only that the address changed, with no part of the new one (No Stranger's Text). It goes to the old address and carries no link (An Email Address Changes).
  • instance names the instance in the body and in the footer. The test email passes the host the request was sent to (POST /email/test); an email with a link passes the host of LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL, port included (LinksState.instance, Links); the notice of an email change passes that host too when the variable is usable, else «LibreFolio».

build_test_message(), build_invite() and build_password_reset() have callers (Flows); build_verification() has one in verification.py; build_email_changed() has one in email_changed_work(); build_admin_setup() has one since workstream A's lot A7a: deliver_setup_link() in backend/app/services/accounts/bootstrap_admin_service.py, for a link the instance generated (a token from the hosting panel is the panel's to deliver, decision D-E11).

docs.title: 🚫 No Stranger's Text
docs.text:
Three kinds can go to an address chosen by someone who is neither an administrator nor the operator: a password reset, an email verification and the notice of an email change. None of them carries text that person chose (night decision N62 of 17/10, to be reviewed):

  • No username. build_password_reset() and build_verification() take no username and open with common.greeting_anonymous, as the invitation does. A reset link an administrator emails (A Link an Administrator Emails) shares the builder, so it greets nobody by name either.
  • Nothing of the new address. build_email_changed() takes neither a username nor a new address, and email_changed.intro has no $address: «The email address of your account on $instance was changed. This message goes to the address it had before.» No mask would do: nothing looks the domain up in the DNS, so even its last label is free text, which mail clients turn into a link. masked_address(), whose only use was the notice, is gone; the log's own mask of an address an SMTP server quotes, _redacted(), stays (What Is Logged).
  • Pinned by tests (EMM-036…041): a username or a new address cannot even be passed to these builders, a TypeError, and no text of their catalogue sections holds $username.

build_admin_setup() and build_test_message() still greet by username: their sender is trusted, the operator or an administrator writing to themselves. The username still shows once a link is opened, on pages of the instance: the reset page names the account from the username of POST /auth/tokens/inspect, and the sign-in names it after a verification, from the username of POST /email/verification/confirm.

docs.title: 🌍 Languages
docs.text: EMAIL_LANGUAGES is ("en", "it", "fr", "es"), exactly the choices of the default_language setting (a test compares the two), so no account can pick a language its emails lack. email_language(tag) lowercases the tag, keeps its primary subtag and falls back to English: it-IT, it_IT and IT give it; de, an empty tag or None give en. Every builder passes its language through it.

docs.title: 🛡️ Rendering Rules
docs.text:
• Placeholders: the texts use string.Template placeholders — $username (in common.greeting alone), $instance, $inviter, $duration — filled with substitute().
  • One line per value: before they fill a placeholder, _render() puts every value on one line (_one_line()). Control characters (Unicode category Cc) and line and paragraph separators (Zl, Zp) become spaces, and the bidirectional embeddings, overrides and isolates (U+202A to U+202E, U+2066 to U+2069) are removed. A username may hold any character: without this it could add lines of its own to the plain-text part, or reorder the text around it.
  • Escaping: every line of the HTML part is escaped (html.escape) after it is filled, so a value that comes from a person — a user name, the name of the instance, the inviter — stays text, never markup. The link is escaped in its href and in the visible fallback address.
  • Subjects: the subject is the catalogue's text, never filled: no user value and no link reaches it, and it stays on one line. Every relay and every notification sees it.
  • Durations: $duration is babel.dates.format_timedelta(ttl, locale=language), Babel's default wording: 30 minutes in Italian gives «30 minuti», 7 days in English "1 week", 72 hours in Italian «3 giorni».
  • The two parts: the plain text holds the greeting, the body lines, for a link kind the action followed by the link verbatim on its own line, the closing lines, then a -- signature line and the footer. The HTML part fills templates/layout.html ($lang, $subject, $body, $footer): a table-based layout with inline styles, a button for the link and, below it, the address to copy (common.button_fallback); <html lang="…"> declares the language.
  • The catalogues and the layout are read once, when messages.py is imported.

docs.title: 📚 The Catalogue
docs.text:
templates/en.json, it.json, fr.json and es.json share one structure: a common section (greeting, greeting_anonymous, button_fallback, footer) and one section per EmailKind value, holding subject, intro and, for the link kinds, action, expiry and ignore; invite adds intro_anonymous and admin_role; test has outro instead, and email_changed advice.

./dev.py test services email-messages guards the catalogue:

  • the four JSON files and layout.html exist in templates/, beside messages.py;
  • each file parses as UTF-8 JSON, with an object at its root;
  • every file has exactly the nested keys of en.json: a text missing in one language is a gap, an extra one is dead;
  • every leaf is a non-empty string;
  • for each key, the $placeholders are the same set as in English: a translation neither drops a value nor invents one;
  • every text is valid string.Template syntax: no stray $ (write $$ for a literal dollar sign).

These texts are the backend's own catalogue: the frontend i18n sources and the dev.py i18n commands do not include them.

docs.title: ➕ Adding a Text or a Kind
docs.text:
A text: add the key to the same section of the four JSON files in one change, with the same $placeholders in every language, then list it in the builder (the before or after keys that _render() assembles).

A kind:

  1. a value in EmailKind, which is also the name of its catalogue section;
  2. that section in the four JSON files, with a subject free of placeholders;
  3. a keyword-only build_* builder that passes the language through email_language(), the link through _checked_link() and the lifetime through _duration(), and puts user values only into body placeholders — none at all when someone other than an administrator or the operator can choose its recipient (No Stranger's Text);
  4. the tests of backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_email_messages.py, which pin every kind and the signature of each builder.

docs.title: 📬 Composing the Message
docs.text:
compose_message(content, *, to, sender, reply_to=None, now=None) returns the EmailMessage to send:

Header Value Subject content.subject From sender, a (display name, address) tuple; a non-ASCII name is encoded as RFC 2047 words To to, exactly one bare address Reply-To Only when reply_to is given Date now, or the current time, in GMT Message-ID make_msgid() in the domain of the sender's address, never the name of the machine Auto-Submitted auto-generated: auto-responders do not answer (RFC 3834) X-Auto-Response-Suppress All: Exchange and Outlook send no automatic reply Content-Language content.language

The body is multipart/alternative, the plain text first and the HTML last: a client shows the last alternative it can display. Content-Language is set after the body, because set_content() clears every Content-* header and turning the message into a multipart moves them into its first part.

to must be exactly one bare address: one @ with something on both sides, and no whitespace (not even a trailing line break: nothing is trimmed), comma, <, > or ". Anything else is an EmailRecipientError (a ValueError), so no message is composed for a second, hidden recipient.

docs.title: 🩺 Configuration Checks (checks.py)
docs.text:
The email section has three checks in the shape of the platform's ConfigCheck (Configuration Checks). Like every configuration check, they read the configuration through email_config_state(), and links_state() for the third, change nothing, never raise and never put a secret in their result:

check_id Severity i18n_key When email.smtp ok email.checks.smtp.off No host: email is optional email.smtp ok email.checks.smtp.ok The configuration is usable email.smtp error email.checks.smtp.invalid A value cannot be used: detail is {"problem": <code>, "variable": <name>}; the summary names the variable and says that email stays off email.smtp_encryption ok email.checks.smtpEncryption.ok Email is not usable, or the mode is starttls or tls email.smtp_encryption ok email.checks.smtpEncryption.localPlain none towards a local host email.smtp_encryption warning email.checks.smtpEncryption.plain none towards any other host: emails, their links and the SMTP password travel unencrypted. Empty detail email.links ok email.checks.links.ok Email is not usable (off included), or LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL is ready email.links info email.checks.links.missing Email is usable and LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL is not set: no email with a link can go out. Empty detail email.links warning email.checks.links.invalid Email is usable and LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL cannot start a link: _usable_base() refuses it (not http or https, no host, a user name or a password, a ? or #, whitespace, a bad port, or not parsable at all). Empty detail

What counts as local: an IP address that classify_ip() (backend/app/utils/runtime/network.py) classes as loopback (127.0.0.0/8, ::1), lan (the private, link-local and unique-local ranges) or vpn (100.64.0.0/10 and Tailscale's fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48); or a name that is localhost, has a single label (a Docker service such as postfix, a host of the LAN) or ends with .localhost, .local, .lan, .home.arpa or .internal. Names are judged as written, nothing is resolved: a tailnet name such as relay.tailnet.ts.net gets the warning, while its 100.x address would not.

The detail travels to the admin interface as the parameters of a translated message, so it never names the host, the user or the sender. The English summary is for the log only, and the plain-text warning's summary does name the host. GET /api/v1/email/status never returns a summary. The keys are written whole, like the platform's; their messages are in the email i18n source of the frontend (The Email Tab). The «Security» tab of Settings › Administration lists the three checks too, from GET /api/v1/security/checks, with the platform's, and links a finding of theirs to the Email tab (SecurityTab).

EMAIL_CONFIG_CHECKS = (check_smtp_configuration, check_smtp_encryption, check_email_links) closes the platform's CONFIG_CHECKS (*EMAIL_CONFIG_CHECKS at the end of the tuple in backend/app/services/platform/config_audit.py), so the three checks run in two places:

  • At startup, log_configuration_audit() logs every check that is not ok, with its summary as the message and check and detail as fields. For email that is the email.smtp error, <variable> cannot be used (<problem>): email stays off until it is fixed; the plain-text warning, LIBREFOLIO_SMTP_TLS=none with <host>: emails, their links and the SMTP password travel unencrypted; use starttls or tls; and the email.links line, at info LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL is not set: emails work, but none with a link (forgotten password, invitation, reset) can go out or at warning LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL cannot start a link (it needs http:// or https:// and a host, with no user name, password, ? or #): no email with a link (forgotten password, invitation, reset) can go out. None of them stops the start. An unusable configuration thus gives two lines: Email configuration cannot be used: email stays off from _report_invalid(), while the check reads the state, then the audit's summary.
  • On demand, GET /api/v1/email/status evaluates EMAIL_CONFIG_CHECKS at every call and returns each result without its summary.

config_audit imports EMAIL_CONFIG_CHECKS at module level to build its tuple, before it defines ConfigCheck. A module-level from backend.app.services.platform.config_audit import ConfigCheck in checks.py would therefore fail whenever config_audit is imported first, on a half-initialized module. So checks.py imports ConfigCheck inside each check, when the check runs, and under TYPE_CHECKING for its annotations (the module has from __future__ import annotations): either module can be imported first. check_email_links() imports links_state() the same way: links.py brings in the accounts services, which config_audit then does not load at import time.

docs.title: ⛓️ Links (links.py)
docs.text:
Every link an email carries, the ones an administrator sends included, is built from LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL alone (developer decision 45): the variable, then the path of the page that takes the token, the token in the fragment (token_service.token_path(), such as /reset-password#token=…). Nothing in a request — its host, its Origin, a link the browser sends — becomes part of an emailed link: otherwise a stranger could have a real token sent to a user inside a link to a site of theirs. Without the variable, no email with a link goes out; the links an administrator copies stay as they are (registration_service.public_link(), the path alone without the variable).

Member Contract links_state() LinksState(base, problem), read now, never raises. base is LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL as public_url() (backend/app/config/accounts.py) gives it, one trailing slash removed, once _usable_base() accepts it: http or https, a host, a valid port, no user name or password (they would travel in every link), no whitespace, and no ? or # at all (even an empty one would swallow the path that follows). problem is PUBLIC_URL_MISSING (unset or blank) or PUBLIC_URL_INVALID (anything else, an address urlsplit() cannot parse, such as https://[::1, included). ready is a base without a problem; instance is the host of base, port included, the name an email gives the instance require_links() The LinksState when ready, else EmailLinksUnavailableError, its code the problem email_link(purpose, token) require_links(), then public_link(token_path(purpose, token)); EmailLinksUnavailableError without a usable base email_instance_config() The email field of GET /system/instance: available is email_config_state().usable and not sending_blocked(), links is available and links_state().ready (below) EmailLinksUnavailableError An EmailError: no email with a link can go out

With email usable, a missing or invalid variable is reported by the email.links check: in the start log and as a notice of the Email tab. Nothing here checks that the address reaches this instance: the server cannot know how its users reach it. The Email tab checks it from the administrator's browser (The Email Tab).

docs.title: 🔀 Flows (flows.py)
docs.text:
services/email/flows.py has one function per email that an action of the application sends. A flow decides the content, the recipient and the language; send_email() checks the configuration and the budget, sends and logs.

Function What it does async account_language(session, user_id) The language of every email of an account: its own user_settings.language, else the instance's default_language global setting, else English. It reads the language column alone and get_setting_value(): a settings row that no longer validates (a theme outside light/dark/auto, say) never stops an email, and an account without a user_settings row is left without one async instance_language(session) The instance's default_language, else English: the language of an email to someone without an account, an invitation async send_test_email(session, user, *, instance) build_test_message() in the account's language, with user.username and instance, sent to user.email with user_id; returns the language. Raises what send_email() raises async send_link_email(session, *, admin, purpose, token, to=None, language=None, now=None) A link an administrator has just created, by email: A Link an Administrator Emails. Returns LinkEmailSent(to, language) async admit_forgotten_password(address, identifier) Whether a «forgot password» request may go on, before anything about the accounts is read: A Forgotten Password async forgotten_password_work(identifier, *, engine=None, now=None) The work of that request, after its answer; never raises async require_email() The configuration (EmailConfigState) when email can be used now, read in a worker thread; else EmailUnavailableError, its code INSTANCE_BLOCKED while the hosting provider blocks the instance (sending_blocked()), EMAIL_NOT_CONFIGURED without a host, else the problem of the configuration. The flows with a link — send_link_email(), the «forgot password» flow and verification.py — call it before they create or send anything link_ttl(record, now) How long the link of a token row still works at now, never negative: the lifetime an email states. verification.py reuses it async email_changed_work(user_id, old_address, new_address, *, engine=None) The notice to the address an account had before its email changed, after the answer: An Email Address Changes. Never raises INSTANCE_FALLBACK "LibreFolio": the name of the instance in an email without a link when LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL gives none
  • supported_email_language() reduces it-IT, it_IT and IT to it, and gives None for a language the emails do not speak or an empty value; email_language() is the same with en instead of None.
  • An account whose own language is one the emails do not speak counts as an account without one: it gets the instance's default_language, then English. A missing default_language setting reads as en.
  • The language rule holds for every email of an account, as the module's docstring says: a new flow for an account takes its language from account_language().

docs.title: ✉️ A Link an Administrator Emails
docs.text:
send_link_email() emails the token that POST /users/invites or POST /users/{id}/password-reset-link has just returned, in this order:

  1. Email usable (EmailUnavailableError), then links ready (EmailLinksUnavailableError).
  2. The token inspected for its purpose (token_service.inspect_token()): any status but valid raises EmailLinkInvalidError, its code the status, expired, consumed, revoked or unknown. A token of the other purpose is unknown.
  3. The link, from the token alone: email_link().
  4. The recipient and the language:
    • an invitation goes to to, else to the address written in it (EmailRecipientRequiredError without either), in language, else the instance's (instance_language()). It names the administrator who sends it as the inviter (inviter=admin.username), and adds its sentence when grants_admin is set;
    • a password-reset link goes only to the address of its account, in the account's language: any to, the account's own address included, raises EmailRecipientNotAllowedError, and language is ignored. A token whose account no longer exists is unknown; an account that is not active raises EmailAccountInactiveError, since the password it would set could not be used yet.
  5. send_email(), then the Link emailed by an administrator event (What Is Logged).

The lifetime the email states is what is left of the token's (link_ttl()): 7 days for an invitation just created, 30 minutes for a reset link.

docs.title: 🔑 A Forgotten Password
docs.text:
Open since lot E4, with the current password for an email change

«Forgot password» opened with lot E4, once changing an account's email asked for the current password (workstream A's lot A6e, Changing the Email). Without that rule, a moment inside someone's session (a stolen cookie, an unlocked machine) would be enough to put one's own address on the account, then reset its password from it: a lasting takeover. The two go together: the hold the feature had since the security review of lot E3 is gone, with FORGOT_PASSWORD_HELD and ForgottenPasswordHeldError, and nothing in the code holds it any more (a night decision of 16/10, to be reviewed).

POST /api/v1/email/password-reset answers before it looks for the account, so that nothing in the answer — its status, its body, its timing — tells which accounts exist:

  1. Admission, admit_forgotten_password(address, identifier), before the answer: email usable, links ready, the limiters per address and per identifier, then the hourly budget, peeked. Every refusal is the same for everyone and depends on no account.
  2. The answer: 202, the same body for everyone.
  3. The work, forgotten_password_work(identifier), a FastAPI background task with a session of its own on the request's engine (the request's session ends with it), in this order:
    1. the account, looked up as the login does (get_user_by_username_or_email(), the identifier stripped); nothing for an unknown or inactive one;
    2. the per-account limits (_reset_emails_allowed());
    3. nothing while a reset link an administrator created for the account is still live (_admin_link_live()): a request never cancels it;
    4. email, links and the hourly budget checked again, since the answer went out: nothing is created when the email cannot go;
    5. the per-mailbox limit;
    6. create_password_reset() (workstream A): a new link, valid 30 minutes, which revokes the account's earlier live reset links, by now only those of earlier requests;
    7. the per-account limits counted again inside the write transaction, the new link included: of two requests that passed the first count together, the second sees the first one's link and rolls back (SQLite writes one at a time), so they cannot both send;
    8. the commit, then the email, to the account's address in its language. If it does not go out, whatever the reason, the new link is revoked: it reached nobody.

Every outcome is a log event without the identifier (What Is Logged).

Limit Counted on Past it delivery.ADDRESS_BUDGET: LIBREFOLIO_SIGNUP_EMAILS_PER_ADDRESS emails an hour, 20 by default, the one count of registrations, «send the link again» and this request. admit_forgotten_password() only peeks it (address_budget_peek(): the same refusal whether an account matches); forgotten_password_work() hits it (address_budget_hit()) just before the commit that precedes the email, once the account, its limits, the mailbox and the budget have admitted; a full counter then ends the work in silence, nothing kept The client address, workstream H's rate_limit_address(request) (Which client address), through its client_rate_key(): an IPv6 client by its /64, which one subscriber usually holds whole; no count behind a reverse proxy LibreFolio does not trust, on a local address 429 EMAIL_RATE_LIMITED FORGOT_BY_IDENTIFIER: 3 requests an hour The identifier stripped and case-folded, whether an account matches or not 429 EMAIL_RATE_LIMITED The hourly budget of the instance budget_status(), peeked at the admission and again in the work: the email spends its unit 429 EMAIL_RATE_LIMITED at the admission; nothing sent in the work FORGOT_BY_MAILBOX: 3 emails an hour The account's address through mailbox_budget_key(), the aliases of one mailbox together, whatever account gives it Nothing sent, in silence: the answer was already 202 One email every 5 minutes, 3 an hour (RESET_EMAIL_MIN_INTERVAL, RESET_EMAILS_PER_HOUR) The account's reset links created in the last hour, whoever created them, counted again inside the write transaction Nothing sent, in silence

The three limiters are SlidingWindowLimiters in the memory of the process, like the budget: with N worker processes they are N times as large, and a restart forgets them. The per-account limits read the database, so they hold across processes. A request without a client address (a unix socket) skips the per-address limit: one shared count would let a single client block the feature for everyone, and the other limits still apply.

Which client address (workstream H, decisions P17 and N70): the routes pass rate_limit_address(request) of backend/app/services/platform/client_address.py (lot E-13). It is None, which every per-address limit here reads as «no count» (a request without an address counts under no key), for a request that came through a reverse proxy LibreFolio does not trust, on a local address (forwarded_by_untrusted_proxy(): an X-Forwarded-For, Forwarded or X-Real-IP header from a loopback, private, link-local, unique-local or CGNAT peer, when neither LIBREFOLIO_CLIENT_IP_HEADER nor uvicorn gave the visitor's address): every visitor shares that proxy's address, and one count would let anyone block the feature for everyone. Otherwise it is client_address(request): the address in the header a trusted proxy sets, when LIBREFOLIO_CLIENT_IP_HEADER names it (Fly-Client-IP on Fly.io, X-Real-IP from Nginx); otherwise the connection's address as uvicorn gives it, which follows X-Forwarded-For only from the proxies listed in FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS (127.0.0.1 by default). A client therefore cannot get a fresh key, and a fresh limit, by forging a header at every request, as long as the variable is set only where every request crosses that proxy. FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS must name the proxy's addresses or networks, never *: with *, uvicorn takes the left-most X-Forwarded-For value, which the client controls. The key is H's client_rate_key(), the one rule for every per-client limit (lot E4c removed the copy this module had, address_key()). The older client_address(forwarded_for, peer) of backend/app/utils/runtime/network.py, which takes the last X-Forwarded-For value whoever sent it, is advice for the connection indicator, never a key for a limit. Behind a proxy LibreFolio does not trust on a local address the per-address limits do not count, and the limits per identifier, per account and per mailbox, and the hourly budget, still hold; behind one on a public address (a CDN) every client still shares the proxy's address and one count. The details: The Client's Address.

docs.title: 🔔 An Email Address Changes
docs.text:
email_changed_work(user_id, old_address, new_address) tells the address an account had before that its email address changed.
