docs.title: 🏦 Crédit Agricole Importer
docs.text:
broker_credit_agricole imports the two Italian exports of Crédit Agricole as one report set (version 2.0.0):

  • the securities movements, Lista Movimenti Deposito Titoli (role securities);
  • the account movements, Lista Movimenti Conto (role account).

Each export is a CSV or an XLSX, and each may be downloaded several times. The plugin lives in backend/app/services/brim_providers/broker_credit_agricole/ and is the second report-set plugin after Danske Bank. It shares its core with Danske (brim_report_set_core.py) and keeps the richest wizard integration of the family — a causale registry, evidence tables, blocking and splitting field todos — which the BRIM Plugin Guide uses as its reference.

This page covers what is specific to Crédit Agricole. The user's view is Crédit Agricole, where the plugin's docs_url points.

Why a set

The two exports show the same facts twice: a coupon, a purchase, a fund redemption or a maturity is a row in each. Read apart (what versions up to 1.5.0 did) every such fact is counted twice, and the securities export, which has no cash of its own, needed an automatic counter-entry for each row. From 2.0.0 the set is paired row by row and one transaction is imported per fact, with the cash the account states.

docs.title: 🗺️ The flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A["Securities exports<br/>(CSV / XLSX)"] --> D["detect_role<br/>describe_member"]
    B["Account exports<br/>(CSV / XLSX)"] --> D
    D --> P["describe_set<br/>(preview: segments, holes, notices)"]
    D --> C["combine → Analysis<br/>rule M, classes, pairs,<br/>balances, truth points"]
    C --> F["Combined file<br/>(lf_*, securities:*, account:*)"]
    F --> R["parse → CombinedParser<br/>+ Booking"]
    R --> H["apply_history<br/>(H0, checkpoints kept)"]
    H --> W["Import wizard<br/>review"]
    W --> G["gap-fix<br/>(cash correction, verifications)"]

combine is a pure function of the files (Analysis in _report_set.py, written out by TableBuilder in _combined.py). parse reads only the combined file (CombinedParser, then Booking in _booking.py). The files of the plugin:

Module Content plugin.py The contract: roles, detect_role, describe_member, describe_set, combine, parse _rows.py Reading the exports as rows and the XLSX header (testata) _classify.py The causale registry and the pure functions that name a row (unchanged since 1.5.0) _report_set.py The analysis: rule M, classes, pairs, balances, truth points, describe_member, describe_set _combined.py The combined file (TableBuilder) and its parse (CombinedParser) _booking.py From one line of the combined file to transactions, todos and notices

docs.title: 🗂️ Roles, formats and detection
docs.text:
Role Export Dated by Settled on Extensions Can be several files securities Lista Movimenti Deposito Titoli (Portafoglio → Lista Movimenti) Data operazione Data valuta .csv, .xlsx yes account Lista Movimenti Conto (Conti → Lista movimenti) Data Op. Data Val. .csv, .xlsx yes

Both roles are required. The account role declares must_cover="securities" (the preview warns when the account starts after the securities period or ends before it) and max_history="P2Y", the two years the bank allows for it.

  • Detection (detect_role in _rows.py): a .csv or .xlsx whose first 60 rows contain the securities header (Data operazione + Causale + Quantità) is securities; the account header (Data Op. + Descrizione + Importo) makes it account. A file that has a column lf_row_kind is a combined file of this plugin and has no role. Anything else has none.
  • can_parse is true for a member (so that the wizard can say which export is missing) and for a combined file.
  • Columns are mapped by label (build_col_index), so the XLSX preamble and extra leading columns do not matter. The securities amount column is Controvalore in Euro (or Ctv in Eur).
  • Rows that are not rows: blank rows, the recap footer (a row without a date whose label starts with TOTALE, RIEPILOGO or SALDO FINALE), a row without a date or a causale, and account rows whose amount is zero. An account amount that cannot be read as a number is kept as class invalid.
  • Numbers. Prezzo, Controvalore, Importo and the figures inside descriptions (NOMINALE:, RITENUTA:) are Italian-formatted; Quantità is plain (dotted decimals for fund units, integers for bond nominals).
  • Currency. Account rows take Divisa, EUR when empty. Securities rows take the first three-letter code among the columns whose header contains Divisa. Cambio is never read.

docs.title: 🧾 The header of the XLSX (testata)
docs.text:
Only the XLSX has a header above the table, and only the XLSX of the account carries the balances:

Label Meaning Saldo Iniziale The balance at the end of the eve of Data dal Saldo Finale The balance at the end of Data al Data dal, Data al The period the export was asked for (can be wider than its rows: the bank cuts old rows)

Both balances are on the operation-date axis and are the only true cash numbers the bank gives. The reader accepts the label and its value in one cell (Saldo Iniziale 1000,00 EUR) or in two neighbouring cells. The securities XLSX header holds the dossier and the supporting account (Dossier n., C/C di appoggio), the cash (Liquidità) and its date (Data Aggiornamento). The dossier and the account numbers are used for one thing — an opaque fingerprint compared in memory — and are never copied into any output, the combined file included.

A five-digit year (25/07/02026) is read in the header only, never in a row.

docs.title: 📚 Several downloads of one export: rule M
docs.text:
The same role may come in several files (blocks of a long period, the CSV and the XLSX of the same export, an export asked again). RoleMerge of the shared core joins them day by day, with the Crédit Agricole policy owner="most_rows", contradiction="not_contained":

  1. Two copies of the same bank row have the same signature (CSV and XLSX included), and identical rows count once.
  2. For a day covered by several files, the file with the most rows that day owns it (ties go to the file that ends last). A bank can cut an export short, never add a row.
  3. The rows of a file that does not own the day are dropped silently when they are the same rows as the owner's, and otherwise become excluded with the reason superseded.
  4. A day is a contradiction (overlap_mismatch in describe_set) only when a file has a row that the owner does not have (not_contained). A file cut halfway through the day, whose rows are all in the owner, is not a contradiction.

The coverage used by rule M is the days of the rows of each file. The period a header declares is used elsewhere, for the cash coverage of the account (below).

docs.title: 🏷️ Row classes
docs.text:
classify_securities and classify_account (in _report_set.py) give every row a class; the class decides what it can be paired with.

Securities causale Class Carries cash CEDOLA coupon yes ACQ.CONT.SU MERC., SICAV: SOTTOSCR buy yes FONDI: RIMBORSO redeem yes TITOLI SCADUTI matured yes GIRO ALTRO DOSSIER, VERS.TITOLI transfer_in no anything else unknown — Account row Class amount that cannot be read invalid TITOLI SCADUTI O ESTRATTI, positive maturity COMPRAVENDITA TITOLI/FONDI/OPZIONI, direction found from the description trade_buy (negative amount) or trade_sell the same causale, direction not found trade_unknown GIROCONTO/BONIFICO, positive, that is a fund redemption redemption CEDOLE, DIVIDENDI, PREMI ESTRATTI, positive, with the word DIVIDEND and a named security dividend the same causale otherwise coupon anything else standalone

A dividend is never paired: it must not be matched with a bond coupon of the securities export that happens to have the same amount and value date.

docs.title: 🔗 Pairing securities and account rows
docs.text:
A securities row and an account row are the same fact when they have:

  • the same kind of fact (coupon, buy ↔ trade_buy, redeem ↔ redemption, matured ↔ maturity);
  • the same amount to the cent, rounded half-up on both sides (1000,005 = 1000,01; known limit: 1000,015 ≠ 1000,01);
  • the same value date (Data valuta against Data Val.);
  • the same currency.

The operation date is not in the key: the securities row and the account row of one fact often have different operation dates (an order on the 17th, the debit on the 25th). A row without a value date, an amount or a pairing class takes part in no pair.

Rows that share a key are paired by core.assign:

  • one against one is a pair;
  • identical twins (the same signature) pair without ambiguity, in file order;
  • larger groups pair when one assignment wins on the names (one name is a prefix of the other: the bank truncates labels); the assignments are compared by what each pair would import (ISIN, withholding, name on the account side), and candidates that would import different things are ambiguous — every row of the group is left out of the pairs and flagged ambiguous;
  • more than 8 candidates on a side are ambiguous without trying.

Nothing is guessed. A pair whose names are not compatible still pairs (the key is unique) and raises a name_mismatch notice.

docs.title: 🧭 Outcomes and zones
docs.text:
Every row gets exactly one outcome (pair, standalone or excluded), a zone and, when it is not a plain pair, a reason.

Zones are on the operation-date axis of the account and exist only when the set states a balance that opens the history: before (up to the opening balance's day), gap (inside a hole) and window (everything else). A set with no usable balance has no zone (empty lf_zone). A pair takes the zone of its account row.

Row Outcome Reason Securities + account, paired pair — Securities transfer_in standalone — Securities with cash, both dates (operation and value) inside one hole standalone in_gap Securities with cash, several account candidates and no certainty excluded ambiguous Securities with cash, no account file at all excluded outside_cash_coverage Securities with cash, settling after the last day the account covers excluded not_yet_settled Securities with cash, settling on a day no account file covers excluded outside_cash_coverage Securities with cash, the account covers its day and has no matching row excluded no_counterpart Securities, causale not in the table excluded unknown_type Account row, amount unreadable excluded invalid Account row, several securities candidates and no certainty standalone ambiguous Account coupon, dividend, redemption, maturity or ordinary row with no securities row standalone — Account COMPRAVENDITA with no securities row standalone no_counterpart A row of a file that lost rule M for that day excluded superseded

The rule behind the asymmetry: an account row is cash the bank really moved, so it is never dropped for lack of a pair — only for being unreadable. A securities row with cash and no counterpart cannot be imported alone without counting the money twice or leaving it without cash, so it is left out and said so.

The cash coverage of the account (cash_spans) is the union of the periods the account files cover: a file whose balances add up (opening + Σ rows = closing, to the cent) covers the period its header declares (it may hold no row on the last day); any other file covers the days from its first to its last row. The day compared is the securities value date against the account's operation-date days, so it can be wrong by a day at the borders.

docs.title: ⚖️ Balances, intervals and holes
docs.text:
The account XLSX states two balances per file. Taken together, in date order, they cut the timeline in intervals; each is classified by explained_by_rows (a pure function):

flowchart TD
    S["Two consecutive statements<br/>start (day S), end (day E)"] --> R["residual = (end − start)<br/>− Σ of the account rows dated after S up to E"]
    R --> U{"a row inside<br/>with an unreadable amount?"}
    U -- yes --> BR["broken"]
    U -- no --> Z{"|residual| ≤ 0.01 ?"}
    Z -- yes --> CL["closed"]
    Z -- no --> N{"any row at all<br/>inside the stretch?"}
    N -- no --> HO["hole"]
    N -- yes --> BR
    CL --> O1["nothing to do"]
    HO --> O2["cash correction proposed,<br/>dated E (the end of the stretch)"]
    BR --> O3["warning, never a correction"]
Interval Meaning Effect closed The rows between the two balances explain the change (within a cent) none hole The change is not explained and no row at all lies in the stretch: no file covers it, so the difference is money the files do not show a cash correction, proposed by the gap-fix, dated at the end of the stretch; warning account_gap broken The change is not explained but rows are there (or a row cannot be summed): the files say something that does not add up warning balance_chain_broken; never a correction

Only a hole becomes a correction because a correction placed on a covered stretch could hide a row that is missing inside it. Example with invented numbers: the balance is 1,000.00 on 30 June and 900.00 on 31 July and no row falls in July — a hole of −100.00, corrected at 31 July with a true cash of 900.00. If a file with the July rows arrives, the interval becomes closed and the correction disappears by itself.

A few details:

  • Two statements on the same day (the Saldo Finale of a file and the Saldo Iniziale of the next, one day later) must agree within a cent; if not, the day is conflicting and the chain is reported as broken.
  • The opening is the earliest Saldo Iniziale (by date) whose interval is closed or hole. If the first interval is broken — for instance a lone file whose bank cut the old rows — there is no opening and that balance is only a verification.
  • After the opening, a broken interval keeps the opening and the holes already found, and adds its warning. A hole after a broken one is reported (account_gap with corrected: false) and its end balance is compared, never corrected: the difference is no longer the hole's alone.
  • A set whose files state no balance (CSV only) has no opening and no hole, and the set notice no_balance says the cash is not compared with the bank.

docs.title: 📍 Truth points
docs.text:
Analysis turns the statements into the truth points the gap-fix compares with LibreFolio:

Truth Where it comes from Becomes Opening The opening statement a checkpoint (opening), with the cash and the opening positions End of a hole The Saldo Iniziale that closes a corrected hole a checkpoint (gap), cash only Verification Every Saldo Finale; a Saldo Iniziale that could not open or that closes a hole not corrected; the Liquidità of the securities header at its Data Aggiornamento, only when an account file covers that day a verification: compared, never corrected

The opening positions are the quantity of each title that the transfers from another dossier prove (exact:transfer_in), brought to the opening day the way LibreFolio records it: the transfers up to the day, plus the purchases and redemptions of the pairs recorded by then. A title with a maturity among its pairs has no proof (the file says quantity 0). Until the optional portfolio role exists they are the same rows that are imported, so they are a check on a re-import rather than independent evidence.

docs.title: ✈️ Cash in flight
docs.text:
A pair is recorded by LibreFolio with the operation date of the securities row and booked by the bank with the operation date of the account row. At the end of a day D the ledger holds the pair when securities date ≤ D, the bank when account date ≤ D. A truth point is therefore stated in the terms of the ledger:

cash(D) = bank balance(D)
          + Σ amount of the pairs in the ledger and not yet in the bank   (order on the 17th, debit on the 25th, balance of the 20th)
          − Σ amount of the pairs in the bank and not yet in the ledger   (account row before the securities row)

The symmetric case exists in the real data (the account row one or two days before the securities row). CashTruth.amount = stated + in_flight.

docs.title: 📄 The combined file
docs.text:
combine writes one line per fact (a pair is one line with both halves) plus the truth lines, sorted by operation date (a pair by the securities date) and then the truth lines of that day. Cells are the file's own, but rewritten to a form the parse can read back: dates as dd/mm/yyyy, amounts in the Italian form (1234,56), quantities with a dot (1867.178), even when the XLSX cell was numeric or a date.

Columns, in order: lf_row_kind, lf_zone, lf_reason, lf_checkpoint, lf_source, lf_match_key, lf_value, lf_currency, lf_proof, then securities:<column> for each securities column (Data operazione, Data valuta, Nome, Causale, Prezzo, Quantità, Controvalore, Divisa) and account:<column> for each account column (Data Op., Data Val., Causale, Descrizione, Importo, Divisa).

lf_row_kind When Notes pair securities + account, paired lf_zone is the zone of the account row; lf_match_key is value date\|amount\|currency standalone an account row on its own; a transfer from another dossier; a securities row in_gap lf_reason: in_gap, no_counterpart or ambiguous excluded an unpaired securities row, an unreadable row, a superseded row lf_reason: outside_cash_coverage, not_yet_settled, no_counterpart, ambiguous, unknown_type, invalid, superseded truth_cash the opening (lf_zone=before) and the end of each corrected hole (lf_zone=gap) lf_checkpoint is the day, lf_value the cash in the ledger's terms, lf_source e.g. account#1:start truth_position the opening positions lf_value is the quantity, lf_proof is exact:transfer_in verification see Truth points never a correction

lf_source names the role and the line of the source, with the file number when the role has several files: securities:12, account#2:7, securities:12 + account#2:7 for a pair.

The summary of the table (kept in the file's sidecar and read by the wizard's analysis detail) holds the rows per role, the outcomes, zones and reasons, the segments, the holes, the checkpoints, the verifications, balance_chain (ok, broken or none) and the number of days with an overlap_mismatch.

The dossier and account numbers are never copied; the combined file gets a generated name, not an original's.

docs.title: 🧾 What the parse writes
docs.text:
parse(combined) books each line; the arms are in _booking.py. Every transaction is dated with the operation date — the securities Data operazione for a pair, Data Op. for an account row on its own — never with the value date (the value date only pairs the rows). There is no auto_cash leg anywhere in a combined file: the real cash is the account's.

Line Transactions pair, coupon INTEREST, quantity 0, on the asset named by the securities row; cash = the account amount plus the withholding when the account description spells it (RITENUTA: 13,36), and then a TAX of minus the withholding tagged withholding_tax. Tags import, credit_agricole; description CEDOLA: <name> pair, purchase (ACQ.CONT.SU MERC., SICAV: SOTTOSCR) BUY of the securities quantity; cash = minus the absolute account amount; no DEPOSIT pair, fund redemption SELL of minus the securities quantity; cash = the account amount pair, maturity (TITOLI SCADUTI) The shared model_bond_maturity with the securities price and the position held by the other securities rows: a SELL at par and, when the amount exceeds par, an INTEREST tagged maturity_premium; the cash is the account's; a derived_quantity todo when the nominal is derived standalone, securities transfer_in ADJUSTMENT, cashless, with cost_basis_override (a bond's Prezzo / 100, otherwise Prezzo), description [CAUSALE — successione / transfer-in] …; one ca_succession_transfer_in info notice for all standalone, securities in_gap the same arm as a pair, with the cash of the Controvalore (coupon +, purchase −, redemption +) and no counter-leg standalone, account the account arm as it has been since 1.0 (below) excluded no transaction; one notice per reason with the rows as evidence truth_cash, truth_position, verification checkpoints and verifications of the output (kind is opening when lf_zone is before, else gap)

An asset is a fake id keyed by the lower-cased security name (the securities export has no ISIN); the ISIN that the account row of a pair names links to the same asset, so a coupon seen only on the account, with that ISIN, uses the same id. The number of INTEREST of a set is the number of its coupons, never the double.

pre_checkpoint_policy is "import": the rows before the opening balance are positions (transfers) and cash that belongs to the history, not cash to summarise, so a checkpoint absorbs nothing (absorbed.count == 0, opening_cash == []). On a first import apply_history sets H0 to the date of the oldest parsed transaction. The tag of the plugin (history_tag) is credit_agricole, the same as before 2.0.0, so H0 is computed on the rows already saved with it.

The warnings of a parse are in Italian (the language of the export); the notices of a set (describe_set) are in English and localised by the wizard.

docs.title: 💳 Account rows on their own
docs.text: The account arm (Booking.book_account_row) is the one the plugin has always had, run row by row over the rows that are standalone. Transactions keep the bank's description verbatim (up to 500 characters; maturities compose their own) and are tagged import, credit_agricole and the causale's slug (slug_causale: CEDOLE, DIVIDENDI, PREMI ESTRATTI → cedole_dividendi_premi_estratti).

docs.title: 🗃️ The causale registry
docs.text:
classify_account_row returns (type, cash, tier). Tiers 2 to 4 all book a DEPOSIT or a WITHDRAWAL by sign — the cash is always right — and differ only in what the plugin declares about the row.

Tier Causali Result 1 typed COMMISS./SPESE SU OPERAZ. TITOLI, COMMISSIONI/SPESE, and INTERESSI/COMPETENZE debits TAX when the description contains CAPITAL GAIN, D.LGS 461, 461/97, IMPOSTA, BOLLO or RITENUTA, else FEE; a positive amount is a refund → DEPOSIT 1 typed CEDOLE, DIVIDENDI, PREMI ESTRATTI, and INTERESSI/COMPETENZE credits DIVIDEND when the description says DIVIDEND and carries an ISIN, else INTEREST; a negative amount is a clawback → WITHDRAWAL 1 typed TITOLI SCADUTI O ESTRATTI credits see Matured securities 2 unresolved COMPRAVENDITA TITOLI/FONDI/OPZIONI rows not booked as a trade; GIROCONTO/BONIFICO credits that are fund redemptions by sign, plus a ca_account_trade_unresolved blocker 3 declared cash PAGAMENTO TRAMITE POS, PAGAMENTO UTENZE, PRELIEVO SPORT. AUTOM. ALTRA BANCA, PRELIEVO NOSTRO SPORTELLO AUTOM., ACCREDITO EMOLUMENTI, GIROCONTO/BONIFICO by sign, silently 4 unknown anything else by sign, plus one ca_unknown_causale info notice for all such rows

docs.title: 🔗 Linking rows to a security
docs.text:
• Income that names an ISIN ([A-Z]{2}[A-Z0-9]{9}[0-9]) is linked to an asset keyed isin:<ISIN>, named after the text before the ISIN, without a leading CEDOLA or DIVIDENDO.
  • Securities charges that name an ISIN (SPESE STACCO CEDOLA … TIT: <ISIN> <name> MOV:…) get the same key, named after the text between the ISIN and MOV:. The bank prints that name in full while coupon lines cut it at 19 characters, so asset_id_for keeps the longer name when one is the other cut short (is_truncation_of).
  • A COMMISS./SPESE SU OPERAZ. TITOLI fee or tax that names no ISIN gets a ca_account_charge_unallocated warning todo on asset_id, shown in the charges panel of the correction step: the user assigns it or keeps it on the account.
  • Withholding. An income credit whose description spells RITENUTA: <x> is imported gross (the credited amount plus x), with a separate TAX of −x on the same asset (tag withholding_tax): the two sum back to the credited amount. A clawback is never grossed up. A coupon that is part of a pair gets the same treatment from book_movement.

docs.title: 🔁 Trades on the account
docs.text:
A COMPRAVENDITA TITOLI/FONDI/OPZIONI row carries the money, not the instrument or the quantity. With no securities row to pair with, try_account_trade books a real BUY or SELL only when the file proves it:

  1. Direction — buy words (NOTA INF. ACQ, ACQUIST, SOTTOSC…) or sell words (NOTA INF. VEND, VENDIT, VEND., DISINVEST, RIMBORS), exactly one family, confirmed by the sign: a buy spends, a sale cashes in. Otherwise the reason is no_keyword or sign_mismatch.
  2. Name — after TIT: (bonds) or after the order reference ORD.:<ref> (funds), cut before DOSSIER:, RUB:, DATA: or MOV:. Otherwise no_name.
  3. Quantity — the NOMINALE stated by the coupons of that security among the account rows of the file, indexed by a prepass (build_identity_indexes) and matched by name prefix in either direction, on at least 6 characters. No such coupon → no_quantity; several securities → ambiguous_name; several nominals → ambiguous_nominal.

A resolved trade takes the nominal as its quantity, the coupon's ISIN as its asset key and the tag account_trade. It always gets a ca_account_trade_bundled_amount warning todo on cash with split_hint: "trade_charges", because this layout never separates the price from the charges: compare_nominal is set on buys only, and the split_suggestions name the securities charges booked within ±3 days. A sale also gets ca_account_trade_sell_quantity_presumed on quantity, because the coupon nominal is the whole position.

An unresolved row stays cash (tier 2) with a ca_account_trade_unresolved blocker on asset_id, whose message and evidence comment depend on the reason (trade_fallback_message). It keeps the split_hint, so the split zone opens as soon as the user types the row into a BUY or SELL. In a set, such a row has the outcome standalone with the reason no_counterpart: no securities row was found for it, so the trade is not known from the securities export either.

docs.title: 🏦 Fund redemptions paid by transfer
docs.text:
A fund pays a redemption by wire, so it arrives as a GIROCONTO/BONIFICO credit, like a salary. sct_fund_redemption_name calls it a redemption only when three signals agree:

  1. the ordering party (ORD:<party> DT.ORD:) has at least 8 letters and digits;
  2. the operation text after it contains RIMBORS, DISINVEST or LIQUIDAZ;
  3. the party is named again inside that text — compared on letters and digits only, so a name wrapped across the column width (AMUNDI PRIMO INVES TIMENTO) still matches.

The third signal keeps a tax refund (RIMBORSO IRPEF) or a utility refund out. In a set such a credit is class redemption and pairs with the FONDI: RIMBORSO row of the securities export. Alone, it becomes a tier-2 DEPOSIT whose blocker has the reason fund_redemption: the user turns it into a SELL and enters the units, which the file does not state.

docs.title: 🪦 Matured securities
docs.text:
An account row TITOLI SCADUTI O ESTRATTI reads RIMB.TIT. <name> (<code>). When it has no securities row, the digits of <code> are matched against the ISIN digits of the coupons paid the same day that state a NOMINALE:

  • found → model_bond_maturity(ctv, held_qty=nominal): a SELL of the nominal at par (tag account_maturity) and an INTEREST for the surplus (tag maturity_premium), on the isin:<ISIN> asset;
  • not found → a ca_account_maturity_unlinked warning, and the whole amount as one SELL at par 100 (nominal = cash) on an asset keyed maturity:<code or name> — never a DEPOSIT, so the proceeds close a position instead of inflating paid-in capital.

A paired maturity (above) uses the securities row instead. Both arms call attach_maturity_notices, which puts the amber maturity banner on the asset-create modal.

docs.title: 🔔 Notices and todos
docs.text:
Code Channel Severity Raised when excluded_<reason> notice warning (info for not_yet_settled and superseded) rows left out of the set: one notice per reason, the rows as evidence (reasons in the outcomes table) name_mismatch notice warning a pair whose two names are not compatible ca_securities_unknown_causale notice warning a securities causale is not in the table (reason unknown_type) ca_account_invalid_amount notice warning an account amount cannot be read (row skipped) ca_succession_transfer_in notice info transfers from another dossier (one notice for all) ca_account_maturity_unlinked notice warning an account maturity has no same-day coupon nominal ca_unknown_causale notice info tier-4 rows (one notice for all) ca_securities_empty notice warning the parse produced no transaction and no other notice derived_quantity todo on quantity warning a maturity nominal was derived from Controvalore / Prezzo ca_account_trade_unresolved todo on asset_id blocker every tier-2 row ca_account_trade_bundled_amount todo on cash warning every resolved account trade (split_hint) ca_account_trade_sell_quantity_presumed todo on quantity warning every resolved account sale ca_account_charge_unallocated todo on asset_id warning a securities charge names no ISIN

ca_securities_unknown_causale, ca_account_invalid_amount and ca_unknown_causale carry context.report_issue, so the wizard shows the link open an issue on GitHub under them: they are rows the importer does not know or cannot read (Rows left out).

The notices of the set (describe_set, English, localised by the wizard as importWizard.reportSet.warning.<code>):

Code Raised when empty_member an export has no rows overlap_mismatch two downloads of one role contradict each other on a day (rule M) account_gap a hole; corrected says whether a cash correction is proposed balance_chain_broken a broken interval or two statements of one day that disagree ambiguous rows that could not be paired with certainty (context.rows) no_counterpart rows with no matching row in the other export (context.rows) no_balance an account export is there and none states a balance (info)

The segments of the set shape are the periods the securities exports cover; its gaps are the days of the holes.

docs.title: 🔖 Versions
docs.text:
Version What changed 1.0 – 1.5.0 Single-file plugin. Each export was imported on its own. The securities export booked, for every buy, sale, coupon or premium, an automatic counter-entry (auto_cash) because it has no cash; the account export booked the real cash. Read together the two exports counted each fact twice 2.0.0 Report-set plugin. Both exports are uploaded together; one transaction per fact with the cash of the account; no auto_cash leg; the balances of the XLSX open the cash and a hole becomes a proposed correction. A file read alone raises BRIMSetRequiredError (HTTP 422 set_required), naming the missing role

The tag credit_agricole is unchanged. There is no warning and no clean-up for transactions already imported with 1.x (developer decision, 25/10/2026).

docs.title: 🧪 Samples and tests
docs.text:
• backend/app/services/brim_providers/sample_reports/ holds the synthetic members of two sets, declared in test_sample_sets:
    • credit_agricole-securities.csv + credit_agricole-account.xlsx: a closed month with every kind of fact (a coupon with withholding, a purchase, a placement, a fund redemption, a maturity, a transfer in) and a securities row with no counterpart;
    • credit_agricole-gap-securities.xlsx + credit_agricole-gap-account-1.xlsx + credit_agricole-gap-account-2.xlsx: two account exports with a month in between, which is a hole.
  • backend/test_scripts/test_external/test_brim_credit_agricole.py (./dev.py test external brim-credit-agricole) pins the plugin's rules, with files written under a temporary folder: reading, detection, rule M, classes, pairing, balances and holes, in-flight cash, zones, describe_set, then the combined file and its parse.
  • The generic suite of report-set plugins (./dev.py test external brim-providers) combines every declared set and parses the combined file; a member alone must raise BRIMSetRequiredError.

docs.title: 🏦 Danske Bank Importer
docs.text:
broker_danske_bank imports the equity savings account (osakesäästötili) of Danske Bank Finland from two exports that only make sense together: the custody transactions (XLSX) and the cash statement (CSV). It lives in backend/app/services/brim_providers/broker_danske_bank/plugin.py (plugin_version 1.1.0, 🔬 Alpha — built from the exports of one account, shared in issue #26) and is LibreFolio's reference report-set plugin.

This page covers what is specific to Danske Bank. The generic machinery — membership by upload batch, /sets/preview and /sets/combine, the history start (H0), /gap-fix — is described in BRIM Architecture → Report sets and BRIM Plugin Guide → Multi-report plugins, the wizard side in Import Wizard → Report sets. The user's view is Danske Bank: the plugin's docs_url points there, and so do the set card's How to export it links.

flowchart LR
    K["custody XLSX"] --> A["_Analysis<br/>read · rule M · classes<br/>pairs · zones · proofs"]
    C["cash CSV"] --> A
    A --> T["_TableBuilder<br/>combined CSV"]
    T --> P["_CombinedParser<br/>transactions · todos<br/>notices · truth points"]
    P --> H["apply_history<br/>H0"]
    H --> G["wizard review,<br/>then /gap-fix"]

describe_set and combine both build an _Analysis of the members; combine writes it out through _TableBuilder, and parse reads back only the combined file (_CombinedParser). A custody or cash file parsed alone raises BRIMSetRequiredError, naming the other role.

docs.title: 🗂️ Exports, roles and detection
docs.text:
Role Export (wizard name) Extension max_history Coverage axis must_cover custody Securities transactions — eBanking Sijoitukset → Tapahtumat .xlsx P1Y trade date (Kauppapäivä) — cash Cash statement — the account transactions of the account's cash account .csv P5Y value date (Pvm) custody

Both roles are required and multiple. The plugin sets settlement_lag_business_days to 5 and pre_checkpoint_policy to summarize, and keeps the default history tag, danske_bank.

Detection. _file_kind(), behind can_parse and detect_role, answers custody, cash, combined or None:

  • .xlsx (and .xlsm) — the first worksheet with data, read with openpyxl (values only), is custody when one of its first 20 rows (_HEADER_SCAN_ROWS) names every required custody column.
  • .csv — decoded with the shared TEXT_ENCODINGS fallback (UTF-8 with or without BOM, Windows-1252, Latin-1) and split on ;. A first row holding lf_row_kind, lf_source, custody:Toimeksiantotyyppi and cash:Saaja/Maksaja is combined; otherwise a header among the first 20 rows naming every required cash column makes it cash.
  • Headers match case- and space-insensitively, a literal <br/> counting as a space (_norm). Any read error means «not ours».

can_parse accepts the three kinds, detect_role only the first two (detection_priority 100). A downloaded combined file uploaded again is therefore an original without a role: the preview reports it as unknown_role. No other plugin's can_parse accepts the sample exports, so the wizard never offers Read alone with ‹plugin› for them.

Export Required columns Also read custody Kauppapäivä, Arvopäivä, Sijoituskohde, Määrä, Kurssi, Summa, Tila, Toimeksiantotyyppi Palkkio sis. Alv; the currency of Summa — Valuutta, or the unnamed column right after Summa (default EUR); Säilytystili, the custody account, read for the account check only and never copied cash Pvm, Saaja/Maksaja, Määrä, Saldo, Tila Tarkastus. There is no currency column: the account is in euro

Dates are d.m.yyyy. Numbers may use a space, NBSP or narrow NBSP as thousands separator, a comma or a dot as decimal separator, and a Unicode minus (_to_decimal).

describe_member() reports rows and coverage. A custody file also gets an account_fingerprint, the SHA-256 of its sorted Säilytystili values: custody files of different accounts make the preview's mixed_accounts, and the set cannot be combined. Several accounts inside one custody file only raise mixed_accounts_in_file.

docs.title: 📈 Custody rows
docs.text:
_classify_custody(): a Tila other than Toteutettu is status; a row without trade date, value date, name or a non-zero quantity, or valued before its trade date, is invalid. Then the order type decides:

Toimeksiantotyyppi Signs Class Rajakurssi, Päivän kurssi, Pikakauppa Määrä > 0 and Summa < 0, or Määrä < 0 and Summa > 0; a Kurssi is required buy, sell Tuotto Määrä > 0 and Summa > 0 income Jakautuminen, vanha Määrä < 0, no Summa demerger_old Jakautuminen, uusi Määrä > 0, no Summa demerger_new anything else — unknown_type

A known order type with other signs is invalid.

docs.title: 💳 Cash rows
docs.text:
_classify_cash(): the label (Saaja/Maksaja) Varaus is checked first, before Tila: it makes the row reservation, whatever its Tila. A reservation is a hold the bank replaces with the booked movement: a known row, left out without a notice (Finnish notices). Then a Tila other than Toteutunut is status; a row without a date, or with a zero or missing amount, is invalid. Then the label and the sign decide (_cash_label_class):

Label Sign Class Becomes Osto <name> − buy half of a pair Myynti <name> + sell half of a pair <name> <10-digit reference> + income half of a pair first word Nosto − withdrawal WITHDRAWAL first word Vero − tax TAX first word starting with Palvelumaksu − fee FEE first word Korko or Hyvityskorko + interest INTEREST any other credit + deposit DEPOSIT, listed by the deposit_assumed notice: only the holder can pay into an equity savings account any other debit, or a known word with the wrong sign unknown_type excluded

docs.title: 🧾 What the parse writes
docs.text:
Combined line Transaction Date Quantity Cash pair of a trade BUY or SELL custody Kauppapäivä custody Määrä cash Määrä pair of a Tuotto DIVIDEND custody Kauppapäivä 0 cash Määrä standalone cash row DEPOSIT, WITHDRAWAL, TAX, FEE or INTEREST Pvm — Määrä standalone demerger line ADJUSTMENT custody Kauppapäivä custody Määrä —

The operation date (1.1.0, lot B-52): every transaction is dated with the day the operation was made, the plugin guide's rule The operation date, and only settled rows under Import philosophy. What comes from the custody export takes its trade date, Kauppapäivä — a purchase made on the 27th is a BUY of the 27th, whenever the bank moves its cash; for a Tuotto and a demerger line the two custody dates are equal in the bank's exports. A cash-only row has no other date than its Pvm. Before 1.1.0, pairs took the cash Pvm and demerger lines Arvopäivä, the value date. Pairing, zones, not_yet_settled and deferred_rows still read the value date, because the bank moves the cash on that day; the truth points bridge the two dates (In flight).

Cash is always EUR, taken as written. Every transaction is tagged import and danske_bank, demerger lines also demerger. Each security gets one fake asset id per normalised name, with the name as its only identifier (extracted_name): the exports carry no ISIN and no ticker.

summarized, deferred and excluded lines write no transaction (the last two feed the notices). On a first import, the standalone rows of the before zone are written but dated before H0, so the review hides them (Import Wizard → Rows before H0).

Sets imported before 1.1.0. The wizard's duplicate check compares exact dates (BRIM Architecture → Deduplication Logic): a set imported with 1.0.x and imported again brings its trades back on their trade date, a few days earlier than the value date they were saved with, so the check does not recognise them. No code bridges the two (the developer, 19/10/2026: the next imports carry the new date, so after the switch everything settles). The transition, once: delete the Danske transactions those files created — the gap_fix corrections included, so that the new import is a first import again — and import the whole set again, or import only from the day after the last imported day. The user page says the same.

docs.title: 🔗 Pairing trades with their cash
docs.text:
_pair_rows() pairs buy, sell and income rows only, on a key of value date, amount to the cent, currency and class — Arvopäivä, Summa and the custody currency against Pvm, Määrä and EUR. The class carries the direction.

  • One custody row and one cash row on a key pair.
  • More than 8 candidates on either side (MAX_MATCH_CANDIDATES) are all ambiguous.
  • Interchangeable candidates — the same name, quantity, price, trade date and order type on the custody side, one label on the cash side — pair in file order, so identical partial fills stay two trades.
  • Otherwise _best_assignment() keeps the assignment with the most compatible names, but only when every best assignment imports the same trades; if not, every candidate of the key is ambiguous. The plugin never guesses.

Two names are compatible when one normalised name is a prefix of the other, because the cash statement truncates its labels. The name is a check, not a key: a pair whose names differ still pairs, and the parse lists it in the name_mismatch notice.

Several files of one role (rule M, _RoleMerge): each day belongs to the file with the latest coverage covering it — custody files by trade date, cash files by value date. The other files' rows of that day count once when identical, and become excluded (superseded) when they differ; describe_set then warns overlap_mismatch.

docs.title: 🗺️ Segments, zones and outcomes
docs.text:
• Segments — the custody files' trade-date spans, merged when they overlap or touch (_raw_segments). Two spans with a hole between them stay apart only when the cash statement proves trades in the hole: an unmatched cash trade valued after the first span and no later than 5 business days after the eve of the second (_proven_segments). Otherwise they merge, hole included. Each hole left between two segments is a gap (gaps(), the preview's gap warning).
  • Checkpoint — the eve of each segment, the day before its oldest trade date (_timeline), the first one included: also when the cash statement starts later (A13). Before 1.1.0 the first one moved to the eve of the first booked cash day.
  • Window — from the day after the checkpoint to the segment's last day plus 5 business days (LAG_BUSINESS_DAYS), capped at the next checkpoint. Its border is the first 5 business days after the checkpoint. Business days skip weekends only: holidays are not known.
  • Zones of a value date (_zone): before (up to the first checkpoint), window, gap (after a window, up to the next checkpoint) and after (beyond the last window).

Every row gets exactly one outcome (_Analysis._settle):

Row Outcome Custody row and cash row on one key pair Deposit, withdrawal, tax, fee or interest standalone, imported with its own date Demerger line standalone Cash trade or income without counterpart summarized in the zone's checkpoint in before and gap, and in its own segment's checkpoint inside the border; valued after the segment's last day, summarized in the next segment's checkpoint, or deferred when there is none; deferred in after; elsewhere excluded (no_counterpart) Custody trade or income without counterpart excluded: not_yet_settled (valued after the cash statement's last day), outside_cash_coverage (outside the statement's spans), else no_counterpart Ambiguous; superseded; status, reservation, unknown_type, invalid excluded with that reason

The cash rows of the before zone — standalone, ambiguous or unknown_type — are also absorbed by the first checkpoint. The full matrix, zone by zone, is in the plugin guide, under Zones and outcomes. When the cash statement starts after the custody export, the opening's border starts on the custody export's eve, which leaves some cash trades no_counterpart (A13).

The wizard's Matching securities ↔ cash reads the combined summary: the outcomes as chips (pairs, standalone rows, summarised in a checkpoint, with the next import, excluded) and one row per reason (Import Wizard → Step analyze):

lf_reason Wizard label For Danske no_counterpart no counterpart a trade or income in one file only, inside a window ambiguous ambiguous candidates that cannot be told apart not_yet_settled not settled yet a custody trade valued after the cash statement's last day outside_cash_coverage settled before the cash statement starts a custody trade valued outside the cash statement's spans; valued before its first day, it belongs to the opening (A13) status not executed or not booked a custody Tila other than Toteutettu, or a cash Tila other than Toteutunut on a row that is no Varaus: the excluded_status warning, with the link to open an issue reservation reserved, not booked a cash row labelled Varaus: no notice, one log line unknown_type unknown type an order type or a label the plugin does not know invalid invalid missing or inconsistent values superseded replaced by a newer file rule M

docs.title: 📄 The combined file
docs.text:
_TableBuilder writes one line per source row — a pair is one line — plus the truth rows (truth_cash, truth_position, verification), sorted by day, the data lines before the truth rows of the same day. The columns are the nine lf_* columns, then the verbatim custody:<column> and cash:<column> values; the custody account (Säilytystili) is never copied.

The core writes the file (write_combined_csv: UTF-8 with BOM, ;) under a generated name, Danske Bank — combined <first day>…<last day>.csv, because the cash statement's own file name may carry an account number. What each lf_* column holds is in the plugin guide, under combine is pure.

summary, kept in the sidecar as combine_summary, holds rows per role, outcomes, zones, reasons, segments, gaps, checkpoints, verifications, balance_chain (ok or broken) and overlap_mismatch_days. combine refuses custody files without a dated row (BRIMParseError, so a 422 combine_failed).

plugin_version covers combine and parse alike: bump it whenever either output changes for the same files. The existing combined files then show To re-combine, and the next analysis rebuilds them.

docs.title: 🏁 Starting point and «After the gap»
docs.text:
One checkpoint per segment, on its eve: the first is opening, the others gap. The wizard titles them Starting point · ‹date› and After the gap · ‹date›. On a later import, apply_history() drops the checkpoints before the eve of H0, turns the ones from H0 on into gap checkpoints and removes what H0 already represents (The history start (H0)).

  • Cash — the cash statement's running balance at the end of the checkpoint day, plus the cash of the border rows summarised in it: trades made before the custody export and settled after the checkpoint (border_cash); plus the cash in flight that day (In flight). For an opening that precedes the statement, the balance is the statement's first balance (A13). Any other day the statement does not cover gets no cash (not_covered).
  • Absorbed rows — every cash row the checkpoint summarises (lf_checkpoint), with date, amount and label. For the opening checkpoint, opening_cash is the checkpoint's cash minus their total: the balance before them. The gap-fix explanation reads both.

Positions come from proofs inside the segment's window, each brought back to the checkpoint by removing the movements imported in between (by value date), then adding the quantity of the security in flight that day — at most one per security:

  • E1 — a Tuotto states the shares that earned it: exact. Discarded when another movement of the security falls in the 30 days up to its trade date (recent_trades), when those 30 days start before both the segment and the cash statement (window_not_covered), or when an excluded row of the security lies between the checkpoint and the proof (excluded_rows).
  • E2 — the old line of a demerger states the whole holding: exact. Discarded on a same-day movement of the security (same_day_movement) or on excluded rows.
  • E3 — when no exact proof holds, selling more than was bought since the checkpoint proves at least the largest shortfall (at_least). Discarded on excluded rows.
  • Exact proofs that disagree, or that give a negative quantity, are all discarded (conflict), and E3 is tried instead.

An excluded row never discards a proof when it belongs to the opening: a custody trade settled before the cash statement starts (_absorbed_by_opening, A13). A discarded proof is written discarded:<rule>:<reason> in lf_proof and listed by the proof_discarded notice. Danske never states a unit_cost.

docs.title: ✅ End-of-period check
docs.text:
One verification, on the last day of the last segment — or on the cash statement's last day when it ends first — provided the running balance covers that day. Its cash is the running balance plus the cash in flight that day (In flight), and the wizard titles it End-of-period check · ‹date›. It is never a checkpoint: the next import brings the not_yet_settled and deferred trades one by one, and a correction there would count them twice (the safety rule of the plugin guide).

The running balance (_chain) takes the booked rows (every class but status, reservation and invalid: _UNBOOKED_CLASSES) by value date — within a day in reverse file order, since the statement lists the newest rows first — and checks each day against Saldo, row by row or at least as a day total. A day that does not add up is a break: the chain goes on from that day's last Saldo, and the cash of every checkpoint becomes a verification instead (balance_chain_broken, warned by both describe_set and the parse).

docs.title: ✈️ In flight
docs.text:
A pair is recorded on its trade date, while the bank moves its cash on its value date, a few business days later. In between, the trade is in flight: LibreFolio already holds it, the bank's balance does not yet. So every truth at a day D adds what is in flight at D (_Analysis.in_flight(day), 1.1.0): the paired purchases and sales with trade date ≤ D < value date — their cash, a purchase negative and a sale positive, and their quantity per security. It applies to:

  • the cash of every checkpoint, and the verification a broken chain gives in its place;
  • the positions of every checkpoint, each for its own security;
  • the end-of-period verification.

The gap-fix then compares LibreFolio, in operation-date terms, with the bank, whose balances are in value-date terms, without false corrections. Only the imported purchases and sales count: a trade left out (not_yet_settled, outside_cash_coverage…) or summarised is never in flight, nor is a Tuotto, whose two dates are equal. The opening never has anything in flight, since every trade of the set comes after it; a gap checkpoint or the end-of-period check may.

docs.title: 🕰️ A cash statement that starts later (A13)
docs.text:
When the cash statement starts after the custody export — case A13 of the design (design-phase00BrimReportSets.md) — the set still opens on the eve of the custody export's oldest trade date, like any set (_timeline): a trade is recorded on its trade date, so the opening must come before every one of them (the developer, 20/10/2026). Until 1.0.2 it opened on the eve of the statement's first booked day.

  • The opening's cash is the statement's first balance, in value-date terms: the balance before its first booked row, on the eve of its first booked day (_checkpoint_lines), plus the border rows as for any checkpoint. Nothing is in flight then.
  • A trade made before the statement starts and settled inside it pairs as usual: it is imported as a BUY or SELL on its trade date, after the opening, with its true cost. The opening's positions subtract it, like any movement between the opening and a proof.
  • A trade settled between the opening and the statement's first day has no cash row. It stays excluded (outside_cash_coverage, with the same excluded_outside_cash_coverage warning as before), but its cash is inside the statement's first balance: it lands in the opening, a few days before the day it was made — at most as many days as the statement starts after the custody export. The developer accepted this explicitly (20/10/2026). Its units belong to the opening too: the row no longer discards a proof of its security (_absorbed_by_opening), so a later proof — a Tuotto, a demerger's old line, a sale of more than was bought — brings them into the opening's position. A security with no proof gets no opening position, as anywhere else.
  • A sale straddling the statement's start, for a security with no exact proof — the «at least» proof E3 gives the opening at least the shares sold, so the position never goes negative (an unchanged rule). Only another excluded row of the security between the opening and the sale — a row of unknown status, an invalid or ambiguous one — discards E3: the security then has no opening position (proof_discarded), and saving refuses the sale's day with balanceAssetNegative unless the broker allows shorting. In such a set that interval now starts on the custody export's eve, no longer on the statement's.
  • A side effect, rare. The opening's border — the 5 business days after the checkpoint — now starts on the custody export's eve too. A cash trade row with no custody counterpart, valued after that border and no later than the segment's last day, is excluded (no_counterpart, a warning) instead of being summarised into the opening: the custody export covers its day, and its row is missing there.

docs.title: 🧮 The gap_fix corrections
docs.text:
compute_gap_fix() (backend/app/services/brim/brim_gap_fix.py) is generic (Plugin Guide → report sets, Import Wizard → Step gapFix); with this plugin's truth points it gives:

  • For each checkpoint in date order, LibreFolio's state at the end of the day: the broker's saved transactions (without pending deletions) plus the editor's unsaved rows, the wizard's selection and the corrections proposed at the earlier checkpoints. Transactions entered by hand count like imported ones.
  • Cash — a difference above 0.01 € becomes a Deposit (DEPOSIT, the bank holds more) or a Withdrawal (WITHDRAWAL, it holds less), dated on the checkpoint, that brings the cash to the checkpoint's: the cash statement's balance, with what is in flight.
  • Positions — an exact position gets an ADJUSTMENT of the difference, positive or negative; an at_least one only the missing part. With no unit_cost from Danske, every positive adjustment carries the blocker todo gap_fix_cost on cost_basis_override: the wizard tags it cost to enter, and the bulk editor waits for the cost. A negative adjustment carries no cost. A position whose security is still unresolved is left out (unresolved_asset).
  • Tags import, danske_bank and gap_fix; description Gap-fix <date> — Danske Bank: <what> at the end of the day, as stated by the bank.
  • The end-of-period verification is compared (ok within 0.01 €), never corrected.

Once saved, a correction counts in H0 from the day after its date. A later set whose segment covers its date gets the preview warning covers_gap_fix (delete the correction after the import, or the cash counts twice); a segment that ends before H0 gets before_history_segment and is not imported.

docs.title: 💶 The commission estimate
docs.text:
The exports give one total per trade: the fee column (Palkkio sis. Alv) is always 0, and the commission is inside Summa. Every paired purchase and sale therefore gets the warning todo danske_trade_charges_included on cash (_charges_todo); dividends get none.

  • Context — split_hint: "trade_charges", so the Corrections step owns the row (isCashSplitWarning) and every trade needs a decision; compare_nominal: false; cash (the absolute amount), currency, row, split_suggestions, and charges when the estimate is plausible.
  • Estimate — gross = absolute quantity × Kurssi, rounded to the cent; charges = absolute amount − gross for a purchase, gross − absolute amount for a sale. It is plausible when 0 ≤ charges ≤ max(15 €, gross ÷ 100): the first suggestion then gives both figures, valid if the price is in euro. Otherwise it says the price may be quoted in another currency, so the commission cannot be computed from the file.
  • The second suggestion always points to the trade confirmation in eBanking.

docs.title: ✂️ Demergers
docs.text:
Jakautuminen, vanha and Jakautuminen, uusi lines are never paired: booked, with the right signs, they become cashless ADJUSTMENTs in any zone, dated on Kauppapäivä (equal to Arvopäivä in the bank's exports; Arvopäivä before 1.1.0) and tagged demerger.

  • New line — blocker todo demerger on cost_basis_override: the file gives no acquisition cost. A demerger is tax-neutral in Finland, and the old cost is split among the new shares in the ratio the Tax Administration publishes. The bulk editor's Save All waits for it.
  • Old line — warning todo demerger_old_leg on quantity: it removes the whole holding without moving its cost to the new lines, so invested capital does not drop by itself.

Neither todo enters the Corrections step: a cost-basis blocker belongs to the bulk editor, and the old-line warning has no split_hint. The old line is also proof E2 of the holding.

docs.title: 🇫🇮 Finnish notices
docs.text:
The parse speaks the language of the files: notice messages, todo messages and evidence comments are in Finnish. Evidence tables are titled Arvopaperitapahtumat (custody columns) and Tilitapahtumat (cash columns), with the line numbers of the combined file.

Notice Severity Says excluded_<reason> warning One per exclusion reason, with its rows: they are not imported. Every reason but not_yet_settled (an info note), status (its own row) and reservation (no notice). No report_issue excluded_status warning The rows whose Tila the plugin does not know (status): not imported. context.report_issue is true, so the wizard shows the link open an issue on GitHub under the message, which asks the user to open one if the rows are real movements, so that the plugin learns the case (the plugin guide's rule Known rows quietly, unknown rows loudly, under Import philosophy) excluded_not_yet_settled info Custody trades valued after the cash statement's last day: not imported this time, they come with the next import. A note since N74, no longer a warning: nothing is wrong (the plugin guide's rule The operation date, and only settled rows, under Import philosophy) deferred_rows info Cash trades after the last custody day come with the next import name_mismatch warning Paired trades whose names differ: check them proof_discarded info Holdings the files could not prove reliably (context.proofs) balance_chain_broken warning The statement's balances are only compared, never used for corrections deposit_assumed info Credits read as deposits: check them

A reservation (reservation, in _SILENT_EXCLUSIONS) gives no notice: the parse writes one backend log line, logger.info with its reason and count, and the rows keep their place in the set's accounting: excluded lines of the combined file, counted in the summary's reasons and labelled reserved, not booked (importWizard.reportSet.reason.reservation). status is the one reason in _REPORTED_EXCLUSIONS, the only excluded_<reason> notice with report_issue.

The todo codes — danske_trade_charges_included, demerger, demerger_old_leg — are in the contract suite's KNOWN_REASON_CODES. The set warnings of describe_set (empty_member, mixed_accounts_in_file, overlap_mismatch, gap, balance_chain_broken) and the gap-fix todo gap_fix_cost are written in English and localised by the wizard (importWizard.reportSet.warning.<code>, importWizard.reportSet.gapFix.todo.<code>).

docs.title: 🚦 Set statuses
docs.text:
Where Status For a Danske set /sets/preview, per role present, missing, excess excess never occurs: both roles are multiple /sets/preview, complete every required role present, no excess, no mixed accounts mixed accounts can only come from custody files /sets/preview, missing the period a missing export must cover a missing cash statement: from the eve of the first custody trade date to the last one; a missing custody export: no period Step upload after an upload, Next stays once on upload while a set of the session is incomplete names the missing export, its extension and its period Set card (data-set-status) loading Checking…, complete Complete, incomplete A file is missing or Cannot be combined, error Check failed Cannot be combined means mixed accounts; Already analysed is added when a parsed combined file of exactly these members exists Files table Set of ‹date›, Incomplete, Combined, Used in a combined file, To re-combine Import Wizard → Badges

The cash role's coverage warnings (must_cover: custody) — coverage_starts_late when the statement starts after the eve of the first custody trade date (the set still opens on that eve: A13), coverage_ends_early when it ends before the last one — never block the set. How the user changes a set (Read as, Remove from the set) is generic: Import Wizard → How a set is read.

docs.title: 🔧 Generic CSV Provider
docs.text:
The Generic CSV Provider (broker_generic_csv) is the fallback import plugin for BRIM. It accepts any CSV file that follows the column conventions below — even if it does not come from a specifically supported broker.

One file per broker

Generic CSV must use one separate file per broker. Each file is assigned exactly one broker; never combine multiple brokers into one flat CSV. The wizard still allows multiple files and brokers, and multiple currencies for a single broker are valid — this is not one file per currency. This reflects the current parser flow, where broker_id is passed per file/parse, not a new restriction on monthly files.

docs.title: 🤖 Tip: Use an LLM to write your conversion script
docs.text:
The fastest way to import data from an unsupported source is to paste this entire page into an LLM and ask it to write a Python script that transforms your data into the Generic CSV format.

Suggested prompt

Here is the LibreFolio Generic CSV format specification:

[paste this page]

I have data in this format: 

[paste your file's header row and 2–3 sample rows]

Write a Python script that reads my file and produces a valid LibreFolio Generic CSV.

The LLM will produce a working script. Import the output CSV directly via BRIM.

Watch for sign convention errors — this is the most common mistake. See Sign Conventions below.

docs.title: ⭐ Key Features
docs.text:
• Header Auto-Detection: Does not rely on fixed column names — maintains a dictionary of common synonyms per field.
  • Flexible Date Parsing: Tries YYYY-MM-DD, DD/MM/YYYY, MM/DD/YYYY, and others automatically.
  • Flexible Number Parsing: Handles both US (1,234.56) and European (1.234,56) formats.
  • Transaction Type Mapping: Maps keywords (buy, acquisto, compra, …) to the TransactionType enum.
  • Low Priority: detection_priority = 0, so specific high-confidence plugins are always tried first.

docs.title: 📋 Column Mapping Reference
docs.text:
Column Required Description date ✅ Always Transaction date. Accepts 2023-12-31, 31/12/2023, etc. type ✅ Always One of: BUY, SELL, DIVIDEND, INTEREST, DEPOSIT, WITHDRAWAL, FEE, TAX, ADJUSTMENT quantity Depends on type Number of units. See Sign Conventions. amount Depends on type Net cash impact. See Sign Conventions. currency Optional ISO 4217 code (EUR, USD). Defaults to EUR. asset Depends on type Asset identifier. See Asset Identifier. description Optional Free text. Used as fallback for asset name resolution when no identifier is available.

TRANSFER, FX_CONVERSION and CASH_TRANSFER are rejected

Paired-leg types (TRANSFER, FX_CONVERSION, CASH_TRANSFER) require two transactions linked by link_uuid, which a flat CSV cannot express. The parser raises Unknown transaction type (or an explicit pairing error) for them. Use manual entry or a broker-specific plugin for paired movements.

docs.title: 🔢 Sign Conventions
docs.text:
This is the most common mistake when writing conversion scripts

LibreFolio uses an investor perspective for signs:

  • quantity: positive when you receive units, negative when you deliver units
  • amount: positive when cash enters your account, negative when cash leaves your account

docs.title: 📋 Per-type quick reference
docs.text:
Type quantity sign amount sign Notes BUY + (receive units) − (pay cash) e.g. quantity=10, amount=-1500.00 SELL − (deliver units) + (receive cash) e.g. quantity=-1, amount=+62.36 DIVIDEND none (0 or empty) + Cash distribution received INTEREST none + Interest income received DEPOSIT none + Cash entering the broker account WITHDRAWAL none − Cash leaving the broker account FEE none − Commission or fee paid TAX none − Tax or withholding paid ADJUSTMENT + or − must be empty Quantity-only correction (splits, gifts, inheritance seeding). No cash movement.

Inherited cost basis (WAC) is PER-UNIT

An ADJUSTMENT row that seeds an inherited or transferred position (you owned it before, with a known purchase cost) carries a frozen cost basis. The generic CSV has no cost_basis column, so the import wizard prompts you to fill it ("Missing inherited per-unit cost basis (WAC)"). Only a row with a positive quantity is flagged: an ADJUSTMENT taking units out has no value (developer decision N78-1), so it takes no cost basis. Enter the cost per single unit (e.g. 42.50 for a share bought at €42.50), not the position's total value. The engine multiplies it by quantity; a total entered here inflates the cost basis by a factor of quantity. For bonds, quantity is the face value and the per-unit cost is near 1.0.

docs.title: 🏷️ Asset Identifier
docs.text:
The asset column accepts:

  • Ticker (e.g. AAPL, VWCE) — for exchange-listed securities
  • ISIN (e.g. US0378331005) — preferred when available; unambiguous across exchanges
  • Name / description (e.g. VIA SILONE, MARINA DI SCARLINO) — for non-listed assets such as P2P loans, real estate, or anything without a market code

First import and asset matching

CSV import does not create assets or choose a provider automatically. Create a missing asset explicitly (a provider is optional); an existing asset can be selected manually or matched automatically when its saved identifiers give a unique match. An issuance/CUM ISIN can differ from the traded ISIN, and tickers can be ambiguous. Keep the appropriate primary and alternate identifiers on the asset so later imports can recognize it.

Non-listed assets (P2P loans, crowdfunding, real estate)

Use a consistent name string as the identifier (e.g. the project name). During BRIM import review you will be asked to map it — choose asset type OTHER since these are not exchange-traded instruments.

If the BUY transaction has no obvious identifier in a dedicated column, extract the project name from the description field in your conversion script.

docs.title: 🔀 When to Use Each Transaction Type
🔀 Multi-leg broker rows
docs.text:
Some broker events are one source row but several LibreFolio transactions. The correct model is to emit multiple TXCreateItems on the same date rather than hiding economics inside one row:

Broker event LibreFolio transactions Securities-only cash buy DEPOSIT for funding + BUY for the security Securities-only sale/redemption SELL for the security + WITHDRAWAL for cash swept away Bond maturity above par SELL at par principal + INTEREST for the above-par premium/FOI amount Portfolio snapshot seed DEPOSIT for cash when present + one cashless ADJUSTMENT per holding

This mirrors shipped broker plugins such as Intesa Sanpaolo (snapshot seed) and Crédit Agricole (automatic cash counter-entries and bond maturity split).

docs.title: 🤝 P2P lending / crowdfunding patterns
docs.text:
P2P platforms often issue a single report row that bundles capital repayment and interest. You need to split this into two transactions for LibreFolio:

Platform event LibreFolio transactions Principal repayment only SELL (quantity=−fraction, amount=+principal) Interest only INTEREST (amount=+interest) Principal + interest on same row Two rows: SELL at exact cost basis + INTEREST for the earnings Tax on interest TAX (amount=−tax, same date as interest)

Example: P2P project repayment

Project "VIA SILONE": bought 1 unit at €3,005. Partial repayment of €300.50 capital + €15.00 interest.

date,type,quantity,amount,currency,asset,description
2024-06-01,SELL,-0.100000,300.50,EUR,VIA SILONE,Rimborso parziale capitali
2024-06-01,INTEREST,,15.00,EUR,VIA SILONE,Interessi progetto VIA SILONE

The SELL quantity is −300.50 / 3005 = −0.100000 — the fraction of the 1-unit position being returned.

docs.title: ↩️ Storno / reversal of a broker error
docs.text:
When a broker incorrectly credits an amount and then reverses it, you have two options:

Option A — Clean history (recommended when the error and reversal are close in time)

Delete both the erroneous credit and the reversal from your CSV. If they were on the same day, just net the amounts: record only the true net value as a single transaction.

This keeps your portfolio charts clean with no artificial spikes.

Option B — Exact ledger (when the two events are weeks or months apart)

Record the reversal as the opposite transaction of the original: - If the error was a SELL (cash in), the reversal is a WITHDRAWAL (cash out, same amount negative) - If the error was a DEPOSIT, the reversal is a WITHDRAWAL

Do NOT use ADJUSTMENT for cash reversals

ADJUSTMENT must have an empty amount — it is strictly for quantity-only corrections (stock splits, share gifts). Using ADJUSTMENT for a cash reversal will leave the cash balance wrong.

docs.title: 💸 Fees and taxes
docs.text:
FEE and TAX are cash-only transactions (no quantity, no asset required):

date,type,amount,currency,description
2024-06-01,TAX,-28.31,EUR,Ritenuta d'acconto su interessi
2024-06-01,FEE,-1.50,EUR,Commissione operativa

docs.title: 🔍 How It Works: A Deeper Look
1️⃣ Column Detection (_detect_columns)
docs.text:
Maps the CSV's header row to LibreFolio's standard fields using a synonym dictionary:

HEADER_MAPPINGS = {
    "date": ["date", "data", "settlement_date", ...],
    "type": ["type", "tipo", "operation", ...],
    "asset": ["asset", "symbol", "ticker", "isin", ...],
    # ...
}

Each header is trimmed and lower-cased before the lookup (csv_col.lower().strip()). Headers that match no synonym are ignored, and when two headers map to the same field the leftmost wins.

The same map drives detection: can_parse — through cannot_parse_reason — accepts a .csv only when both date and type are mapped, so the wizard offers the plugin only for such files. If the user forces it on another file, parse_file refuses it with Plugin 'Generic CSV' cannot parse file '<file name>': required column 'date' not found in the CSV header (HTTP 400), and the file moves to failed. Each refusal also has a code the import wizard translates — csv_only, file_unreadable, no_header_row, missing_columns (see Saying why with a code).

docs.title: 2️⃣ Row Parsing (_parse_row)
docs.text:
1. Extract Values via column_map
  2. Parse Date — tries multiple strptime formats
  3. Parse Type — looks up lowercase string in TYPE_MAPPINGS
  4. Parse Numbers — handles US and European decimal formats
  5. Handle Assets — classifies identifier as ticker/ISIN/name; assigns consistent fake asset IDs for batch mapping in BRIM review

Errors. An exception raised for a row — an empty or unreadable date, an unknown type, a TRANSFER (refused: it needs a link_uuid pair), a currency code that fails the ISO 4217 check — becomes the warning Row N: <message> (the header is row 1) and the row is skipped. A row that parses but breaks a business rule (signs, missing cash; see validate_transaction_business_rules) is not created either: _create_transaction records it in validation_issues. An asset-required type with an empty asset gets the placeholder identifier UNKNOWN_ROW_<n>, to be mapped in the review. The EUR default applies only when no currency column is mapped: with the column present, an empty cell on a row with an amount fails the ISO 4217 check, so that row is skipped. A file that yields no transaction adds the warning No valid transactions found in file.

docs.title: 📐 3. The "Gold Standard" Example
docs.text:
The Generic CSV Provider is the perfect starting point for a new broker plugin. Copy its structure and:

  1. Increase detection_priority to 100
  2. Add a can_parse() method to reliably detect your broker's file
  3. Customize HEADER_MAPPINGS and TYPE_MAPPINGS
  4. Refine parsing for any broker-specific quirks

docs.title: 📌 Complete Example Row by Row
docs.text:
This example shows a P2P portfolio lifecycle on a single platform (adapted from a real Recrowd import):

date,type,quantity,amount,currency,asset,description
2022-11-03,DEPOSIT,,6015.00,EUR,,Bonifico iniziale
2022-11-03,BUY,1,-3005.00,EUR,VIA SILONE,Investimento progetto VIA SILONE
2022-11-05,BUY,1,-2005.00,EUR,MARINA DI SCARLINO,Investimento progetto MARINA DI SCARLINO
2023-08-01,SELL,-0.031102,62.36,EUR,MARINA DI SCARLINO,Rimborso parziale capitali
2023-08-01,INTEREST,,15.20,EUR,MARINA DI SCARLINO,Interessi parziali
2023-08-01,TAX,,-3.95,EUR,,Ritenuta acconto interessi
2023-12-18,SELL,-1.000000,1005.00,EUR,EX ALBERGO VELA,Restituzione capitali completi
2023-12-18,INTEREST,,108.87,EUR,EX ALBERGO VELA,Interessi finali
2023-12-18,TAX,,-28.31,EUR,,Ritenuta 26% su interessi
2024-06-30,WITHDRAWAL,,-360.87,EUR,,Prelievo verso conto personale

Key points demonstrated:

  • DEPOSIT: positive amount, no asset, no quantity
  • BUY: positive quantity (receive units), negative amount (pay cash)
  • SELL: negative quantity (deliver units), positive amount (receive cash)
  • INTEREST: positive amount, asset optional, no quantity
  • TAX: negative amount, no quantity, no asset required
  • WITHDRAWAL: negative amount, no quantity, no asset

docs.text:
This page lists all the broker import plugins (BRIM Providers) currently available in LibreFolio.

Provider Code Formats Status Notes Interactive Brokers broker_ibkr CSV 🧪 Beta Reads an Activity Flex Query CSV whose first line holds the quoted Buy/Sell, TradeDate, ISIN and IBCommission columns (can_parse): buys and sells with an ISIN, each commission as a separate FEE. Rows without an ISIN (currency trades) are listed in a warning with a link to open an issue, and not imported; no dividends, taxes or cash movements. Degiro broker_degiro CSV ✅ Stable Account Statement CSV in any language, read by column position; currency conversions become linked FX_CONVERSION pairs (see Linked pairs). Notices in the file's language (EN, NL, DE, FR, ES; English otherwise). eToro broker_etoro CSV 🧪 Beta Reads the account activity CSV whose header holds Date, Type, Details, Amount, Units and Realized Equity: opened and closed positions as buys and sells, dividends, interest, deposits, withdrawals, and withdrawal and conversion fees. Ticker and currency come from Details (SYMBOL/CURRENCY). A CFD position is read like any other position; overnight fees are imported as Fee, their refunds as Interest (money given back, no asset) and UK stamp duty (SDRT) as Tax. Any other type is skipped with a warning. Directa SIM broker_directa CSV, XLSX ✅ Stable Italian broker Directa; reads both CSV and XLSX (identical layout). Charles Schwab broker_schwab CSV 🧪 Beta Parses US-formatted CSV exports. Revolut broker_revolut CSV 🧪 Beta Handles both Revolut invest and crypto exports (variant auto-detected by header). Coinbase broker_coinbase CSV 🧪 Beta For crypto transactions from Coinbase. Freetrade broker_freetrade CSV 🧪 Beta For UK broker Freetrade. Finpension broker_finpension CSV 🧪 Beta Swiss pension platform. Trading212 broker_trading212 CSV 🧪 Beta Parses Trading212's standard CSV export. Avanza broker_avanza CSV 🧪 Beta Swedish broker; semicolon CSV, SEK, Swedish transaction types. Saxo Bank broker_saxo CSV 🧪 Beta Trades, dividends, cash transfers and custody fees; localized trade verbs supported. Swissquote broker_swissquote CSV 🧪 Beta Swiss broker; forex conversion legs are not imported yet and are listed in a warning with a link to open an issue. Trade Republic broker_traderepublic CSV 🧪 Beta European neobroker; semicolon CSV, EUR. XTB broker_xtb CSV 🧪 Beta Quantity/price parsed from the transaction comment field. InvestEngine broker_investengine CSV 🧪 Beta UK ETF broker; GBP, combined name/ISIN column. Parqet broker_parqet CSV 🧪 Beta Portfolio aggregator; semicolon CSV (underlying broker kept in description). Disnat broker_disnat CSV 🧪 Beta Canadian broker (Desjardins); French headers, CAD. BUX broker_bux CSV 🧪 Beta European neobroker; deposits, trades, dividends. Rabobank broker_rabobank CSV 🧪 Beta Dutch bank investing; EUR, semicolon CSV. Fineco broker_fineco CSV ✅ Stable Italian bank; "Movimenti Dossier Titoli" report, both layout variants (with/without commissions). Verbatim amounts in the report currency (no FX). Intesa Sanpaolo broker_intesa CSV, XLSX 🧪 Beta Italian bank; auto-detects movements vs patrimonio snapshot. Movements map cedol*→INTEREST, dividend*→DIVIDEND, commission*→FEE, tax keywords→TAX, and skip unknown banking rows with warnings; snapshot seeds cash DEPOSIT when liquidity exists plus one ADJUSTMENT per holding with per-unit cost basis. Crédit Agricole broker_credit_agricole CSV, XLSX ✅ Stable Italian exports, version 2.0.0. Report set: the securities movements ("Lista Movimenti Deposito Titoli") and the account movements ("Lista Movimenti Conto"), uploaded together, are paired fact by fact (one transaction per coupon, purchase, redemption or maturity, with the account's cash). The balances of the account XLSX open the cash, and a month no account file covers becomes a proposed cash correction.
