docs.title: 🧪 Status Levels
docs.text: Level Meaning 🔬 Alpha Early development — may have significant bugs 🧪 Beta Tested with sample files — edge cases may exist ✅ Stable Well-tested and reliable for supported formats

docs.title: 🏦 Scalable Capital Importers
docs.text:
broker_scalable and broker_scalable_deposit import the two accounts of Scalable Capital, each into a LibreFolio broker of its own: the broker account (Scalable Capital broker) and the overnight account (Scalable Capital overnight account). They live in backend/app/services/brim_providers/broker_scalable/plugin.py and broker_scalable_deposit/plugin.py (plugin_version 1.1.0, .csv only, detection_priority 100), which hold only their properties and calls to the shared reader, _scalable.py: recognition, refusals and parsing are written once, for both accounts. The leading underscore keeps _scalable.py out of the registry's auto-discovery.

This page covers what is specific to Scalable. The user's view is Scalable Capital, where the docs_url of both plugins points.

docs.title: 🗂️ Files and detection
docs.text:
Every file starts with the 14 columns of Scalable's own CSV export (PRIME_COLUMNS):

date;time;status;reference;description;assetType;type;isin;shares;price;amount;fee;tax;currency
File Header Read by Scalable's own CSV — PRIME and PRIME+ plans, broker account only the 14 columns broker_scalable The LibreFolio exporter's broker file the 14 columns, then lf_*; lf_account is broker broker_scalable The exporter's overnight account file the 14 columns, then lf_*; lf_account is deposit broker_scalable_deposit
  • Recognition (read_file, behind can_parse): a .csv whose first line holds the 14 columns, in any case and any order, split on the delimiter the base class detects. Without an lf_account column the file is Scalable's own CSV, always the broker account; with it, the lf_account values give the account — broker, deposit, both (mixed), or none for an export without rows, which both plugins accept. The file name is never read: the user may rename the file. A file that cannot be read is simply not a Scalable export: recognition never raises.
  • Refusals (refusal): each plugin refuses the other account's file, and both refuse a mixed one, with a code and — except for the mixed file — the plugin that reads it. The codes are listed in Saying why with a code. Any other file gets no refusal.
  • Values are read by column name. The 14 columns use the decimal comma (to_decimal_it) and date is YYYY-MM-DD. Of the exporter's own columns, described in its format, the reader uses lf_account, lf_id, lf_subtype, lf_is_cancellation, lf_ordered_shares and lf_account_index.

docs.title: 📝 What is imported
docs.text:
_Reader takes the data rows in file order. A reversal (lf_is_cancellation is true) and a row whose status is not Executed or Settled are left out (see Only executed rows below for what each status gets), and so is a row without a readable date, amount or currency. Then type, compared lower-case, decides:

In the file (type) Imported as Buy, Savings plan BUY on the gross amount — the value of the shares, as Scalable's CSV and exporter 1.0.1 or later write it — with fee as a FEE and a positive tax as a TAX of the same asset. A negative tax, given back, becomes a DEPOSIT without asset Sell SELL, the same way a type containing Distribution DIVIDEND, gross — amount plus the tax withheld in tax — with that tax as a TAX of the same asset; net when tax is empty Interest INTEREST, gross, with the tax withheld as a TAX, both without asset; net when tax is empty Deposit, Withdrawal — bank transfers, and transfers between the two accounts DEPOSIT, WITHDRAWAL Fee FEE, without asset Taxes, Tax TAX, without asset; a positive amount, a refund, becomes a DEPOSIT Any other row whose assetType is Cash, such as a bonus DEPOSIT or WITHDRAWAL, by the sign of amount Security transfer, Corporate action and any other type Not imported: the scalable_not_imported notice lists them
  • Signs: a cash row whose sign contradicts its type — a negative Deposit, a positive Withdrawal or Fee — is booked by its sign, and so is a negative dividend or interest (scalable_cash_by_sign). A cash row, a dividend or an interest of zero is not imported (scalable_not_imported).
  • Trades without their details: in an exporter file, an empty fee means the details were not read, and the trade is booked on amount as it is, without legs (scalable_fees_unknown).
  • Exporter 1.0.0 is not supported: its trades carry the fee and the tax inside amount (added on a purchase, taken away on a sale), so both would be counted twice; the user exports again with 1.0.1 or later.
  • Only executed rows are imported (status Executed or Settled, compared lower-case). What the others get follows the rule known rows quietly, unknown rows loudly (plugin guide), in _Reader._not_executed:
    • A Pending row with lf_ordered_shares and some shares already executed is an order filled in part (scalable_open_partial): it comes, executed, with a later export.
    • pending, cancelled, canceled, expired and rejected (_NOT_EXECUTED) are known, and not a movement: no notice, one log line at the end of the file with the count of each status. An order executed later comes with the next export.
    • Any other status goes to the shared notice rows_not_recognized (reason status: <value>); an empty one goes to rows_unreadable (reason status). The notice scalable_not_executed no longer exists.
  • Assets: one fake asset id per ISIN — per description when the row has no ISIN — counting down from FAKE_ASSET_ID_BASE in order of first use, with extracted_isin and extracted_name (description) and no symbol; only the assets of written transactions are returned. The user matches them to LibreFolio's assets in the wizard's Review step. A trade or a dividend with neither ISIN nor description is unreadable.
  • Descriptions (_description): an optional leg prefix — Order fee, Tax, Tax refund — then the row's description (its type when empty, Scalable Capital when both are) cut to 350 characters, then id <lf_id> in exporter files and ref <reference> when the row has one, joined by ·. The id keeps two identical movements of one day apart and lets a new export recognise the rows already imported: the deduplication makes a match on the key fields LIKELY, unticked, only when the descriptions match too. Only the exporter's descriptions carry id …, so a row imported from one layout comes back from the other as a POSSIBLE duplicate, ticked.
  • Transfers between the two accounts (lf_subtype CASH_TRANSFER_IN or CASH_TRANSFER_OUT) are imported as plain DEPOSIT and WITHDRAWAL and listed by scalable_internal_transfers: a CASH_TRANSFER links two brokers, so the user merges the two halves in the bulk editor (Transfers). A merged half still matches when it is exported again (Merged transfers and exchanges).
  • Tags: import and scalable (_TAGS), from both plugins, so the two halves of a merged transfer carry the same tags. Both plugins declare history_tag scalable to match: broker_scalable by default, broker_scalable_deposit by override, since its default would be scalable_deposit.
  • Amounts are copied from the file, never recomputed or converted — a gross dividend or interest is the sum of amount and the tax withheld — and the currency comes from each row's currency: a value that is not an ISO 4217 code makes the row unreadable.

docs.title: 🔔 Notices
docs.text:
_NOTICES holds the ten notices of Scalable's own in display order, each with its severity, an English message and the comment of its evidence table. A notice comes only when it has rows, with context.count and one BRIMEvidence: those rows under the file's header, with their line numbers and an empty title, so the wizard captions the table itself. The wizard words the message as importWizard.brimNotice.<code> and the comment as importWizard.brimEvidence.<code>, keys present in the four catalogues; the English texts are the fallback (Talking to the import wizard).

Code Severity Rows scalable_unreadable_rows warning, report_issue A date, an amount, a currency, the shares or the security missing or unreadable: not imported scalable_fees_unknown warning Exporter rows without their fee and tax details: imported on the amount shown, without legs scalable_open_partial warning Orders filled in part and still open: not imported yet scalable_reversal warning Reversals of a transaction already booked: not imported scalable_not_imported warning, report_issue Security transfers, corporate actions, other types and zero amounts scalable_several_overnight_accounts warning The first row of each overnight account (lf_account_index), when the file holds more than one: they all go into one broker scalable_internal_transfers info Transfers between the two accounts: imported, to be merged scalable_dividends_net info Dividends without tax: imported net scalable_tax_refund info Tax refunds: imported as DEPOSIT scalable_cash_by_sign info Cash rows of an unknown type, or with an unexpected sign: booked by the sign of amount

The two warnings marked report_issue carry context.report_issue = True: the wizard shows the link open an issue on GitHub under them, because a row the importer cannot read, or does not import, may move shares or cash. Besides these ten, _Reader.skips (a RowSkips, built on the file's header) collects the rows with an unknown or empty status into the two shared notices rows_not_recognized and rows_unreadable, appended after the ten; their texts are written once for every plugin (BRIM Architecture → Rows left out).

docs.text:
• backend/app/services/brim_providers/sample_reports/ holds scalable-prime-export.csv (Scalable's own CSV), scalable-broker-export.csv and scalable-deposit-export.csv (exporter 1.0.1, one file per account, whose internal transfers mirror each other): invented values on the real layout, described in the folder's README.md.

docs.title: 💱 FX Architecture
docs.text: The Foreign Exchange (FX) system is responsible for fetching, storing, and providing exchange rates for currency conversion.

docs.title: 🔌 Multi-Provider Support
docs.text: LibreFolio supports multiple FX rate providers (e.g., ECB, FED). This ensures redundancy and allows users to choose the source that best fits their needs (e.g., a US user might prefer FED rates, while a European user prefers ECB).

docs.title: 📋 The FXRateProvider Interface
docs.text:
All providers must implement the FXRateProvider abstract base class:

class FXRateProvider(ABC):
    @property
    def base_currency(self) -> str:
        """The provider's base currency (e.g., 'EUR' for ECB)."""
        pass

    async def fetch_rates(self, date_range, currencies) -> dict:
        """Fetch rates from the external API."""
        pass

docs.title: 📐 Normalization and Storage
docs.text:
Providers typically return rates relative to a specific base currency (e.g., ECB returns 1 EUR = X USD).

To simplify storage and querying, LibreFolio normalizes all rates before saving them to the database. The rule is: Base currency is always alphabetically smaller than Quote currency.

  • Input: EUR/USD (EUR < USD) -> Stored as base='EUR', quote='USD', rate=1.08
  • Input: USD/GBP (USD > GBP) -> Stored as base='GBP', quote='USD', rate=1/0.78

This ensures that we only need to store one rate per pair, and we can easily calculate the inverse if needed.

Rate writes keep to the last storable date of the prices: tomorrow by the server's calendar (latest_stored_date(); X-R65, night decision N83), with no first date since the developer lifted the 1900-01-01 floor on 19/10 (N83's revision). POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/rate (upsert_rates_endpoint()) checks every item's date before its loop: a single date after tomorrow refuses the whole request with the same 422 date_out_of_range (date_out_of_range_detail(), params {"max"}), its items {"index", "date"} (the item's 0-based index; at most ten), its count all of them. Nothing is written, not even the valid items, unlike the endpoint's per-item errors. An earlier date, 0001-01-01 included, passes. The provider sync has no floor either: in sync_pairs_bulk(), the live sync path, _is_date_within_sync_range() (backend/app/services/fx/sync.py) keeps the dates of the requested range and nothing else, so a provider's rate dated before 1900 inside it, start: "min" included, is kept like any other; its end stays the requested one, today at the latest. Before N83's revision it was false for a day before 1 January 1900, whatever the start; that floor no longer exists.

docs.title: 🔢 Priority System
docs.text:
When converting currency, the system needs to decide which rate to use if multiple providers have data for the same pair and date.

fx_rates holds one rate per pair and date, so the decision is taken when the rate is fetched, not when it is read. Each pair has one or more routes in fx_conversion_routes, ranked by priority (1 = primary). sync_pairs_bulk() — the live sync path, called by POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/sync and by the scheduler's history-sync job — walks a pair's routes in priority order and falls back to the next one when a route fails. See FX Configuration & Routing for routes, chains and the MANUAL sentinel.

ensure_rates_multi_source() is an older single-provider orchestrator with no production caller: it is kept, unwired, as the extension point for future multi-base providers.

docs.title: 🆕 A new pair syncs its full history
docs.text:
Saving a new pair does not sync it on the server: the frontend does it right after the save. finishFxPairCreation() (frontend/src/lib/services/fxCreationSync.ts) calls POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/sync with start: "min" and end = today when the new pair has a non-MANUAL provider. "min" is the backend's sentinel for "everything the provider publishes": the request's start is a SyncStartDate (date | Literal["min"], backend/app/schemas/refresh.py), and the sync passes it to the providers as an FXProviderStartDate (backend/app/services/fx/base.py). Asking for the whole history, rather than the period of the page that opened the dialog, gives older transactions a rate too. A full history can outlast the client's default timeout, so this request waits up to 120 s (FX_SYNC_TIMEOUT_MS), like the Dashboard's rate sync. The sync windows (FxSyncModal, AssetSyncModal, PageSyncModal) instead give each request the limit of their Timeout field (SyncModalBase, default max(20, item count) s): syncRequestTimeoutMs() (frontend/src/lib/utils/sync/syncHelpers.ts) returns max(120 s, field + 5 s), so a larger field lengthens the request and a smaller one keeps the 120 s floor.

The request carries the new pair and the intermediate pairs saved with Also create intermediate pairs. A pair saved with no route (the MANUAL sentinel only) starts no sync and gets a Created success toast instead; saving the routes of an existing pair (edit mode) starts none either. After the sync, classifyFxSyncOutcome() grades the response:

Outcome When Toast failed / transport-error The request failed, a requested pair is missing from the response, the response has operation errors, or any pair is failed error skipped Every pair is skipped info partial Any pair is not ok warning ok Every pair is ok success

A refresh callback that fails turns a success or info toast into a warning. Both toasts link the pair name to its detail page (fxPairHtml(…, {linkToDetail: true})).

docs.title: 🔄 Conversion Logic
docs.text:
convert_bulk() (backend/app/services/fx/conversion.py) is the shared conversion function: POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/convert, the portfolio engine and service, lots analysis, Yield on Cost, asset price queries, the fixed-period changes of the Assets and FX tables, risk eligibility and AI Export components call it with a list of (Currency, to_currency, date) items. For each item:

  1. Identity: same currency in and out — the amount is returned as is, with no lookup.
  2. Stored pair: the pair is normalized alphabetically, the way rates are stored. The amount is multiplied by the rate when converting from the stored base, divided by it otherwise.
  3. Backward fill: the rate is the latest usable one on or before the requested date, with no time limit. The result carries the rate's date and whether backward fill applied; the convert endpoint turns them into backward_fill_info (actual_rate_date, days_back).
  4. No rate: when the pair has no usable rate on or before the date, the item fails — RateNotFoundError with raise_on_error=True, or a None result plus an error message otherwise (No FX rate found for B/Q on or before D).

A usable rate is one fx_rates.rate can keep (X-R38, see Chain Dates, Writes and Counters). A row the column cannot keep, written by an older release (an infinite rate, 0, 20 digits before the decimal point), is a missing rate for its date: backward-filled from the latest usable rate before it, as a date without a row would be, or the missing-rate error. A conversion never divides by zero nor returns an infinite amount. Read through the model, such a row still gives Decimal('Infinity') for a stored inf (see Decimal Columns); the FX writers no longer send one.

There is no triangulation at conversion time. A pair that no provider quotes directly gets its rates at sync time from a multi-step chain route, which stores the composite rate under the pair itself (source = "CHAIN:…") — see Direct vs. Chain Routes.

POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/convert expands each conversion's date_range into one convert_bulk() item per day, both ends included; with signals, a second series of one-unit items runs from the start of their warm-up to the same end. An amount of 0 is sent as one unit too, so its results answer 0 with the day's real rate instead of dividing 0 by 0 (X-R41). Both ends have a limit (X-R55). The end is cut at tomorrow by the server's calendar (datetime_utils.latest_range_end(), the helper R13-SEC7-1 also uses), a day of margin for a user whose today is already the server's tomorrow. The start, the warm-up included, goes back at most RANGE_SPAN_LIMIT_DAYS (36,525 days, 100 years) before that end (range_span_floor(), never before date.min; both in backend/app/utils/date_range_limits.py). A conversion that starts after the cut asks for nothing: no result, no error, and its signals run on an empty series; the other conversions are unaffected. The date_range of each signal_results item (FXSignalQueryResult) is the range its signals cover, the cut one; a conversion that starts after the cut echoes its requested range there, with no points. Before, nothing bounded the expansion: from 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31 it built about 3.65 million items, then failed with a 500 (OverflowError). The ceiling is the endpoint's: convert_bulk() itself, which the other callers use directly, has none.

The endpoint also caps each request (Z-25, night decision N77), as POST /assets/prices/query does (bulk request limits): X-R55 bounds each conversion, not how many one request holds, and 1,000 conversions of 100 years would build about 36.5 million daily items. More than MAX_BULK_ITEMS (1,000) conversions get a 422 {"code": "bulk_too_many_items", "message", "max_items", "items"} before any work, nothing converted; exactly 1,000 pass. The handler then plans the conversions one by one — each one's cut range, signal plan and warm-up — and counts the daily items and the one-unit signal items, warm-up included, that each would build; a conversion that starts after the cut counts zero, and its signals still run on an empty series. At the end of a conversion, a running total over MAX_BULK_ITEM_DAYS (1,000,000, lowered by R13-SEC9-2) gets a 422 {"code": "bulk_too_many_days", "message", "max_item_days", "item_days"}, item_days being the count through that conversion: more than the budget, a lower bound of the request's total. The message says so, «this one would build at least N» (bulk_too_many_days_detail() with at_least=True), where the price route's says «would build N»: its count is exact. No item is built or converted until the whole request is within the budget; only then are the planned blocks expanded day by day, in request order and each conversion's daily items before its signal items, and converted in one convert_bulk() call. A refused request costs its planning, not its items. Like the ceiling, the caps are the endpoint's: convert_bulk() has none. The FX list sends its conversions in batches under both (Z-27, Bulk requests in batches).

docs.title: 🗜️ Sampled conversions
docs.text:
A card of the FX list draws a few hundred points at most. POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/convert can answer a conversion with the results of one day a week or a month instead of every day (Z-29fx), with the rule of the asset price query (Sampled Price Series):

  • The fields. FXConversionRequest takes key, max_points (1 … 10,000), resolution (daily, weekly, monthly) and sample_like: at most one of the last three, none of them with annotation_requests. key and sample_like take 1 to 64 characters among ASCII letters, digits, _, ., : and - (SAMPLE_KEY_PATTERN).
  • The step. A conversion's fill starts on its first day F, the first day of its cut range that converts: the range's start when a rate precedes it, else the pair's first rate in the range. With max_points the step is choose_resolution(F, end, max_points), the finest of daily, weekly (ISO, Monday to Sunday) and monthly whose count fits, monthly the floor; with resolution the one asked. A sample_like follower takes the step of the conversion it names, on that conversion's own fill (on its own fill when the named one has none), from the later of the two first days. plan_conversion_samples() in backend/app/services/fx/sampling.py plans them; the dates are sample_dates(), the last day of each bucket, the last one cut at the range's end.
  • The results. The conversion is still computed day by day — its signals and the day budget need every day — and a weekly or monthly one keeps, in results, only the daily results on its dates, each unchanged (amount, rate, backward fill). A daily one answers every day, a follower from its later first day. Every result carries request_index, the position of its conversion in the request.
  • samples. One FXConversionSample per conversion, in request order: its resolution (daily by default) and, weekly or monthly, sample_bounds (FXSampleBounds): the daily result on F (first, the base of a card's percentage view and of its line's colour) and on the end (last). A conversion with nothing to fill answers no result and a daily step.
  • References. resolve_sample_references() checks every sample_like before anything runs: a fault is the price query's 422 {"code": "sample_reference", "reason", "item", "key", "message"} (unknown_key, duplicate_key, chained, range_mismatch).
  • Signals. Computed every day, as without the fields; on a weekly or monthly conversion each series is then reduced onto its dates by its output's aggregation_profile and the series of one signal aligned, through sample_signal_result() (backend/app/services/signals/sampling.py), the function the price query uses too. The calendar rolling return (ASSET_CALENDAR_ROLLING_RETURN) is offered in the FX domain: its points are the elements themselves (last_with_range), with their provenance.
  • Budget. A sampled conversion costs the days of its fill, as the daily one does (request limits).

Tests: backend/test_scripts/test_api/test_fx_convert_sampling.py (./dev.py test api fx-convert-sampling, PURE: the handler in process, convert_bulk() replaced by a double). The web app's FX list does not send these fields yet (the FX half of Y-40).

docs.title: 🪟 Loading only the usable rate window
docs.text:
Calculations call convert_bulk() with thousands of items (before P3 the portfolio engine preloaded a rate for every non-reporting currency and every day of the range, and before L1b the lots analysis asked one conversion per day of its market price series; both now read steps). So the function reads only the rows the batch can use, in one query for up to FX_PAIRS_PER_QUERY (500) pairs — more pairs take several queries (R13-SEC9-2: SQLite refuses an OR of about a thousand terms, «Expression tree is too large», and a request of some 990 pairs answered 500; _first_rate_days_inside() of the fixed-period changes reads in the same chunks):

  • for each pair it tracks the earliest (min_date) and latest (max_date) requested dates;
  • it loads the rows from the backward-fill anchor — the last rate on or before min_date, a MAX(date) scalar subquery — up to max_date. The anchor keeps the unlimited backward fill exact: the earliest item still finds its rate, however old;
  • it reads only the usable rates (X-R38): rate >= 1E-10 AND rate < 1E+14, the bounds of usable_fx_rate_bounds() (backend/app/db/precision.py), in the anchor subquery as in the window, so a legacy unusable row neither anchors the window nor is loaded. There is no per-row check in Python: any double within those bounds reads back as a rate storable_fx_rate() keeps, and this path is hot;
  • it selects plain columns (base, quote, date, rate), not ORM objects;
  • each item finds its rate with bisect_right over the pair's ascending dates.

The read — the anchor, the usable filter, the chunks, the plain columns — is the private helper _usable_rates(), shared with unit_rate_steps(), so the two never diverge.

The writers keep to the same upper bound (X-R50). SQLite keeps the rate as a double, so a rate within about 0.008 of 1E+14 with more digits than a double holds (99999999999999.995) has 14 digits before the point but would be stored as 1E+14: storable_fx_rate() refuses it too, so a manual one is refused and a provider's skipped, as for any rate the column cannot keep (99999999999999.99 stays the double 99999999999999.98 and is kept). Before, the limit was on the digits alone, as for W-B58: the writers accepted 99999999999999.999, stored it as 1E+14, and these bounds then skipped it as unusable.

Apart from the unusable rates left out, return values and errors are those of the full-history version this replaced, which loaded every pair's whole history up to the latest requested date and scanned it linearly for each item (PR #30 by Martin Sova, commit 6f42b2882).

docs.title: 🪜 One unit's rate as steps
docs.text:
The portfolio engine (_preload_fx_rates()) and the native cash (compute_native_cash()) need one unit of each foreign currency on every day of long ranges: asked of convert_bulk(), one item per currency and per day. A rate only changes on the days a row is stored, so unit_rate_steps(session, requests), in the same module (P3 of MF's fast-formulas plan), answers the same values as steps, with far fewer items. Since MF's P3 both read it: the engine in a map that answers on the asked days only (financial_math/fx_rates.AskedDayRates), the native cash through the steps themselves. Since lot L1b the lots analysis reads it too: its FxRateResolver asks one window per currency of the market price series, and keeps the rates in the same AskedDayRates.

requests maps (source, destination), two currency codes as stored, whichever of them is the stored base, to its windows (first_day, last_day), both days included; the windows of a pair may touch, overlap or lie apart. Every pair asked gets an entry, a frozen UnitRateSteps: source, destination and three tuples of one length, days, values and rate_days. From days[i] on, one unit of source is worth values[i] in destination, read from the stored row of rate_days[i]. The entry is empty when the pair has no usable rate for any day of its windows. The steps of a pair are:

  • the first day of each window, with the rate of the backward-fill anchor, the last usable row on or before it; no step when the pair has no usable row by then;
  • every day inside a window that has a usable row of the pair. Two rows with the same rate are two steps, each with its own rate date.

Rows between two windows are no steps. With rows on 1, 5, 9, 11 and 15 March and the windows 3–7 and 13–17 March, the steps are 3 March (the row of 1 March), 5 March, 13 March (the row of 11 March) and 15 March.

at(day) and rate_day_at(day) read the last step on or before day, None before the first. On every day of the windows, at(day) is exactly the amount convert_bulk() gives for Currency(code=source, amount=Decimal("1")) on that day, to the digit and the exponent, and rate_day_at(day) is its rate date; both are None where convert_bulk() has no rate. It holds because the two functions read and compute through the same private helpers, convert_bulk() with its behaviour unchanged:

  • _usable_rates(), the read: the same rows, from each pair's backward-fill anchor up to its last date, the same X-R38 usable filter in the anchor and in the window, the same chunks, one statement per FX_PAIRS_PER_QUERY (500) stored pairs (above);
  • _converted(), the arithmetic: the amount times the rate when it is in the stored base, divided by it otherwise.

Outside the windows, at(day) still reads the last step on or before the day, which is how NativeCash._rate_at() reads its rates. That is not convert_bulk()'s answer there: in the example, on 10 March at() gives the step of 5 March and convert_bulk() the row of 9 March; on 2 March, None and the row of 1 March. Which days a value is asked for stays with the caller.

ValueError refuses the whole call, before any read. It is part of the contract agreed with MF, who owns the engine and the native cash:

  • a pair of one currency: convert_bulk() answers it with the amount itself and no rate, dated the day asked, a rate date that moves with the day, which no step can express;
  • a window whose last day comes before its first.

Tests: ./dev.py test services fx-rate-steps (backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_fx_rate_steps.py, 63 cases, isolation pure) pins the match with an oracle against convert_bulk() on every day of every window.

docs.title: 🧩 Converting once for each stretch
docs.text:
A rate row stays in force until the next one is stored, so the days of a long range between two rows convert the same amount under the same rate. convert_by_stretch() (backend/app/services/fx/stretch_conversion.py, X-Q3) answers a list exactly as convert_bulk(session, conversions, raise_on_error=False) does (same results to the digit, same errors), but hands convert one conversion for each distinct (amount as printed, pair, rate row), on the first day it meets it, and copies the answer to the other days of the stretch.

flowchart LR
    I["conversions<br/>(Currency, to, day)"] --> K{"item"}
    K -- "same currency" --> A["answered:<br/>amount, dated as asked"]
    K -- "no rate on or before day" --> E["answered: own error<br/>'Conversion N: No FX rate found…'"]
    K -- "rate row R" --> G["group (amount, pair, R)"]
    G -- "first day of each group" --> C["convert = convert_bulk"]
    C --> X["copied to every day of the group<br/>backward-fill flag: rate date before day"]
  • The rate row of each day comes from unit_rate_steps() (above), which reads the same usable rows as convert_bulk().
  • Per item, as in convert_bulk(): an identity (the amount, dated as asked, no backward fill); a day with no usable rate (its own error, numbered by its position in the list, never asked of convert); the backward-fill flag (rate date < day).
  • The amount counts as printed. Decimal("1.0") and Decimal("1") convert to different exponents, so they are different groups.
  • A failure of convert for a group fails each of its days, each error numbered by its own item.
  • The seams are the keyword arguments convert (default convert_bulk) and steps (default unit_rate_steps), so a test can stand in for either read.

POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/convert (convert_currency_bulk() in backend/app/api/v1/fx/currencies.py) calls it for its daily and signal blocks, so the expansion into one item per day is unchanged while convert_bulk() receives fewer items. The price query applies the same idea to a price series through observed_prices.py, which asks convert_bulk() itself for each (price row, rate row) pair. Measured on a 10-year USD asset asked in EUR (3,650 points, rates on every weekday): 2,608 conversions instead of 3,650 with identical points, in the same time (0.26 s against 0.25 s), so it saves conversions, not time.

Tests: ./dev.py test services fx-stretch-conversion (backend/test_scripts/test_services/test_fx_stretch_conversion.py, isolation pure): item-for-item parity with convert_bulk() (direct, inverse, identity, no rate, gap, amount exponent), convert handed stretches and not days, and the handler answering what it answered with every day converted, signals and samples included.

docs.title: 📅 Fixed-Period Changes
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/period-changes returns the fixed-period changes of the FX table: 1D, 1W, 1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y, 2Y, 3Y and 5Y (developer decision D-MF6 b). get_fx_period_changes_bulk() in backend/app/services/fx/period_changes.py values the days. The change itself is the house's fixed_period_changes() (Financial Math Layer).

  • Request: a list of {base, quote, as_of, range_start?}. From the schema, 422 when base and quote are the same, or when range_start is after as_of; as_of and range_start are any day of the calendar, with no first day (D-P4, 26/10/2026; the schema once refused a day before 1 January 1900). A period whose reference day falls before 0001-01-01 has none: its change is null (day_before() in financial_math/returns.py). The route then checks the request with period_changes_request_refusal() (backend/app/schemas/common.py), before any conversion (MF-P2b, finding R13-SEC8, aligned with Z-25):
    • more than MAX_BULK_ITEMS (1,000) pairs get the 422 {"code": "bulk_too_many_items", "message", "max_items", "items"} of POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/convert (request limits); exactly 1,000 pass;
    • more than PERIOD_CHANGES_MAX_AS_OF_DAYS (5) distinct as_of days, or as many distinct range_start days, get the 422 {"code": "period_changes_too_many_days", "message", "field", "max_days", "days"}, field naming the one over the limit (as_of checked first).
  • Rate on a day: the conversion of 1 base into quote on that day by convert_bulk(), with its unlimited backward fill. It is the rate POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/convert returns for that day, up to that endpoint's ceiling: as_of has none. One convert_bulk() batch serves every pair and day of the request.
  • Response: items[], in request order, of {base, quote, as_of, periods[], range_change, errors[]}. Each period is {key, days, change_ratio, inverse_change_ratio}. range_change is null unless the item sends a range_start (below).
  • change_ratio: rate(as_of) / rate(as_of − days) − 1, the pair as asked (quote per base).
  • inverse_change_ratio: rate(as_of − days) / rate(as_of) − 1, the change of the inverted pair (base per quote).

Both are fractions, null when either rate is missing. A rate is never 0 here: the API keeps rates > 0, and convert_bulk() skips a stored rate below its usable bound (X-R38), so the house's −100 % for a value written down to 0 never reaches an FX pair. A day without a rate adds No B/Q rate on or before D to errors.

An item may also send range_start, the first day of the range the page shows, for the whole-range Δ Abs and Δ % of the FX pages (X-R59, decision N80); its limits are in the Request bullet above.

  • range_change: {reference_date, change_abs, change_ratio, inverse_change_abs, inverse_change_ratio}, the house's range_change() (Financial Math Layer), with reference the reference rate: change_abs = rate(as_of) − reference and change_ratio = rate(as_of) / reference − 1, the pair as asked (quote per base); inverse_change_abs = 1 / rate(as_of) − 1 / reference and inverse_change_ratio = reference / rate(as_of) − 1, the inverted pair (base per quote). All four are null when either rate is missing.
  • Reference: the rate on range_start, one more item per request in the same convert_bulk() batch, with its unlimited backward fill, and reference_date = range_start. A pair with no rate on or before range_start takes its first stored rate inside the range, after range_start and up to as_of, converted on its own day, with that day as reference_date. Its day comes from one query per distinct (range_start, as_of) window, for those pairs only: MIN(FxRate.date) … GROUP BY base, quote over the pairs as fx_rates stores them (alphabetical order), within the usable bounds of X-R38; a second convert_bulk() batch then reads those days' rates. Either way it is the first point of the series POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/convert returns for the range, which drops the days without a rate. A pair with no rate up to as_of gets a range_change with every field null, reference_date included; a missing reference adds nothing to errors. The anchor is the rate on as_of, as for the periods.

The change is on this endpoint, not on POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/convert: the FX store composes a pair's series from the gaps it loads separately (ensureFxRangeLoaded()), so a change attached to a series response would not be the visible range's. The web app sends it: fetchFxPeriodChanges(pairs, asOf, rangeStart) (frontend/src/lib/utils/periodChanges.ts) gives each item the first day of the range on screen, as it is (rangeStartFor(), frontend/src/lib/utils/rangeChange.ts; no longer raised to 1 January 1900), none for a day the backend would refuse (after as_of, or not a calendar day), and reads range_change both ways with fxRangeDeltas(). The FX table's Δ Abs and Δ % columns, the FX card's Δ % and the pair page's summary show it, from the inverse_* fields for a pair shown the other way round; the browser no longer computes it (displayFxDelta() is gone). The FX list keeps those values with a PeriodChangesLedger of their own, which marks each request with the whole range rather than its last day, so a failed request keeps only the values of the same range; the pair page asks for its one pair on load, on a range change and after a refresh (a sync ends with one).

The FX list calls the endpoint through fetchFxPeriodChanges() (frontend/src/lib/utils/periodChanges.ts): one request for every configured pair, with as_of the end of the selected range, and one for a single pair when that pair reloads on its own (its Reload, or after its Sync: fetchPairData()). A pair shown swapped (⇄) reads inverse_change_ratio, the others change_ratio. Besides its fixed 1D column, the table shows each period whose days fit in the range's whole calendar days (visiblePeriodColumns()). Past 1,000 configured pairs that request goes in batches (X-R64): the function hands the pairs to sendBulkBatches(items, () => 0, send) (frontend/src/lib/api/bulkBatches.ts, Z-27, Bulk requests in batches), which sends consecutive batches of at most BULK_MAX_ITEMS (1,000) pairs, in the order given, one request after the other. There is no day estimate: the endpoint has the item cap, not the item-days budget of the conversions, and every batch asks up to the same as_of. The answers merge as if one request had answered, the periods taken from the first item that has any; up to 1,000 pairs it is one request, as before. All or nothing: a batch that fails rejects the whole call with its own error and nothing is sent after it, so the list never shows a partial answer.

Several of these requests can be in flight at once, a pair's Sync during a range change for instance: the list keeps a PeriodChangesLedger (periodChanges.ts, X-R60) that says which answer it keeps.

  • A full request, for every pair (the first load, a range change, a refresh), replaces every request before it: an older answer that lands later is not kept.
  • A single pair's own request (loadPairPeriodChanges(), run by fetchPairData()) is fresher, for that pair, than a full request begun before it, whichever answer lands first. One begun before a newer full request is moot.
  • The page's data-busy (data-testid="fx-page") stays true while any request whose answer would still be kept is in flight, a single pair's included.
  • A failed full request keeps the Δ computed up to the same as_of (the end of the range) and drops the others; it is logged to the browser console, unless a newer full request has replaced it. A failed single-pair request is logged and changes nothing.
  • The signals' retry, a chart-settings save and swapping a pair (⇄) reload only the rates and signals (fetchAllPairSeries(); a save, only when it changes the backend signals), never the period changes: the Δ come both ways and do not depend on the signals.

docs.title: 🧹 Rate writes clear the portfolio caches
docs.text:
Every write that changes stored rates drops the two portfolio cache layers, portfolio_layer2 and portfolio_blob, through clear_cache(), so the next report recomputes with the new rates:

Write Function Clears when Provider sync (POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/sync, scheduler) sync_pairs_bulk() At least one rate point changed Manual rates (POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/rate) upsert_rates_bulk() After the commit (any non-empty batch) Rate deletion (DELETE /api/v1/fx/currencies/rate) delete_rates_bulk() At least one row was deleted

Limits and chunks (MF-SEC9a, from E's review of R13-SEC9). POST and DELETE /api/v1/fx/currencies/rate take at most MAX_BULK_WRITE_ITEMS (10,000) rates or deletions, a 422 bulk_too_many_items before any write: the FX page saves a CSV import in one request, and daily rates since 1999 are about 7,000 rows. The statements behind them hold one OR term per rate or deletion, so they run in chunks of OR_TERMS_PER_QUERY (500, utils/sql_chunks.py, the value of FX_PAIRS_PER_QUERY), in the same transaction: the read of the stored rates and the INSERT … ON CONFLICT of upsert_rates_bulk(), the read of the matching rates of delete_rates_bulk() (a deletion of more than 1,000 separate days, which the FX page sends as as many ranges, answered 500; each deletion then takes its rates by bisection over its pair's sorted dates, not by a scan of them, which at the cap held the event loop for seconds), and the read of the stored rates a provider sync compares with (_stored_rates(); refused, it was taken for a missing table and every rate counted as new). An error answers with a fixed message, never the database's, and is logged.

Both layers also key their entries on an FX fingerprint of the scope (compute_portfolio_fx_cache_identity() in financial_math/portfolio/engine.py); the explicit clear drops entries right away instead of leaving them to their TTL. See Cache Registry & Admin Endpoints for the caches themselves.

docs.title: 🔀 FX Configuration & Routing
docs.text: LibreFolio supports a sophisticated multi-provider routing system for Foreign Exchange (FX) rates. This allows administrators to define exactly which provider should be used for each currency pair, with automatic fallback capabilities and multi-step conversion chains.

docs.title: 🛤️ The Routing Logic
docs.text: When the system needs to fetch FX rates (e.g., via the /api/v1/fx/currencies/sync endpoint), it consults the fx_conversion_routes table.

docs.title: 🔢 Priority System
docs.text:
Each currency pair can have multiple routes assigned, ranked by priority (1 = highest/primary).

  1. Primary Route: The system first attempts to use the route with priority=1.
  2. Fallback: If the primary route fails (API error, timeout, provider down, provider paused after «too many requests»), the system automatically tries the route with priority=2, and so on.
  3. Failure: If all configured routes fail, the sync operation reports an error for that specific pair.

docs.title: 🔗 Direct vs. Chain Routes
docs.text:
Each route is defined as a chain of steps (chain_steps JSON array):

  • Direct (1-step): A single provider converts the pair directly. Example: EUR → USD via ECB → [{"from": "EUR", "to": "USD", "provider": "ECB"}]

  • Multi-step (chain): Multiple steps are chained to compute a derived rate. Example: RON → USD via ECB+ECB → [{"from": "RON", "to": "EUR", "provider": "ECB"}, {"from": "EUR", "to": "USD", "provider": "ECB"}]

A chain's steps do not need to use distinct providers: RON → USD above uses ECB twice, once per leg, and that is a valid 2-step chain — "multi-step" only means "more than one step", not "more than one provider".

The system multiplies the intermediate rates to compute the final derived rate, which is stored in fx_rates with source = "CHAIN:ECB+ECB".

docs.title: 📋 Example Configuration
docs.text:
Base Quote Priority Chain Steps Description EUR USD 1 EUR →[ECB]→ USD Direct via ECB (primary) EUR USD 2 EUR →[FED]→ USD Direct via FED (fallback) RON USD 1 RON →[ECB]→ EUR →[ECB]→ USD 2-step chain via ECB GBP USD 1 GBP →[BOE]→ USD Direct via BOE

In this example:

  • For EUR/USD, the system prefers ECB. If ECB is down, it falls back to FED.
  • For RON/USD, no provider offers this pair directly, so it uses a 2-step chain through EUR.
  • For GBP/USD, it uses BOE directly.

docs.title: 🗃️ Database Schema
docs.text:
The configuration is stored in the FxConversionRoute model:

class FxConversionRoute(SQLModel, table=True):
    __tablename__ = "fx_conversion_routes"

    id: int                     # Primary key
    base: str                   # e.g., "EUR" (alphabetically first: base < quote)
    quote: str                  # e.g., "USD"
    priority: int               # 1 = primary, 2+ = fallback
    chain_steps: str            # JSON array of conversion steps
    fetch_interval: int | None  # Optional refresh frequency (minutes), default 1440
    created_at: datetime
    updated_at: datetime

chain_steps JSON format:

// Direct (1-step):
[{"from": "EUR", "to": "USD", "provider": "ECB"}]

// Multi-step chain (2-step):
[
  {"from": "RON", "to": "EUR", "provider": "ECB"},
  {"from": "EUR", "to": "USD", "provider": "ECB"}
]

// Manual-only pair:
[{"from": "NOK", "to": "SEK", "provider": "MANUAL"}]

Validation rules:

  • Continuity: step[i].to == step[i+1].from for consecutive steps
  • No repeated edges: The same currency pair cannot appear twice in a chain (any direction)
  • Alphabetical ordering: base < quote constraint

docs.title: 🌐 API Endpoints
docs.text: Configuration is managed via the /api/v1/fx/providers/routes endpoints.

docs.title: 📋 List Routes
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/fx/providers/routes

Returns all configured routes ordered by base, quote, and priority. Each route includes the full chain_steps array plus two response-only fields, derived from the stored steps and not stored themselves:

Field Type Meaning is_chain bool true if the route has more than one step (len(chain_steps) > 1) providers_used list[str] Sorted unique list of provider codes appearing in chain_steps (including MANUAL)

providers_used is a sorted unique list representing membership, not an ordered traversal and not proof that a fetch succeeded: it lists which provider codes are configured on the route, so a route with two ECB steps still reports ["ECB"], and a MANUAL-only route reports ["MANUAL"] with is_chain: false.

Example — for the EUR/USD primary route and the RON/USD chain route from the table above:

{
  "items": [
    {
      "base": "EUR",
      "quote": "USD",
      "priority": 1,
      "chain_steps": [
        {"from": "EUR", "to": "USD", "provider": "ECB"}
      ],
      "is_chain": false,
      "providers_used": ["ECB"]
    },
    {
      "base": "RON",
      "quote": "USD",
      "priority": 1,
      "chain_steps": [
        {"from": "RON", "to": "EUR", "provider": "ECB"},
        {"from": "EUR", "to": "USD", "provider": "ECB"}
      ],
      "is_chain": true,
      "providers_used": ["ECB"]
    }
  ]
}

Note that RON/USD is is_chain: true (2 steps) with a single-member providers_used — the flag and the set answer different questions: "how many steps" versus "which providers are configured".

docs.title: ➕ Create/Update Routes (Bulk)
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/fx/providers/routes

Creates or updates multiple conversion routes atomically.

Request:

[
  {
    "base": "EUR",
    "quote": "USD",
    "priority": 1,
    "chain_steps": [
      {"from": "EUR", "to": "USD", "provider": "ECB"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "base": "EUR",
    "quote": "USD",
    "priority": 2,
    "chain_steps": [
      {"from": "EUR", "to": "USD", "provider": "FED"}
    ]
  },
  {
    "base": "RON",
    "quote": "USD",
    "priority": 1,
    "chain_steps": [
      {"from": "RON", "to": "EUR", "provider": "ECB"},
      {"from": "EUR", "to": "USD", "provider": "ECB"}
    ]
  }
]

The request body's inputs remain base, quote, priority, and chain_steps — clients simply omit the derived is_chain/providers_used metadata. If a client supplies them anyway, the values are ignored: they are never writable or authoritative, and are recomputed server-side from chain_steps for the response.

Result:

Each submitted item gets one result carrying the same is_chain/providers_used pair described for GET, computed from that item's own chain_steps, plus success, action ("created" or "updated"), and an optional message.

Validation failures and the transaction

If any submitted route references a provider code not registered in the provider registry, that item's result reports success: false, action: "error", and a message naming the unknown code(s) — with providers_used still derived from the submitted chain_steps, so an unknown code appears in providers_used too (it is membership of what was posted, not a check that the code is valid). When at least one item fails validation, the whole batch is rolled back and the endpoint responds 400 with the per-item results (including the successful ones, none of which were actually persisted) in the error detail body.

Replacing a pair's routes: ?replace=true

By default the endpoint only creates or updates the priorities it is given: a route at another priority stays. With POST /api/v1/fx/providers/routes?replace=true, each pair the request names keeps exactly the routes posted for it, and its other priorities are deleted in the same transaction, after the validation (X-R75). An edit is then one request: a refusal (400, 409, 500) or a request that never arrives leaves the pair as it was. The MANUAL rules are the same: a real provider posted removes the MANUAL route, and the MANUAL item alone ({"from": base, "to": quote, "provider": "MANUAL"}, priority 999) leaves the pair manual. A pair not configured yet is created; one another request configured in the meantime keeps only what this one posts for it.

The web app's provider editor (FxPairAddModal, the pair's detail page) saves this way. Before X-R75 it deleted the whole pair first and then posted the new routes, so a failed post left the pair with no route at all, and removing every route deleted the pair instead of leaving it manual. The intermediate pairs it adds for a chain go first, in a plain request, so that replace names only the pair being edited (X-R79).

docs.title: 🗑️ Delete Routes
docs.text:
DELETE /api/v1/fx/providers/routes

Removes routing rules. Can delete a specific priority or all rules for a pair.

Request:

[
  {
    "base": "EUR",
    "quote": "USD",
    "priority": 2
  }
]

If priority is omitted, all routes for the pair are deleted, MANUAL included: the pair is removed, and no MANUAL route is reinstated. When a delete that names a priority leaves the pair without a real provider, a MANUAL sentinel route is reinstated to keep the pair in the system.

docs.title: 🔄 Auto-Sync Behavior
docs.text:
When calling POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/sync:

  1. The system queries fx_conversion_routes to find all configured pairs and their routes.
  2. For 1-step routes, it groups target currencies by provider and fetches in batch.
  3. For multi-step (chain) routes, it fetches each leg's rates from the respective providers, then computes the derived rate by multiplying the intermediate rates.
  4. If a route fails, the system tries the next priority route for that pair.
  5. Results are saved to the fx_rates table. Chain-derived rates are stored with source = "CHAIN:provider1+provider2".

This ensures resilience to individual provider outages and supports currency pairs that no single provider covers directly.

docs.title: 📅 Chain Dates, Writes and Counters
docs.text:
• Strict date matching. compute_chain_rate() (backend/app/services/fx/conversion.py) produces a chain rate for a date only when every leg has a rate on that exact date; a missing leg skips the date. A chain through a sparse series therefore has rates only on the dates that series publishes. A leg that is present but unusable (one storable_fx_rate() refuses, or at most 0) counts as missing (X-R38): a chain never divides by zero, nor yields an infinite or absurd rate.
  • Upsert, the provider wins. Rates are written with INSERT … ON CONFLICT (date, base, quote) DO UPDATE, which replaces rate, source and fetched_at. A synced date overwrites whatever was stored, including a rate entered by hand through POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/rate (upsert_rates_bulk(), the same upsert). Dates outside the requested range are not written; a date before 1900-01-01 inside it is, whatever the start, "min" included (_is_date_within_sync_range(), no floor since N83's revision; see Normalization and Storage).
  • What the column keeps. fx_rates.rate is RealDecimal(24, 10) (since W-B63; the DDL is still NUMERIC(24, 10)): 10 decimal places and 14 digits before the decimal point (max_integer_digits(), precision − scale). storable_fx_rate() (backend/app/db/precision.py; X-R38, the FX side of W-B58) answers the rate as the column keeps it (truncate_fx_rate(): 10 decimal places, rounded down), or None when it is not finite, has more than 14 digits before the point, or is 0 once truncated (below 1E-10): a rate is never 0, since its inverse and the conversions divide by it. It also answers None when the truncated rate's double reaches 1E+14 (float(stored) >= 1E+14; X-R50): SQLite keeps the rate as a double, and a rate within about 0.008 of 1E+14 with more digits than a double holds, such as 99999999999999.995, has 14 digits before the point but would be stored as 1E+14, which the conversions skip as unusable (Loading only the usable rate window); 99999999999999.99 stays the double 99999999999999.98 and is kept. Like W-B58's helpers (see Decimal Columns), it counts the digits without a decimal context and never raises: 1E+1000000 and 1E-2000000 are refused, never an overflow or a zero. A negative rate is its callers' to refuse.
  • A provider's rate the column cannot keep is skipped. While a provider's answer is read (_collect_leg_rates()), an observation that is not a finite rate above 0, or whose inverse overflows or underflows to 0, is set aside (normalize_storable_rate()) instead of making every leg of that provider fail. A rate storable_fx_rate() refuses once normalized is skipped when stored; before, from 1E+50 up the route failed with none of the pair's dates stored, and a failing primary route switched the pair to its fallback route. For a chain (_storable_chain_rates()), a date whose leg is present but unusable, or whose chain rate the column cannot keep (1E+20, or 0 once truncated), is skipped. A skipped rate is never stored and never fails the pair: its other dates are stored. One warning per pair and per sync (_warn_unusable_rates()), FX rates skipped: the column cannot keep them, covers its skipped rates, the observations of its legs set aside included, with pair, provider (the CHAIN:… source for a chain), skipped (the count), dates (the earliest ten, ISO) and limits (fx_rate_limits_text()). The unwired ensure_rates_multi_source() follows the same rules: one normalization pass, the rate skipped, one warning per pair.
  • A manual rate the column cannot keep is refused. upsert_rates_bulk() (backend/app/services/fx/storage.py) refuses a base equal to its quote and a finite rate ≤ 0 (Rate must be positive), then puts the pair in alphabetical order, inverting the rate when the base comes after the quote, and checks the limits on the rate as stored, never on the rate typed: MMK → KHR 1E-13 is stored as KHR/MMK 1E+13, accepted. A rate that is not finite, whose inverse overflows (1 / 1E-1000000) or underflows to 0 (1 / 1E+1000027), or that storable_fx_rate() refuses is an FXRateNotStorableError, a ValueError (X-R46), naming the pair in stored order, the date and the limits (fx_rate_refusal()): The rate of KHR/MMK on 2024-01-02 cannot be stored: an exchange rate keeps at most 14 digits before the decimal point and 10 decimal places, stays below 100000000000000 (as the database stores it), and must stay above 0 once cut to them (the bound below 1E+14 since X-R51, so that a rate of 14 digits the double rule refuses is told why). Nothing of the call is written; before, 1E+400 was stored as a REAL inf, and its inverse and 1E-11 as values that read back 0. A valid rate is still written as normalized, not truncated.
  • The manual-rate endpoint. POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/rate (upsert_rates_endpoint(), backend/app/api/v1/fx/currencies.py) handles its items one by one: a refused item is left out while the others are stored (200), and the answer names it (next bullet). Before handling any of them, it checks every date: one after latest_stored_date() (tomorrow) refuses the whole request with a 422 date_out_of_range, nothing written, not even the valid items (X-R65, N83; Normalization and Storage); an earlier date, before 1900 included, passes. Its own inversion runs inside the item's try (normalize_storable_rate()), so an inverse that overflows is that item's error, never a 500, and one that underflows to 0 is refused naming the limits, like any rate the column cannot keep (X-R50; before, the item's error was Rate must be positive (got 0E-1000026)). The schema answers 422 to a rate that is not a number ("abc", true, "0x10"), not finite (the JSON number 1E+400, which JSON parsing turns into inf; NaN; "Infinity") or ≤ 0 (gt=0): FXUpsertItem.coerce_rate() reads a finite float through its shortest decimal text (0.1 → Decimal("0.1")) and hands anything else to Pydantic as it came, a non-finite float as its text ("inf"), which the 422 can echo. Before, "abc" made the validator raise InvalidOperation past Pydantic, and a non-finite rate was echoed as Decimal('Infinity'), which the JSON renderer cannot write: both were a 500.
  • A refused item is named twice. Since X-R46, the 200 keeps its sentence in errors, unchanged (Rate N: …, N the item's 0-based index), and adds an entry to rejected, {"index", "date", "reason"} (FXRateRejection in backend/app/schemas/fx.py), in request order; rejected is empty when every item is stored. When every item is refused, the answer is 400 and its detail is an object instead of a string: {"code": "fx_rates_refused", "message", "rejected"}, where message is the former string, All rates failed: followed by the errors joined with "; ", and rejected lists every item, as the 200 would. The web app's FX data editor counts only the results as saved and names the refused dates (up to five, then a count) with their reasons: in a warning after a 200, in its error banner and toast after the 400 (frontend/src/lib/api/writeRefusal.ts). The reason is one of:
    • same_currency: the base is the quote; errors says Rate N: Base and quote must be different (got EUR);
    • rate_not_storable: a rate fx_rates.rate cannot keep once normalized (the limits above, X-R38), raised as FXRateNotStorableError by the endpoint or by upsert_rates_bulk(); errors says Rate N: Validation error: followed by fx_rate_refusal()'s text;
    • invalid_rate: any other ValueError of the item (Rate N: Validation error: …);
    • internal_error: an unexpected error, logged (FX rate upsert failed) and never echoed; errors says Rate N: Failed: internal error.
  • Counters. points_fetched counts the rates computed for the pair in the range, the skipped ones left out; points_changed counts the new dates plus the dates whose value changed, compared at storage precision (_count_actual_changes(), which reads the stored rate through storable_fx_rate()). A legacy stored rate the column cannot keep (an infinite one, 1e60, 0) compares as a change, and the upsert overwrites it; before, a stored inf or 1e60 made the comparison raise and the pair's sync fail. ensure_rates_multi_source() compares the same way.
  • Empty is not a failure. The next route is tried only when a leg of the current one fails, its wait for the legs times out (120 s) or its computation raises; a rate the column cannot keep does none of these. A route that answers with no rate in the range ends the pair as partial: the next route is not tried. A single-step route whose every rate in the range was skipped says so in its message, Provider P returned no rate the database can keep for B/Q in start–end: followed by the limits; a chain keeps its Chain … produced no complete rates message, and the warning names the dates.
Status When ok The route produced at least one rate in the range partial The route answered but produced no rate in the range, or none the column can keep; message and detail (per leg: dates_available, error) say why skipped Every route of the pair is MANUAL failed The pair has no route, or every route failed; errors lists the failure of each route

The scheduler's history-sync job (run_history_sync(), backend/app/services/platform/scheduler/jobs.py) calls the same function once for every pair with a route that has no MANUAL step, up to today, from today minus scheduler_history_sync_horizon_days (default 14), or earlier when a pair's last saved rate is older: the day after the oldest of them, at most a year back (see History Sync).

docs.title: ⏸️ Paused Providers
docs.text:
Every call to an FX provider goes through call_fx_provider() (backend/app/services/fx/runtime.py): the fetches of sync_pairs_bulk(), those of the older ensure_rates_multi_source(), and the supported-currency catalogue. A provider that refused for too many requests is paused, as the asset providers are (Provider Pauses): until the pause ends, the boundary raises FXRateLimitedError (error_code = "RATE_LIMITED", retry_after = the seconds left) without calling it. A refusal met during a fetch pauses the provider the same way, and the error carries the pause decided.

  • A paused provider is a failed leg. _fetch_provider() records the refusal and fails every leg of that provider with its message, logged at INFO with no traceback. The pair goes on to its next route, as after any failed leg; the legs of every route were fetched in the same pass, so the next route is not delayed.
  • The cache comes first. A fetch found in the 5-minute cache of the sync (_fx_fetch_cache) is used even while its provider is paused.
  • The pair result. A pair that ended failed or partial while one of its routes uses a provider that refused or was paused carries error_code: "RATE_LIMITED" and retry_after: the shortest wait among those providers, the first moment one of its routes may work again. A pair that another route served (ok), and a skipped pair, carry neither.
  • The catalogue (GET /fx/providers) answers with the provider's last known list, as after any failure, and asks again 5 minutes later.

docs.title: 🔌 FX Providers (Developer)
docs.text: This section provides the technical documentation for each Foreign Exchange (FX) rate provider implemented in the LibreFolio backend. For the end-user perspective, see the User Manual — FX Providers.

docs.title: 🏛️ Providers at a Glance
docs.text: Provider Code Base Currency Currencies API Format API Key Test Level European Central Bank ECB EUR ~45 JSON/XML No Stable Federal Reserve FED USD ~20 CSV No Beta Bank of England BOE GBP ~15 CSV/HTML No Beta Swiss National Bank SNB CHF ~25 JSON No Beta

docs.title: 📝 General Notes
docs.text:
• Base Currency: The currency against which all other rates are quoted by the provider. LibreFolio automatically handles conversions between any pair, regardless of the provider's base currency.
  • Update Frequency: ECB, FED and BOE update their rates once per business day (weekdays only). The SNB publishes monthly averages only, stored on the 1st of each month.
  • No API Keys: All core providers use publicly accessible APIs — no registration or API keys required.

docs.title: 📚 Technical Details
docs.text:
• 🇪🇺 ECB (European Central Bank)
  • 🇺🇸 FED (Federal Reserve FRED)
  • 🇬🇧 BOE (Bank of England)
  • 🇨🇭 SNB (Swiss National Bank)

docs.title: 🔗 Related Documentation
docs.text:
• 💱 FX Configuration & Routing — Technical details on the routing algorithm and configuration.
  • 💱 FX Architecture — Main backend service architecture.

docs.title: 🇬🇧 BOE — Bank of England
docs.text: Property Value Code BOE Base Currency GBP API Endpoint https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/boeapps/database/fromshowcolumns.asp API Format CSV (HTML response with embedded data) API Key Not required Currencies ~15 major currencies Update Frequency Daily, UK business days Historical Data Deep historical coverage (decades for major currencies) API Docs BOE Statistical Interactive Database

docs.title: ⚙️ How It Works
docs.text:
The Bank of England provides exchange rates through their Statistical Interactive Database (IADB). Each currency has a unique series code.

  • Series codes: Format XUDL{XXX} where XXX varies by currency (e.g., XUDLUSS for USD).
  • Quotation: "Foreign currency per 1 GBP" — the provider normalizes these automatically.
  • Too many requests: an HTTP 429 on any currency's request refuses the whole call. After the parallel fetch, raise_longest_refusal() raises the FXRateLimitedError with the longest Retry-After, and the core pauses the provider (Paused Providers).

docs.title: 💰 Supported Currencies
docs.text: USD 🇺🇸, EUR 🇪🇺, JPY 🇯🇵, CHF 🇨🇭, CAD 🇨🇦, AUD 🇦🇺, NZD 🇳🇿, SEK 🇸🇪, NOK 🇳🇴, DKK 🇩🇰, CNY 🇨🇳, HKD 🇭🇰, SGD 🇸🇬, ZAR 🇿🇦, INR 🇮🇳.

docs.title: ⚠️ Limitations
docs.text:
• The API returns HTML with embedded CSV data — parsing is more complex than pure JSON/CSV APIs.
  • One request per currency, sent in parallel (asyncio.gather).
  • Some currencies have limited historical coverage.

docs.title: 🇪🇺 ECB — European Central Bank
docs.text: Property Value Code ECB Base Currency EUR API Endpoint https://data-api.ecb.europa.eu/service/data/EXR/ API Format JSON (SDMX) API Key Not required Currencies Discovered at runtime by get_supported_currencies(): on 2026-10-08, 29 published daily and 44 plus EUR in the history. GET /fx/providers caches the list for 24 h (backend/app/services/fx/catalog.py) Update Frequency Daily, ~16:00 CET on ECB business days Historical Data Available from 1999 API Docs ECB Data Portal API

docs.title: ⚙️ How It Works
docs.text:
The European Central Bank publishes daily reference exchange rates for the Euro against about 30 currencies. The provider queries the ECB Statistical Data Warehouse using the SDMX REST API; get_supported_currencies() (backend/app/services/fx_providers/ecb/plugin.py) reads the currency list from the same API, so it also returns the discontinued currencies that are still in the history.

  • Dataset: EXR (Exchange Rates)
  • Frequency: D (Daily)
  • Series: SP00 (Spot rate)
  • Quotation: Rates are "1 EUR = X foreign currency" — stored directly in LibreFolio's format.
  • Too many requests: an HTTP 429, on the rates or on the currency list, raises FXRateLimitedError with the response's Retry-After. fetch_rates() asks for one currency at a time (the ECB's bot protection reacts to parallel requests) and stops at the first refusal: the whole call is refused, and the core pauses the provider (Paused Providers).

docs.title: 💰 Supported Currencies
docs.text:
Published daily (29 on 2026-10-08, from the ECB's eurofxref-daily.xml): AUD, BRL, CAD, CHF, CNY, CZK, DKK, GBP, HKD, HUF, IDR, ILS, INR, ISK, JPY, KRW, MXN, MYR, NOK, NZD, PHP, PLN, RON, SEK, SGD, THB, TRY, USD, ZAR.

History only: discontinued currencies such as BGN (last rate 2025-12-31, before Bulgaria adopted the euro), HRK and RUB. fetch_rates() gets their past observations from the same EXR series and nothing after the last one.

docs.title: ⚠️ Limitations
docs.text:
• No data on weekends or ECB holidays.
  • Some emerging market currencies may have gaps during local holidays.
  • Historical data before 1999 is not available.

docs.title: 🇺🇸 FED — Federal Reserve (FRED)
docs.text: Property Value Code FED Base Currency USD API Endpoint https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv API Format CSV (public download, no API key) API Key Not required Currencies ~20 major currencies Update Frequency Daily, US business days API Docs FRED Economic Data

docs.title: ⚙️ How It Works
docs.text:
The Federal Reserve provides exchange rate data through FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data). The provider downloads CSV files for each currency series.

  • Series IDs: Format DEXXX (e.g., DEXUSEU = USD per 1 EUR).
  • Quotation: "USD per 1 foreign currency" — the provider inverts these automatically to get LibreFolio's standard format.
  • Multi-unit currencies: None (FRED quotes all currencies per 1 unit).
  • Too many requests: an HTTP 429 on any currency's request refuses the whole call. After the parallel fetch, raise_longest_refusal() raises the FXRateLimitedError with the longest Retry-After, and the core pauses the provider (Paused Providers).

docs.title: 💰 Supported Currencies
docs.text: EUR 🇪🇺, GBP 🇬🇧, JPY 🇯🇵, CAD 🇨🇦, CHF 🇨🇭, AUD 🇦🇺, INR 🇮🇳, BRL 🇧🇷, MXN 🇲🇽, ZAR 🇿🇦, SGD 🇸🇬, HKD 🇭🇰, KRW 🇰🇷, TWD 🇹🇼, NZD 🇳🇿, THB 🇹🇭, SEK 🇸🇪, NOK 🇳🇴, DKK 🇩🇰, CNY 🇨🇳.

docs.title: 🗺️ Series ID Mapping
docs.text: Currency FRED Series Direction EUR 🇪🇺 DEXUSEU USD per 1 EUR GBP 🇬🇧 DEXUSUK USD per 1 GBP JPY 🇯🇵 DEXJPUS JPY per 1 USD CHF 🇨🇭 DEXSZUS CHF per 1 USD CAD 🇨🇦 DEXCAUS CAD per 1 USD AUD 🇦🇺 DEXUSAL USD per 1 AUD

docs.title: ⚠️ Limitations
docs.text:
• One HTTP request per currency, sent in parallel (asyncio.gather).
  • No data on US holidays and weekends.
  • Some series may have occasional gaps.

docs.title: 🇨🇭 SNB — Swiss National Bank
docs.text: Property Value Code SNB Base Currency CHF API Endpoint https://data.snb.ch/api/cube API Format JSON — /devkum/dimensions/en (currency list), /devkum/data/json/en (rates) API Key Not required Currencies ~25, read from the dataset's dimensions at first use (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CNY, AUD, CAD, …). GET /fx/providers caches the list for 24 h (backend/app/services/fx/catalog.py) Dataset devkum — monthly averages (M0); month-end values (M1) are not used Update Frequency Monthly, published around the 2nd business day of the following month API Docs SNB Data Portal — devkum

docs.title: ⚙️ How It Works
docs.text:
The Swiss National Bank provides exchange rates through their Data Portal API. The SNB offers no daily-rate API: the devkum dataset holds monthly averages, and the provider stores each one on the 1st of its month to fit the daily-rate storage model.

  • Currency map: loaded once per process from the dimensions endpoint (class-level cache). Forward rates (USD3M, USD6M) and the SDR (XDR1) are skipped. If the call fails, the provider raises FXServiceError ("Cannot load SNB currency list"), or FXRateLimitedError for an HTTP 429.
  • Request: the filtered JSON endpoint with dimSel=D0(M0),D1(…) — only monthly averages, only the requested currencies — and fromDate/toDate in YYYY-MM.
  • Quotation: "X CHF per 1 (or 100) units of the foreign currency". The provider divides by the unit count and returns CHF per 1 unit; the FX service normalizes the direction for storage.
  • Too many requests: an HTTP 429, on the currency map or on the rates request, raises FXRateLimitedError with the response's Retry-After, and the core pauses the provider (Paused Providers).

docs.title: 🔢 Multi-Unit Currency Handling
docs.text: Each series id carries its unit count: EUR1 is CHF per 1 EUR, CNY100 is CHF per 100 CNY. The provider parses it (CNY100 → CNY, 100) and divides the value by it, so a CNY100 value of 12.5 becomes 0.125 CHF per CNY.

docs.title: ⚠️ Limitations
docs.text:
• One value per month, dated the 1st: no daily movement.
  • In chain routes, compute_chain_rate needs a rate on the exact same date for every leg, so a chain through SNB yields rates only on the 1st of each month. The provider's warning_i18n surfaces this as ⚠️ on such routes.
  • Multi-unit quotation requires special handling (automated by the provider).

docs.title: 📉 Risk Engine
docs.text:
The risk engine measures how a portfolio, a broker, a single asset or a hand-picked selection of assets has behaved, and how it could behave: drawdowns, Value at Risk, correlations, risk contributions, benchmark comparisons, stress scenarios and simulations. It is a bulk, plugin-based service behind /api/v1/risk. One request names one scope, one period, one target currency and one mode, and asks up to 32 analytics about them. The engine resolves the scope and prepares the price series once, then runs every analytic in isolation: a refusal or a crash in one analytic never takes the others down.

This page is for developers who change the engine, add an analytic or build a surface on top of it. The mathematics lives in the Risk Metrics theory section. What users see is described on the Dashboard Risk tab page, on the Correlation tab page of the Assets list, and on the asset detail page; the frontend side of the first two is in Risk UI.

docs.title: 🧭 Who Calls It
docs.text:
Caller Scope it sends Entry point Dashboard, Risk tab {kind: "portfolio", broker_ids}: the brokers the user owns with a positive share, a share never set counting as 100% for the owner (getOwnedBrokers(), stores/reference/brokerStore.ts:262), whatever the broker filter. The panel mounts only once they are known: without broker_ids the backend would widen the scope to every broker the user can see, editor and viewer ones included (routes/(app)/dashboard/+page.svelte:1101-1110) levels/RiskLevelsPanel.svelte Broker Detail, Risk tab {kind: "portfolio", broker_ids: [id]} levels/RiskLevelsPanel.svelte Assets page, Correlation tab (the Asset Global lab) {kind: "asset_set", asset_ids: [...]} AssetSetRiskPanel.svelte Asset Detail, Risk & Scenarios tab {kind: "asset", asset_id} AssetRiskScenariosView.svelte → RiskAnalysisPanel.svelte AI Export drawdown context Portfolio, broker or asset; drawdown_summary only RiskService.execute(), called in-process by backend/app/services/ai_export/components/drawdown_context.py

The Svelte paths are relative to frontend/src/lib/features/risk/. The AI Export side is described in AI Export Composition.

docs.title: 🗺️ Source Map
docs.text: Source Responsibility backend/app/api/v1/risk.py The four routes; maps scope errors to 403 and 404. backend/app/schemas/risk.py Request, scope, result, metadata and output contracts, and every enum (RiskMode, RiskResultStatus, RiskErrorCode, RiskOutputKind, …). backend/app/schemas/risk_scenarios.py Typed scenario catalogue contracts. backend/app/services/risk/service.py RiskService: execute() orchestrates a query through the five modules below (pre-flight, gates, per-analytic isolation, the failed envelope); asset_eligibility() gives the eligibility verdicts; catalog() lists the analytics. backend/app/services/risk/plan.py AnalyticPlan — a requested analytic with its plugin and validated parameters — and the predicates on the kind of calculation it asks for (is_historical_replay_plan(), is_hypothetical_plan(), is_geography_hypothetical_plan(), reads_the_twrr_alone()). backend/app/services/risk/scope.py The scope: access, holdings and weights (load_scope_inputs() into ScopeInputs), the asset lookups, the bulk price load (prepare_asset_series()), the exclusions (scope_exclusions()); RiskScopeAccessError and RiskScopeNotFoundError, which the API maps to 403 and 404. backend/app/services/risk/replay.py A historical replay's own window and series (prepare_historical_replay_context()), and the shorter window it may suggest (verified_replay_range()). backend/app/services/risk/results.py The execution context (build_execution_context()), the gate rules (available_observations(), requires_valid_composition()), the result envelopes and their metadata (success_result(), unavailable_result(), result_metadata()), the portfolio TWRR series (portfolio_twrr_returns()), the warnings and their asset names (with_warning_asset_names()). backend/app/services/risk/data_quality.py The data-quality report a result is judged on (plan_data_quality()), its warnings (data_quality_warnings()), and the banner issues of an asset_set scope (with_asset_set_quality_issues()). backend/app/services/risk/base.py The plugin contract: RiskAnalytic, RiskExecutionContext, RiskComputation, RiskUnavailableError, RiskSeriesInputs. backend/app/services/risk/eligibility.py Per-asset window facts, analysis eligibility, replay coverage, common and suggested periods. backend/app/services/risk/metrics.py Pure numeric primitives: volatility, Sharpe and Sortino, drawdown episodes, VaR/CVaR, correlation, risk contributions, buy-and-hold replay. backend/app/services/risk/acquired.py Measures re-implemented from the Riskfolio-Lib catalogue in the project's sign conventions; the library is their test oracle, never a runtime dependency. backend/app/services/risk/analytic_helpers.py Extraction helpers that turn a missing input into a declared refusal (require_primary_returns, prepared_scope_series, …). backend/app/services/signals/risk_adapters.py Adapters reused by the four risk-family signal plugins that read the prepared series (drawdown and rolling volatility, Sharpe, beta). backend/app/services/risk/quant/ The simulation and optimization boundary: engine request and result models, content-keyed caches, spawn worker pools, the QuantLib and Riskfolio workers, the NumPy block bootstrap. backend/app/services/risk/scenario_catalog/ Built-in YAML scenarios and the loader that runs at startup. backend/app/services/risk_plugins/ The analytics, one folder each: the code in <analytic_code>/plugin.py, the risk.analytics.* name and description in its i18n/ fragment. backend/app/services/risk/registry.py RiskAnalyticRegistry. backend/app/services/provider_registry.py The register_plugin decorator and the folder discovery shared by every plugin registry. backend/app/services/market_series.py Joint calendar, target-currency conversion, carried points. prepare_asset_series_set() reads one point per calendar day; prepare_asset_series_set_from_readings() gives the same PreparedAssetSeriesSet from readings that hold only an asset's observations (first_point_date, observation_dates, point_on(day)), building points on the few days the preparation uses: the baseline day, the days some asset quotes, the first day of each asset's rate, and the stored rows with the day before each (J5-2, R1). The simple returns (float_price_return()) and the observed annualization factor (observed_annualization()) come from financial_math/returns.py (Financial Math Layer). backend/app/services/assets/market_calendar.py The market holiday table and the rule that tells a stored carry from a quote. backend/app/services/platform/data_quality_thresholds.py Thresholds shared with the portfolio's data-quality banner. backend/app/config/__init__.py RISK_SIMULATION_* and RISK_OPTIMIZATION_* worker settings. frontend/src/lib/features/risk/riskRequest.ts Request builders and canonicalization. frontend/src/lib/features/risk/ riskStore (session cache), riskPanelController (the plumbing behind every panel), riskBenchmarkStore (the shared benchmark). frontend/src/lib/features/risk/ Panels, levels, the lab, BenchmarkSelect, eligibility wording.

docs.title: 🔄 Request Flow
docs.text:
---
config:
  layout: elk
---
flowchart TD
    subgraph UI["🎨 Frontend"]
        Panel["Risk panel<br/>levels L1–L4 · lab sections"]
        Ctrl["riskPanelController<br/>base waves · on-demand runs"]
        Picker["BenchmarkSelect · lab picker"]
