docs.title: 🏗️ Build & Development
docs.text:
Frontend tasks are managed via dev.py front:

# Start Vite dev server with Hot Module Replacement
./dev.py front dev

# Build for production (output in frontend/build/)
./dev.py front build

# Build with source maps for debugging
./dev.py front build --debug

# Type-check with svelte-check
./dev.py front check

# Preview production build locally
./dev.py front preview
Command Description front dev Starts Vite at localhost:5173, proxies API calls to backend front build Production build with minification and tree-shaking front build --debug Build with source maps (useful for debugging deployed code) front check Runs svelte-check for TypeScript and Svelte diagnostics front preview Serves the production build locally for testing

docs.title: 🛡️ DataQualityBanner Component
docs.text: Component and model for unified data quality warnings across the LibreFolio UI.

docs.title: 🔍 Overview
docs.text:
DataQualityIssue is the standard model for surfacing data quality problems (missing prices, missing FX, incomplete NAV, etc.) across three key pages: - Dashboard 📊 - Asset Detail 📈 - Forex Detail 💱

DataQualityBanner is the single, reusable UI component that renders these issues consistently. Before this system existed, each page had its own ad-hoc inline banners — separate markup, no consistency, and no Call-To-Action (CTA). Now, all three pages share the same component and issue model.

docs.title: 📁 File Mapping
docs.text: File Role 🐍 backend/app/schemas/portfolio.py Defines IssueCode, IssueSeverity, IssueDomain, DataQualityIssue, and DataQualityReport schemas. ⚙️ backend/app/services/financial_math/portfolio/data_quality.py build_data_quality_report() — generates portfolio-wide issues from the engine's daily states; DerivedViewsBuilder.build_data_quality_report() (derived_views.py) passes its daily states to it. 📊 backend/app/services/portfolio_service.py get_summary() / get_report() — collect the missing FX pairs, the assets without cost basis and the assets with an invalid split ratio, then call build_data_quality_report(). 🎨 frontend/src/lib/components/ui/feedback/DataQualityBanner.svelte Reusable UI component (supporting grouped and flat modes). 🌐 frontend/src/lib/i18n/dataQuality/{en,it,fr,es}.json dataQuality.* translation namespace for localized warnings: the dataQuality subsystem, one of the sources of the generated catalogue (see Internationalization).

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture & Data Flow
docs.text:
Here is how data quality reports are computed in the backend and rendered inside SvelteKit pages:

graph TD
    Engine["⚙️ Backend Engine<br>(DerivedViewsBuilder)"] -->|"Computes issues"| Report["📄 DataQualityReport<br>Schema"]
    Report -->|"JSON payload"| API["📡 API Endpoint<br>(POST /portfolio/report)"]
    API -->|"issues[]"| Dash["📊 Dashboard Page"]
    Dash -->|"grouped mode"| Banner["🛡️ DataQualityBanner"]
    Detail["📈 Client Pages<br>(Asset/FX Detail)"] -->|"flat mode (per-issue)"| Banner

docs.title: 1. grouped — Dashboard 📊
docs.text:
• One container grouping all issues, in the tone of its worst issue: danger when any issue is an error, else warning, else info (getGroupedSeverity(); severity → tone through DATA_QUALITY_TONE in frontend/src/lib/theme/toneClasses.ts: error → danger, warning → warning, info → info). Each row keeps the tone of its own severity (data-tone on the container and on every row).
  • Issues are sorted by severity: Error 🔴 → Warning 🟡 → Info 🔵.
  • The header counts errors and warnings only, naming just the non-zero counts: "1 error(s)", "2 warning(s)" or "1 error(s), 2 warning(s)" (dataQuality.headerErrors, dataQuality.headerWarnings). With neither — info issues only — it reads "Data quality note" (dataQuality.headerInfoOnly).

  • The banner starts collapsed, showing only its header (let expanded = $state(false)). The header is itself the toggle: a button (test id data-quality-toggle, with aria-expanded and a chevron) that opens and closes the whole list. Once open, the errors and warnings — the issues the header counts — sit indented under it (data-quality-actionable); the info issues follow apart, not indented (data-quality-info), below a thin rule when errors or warnings precede them.

  • Layout of a category (since T2, 19/10/2026; fixShape() in the component). Each category puts its action where it says what it fixes:

    • a button that fixes the whole category (sync_fx_pair, sync_asset_prices) comes first, at the top; the message and the items it fixes hang below it: the pairs, or the asset names of STALE_PRICE (at most 3, then «+N»);
    • an action that works on one item at a time is one chip per item, under the message: navigate_asset one chip per affected asset, and add_fx_pair / navigate_fx one chip per FX pair, like the assets;
    • an issue with no action shows the message alone.
  • The chips and buttons inside a banner stand on the card (bg-lf-card) with an edge in the state colour (STATUS_TONES.bannerChip, proposal a, T3-b), and take a soft tint of that state on hover.
<DataQualityBanner issues={dataQualityIssues} mode="grouped" onaction={handleBannerAction} />

docs.title: 2. flat — Asset Detail / FX Detail 📈 💱
docs.text:
• One banner is rendered per issue.
  • Each banner displays: icon + message + FX pair flags + asset context (in parentheses) + CTA button, in the tone of its own severity. The layout is unchanged by T2: the button stays at the end of the line.
<DataQualityBanner issues={assetDetailIssues} mode="flat" onaction={handleBannerAction} />

docs.title: 🎨 Severity and tone — the rule for any banner
docs.text:
Tone Use it for 🔴 danger (red) A real error: it stops a calculation or makes it wrong. 🟡 warning (amber) Missing or incomplete data that, once supplied, lets the work continue. 🔵 info (blue) A note: something the app noticed, nothing to fix. 🟢 success (green) A success.

The severity is decided condition by condition, where the issue is raised (the backend's severity, error → danger): the component only maps it to a tone and never decides it. The same code can therefore differ by context: the risk lab's MISSING_PRICE (backend/app/services/risk/data_quality.py) is a warning, because the analysis runs on the other assets and a partial result is still worth reading; the portfolio's MISSING_PRICE, whose asset leaves the NAV, stays an error.

docs.title: 🖱️ CTA (Call-to-Action) System
docs.text:
The component emits intent — it does not navigate or open modals itself.

onaction?: (action: string, target: string | null, issue: DataQualityIssue) => void

docs.title: 🎯 Active CTA Actions
docs.text:
Action Target Handled By Description navigate_asset asset_id string goto('/assets/' + target) Redirects the user to the specific asset details page. navigate_fx FX pair slug goto('/fx/' + target) on the dashboard; the asset detail adds ?start=...&end=... Redirects to the FX pair details page. add_fx_pair FX pair slug FxPairAddModal Opens the modal to configure the missing FX pair. sync_fx_pair First affected pair, unused — the handler syncs every pair in issue.affected_fx_pairs (cta_target only when that list is empty) POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/sync (dashboard syncMissingFxRates) Body built by buildMissingFxRatesSyncRequest (utils/sync/syncRange.ts): {pairs, start, end}, the pairs as alphabetical slugs and the issue's message_params.date_from…date_to widened by padSyncRange to 7 days either side, the end capped at today — the margin buildComparisonSyncRange also uses. E.g. 2022-11-03…2023-06-27 → start: '2022-10-27', end: '2023-07-04'. Without usable dates: the full history (start: 'min', end: today). Timeout 120 s (FX_SYNC_TIMEOUT_MS). After the answer — not after a transport error — the dashboard bumps refreshVersion and reloads its report. refreshVersion is the signal Refresh sends too (How a page uses the cache): new rates change the lots and risk figures, so an open LotsAnalysisPanel asks POST /api/v1/portfolio/lots/analysis again with force and drops a warning the sync fixed, and a mounted RiskLevelsPanel (Risk tab) reloads too. Then the dashboard emits one notification, fx.rates.synced, detail {origin: 'dashboard-banner', pairs, start, end, outcome, stillMissing} (stillMissing is null when the report was not reloaded); its toast has one line per pair. When the sync answered ok or partial but the reloaded report still has a sync_fx_pair issue for one of those pairs, the toast appends dataQuality.missingFxRatesAfterSync and a success becomes a warning. sync_asset_prices First affected id, unused — the handler syncs every id in issue.affected_asset_ids POST /api/v1/assets/prices/sync (dashboard handleBannerAction) Sends one item per affected asset: {asset_id, date_range: {start: 'resume', end: <dashboard end date>}}. 'resume' is the backend sentinel for "the day after the last stored price" (full history when there is none). After the answer — not after a failed request, which shows one error toast and reloads nothing — it shows one toast per asset result, bumps refreshVersion as sync_fx_pair does (new prices change the lots and risk figures too: an open LotsAnalysisPanel and a mounted RiskLevelsPanel ask again), and reloads the dashboard report.

In grouped mode, navigate_asset renders one chip per affected asset (data-quality-nav-asset-{id}) and add_fx_pair / navigate_fx one chip per FX pair (data-quality-fx-pair-{pair}); every other action, sync_fx_pair and sync_asset_prices included, renders a single CTA button at the top of its category. While a sync request runs, the dashboard passes the issue's code as the busyCode prop: that issue's CTA button shows a spinner and stays disabled until the request settles. The CTA test id (data-quality-cta-{code}) and busyCode are keyed by the issue code alone; the per-item chips take no busyCode.

docs.title: 🏷️ Active IssueCodes
docs.text:
Do Not Add Future-Proof Codes

Every IssueCode must be actively generated by the backend engine or constructed client-side. Add a new code only in the same step where it is generated. Do not define unused placeholder codes.

docs.title: 📊 Portfolio Issues (generated by DerivedViewsBuilder.build_data_quality_report)
docs.text:
Code Severity Condition CTA Action MISSING_PRICE 🔴 Error Open position with no price and no known cost on the end date: no market quote, no BUY or SELL and no transfer cost estimate on or before it, and a cost not known in the report currency — an acquisition without a cost basis, or one whose rate is missing (ValuationSource.MISSING). With its cost known, the position is valued at cost instead (VALUED_AT_COST, rules below). The NAV leaves the asset out navigate_asset TRANSACTION_IMPLIED 🟡 Warning Open position valued on the end date at the price of its last BUY or SELL, or at the cost of an incoming TRANSFER taken as an estimate (ValuationSource.LAST_TRADE_PRICE), instead of a market quote, for an asset with a provider, outside the 14-day grace period after its last quote — after its first BUY or SELL when it was never quoted, after the transfer's arrival when a transfer cost estimate is all it has (full rule below). message_params: count, as_of_date; group transaction_implied navigate_asset VALUED_AT_COST 🟡 Warning Open position valued on the end date at its book cost (ValuationSource.ESTIMATED_AT_COST): no market quote, no BUY or SELL and no transfer cost estimate on or before it, its cost known in the report currency; for an asset with a provider, once the 14-day grace period has passed, counted from the asset's first acquisition (full rule below). message_params: count, as_of_date; group valued_at_cost navigate_asset STALE_PRICE 🟡 Warning Open position valued at a market price carried forward more than 7 days, on an asset with a provider (full rule below) sync_asset_prices MISSING_COST_BASIS 🟡 Warning An acquisition of the asset has no known cost: a TRANSFER or ADJUSTMENT adding quantity without cost_basis_override (full rule below). Also emitted by the FIFO lots analysis for the analysed asset. message_params: count; group missing_cost_basis navigate_asset INVALID_SPLIT_RATIO 🟡 Warning A SPLIT event linked to a replayed transaction has a stored ratio the layer cannot use (is_valid_split_ratio(): missing, not finite, or not above 0). It counts as missing: only its ratio is dropped (full rule below). Message dataQuality.invalidSplitRatio; message_params: count (the assets); group invalid_split_ratio navigate_asset NON_ISO_CURRENCY 🟡 Warning A stored currency value is not an ISO 4217 code as stored — 978, EURO, eur, which an earlier version saved as written — on a side of a missing pair, on a held asset, or as the report's own currency. One issue per value, and a pair with such a side is in no MISSING_FX_* issue (full rule below). Messages dataQuality.nonIsoCurrencySuggestion, …Candidates and …Unknown; for the report currency dataQuality.nonIsoReportCurrency and …Unknown. message_params: value (at most 16 characters), with suggestion or candidates; group non_iso_currency:<value> none MISSING_FX_MARKET 🟡 Warning A conversion the report needed (sources below) has no configured FX pair add_fx_pair MISSING_FX_RATES 🟡 Warning A configured pair with a real (non-MANUAL) provider in at least one route step cannot convert an amount on some dates: no rate exists on or before them (convert_bulk backfills without limit), so they precede the pair's first stored rate. Movement dates come from the whole history up to the end date, valuation dates only from the period (sources below). message_params: count, date_from/date_to (span over all affected pairs), dates_count; group missing_fx_rates sync_fx_pair MISSING_FX_RATES 🟡 Warning Same, for configured pairs whose routes are all MANUAL. message_params: count only; group missing_fx_rates_manual navigate_fx NAV_INCOMPLETE 🔵 Info One or more days of the period had an incomplete NAV: an asset held that day had no price and no known cost (the MISSING_PRICE condition, day by day); a position valued at cost does not make it incomplete none MWRR_NOT_CALCULABLE 🔵 Info The summary has no MWRR (mwrr_available=False): no net invested capital in the period (the first day's value plus the flows after it: decision N54, so a portfolio younger than the range still has its deposit), a NAV of zero or less on the end date, a period of zero days, or no rate that solves the flows' equation (the solver, _solve_xirr, returns only a verified root). The rule is returns.period_mwrr(), and the history's MWRR points come from returns.period_mwrr_series(), the same rule on each day (developer decision D-MF5): after the first point, pinned to 0, a day whose NAV is zero or less, or whose net invested capital up to that day is zero or less, has null mwrr_annualized/mwrr_cumulative, so the chart line has a gap; the summary's MWRR is the line's last point. A get_report() without a summary always reports it none TRANSFER_SHARE_MISMATCH 🔵 Info A linked internal TRANSFER, CASH_TRANSFER or FX_CONVERSION pair between two brokers of the scope owned at different shares (effective_share: an EDITOR or VIEWER broker counts at 1), on any dates, complete (its later leg) by the end date. Each leg counts at its own broker's share, so what leaves one broker and what reaches the other differ, and the gap is booked as a gain or loss, never as capital (D-MF4 = a): this note explains it. One issue counts the pairs (message_params: count; group transfer_share_mismatch); share_mismatch_warnings names each pair, its two brokers and shares. The classifier records them (ScopeAwareTransactionClassifier, ShareMismatch), the engine result carries them (PortfolioCalculationResult.share_mismatches), and both get_summary() and get_report() pass them on (J-43, night decision N72) none

TRANSACTION_IMPLIED rule. The engine values every holding through the unified price resolver: DailyStateBuilder._value_held_position() (backend/app/services/financial_math/portfolio/daily_state.py) asks _market_value_for(), which reads a per-asset AssetPriceSeries (backend/app/services/financial_math/price_marks.py). The series holds market quotes (PriceHistory) and trade prices: the unit price of each BUY or SELL of the asset at the brokers in scope that carries an amount and is not linked to a split, and the cost of an incoming TRANSFER while the asset has, on or before its day, no quote and no other operation (W-B94, see Transfer cost as an estimate). An ADJUSTMENT is never a price, with or without a cost basis (see Price Resolver). Trades of the same day are averaged, and a quote of that day wins over them. For each day the resolver takes the latest observation on or before it: a quote values the holding at MARKET_PRICE, a trade at LAST_TRADE_PRICE; with no observation at all the holding counts at its book cost when that cost is known (ESTIMATED_AT_COST, see the VALUED_AT_COST rule below) and is MISSING otherwise (MISSING_PRICE). Each daily state collects its LAST_TRADE_PRICE assets in transaction_implied_asset_ids, and the date of each one's last market quote on or before that day in transaction_implied_last_quote_dates (AssetPriceSeries.last_market_date(), None before the first quote). PortfolioService.get_summary() reads both on the end-date state only — an asset quoted since its latest trade is not listed, whatever its past — and transaction_implied_assets_to_report() (backend/app/services/financial_math/portfolio/data_quality.py) drops:

  • the assets still within the grace period of TRANSACTION_IMPLIED_GRACE_DAYS (14, backend/app/services/platform/data_quality_thresholds.py) days, counted from the asset's last market quote on or before the end date (developer decision 30): an asset quoted yesterday and bought again today is valued at today's trade, which is no gap, while a feed that stopped long ago is reported at once. An asset never quoted counts from its first BUY or SELL (first_position_dates, the earliest over its brokers): a normal placement lag, e.g. a bond bought at issue before its first quote. An asset priced only by a transfer cost estimate, never quoted, bought or sold, counts from its first lot movement — the transfer's arrival —, the earliest of first_lot_txn_dates over its brokers (W-B94), as the VALUED_AT_COST grace does. An asset with no date at all gets no grace period;
  • the assets without a provider (no AssetProviderAssignment): valuing them at their last trade price is their intended behaviour.

The list holds one entry per open position, so an asset held at two brokers counts twice in count. as_of_date is the date of the last daily state. The English message of dataQuality.transactionImplied reads "{count} asset(s) valued at their last transaction price — no market price available for over 2 weeks (as of {as_of_date})": the engine does value these assets at the price of their latest BUY or SELL, and the "over 2 weeks" matches the 14-day grace period, which counts from the latest quote. For an asset valued at a transfer cost estimate (W-B94), the "last transaction price" is that transfer's cost, and the two weeks count from its arrival.

VALUED_AT_COST rule. With no observation on or before the day, _value_held_position() counts a held position whose average-cost pool is complete in the report currency (CostStep.report_complete) at its book cost — each acquisition converted at its own date — as ValuationSource.ESTIMATED_AT_COST: a declared estimate, not a price. The position has no current_price (valuation_effective_unit_price and the reference fields are null), its gain_loss is 0, it is never stale and it does not make the NAV incomplete; with its cost unknown or incomplete it stays MISSING (see No observation: valued at cost). PortfolioService.get_summary() lists the end-date positions valued at cost through the same transaction_implied_assets_to_report(), with no quote dates (such an asset has none on or before the end date), and keeps only the assets with a provider: for a manual asset the cost is its intended value, and the banner says nothing. The grace counts from the asset's first acquisition: its earliest BUY, SELL, ADJUSTMENT or TRANSFER across the brokers (first_lot_txn_dates). An asset at cost has no BUY or SELL — an ADJUSTMENT, or a TRANSFER that gave no estimate (no cost basis, or a row of the scope before it), brought it in — so the first position date of TRANSACTION_IMPLIED, which records only those two types (_HOLDING_TYPES), would list it at once. The list holds one entry per open position of a listed asset (MissingPriceAsset), and as_of_date is the date of the last daily state. The English message of dataQuality.valuedAtCost reads "{count} asset(s) valued at cost — no price available for over 2 weeks (as of {as_of_date})". The issue does not change the report's derived data_quality_status.

STALE_PRICE rule. PortfolioService.get_summary builds the list and passes it to build_data_quality_report as stale_prices_dto. An asset is listed when, at the end date, all of these hold:

  • its position is open (quantity above the dust threshold);
  • the position is valued at a market price (ValuationSource.MARKET_PRICE), not at a trade price;
  • that price is carried forward more than STALE_PRICE_THRESHOLD_DAYS (7) days, so a quote exactly 7 days old is still current;
  • the asset has a provider assignment.

Each asset appears once, whatever the number of brokers holding it, as StalePriceAsset{asset_id, name, last_price_date, stale_days}, with stale_days counted from last_price_date to the end date. Left out on purpose: manual assets, which have nothing to sync (those valued at their last trade price, such as crowdfunding or HOLD assets, are stale by design); provider assets valued at a trade price, which are TRANSACTION_IMPLIED's case, or with no price at all, which are VALUED_AT_COST's when their cost is known and MISSING_PRICE's otherwise; closed positions. With stale prices and nothing that makes it partial, the report's derived data_quality_status is carried_forward (source-data status), so portfolio risk results that read it can turn PARTIAL.

MISSING_COST_BASIS rule. PortfolioService._missing_cost_basis_assets() lists the assets whose average cost, in the engine run behind the report, has an acquisition of unknown cost (AverageCost.unknown_cost_movement_ids): a TRANSFER or ADJUSTMENT adding quantity, not split-linked, without cost_basis_override (see WAC & Cost Basis). The engine replays the whole history up to the end date, so the position does not have to be open any more. Each asset appears once, as (asset_id, name), whatever the number of brokers. The average cost adds the quantity without any cost: the units count at zero in the purchase cost (open_cost_basis), and the position's wac_per_unit, gain_loss and annualized_return are null until the pool empties. In grouped mode the issue renders one link per affected asset, labelled with the asset's name.

Two producers build this issue, both through build_data_quality_report(missing_cost_basis_assets=...):

Producer Assets listed Where it shows PortfolioService._missing_cost_basis_assets() Every asset with an acquisition of unknown cost in the engine run behind the report Dashboard banner (summary.data_quality, or the report's own data_quality without a summary) LotsAnalysisService._report_gaps() The analysed asset, when one of its WAC lines has an acquisition of unknown cost; the analysis also turns DEGRADED FIFO lots analysis data_quality, rendered by LotDataQualityBanner without call-to-action buttons

INVALID_SPLIT_RATIO rule. The portfolio engine checks the ratio of each split link with is_valid_split_ratio() (financial_math/splits.py). Before lot MF-D4 an unusable ratio raised ValueError, and the report answered 500. Now the split counts as missing, and only its ratio is dropped. Its linked ADJUSTMENT rows stay in split_linked_tx_ids: they remain the split's rescale, their cost is kept, and they are never in-kind capital nor MISSING_COST_BASIS. The event adds no SplitRecord to split_history, so a trade price observed before the split is not restated by its ratio. It goes once into PortfolioCalculationResult.invalid_split_events (InvalidSplitEvent(event_id, asset_id, date), sorted by event id). PortfolioService._invalid_split_assets() turns them into one (asset_id, name) per asset, ids ascending, in get_summary() and in get_report() without a summary. The CTA opens the first asset: the user fixes the ratio in its events, where the API refuses a ratio not above 0 (see Asset Events). The FIFO lots analysis skips the split and reports no issue for it (see Lots Analysis Service).

NON_ISO_CURRENCY rule. Since lot E-18 a write takes only an ISO 4217 alphabetic code, while an earlier version saved what it accepted as written. Such a value still reads, but no FX rate is stored under it, so its conversions fail, and an edit of its rows is refused until the code is corrected (lot E-19). build_data_quality_report() collects the stored values that are not canonical (is_canonical_iso_currency(), backend/app/schemas/common.py) from three places:

  • the sides of the missing pairs, split as their producers write them, FROM/TO: the TO side is the report currency when the pair ends with it, so a stored value holding a / is never cut in two; otherwise the last / splits. A pair without /, an older dash form, keeps both sides as ISO codes;
  • non_iso_currency_assets: the held assets whose currency is not canonical, (asset_id, name, currency), from PortfolioService._non_iso_currency_assets() over HeldAssetQuoteFacts, the assets held at the end of the period (position_states_end, quantity above the dust threshold);
  • report_currency, the currency the report converts to.

One warning per value, sorted, right after INVALID_SPLIT_RATIO. affected_asset_ids and affected_asset_names list the held assets in that value, and count their number (null without one); affected_fx_pairs stays empty; group_key is non_iso_currency:<value>, with the whole value, because the banner keys its rows by code and group. The message says what the value stands for: one ISO code (suggested_iso_currency()), several (iso_currency_candidates(), joined by ,: Bolívar Soberano may be VED or VES), or none. A minor unit (GBp, minor_unit_factor()) gets no code: pence relabelled as pounds would count 100 times. For the report's own currency the message points to Default Currency in Settings › Preferences. A missing pair with a side that is not canonical is in no MISSING_FX_* issue, since no FX pair can fix it: before lot E-19b, 978/EUR showed as 978-EUR with an add_fx_pair button that got a 422, and a stored eur as the pair EUR-EUR. missing_fx_pairs keeps the raw list. There is no CTA until the developer decides how such a code is corrected (decisions D1 and D2 of E-19): in the asset modal, choosing the right code is a currency change, which deletes the asset's prices and events. A caller without the two parameters, the FIFO lots analysis, still gets the warnings of the pairs' sides and the filtering. Pinned by TestNonIsoCurrencyIssue and TestNonIsoCurrencyAssets (test_data_quality_report.py), test_portfolio_api.py::TestNonIsoCurrencyDataQuality and, for the banner's rows, DataQualityBanner.nonIso.test.ts.

docs.title: 💱 Where missing FX pairs come from
docs.text:
PortfolioService.get_summary() merges every conversion it could not make into summary.missing_fx_pairs (pair FROM/TO with its dates, _merge_missing_pairs()), and build_data_quality_report() turns them into MISSING_FX_MARKET / MISSING_FX_RATES issues. Two sources feed the list:

Source Conversions Dates kept The summary's own conversions Transaction cash amounts at their dates, from the engine's native cash (NativeCash.missing_conversions()); holding prices at the end date; the previous day's price for Δ1; Yield on Cost income As requested The engine, through _engine_missing_fx_pairs() Movements — PortfolioCalculationResult.missing_fx: the average cost of each acquisition (report and asset leg), cash amounts, external cash flows, the cost of assets in transit (at the arrival date) Every date, whenever the movement happened Valuations — DailyPortfolioState.missing_fx_pairs: market prices and in-transit cash, day by day Only the days of the period shown, [date_from, end date]; the first one is the period's opening state

So a purchase made years ago whose rate is missing is reported, because its cost weighs on today's figures, while a valuation gap before the period changes nothing on screen and is left out. A pair with a side that is no ISO 4217 code is reported as NON_ISO_CURRENCY instead (rule above). When get_report() builds no summary, its own data_quality takes its missing pairs from the engine source only, and still reports MISSING_COST_BASIS, INVALID_SPLIT_RATIO and NON_ISO_CURRENCY.

The FIFO lots analysis reports in its own data_quality every conversion it could not make — in its WAC lines, its daily valuation and every other figure it returns (value, return, price, market price and performance histories, lot summary, Gantt segments, event rows, income events), merged per pair — and the WAC lines' acquisitions of unknown cost. Any such gap turns a COMPLETE analysis DEGRADED; see Lots Analysis Service — FX Conversion and WAC Lines.

docs.title: 📊 Dashboard
docs.text: Issue How to Trigger MISSING_PRICE Hold an asset that has no PriceHistory row, no BUY or SELL, and an acquisition whose cost is not known in the report currency: one brought in by an ADJUSTMENT without a cost basis (for an asset with no BUY: a row left by an older version, or the P-10 path — see MISSING_COST_BASIS below), or by an ADJUSTMENT whose cost basis is in a currency with no rate on or before its date. A cost basis of 0 is a known cost, not a missing one: that asset is valued at cost, at zero (ESTIMATED_AT_COST, see VALUED_AT_COST). A BUY is not enough either: its own price values the holding. The NAV leaves the asset out. TRANSACTION_IMPLIED Buy an asset with a provider that has no quote yet (e.g. a BTP in collocamento), then look at a dashboard end date more than 14 days after that first BUY, still before its first quote. Within those 14 days the asset is valued at its trade price without an issue; the issue goes away once the asset has a quote at least as recent as its latest trade, on or before the end date. A manual asset is never listed. VALUED_AT_COST Hold an asset with a provider that has no quote and no BUY or SELL, brought in by an ADJUSTMENT with a cost basis — e.g. a fund received by succession before its first price sync. The holding is valued at that cost on every day, with no price and an unrealized P&L of 0, and the issue shows once the 14-day grace has passed, counted from the ADJUSTMENT's date. A manual asset is never listed. A quote on or before the end date clears it; a BUY or SELL turns the asset into TRANSACTION_IMPLIED's case. STALE_PRICE Hold an open position in an asset with a provider whose newest market price, with no trade of the asset after it, is more than 7 days before the dashboard end date, e.g. prices seeded with POST /api/v1/assets/prices and ending 10 days ago. Any fresh quote clears it, including the live-price polling of the asset pages (POST /api/v1/assets/prices/current stores today's quote). e2e/portfolio/stale-price-banner.spec.ts seeds a holding that stays stale: mockprov with INVALID_TICKER_12345, the one identifier the mock refuses a current price for, and it intercepts the sync the CTA sends. MISSING_COST_BASIS Hold an asset with a TRANSFER or ADJUSTMENT adding quantity, not split-linked, without cost_basis_override. The app refuses to save such a row with costBasisRequired (TransactionService._requires_cost_basis): validate_cost_basis (backend/app/services/transactions/batch_costs.py) checks every create and promote of a batch — new promoted rows as creates, saved ones on the promote that paired them — and, in _check_update_cost_basis, every update that changes the row's type, quantity, cost basis or its asset event link from what was stored before the batch, or names a cost_basis_mode: an edit of only the notes, tags or date of a row stored without cost basis gets no costBasisRequired, and the row keeps its unknown cost. Auto rows skip the check: the Auto step writes their cost, or blocks the batch when a rate is missing. The condition survives only in rows left by an older version: a TRANSFER pair, or an ADJUSTMENT adding quantity, stored without cost basis — including an ADJUSTMENT whose SPLIT was retyped before release 1.3. The app path P-10 closed: an ADJUSTMENT linked to a SPLIT and saved in Auto is stored without cost basis, since the split rescales the pool instead (TransactionService._compute_wac_for_auto_items); without the split it would be an acquisition of unknown cost, so the app no longer takes the split away from it. A retype of the SPLIT is refused with 409 EVENT_SPLIT_ADJUSTMENTS_WITHOUT_COST, and a deletion of the linked event with EVENT_IN_USE; the retype goes through once the ADJUSTMENT has a cost, 0 included (a currency change no longer meets this rule: since N68 it keeps the SPLITs and the transactions linked to them, and no refusal MARKET_DATA_SPLIT_ADJUSTMENTS_WITHOUT_COST exists) — pinned by backend/test_scripts/test_api/test_lots_wac_history.py::TestPortfolioWACSplit::test_forward_split_whose_adjustment_has_no_cost_is_retyped_only_once_the_adjustment_has_one. How the tests produce it: the backend inserts the rows through the session (test_portfolio_cost_currency.py, S5 and S7); in E2E, e2e/portfolio/data-quality-legacy.spec.ts has backend/test_scripts/test_db/legacy_cost_rows.py write legacy rows — only into the lane's test database, for brokers the given user owns — and e2e/portfolio/data-quality-real.spec.ts (E2) checks that the P-10 path no longer produces it. INVALID_SPLIT_RATIO Hold an asset with an ADJUSTMENT linked to a SPLIT event whose stored ratio is 0 or below. The app no longer stores one: the API refuses it with EVENT_INVALID_SPLIT_RATIO, and a provider sync drops it (X-R47). Only a split stored before X-R47, or written straight into the database, still has one. NON_ISO_CURRENCY Hold an asset, or cash, in a currency stored as a number or a name, such as 978. The app no longer stores one (E-18 refuses it at the write); only a row stored by an older version, restored from its backup, or written straight into the database still has one, and ./dev.py db currencies lists them. Offline, test_portfolio_api.py::TestNonIsoCurrencyDataQuality writes 978 with the ORM on its own rows, in the lane's test database only. MISSING_FX_MARKET Hold an asset in a foreign currency (e.g. buy a USD asset) when the dashboard target currency is EUR and the EUR/USD pair is not configured. MISSING_FX_RATES Pick a currency X and configure its pair with the dashboard currency through a route that has a real (non-MANUAL) provider, but no rate on or before the dates of the movements in X — cash movements, purchases or sales paid in X: e.g. deposit X at a broker and buy an EUR asset with it, before the pair's first stored rate. The issue names the pair and the missing dates, with sync_fx_pair (Sync rates). When every step of the pair's routes is MANUAL, the same gap lands in the missing_fx_rates_manual group with navigate_fx. To run the sync offline, as e2e/portfolio/data-quality-real.spec.ts (E1) does, route the pair through the test-only MOCKFX provider (backend/app/services/fx_providers/mockfx/plugin.py: 1.2345 for every day and currency, hidden from GET /api/v1/fx/providers): Sync rates really stores the rates, the reloaded report drops the issue and its banner row goes. NAV_INCOMPLETE Same scenario as MISSING_PRICE — appears automatically when NAV is incomplete for ≥1 day of the period shown. MWRR_NOT_CALCULABLE A portfolio that withdraws more than it has invested in the selected period: deposit 1000, let it grow, then withdraw 1500 while some value remains. From the withdrawal day the net invested capital (the first day's value plus the flows after it) is below zero: the summary has no MWRR and the chart's MWRR line has a gap from that day. A single deposit inside the range is not a trigger: since decision N54 it has its MWRR. TRANSFER_SHARE_MISMATCH Own two brokers at different shares (e.g. one at 100 % and one at 50 %, or a broker you own at 30 % and one you only view), deposit at the first and move cash or securities to the second with a linked CASH_TRANSFER or TRANSFER pair, on the same day or not. The mock data does this for e2e_test_user (Interactive Brokers at 30 %) and the admin (at 40 %).

docs.title: 🔍 Debugging: Verify data_quality.issues Payload
docs.text:
Open browser DevTools → Network → find the POST /api/v1/portfolio/report request.

In the response JSON, look for:

{
  "data_quality": {
    "issues": [
      {
        "code": "MISSING_PRICE",
        "severity": "error",
        "count": 2,
        "affected_asset_names": ["BTP Più SC", "Apple Inc"],
        "cta_action": "navigate_asset",
        "cta_target": "123"
      }
    ]
  }
}

Note: The issues[] array is the single source of truth for dashboard banners. For asset/forex detail, issues are constructed client-side (no network request to inspect).

docs.title: 🛠️ How to Add a New IssueCode
docs.text:
1. Add the code to IssueCode enum in backend/app/schemas/portfolio.py.
  2. Generate it in the backend engine (build_data_quality_report) or construct it client-side on the relevant page.
  3. Set severity (by the rule above), cta_action, cta_target, affected_* fields appropriately.
  4. Add message_i18n_key and its translations in all 4 language files under dataQuality.*.
  5. If a new cta_action is needed, add its label in dataQuality.cta.* and handle it in the parent onaction callback.
  6. Update this document.
  7. Add a backend unit test (if generated by engine) or E2E test (if visible in the UI).
  8. Document how to trigger the issue manually.

docs.title: 🐍 Backend Unit Tests (test_data_quality_report.py)
docs.text:
• 39 tests. 38 cover 7 of the 9 portfolio codes — MISSING_PRICE, TRANSACTION_IMPLIED, STALE_PRICE, MISSING_FX_MARKET, MISSING_FX_RATES (both groups), NAV_INCOMPLETE and MWRR_NOT_CALCULABLE: severity, affected fields, CTA, count, date_range. The last one, TestValuedAtCostIssueCode, pins only that VALUED_AT_COST is an IssueCode.
  • Empty inputs produce no issues.
  • Codes together in one report: test_all_five_codes_can_appear_together (MISSING_PRICE, STALE_PRICE, MISSING_FX_MARKET, NAV_INCOMPLETE, MWRR_NOT_CALCULABLE) and test_all_six_codes_can_appear_together (the same plus TRANSACTION_IMPLIED).
  • TestStalePriceIssue: the sync_asset_prices CTA, the unchanged dataQuality.stalePrice message contract (count, aligned affected ids and names) and the carried_forward status of a stale-only report.
  • TestNonIsoCurrencyIssue and TestNonIsoCurrencyAssets: the NON_ISO_CURRENCY rule — the values from the pairs, the held assets and the report currency, the key by what the value stands for, the minor unit, the values holding a /, the filtering of the three MISSING_FX_* groups, the raw missing_fx_pairs, the place in the issue order — and TestNonIsoCurrencySentences, the five keys written as literals for the sentence check.
  • Not in this file: MISSING_COST_BASIS, covered by test_portfolio_cost_currency.py, and the VALUED_AT_COST issue itself, covered through get_summary by test_portfolio_service.py (both below).

docs.title: 🗄️ Backend Service Tests (test_portfolio_service.py)
docs.text:
TestStalePriceDataQuality checks the STALE_PRICE rule through get_summary, on a DB-backed portfolio:

  • a provider asset last quoted 10 days ago is flagged once, with its last_price_date, its stale_days and the sync_asset_prices CTA, and the status is carried_forward;
  • not flagged: a quote exactly 7 days old, a fresh quote, a manual asset with the same 10-day-old quote, a position sold before the end date, a provider asset valued at its trade price (left to TRANSACTION_IMPLIED);
  • an asset held at two brokers is a single StalePriceAsset.

TestValuedAtCostHoldings and TestValuedAtCostDataQuality check the valuation at cost and the VALUED_AT_COST rule the same way, each asset held only through an ADJUSTMENT with a cost basis:

  • an LKR asset received as 10 units at 3,000 LKR when 1 EUR was 150 LKR is still worth its 200 EUR cost on a day when 1 EUR is 120 LKR: ESTIMATED_AT_COST, no current_price, gain_loss 0, no missing pair, a net worth of 200;
  • a provider asset at cost for 20 days raises one VALUED_AT_COST warning with its whole shape (dataQuality.valuedAtCost, count and as_of_date, group valued_at_cost, navigate_asset on the asset), and is listed neither under TRANSACTION_IMPLIED nor under MISSING_PRICE;
  • the grace counts from the ADJUSTMENT: an asset at cost for 5 or 14 days is not listed, one at cost for 15 days is;
  • a manual asset at cost is listed under none of the three codes.

docs.title: 🗄️ Backend Service Tests (test_portfolio_cost_currency.py)
docs.text:
On a DB-backed portfolio whose rows are inserted directly through the session:

  • TestCostDiagnostics: a purchase, or an opening cost, in a currency without rates leaves the position's cost incomplete and reaches the banner with its pair (S4, S4b); an ADJUSTMENT adding quantity without cost basis raises MISSING_COST_BASIS and leaves the row without WAC or P&L (S5); the engine's failures reach missing_fx_pairs with the purchase date and only the period's valuation days (S6); 4 units that reach a second broker by a TRANSFER without cost basis — linked to a −4 out of the first broker, or an orphan in-leg — raise MISSING_COST_BASIS for the asset: the receiving broker's row has no WAC nor P&L (its value stays known), while the sending broker keeps what it paid, complete (S7).
  • TestLotsAverageCostLines: a purchase that cannot be converted is reported by the lots analysis (pair, issue, DEGRADED) and blanks its WAC lines until the pool empties (L2); an ADJUSTMENT adding quantity without cost basis does the same — DEGRADED, lines blank until the pool empties — with a MISSING_COST_BASIS issue for the asset instead of a pair, reported once for both lines, while its control with a cost basis stays COMPLETE (L3); S7's linked TRANSFER arrival is a MISSING_COST_BASIS issue for the asset, the only one — the FIFO engine itself raises nothing — and the analysis is DEGRADED (L4). The orphan in-leg is left to S7: it fails the FIFO lots (TRANSFER_PAIR_MISSING).

Run both backend suites: 

pipenv run ./dev.py test services roi-fifo-utils
pipenv run ./dev.py test services roi-fifo-utils TestStalePriceIssue TestStalePriceDataQuality   # STALE_PRICE only
pipenv run ./dev.py test services roi-fifo-utils TestValuedAtCostIssueCode TestValuedAtCostHoldings TestValuedAtCostDataQuality   # valuation at cost and VALUED_AT_COST only
pipenv run ./dev.py test services roi-fifo-utils TestCostDiagnostics TestLotsAverageCostLines   # missing cost and FX only
(Covers test_services/test_financial/ — includes test_portfolio_engine/test_data_quality_report.py, test_portfolio_service.py and test_portfolio_cost_currency.py)

docs.title: 🎭 Frontend E2E Tests (e2e/portfolio/data-quality-banners.spec.ts)
docs.text:
Every test signs in as the shared E2E user (TEST_USER) and runs on the seeded data, in parallel with other specs. The dashboard states it needs are portfolio-wide: seeding them for real would mean committing transactions that move the NAV those specs read. So the file injects the issues into the real report it intercepts (injectDashboardIssues, and serveMissingFxRates for MISSING_FX_RATES; both first drop any real issue with the same code, so the row under test is the only one with its code), and it fakes the FX sync (holdFxSync: no provider is reached, no rate is written). What it tests is the rendering, the request a CTA builds and what the page does with the answer, not whether the engine emits the issue. data-quality-real.spec.ts (below) is the counterpart that mocks nothing: it follows the engine's own issues on disposable accounts.

Dashboard (grouped mode)

  • The dashboard loads without JS errors, shows its page and its KPI row (kpi-row), and no longer renders the pre-migration banners dashboard-missing-prices-banner and dashboard-missing-fx-banner (three tests).
  • Two data-conditional checks on the seed's own issues: a banner on screen is a single grouped container with at least one issue row, and its header names no zero count (no "0 error", no "0 warning"). When the seed shows no banner, each test records an info annotation and passes.
  • NAV_INCOMPLETE, injected with date_from 2019-03-04 and date_to 2019-03-06: its row shows both dates, interpolated from message_params.
  • MISSING_PRICE, injected with two assets: its row renders one navigate_asset link per asset. The links are counted inside the row (data-quality-nav-assets-MISSING_PRICE), because every navigate_asset issue names its links with the same pattern, data-quality-nav-asset-{id}. A TRANSACTION_IMPLIED sibling, injected beside it with a third asset, shows its link in its own row: the page has another link, and the count leaves it out by scope.
  • Sync rates on an injected MISSING_FX_RATES issue for EUR-USD, missing dates 2022-11-03…2023-06-27: nothing syncs before the click, then one POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/sync with {pairs: ['EUR-USD'], start: '2022-10-27', end: '2023-07-04'}, a week either side. While holdFxSync holds it, the CTA is disabled and the page's data-busy is true. Once the canned ok answer is released, the dashboard reloads its report and emits fx.rates.synced with {origin: 'dashboard-banner', pairs, start, end, outcome: 'ok', stillMissing: false}; one click, one sync.
  • Sync rates with missing dates from 30 to 2 days ago: the request starts 37 days ago and ends today, not 5 days ahead — the end is capped at today — and fx.rates.synced carries that range.
  • Sync rates when the reloaded report still carries the issue (serveMissingFxRates keeps it after the sync, as when the provider had nothing for those dates): fx.rates.synced reports outcome: 'ok' with stillMissing: true, and a warning toast is on screen.

Asset Detail (flat mode)

  • The first asset of the assets page opens without JS errors, without the pre-migration asset-archived-banner, and without a grouped container: flat mode never renders data-quality-banner (three tests).
  • FX_PAIR_MISSING: the FX routes the page reads (GET /api/v1/fx/providers/routes) are stubbed to none (stubFxRoutes), and injectForeignEvent appends to every POST /api/v1/assets/prices/query result a DIVIDEND in USD (GBP for a USD asset) without original_value — how the backend returns an event whose conversion failed. The event's pair is required and not configured: the issue row and its CTA button (add_fx_pair) are visible.
  • FX_PAIR_NO_DATA: the same injected event, in a currency the asset's currency has a configured route with (the real routes): the pair exists but the event came back unconverted, so the row and its CTA button (navigate_fx) are visible. Neither FX test clicks the CTA, and both pick a seeded asset first (Apple, Microsoft, NVIDIA): the shared listing also holds assets that neighbouring specs have just created, usually with no data.

FX Detail (flat mode), on EUR-USD

  • The pair's page loads without JS errors and renders no grouped container (two tests).
  • Data-conditional: /fx/EUR-USD?start=2000-01-01&end=2000-12-31 shows RANGE_BEFORE_FIRST_DATA, whose message names the first available date (the test looks for a year). When the issue does not show — the pair's data starts before 2000 — the test records an info annotation and passes.

Run test suite: 

pipenv run ./dev.py test front-portfolio banners

docs.title: 🎭 Frontend E2E Tests (e2e/portfolio/stale-price-banner.spec.ts)
docs.text:
• On a disposable account, a provider-priced holding last quoted 10 days ago is reported as STALE_PRICE with the sync_asset_prices CTA.
  • The grouped banner shows the issue with its single CTA button, not per-asset links.
  • The CTA posts one item per affected asset to POST /api/v1/assets/prices/sync (start: 'resume', end: the dashboard end date), and the button is disabled while the sync runs.
  • Once the sync answers, the dashboard reloads its report and the CTA is enabled again. The sync is intercepted with a canned response: no provider is called and no price is written.
  • A second test, on an account of its own, opens the dashboard with the stale holding's lots panel already open (?tab=posizioni&asset={id}), the lot of the seeded BUY on screen. Once Sync prices — intercepted the same way — has answered, the open panel asks POST /api/v1/portfolio/lots/analysis again by itself, and the answer still lists the lot, in the same document: nothing reloaded the page (performance.timeOrigin unchanged). The canned sync moves no figure, so asked and answered is the whole claim — E1's lots-panel check (below), for Sync prices.

Run test suite: 

pipenv run ./dev.py test front-portfolio stale-price-banner

docs.title: 🎭 Frontend E2E Tests (e2e/portfolio/data-quality-real.spec.ts)
docs.text:
Unlike data-quality-banners.spec.ts, which injects issues into the report it intercepts, this spec routes and mocks nothing: each test registers a disposable account that owns the whole dashboard, writes its data through the API and follows the engine's own issues from the report to the screen. The positions cells are read by column: DataTable's data cells (<td class="td-data"> in frontend/src/lib/components/table/DataTable.svelte) carry data-column-id, so this spec and data-quality-legacy.spec.ts read the pnl, pnl-percent and pmc cells of the holdings row data-row-id="{asset_id}-{broker_id}".

  • E1 — a missing rate is reported, never counted at zero. An EUR asset is bought and partly sold with cash in a currency whose pair has a MOCKFX route and no rate yet. The report raises one MISSING_FX_RATES issue (sync_fx_pair) with the pair and the two movement days (dates_count: 2), and the holding's wac_per_unit, gain_loss and gain_loss_percent are null; the banner row shows the pair and both dates, the P&L, P&L % and average-cost cells read «—», and the lots panel reports the issue. No sync request leaves before the click. Sync rates posts the issue dates a week either side, MOCKFX answers ok, and fx.rates.synced reports outcome: 'ok', stillMissing: false. The first movement day then converts at its own stored rate, the reloaded report has no MISSING_FX_RATES, the figures come back and the banner row goes — and the lots panel that was already open asks POST /api/v1/portfolio/lots/analysis again by itself, without a reload, and drops the issue.
  • E2 — no unknown cost through the split path (P-10). A BUY, a SPLIT event, and an ADJUSTMENT linked to it, saved in Auto, which stores no cost on a split-linked row. Retyping the event to PRICE_ADJUSTMENT is refused with 409 EVENT_SPLIT_ADJUSTMENTS_WITHOUT_COST, whose params name the split, its date and the ADJUSTMENT without a cost, and nothing changes: the event is still the SPLIT, the ADJUSTMENT still linked and without a cost. The dashboard and the broker page (/brokers/{id}?tab=posizioni) show figures in the three cells, and neither the banner nor the lots panel reports a missing cost. With a purchase cost of 0 per unit on the ADJUSTMENT, the same retype goes through, the event keeps its id, and still no cost is unknown.
  • E3 — the «Unrealized change» breakdown. One asset quoted in a foreign currency and one in EUR, both bought with EUR, with hand-entered rates that move after the purchase. The report's period_unrealized_breakdown splits the period's change per asset currency into the assets' own change (asset) and the exchange-rate effect on their cost (fx), in the backend's order, adding up to period_unrealized_gain_loss_delta. The tooltip of the Unrealized change bar of KPI card 1 (kpi-unrealized-delta) shows exactly those rows (kpi-unrealized-breakdown-{kind}-{currency}), in that order and to the cent, the loss with its minus.

FX rates and routes are global tables, so each FX test reserves one currency per Playwright project, used by no other test, seed or spec, and deletes the pair's rates and routes before and after. Brokers, assets and the account are deleted by id in the fixture teardown.

Run test suite: 

pipenv run ./dev.py test front-portfolio data-quality-real

docs.title: 🎭 Frontend E2E Tests (e2e/portfolio/data-quality-legacy.spec.ts)
docs.text:
One test, E4 in the numbering above: MISSING_COST_BASIS from rows an older version left behind, which the API can no longer create. A disposable account creates through the API brokers A and B, two manual EUR assets, a DEPOSIT and a BUY of 10 units at A for 200 EUR. The spec then runs backend/test_scripts/test_db/legacy_cost_rows.py in a child process (python -m backend.test_scripts.test_db.legacy_cost_rows, which inherits TEST_PORT and LIBREFOLIO_TEST_DATA_DIR). In one database transaction the helper writes a TRANSFER pair of 4 units from A to B, linked both ways, and an ADJUSTMENT adding 5 units of the second asset at B — no cost basis, no cash, no asset event — and prints their ids as one line of JSON. It writes only into the lane's existing test database, and only for brokers that --user-id owns as OWNER; otherwise it writes nothing. The spec reads the rows back through the API, then checks:

  • one MISSING_COST_BASIS warning naming both assets, ids ascending, with navigate_asset and count: 2; the units at B have no average cost nor P&L, while A keeps what it paid (6 units at 20, +60);
  • the banner row has exactly one link per asset, labelled with its name;
  • «—» in the pnl, pnl-percent and pmc cells of both rows at B, figures on A's row;
  • the lots panel of the transferred asset, opened by the URL, carries the same warning, and the analysis is DEGRADED;
  • the adjusted asset's link opens its page.

The teardown deletes the brokers with force — the helper's rows go with them — then the assets and the account.

Run test suite: 

pipenv run ./dev.py test front-portfolio data-quality-legacy

docs.title: 🧪 Designer Lab
docs.text:
The Designer Lab is a hidden page, /designer-lab, that exists only in debug builds. A designer opens it in one browser tab and changes the app's colours; the app, open in other tabs of the same address, repaints at once — charts included. The designer can also point at an element in an app tab: the Lab shows what sets each of its colours in the code, and can change one of them for that component alone. At the end of a round the Lab exports the changes, with the file and line of every occurrence, so that an agent can apply them to the code.

  • Designers edit colours while looking at the real app: no code, no install.
  • Developers start the server for them and receive the export.
  • Agents verify the export and apply it with the skill designer-lab-apply.

Developer tooling, not a feature

The Lab never reaches a release build, calls no backend API and stores nothing on the server. It has no entry in the user changelog, and its texts stay outside the app's translation catalogue.

docs.title: 🔀 The Build Switch
docs.text:
__LF_DESIGNER_LAB__ is a constant replaced at build time (define in frontend/vite.config.ts, declared in src/app.d.ts). Its value comes from designerLabEnabled() in frontend/scripts/designer-lab/vite-plugin.mjs:

Build __LF_DESIGNER_LAB__ VITE_DEBUG=true: npm run build:debug, ./dev.py front build --debug true vite build --mode development true vite dev (npm run dev) true npm run build, ./dev.py front build (release) false LF_DESIGNER_LAB=1 or LF_DESIGNER_LAB=0 in the environment forced on or off, whatever the build

LF_DESIGNER_LAB=0 gives a debug build without the Lab, to compare two gallery captures with and without it.

The value is a literal, so a release build turns every if (__LF_DESIGNER_LAB__) into if (false): Rollup drops the branch and the dynamic import() inside it, and no Lab chunk is emitted. Three places import the Lab inside such a branch:

File What the branch does src/routes/+layout.svelte (onMount) Imports and starts the Lab client, on every page src/routes/designer-lab/+page.ts load() answers error(404) when the switch is off src/routes/designer-lab/+page.svelte Imports DesignerLab.svelte in onMount 
// src/routes/+layout.svelte — onMount
if (__LF_DESIGNER_LAB__) import('$lib/dev/designer-lab/client').then((lab) => lab.start()).catch(() => {});

A fourth branch, in src/lib/theme/chartCategories.ts (workstream DV), imports nothing: it asks the published hook for an edited category colour, and a release build drops it too — see Chart Categories.

docs.title: 🧪 Test Server, E2E and Gallery
docs.text:
./dev.py server --test always builds and serves the debug bundle: --test forces debug mode, and frontend/build/.build-debug records the mode of the last build. The E2E runs and the gallery use the test server, so they all load the Lab client, and they must stay identical as long as nobody uses the Lab. They do, because in a browser context where the Lab was never opened — every gallery context, and every E2E context but those of the Lab's own specs — the client stays idle:

  • the client publishes its debug hook and adds one storage listener: it loads no engine and no picker, and touches no stylesheet, variable or chart. The hook's categoryColor, which every chart asks for its categories, answers nothing, so the charts keep their tables' colours;
  • the Alt+Shift+D shortcut adds one keydown listener, and only in a browser where the Lab has been opened (lf-designer-lab/seen, written by the Lab page);
  • the engines and the element picker are dynamic imports, separate chunks loaded the first time a state with an effect, or a pick request, appears.

Measured on 14/10/2026 in a debug build: the client chunk weighs 6.2 KB and reaches the picker (73.6 KB, test-id index included) and the engines only through dynamic imports.

docs.title: 🛡️ Release Builds
docs.text:
• /designer-lab keeps only a stub. The backend's SPA fallback answers the URL with 200.html (HTTP 200), then +page.ts throws the 404 and the client renders +error.svelte.
  • The Vite plugin guards the switch in a build without the Lab:
    • generateBundle fails the build when an emitted file contains the marker lf-designer-lab, and names the files. The Lab's code carries it in its storage keys, in the ids of the styles it injects, in its cascade layer and in its dev-server event;
    • load fails the build if anything imports virtual:lf-color-catalog or virtual:lf-testid-index.
  • Checked on 14/10/2026 with the element picker in place: npm run build emitted no file with the marker and no trace of the picker or of the test-id index, and the /designer-lab stub node kept its 488 bytes.

Import the Lab only inside a branch

Every import of $lib/dev/designer-lab must be a dynamic import() inside an if (__LF_DESIGNER_LAB__) branch. A static import would carry Lab code into the release bundle; the marker guard stops ./dev.py front build when that code holds the marker, as the client's store, the engines and the page do.

docs.title: 🔓 No Login
docs.text: The route sits outside the (app) group: no login and no app shell. The Lab calls no API — it reads the catalogue bundled with the build and the state saved in the browser. The app in the other tabs asks for its login as usual.

docs.title: 🎨 Opening It for a Designer
docs.text:
scripts/visual_review/designer_live.sh starts a test server for a designer's review on its own lane: port 6160, data in /tmp/librefolio-color-review, copied from the latest gallery run (--from picks the source lane, --refresh copies it again). The server listens on 0.0.0.0, so a designer on the same network can reach it.

# In a linked worktree, reuse the main venv: the script refuses to start without it
export PIPENV_CUSTOM_VENV_NAME=<main venv name>
scripts/visual_review/designer_live.sh
  • The Lab: http://<this-machine>:6160/designer-lab.
  • The app, in other tabs: http://<this-machine>:6160, logged in with the E2E admin user the script prints.

--test already serves the debug build: the Lab is there without the script's --debug option.

./dev.py server lists http://localhost:<port>/designer-lab in its «Available endpoints» whenever the build it serves holds the Lab's marker: a --test or --debug build, not a release or LF_DESIGNER_LAB=0 build. ./dev.py front dev (port 5173) prints it too, unless LF_DESIGNER_LAB=0.

One address for every tab

The state and the picker's messages live in localStorage and travel through the storage event, both scoped to one origin. http://localhost:6160 and http://192.168.1.20:6160 are two origins that share nothing: open the Lab and the app with the same host name.

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture
docs.text:
The Lab has two halves. The catalogue, built from the sources at build time, gives completeness and provenance: every colour of every file, with file and line, even in components the page has not loaded. The runtime engines give the immediate preview, acting on what the browser has really loaded. The export joins the two: what changes, and where. The element picker starts from the other end: from an element on screen, it proves which declaration sets each of its colours, and the Lab finds that declaration in the catalogue.

---
config:
  layout: elk
---
flowchart LR
    subgraph BUILD["🛠️ Build time: debug builds and vite dev"]
        SRC["frontend/src<br/>+ app.html, offline.html, manifest.json"] --> SCAN["scan-colors.mjs"]
        SCAN --> CAT["virtual:lf-color-catalog<br/>lf-color-catalog/1, built on first import"]
        SCAN --> IDX["virtual:lf-testid-index<br/>the test ids only"]
    end
    subgraph LAB["🧪 Lab tab: /designer-lab"]
        UI["DesignerLab.svelte<br/>editor, element, contrast, export"]
    end
    subgraph TABS["🖥️ Every tab of the same origin"]
        CLIENT["client.ts<br/>started by the root layout"]
        ENGINE["engine/ — lazy chunk<br/>L1 variables · L2 stylesheets · L3 charts<br/>categories · specialisations · colour vision"]
        PICKER["picker/ — lazy chunk<br/>veil · describe · anchor"]
    end
    CAT -->|"Lab page only"| UI
    IDX -->|"picker only"| PICKER
    UI -->|"writeState()"| STORE[("localStorage<br/>lf-designer-lab/v1")]
    STORE -->|"storage event"| CLIENT
    UI -.->|"applyNow() in its own tab"| CLIENT
    CLIENT -->|"first state with an effect"| ENGINE
    UI -->|"start · cancel"| PICK[("localStorage<br/>lf-designer-lab/pick")]
    PICK -->|"storage event"| CLIENT
    CLIENT -->|"pending start or Alt+Shift+D"| PICKER
    PICKER -->|"result · cancel"| PICK
    PICK -->|"storage event"| UI
    UI -->|"Export"| EXPORT["designer-lab-changes.json + .md"]
    EXPORT --> VERIFY["verify-export.mjs"] --> AGENT["🤖 Agent: skill designer-lab-apply"]

docs.title: 🔄 The Client
docs.text:
client.ts, with store.ts and pick.ts, is all of the Lab that an app page loads. start() is idempotent: it publishes window.__lfDesignerLab, adds one storage listener, then reads the three keys once, as if each had just changed. The listener follows them (null, which localStorage.clear() sends, counts for the first two):

Key What the client does lf-designer-lab/v1, the state While no engine is loaded, stop unless the state has an effect — not suspended, with at least one change or a colour-vision mode; otherwise import engine/ (a separate chunk) once, and call applyState(state) lf-designer-lab/pick, the picker's messages While no picker is loaded, stop unless a start is pending; otherwise import picker/overlay.ts (another chunk) once, and let it follow the message. The Lab's own page never picks lf-designer-lab/seen Install the Alt+Shift+D shortcut — see The Two-Tab Flow

The Lab page writes the state itself, and a tab gets no storage event for its own writes, so the page calls applyNow(). Nothing else runs while idle: no BroadcastChannel, no observer, and no keyboard listener in a browser where the Lab was never opened. The engine adds its observers — theme switches on <html>, late stylesheets in <head> — only while a state is active; applyState(null), or a suspended state, undoes everything and leaves the module loaded but idle.

docs.title: 💾 The Shared State
docs.text:
store.ts keeps one JSON document in localStorage['lf-designer-lab/v1'], schema lf-designer-lab-state/1. A state with another schema is ignored.

Field Content changes The changes, in the order they were first made suspended Show the original colours without losing the changes cvd Colour-vision simulation: none, protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia, achromatopsia notes, author The general note and its author, both exported variants, activeVariant Named snapshots of changes, for A/B comparison updatedAt Time of the last write

A change has an id — <layer>:<target>@<scope>, plus #<literal id> when it is restricted to one stylesheet occurrence, and element:<property>[:<colour key>]@<scope>~<selector> for a specialisation — a layer, a target (a variable name, a colour key, a chart category such as type:ETF, or a specialisation's selector), a scope (light, dark or both), from, to (any CSS colour, var(--x) included), alphaVariants (default true), occurrence and match for a single occurrence, property and colorKey for a specialisation, an anchor (the picked element the change was decided on: set on every element change the Lab makes, context on the other layers), a note and shots. isSafeCssValue() refuses a to longer than 200 characters or holding a semicolon, a brace, an angle bracket, a quote, a backtick, a backslash or a comment opener, so a typo cannot break out of a style rule. isSafeSelector() guards a specialisation's selector the same way: at most 600 characters on one line, without a brace, a semicolon, a < or a comment opener.

The picker's messages travel under two other keys, outside this document: see The Two-Tab Flow.

docs.title: 🎛️ L1 — CSS Variables
docs.text:
engine/vars.ts writes one <style id="lf-designer-lab-vars"> in <head>, with one rule per css-var change. The selector carries the scope (VAR_SELECTOR) and names, besides <html>, the .light or .dark subtrees of the scope's themes: the elements on which the token blocks of tokens.css define the colour roles (Colour Roles):

/* example values — scope both, light, dark */
html, .light, .dark { --color-emerald-600: oklch(62% 0.13 160) !important; }
html:not(.dark), .light { --theme-text-muted: #5b6370 !important; }
html.dark, .dark { --theme-text-muted: #a3adbd !important; }

An !important declaration beats every normal one, inside @layer theme or not, so everything that reads the variable follows at once:

  • Tailwind classes, which read the palette at runtime (.text-red-500{color:var(--color-red-500)});
  • their opacity modifiers (color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-red-500) 20%, transparent));
  • the role utilities, which read the role itself (.bg-lf-card{background-color:var(--lf-surface-card)}), and the derived roles built on it;
  • the brand (--color-libre-*) and the --theme-* variables of app.css.

A .light or .dark subtree — an element forced into one theme, which redefines the roles for itself — gets the overrides of its theme too. The derived roles, which tokens.css defines on :root, .light, .dark, recompute from the overridden values, on <html> and in the subtree alike. applyVars() writes every both rule before the light and dark ones, keeping the changes' order otherwise: when a variable has both kinds of change, the theme's rule wins on <html> anyway (html.dark beats the both rule's .dark), and on an island, where the two rules tie on .dark or .light, it wins by coming later.

The reach is the variable: changing --color-emerald-600 changes every class that uses it. The editor shows the impact — uses, files, the most used classes, where the sources define the variable. A role's impact counts the utilities that read it through their alias.

This path serves the variables the whole page inherits, scope: root in the catalogue (:root, html, @theme, html.dark, .light, .dark…), the colour roles included. Variables that a component defines on its own elements (--highlight-*, --cropper-*, --lf-price-flash-*…) are scope: scoped: L2 rewrites their defining rule instead.

docs.title: 🖌️ L2 — Stylesheet Colours
docs.text:
engine/stylesheets.ts rewrites colours in the CSSOM: every rule of every readable stylesheet, nested rules (@media, @supports, @layer) included, minus the Lab's own styles (data-lf-lab-own).

  • By parsed colour, never by text. Chrome serialises #64748b as rgb(100, 116, 139) and expands shorthands into longhands: each colour token of a declaration is parsed and compared by its colour key.
  • Reversible. A rewritten declaration keeps its priority and its original text is saved: each new plan, or none, starts from the page as it was.
  • Alpha variants. Translucent writings of the colour share its key and change too, keeping their alpha. A change can opt out (Translucent variants too).
  • Late stylesheets. SvelteKit loads CSS per route. While a plan is active, a MutationObserver on <head> rewrites each <link rel="stylesheet"> when it loads and each <style> as it arrives.
  • Component variables. A css-var change to a variable defined on a non-root rule rewrites that definition.
  • Variables' definitions. A colour written inside a custom property's definition is rewritten like any other, and the variable changes wherever it is read: a role that tokens.css writes as a literal changes with a Stylesheets edit of that value, as with an L1 edit of the role. The charts that read roles when they draw hear of it through the redraw signal, C4 (Chart Categories).
  • One occurrence. A change restricted to one occurrence carries the selector and property that the catalogue recorded. The engine compares them with each rule after normalizeSelector() — .svelte-… scope classes dropped, :global() unwrapped, spaces and case normalised — and accepts a longhand of the recorded property (border → border-top-color). Occurrence changes are tried before value changes of the same colour. While no loaded rule matches them (its component is not on screen), the change shows nothing: by design, the engine does not fall back to every occurrence of the colour. The change is exported all the same.
  • Theme. A light or dark change applies only while that theme is on, whatever the rule's selector; the engine re-plans at every theme switch. The editor warns when a one-theme change reaches rules written for both themes.

The step 0 spike measured the technique on /transactions: 24 stylesheets and 3,718 rules scanned in 13.5 ms, 33 declarations rewritten in 0.3 ms.

docs.title: 📈 L3 — Chart Colours
docs.text:
ECharts options are built in JavaScript: there is no stylesheet to rewrite. engine/charts.ts combines two mechanisms:

  1. A wrapper on the shared prototype. At the first non-empty chart plan the engine imports echarts — the module the app imports, so every instance shares one prototype — takes an instance on screen, or a 1×1 probe on a detached <div>, and wraps setOption on its prototype. From then on every option an instance receives (first render, new data, theme switch) has its colours mapped. With an empty plan the wrapper is a pass-through.
  2. A live re-apply of the instances on screen. The engine finds them through [_echarts_instance_] and getInstanceByDom(), reads each getOption(), builds a sparse patch with only the colour paths that change, and merges it with the original setOption. Component lists at the root get {} placeholders, because ECharts merges them by index; other arrays (data, colorStops, a palette) are sent whole. Zoom and data stay as they are.

The re-apply exists because forcing a redraw is not enough: at the step 0 spike, 5 of the 17 chart components did not redraw when the class of <html> changed without a theme switch. ScatterChart, CorrelationHeatmap, ExposureBars and ExposureMaps only stored the dark flag, and SemiDonutChart had no observer at all. The spike confirmed it on the correlation heatmap, the scatter and the semi-donut; the re-apply updated 6 instances out of 6, in 1.9–6.8 ms each, with patches of 151–650 bytes. SemiDonutChart now redraws on every class change, while the other four still store the flag only. Some charts also rebuild their option on the Lab's redraw signal, C4 (Chart Categories), which the engine sends when the variables or the categories the charts read change — an L1 edit, a category edit, or a variable's definition the stylesheet pass rewrote — not for chart colours: L3 patches those itself.

The mapping:

  • is copy-on-write: the app's objects are never mutated;
  • walks strings (rgba() keeps its alpha; tooltip HTML included), gradients (colorStops) and functions: formatter, color and renderItem are wrapped once, and their return value is mapped with the plan in force at call time;
  • is reversible: every string the engine writes is remembered with the original it replaced, so a new plan, or none, starts from the app's own colours;
  • writes canvas colours as sRGB rgba(r, g, b, a) with a four-decimal alpha, clamped to the sRGB gamut: a form no colour of the app uses, so the engine recognises its own output when it reads an option back;
  • keeps one plan per theme, and reads the theme in force when it maps; an instance's plan also takes the chart specialisations whose selector contains it (see below).

docs.title: 🍩 Chart Categories
docs.text:
The charts draw each asset type and each sector in a fixed colour, chosen by key: 11 asset-type families and 14 sectors, plus two buckets that both kinds share, Liquidity (the cash) and Unknown. Workstream DV keeps them in frontend/src/lib/theme/chartCategories.ts, under a contract with the Lab:

  • C1, one read point. Every chart reads a category's colour through categoryColor(kind, key, dark): the allocation pie and the allocation history, with their legends and tooltips; the PAC planner's exposure bars, for the actual weights (actualColours() in exposureBarColours.ts: an asset type by its family, its subtypes shaded with familyShade, a sector by its key, the uncategorised remainder as Unknown). The colours borrowed from a category go through it too (see Reach below): the owners of the semi-donut and the countries of the allocation history through sequenceColor, the Growth chart's broker lines and their tooltip rows through growthBrokerColor(). The GR4 subtype shades are mixed from the colour it returns.
  • C2, one literal per line. The tables write one literal per line, each entry under its key, as light: and dark:: an edit is exported by file and line.
  • C3, a hook in debug builds. categoryColor first asks globalThis.__lfDesignerLab?.categoryColor?.(kind, key, dark), inside a typeof __LF_DESIGNER_LAB__ !== 'undefined' && __LF_DESIGNER_LAB__ branch that a release build drops. The app imports nothing of the Lab. The release guard looks for lf-designer-lab, which the name __lfDesignerLab does not hold: the minifier is what keeps the branch out, and DV's chartCategories.test.ts checks it on a minified build.
  • C4, a redraw signal. src/lib/theme/themeMode.ts has onChartColorsChange(cb) and notifyChartColorsChange(): the event lf:chart-colors-change on document. A chart that hears it rebuilds its whole option, so it reads its categories again, and the roles it reads through chartRoles (roleColors.ts, the sRGB bridge).

By key, not by value. Types and sectors share values (ETF and Technology, BOND and Utilities…), and some category values are written elsewhere too, by a role or another chart: a change of the value in the Charts tab would recolour several categories at once. A category change — the sixth change layer — names one category by its key: type:<KEY>, sector:<Key>, bucket:Liquidity or bucket:Unknown, as the table writes it. Its id is category:<target>@<scope>, and its value any colour the editor accepts: a literal, a var(), a mix with transparent.

The engine. engine/categories.ts, part of the engine chunk of the app tabs, holds the category changes of the applied state and answers the hook, which client.ts publishes as categoryColor (The Debug Hook). The hook answers nothing until a state with an effect loads the engine, nor while the state is suspended: the table's colour then stands. Otherwise, for a category with a change in the asked theme:

  • a change for that theme wins over one for both, as in L1;
  • the value is resolved at each ask: a var() follows the page's current value of the variable, an L1 edit included, and a value that does not resolve now gives no answer;
  • the answer is a colour the canvas reads, clamped to sRGB: #rrggbb when opaque, the form the GR4 shades mix, and rgba() when translucent;
  • keys go through DV's own lookupKey (chartCategories.ts), as in categoryColor: case, spaces and underscores ignored (Health Care, HEALTH_CARE), so an edit and the table it overrides always agree on what the same key is; the two buckets answer for both kinds.

stats().categoryOverrides counts the category changes the engine holds.

The redraw (C4). The engine calls notifyChartColorsChange() when what the charts read at their draw has changed since its last check (signalChartInputs() in engine/index.ts). It compares one signature of it:

  • the css-var and category changes, by id and value;
  • the custom-property declarations the stylesheet pass rewrote, on a root rule or a component's, as selector, property and value (variableRewrites() in engine/stylesheets.ts). The roles of tokens.css, the derived ones aside, are written as literals, so a Stylesheets edit of such a value changes the role.

The check runs at the end of applyState(), once every engine is applied — a change added, edited or removed, the state suspended, resumed or reset — and again after the theme observer has re-planned the stylesheets. A literal scoped to one theme rewrites a role in that theme only: after the switch the check signals once, whatever order the theme observers ran in, and a chart that redrew before the re-plan reads the role again. Nothing is sent while the signature stays the same: the same changes applied again, and the changes the charts do not read at their draw — stylesheet literals that define no variable, chart colours and chart specialisations (L3 patches the charts already drawn), the colour-vision simulation. The signal brings an edit of a role, from L1 or from the stylesheets, to the charts that read roles through chartRoles — today the allocation pie, the allocation history, the semi-donut, the correlation heatmap and the PAC planner's exposure bars — at once, where it used to wait for their next draw. A stylesheet that arrives later sends no signal of its own (Known Limits).

Reach. A category's colour is the base of its family's GR4 subtype shades, and the categories without a key of their own borrow it by rank (GR5, sequenceColor): the owners of the semi-donut take the first eight asset types, the countries of the allocation history the sectors. The Growth chart's broker lines borrow the same eight types, cycled without a shade: broker line i takes the colour of the asset type CATEGORY_SEQUENCE[i mod 8] (growthBrokerColor() in src/lib/theme/chartPalettes.ts, read each time the series are built). Every chart that reads a category redraws on C4 — the allocation pie, the allocation history, the semi-donut, the Growth chart and the PAC planner's exposure bars — so a category change reaches all of them at once, the subtype shades and the borrowed colours included: a type edit also recolours the broker lines that borrow it.

docs.title: 📌 Specialisations — element Rules
docs.text:
