A specialisation changes one colour property of a picked element in every instance of its component, without touching the shared source — the variable, the class or the rule the rest of the app keeps using. engine/anchors.ts writes one rule per specialisation into <style id="lf-designer-lab-elements">, for every theme at once (the prefix keeps them apart, as in L1):

/* example value — the header cells of the transactions table, light theme */
@layer lf-designer-lab {
html:not(.dark) :is([data-testid="tx-table"] > div > div > table > thead > tr > th) { color: #475569 !important; }
}

The cascade layer is the point. A <style>@layer lf-designer-lab;</style>, prepended to <head> (id="lf-designer-lab-layer-order"), declares it before any other layer, and among !important declarations the cascade reverses: the first layer wins over the later layers — Tailwind's ! utilities such as !bg-white, in utilities — and over the unlayered declarations — the P1 dark overrides of app.css. So the preview shows the new colour whatever the app writes there; only an inline !important style stays on top. Both styles leave <head> when no specialisation is left.

A rule is written only when the browser parses the selector, isSafeSelector() and isSafeCssValue() accept the selector and the value, and the property is one of ELEMENT_PROPERTIES (cssProps.ts): color, background-color, border-color (the four sides) or one side's border-*-color, outline-color, text-decoration-color, fill, stroke. The picker reports box-shadow and gradients too, but they cannot be specialised.

A chart specialisation (property: 'chart', with the colorKey it replaces) writes no CSS. L3 keeps it in a list per theme, and planFor(instance) adds it to the plan of an ECharts instance only when the instance's DOM sits inside an element the selector matches (dom.closest(selector)). Values that functions return — formatter (tooltips), color, renderItem — are computed later, without their instance, and keep the global plan.

The L2 engine and the picker skip these styles, like every style the Lab injects (data-lf-lab-own), and stats().elementRules counts the rules written.

docs.title: 👓 Colour-Vision Simulation
docs.text: engine/cvd.ts applies an SVG feColorMatrix filter to <html>: protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia with the matrices of Machado, Oliveira & Fernandes (2009) at severity 1, in linear RGB, and achromatopsia with the Rec. 709 luminance weights. The root element is the one place where filter does not turn the element into the containing block of its fixed descendants, so modals and sticky headers keep their place. The mode is part of the state: every tab follows, the Lab's own included.

docs.title: 🔍 The Debug Hook
docs.text:
start() publishes window.__lfDesignerLab (typed in src/app.d.ts) in every tab of a debug build, for E2E tests, the browser console and the charts' category colours:

Member Returns active() Whether an engine is active in this tab picking() Whether this tab is in picking mode, waiting for a click stats() {cssRules, chartInstances, varOverrides, elementRules, categoryOverrides}: declarations rewritten, chart instances patched, variable overrides written, specialisation rules written, category changes held chartColors(selector) A promise of the distinct colours of the ECharts instance in the first element matching selector categoryColor(kind, key, dark) The colour a category change gives that chart category in that theme, or undefined: what categoryColor of chartCategories.ts asks first (C3)

An idle tab answers active() === false, picking() === false, zero stats and no category colour.

docs.title: ▶️ The Scanner
docs.text:
frontend/scripts/designer-lab/scan-colors.mjs is a Node ESM module without dependencies. The Vite plugin calls it, and it runs as a CLI for agents:

node frontend/scripts/designer-lab/scan-colors.mjs --summary                           # summary only
node frontend/scripts/designer-lab/scan-colors.mjs --out /tmp/catalog.json --summary   # catalogue + summary

--pretty indents the JSON, --root <dir> scans another frontend/ tree, --app-version <v> stamps meta.app_version. Without --out the summary is printed anyway.

It reads every .svelte, .ts, .js and .css file under frontend/src — outside node_modules, without the generated API clients (file names starting with generated, or containing openapi or tool-contract-map) and without the Lab's own folders — plus three documents outside the bundle: src/app.html, static/offline.html and static/manifest.json. Test files (__tests__, __mocks__, .test., .spec.) only count towards the var() and definition totals of meta.parity, as in the Python inventory; they never enter the catalogue. In the markup of .svelte files the scanner also indexes the test ids, for the element picker (Test Ids).

Colour parsing lives in src/lib/dev/designer-lab/color.js, plain ESM with JSDoc types: the scanner (Node) and the engines (browser) import the same file, with no compile step in between.

A scan costs about 1.6 s of CPU for ~1,050 files (the wall time grows on a busy machine) and produces about 870 KB of JSON (measured on 14/10/2026).

docs.title: 📐 Schema lf-color-catalog/1
docs.text:
Key Content meta schema, app_version, generated_at, hash, scan_ms, parity (the totals shared with the Python inventory), layers (literals per layer), excluded (the Lab's folders) files Paths relative to frontend/; the other sections point into this list by index css_vars Every custom property defined or read with var(): name, defs (file, line, value, zone, selector, theme and scope, root or scoped; inline and alias_of for a definition inside @theme inline), uses, uses per file, and use_sites, the [file, line, selector] of every var() read (the selector null outside a stylesheet rule) palette Every colour variable a Tailwind class reaches (text-emerald-600 → --color-emerald-600, bg-libre-green → --color-libre-green, bg-lf-card → --color-lf-card): uses, uses under dark:, classes, files, occ, the [file, line, classIndex] of every use — classIndex points into Object.keys(classes) — and role for the alias of a colour role literals Every hand-written colour: id, file, line, col, raw, kind (hex, fn, mix), key, alpha, zone, theme, layer, preview, snippet. Stylesheet colours add selector, at (the enclosing at-rules) and property; script colours add chart; markup colours add via; a line of the chart category tables adds category, the category it colours (type:ETF) by_value Colour key → literal ids categories The chart categories, in the order of their tables: target (type:ETF, sector:Health Care, bucket:Liquidity), kind (type, sector or bucket), key as the table writes it, and light and dark, the id of the literal that holds each theme's value (null when the table writes none) testids Every static test id → the [file, line, via] of each place that writes it: via is attr for data-testid=, prop for a prop that a component renders as its data-testid (testid=, optionTestId=…), script for a property or variable of a script (testId: 'x') testid_prefixes The templated test ids (row-{id}): [prefix, file, line, via], longest prefix first

testids, testid_prefixes, the class index of palette[].occ and css_vars[].use_sites serve the element picker; inline, alias_of and role serve the colour roles; categories and the literals' category serve the chart categories. They are additions: the schema keeps its name, lf-color-catalog/1, and none of them enters meta.parity.

meta.hash is a sha256: of the body only, without volatile fields such as generated_at and scan_ms: it stays the same on an unchanged tree, and the export records it as catalog_hash.

Colour key. Equal colours are grouped whatever their notation: #rrggbb (lower case, alpha dropped) inside sRGB, a rounded oklch(…) outside. Alpha is not part of the key, so the translucent variants of a colour share it. Expressions (color-mix(), var()) have key: null.

Zones and layers. Where a colour is written decides whether the Lab can preview it:

Zone Where the colour is written Layer Live preview svelte-style A <style> block of a .svelte file css-literal ✅ css-file A .css file css-literal ✅ svelte-markup Markup, inside a Tailwind arbitrary class (bg-[#…]) css-literal ✅ svelte-markup Markup, in a style= attribute or elsewhere markup ❌ svelte-script, ts The script of a chart file chart-color ✅ svelte-script, ts Any other script (.ts and .js) script ❌ static app.html, offline.html, manifest.json static ❌

A chart file is one under components/charts, a charts/ folder anywhere, features/dashboard/, features/risk/, features/brokers/lots/ or features/tools/pac-allocator/planner/result/, one whose name holds chart in any case (chartCategories.ts, GrowthChart.svelte), or any file that imports from 'echarts'. It is a heuristic: a chart-color previews only where it reaches an ECharts option.

Theme hint. In stylesheets, dark or light when the rule, or a block around it, is limited to one theme: by a prefers-color-scheme media query, or by a selector list whose selectors all name the same theme — .dark or :not(.light) for dark, .light or :not(.dark) (html:not(.dark)) for light. A list that mixes themes (.a, html.dark .b) applies in both and fixes nothing; both otherwise. In scripts, dark or light from an object key (dark: '#…') or from the side of a ternary whose condition names the dark theme, on one line (isDark ? … : …) or split as Prettier writes it (isDark ending a line, ? '#…' and : '#…' on the next ones); a negated condition (!isDark, !$isDark) swaps the sides. In markup, dark when the class holding the colour carries a dark: variant (dark:bg-[#1e293b]), never from a neighbouring class. null otherwise.

Chart categories. In src/lib/theme/chartCategories.ts (CATEGORY_FILE), categoryLines() reads the tables of the chart categories line by line: ASSET_TYPE_COLORS and SECTOR_COLORS, one entry per key, and the two buckets, LIQUIDITY_COLOR and UNCLASSIFIED_COLOR. Each literal on one of their lines gets category, the target a change names (type:ETF, sector:Health Care, bucket:Liquidity), and as theme the property it is written in, light: or dark:; categories lists the categories in table order. The file is a chart file by its name, so these literals stay in the chart-color layer, and the Charts tab still lists their values.

docs.title: 🎭 Colour Roles
docs.text:
Workstream T moves the interface colours to colour roles, in frontend/src/lib/theme/tokens.css:

  • a role is a variable --lf-<group>-<name>, such as --lf-surface-card. The token blocks define the roles on :root, html.light, .light (light) and html.dark, .dark (dark), and the derived ones — color-mix(), references to other roles — on :root, .light, .dark;
  • an @theme inline block turns each role into Tailwind utilities: --color-lf-card: var(--lf-surface-card) gives bg-lf-card, border-lf-card, ring-lf-card…

With inline, Tailwind writes the role into the utility — .bg-lf-card{background-color:var(--lf-surface-card)} — and emits no --color-lf-card at runtime. The alias exists only in the sources: editing it would change nothing, so the Lab edits the role. The catalogue records the link:

  • Classes. The custom-token class expression covers the role utilities: lf-[a-z0-9-]+, next to libre-*, theme-*, primary* and accent* — TW_CUSTOM_RE in scan-colors.mjs and tw_custom_re in color_inventory.py, changed together. Its prefixes are the palette expression's list, PREFIXES (decision D-a, 15/10/2026): besides bg-, text-, border-, ring-, outline-, divide-, fill-, stroke- and the gradient stops, the side borders (border-t-, -b-, -l-, -r-, -x-, -y-), ring-offset-, shadow-, accent-, caret-, decoration- and placeholder-. So the shadow roles' utilities, shadow-lf-shadow and shadow-lf-shadow-card, count and have their chips. A role name may hold digits, as T's own ROLE_CLASS_RE (frontend/scripts/theme/theme-roles.mjs) allows. A role utility, variants and opacity included (hover:border-lf-card/50), counts among the custom-token classes and enters palette under its alias, --color-lf-<name>.
  • Definitions. A definition inside an @theme inline block gets inline: true and alias_of: the variable it names when its value is exactly var(--x), else null. The two fields are written only for such definitions.
  • Palette. A palette entry gets role when every definition of its variable is an inline alias of one same variable: --color-lf-card → --lf-surface-card. The rule is generic, not tied to the lf prefix.

Wherever the Lab meets an alias it edits the role — the palette chips and the editor's impact, the export's occurrences, the picker's candidates: each section below says how — and L1, above, writes its overrides where the token blocks define the roles. An alias that is not exactly var(--x) gets no role: see Known Limits.

docs.title: ⚖️ Parity with the Python Inventory
docs.text:
scripts/visual_review/color_inventory.py, the inventory of the visual-review toolkit, counts the same tree with the same file selection and the same regular expressions, line by line. meta.parity holds the totals the two share: files, Tailwind palette classes, custom-token classes, arbitrary classes, hex literals, colour functions, var() uses and custom property definitions. On 14/10/2026 both reported 1,047 files, 1,610 hex literals and 211 colour functions, with the same occurrences line by line. The picker's additions — test ids, use_sites, the class index of occ — are annotation, not counting: the Python inventory has no counterpart for them, and the parity totals did not move when they arrived. The same holds for the roles' inline, alias_of and role, and for the chart categories' categories and category; what the roles did change is the class expression. On 15/10/2026, on the base dac0fe43e, which carries the first wave of workstream T, the two class expressions took in the role utilities in the same change (Colour Roles), and the inventories stayed identical line by line: the custom-token classes went from 764 to 912, while the 1,080 files, 1,291 hex literals and 238 colour functions did not move. Later that day, on the base b627c8ef6, both took the palette's prefix list (decision D-a), and the inventories stayed identical again: the custom-token classes went from 1,358 to 1,375. The lf uses went from 611 to 619 — 7 more shadow-lf-shadow and 1 shadow-lf-shadow-card — which is now the count of T's ROLE_CLASS_RE; the other 9 are libre-green uses under accent-, decoration-, border-l- and border-t-.

Change one, change the other

A new regular expression, extension or exclusion in one scanner must land in the other in the same change, or the two inventories drift apart. The Lab's own folders, src/lib/dev/designer-lab/ and src/routes/designer-lab/, are excluded from both (LAB_DIRS in each file): they are tooling, not the app.

docs.title: 🔌 The Vite Plugin
docs.text:
designerLabPlugin() (frontend/scripts/designer-lab/vite-plugin.mjs, registered in vite.config.ts):

  • serves two virtual modules. virtual:lf-color-catalog is the catalogue, built on the first import only — a build or a dev server that never reaches the Lab never scans. virtual:lf-testid-index is testidIndex(catalog), {statics, prefixes}: the test ids alone, for the picker that runs in the app tabs (Test Ids). Both are emitted as JSON.parse of a string literal, cheaper to evaluate than an object literal of this size. In a build they are snapshots of the sources that ship only with the Lab's lazy chunks: the catalogue with the Lab page, the index with the picker. src/lib/dev/designer-lab/virtual-catalog.d.ts types both: an ambient file, because app.d.ts is a module;
  • under vite dev, forgets the catalogue when a scanned source changes, invalidates both modules and sends the lf-designer-lab:catalog-stale event: an open Lab then asks for a reload;
  • in a build without the Lab, runs the guard described in Release builds.

docs.title: 🏷️ Test Ids
docs.text:
The picker says where an element is with the project's own names: its data-testid chain. To write a templated id the way the code writes it, and to find where the code writes it, the scanner indexes the test ids of the sources:

  • In markup (.svelte): data-testid= attributes (via: attr), and the props components render as their data-testid — testid=, testId=, or a name ending in TestId such as optionTestId= or valueTestId= (via: prop). A name that goes on after it, such as testIdPrefix=, is not one. testidValues() reads a quoted value, or the literals of a {…} expression up to its closing brace on the same line.
  • In scripts (a .svelte <script>, .ts, .js): a property or variable whose name ends with testid or testId and takes a literal — testId: 'tab-a', const rowTestId = `row-${id}`, a parameter default (via: script). scriptTestidValues() reads the expression up to the end of the property or statement on the same line. Never a comparison, a …Prefix name, or a type annotation (testId: string holds no literal).
  • Which literals. Only those in value position: at the start of the expression, after ?, :, ??, ||, &&, an arrow => or a grouping ( — never the operands of a comparison, nor the arguments of a call (fn('x')). So {active ? 'tab-on' : 'tab-off'} gives two ids and {x ?? `tab-${id}`} one prefix.
  • Static or templated. A ${…} or {…} cuts the value into a prefix of at least three characters (row-{id} → row-); a value with nothing static before the cut — a pass-through such as {testId} — is not indexable. Static ids go to testids, prefixes to testid_prefixes.
  • In the app tab. virtual:lf-testid-index carries {statics, prefixes}, and only picker/describe.ts imports it: the index rides in the picker's lazy chunk, never in the client. An id of the page that is not static but starts with a known prefix is an instance of a templated id: the selector writes [data-testid^="row-"], the chain and the export row-*.
  • Ids the index does not know are cut by recordPrefix() before their first token that looks like a record: a whole number, or a token with a capital letter — row-42 → row-*, asset-row-42-menu → asset-row-*, kpi-gain-EUR → kpi-gain-* — when at least three characters are left. Digits inside a word do not count (risk-l2-weight stays whole): the project writes its static ids as lower-case kebab words, without capitals. An id with no such token is written as it is.

Writing prefix* keeps record values — a currency code, a row id — out of the export, and makes the selector reach every instance of the component. The limits of the index are in Known Limits.

docs.title: 🖥️ The Lab Page
docs.text:
DesignerLab.svelte reads the catalogue and the saved state, and writes every edit back to the state (writeState(), then applyNow()). When the browser refuses the write — storage full or disabled — the Lab shows an error status and keeps the last saved state, the one the other tabs see.

Header.

  • Point at an element asks the app tabs to enter picking mode; while the Lab waits, the button reads Cancel picking. Next to it, a reminder that Alt+Shift+D does the same from an app tab. See The Element Picker.
  • Editing: the theme the next change applies to — light, dark or both; the theme on screen by default, then the theme of each new pick, unless both is selected.
  • Suspend / Resume: every tab shows the original colours; the changes are kept.
  • Variant: Save variant stores the current changes under a name. Choosing another variant first saves the changes on screen into the active one (into current when none is active), then loads the chosen one: A/B in one click.
  • Colour vision: the simulation mode, for every tab.
  • Export JSON + MD, JSON, MD, Copy summary, Import, and Reset all, which asks for confirmation and keeps notes, variants and the colour-vision mode.

Tabs. A search box (name, value or file) filters the palette, variable, value and category tabs. Once an element is picked, the checkbox Only the picked element's colours next to it narrows the palette, variable and value lists to that element (what it keeps). The Categories tab hides the checkbox, which would filter nothing there: the picker does not name a category yet (Known Limits).

Tab Content Overview Hand-written colours per layer and how many are live-editable, palette and app variables in use, catalogue schema, file count and scan time Element The picked element: where it is, each of its colours with its source, Edit the source and Specialise here — see The Element Tab Tailwind palette The --color-* variables the classes reach, by family and shade, with their uses; the role utilities form the family lf App variables Variables the app defines with a colour value: brand, --theme-*, the colour roles, component variables — never an inline alias Stylesheets css-literal colours grouped by value, alpha variants together, with occurrences, files, alphas and theme hints Charts chart-color colours, grouped the same way Categories The chart categories in three groups — asset types, sectors, cash and unclassified — each row with its light and dark swatches and values; a row opens the editor on its category No preview script, markup and static colours: proposals only Changes The current changes, from → to, with layer, theme and note; a specialisation shows its property, and opens the editor with its anchor Contrast WCAG ratios before and after the changes, in both themes, plus a free pair Notes Author and general note, both exported

Roles in the palette. The family lf holds the role utilities, one chip per alias, whose shade is the rest of the alias's name (--color-lf-card → card, --color-lf-action-hover → action-hover). A chip keeps its alias's test id, lab-item-var-<alias> (lab-item-var---color-lf-card), but edits the role (Colour Roles): data-target="--lf-surface-card", title --color-lf-card → --lf-surface-card, and its swatch and changed state follow the role. The search finds a chip by its role too. App variables lists the roles, as root variables, and omits the inline aliases (appVars()), which no stylesheet defines at runtime.

Editor (ColorEditor.svelte), opened from any entry:

  • a text field that accepts any CSS colour, OKLCH sliders (L, C, H), and a warning when the value leaves sRGB;
  • a fourth slider, A, for the opacity (0–100%). Some roles carry one, written color-mix(in oklab, <base> p%, transparent) — the backdrop --lf-surface-overlay, --lf-selected. Mixing with transparent keeps the base colour and gives it opacity p, whatever the interpolation space: the editor reads that form (colorValue.ts), and A changes p and keeps the base, so a role in the base (var(--lf-focus)) stays referenced; at 100% the value becomes the bare base. On a var(--x), A writes that form; on a literal, it sets the alpha — oklch(… / a) for an oklch() literal or one outside sRGB, #rrggbbaa otherwise. Both swatches sit on a checkerboard, so the opacity shows. L1 previews the value as typed; for a stylesheet or chart colour, L2 and L3 multiply the alpha of each occurrence they change by the value's (resolveTarget() resolves the mix);
  • <input type="color"> as an sRGB shortcut, and Snap to a variable, which writes var(--x): a proposal to unify two colours. Its list offers the roles, never their inline aliases. Like the L, C, H sliders, both change the colour and keep the opacity (withBase()): a translucent value stays translucent, a mix stays a mix;
  • for values, Translucent variants too and, in stylesheets, Reach in the code: every occurrence, or one occurrence with its selector — preselected on the picked element's rule when the editor is opened from the Element tab and exactly one catalogue occurrence matches it;
  • for a chart colour that is also the colour of chart categories, a warning that names them and points to the Categories tab: a change of the value would recolour them all at once;
  • a note and gallery screen codes such as dashboard/kpi-top — the codes of the designer package;
  • the impact of a variable (uses, files, most used classes, definitions), or the occurrences of a value (file, line, selector, property, theme, snippet). varImpact() (catalogView.ts) adds up the palette entries that read the variable, directly or through an inline alias, and the variable's own var() uses: a role's impact counts its utilities, and its definitions are those of tokens.css;
  • in element mode, opened by Specialise here: the selector, the property (and the colour key for a chart), the reminder that only this component changes, how many elements the selector matched when the element was picked, and where an agent would bind the new variable. The current value is the one the picker read on the element;
  • for a category, opened from the Categories tab: the value its table writes in the theme being edited as the current one, a note on the reach — every chart reads the colour through categoryColor, the subtype shades follow, and only this category changes, even where another one has the same value — and Written at, the line of each theme in chartCategories.ts, with its value. There is no translucent-variant or reach choice: the change is by key.

Contrast (contrast.ts, ContrastPanel.svelte). The declared pairs come from the catalogue: every root --theme-text-* on every root --theme-bg-* except the hover surfaces (AA at 4.5:1, AAA at 7:1), and every --theme-border-* on the card surface (3:1, the threshold of UI components). Before uses the value the sources define for each theme (sourceVarValue()): the definition for that theme, else one both themes share (:root, @theme) — never the other theme's — and at equal footing the later one, as in the cascade. After applies the css-var changes; a translucent foreground is composited over the background first. Changes to literal colours, chart categories and specialisations do not enter this table.

docs.title: 🎯 The Element Picker
docs.text:
The designer points at an element in an app tab, and the Lab shows what sets each of its colours in the code. Two ways to change one follow:

  • Edit the source: the shared variable, class value or rule. Every element that uses it changes, so the designer can tour the app and see the effect on the rest.
  • Specialise here: this component only. The shared source stays as it is, and the export tells an agent where to bind a new variable.

The app tab reports facts — computed colours, the declarations proved to set them, test ids, CSS — without the catalogue; the Lab tab matches them with the catalogue.

docs.title: 🔀 The Two-Tab Flow
docs.text:
This is the reference workflow: the Lab in one tab or window, the app in another. They talk through localStorage, the channel the colour state already uses, with two keys of their own (pick.ts):

Key Content lf-designer-lab/pick The last message: start (the Lab asks the app tabs to pick), cancel, or result (an app tab reports the element it picked, with its facts). Each has an id and a time at lf-designer-lab/seen Written by the Lab page when it mounts: this browser has opened the Lab
  1. Point at an element writes a start with a new id. Every app tab of the origin gets the storage event, loads the picker chunk and enters picking mode. A start younger than five minutes (PICK_FRESH_MS) is pending: a tab that loads or reloads meanwhile joins it; an older one is a forgotten request.
  2. Alt+Shift+D in an app tab enters picking mode in that tab only, without a start. The client reads the key from event.code === 'KeyD', not from event.key: on macOS, Alt+Shift+D types «Î». The listener exists only where lf-designer-lab/seen is set — tabs already open install it as soon as the Lab is opened in the same browser — and the shortcut does nothing on the Lab page itself, with Ctrl or Cmd, or on a repeated key.
  3. A click on an element writes a result. The Lab takes any result, from its own request or from a shortcut, and opens the Element tab on it; every tab still picking leaves picking mode.
  4. Esc in the picking tab writes a cancel for its request: the other tabs waiting for the same request leave picking mode, and the Lab, if it was the one waiting, shows «Picking cancelled». Cancel picking in the Lab does the same from the other side, and so does leaving the Lab while it waits: it writes the cancel when it unmounts (in-app navigation) and on pagehide (its tab closed, reloaded or left for another site).

A result ends picking everywhere, a cancel ends the request it names, and removing the key ends any. A pick started with the shortcut has its own id, so the Lab's cancel leaves it alone. When the Lab opens, it shows the last result left in the key.

Picking mode (picker/overlay.ts), in the app tab:

  • A veil (data-testid="lf-lab-pick-veil"): a transparent <div> fixed over the whole window, at the top of the z-index range, with a crosshair cursor. It takes every pointer event, so the element below is never hovered: the picker reads its resting colours. The app opens no <dialog> with showModal() and no popover, so no top-layer element of the app covers the veil.
  • A frame and a label follow the element under the pointer, once per animation frame: the frame outlines its box, and the label names its tag and nearest test id (div · tx-table). The element under the pointer is the first one document.elementsFromPoint() returns outside the Lab's own nodes; a shape inside a lucide icon stands for the icon's <svg>.
  • Events — pointer, mouse and touch events, clicks, contextmenu and keys — are stopped at window, in the capture phase (preventDefault() and stopImmediatePropagation()): no handler of the app's elements runs, and a click never reaches the app. Key combinations with Ctrl or Cmd pass through, so the browser's shortcuts keep working. The wheel is replayed by hand on the scrollable container under the pointer, or the page: over the veil, the browser would scroll the page alone.
  • Inline styles only. The veil, the frame and the label carry inline styles and the data-lf-lab-own attribute: L2 never rewrites them, and the picker skips them.
  • A click with the main button describes the element (describeElement()), writes the result and leaves picking mode. If the description fails, the tab logs the error and writes a cancel instead.

When a result arrives, the Lab:

  • replaces the previous pick and opens the Element tab;
  • closes an editor left open on a specialisation of the previous pick, which would edit the wrong element;
  • switches Editing to the theme the element was picked in — a P1 dark override shows only there — unless it is both.

docs.title: 🔬 Finding What Sets a Colour
docs.text:
picker/describe.ts runs in the app tab. For each colour the designer sees on the element, it reports the computed value and the declaration that sets it: proved, not guessed from selectors.

The colours read (analyseAll()):

Property When color Always. It is inherited: the search walks up the ancestors (below) background-color, background-image The background the designer sees: the element's, or that of the first ancestor whose background is not transparent. background-image only when it holds colours, a gradient border-*-color Each visible side: width above 0, style not none or hidden. Four equal sides — same value, same winning declaration — merge into one border-color outline-color A visible outline text-decoration-color Any text decoration fill, stroke SVG elements, unless none box-shadow A shadow with colours

The candidates. collectRules() walks every readable stylesheet but the Lab's own, and keeps the style rules that declare a colour property, each with its cascade layer (utilities; nested layers dotted), the conditions around it and its stylesheet. It enters an @media or @supports block only when its condition holds now, and gives a nested rule an absolute selector (& stands for the parent). For a property, the candidates are:

  • the declaration of every rule the element matches: the longhand, or a shorthand that sets it (SHORTHANDS in cssProps.ts: background, border, border-top, border-color, the logical border-block-* and border-inline-* forms…). The shorthand matters with var(): the CSSOM then leaves the longhand empty, and only the shorthand holds the text;
  • the rules that would match in a state the element is not in — :hover, :focus, :focus-visible, :focus-within, :active, found by stripping those pseudo-classes. They are listed, so the designer sees them, but never tried and never winners;
  • the inline style;
  • the presentation attribute of an SVG element (fill="…", stroke="…", color="…").

Rules on pseudo-elements (::before, ::placeholder…) are left out: the picker reads the element itself. Each candidate records its text as written, before any Lab change (originalValue() of L2).

The proof. The candidates are sorted by an estimated cascade order: !important first; then inline styles, rules, attributes; unlayered before layered for normal declarations, the reverse for !important ones; later in the document first. The estimate ignores specificity: the proof settles it. prove() takes the candidates in that order:

  1. it sets the property to a probe colour in the candidate's block, with the same priority: rgb(1, 2, 3) — 0 0 0 1px rgb(1, 2, 3) for a shadow, a gradient of it for an image;
  2. it reads the computed value of the property;
  3. it puts the declaration back exactly, restoring the whole cssText of its block (or the attribute);
  4. the first candidate whose probe changed the computed value is the one that sets it.

At most 12 candidates are tried per property. All the probing runs in one synchronous task inside withoutTransitions(): a <style data-lf-lab-own> turns transitions off, and styles are flushed before and after. Nothing is painted in between, and no transition starts. The Lab's own specialisation sheet is disabled meanwhile, since a specialisation would win every probe; the property is flagged «already specialised» when one of its rules applies.

Up the tree. color, fill and stroke are inherited. When the element declares none, or its winner is inherit or unset — Tailwind's preflight writes color: inherit on buttons and inputs — or currentColor for color, the search moves on to the parent, and further up. The property then records the depth, the tag and the nearest test id of the declaring ancestor. A background seen through from an ancestor is recorded the same way. A colour whose winner writes currentColor, or which equals color with no winner, is flagged: it follows the text colour.

Charts. Inside an ECharts instance ([_echarts_instance_]), the facts add the chart: the selector of its component (its nearest test id, else its CSS path), the colours of its option as the app wrote them — L3's changes undone, at most 40 — and the colour of the shape under the pointer. That colour comes from zrender's hit test, not a documented ECharts API: when it fails, the colour is unknown.

What the app tab reports (PickedElement in types.ts): the route (SvelteKit's route id, see The Anchor), the theme, the test-id chain (nearest first, at most 8), the CSS path (positions included), the tag, the classes without Svelte's scope class (reported apart), the element's own component selector and, per property, the computed value, its colours, the depth, the declarations with the winner first, and the specialisation selector. Never the element's text.

docs.title: 🧷 The Specialisation Selector
docs.text:
A specialisation needs a selector for «this element, in every instance of its component» — decision (a) of 14/10/2026. build() in describe.ts computes one per property, with the helpers of picker/anchor.ts:

  1. Which element. The element that declares the colour, when it sits inside the picked element's component, whose root is the picked element's nearest test id: a header text whose colour the th declares, a card whose background shows through. Above the component — the page, body — the picked element itself.
  2. Where it is. The nearest test id above it — [data-testid="x"], or [data-testid^="prefix"] for an instance of a templated id — then the path down to the element, tag by tag, with child combinators and without positions: the same node of the same template, in every instance. Beyond six segments, the selector keeps the last six, after a descendant combinator. An element with its own test id is that test id alone.
  3. Which classes. On the element, only the classes the winning rule names (selectorNames()): p.text-gray-500 keeps its colour class, while a layout or state class — flex, sorted — neither widens nor narrows the selector. Svelte's scope classes never enter: they change with every build. A selector longer than 400 characters falls back to the test id followed by the element, as a descendant.
  4. No test id around. The element's own CSS path from body, positions included: breadth: element, this element only.

Next to Specialise here, the Lab shows the selector and how many elements it matched on the open page when the element was picked (countMatches()). That count is the check. In the first live test, a design that wrote the test id, the tag and all the element's classes took 52 elements for a layout div inside a header cell of the transactions table, body cells included. The shipped design specialises the th that declares the colour, and takes the 12 header cells, nothing else:

[data-testid="tx-table"] > div > div > table > thead > tr > th

docs.title: 🧭 The Element Tab
docs.text:
pickView.ts resolves the facts against the catalogue, and PickedElement.svelte shows them:

  • where the element is: route, theme, tag and classes; the test ids, nearest first (tx-table ‹ transactions-page ‹ app-shell); its component node with breadth and match count; its CSS path;
  • each colour: a swatch, the property and its computed value, the kind of source, the source itself — the class, the variable chain, the winning rule — and up to three file:line from the catalogue; then the two actions and, folded, Where to bind it in the code and Declarations (every candidate, the winner first, state rules muted, with layer, conditions and stylesheet).

Source kinds (classify()):

Kind When Edit the source opens var A rule outside Tailwind's utilities reads a variable The variable (css-var) tailwind-class The winning rule is in the cascade layer utilities; the class is its first class, unescaped (.dark\:text-gray-400 → dark:text-gray-400) The variable the class reads, or its colour value rule-literal A rule writes the colour The value (css-literal), preset on the matched occurrence when there is exactly one inline The style attribute The variable it reads, or a proposal attribute An SVG presentation attribute A proposal current-color The value is currentColor — edit color chart A colour of the chart under the pointer The chart colour (chart-color) unknown No candidate was proved —

A role utility is a tailwind-class source like any other: the winner .bg-lf-card, in the layer utilities, holds var(--lf-surface-card), so the chain starts at the role and Edit the source opens --lf-surface-card (Colour Roles).

Around the source:

  • The variable chain: the variable the winner reads, then the variable its root definition reads in the picked theme — that theme's definition, else a shared one, as for contrast — and so on, up to six steps (varChain()). Each name opens the editor on that variable, with the property's anchor as context.
  • Badges: «dark-theme !important override» when the winner is an !important rule whose selector names html.dark — the P1 overrides, whose file shows among the candidates; «over the class …» with the Tailwind class the winner overrides; «already specialised»; «inherited from …» and «background of …» with the declaring ancestor's tag and test id (<th> in tx-table); «follows the text colour».

Where to bind it in the code lists the candidates: the places an agent would bind a specialisation, each with the text expected there and why. Exact places come first, then the test-id places; duplicates go, and at most 12 stay.

why The place How the Lab finds it matched-rule The stylesheet rule that sets the colour Catalogue literals with the winner's colour key and a declaration of the property, shorthands included, whose selector equals the winner's after normalizeSelector(): those in the component's files, else the first six anywhere. A nested or wrapped rule does not compare: the colour's literals in the component's files stand in class-use The colour class on that line The uses of that exact class (palette[].occ with its class index): in the component's files, else all of them when there are at most six. A role utility's uses are found through the role: the alias entry that lists the class (--color-lf-card for bg-lf-card) var-use The rule that reads the variable For var, or a class whose uses were not found: css_vars[].use_sites by the winner's selector, else in the component's files, else all when at most six literal An inline style or an SVG attribute; for a chart, a chart colour The markup literals of the colour, by the same rule; for a chart colour, its chart-color literals in the component's files testid Where a test id of the chain is written The nearest id of the chain that the catalogue knows: a static id's places; for prefix*, or an id the scanner saw only as a template, the places of the longest catalogue prefix it extends; at most four

«The component's files» are the files that write the nearest test id of the chain the catalogue knows — the places of the testid candidates. A class, a variable or a markup value used in more than six places, none of them in those files, gives no candidate: by itself it is no anchor.

The two actions:

  • Edit the source opens the usual editor on the shared source (table above), with the anchor as context.
  • Specialise here opens the editor in element mode on the property's selector, shown next to the button with its match count. It is offered for the properties a specialisation can set (Specialisations), and not for a background seen through from outside the component: only the picked box would change there, so the source is the thing to edit.

A chart's colours follow the properties, the colour under the pointer first, each with the same two actions: a chart-color change of the source, or a specialisation with property: 'chart' for this chart's component.

The filter. Only the picked element's colours narrows the palette, variable and value lists to: the variables of every chain, the colour keys of the computed values and of the matched literals, the chart's colours, and — so that the class an app.css override hides, or a hover colour, still shows — the variables and colours of every declaration found, winners or not. A role in those chains brings its alias names too (--color-lf-card for --lf-surface-card): the palette lists a role's utilities under their alias, so their chips show.

docs.title: 🧱 The Six Change Layers
docs.text: Change layer What it changes Engine Reach css-var A custom property: Tailwind's --color-*, the brand --color-libre-*, --theme-*, a colour role, a component variable L1 on <html> and the .light/.dark subtrees; L2 for a component variable Every use of the variable css-literal A colour written in a stylesheet: a component <style>, app.css, a Tailwind arbitrary class L2 The value with its translucent variants, or one occurrence chart-color A colour written in a chart script, as it reaches an ECharts option L3 The value with its translucent variants proposal Colours with no live path: inline styles, other markup and scripts, generated colours, app.html, offline.html, manifest.json — Exported only, with preview: false element A specialisation: one colour property of a picked element, or one colour of the charts inside its component Specialisation rules; L3 for a chart colour The elements the selector matches, in every instance of the component category The fixed colour of a chart category: an asset type, a sector, or the Liquidity or Unknown bucket — type:<KEY>, sector:<Key>, bucket:… engine/categories.ts, through the hook categoryColor asks (C3), then the redraw signal (C4) That category in every chart that reads it, its subtype shades included; never another category with the same value

docs.title: ⚠️ Known Limits
docs.text:
• By value, not by meaning. Until colours become tokens, a change reaches every place that writes the value (problem P5 of the colour analysis): the spike found the same #64748b in 33 rules of /transactions — a modal, the pagination, the data table. The editor lists the occurrences, and a stylesheet colour can go down to one occurrence; a chart colour cannot, because an ECharts option carries no provenance. The export lists the catalogue's occurrences for both. A specialisation narrows either to one component, chart colours included. The fixed colours of the chart categories are the exception: the Categories tab changes them by key (Chart Categories).
  • ECharts' default palette (#5070dd, …) is not written in the app's sources: it is not in the catalogue, and the Lab does not offer it.
  • Derived and generated colours. A colour computed before setOption — a shade derived from a literal (familyShade, the GR4 shades), an HSL generated from an index (getIndexColor, lotColor) — reaches the option as a value no change targets. The preview changes a base colour only where the option carries it unchanged; the export still points at the literal in the source. The shades of a chart category are the exception: they are mixed from what categoryColor returns, so a category change reaches them.
  • No preview for the proposal layer.
  • Variables redefined in a subtree. L1 writes its overrides on <html> and on the .light and .dark subtrees (VAR_SELECTOR in engine/vars.ts), where the token blocks of tokens.css define the roles: a theme island that redefines the roles takes the override too. A definition under any other selector — a component's own — is rewritten by L2 instead; only one in a style attribute, which no engine rewrites, keeps its value for its subtree, as the nearer definition. Conversely, L1 runs in the app tabs without the catalogue (designerLabImports.gate.test.ts lets only the Lab page import it), so its selectors are the same for every variable: it cannot know where each one is defined. A variable the app defines on <html> only — a --theme-* of app.css, a palette shade — thus also gets a one-theme override inside a .light or .dark island of that theme placed in the other theme, where the code does not redefine it: the preview there shows a value the edited definition would not reach. Today no element but <html> carries light or dark (themeStore.ts and the inline script of app.html set them on document.documentElement), so no such island exists yet.
  • Inline aliases that are not var(--x). An @theme inline alias with any other value — a color-mix(), say — gets no role (Colour Roles): its chip edits the alias itself, a variable that does not exist at runtime, so nothing changes. Edit the roles it mixes. tokens.css has none today.
  • Other color-mix() values. The editor reads a mix with transparent, the A slider's form, but not a mix of two colours, nor one whose two percentages do not add up to 100: for such a value it shows Unrecognised colour and no sliders, and keeps Apply disabled until a new value — typed, from the sRGB input or snapped to a variable — replaces it.
  • Class names in comments count as uses, in the scanner and in the Python inventory alike: the header comments of app.css and tokens.css name role utilities (bg-lf-card, text-lf-muted…; shadow-lf-shadow-card is written only there). They show among the uses, in the editor's impact, and among the export's occurrences, where an agent finds a comment line.
  • Wide gamut. Stylesheets keep the value as typed, so an oklch() outside sRGB stays wide; charts receive it clamped to sRGB. The editor warns when a value leaves sRGB. <input type="color"> and the gallery screenshots are sRGB only, so a wide-gamut display shows such colours more saturated than the PNGs.
  • Late stylesheets and the redraw signal. A stylesheet that arrives after the state is applied — a route's CSS — is rewritten when it loads, without a redraw signal of its own: a variable it defines that a chart reads at its draw would wait for the chart's next draw. The roles chartRoles reads are all defined in tokens.css, which app.css imports: the global sheet, not a route's.

The chart categories:

  • The picker does not name a slice's category. It reports the colour of a pie slice as a chart colour, and one value can belong to two categories: open the category from the Categories tab. While a category change applies, the slice reports the edited colour, not the table's. Naming the category is in L's backlog.
  • Translucent category colours. For a translucent value the engine answers rgba(), and the charts draw the category with it. Its GR4 subtype shades, though, are mixed from the colour alone — familyShade reads the channels and drops the alpha — so they come out opaque.
  • bucket:Unknown and keys outside the tables. An edit of bucket:Unknown reaches the categories the tables call Unknown, of both kinds, and the charts that ask for Unknown by name (the unclassified countries of the allocation history). categoryColor also draws a key outside its tables in the Unknown colour, but the edit does not reach such a key: it keeps the table's colour. The enum gates keep such keys out of real data.

The element picker:

  • Pointer-transparent elements. document.elementsFromPoint() skips elements with pointer-events: none: such an element cannot be picked, and the element under it is picked instead.
  • Resting colours only. Rules for :hover, :focus or :active are listed with the declarations but never proved, and cannot be specialised; pseudo-elements (::before, ::placeholder) are not read.
  • Conditions not evaluated. @container, @scope and the other grouping rules are walked without evaluating their condition, which is only recorded: the probe decides whether the declaration applies.
  • Rules that do not compare. The selector of a nested or wrapped rule does not match the catalogue's after normalisation: the candidates fall back to the colour's literals in the component's files.
  • A structural selector. The path below the test id is exact for today's DOM: a wrapper added later breaks the preview selector. The export keeps the candidates and the test ids, which verify-export checks.
  • Backgrounds from outside. A background seen through from outside the component cannot be specialised: edit the source.
  • Shadows and gradients are reported, not specialised.
  • Inline !important beats a specialisation, as it beats every rule.
  • Svelte scope classes never enter a selector: they change with every build. The anchor reports the element's scope class apart, as context.
  • Lower-case values in unknown ids. The index covers the markup's test-id attributes and props and the scripts' …testId properties and variables; an id it does not know is cut before its first number or capitalised token. A data value inside such an id that is a lower-case word — no digit, no capital — cannot be told from the code's own words: the chain, the selector and the export write it as it is.

docs.title: 📤 Export for Agents
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Dev as Developer
    participant D as Designer
    participant Lab as Designer Lab
    participant A as Agent
    Dev->>Dev: scripts/visual_review/designer_live.sh (port 6160)
    D->>Lab: open /designer-lab, the app in other tabs
    D->>Lab: point at elements in the app (Alt+Shift+D)
    D->>Lab: change colours, add notes and screen codes
    Lab-->>D: designer-lab-changes.json + .md
    D->>Dev: send the export

docs.title: 📄 What the Designer Downloads
docs.text:
• designer-lab-changes.json, schema lf-designer-lab/1, for the agent.
  • designer-lab-changes.md, its twin for people: one section per change (from → to, reach, impact, note, screen codes, definitions) and a table of up to 40 occurrences, the rest only in the JSON. A change decided on a picked element adds the element (route, theme, tag, test ids), its source and its CSS path. A specialisation adds its selector, with breadth and match count, and its table is Where to bind the new variable — file, line, expected text, why — in place of the occurrences. Headings follow the Lab's language.
  • Copy summary puts a header and one line per change on the clipboard, for a chat or an e-mail; a specialisation's line names its selector and property, and counts candidates instead of occurrences.

The export is a browser download: nothing is stored on the server. Keep it outside the repository, in lab-exports/ of the visual-review work directory: --work-dir, else $LF_VISUAL_REVIEW_DIR, else LibreFolio_subRepo/LibreFolio_visual_review next to the main checkout when that folder exists, else ~/LibreFolio_visual_review (scripts/visual_review/README.md).

docs.title: 🧾 Schema lf-designer-lab/1
docs.text:
An abridged export (occurrence lists and classes cut):

{
  "schema": "lf-designer-lab/1",
  "app_version": "v1.2.0-11-g27228466c",
  "catalog_hash": "sha256:39340076…",
  "exported_at": "2026-10-20T15:02:11+02:00",
  "author": "",
  "notes": "Greens too bright in light mode.",
  "changes": [
    {
      "id": "css-var:--color-emerald-600@light",
      "layer": "css-var",
      "scope": "light",
      "preview": true,
      "target": "--color-emerald-600",
      "from": "oklch(59.6% 0.145 163.225)",
      "to": "oklch(62% 0.13 160)",
      "occurrences": [{"file": "src/lib/components/assets/AssetCard.svelte", "line": 133}],
      "impact": {"uses": 52, "files": 27, "classes": {"text-emerald-600": 46, "bg-emerald-600": 3}},
      "note": "gains green too bright",
      "shots": ["assets/list"]
    },
    {
      "id": "css-literal:#374151@dark",
      "layer": "css-literal",
      "scope": "dark",
      "preview": true,
      "target": "#374151",
      "from": "#374151",
      "to": "#3b4556",
      "occurrences": [
        {
          "file": "src/lib/components/ui/feedback/LoadingSpinner.svelte",
          "line": 60,
          "col": 23,
          "raw": "#374151",
          "layer": "css-literal",
          "theme_context": "dark",
          "selector": ":global(.dark) .spinner",
          "property": "border-color",
          "snippet": "border-color: #374151;"
        }
      ],
      "granularity": "value",
      "alpha_variants": true
    }
  ],
  "contrast": [{"fg": "--theme-text-muted", "bg": "--theme-bg-primary", "scope": "light", "before": 4.83, "after": 5.12}],
  "variants": {}
}
Field Meaning app_version, catalog_hash The build (__APP_VERSION__) and the catalogue the export was made with exported_at ISO 8601 with the local offset author, notes From the Notes tab changes[].id, layer, scope, target As in the state: for element, target is the specialisation's selector; for category, the category (type:ETF) changes[].preview false only for proposal changes[].from, to The value the Lab saw, and the new value (any CSS colour, var(--x) included) changes[].granularity, alpha_variants css-literal, chart-color and proposal: value or occurrence, and whether translucent writings change too changes[].impact, definitions css-var: uses, files and Tailwind classes, the editor's figures (varImpact()); where the sources define the variable (file, line, selector, theme, value) changes[].property, color_key element: the property specialised, or chart with the colour key it replaces in the charts the selector reaches changes[].anchor The picked element the change was decided on: on every element change the Lab makes, and on a change of another layer opened from the Element tab — see The Anchor changes[].category category: the chart category as its table writes it, {kind, key} — kind is type, sector or bucket changes[].occurrences css-var: the file and line of every class use, and raw, the class, for a utility that reads a colour role. element: the anchor's candidates, as file, line, raw (the text expected there) and why. Other layers: file, line, col, raw, layer, theme_context, selector, property, snippet — for category, only the category's own line in each theme of the change changes[].note, shots The designer's note and gallery screen codes, when given contrast The declared pairs whose ratio changed: fg, bg, scope, before, after variants The named variants, as the Lab stores them

The to of a change is recorded as typed, so it may be a color-mix(…, transparent), the translucent form of the A slider: the schema is unchanged, and the skill applies such a value as written, which keeps a var() base referenced.

A css-var change on a colour role (--lf-surface-card, see Colour Roles) takes its impact from varImpact(): uses and files count the role's utilities and its own var() uses, and classes lists the utilities (bg-lf-card…). Its occurrences[] are the lines of those utilities, each with raw, the class: the line names neither the role nor a palette shade, so the class is the text verify-export looks for there. definitions[] lists the role's definitions in tokens.css. The schema is unchanged: occurrences already had raw.

A category change (Chart Categories) adds category: {kind, key}, and its occurrences[] are the lines of chartCategories.ts that write the category's colour in the themes of the change: the light: line, the dark: line, or both for both, each with raw, the value written there, and theme_context, the theme of the line. They are never the other places that write the same value, and verify-export finds them again by key and theme, not by value. A category change has no granularity and no alpha_variants. These are additions too: the schema keeps its name, lf-designer-lab/1.

The occurrences of a value change are the catalogue literals with the same colour key, in the change's layers (proposal covers script, markup and static); translucent ones are listed only with alpha_variants. A one-theme change leaves out the other theme's occurrences only where their theme is certain: in stylesheets (css-file, svelte-style), where the rule's selectors and media queries give it, and in markup (svelte-markup), where the dark: variant of the colour's own class gives it. A script occurrence (ts, svelte-script) is always kept, whatever its hint: a script's theme is a guess from names and ternaries, so the agent reads its theme_context.

docs.title: ⚓ The Anchor
docs.text:
An anchor (LabAnchor in types.ts, snake case as in the export) says where a change was decided: the element picked in the app, with the route, the test ids and CSS.

Field Content route SvelteKit's route id (page.route.id) without its (group) segments, dynamic segments kept as [param] — /assets/[id], /fx/[pair], never the record's id — plus ?tab= when there is one; the path only where SvelteKit has no route id theme The theme on screen when the element was picked: light or dark testids The test ids from the element up, nearest first, as the code writes them — prefix* for an instance of a templated id; at most 8 css_path The element's own path below its nearest test id (or body), positions included element tag, classes (without Svelte's scope class) and scope_class, that class apart: per-build context selector, breadth The property's specialisation selector; component (every instance) or element (no test id around: this element only) matches How many elements selector matched in the app tab when the element was picked property, computed The property and its computed value source What sets it: kind (one of the source kinds), the winning rule's selector, the var it reads (the head of the chain), the Tailwind class candidates Where to bind a specialisation: file, line, why and needle, the text expected there

No element text in an export

The anchor says where the element is — route, test ids, CSS — and never what it shows: no text content, no cell value. A debug build can run on real data (./dev.py server --debug), and an export travels by e-mail or chat. A templated test id is written as prefix*, so the record it names stays out too; an agent finds the component by test id, path and candidates, never by content. Keep it that way when you extend the picker, and mind the one gap left, in Known Limits.

The live export of the final picker check (14/10/2026), one entry of changes, compacted. The designer pointed at the layout div in the selection column's header cell of the transactions table; #ff00aa is the check's test value, and the Svelte scope class (svelte-1utaimv) belongs to that build:

{
  "id": "element:color@light~[data-testid=\"tx-table\"] > div > div > table > thead > tr > th",
  "layer": "element",
  "scope": "light",
  "preview": true,
  "target": "[data-testid=\"tx-table\"] > div > div > table > thead > tr > th",
  "from": "rgb(100, 116, 139)",
  "to": "#ff00aa",
  "occurrences": [
    {"file": "src/lib/components/table/DataTable.svelte", "line": 1607, "raw": "#64748b", "why": "matched-rule"},
    {"file": "src/lib/features/transactions/TransactionsTable.svelte", "line": 993, "raw": "tx-table", "why": "testid"}
  ],
  "property": "color",
  "anchor": {
    "route": "/transactions",
    "theme": "light",
    "testids": ["tx-table", "transactions-page", "app-shell"],
    "css_path": "[data-testid=\"tx-table\"] > div:nth-of-type(1) > div > table > thead > tr > th:nth-of-type(1) > div",
    "element": {"tag": "div", "classes": ["flex", "items-center", "justify-center", "gap-1"], "scope_class": "svelte-1utaimv"},
    "selector": "[data-testid=\"tx-table\"] > div > div > table > thead > tr > th",
    "breadth": "component",
    "matches": 12,
    "property": "color",
    "computed": "rgb(100, 116, 139)",
    "source": {"kind": "rule-literal", "selector": "th.svelte-1utaimv", "var": null, "class": null},
    "candidates": [
      {"file": "src/lib/components/table/DataTable.svelte", "line": 1607, "why": "matched-rule", "needle": "#64748b"},
      {"file": "src/lib/features/transactions/TransactionsTable.svelte", "line": 993, "why": "testid", "needle": "tx-table"}
    ]
  }
}

The picked div (anchor.element, anchor.css_path) inherits its colour from the th, which declares it: the specialisation targets that th in every instance of the transactions table (selector, the 12 header cells on the page). Read together, the candidates give the binding: the rule at DataTable.svelte:1607 would read a new variable, set by the transactions table where its test id is written (TransactionsTable.svelte:993), so that the other tables keep their colour — the skill designer-lab-apply has the details. The same change in the Markdown twin:

## element · `[data-testid="tx-table"] > div > div > table > thead > tr > th` · color · light

- `rgb(100, 116, 139)` → `#ff00aa`
- element: `/transactions` · light · `div` · `tx-table` ‹ `transactions-page` ‹ `app-shell`
- selector: `[data-testid="tx-table"] > div > div > table > thead > tr > th` (component, 12 elements on the page)
- source: rule-literal · `th.svelte-1utaimv`
- css_path: `[data-testid="tx-table"] > div:nth-of-type(1) > div > table > thead > tr > th:nth-of-type(1) > div`

Where to bind the new variable:

| File | Line | Expected text | Why |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `src/lib/components/table/DataTable.svelte` | 1607 | `#64748b` | matched-rule |
| `src/lib/features/transactions/TransactionsTable.svelte` | 993 | `tx-table` | testid |

docs.title: 📥 Import
docs.text:
Import reads an export back (parseImport() in export.ts):

  • it requires the schema lf-designer-lab/1; a change with an unknown layer or scope, or an unsafe to, is reported and skipped;
  • a specialisation (element) is skipped as invalid unless its selector passes isSafeSelector(), its property is one a specialisation can set, and a chart one carries a color_key (#rrggbb or oklch(…));
  • a category change is skipped as an unknown category unless its target has a safe shape — type:, sector: or bucket:, then at most 60 letters, digits, spaces or _&.- — and names a category of the running catalogue;
  • an anchor, on any layer, goes through sanitizeAnchor(), which keeps only the shape and the sizes the Lab writes: one-line strings within limits (route 300 characters, selectors 600, at most 8 test ids, 40 classes and 20 candidates), the enums (theme, breadth, source.kind, why), positive line numbers and a --name for source.var. An anchor without a readable route, safe selector, property or tag is dropped with a warning; the change is kept;
  • it warns when catalog_hash differs from the running catalogue: the code changed since the export;
  • it finds a single-occurrence css-literal change again by file, line and raw value; when that occurrence is gone, the change falls back to every occurrence of the value, with a warning;
  • it keeps one change per id, as the Lab does: a repeated change replaces the earlier one, in its place, with a warning;
  • the imported changes replace the current ones; notes, author and variants come from the file when it has them.

docs.title: ✅ Verifying an Export
docs.text:
verify-export.mjs checks an export against the code as it is now:

node frontend/scripts/designer-lab/verify-export.mjs designer-lab-changes.json          # human summary
node frontend/scripts/designer-lab/verify-export.mjs designer-lab-changes.json --json   # lf-designer-lab-verify/1 report

It rebuilds the catalogue to compare its hash with catalog_hash, then looks for every occurrence on its file:line, case-insensitively. The text it looks for is the occurrence's raw when it has one — a literal, or the class of a role utility — else, for a css-var change, the family-shade of its --color-* target (emerald-600), for a Tailwind class use. Each occurrence is:

  • ok: still there;
  • moved: elsewhere in the same file, reported with the nearest line;
  • missing: nowhere in the file.

Variable definitions are checked the same way, and value_now reports a definition whose value changed since the export. --root <dir> checks another frontend/ tree. An export is input: a path that leaves the checked tree (../../etc/hosts) is never read, and counts as missing (as gone, for a candidate).

Specialisations and anchors. The candidates of an element change are located the same way, on their raw text, but counted apart — candidates_ok, candidates_moved, candidates_missing: a candidate that moved or is gone is a hint, not an error. Every change with an anchor, and every element change, gets an anchor.status:

anchor.status Meaning ok For a specialisation, at least one candidate is still there; and every test id of the anchor is still written in the code testid-missing A test id of the anchor is no longer written — listed in testids_missing; the component moved or was renamed. A warning no-candidates A specialisation that lists no candidate: the agent binds it by test id lost A specialisation none of whose candidates is still there, in place or moved: exit code 1

no-candidates and lost come first; testid-missing only when neither applies. The test ids are checked against the rebuilt catalogue (testidKnown()): a static id must still be written, or produced by a known prefix; a prefix* is known when it extends a catalogue prefix, or when static ids start with it — the picker may have cut an id the index did not know. The totals add anchors_lost and anchor_testids_missing, and the human summary a line for the specialisations.

Chart categories. The occurrences of a category change are found by key and theme, never by value (locateCategory()): categories share values, and a search for the value could land on another category's line. categoryLines() of the scanner reads the occurrence's file, and the line that writes the change's target in the occurrence's theme_context decides. The occurrence is ok when that is its own line, moved when the key and theme are written on another line now (reported with that line), and missing when the key is gone or its line holds a value other than raw: the export's starting value is stale.

Exit code Meaning 0 Nothing is missing and no specialisation is lost: moved occurrences, moved or gone candidates, testid-missing and no-candidates are fine 1 At least one occurrence is missing, or a specialisation is lost 2 Bad input: no file, not JSON, or not an lf-designer-lab/1 export

docs.title: 🤖 The Skill designer-lab-apply
docs.text:
.github/skills/design-tools/designer-lab-apply/SKILL.md tells an agent how to apply an export:

  1. verify it with verify-export.mjs;
  2. group the changes by layer;
  3. apply them occurrence by occurrence — never a blind replace of a value everywhere — respecting scope and theme_context, and the owners of app.css and of the token files;
  4. prove the effect with a same-day gallery diff (scripts/visual_review/README.md);
  5. report every change, including those not applied and why.

A specialisation (element) leaves the shared source as it is: the agent creates a component-scoped variable, or a role token, and binds it at the places the candidates list. The selector in target is the preview's, context rather than code to paste; since no element text is exported, the component is found by route, test ids and CSS path, never by content.

A category change is applied on the lines its occurrences[] list in chartCategories.ts, one per theme of the change, and never by value: another category, a role or another chart may write the same value. The subtype shades follow the new colour by themselves, and a bucket change edits the one entry both kinds share.

Changing how the app looks is a decision: an agent applies an export only when the developer asks, in a workstream allowed to change the appearance.

docs.title: 🎨 The Lab Never Repaints Itself
docs.text: The Lab's own colours reach the page only as --lab-* custom properties in the inline style of its root element (labTheme.ts, one set for light and one for dark, following the class of <html>). Its stylesheets hold no colour, only var(--lab-*), and its markup uses no Tailwind colour class. The engines rewrite stylesheet rules and the variables of <html> and of the .light/.dark subtrees — classes the Lab's markup never carries — never an inline style, so editing the app's colours never repaints the Lab. Specialisation rules aim at the app's elements: a component selector starts from an app test id, which the Lab's markup never carries. The colour-vision filter sits on <html> and applies to the Lab as well.

docs.title: 🌐 Language
docs.text: The Lab speaks Italian and English through its own small dictionary, i18n.ts (labT, labLang): Italian when the app's locale is Italian, English for every other language. This is a developer decision: the Lab is a debug tool and stays outside the app's translation catalogue, an exception to the four-language rule of the UI. Do not add Lab keys to the app catalogue.

docs.title: 🧪 Tests and Gates
docs.text:
• The Lab lives under frontend/src, so the source gates that walk the whole tree cover it too. In frontend/src/: no {@html} (htmlSink.gate.test.ts), clipboard writes only through writeTextToClipboard (clipboardSink.gate.test.ts), htmlInterpolation.gate.test.ts, flagFont.gate.test.ts and routes/documentTitle.guard.test.ts. See Security Architecture for the output-escaping gates.
  • Coverage runs exclude the Lab's folders (exclude of the istanbul plugin in vite.config.ts): debug tooling would only add never-run files.
  • The test runner groups the Lab's tests in the category front-designer-lab (./dev.py test front-designer-lab <action>): unit runs the Vitest files; live, picker and neutral run one E2E spec each — the engines between two tabs, the element picker, the idle client of a context that never opened the Lab; e2e runs the E2E specs in one Playwright invocation; all runs the units, then the E2E specs.
  • Unit tests sit next to the sources, as *.test.ts files in frontend/src/lib/dev/designer-lab/, and the route has its own, frontend/src/routes/designer-lab/page.test.ts. The E2E specs live in frontend/e2e/designer-lab/ (designer-lab-live, designer-lab-picker, designer-lab-neutral, with lab-helpers.ts) and run on the test server's debug build.
  • A source gate, designerLabImports.gate.test.ts, checks the Lab's imports on the syntax tree, before any build: outside the Lab's folders, only the root layout's guarded import() of the client; the catalogue imported by the Lab page only, the test-id index by picker/describe.ts only; client.ts reaching engine/ and picker/ only through import(); the route files reaching the Lab only through a guarded import(). It is the static side of the release guard (Import the Lab only inside a branch).
  • Seams for tests: the pure modules (color.js, colorValue.ts with parseTransparentMix(), resolveValue(), withOpacity() and withBase(), store.ts, pick.ts, cssProps.ts, catalogView.ts with varImpact(), editTarget(), isInlineAlias(), categoryRows() and sourceCategoryValue(), contrast.ts, export.ts with sanitizeAnchor(), pickView.ts); the DOM helpers of picker/anchor.ts, which take the test-id index as a parameter and run under jsdom; elementRule() and applyElementRules() in engine/anchors.ts; applyVars() and VAR_SELECTOR in engine/vars.ts; categoryKey (DV's lookupKey, re-exported), categoryTargetKey(), setCategoryChanges() and categoryColor() in engine/categories.ts; collectRules() in picker/describe.ts; the exported functions of the scripts (scanColors(), scanSource(), listSourceFiles(), testidValues(), categoryLines(), designerLabEnabled(), filesWithMarker(), testidIndex(), verifyExport(), locate(), locateCategory(), testidKnown()); mapChartOption() and chartPatch() in engine/charts.ts, kept for tests.
  • In the browser: window.__lfDesignerLab (picking(), categoryColor(), stats().elementRules and stats().categoryOverrides included) and the test ids. The page root is data-testid="designer-lab", with data-catalog-hash and data-changes; every control has a lab-… test id. A palette chip is lab-item-var-<variable>, with data-target, the variable it edits; the picker's are lab-pick, lab-pick-cancel, lab-tab-element, lab-picked-… (with data-property, data-kind, data-matches) and lab-filter-picked. The Categories tab is lab-tab-categories, its list lab-categories and a row lab-item-category-<target> (lab-item-category-type:ETF); in the editor, a category's reach note and lines are lab-editor-category-reach and lab-editor-category-lines, and the warning on a chart value that is also a category's colour is lab-editor-category-warning. In the app tab, the veil is lf-lab-pick-veil.
  • The app's side of the chart categories contract has DV's own tests: src/lib/theme/chartCategories.test.ts pins C3 — the hook asked first in a debug build, never asked without the switch, and gone from a minified build with the switch off — and src/lib/theme/themeMode.test.ts pins the C4 event. On the Lab's side, categories.test.ts holds the engine's key rule to DV's real categoryColor and runs C3 end to end, and chartColorsSignal.test.ts checks when applyState() sends C4.

docs.title: 🔁 Rebuilds
docs.text:
The switch, the catalogue and the test-id index are fixed when the bundle is built, and dev.py decides whether to rebuild from the timestamps of frontend/src and of a few config files: it sees neither frontend/scripts/ nor an environment variable. After changing the scanner or the plugin, or LF_DESIGNER_LAB, force a rebuild (./dev.py server --test --rebuild, or ./dev.py front build --debug).
