Measured before the render, the inset is conservative: equal to, or a few px wider than, what ECharts draws. axisLabelMeasure(chart, fontSize) gives the measure: the width echarts.format.getTextRect() returns in the font of axisLabelFont(chart, fontSize), the chart model's textStyle.fontFamily or, before a first option, ECharts 6's own default (sans-serif, Microsoft YaHei on Windows). It is lazy on purpose: the font is resolved at the first measure and echarts.format read only inside the call, so a test that mocks ECharts without format still mounts a chart that measures nothing.
  • Wide labels: no axisLabel overrides, only the formatter, which the consumers apply in both modes: ECharts' own labels are English on a time axis and raw ISO dates on a category one.
  • Time axis (buildTimeAxisFormatter): a label names the tick ECharts places, not the length of the period, so ticks a week apart read 8 Aug, 15 Aug (in en-GB), never Aug Aug. A day tick reads 15 Jul and 1 January 2026. The 1st of another month reads Aug when the ticks are months (tick level 0), 1 Aug when it is a month boundary among day ticks. A tick off local midnight gets no label: it would repeat a day already on the axis. When compact, with the end labels forced on, the first and last data points keep their day, plus a two-digit year when the range crosses a calendar year; the midnight of a last day that ends mid-day gets no label.
  • Category axis (buildCategoryAxisFormatter): a compact axis labels one point every interval + 1. Month names stand alone only when every two neighbouring labels fall in different months; otherwise a label reads day and month. The two-digit year appears where it changes from the previous label, and on the first and last point when the data crosses a year. A label off the regular grid (the last point, or one moved by zoom) keeps its day. A wide axis has no interval: ECharts picks the labels, so each carries what it needs, the month for monthly data, the day otherwise, the year whenever the data crosses one.

The category axis serves PriceChartFull (asset and FX detail, with its CandlestickChart) and LineChart (the Chart Settings preview and the risk charts; the asset and FX cards draw it through PriceChartCompact, date axis hidden). The time axis serves GrowthChart in its time-axis views (the Candles and Income ladders plan their own labels, above), AllocationHistoryChart and the broker lots charts (LotWacPriceChart, LotComparisonChart and LotGanttChart, which pass their own padding). When a chart goes back from compact to wide, its consumer rebuilds the whole option, or merges categoryAxisLabelPatch() on a zoom, so compact-only keys such as alignMaxLabel do not linger.

Three of the time-axis charts take the right inset. GrowthChart (base: '4%', 14 px labels) computes it in its time-axis views only (the ladders keep '4%': their plan keeps the outermost labels inside the canvas, above), in the full option, in the partial update (new dates are new labels, so the inset travels with the axis they are drawn on) and on resize, since '4%' stands for other pixels at another width; the resize applies it at once, not lazily, because syncPlotGeometry() reads the grid that call lays out. AllocationHistoryChart ('4%', 14 px) computes it with every option it builds and on resize (lazyUpdate). LotComparisonChart (base: 18 px, 12 px labels) computes it on its axis date range (xAxisRange, else the series' own) only when it builds the option: a px base does not follow the width. LotWacPriceChart and LotGanttChart keep a fixed 18 px (GRID_RIGHT_PX).

docs.title: Chart Text and Tooltips
docs.text: ECharts reads none of the app's CSS: it draws legends, labels and axes on a canvas, and writes its tooltip as HTML with an inline font. Two rules follow, one for the font of that text and one for the tooltip's HTML.

docs.title: Flags in chart text
docs.text:
The app draws flags (the regional indicator symbols U+1F1E6–1F1FF) with the 'LF Flags' face that starts its CSS font stacks (Fonts). That CSS never reaches chart text: ECharts drew it in its own default family, and a flag in a legend, a label, an axis or a tooltip fell back to the system, which prints two letters where it has no flag glyphs (Windows among them).

lib/components/charts/chartFont.ts exports the charts' font:

  • CHART_FONT_FAMILY: 'LF Flags', then ECharts' own default family (sans-serif, or 'Microsoft YaHei' on Windows, chosen the way ECharts chooses it). The face covers the flags and nothing else, so every other character falls through to that default and keeps its font.
  • CHART_INIT_THEME: {textStyle: {fontFamily: CHART_FONT_FAMILY}}.

Every chart is created with that theme, and with the options of chartInitOptions:

chartInstance = echarts.init(chartContainer, CHART_INIT_THEME, chartInitOptions(chartContainer));

A theme's textStyle is ECharts' global font: the canvas text and the tooltip's inline font use it unless a component sets its own fontFamily. It is a theme rather than a textStyle in each option because ECharts merges the theme again on every setOption, a notMerge one included, so no option builder has to repeat it. A component that sets its own family uses CHART_FONT_FAMILY, as CorrelationHeatmap does on its axis labels, which it measures with a canvas context in that same font. The code that measures chart text from the chart model (axisLabelFont, see Responsive Date Axis, and GrowthChart's ladder labels) reads its textStyle.fontFamily, which is this family too.

The chart colours stay in lib/theme/chartTheme.ts, and the font is kept out of it on purpose: that module holds colours only, and chartTheme.test.ts requires every string it exports to be a colour.

Loading the face. A canvas paints its text once, with the faces loaded at that moment, and the browser fetches a unicode-range face only for page text that needs it: canvas text does not count. Two steps cover this:

  1. chartFont.ts asks for the face when the first chart module loads, before any chart can paint: chartFontReady() calls document.fonts.load() once, with a flag as sample text (other text would load nothing), and never rejects, so a face that fails to load leaves the system fallback. Without document.fonts, in a test or on the server, it resolves at once.
  2. scheduleFirstRenderStabilityFix (echartsTooltipHelpers.ts), which a chart calls once after its first full setOption, checks chartFontLoaded(): when the face is not in yet, it repaints the chart (resize()) once the request of chartFontReady() settles. Every chart calls it except LotGanttChart.

docs.title: Pixel density
docs.text:
A chart's canvases hold its CSS size times a pixel density. zrender reads the screen's density once, when its module loads, and fixes it for a chart at init: a tab opened on a 1× screen drew every chart at 1×, the ones opened later too, and blurred them once the window moved to a Retina screen or the browser zoomed in. lib/components/charts/chartPixelRatio.ts handles both moments:

  • At creation: chartInitOptions(element) gives echarts.init the canvas renderer and the screen's density at that moment (devicePixelRatio, never under 1, zrender's own rule).
  • When the density changes: one matchMedia resolution query for the whole app, armed by the first chart and re-armed at each change. Every chart created through chartInitOptions and still alive is brought to the new density in place (setChartPixelRatio): its zoom, legend, selection and handlers stay, and nothing is drawn again from its options.

In place means the members of zrender 6's canvas painter that its own resize() uses (painter.dpr, getLayers(), each layer's dpr, ctx.dpr and resize(), then refresh(true)). They are checked before anything is touched: when one is not there, the chart keeps its density, with a warning in debug builds.

docs.title: Tooltip HTML
docs.text:
ECharts sets what a tooltip formatter returns as innerHTML. Every value a formatter takes from the data or from currency metadata (names, captions, currency codes, flags, event types) goes through the shared escapeHtml (lib/utils/core/escapeHtml.ts) where it is interpolated; a flag is such a value, read from getCurrencyInfo(code).flag_emoji. A series label with its icon goes through signalLabelToHtml (lib/charts/signalLabel.ts), which escapes it.

The frontend sources hold one HTML escaper: write no local copy. escapeHtml escapes &, <, >, " and ', so its output is also safe inside an attribute, whichever quote the call site uses; a copy that escapes fewer characters is the defect this rule removes. One file is exempt: lib/utils/inlineMath.ts, whose KaTeX variant keeps the apostrophe on purpose (f'(x) is prime notation). The rule for every hand-built HTML string, and its other gates, is in Output Escaping.

docs.title: Guards
docs.text:
./dev.py test front-portfolio chart-safety-unit runs them:

Test Checks lib/components/charts/chartFlagFont.test.ts With the real ECharts, rendered server-side to SVG: a chart created with CHART_INIT_THEME draws its legend, axis and pie labels with 'LF Flags' first, also after setOption(option, true). A static scan of the production sources: every echarts.init( passes exactly CHART_INIT_THEME as its second argument and chartInitOptions(<its element>) as its third, every chart included since DV-14. PIXEL_RATIO_PENDING is kept, empty, for a chart that cannot migrate at once: a listed file that passes it, has no call or is gone fails the gate. And no module reaches ECharts' init under another name. The scan skips lib/dev/designer-lab/, whose engine creates a 1×1 probe that never paints. lib/components/charts/chartFont.load.test.ts The face is requested before the first paint, and a chart that painted before it arrived paints again once it is in. lib/components/charts/chartPixelRatio.test.ts A chart is created at the density of that moment; a change of density re-arms the query and brings every live chart to it; the update in place runs on the real zrender, so an upgrade that moves its painter's members fails here. What it does not recognise, an SVG chart or a disposed one, it leaves alone, never throwing. *.tooltipEscape.test.ts: AllocationPieChart, CandlestickChart and PriceChartFull beside the charts, CorrelationHeatmap in lib/features/risk/ Fed a value that carries markup, the tooltip injects no element and shows the value as text; the heatmap's also requires the shared escapeHtml's output, quotes included. lib/utils/core/escapeHtml.single.test.ts No production source holds an HTML escaper (& mapped to &) outside escapeHtml.ts and the exempt inlineMath.ts; an exempt file that no longer holds one fails too, so an exemption cannot go stale.

Beside them, SemiDonutChart.test.ts checks that a chart's init receives the canvas renderer and the screen's density, and ./dev.py test front-portfolio chart-pixel-ratio (e2e/portfolio/chart-pixel-ratio.spec.ts) changes the density of a live Dashboard through Chromium's device metrics: its charts follow in place, the same instances and canvases, and a chart opened after the change is born at the new density.

docs.title: Pie Charts (AllocationPieChart)
docs.text:
lib/components/charts/AllocationPieChart.svelte draws the allocation pies of the Dashboard and Broker detail (AllocationPanel, type and sector tabs) and the sector distribution of the asset detail page. It uses segment morph animation:

  • Data-only updates send just the slices' data; ECharts matches slices by name and animates the arcs.
  • mode="type" groups asset types by family (assetTypeFamily, through allocationHierarchy.ts). As soon as one family on screen contains a subtype, the chart draws two rings (buildAllocationRings, allocationRings.ts): the inner ring holds one arc per family, the outer ring splits the families that have subtypes into their members and gives the others a filler drawn invisibly, so the two rings stay aligned. Without subtypes the single ring is drawn as before; mode="sector" always draws one ring.
  • With two rings, a data-only update refreshes both series by id (alloc-base, alloc-outer): updating only the first would leave the outer ring on the previous numbers, with no error.
  • A full option is built on init, on a dark-mode change, on resize (without animation), and when the set of asset types on screen — the ring layout included — differs from the last full build.
  • setOption merges series by index. When the layout switches between one ring and two (rings !== lastRings), the full option is applied with replaceMerge: ['series'], so the old ring series do not stay on screen; every other full build merges with notMerge: false alone.
  • Every arc of both rings takes its family's label as its name, so the legend lists families only and one click hides a family's arcs on both rings. The inner ring shows the family icon only on arcs of at least 18° (minShowLabelAngle); the outer ring captions each member outside with its share, the generic member as dashboard.allocationGeneric ("Generic ETF"), and its tooltip adds a ↳ <family> <share>% line.
  • Shades (shadeForDepth, allocationHierarchy.ts): the generic member keeps the family colour, each subtype is shaded by its rank among the subtypes. With one or two subtypes the lightness walks away from the nearer extreme; from three on, the shades spread on both sides of the base within lightness 10–90, every other one at half saturation.

AllocationPanel persists its view and tab per user (dashboard-allocation-view, dashboard-allocation-tab), shared with Broker detail; a restored History requests its data on mount, as the click does. Its History view, AllocationHistoryChart, groups types by the same families but draws one area per family, without shades; the tooltip lists each family's members, the generic one as dashboard.allocationGeneric.

docs.title: Numeric Values (TweenedValue)
docs.text:
The TweenedValue.svelte component interpolates between numbers:

<TweenedValue value={navHeroAmt} format={(v) => formatCurrencyAmountPlain(v, displayCurrency, {showSign: false})} />
  • Uses Svelte's tweened() store with cubicOut easing
  • Default duration: 900ms (duration prop)
  • loading shows a skeleton pulse instead of the number
  • Used by KpiSection (hero values), KpiMetricBar (when numericValue is set) and RiskMetricCard

A value counts up from 0 when it first appears. A page that already knows its figures — served from the page cache — calls setTweenHydration(isHydrated) during its init: every TweenedValue below it that mounts while isHydrated() is true starts at its value, and still tweens on later changes. The Dashboard and Broker detail pages do this.

docs.title: KPI Bars (CSS transitions)
docs.text:
Both bars live in lib/components/ui/display/ (see Display blocks):

  • KpiMetricBar: bar width and marker position animate via duration-700 transitions; its value tweens over 700 ms
  • KpiDivergingFlowBar: the left and right bars animate independently (transition-all duration-700)
  • Color changes: transition-colors duration-300

docs.title: Stale-While-Revalidate Pattern
docs.text:
Dashboard loading states are designed to never blank the screen on subsequent visits:

// summaryLoading only true when NO data exists yet
let summaryLoading = $derived(reportLoading && !summary);

When the user changes period: 1. Old data stays visible (summaryLoading = false because summary ≠ null) 2. Backend fetch runs in background 3. New data arrives → reactive updates trigger → charts animate to new values

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text:
// echartsAnimationConfig.ts
export const CHART_ANIMATION_CONFIG = {
    animation: true,
    animationDuration: 600,        // New elements enter
    animationDurationUpdate: 800,  // Existing elements update
    animationEasing: 'cubicOut',
    animationEasingUpdate: 'cubicOut',
};

export const CHART_SET_OPTION_OPTS = {
    notMerge: false,               // Enable diffing against previous state
    replaceMerge: ['series'],      // Replace series (matched by name) with animation
};

docs.title: DOM Persistence
docs.text:
Chart containers must never be destroyed between data updates:

<!-- ✗ WRONG: container destroyed when loading changes -->
{#if loading}
    <Skeleton />
{:else}
    <div bind:this={chartContainer}></div>
{/if}

<!-- ✓ CORRECT: container always present, skeleton as overlay -->
<div class="relative">
    {#if loading}
        <div class="absolute inset-0 z-10"><Skeleton /></div>
    {/if}
    <div bind:this={chartContainer} class:invisible={loading}></div>
</div>

If the DOM element is destroyed, the ECharts instance is lost and must be recreated from scratch — eliminating any possibility of transition animation.

docs.title: ⚛️ UI Atoms
docs.text: Small, standalone UI primitives, input helpers and display blocks, in lib/components/ui/ and its input/, date/ and display/ subfolders.

docs.title: 🌓 ThemeToggle
docs.text:
A light/dark toggle in the header (and on the login page).

  • Shows 🌙 in light mode and ☀️ in dark mode; a click switches to the other theme
  • Writes the device preference through applyTheme() (lib/stores/app/themeStore.ts, localStorage key librefolio-theme); while the stored preference is auto, the icon follows the operating system
  • The three-way choice — light, dark, auto — saved in the user settings lives in the Preferences tab; at login the saved theme is applied

Used by: Header.svelte, the login page.

docs.title: 🙈 PrivacyToggle
docs.text:
The header's eye button that hides or shows every monetary amount (ui/PrivacyToggle.svelte).

  • Flips the device-local flag of lib/stores/app/privacyStore.svelte.ts (isPrivacyEnabled(), togglePrivacy()); aria-pressed reflects it, test id privacy-toggle
  • It sits in the header, not in Settings, because the need is contextual: someone walks up to the screen

How the flag reaches the formatters is in Privacy masking.

Used by: Header.svelte.

docs.title: 📖 DocsLink
docs.text:
A help icon that opens a documentation page (ui/DocsLink.svelte).

  • path (required) is relative to the docs root; the link opens /mkdocs/{lang}/{path} in a new tab, in the current UI language (no prefix for English)
  • localizedFallbackPath replaces path in the other languages, for pages that exist only in English
  • icon: help (default) or book; label is the tooltip and the accessible name, math renders LaTeX in it; labelDisplay: hidden (default), responsive or visible
  • Literal path values are checked by ./dev.py mkdocs check-links (scripts/docs_links.py)

Used by: metric cards (RiskMetricCard, KpiSection), the risk levels, the chart signals section, the Tools hub, the asset detail page.

docs.title: 🌊 AnimatedBackground
docs.text:
Animated chart-like background for the login and error pages.

  • Three wave layers and an SVG with three chart lines, animated with CSS
  • Theme-aware colours (adapts to light/dark mode)
  • Fixed behind the page (z-index: -10)

Used by: routes/+page.svelte (login, behind LoginCard/RegisterCard), routes/+error.svelte.

docs.title: 📋 OrderableList
docs.text:
A drag-and-drop reorderable list (ui/OrderableList.svelte).

  • HTML5 drag and drop on desktop, with a grip handle and a green left border on the drop target
  • Up/down arrow buttons below the md breakpoint
  • Items rendered by a caller snippet; keyFn gives each a stable key
  • Optional equal-width responsive grid and per-item warning tone
  • Reports the new order through onReorder(items)

Used by: DataTable column reorder (in ColumnVisibilityToggle), FxProviderSelect, ChartSignalsSection, ImportWizardModal, the PAC planner steps.

docs.title: 🔑 PasswordInput
docs.text:
Located in lib/components/ui/input/

A password field with visibility toggle (eye icon).

  • Toggle between type="password" and type="text"
  • Eye / EyeOff icon from lucide-svelte, on a type="button" that never submits the form and is disabled with the field
  • The eye button is named after what a press does: aria-label and title are $_('auth.showPassword') while the field is masked, $_('auth.hidePassword') while it shows the text. It is in the tab order, and has no aria-pressed on purpose: a toggle whose name changes must not also report a pressed state (WAI-ARIA APG, Button pattern)
  • autocomplete (current-password by default, or new-password, off, on), id and name are passed to the input: password managers rely on them — see the password-manager contract

Used by: LoginCard, RegisterCard, PasswordChangeModal.

docs.title: 💪 PasswordStrength
docs.text:
Located in lib/components/ui/input/

A password strength indicator powered by @zxcvbn-ts/core.

  • Strength bar with a label, from score 0 (very weak) to 4 (very strong), in three colours: danger, warning, success
  • With showRules (default), a checklist of the password rules the server publishes (GET /system/instance), the five of release 1.3 until it answers, or of the rules a caller passes in rules, such as a secure backup's; its bindable valid tells a form whether they all hold
  • Hidden while the password is empty

Details: PasswordStrength.

Used by: RegisterCard (below password field), ResetPasswordCard, PasswordChangeModal, BackupDownloadCard (a secure backup's password, with rules).

docs.title: 🔢 ExactDecimalInput
docs.text:
Located in lib/components/ui/input/

A decimal text field that never goes through a JavaScript number.

  • type="text" with inputmode="decimal": , and . both work as the decimal separator, and characters that can never belong to a number are filtered out while typing
  • A number pasted in scientific notation is read exactly, never stripped of its e (W-B66; filterDecimalInput, and normalizeDecimalInput for every field that reads through it, in lib/utils/core/parseDecimalInput.ts): a text that is wholly such a number, with . or , as its decimal mark, is expanded to a plain decimal when its exponent is within ±100 (MAX_DECIMAL_EXPONENT, the backend's bound): 1e-8 → 0.00000001, 1,5E+3 → 1500. The usual checks then apply to the result. Any other text holding an exponent — past ±100 (3E+150), or not wholly a number (1e5x, 1.234,5e2) — stays as typed, invalid, with a <p> after the field: data-testid="<testid>-exponent-error", data-max 100, and common.decimalExponentOutOfRange (Write the number out in full…). A text without an exponent filters as before: a lone typed e is dropped, EUR 12,34 gives 12,34. Before, the filter dropped the e, so a pasted 1e-8 became 18, silently
  • value (bindable string) is the field text; on blur or Enter a valid value is rewritten in canonical form (. separator, trailing zeros trimmed), then oncommit fires. An invalid value stays as typed: never cut, never coerced on blur
  • Validation is exact: digit budget (maxIntegerDigits, maxFractionDigits, default 12 each), min/max (strings, compared as exact decimals with the value stripped of the zeros the budget does not count, once the digits fit the budget: a longer value is invalid anyway, and comparing the text would build a BigInt of every pasted digit, zeros included), required, allowNegative; onvaliditychange reports {normalized, empty, syntaxValid, requiredValid, digitsValid, rangeValid, valid}, and externalInvalid lets the parent mark it invalid. The digits are counted as the backend counts them (_digit_counts in backend/app/db/precision.py; W-B64): leading integer zeros and trailing fraction zeros are not digits of the value, so 0.10000000000 has one decimal, 5.0 none and 007 one integer digit. decimalDigitCounts(value) (lib/utils/core/parseDecimalInput.ts) gives these counts for a canonical decimal, with the value without those zeros (stripped). So 0.10000000000 is valid at maxFractionDigits={10}, 5.0 at maxFractionDigits={0} (the PAC priority fields; a blur commits it as 5) and 0000000000001.5 at the default 12 integer digits
  • A fraction longer than maxFractionDigits, its trailing zeros not counted, is flagged (digitsValid: false, aria-invalid, red border) and also said under the field: a <p> rendered right after the <input>, as its sibling, with data-testid="<testid>-digits-error" (when testid is set), data-max set to the budget, and a text that follows the budget (common.decimalPlacesExceeded, an ICU plural): Whole numbers only for maxFractionDigits={0}, as in the PAC priority fields, At most 1 decimal place for 1, At most N decimal places above. It is withdrawn as soon as the value is back within the budget. Too many integer digits and the other limits are flagged without a message. The field has no maxlength: the browser silently cut a longer paste down to a number that looked valid
  • ↑/↓ step by step in exact decimal arithmetic, clamped to the bounds (to 0 without allowNegative); accelerateOnHold (default false) climbs by powers of ten while the key is held. A value whose text fits the budget steps from that text, its typed places kept (1.50 → 2.50 at step 1); one whose text is longer, within the budget only because the zeros it starts or ends with are not counted, steps from the value without them, so no BigInt is as long as the text (5. followed by 40 000 zeros, ↑ at step 1 → 6; W-B64). A value past the digit budget, or a text kept for its exponent, is not stepped
  • The checks stay linear on a long paste: the regular expressions of normalizeDecimalInput and formatDecimalForDisplay (lib/utils/core/formatDecimal.ts) and its trailing-zero strip used to backtrack quadratically, about 3 s on a 40 000-character text, in the paster's own tab (W-B66); decimalDigitCounts drops its zeros with two loops, never a /0+$/, for the same reason

Used by: the PAC planner steps (targets, routing, fees, liquidity, prices).

docs.title: 📦 ExactQuantityInput
docs.text:
Located in lib/components/ui/input/

ExactDecimalInput for quantities, with a controlled value.

  • value is always the normalized draft (. separator), while the text the user types stays in a private buffer: a parent echoing the value back never rewrites 1,20 into 1.20 mid-typing; resetKey forces the buffer to reload
  • A new value from the parent is shown in canonical form (formatDecimalForDisplay: . separator, trailing zeros trimmed) when its digits fit the budget, counted as ExactDecimalInput counts them: 0.10000000000 at maxFractionDigits={10} is shown 0.1 (W-B64). A value past the budget is shown as given, and refused: formatting would cut it to fit
  • signRule: positive, negative, nonzero, zero or any (default) — a sign that breaks the rule makes the value invalid and the border red, a matching one turns it green
  • accelerateOnHold defaults to true
  • testid is passed to the inner field, so the message under it is <testid>-digits-error

Used by: the quantity field of TransactionFormModal (tx-form-quantity), with at most 15 integer digits (the backend's limit for a quantity, decision N63) and 10 fraction digits (the 10 decimals the backend keeps for a quantity), so a longer fraction shows tx-form-quantity-digits-error.

docs.title: ⏱️ CompactDurationBadge
docs.text:

A "Custom" duration chip that turns into an inline editor.

  • Every valid draft — within min/max and accepted by isAllowed(amount, unit) — is applied at once (amount, unit are bindable, onapply fires); a click outside or Escape closes the editor

Used by: the custom window of DateRangePicker, the calendar-return window of the asset detail page.

docs.title: ✏️ DataEditor
docs.text:
An inline tabular editor for structured data (add, edit, delete rows).

  • Editable cells with type-aware inputs (text, number, date)
  • Add row button with empty row template
  • A new row's date is chosen with SingleDatePicker, which disables the dates the row may not take: those of the other rows, or, with importMatchKeys, only those of the rows with the same values for those keys, so a new event moves to a day that holds only an event of another type (takenDates; the move itself is checked the same way)
  • Delete row: the row is only marked deleted, and its Undo action restores a deleted or edited row and removes a new one; selected rows can be deleted together. Nothing is written until the owner saves
  • Validation per cell with error highlighting
  • Toolbar counters: N modified, N deleted, N new
  • Rows carry a staleDays count (backward-filled points); when any exist, a switch with a ⚠️ N counter hides them (dataEditor.staleTooltip)
  • readonly rows (with a readonlyReason tooltip) can be deleted but not edited
  • Optional numeric columns flagged erasable render ErasableNumberCell: its eraser (or Delete in an empty input) sets CLEARED_CELL ('clear', exported by DataEditorTypes.ts; N92) without a confirmation, since the row's Undo covers a slip, and the cell shows it as cleared, Not set in red italics. The asset wrapper sends 'clear', which the backend price upsert writes as NULL (the F.4 merge). A number is always a number, -1 included, shown in the field (a typed negative is clamped to the column's min, 0 for prices), and an erased cell sorts and filters as an empty one. Only the eraser sets 'clear': the CSV parser refuses a text. Before N92, the eraser set the sentinel -1
  • Import CSV merges each parsed line into the row with the same date and the same values for the importMatchKeys columns (prop, default []: the date alone, as for prices and FX rates; the asset events editor passes ['type']). Among several matches an editable row wins over a read-only one, and a line whose every match is read-only is skipped; only non-empty values are merged. An unmatched line is appended under a unique rowId, the date then date#2, date#3…, so two new rows can share a date
  • scrollToDate(date) scrolls to a row

Used by: the FX detail page (fx/FxDataEditorSection.svelte) and the asset detail page (assets/AssetDataEditorSection.svelte), below.

docs.title: 💾 Saving: the FX and asset wrappers
docs.text:
DataEditor never writes: its wrapper collects the dirty rows and saves them on Save.

FX (FxDataEditorSection) Asset (AssetDataEditorSection) Tables and columns one table: rate Prices: close (required), open, high, low, volume (erasable). Events: type (one of the five event types) and amount (required), notes Written through POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/rate; a pair shown inverted (its base after its quote in alphabetical order) stores 1 / rate under the alphabetical pair POST /api/v1/assets/prices; for events, one POST /api/v1/assets/events per save, with one item {asset_id, delete_ids, events}: a saved event with its id (edited in place, type included), a new one without Deleted through DELETE /api/v1/fx/currencies/rate DELETE /api/v1/assets/prices; events in that same POST: the ids of the saved rows marked deleted, as delete_ids, which the server deletes first. No DELETE is sent during a save, and an event row never saved is not sent at all Rows not sent A rate that is not a number above 0, counted as skipped (invalid). When every row is invalid and none is deleted, the save stops with Rate must be strictly greater than zero (0 is not allowed). A price whose close is not a number above 0, or whose open, high, low or volume is a negative number (N92; only an imported CSV can bring one), counted as skipped (invalid) (pricesSkipped); an event without a type or a numeric amount

Both wrappers:

  • merge consecutive deleted dates into ranges;
  • draw the pending values as a purple preview line (__preview__, #a855f7) until saved or cancelled; the FX one draws only rates above 0;
  • after a save that appended rows outside the loaded range, hand the page the widened range through onsave, and the page moves its period there;
  • expose scrollToDate(date): with the editor open, a double-click on the chart (a long press of about 0.8 s on touch) scrolls to that date.

What the server refused (X-R46) is worded by frontend/src/lib/api/writeRefusal.ts, in the interface language, with ISO dates, the same way in both wrappers:

  • A save refused whole: the catch shows saveErrorText(error, t). writeRefusalMessage() words the coded refusals: 422 date_out_of_range (the dates and the bounds), 422 price_currency_mismatch (the dates and both currencies; the editor sends no currency, so its own saves never meet it), 422 bulk_too_many_items (common.writeRefusal.tooManyItems: the maximum, the count, Save them in smaller parts) and 400 fx_rates_refused (each date with its reason, through rejectedMessage()). Any other error falls back to extractErrorMessage(), which prefers the server's own detail (its message, for an object) to Axios's Request failed with status code …; an events refusal, already worded by eventSaveErrorMessage(), keeps its sentence. The sentence fills the Failed to save: … banner and the error toast (FX save failed: … on the FX page), and onsave is not called: the editor stays open with the pending rows.
  • A save taken in part: a 200 names the dates it left out in rejected (FX) or in its asset's results[].rejected (asset), and the counts come from the answer: results.length saved and rejected.length refused for FX (fxDetail.refusedCount), the asset's count saved and its rejected as pricesRefused for the asset (assets.dataEditor.pricesRefused, and in the assets.data.saved event). rejectedMessage() names up to five refused dates, then and N more, each with its reason (common.writeRefusal.reason.*), and the summary toast is a warning that stays 20 s (REFUSAL_TOAST_MS) instead of a success. The asset wrapper adds its result's message when the result accounts for fewer prices than were sent (the asset deleted meanwhile).

Asset only:

  • Two tabs, Prices and Events, whose badges count the dirty rows, share one Save (n) / Cancel bar. The chart jump picks the Events tab when the date has an event marker, the Prices tab otherwise.
  • No currency column. The backend rejects a price in a currency other than the asset's (HTTP 422 price_currency_mismatch, the whole request) and such an event (HTTP 400); the editor sends no currency with prices, and a label beside the tabs reads Prices in USD / Events in USD. An event goes with its row's currency when it has one, the value an imported CSV line brought, and with the asset's otherwise: a line in another currency is refused with its row (EVENT_CURRENCY_MISMATCH), not relabelled with an amount that would be wrong.
  • Auto events (is_auto) are readonly: a provider rewrites them at its next sync (see Asset Events).
  • Saved events travel with their id. A saved event row's rowId is its DB id, read back by dbEventId(row) (null for a row never saved, whose rowId is a date: 2026-03-15, 2026-03-15#2). The upsert sends that id, so the server edits the row in place, its type included: changing the Type of a saved event no longer adds an event and leaves the old one. A row deleted before its first save is not sent. Since the server deletes first, one save can delete an event and retype another onto its date and type. The events DataEditor gets importMatchKeys={['type']}: an imported line merges into the row of the same date and type, under the Import CSV rules above, and a line of another type on that date is added.
  • A refused save keeps no event change, its deletions included: the events request is one transaction (decision 22). eventSaveErrorMessage() (transactions/events/eventSaveError.ts, keys events.saveError.*) turns the refusal into one sentence in the user's language, which names the row at fault when the refusal points at one: its date and type, with the currency for EVENT_CURRENCY_MISMATCH, the number of linked transactions for EVENT_IN_USE, the three maxima of params (decimal places, significant digits, digits before the decimal point) for EVENT_TOO_MANY_DIGITS (events.saveError.tooManyDigits: the first event at fault, and how many more), the split's ratio for EVENT_INVALID_SPLIT_RATIO (events.saveError.invalidSplitRatio: the first split at fault, and how many more), and the value typed for a 422 on a type (EVENT_NOT_EDITABLE, EVENT_NOT_DELETABLE and EVENT_ASSET_NOT_FOUND ask for a reload instead). It shows as a Failed to save: … toast and a banner above the tabs, and onsave is not called: the editor stays open with the pending rows. Prices are sent before events, so the prices of that save may already be stored.
  • Refresh while editing: a chartData or events refresh that lands while a tab has dirty rows is held back until it is clean, so pending edits are never discarded. The FX wrapper rebuilds its rows on every refresh.

The asset import modals wrap DataImportModal, each with a format banner and a 📖 button that opens the user page (user/assets/detail/data-editor/ and user/assets/detail/events/, with the locale prefix):

  • PriceDataImportModal — header date;currency;close, optional open;high;low;volume. currency is a required column for the parser but is not sent: the save uses the asset's.
  • EventDataImportModal — header date;currency;type;amount;notes, with currency and notes optional. amount also reads a value column (an alias), the name the events export (GET /api/v1/backup/asset/{id}/events?format=csv) gives it, so an exported events file imports back with its other columns ignored. Its notes column has a parse, unescapeFormulaText (exported from the modal's <script module>), which drops the one leading apostrophe the export puts in front of a note that starts, after any apostrophes, with =, +, -, @, a tab or a carriage return, so that such a note imports back exactly as it was (lot B-39, Output Escaping). Its source column is not read (every row becomes a manual event). Its type column is a matchKey: two rows are duplicates only when they share the date and the type, so a dividend and a split of one day import together.

docs.title: 📄 CsvEditor
docs.text:
A CSV preview and editor with column detection and per-row validation.

  • Parses CSV content and displays as table
  • Detects the separator, ; or ,, from the first non-empty line (a line starting with date; or date, decides at once, otherwise the first of the two to appear), and reads quoted fields RFC 4180-style. No other separator is recognised
  • Requires a header on the first non-empty line and matches it by column name, case-insensitively and in any order: extra columns are ignored, missing required ones produce one consolidated error. A column may list aliases (CsvColumnDef.aliases), tried after its label: with both present, the label wins. A token A<B reads as B>A, so an FX header can name its direction either way
  • The identity column is date (YYYY-MM-DD) unless the caller passes another, such as a distribution's name
  • Numbers (parseNumber): _ is dropped as a thousands separator; with both . and ,, the last one is the decimal separator and the other is dropped; a lone , is the decimal separator (a second one makes the value invalid). What remains must be a plain number (sign, digits, optional decimals and exponent), so an inner space or a letter is invalid. A column may also pass its own parse and validate
  • Highlights rows with errors (red) or warnings (yellow), such as a duplicate: two lines with the same identity value and the same values in every column flagged matchKey (CsvColumnDef.matchKey; only the events import flags one, type)
  • Editable cells for manual correction

Its messages, one per invalid line:

Where Message Header Missing required columns: <labels>, or Expected header: <identity>;<labels…> when the first line has no identity column; every data row then reads Fix header first Row Invalid quoted CSV field Row Invalid date format: "<value>". Use YYYY-MM-DD, Invalid date: "<value>", or Invalid <identity>: "<value>" for another identity column Row Required column "<label>" is empty Row Invalid number in "<label>": "<value>", or Invalid value in "<label>": "<value>" when a column's parse rejects it Row The column's own validate message, such as Weight must be between 0 and 100 Duplicates Duplicate <identity>: <value> on every row sharing that value, or Duplicate date · type: <date> · <type> with a matchKey column; none of them is imported

Used by: DataImportModal (FX CSV import preview and the asset price, event and distribution imports).

docs.title: 📥 DataImportModal
docs.text:
A modal for importing data from CSV files. Extends ModalBase.

  • Drag & drop file upload zone
  • Direction bar for FX pair direction (with swap button)
  • Uses CsvEditor for preview
  • Validation summary before import: N valid row(s), the error count, and duplicates
  • Import (N) imports the valid rows only, by default: rows with errors and every duplicated row stay out. A strict caller (the distribution import) allows the import only with no error and no duplicate, and a validateRows check on the whole set (the distribution total) blocks it with its message
  • Closing after typing, pasting or dropping data asks to confirm (Discard import?)

Used by: FX detail page — "Import CSV" action, and the asset wrappers PriceDataImportModal, EventDataImportModal and DistributionDataImportModal. See FX CSV Import and Asset Data Editor for user documentation.

docs.title: 📊 DataTable Component
docs.text: The DataTable is a powerful, generic table component built with Svelte 5 Runes. It provides a rich set of features similar to Excel or advanced data grids.

docs.title: ⚡ Features
docs.text:
• Sorting: Click column headers to sort ASC/DESC.
  • Filtering: Excel-style column filters (Text, Number, Date, Enum, Multi-enum, Size, Currency).
  • Pagination: Client-side pagination in a floating balloon, with configurable page sizes — see Pagination.
  • Selection: Row selection with checkboxes, "Select All" on the current page, and a "show selected only" filter in the checkbox header.
  • Column Management: Resize columns by dragging a header cell's right edge, with a mouse, a finger or a pen — see Column resize; show/hide and drag-to-reorder through ColumnVisibilityToggle, which the caller places in its own toolbar and hands the table instance (tableRef, plus additionalTableRefs to drive several tables at once); it works through the public methods.
  • Persistence: Page size, column order, widths and visibility overrides are saved to localStorage under per-user keys (lf_{userId}_dataTable_{storageKey}_{suffix}). Sorting and filters are not persisted; filters can round-trip through the URL (initialFilters, onFiltersChange). A column absent from columns for a while — the Assets and FX tables' Δ period columns until the backend lists the periods, or those longer than a short date range — keeps its saved place, visibility and width: the table adds only the columns it has never seen, at their natural place (right after the last column that precedes them in columns), and a reorder in ColumnVisibilityToggle, which lists only the columns present, puts an absent column back right after the one it followed. resetColumnLayout() returns to the defaults of the columns present and forgets the absent ones.
  • Actions: Per-row actions behind a ⋮ button in the actions column, and bulk actions on the selected rows. Actions with requireConfirm go through a ConfirmModal.
  • Context Menu: Right-click on a row opens the same menu as ⋮, built from rowActions.
  • Sticky Columns: The header row sticks inside the table's scroll area; the selection column, pinned columns and, by default, the actions column stick to their edge while the table scrolls sideways — on phones the selection and actions columns scroll with it. See Sticky columns.

docs.title: 💻 Usage
docs.text:
<script lang="ts">
  import { DataTable } from '$lib/components/table';
  import type { ColumnDef, RowAction } from '$lib/components/table/types';
  import { Pencil, Trash2 } from 'lucide-svelte';

  // Define your data type
  type User = { id: string; name: string; role: string; };

  // Define columns
  const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
    {
      id: 'name',
      header: 'Name',
      // Simple text cell
      cell: (row) => row.name,
      sortable: true,
      filterable: true,
      type: 'text'
    },
    {
      id: 'role',
      header: 'Role',
      // Badge cell
      cell: (row) => ({
        type: 'badge',
        text: row.role,
        variant: row.role === 'admin' ? 'success' : 'default'
      }),
      type: 'enum',
      enumOptions: [
        { value: 'admin', label: 'Admin' },
        { value: 'user', label: 'User' }
      ]
    }
  ];

  // Define row actions
  const rowActions: RowAction<User>[] = [
    {
      id: 'edit',
      icon: Pencil,
      label: 'Edit',
      onClick: (row) => console.log('Edit', row)
    },
    {
      id: 'delete',
      icon: Trash2,
      label: 'Delete',
      variant: 'danger',
      requireConfirm: true,
      onClick: (row) => console.log('Delete', row)
    }
  ];
</script>

<DataTable
  data={users}
  columns={columns}
  rowActions={rowActions}
  getRowId={(row) => row.id}
  storageKey="users-table"
/>

docs.title: 📋 Props
docs.text:
The source of truth is the Props interface of lib/components/table/DataTable.svelte.

Data and identity

Prop Type Default Description data T[] Required Rows to show. columns ColumnDef<T>[] Required Column definitions. getRowId (row: T) => string Required Unique id of a row. storageKey string Required Key of the persisted preferences. fullData T[] — Full dataset for the filter boundaries (min/max, currencies) when data is a pre-paginated slice. isLoading boolean false Shows a loading row (dt-loading). emptyMessage string common.noData Text of the empty table. tableLayout 'fixed' \| 'auto' 'fixed' fixed sizes the columns from their header cells' widths; auto from their content as well, so a width becomes a preference — see Column resize.

Selection

Prop Type Default Description enableSelection boolean true false is the same as selectionMode="none". selectionMode 'multi' \| 'single' \| 'none' 'multi' Checkboxes, single-row click selection, or none. selectionColumnWidth string '48px' Width of the checkbox column. initialSelectedIds string[] — Rows selected at mount (e.g. returning to a wizard step). selectedRowId string \| null null Controlled selection in single mode. onSelectionChange (ids: string[]) => void — Called when the selection changes. isRowSelectable (row: T) => boolean — false hides the checkbox (⊘ instead) and excludes the row from bulk selection. disabledRowTooltip (row: T) => string \| null — Tooltip of the ⊘ icon. enableTouchSelection boolean false A 500 ms long-press toggles the row's selection. Without it, a long-press runs onRowDoubleClick. onShowSelectedOnlyChange (active: boolean) => void — The "show selected only" toggle changed.

Rows and actions

Prop Type Default Description onRowClick (row: T) => void — Row click. onRowDoubleClick (row: T) => void — Row double-click. getRowHref (row: T) => string \| undefined — Middle-click opens the URL in a new tab. getRowClass, getRowStyle (row: T) => string — Extra classes / inline style per row. getRowDisplayName (row: T) => string — Name of a row in the confirmation lists (falls back to the id). enableActions boolean true Shows the actions column when rowActions is given. rowActions RowAction<T>[] \| (row: T) => RowAction<T>[] [] Actions of each row (⋮ menu and context menu). bulkActions BulkAction<T>[] [] Actions on the selected rows. actionsColumnWidth string '64px' Width of the actions column. actionsLabel string table.actions Header and ⋮ label of the actions column. stickyActions boolean true Whether the actions column sticks to the right edge, above 768 px — see Sticky columns. enableContextMenu boolean true Right-click menu on rows.

Columns, sorting, filters

Prop Type Default Description enableSorting boolean true Column sorting. onSortChange (state: SortState \| null) => void — Sort changed or cleared. onRowOrderChange (rowIds: string[]) => void — Row ids in display order (after filters and sort, across all pages); called after mount and whenever that order changes. enableColumnFilters boolean true Column filters. initialFilters Record<string, FilterValue> — Filters applied at mount (from the URL). onFiltersChange (filters) => void — Filters changed (for URL sync). enableColumnResize boolean true Resize handles on the data columns (a column opts out with resizable: false) — see Column resize. onColumnResize (columnId: string, width: number) => void — Called at the end of a resize with the width written for the column, to mirror it on other tables through setColumnWidth. stickyHeader boolean true Whether the header row sticks to the top of the table's own scroll area — not the page; see Sticky columns. footerCells FooterCells<T> — Aggregate footer, computed on the selected rows, or on the filtered rows when nothing is selected.

Pagination

Prop Type Default Description enablePagination boolean true Client-side pagination. defaultPageSize number 10 Page size until the user picks one (the stored choice wins). pageSizeOptions number[] [10, 25, 50, 100, 0] Choices of the page-size menu; 0 means "all" (shown as ∞). alwaysShowPagination boolean false Show the bar whenever there is at least one row.

enableColumnVisibility is accepted but not read: column visibility is driven from outside, through ColumnVisibilityToggle and the public methods.

docs.title: 📌 Sticky columns
docs.text:
• The header row sticks to the top of the table's own scroll area, div.table-wrapper (data-testid="dt-scroll"), never to the page (stickyHeader, default on). The wrapper's overflow-x: auto makes its overflow-y compute to auto too, so the wrapper is the scroll container its sticky cells stick within: the header sticks only when the wrapper itself scrolls vertically, which needs a bounded height on it. When the page scrolls, the header leaves with the table.
  • The selection column (th-select/td-select, left: 0) and the columns with pinned: 'left' | 'right' stick to their edge while the table scrolls horizontally.
  • The actions column (th-actions/td-actions, right: 0) sticks to the right edge by default. With stickyActions={false} it scrolls with the table, and its header stays at the end of the table, aligned with its cells. The transactions table, the bulk editor and the import wizard tables turn it off.
  • At 768 px and below (the @media (max-width: 768px) block of DataTable.svelte), the selection and actions columns scroll with the table — header, body and footer cells alike (decision D-Y17). The body and footer cells become position: static; the header cells drop only their horizontal pin (left: auto; right: auto) and keep position: sticky — and, with stickyHeader, top: 0 — so the header row still sticks inside its scroll area. Data columns with pinned keep their pin at every width.
  • A row's tint keeps the fixed cells opaque. A body row paints the card and, over it, the tint of its state, --dt-row-tint (hover, selected, highlighted, analyzed), as one image layer (linear-gradient(tint, tint) over --lf-surface-card). --dt-row-tint is registered with @property (<color>), so a change of state fades. The row is therefore opaque, and the fixed cells, which inherit its background, hide what scrolls under them. A list that tints its rows through getRowClass sets --dt-row-tint on the row, never the row's background — a translucent background would let the scrolling cells show through the fixed ones. Example: AssetTable, whose asset-row-inactive class sets --dt-row-tint: var(--lf-warning-soft) for the inactive asset.
  • A deleted row (tr.row-deleted, set through getRowClass by the data editor and the transactions bulk editor) is not faded with opacity: its cells are opaque (the danger tint at 55 % over the card) and a veil (td::after, the same background at 45 %, pointer-events: none) fades the content, so fixed cells never show what scrolls beneath (TC-21).

The header and body cells of the two columns carry test ids: dt-select-header and dt-select-cell-{rowId}, dt-actions-header and dt-actions-cell-{rowId} (the footer cells have none). frontend/e2e/layout/datatable-mobile.spec.ts, run by ./dev.py test front-utility datatable-mobile, checks the phone layout at 390 px on the transactions table (stickyActions={false}) and on the Files static list (sticky actions), and guards the header row's stickiness inside a scroll area it bounds to the header and two rows.

Undoing a pin takes a more specific selector

thead.sticky-header th (0,1,2), the rule that makes the header cells sticky, outranks a bare .th-actions (0,1,0): a plain .th-actions { position: static } leaves the Actions header pinned at the right edge while its ⋮ cells scroll away. Each phone override is one class more specific than the pin it undoes — .datatable .th-select against .th-select, .datatable .th-actions.th-fixed against .th-actions.th-fixed, .datatable .td-select and .datatable .td-actions against .td-fixed — and the header cells change only left and right, never position. These are the specificities of the source selectors: Svelte's scoping class adds the same to every rule.

docs.title: 📏 Column resize
docs.text:
A data column's header cell ends in a resize handle: span.resize-handle in DataTableColumnHeader.svelte, the cell's last 6 px, with cursor: col-resize, transparent until the cell is hovered. It is there when enableColumnResize is on and the column is not resizable: false; the selection and actions columns have none. The drag runs in DataTable.svelte (decision D-Y18):

  • Any pointer. The handle answers Pointer Events: startResize, its onpointerdown, captures the pointer, and pointermove, pointerup and pointercancel listeners on document follow it, so a mouse, a finger or a pen resizes the column. Only the primary mouse button starts a drag, and the moves and releases of other pointers are ignored. touch-action: none on the handle keeps a finger drag from panning the table. The listeners are removed when the drag ends, or when the table unmounts mid-drag.
  • The drawn width follows the pointer. The drag starts from the width the column is drawn at (the header cell's getBoundingClientRect().width), not the configured one, and aims at that width plus the pointer's travel, clamped to the column's minWidth (default 50) and maxWidth (default 600). A table that shares its spare width among its columns — tableLayout="auto", or a fixed table narrower than its box — draws a column wider than the width it is given, so fitDrawnWidth() writes a width (and the same min-width) on the header cell, measures the cell and corrects the width — first assuming the drawn width is proportional to the given one, then by a few secant steps — until the drawn width matches the target. On a fixed table wider than its box the first guess is exact.
  • A resized column keeps its width. A column whose width differs from its default (width ?? 150) — resized, restored from localStorage or set through setColumnWidth — also gets that width as its header cell's min-width (columnMinWidth()), so an auto-layout table keeps it, for example on a narrow screen where auto would otherwise draw every column at its minimum. The other columns keep minWidth || 60; resetColumnLayout() restores the default widths, and with them those minimums.
  • End of the drag. On pointerup or pointercancel the widths are saved to localStorage, and onColumnResize(columnId, width) receives the width written: on a table with spare width it is smaller than the drawn one. It is the value setColumnWidth takes on the tables that mirror the resize.

E2E specs find the handle by what it is to the pointer — the element under the header cell's right edge whose computed cursor is col-resize — never by its class (datatable-resize.spec.ts, risk-lab.spec.ts, risk-analysis.spec.ts): keep that cursor on the handle. frontend/e2e/layout/datatable-resize.spec.ts, run by ./dev.py test front-utility datatable-resize, drags it with a mouse on the Files static list (tableLayout="auto") at 1280 px and at 390 px, where the table is wider than its box and the table's scroll width must grow with the column (a resized column keeps its width); on the transactions table (fixed, the control); and with a finger at 390 px on the transactions table, to test the input path alone: every drag must change the drawn width by its own length, within 4 px.

docs.title: 📄 Pagination
docs.text:
The pagination bar (DataTablePagination.svelte) floats in a balloon that sticks to the bottom of the scroll area. It appears when pagination is on and the filtered rows outnumber the smallest non-zero entry of pageSizeOptions — or, with alwaysShowPagination, as soon as there is one row. Changing the page size returns to the first page and is saved under the table's storageKey.

The page-size menu is positioned with fixed coordinates computed from its trigger (getFixedDropdownPosition, lib/utils/layout/dropdownPosition.ts): it opens below the trigger, or above it when there is no room, stays inside the viewport, scrolls internally when taller than the screen, and follows the trigger on resize and on any scroll. So in a short table inside a scrollable modal the menu is not clipped by the modal's overflow and every option stays reachable.

Short tables can offer smaller steps: the bulk editor and the import wizard pass pageSizeOptions={[5, 10, 25, 50, 0]}-style lists.

docs.title: 🧭 Public methods
docs.text:
Bind the component (bind:this={tableRef}) to call them.

Method Description navigateToRowId(rowId) Moves to the page that holds the row (with the current filters and sort), highlights it with a short pulse and scrolls it into view (smooth, centred). Unknown ids are ignored. The highlight clears on the next row click or key press in the table. getSortedRowIds() Ids of all matching rows in display order, before pagination — check it first to tell a hidden row from a missing one. getPageRowIds() Ids of the rows on the current page. clearSelection(), toggleRowSelectionById(id) Selection control. clearFilters() Removes every column filter (and reports it through onFiltersChange). getColumnsForVisibility(), toggleColumnVisibilityById(id), setColumnOrder(ids), resetColumnLayout(), setColumnWidth(id, width) Column layout, for ColumnVisibilityToggle and for syncing widths across tables.

navigateToRowId is how a banner or a list sends the user to a row: the bulk transaction editor jumps to the row of a validation issue or of a todo (getSortedRowIds() first, and a warning toast when the row is filtered out); the lots panel, DataEditor ("Add row", chart point click) and TransactionsTable use it as well. The highlighted row carries data-highlighted="true".

docs.title: 🔧 Column Definition (ColumnDef<T>)
docs.text:
The main fields; lib/components/table/types.ts has the full interface.

Field Type Description id string Unique identifier for the column. header string \| () => string Header text (a function for i18n). headerHtml replaces it with markup; displayName names the column in the visibility menu. cell (row: T) => CellContent Cell content, see below. type 'text' \| 'number' \| 'date' \| 'enum' \| 'multi-enum' \| 'size' \| 'currency-stack' \| 'custom' Drives the filter UI and the sort. getValue (row: T) => unknown Raw value for sorting and filtering, when it differs from the rendered cell. sortable, filterable, resizable boolean Default true. width, minWidth, maxWidth number Pixels. width defaults to 150. A resize stays within minWidth (default 50) and maxWidth (default 600); the header cell's min-width is minWidth (default 60) until the column's width differs from its default — see Column resize. enumOptions EnumOption[] {value, label, iconUrl?, dotColor?, searchText?} for enum columns. getMultiValue (row: T) => string[] Values of a multi-enum row (e.g. tags). getCurrencyValue, currencyOptions — currency-stack columns: {code, amount} of a row, and the currencies on offer. hiddenByDefault boolean Hidden until the user shows it. pinned 'left' \| 'right' Sticks to that edge while the table scrolls sideways, at every width — see Sticky columns. align 'left' \| 'center' \| 'right' Cell and header alignment. headerTooltip, headerTooltipUrl string \| () => string headerTooltip alone puts a tooltip on the header label. With headerTooltipUrl as well, an info icon appears that opens the documentation page in a new tab. headerTooltipLinkMode 'direct' \| 'gesture' How the info icon opens the page: a plain link ('direct', the default), or a button that opens it on double click, Shift+Enter or long press ('gesture'). urlKey string URL parameter of the column's filter (default: the id). integerOnly boolean Integer-only number filter.

docs.title: 📅 Date filter
docs.text:
The filter of a date column (DataTableColumnFilter.svelte) is a DateRangePicker without presets (compact, stacked), and it applies a DateFilter, {type: 'date', from?, to?} (types.ts). Either end may stay blank: matchesColumnFilter (dataTableLogic.ts) drops a row only before from or after to, as does TransactionsTable's own pre-filter, so a date in «From» alone keeps the rows from that day on, and one in «To» alone the rows up to that day. In the URL the filter reads from,to, either side empty (lib/utils/urlFilters.ts); the Transactions page keeps its own date_start and date_end (lib/features/transactions/filterState.ts).

The picker cannot make a filter of one day (No range of a single day). Until Y-N65, a date typed in «From» alone filled «To» with the same date, so the filter kept that day only. A one-day filter that arrives through the URL still applies as it is.

docs.title: 🎨 Cell Content Types
docs.text:
The cell function can return a simple string/number or a structured object:

  • Text: string or number
  • Icon + Text: { type: 'icon-text', icon: Component, text: string, iconClass?: string }
  • Image: { type: 'image', src: string, alt: string, text?: string, fallbackIcon?: Component, size?: number, circle?: boolean } (thumbnail with fallback icon, default 32 px)
  • Badge: { type: 'badge', text: string, variant: 'success'|'warning'|'error'|'info'|'default', customStyle?: string }
  • Date: { type: 'date', value: Date | string, format?: 'date'|'datetime'|'time'|'relative' }
  • Size: { type: 'size', bytes: number } (Auto-formats to KB/MB/GB, i18n-aware)
  • Link: { type: 'link', text: string, href: string, external?: boolean }
  • HTML: { type: 'html', html: string, tooltip?: {...}, onClick?: () => void, testId?: string }
  • Editable: editable-number, editable-text, editable-select, editable-checkbox — inline inputs that report through their onchange
  • Custom: { type: 'custom', component: Component, props: object }

html is rendered as-is

html cells, headerHtml and html footer cells go through {@html} without sanitising, in DataTableCellContent.svelte (cells and footer cells) and DataTableColumnHeader.svelte (headerHtml), both listed as reviewed sinks in frontend/src/htmlSink.gate.test.ts. Escape every user- or provider-supplied value with escapeHtml ($lib/utils/core/escapeHtml.ts) when you build the string. The gate frontend/src/htmlInterpolation.gate.test.ts flags HTML templates that interpolate such a value unescaped.

docs.title: 📦 State Management (Internal)
docs.text:
The component uses Svelte 5 Runes for internal state:

  • $state for sorting, pagination, filters, selection and the column layout.
  • $derived for calculating filtered/sorted/paginated data efficiently.
  • Preferences are read from localStorage on mount and written back when they change.
  • The pure decision logic — cell value extraction, filter predicates, typed comparison, min/max, enum options and the column-order rules (withNewColumns for the effect that syncs the order with columns, reorderKeepingAbsent for setColumnOrder) — lives in dataTableLogic.ts, unit-tested in dataTableLogic.test.ts; DataTable.test.ts covers the wiring and the public methods.

Where DataTable's code lives. Consumers use DataTable.svelte only. It renders two children that are internal — table/index.ts does not export them — and that hold markup and styles, but no table state:

File Holds DataTable.svelte The public API (the Props interface and the public methods), all the table's state ($state, $derived), its effects and its handlers. The structure of the table: table, thead, tbody, tfoot; the rows with their handlers (click, double click, middle click, context menu, long press); every th and td with its classes, sticky offsets and test ids; the selection and actions columns, the loading and empty rows, the pagination, the context menu and the two confirm modals. And the styles of all that, structural rules included: sticky columns, z-index, row states. DataTableColumnHeader.svelte The content of one data-column header (div.header-content inside th.th-data): the sort button with the header text or the headerHtml, wrapped in the headerTooltip when there is one; with a headerTooltipUrl as well, the info icon — a link, or with headerTooltipLinkMode: 'gesture' a button that opens the URL on double click, Shift+Enter or long press; the filter button and its DataTableColumnFilter popover; the resize handle. The parent's state and handlers arrive as props under their parent names, and openFilterColumnId is bound, since the parent owns it; the header's only $state is filterBtn, the popover's anchor. The tooltip's long-press timer stays in the parent, whose onDestroy cancels it. DataTableCellContent.svelte The switch over the kinds of CellContent listed above, with their styles and the input handling of the editable kinds. Footer cells render through it too — FooterCellContent (text, number or html) is a subset of CellContent — so a clickable html footer cell with a testId now carries its data-testid, exactly like a body cell. dataTableLogic.ts The pure logic of the last bullet above. Each component imports what it uses: the parent the filter predicate, the comparison and the column-order rules, the header the filter's boundaries and options, the cell formatCellDate.

Like the parent, each child imports $lib/theme/components/table.css, the area file of the --lf-cmp-datatable-* tokens it reads: the token gate (frontend/src/themeComponentTokens.gate.test.ts) requires that import in every component that reads a token. Svelte scopes styles per component, so the selectors that cross the boundary use :global — the parent's :has(:global(.cell-editable-select-wrapper)), on the td and the tbody tr that hold an editable select, and the header's :global(th:hover) .resize-handle — and Svelte checks neither against the other side's markup: a rename there breaks them silently. The .filter-btn rules are in both files, the same in each: the parent's for the "show selected only" toggle of the selection header, the header's for the column filter.
