docs.title: 🧪 Risk UI: Correlation and Dashboard Risk Tabs
docs.text:
This page covers the UI rules of two risk surfaces. The Correlation tab of the Assets page — the Asset Global lab — runs the risk engine on a hand-picked selection of assets ({kind: "asset_set", asset_ids: [...]}): how the selection is built and kept, how the engine's eligibility verdicts are used, which requests each section sends, and how each section draws and discloses its results. The Risk tab of the Dashboard and of Broker Detail runs it on a portfolio ({kind: "portfolio", broker_ids: [...]}) as four levels: see Dashboard Risk Tab.

It does not repeat the engine. The request flow, the analytics, the eligibility rules and thresholds, the panel controller and the shared benchmark store are in Risk Engine; the mathematics is in Risk Metrics; what users see is in the Correlation Tab and Risk Tab user pages.

Paths are relative to frontend/src/lib/features/risk/ unless stated otherwise. The lab never shows an amount of money: a selection has no weights.

docs.title: 🗺️ Source Map
docs.text:
Source Responsibility frontend/src/routes/(app)/assets/+page.svelte Mounts the lab on the Correlation tab with the page's full asset list; hides the list filters there (l.1405); its toolbar's Sync selection and Reload All call the lab's openSync() and reload() (l.1604, l.1619); onfitperiod moves the toolbar range (l.1704-1709); targetCurrency is the instance default currency (l.1713). AssetSetRiskPanel.svelte The lab: selection card, eligibility, holdings command, benchmark picker snippet, banner and notice, and the four sections (l.847-864). assetSetSelection.ts Opening selection, persistence, bulk actions, labBenchmarkId(), labL3Waits(). eligibility.ts Reads and words the engine's verdicts; batches; fitPeriodOffer(). LabAssetPicker.svelte The +: AssetPickerPanel in multi mode. AssetSetCorrelationSection.svelte, CorrelationHeatmap.svelte, CorrelationPairsList.svelte, correlationHelpers.ts, matrixMetadata.svelte.ts Correlation section. AssetSetComparisonLevels.svelte, AssetSetLossComparisonSection.svelte, AssetSetRiskReturnSection.svelte, RiskReturnLevel.svelte, assetSetLevels.ts, assetSetTable.ts L1° (losses) and L3° (risk and return). AssetSetReplaySection.svelte, levels/l4/L4Replay.svelte, levels/l4/TornadoChart.svelte L4° (historical replay). levels/RiskLevelSection.svelte, levels/RiskPartialNotice.svelte, levels/partialNotice.ts, levels/levelMetadata.ts, syncTargets.ts Section frames, the shared notice, banner actions.

The UI strings live under risk.assetSet.* (lab-only) and risk.levels.* (shared with the Dashboard).

docs.title: 🚪 Opening Selection
docs.text:
resolveInitialSelectionWithSource() (assetSetSelection.ts:137) picks the first rung that yields ids, and the card publishes it as data-selection-source (AssetSetRiskPanel.svelte:707):

  1. persisted — the last selection, stored in localStorage under lf_<userId>_assetGlobal.riskSelection.v1 (assetSetSelection.ts:39, l.64) and intersected with the page's list, so deleted or merged ids drop out.
  2. mine — the assets held on dateEnd in every accessible broker. heldAssetIds() reads a light fetchReport() without the daily and allocation histories (AssetSetRiskPanel.svelte:509), asks once more when it answers null (l.510-516), and keeps only ids of the page's list.
  3. fallback — the FALLBACK_SELECTION_SIZE (6) active assets with the most transactions, ties by id (assetSetSelection.ts:37, l.165).

Every rung is capped at MAX_SELECTED_ASSETS (100, assetSetSelection.ts:31), which is the API's limit for the scope. A change the user makes while rung 2 is loading wins: the late seed is dropped (selectionTouched, AssetSetRiskPanel.svelte:466). Every later change is written back (l.479).

docs.title: 🧰 Bulk Actions and Holdings
docs.text:
• applyBulkAction() (assetSetSelection.ts:198) acts on candidates: the page's list minus the ineligible assets (AssetSetRiskPanel.svelte:347). Neither the + filters nor the Assets-tab filters narrow it. all adds every candidate, inactive ones included, up to 100; none empties the selection, parked assets included; invert swaps the candidates and leaves parked assets where they are.
  • My assets runs runHoldingsPreset(brokerId | null) (AssetSetRiskPanel.svelte:537): it replaces the selection with the assets held on dateEnd (all accessible brokers, or one), sliced to 100 (l.554), ineligible ones included. It is a command, not a filter: a date change does not run it again. A failed report sets risk.states.loadFailed (l.547); nothing held leaves the selection as it was and shows risk.assetSet.preset.noneHeld (l.551).
  • The + is LabAssetPicker.svelte, a thin wrapper around AssetPickerPanel in multi mode: rows in name order, a search over the name, the currency and the type label (searchText, LabAssetPicker.svelte:60), and room = 100 − selection size (AssetSetRiskPanel.svelte:368). The panel's own behaviour (Select visible, filters, blocked section) is documented there.

docs.title: ✅ Eligibility in the Lab
docs.text:
The rules behind POST /api/v1/risk/eligibility — the reasons, the 20-quote floor, the seven-day lateness, common_range and suggested_range — are in Analysis Eligibility. The lab uses the verdicts in three ways:

  • The whole list is asked, in batches of ELIGIBILITY_BATCH (500, eligibility.ts:47), after a 300 ms debounce (AssetSetRiskPanel.svelte:246), and again when the list, the period or the currency changes; a superseded answer is dropped. A failed call leaves no verdict (l.294-295): every asset stays selectable and the card shows risk.assetSet.eligibilityFailed.
  • An ineligible asset is parked: it stays in selectedAssetIds as a dashed chip, with the reasons in its tooltip, but only analysedIds (l.357) reaches the sections. The counter shows analysedIds.length of candidates.length (l.791). A warning chip is analysed.
  • The selection is asked again on its own (selectionVerdicts, l.316-340), so that unselected assets cannot narrow the period offered. fitPeriodOffer() (eligibility.ts:109) returns the answer's suggested_range when at least one selected asset is not eligible and is not no_price_history. The ranges survive only a single-batch answer, which a selection of at most 100 ids always is. The strip's button calls onfitperiod; the page clears its preset badge and applies the range to the toolbar (+page.svelte:1609-1614).

docs.title: 🔌 Requests and the Shared Window
docs.text:
Each section owns a controller (createRiskPanelController), and all four are mounted under the panel's {#if analysedIds.length > 0} (AssetSetRiskPanel.svelte:847), so an empty selection never reaches the API. Which analytics each section asks for is the table in By Level.

Section Controller Benchmark Correlation AssetSetCorrelationSection.svelte:64 Never L1° How much did each of these hurt? lossController, includeAssetSetLossLevels (AssetSetComparisonLevels.svelte:114-123) Never L3° What did each of these pay for its risk? RiskControllerHost, includeAssetSetPaidLevels (AssetSetComparisonLevels.svelte:244) assetSetBenchmarkId (l.138) L4° What if…? AssetSetReplaySection.svelte, replay on demand Never
  • Rates. Every lab controller sends appliedRiskFreePercent: 0 (AssetSetCorrelationSection.svelte:72, AssetSetComparisonLevels.svelte:120, l.136, AssetSetReplaySection.svelte:84), and the KPI and the comparison send target_annual_return: 0 (riskAnalysisHelpers.ts:336, l.370-373). The lab has no control for either.
  • Bad month. MONTHLY_VAR_HORIZON_DAYS = 30 calendar days (riskAnalysisHelpers.ts:282, used at l.321 and l.342). The engine turns them into observations at the observed frequency — about 21 on a trading-day calendar, 30 on an every-day one — as explained in Value at Risk.
  • One calendar per request. The engine prepares one joint calendar per request from the scope, the window and the currency (Request Flow, step 4). Requests that agree on those three share it, so a matrix cell, an L1° row and an L3° dot cover the same dates (AssetSetComparisonLevels.svelte:20-29). A benchmark joins only L3°'s request, so only L3°'s window can move with it; its period line says so. How a short history narrows the calendar is in Alignment.
  • L3° waits. labBenchmarkId() (assetSetSelection.ts:228) passes a benchmark only in state set. labL3Waits() (l.245) keeps L3°'s controller unmounted while the picker is pending, or while a chosen benchmark waits for the lab's verdicts, so L3° asks once and never tries a benchmark that turns out blocked. The Beta and Correlation columns follow the answer, not the choice: benchmarkApplies = benchmarkId !== null && comparison.status === 'ok' (AssetSetComparisonLevels.svelte:207).
  • Sync and reload. openSync() opens a PageSyncModal on the selection's prices and the configured FX pairs that convert them (buildSyncTargets(), syncTargets.ts:43). After an accepted sync, and on reload(), the panel calls invalidateRisk() and bumps refreshVersion for every section (AssetSetRiskPanel.svelte:200-228); the replay also forgets its answer (AssetSetReplaySection.svelte:99).

docs.title: 🕸️ Correlation Section
docs.text:
• Triangle. Only the strict lower triangle is drawn: the first asset has no row and the last has no column (CorrelationHeatmap.svelte:172, lowerTrianglePoints() in correlationHelpers.ts:439). Fewer than two assets draw nothing (l.424). A cell prints ρ with two decimals (l.506); the tooltip gives ρ with three, its band, the observations and coverage of the pair, and each asset's three largest sectors and countries plus a folded rest (l.343, l.487-489). The colour scale runs red at −1, neutral at 0 and blue at +1 (l.128-129).
  • Bands and lists. correlationBand() (correlationHelpers.ts:69-82): high above 0.7, inverse at −0.3 or below; near-identical at 0.9 or above (NEAR_IDENTICAL, l.268). topPairs() (l.290) lists only high pairs (The most alike) and inverse pairs (The ones that offset), five each; past PAIR_LIST_THRESHOLD (20) assets it lists eight, and the lists move ahead of the matrix on lg screens (CorrelationHeatmap.svelte:290, l.616). The opposite tag starts at OPPOSITE = −0.7 (CorrelationPairsList.svelte:47); a pair's colour follows the heatmap's polarity (l.62).
  • Orderings. similarity, the default, is clusterOrder() (correlationHelpers.ts:148): average-linkage clustering on 1 − |ρ|, a missing pair at distance 1 (l.124-127), ties broken by position. type follows the asset-type menu order, then the name. sector and region use dominantExposure() (l.362): the key holding at least DOMINANT_SHARE (0.5, l.337) of the classified weight, Other left out; exposureOrder() (l.396) then sorts named groups, Diversified, Other only and Unclassified. A mode is offered only when its data exist (CorrelationHeatmap.svelte:93). The sector and country distributions come from one bulk GET /api/v1/assets?asset_ids=… (matrixMetadata.svelte.ts:85); a failed read only hides those two buttons.

docs.title: 📉 Loss Table (L1°)
docs.text:
• Columns by horizon: Bad day, Bad month, Worst fall (with its lasted N d line), Below peak now, Rise to peak (AssetSetLossComparisonSection.svelte:178-224). The order is the point: a one-day loss printed beside a multi-year drawdown must not read as something to add up.
  • Signs. The VaR/CVaR contract is positive and the drawdown contract negative; both are drawn as falls with U+2212 (fall(), l.106) and sorted as drawn (drawnLoss(), l.120), an unmeasured cell last. Every loss uses one red (l.124): no per-asset colour, no ranking.
  • Rows. Rows come from the selected ids, so every analysed asset has one and a blank is a dash whose tooltip explains it (figureCell(), assetSetTable.ts:25).
  • Widths. Each figure column opens at its title's measured width, which is also its minimum (titleWidth(), l.137; headerWidth(), riskReturnLevel.ts:106).
  • Mixed outcomes. asset_set_drawdown needs 2 observations and the other four analytics 20, so a short window returns one ok beside four unavailable (AssetSetComparisonLevels.svelte:39-47; floors in The Analytics).

docs.title: ⚖️ Risk and Return (L3°)
docs.text:
• Shared level. RiskReturnLevel.svelte also renders the portfolio's L3. The lab declares capabilities={{ratios: true, benchmark: benchmarkApplies}} and no weight (AssetSetRiskReturnSection.svelte:198), so Beta and Correlation exist only with a measured benchmark (RiskReturnLevel.svelte:261).
  • Benchmark row. withBenchmarkRow() (assetSetLevels.ts:296) adds a ref-<id> row for a benchmark outside the selection; a selected benchmark keeps its own row. referenceRowsFirst() opens the table with it (RiskReturnLevel.svelte:95).
  • Chart and line. The chart needs two placeable points (l.101). capitalMarketLineAnchor() (frontend/src/lib/components/charts/scatterChartHelpers.ts:160) anchors the line on a benchmark with positive volatility, else on the portfolio, which a selection never has: no benchmark, no line. The notes come from riskReturnNotes() (riskReturnLevel.ts:174): above and line only with a line, return and priceOnly always. The line starts at LAB_RISK_FREE_RATE = 0 (AssetSetRiskReturnSection.svelte:137).
  • Period line. assetSetCalculationWindow() (assetSetLevels.ts:391) reads the first result with metadata — from end − calendar_days + 1 to end — and sets narrowed when that start is more than NARROWED_AFTER_DAYS (7, l.368) after the toolbar's start, or that end more than 7 days before the toolbar's end. The length is spelled in calendar units by calendarLength() (l.436).
  • Selection. Rows and dots share the table's single selection; a selected asset's dot is drawn larger in the selection green, while the benchmark keeps its colour (the same scatterChartHelpers.ts, l.101).

docs.title: ⏮️ Replay (L4°)
docs.text:
• One rung. AssetSetReplaySection.svelte hands L4WhatIf the replay snippet only (l.135): no hypothetical shock and no simulation on an unweighted scope. The frame is collapsible and loads the scenario catalogue on first open (l.133); showMoney={false}.
  • Controls. L4Replay.svelte puts No preset first (l.95). A preset sets the dates; a quick range or a typed date drops the preset; both reset the answer (l.151-170). The quick ranges exclude MAX (l.231). The composition total is withheld when portfolio_return is null, as it is on every unweighted scope (l.269), and TornadoChart drops the weight, contribution and amount columns when no row carries them (levels/l4/TornadoChart.svelte:57-60).
  • Lifetime. A finished replay is discarded when the base signature moves, i.e. the selection or the dates (The Panel Controller), and after an accepted sync (AssetSetReplaySection.svelte:99). Coverage, exclusion reasons and the suggested replay period are in Replay Coverage.

docs.title: 🚩 Notices and Frames
docs.text:
• One notice. partialNotice() (levels/partialNotice.ts:40) runs over the results of the correlation section and the two levels, read through each section's qualitySource() (AssetSetRiskPanel.svelte:625). The replay hands it no results (AssetSetReplaySection.svelte:127) and keeps its own status. Only partial results become badges; the two VaR instances are labelled Bad day and Bad month (VAR_LABELS, AssetSetComparisonLevels.svelte:158). The notice is blue, titled Holdings without prices…, only when every reason is no_price_source, and titled Worth knowing… when nothing is partial (levels/RiskPartialNotice.svelte:42, l.54).
  • One banner. The four controllers' dataQualityIssues are merged by mergeQualityIssues() (AssetSetRiskPanel.svelte:633) and rendered by DataQualityBanner in grouped mode. labQualityAction() (syncTargets.ts:78-82) maps any sync_* action to the lab's own sync, and navigate_asset, navigate_fx and add_fx_pair to navigation.
  • Frames. RiskLevelSection keeps under each section only what did not come back (levelErrorHealth(), levels/partialNotice.ts:49), in an amber alert (levels/RiskLevelSection.svelte:179), plus answer_discarded (ANSWER_DISCARDED_CODE, frontend/src/lib/features/risk/riskPanelController.svelte.ts:57) once the controller's re-asks are exhausted — the bound and the wording are in The Panel Controller. The section bodies offer Retry (loadBase(true)) when they have no figure to show, for example AssetSetCorrelationSection.svelte:139, l.153.
  • Calculation details. The frame's <details> (levels/RiskLevelSection.svelte:229) lists the observations, coverage, annualization factor and return basis. levelMetadata() (levels/levelMetadata.ts:54) collapses analytics that agree into one row, and leaves out method.
  • Manual links. Each frame's book icon (docsPath) opens the theory: the correlation page, the risk metrics index for L1° and L3°, the historical replay page for L4°.

docs.title: 🛡️ Dashboard Risk Tab
docs.text:
The Risk tab of the Dashboard and of Broker Detail mounts levels/RiskLevelsPanel.svelte: one createRiskPanelController, a header (levels/RiskPanelHeader.svelte), the shared notice and four levels, L1–L4. The two hosts pass the same props with a different scope. What users see is in the Risk Tab user page; which analytics each level asks for is in By Level.

Host Scope What differs frontend/src/routes/(app)/dashboard/+page.svelte:1109-1123 broker_ids: ownedBrokerIds (l.230): the brokers the user owns with a share above 0 (getOwnedBrokers(), frontend/src/lib/stores/reference/brokerStore.ts:262) The broker filter is not applied: subtitle becomes risk.dashboardFullPortfolio while it is on (l.1117), and scopeValue is null then (l.1115), because the summary follows the filter. assetIds are the summary's holdings (l.1114). frontend/src/routes/(app)/brokers/[id]/+page.svelte:753-767 broker_ids: [broker.id] scopeValue is that broker's net worth (l.759); internalSubset prints risk.internalSubset (l.761).
  • No owned broker, no request. The Dashboard host mounts the panel only when canAsk (l.234); otherwise it shows common.noData (l.1125), or a spinner while the brokers load (l.1128).
  • Waves. The controller opts into includeDrawdownSummary, includeMonthlyVar and includeCurrentCompositionRiskReturn (levels/RiskLevelsPanel.svelte:85-103; the options are in The Panel Controller). The historical wave reads the portfolio's TWRR (The Primary Series), which is why deposits and withdrawals are neither gains nor losses here. Neither host sends a slice, so the backtest notice (backtestDeclared(), l.249, l.322) never shows on these pages.

docs.title: 📉 How Much Can It Hurt?
docs.text:
levels/L1HowMuchItHurts.svelte, over historical_var (two instances), drawdown_summary and historical_kpi (L1_CODES, levels/RiskLevelsPanel.svelte:126).

  • Cards. buildHurtRows() (levels/levelHelpers.ts:368) builds day → month → worst. The day and month cards lead with the CVaR at 95 % (l.378); the VaR is computed as secondaryLoss but never drawn, and appears only as the histogram's cut. The 30-day horizon is the lab's: see Requests, Bad month. A rung whose analytic failed is omitted, never zero-filled (l.363).
  • Worst fall. The depth comes from drawdown_summary, falling back to historical_kpi (levelHelpers.ts:396-397); the duration follows the depth's source (l.405), so the two never come from different analytics. The recovery needed line is computed by the backend, not here: drawdown_summary's maximum_drawdown_trough_to_peak_ratio (required_recovery_return(), backend/app/services/financial_math/returns.py:239: −50 % needs +100 %), read as it comes (l.408) and only on the summary's own depth (summaryDepth, l.396) for a fall above 0. No fallback: a depth from historical_kpi has no recovery. A total loss has none either: the backend leaves the ratio null and states the total_loss_no_recovery warning, which does not degrade the result (The Drawdown Episode). The line is drawn at L1HowMuchItHurts.svelte:155; a null omits it (l.152), as L1 omits every absent sub-measure.
  • Current drawdown. buildCurrentDrawdown() returns null at a peak (levelHelpers.ts:435), so the card exists only below one (L1HowMuchItHurts.svelte:176). Its recovery needed line is the backend's remaining_to_peak_ratio, read as it comes (levelHelpers.ts:442) and drawn at L1HowMuchItHurts.svelte:183; it is null for a total loss, and the line is then omitted.
  • Tail measures as second rows. The worst realization sits under the day card; drawdown at risk and conditional drawdown at risk under the worst fall (L1HowMuchItHurts.svelte:161, l.167, l.170; buildTailMeasures(), levels/l1/l1Helpers.ts:281). The ulcer index is the caption of the underwater chart (levels/l1/UnderwaterChart.svelte:65-70, value at l.67).
  • Histogram. buildReturnHistogram() (l1Helpers.ts:138) flags the bin holding the VaR cut (holdsCut, l.94), drawn amber, and the bins wholly beyond it (belowCut, l.103), drawn red. The straddling bin is the amber holdsCut one and is never counted as tail: its belowCut is false (l.175-176), as stated at levels/l1/ReturnHistogram.svelte:18 and applied by barClass() (l.40-43). A bar's title gives its range (l.68).
  • Money. lossMoney() is scopeValue × loss (L1HowMuchItHurts.svelte:72), shown only for a positive scopeValue (l.65): on the Dashboard, never while a broker filter is on; on Broker Detail, over that broker's own net worth (frontend/src/routes/(app)/brokers/[id]/+page.svelte:759).
  • Labels and links. Each card prints a technicalName line (frontend/src/lib/components/ui/display/RiskMetricCard.svelte:108, keys risk.levels.l1.technical.*) and links its own metric page (DOC_PATHS and TAIL_DOCS, L1HowMuchItHurts.svelte:103, l.113).

docs.title: 🧩 Diversification
docs.text:
levels/L2Diversification.svelte, over risk_contribution (current composition, portfolio scope only: The Analytics) and correlation (historical wave).

  • Rows. buildDivergenceRows() (levels/levelHelpers.ts:476) drops a row without weight or contribution (l.485) and sorts on the signed gap contribution − weight (l.496). Eight rows show before Show all (visibleRows, L2Diversification.svelte:77, l.338).
  • Lead. leadDivergence() returns the top row only when its gap reaches 5 points (minimumGap, levelHelpers.ts:507); levels/RiskLevelsPanel.svelte:307 words it.
  • Cards. buildConcentration() (levelHelpers.ts:556) returns the effective number of assets and the diversification ratio together or not at all. The first card's caption compares the index with the measured rows — above, below or equal (effectiveAssetsReading, L2Diversification.svelte:149). uncoveredWeight() (levelHelpers.ts:601) splits cash_weight into cash and excluded_weight, worded by uncoveredCaption (L2Diversification.svelte:172). A card whose metric the scope lacks is not drawn (l.243).
  • Matrix. The shared heatmap (Correlation Section) receives only output and assetLabels (L2Diversification.svelte:363): no type, sector or region data, so only similarity and name are offered and no exposure badges show. When no pair reaches NEAR_IDENTICAL, a line says so (hasRedundantPair, l.114, l.359). On both surfaces, a click on a listed pair reveals, highlights and opens its cell, and a second click closes it (selectPair(), CorrelationHeatmap.svelte:393).

docs.title: ⚖️ Being Paid
docs.text:
levels/L3Benchmark.svelte (the picker) and levels/L3RiskAdjusted.svelte (table and chart), over the current-composition historical_kpi and asset_risk_return and the on-demand comparison.

  • Perimeter. selectKpiWave() (levels/l3Helpers.ts:64) reads historical_kpi from the current-composition wave, falling back to the historical one; the title appends risk.levels.l3.perimeter.* from the answer's metadata.mode (L3RiskAdjusted.svelte:59-61).
  • Benchmark. Picker and store are Benchmark and Eligibility. Instead of the lab's labL3Waits() (Requests): measuredAssetIds={[]}, so a held asset may be the benchmark (L3Benchmark.svelte:158); an effect asks the comparison once per baseEpoch|benchmark when the picker reports set and the catalogue is ready (l.83-93); any other state bumps the generation and drops the answer (l.101-107).
  • Rates. The comparison runs on current_composition with the page's risk-free rate and target_annual_return: 0 (L3Benchmark.svelte:133). That rate is appliedRiskFreePercent = 0, with no control (levels/RiskLevelsPanel.svelte:77): the same zeros as the lab (Requests, Rates).
  • Table and chart. The shared RiskReturnLevel (Risk and Return (L3°)), with capabilities={{weight: true, ratios: true, benchmark: benchmarkApplies}} (L3RiskAdjusted.svelte:113). benchmarkApplies is a measured beta or a benchmark row (l.97), not the lab's status === 'ok'. The portfolio gets a reference row from the KPI (l.93) and a dot from asset_risk_return's portfolio figures (levels/l3Helpers.ts:142-151), so with no measured benchmark the line runs through the portfolio instead of vanishing. weight: true adds the weight column and the dot-size note (riskReturnLevel.ts:187); widths and visible columns persist under storageKey="risk-l3" (L3RiskAdjusted.svelte:117), and the column menu sits in the level's header (levels/RiskLevelsPanel.svelte:342-346). Only a click on a column title sorts (RiskReturnLevel.svelte:14). Dashes: a blank figure has the blankNote tooltip (l.227), an uncalculated ratio a bare dash (l.224), the benchmark's own beta and correlation referenceItself (l.212), and a benchmark nobody holds notHeld under the weight (l.216).

docs.title: 🔮 What If…?
docs.text:
levels/L4WhatIf.svelte with three snippets — L4Replay, L4Shock, L4Simulation (levels/RiskLevelsPanel.svelte:366-376) — in a collapsible frame that loads the scenario catalogue on first open (l.364).

  • Tool selector. With more than one snippet the level is selectable (L4WhatIf.svelte:88): one Add: button per tool, always in L4_TOOLS order (l.7). The open set is read at mount from risk.l4.openTools in user storage (l.13, l.90, l.100), so the Dashboard and every broker page share it, and written by add() and close() (l.109, l.113); close() also resets that tool's analysis. Folding the frame unmounts the body (levels/RiskLevelSection.svelte:170) and keeps the controller's answers.
  • Replay. Controls and lifetime are the lab's (Replay (L4°)); coverage, exclusions and the suggested period are in Replay Coverage. On a weighted scope the excluded weight becomes a zero-return residual (backend/app/services/risk_plugins/stress/plugin.py:562), worded by excludedHeader() (levels/l4/L4Replay.svelte:205). showMoney follows the result's scope (scopeKind === 'portfolio', l.100–101) unless the parent passes showMoney, so the total sentence (l.272–273) and the amounts show here.
  • Shock. A preset click adopts the scenario's dimension and bucket shocks and runs it (levels/l4/L4Shock.svelte:82); nothing runs without buckets (l.73); editing a bucket clears the preset and the answer (l.91); a note shows when classification_coverage < 1 (l.170).
  • Simulation. Defaults and the five modes are in Simulation Parameters. In the UI the sampling select exists for GBM only (levels/l4/L4Simulation.svelte:62), the seed input is hidden on QMC (l.64), and SOBOL_START_INDEX is fixed at 0 (l.45). The answer shows the terminal mean, the probability of loss and the P5–P95 band (l.216-222), the drift-uncertainty note (l.225) and SimulationProvenance (l.244). The beta banner and the model warning are drawn in the simulation box only (L4WhatIf.svelte:156-160).
  • Disclosure. L4 keeps its own: every degraded status, named per step (L4_STEP_LABELS, RiskLevelsPanel.svelte:229), its reasons (l.239), its errors with discarded runs (l.240) and its metadata (l.241). The replay enters through replaySectionView() (l.214), so its warnings are read in the replay block alone.

docs.title: 🚩 Notices and Refresh
docs.text:
• Header. levels/RiskPanelHeader.svelte draws the title and subtitle, Sync and Refresh (l.84-104), the load error (l.109-113) and the DataQualityBanner in grouped mode over the controller's merged issues (l.116). Instead of the lab's labQualityAction(), handleQualityAction() (l.66) opens the header's own PageSyncModal for any sync action and navigates for navigate_asset, navigate_fx and add_fx_pair.
  • Sync targets. syncAssets are the host's assetIds — on the Dashboard the summary's holdings, which follow the broker filter — and syncFxPairs the configured pairs between their currencies and the target (RiskPanelHeader.svelte:38-64); the button is disabled when both are empty (l.89). After a sync, handleSynced() marks the answers stale and the host's onsynced reloads its own data (Dashboard host l.1050, Broker Detail host l.690).
  • Notice. The shared notice is described in Notices and Frames. Here it reads the L1 results, risk_contribution, correlation and the L3 results (levels/RiskLevelsPanel.svelte:154), groups each partial badge under the first level that renders it (levelOf, l.162), and names the two VaR instances and L3's KPI as the levels show them (L1_LABELS, l.128; l.141). The L1–L3 frames keep only unavailable and failed (levelErrorHealth, l.334-346); L4 keeps its own (above). Calculation details are per level (l.191-193, l.241), as in Notices and Frames.
  • Refresh and retry. There is no Retry button. The header's Refresh is loadBase(true) (levels/RiskPanelHeader.svelte:98); the Dashboard's own Refresh bumps refreshVersion (Dashboard host, l.695-698), which the controller turns into loadBase(true) (frontend/src/lib/features/risk/riskPanelController.svelte.ts:647-656). Re-asks, answer_discarded, the page cache and loadError are in The Panel Controller. A price catch-up reloads the base waves on screen by itself, in silence (loadBase(false, true)), not through refreshVersion; the on-demand analyses are left alone. Here onrefreshfailed toasts risk.states.loadFailed (RiskLevelsPanel.svelte:82), setTweenHydration() stops cached cards from counting up (l.106), and loadError replaces the notice and the levels (l.328).
  • Signature. A new period, currency or scope discards the on-demand answers and relaunches only those in flight (The Panel Controller); L3's comparison is asked again by its own effect (levels/L3Benchmark.svelte:84-92).
  • Manual links. Every level's book icon opens the risk-metrics index without an anchor, which would break on the translated sites (levels/RiskLevelsPanel.svelte:331-333); cards and second rows link their own metric pages (levels/L1HowMuchItHurts.svelte:117, l.127; levels/L2Diversification.svelte:258, l.268, l.284).

docs.title: ⚙️ Settings Components
docs.text: This section documents the components used for the Settings pages (User Preferences, Global Settings, Profile, Users, Security).

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture
docs.text: The settings system uses a modular architecture based on a common layout and reusable field components.

docs.title: 🗂️ Tab registry
docs.text:
The tabs of the Settings page are a registry: SETTINGS_TABS in lib/features/settings/settingsTabs.ts. routes/(app)/settings/[...path]/+page.svelte names no tab itself: it draws its two bars and the active body from that list. Each entry is a SettingsTab:

Field Role id The suffix of its settings-tab-{id} test id, and the ?tab= value of 1.2, still read path Its address (lot B10), from the table of settingsPaths.ts: /settings/<tab>, or /settings/admin/<tab> for a member of Administration labelKey Catalogue key of the label, drawn as $_(labelKey) on the tab and in the heading shown on a phone icon Lucide icon of the tab button order Position in the bar, left to right; for a member of a group, in the group's second bar component The tab body visible?(ctx) Who sees the tab; when absent, everyone does props?(ctx) Props spread on the body group? The id of the group of SETTINGS_TAB_GROUPS the tab belongs to: the top bar shows the group as one entry, and a second bar lists its members badge?(ctx) The number its button shows, none for 0; a group's entry shows the sum of its visible members' prefetch?(ctx) What the page starts loading before the tab is opened, so that badge can count: run when the page opens, and again when the context changes, for every visible tab that has one alignEnd? On a wide screen, starts the right-hand side: this entry and every entry after it sit on the right (sm:ml-auto on its button). One tab or one group carries it: today the administration group, and no tab

ctx is a SettingsTabContext, {isSuperuser}, which the page derives from the auth store ($auth.user?.is_superuser ?? false). The registry holds nine tabs:

id order Body Visible to group Extras profile 10 ProfileTab everyone — — preferences 20 PreferencesTab everyone — — plugins 25 PluginSettingsTab everyone — — about 30 AboutTab everyone — — admin 100 GlobalSettingsTab administrators administration Label settings.globalSettings (Global Settings), icon Settings2; visible: (ctx) => ctx.isSuperuser (lot N69-2, decision D4 a); props: (ctx) => ({canEdit: ctx.isSuperuser}), kept: see GlobalSettingsTab users 110 UsersTab administrators administration visible: (ctx) => ctx.isSuperuser backup 120 BackupTab administrators administration visible: (ctx) => ctx.isSuperuser email 130 EmailSettingsTab administrators administration visible: (ctx) => ctx.isSuperuser security 140 SecurityTab administrators administration visible: (ctx) => ctx.isSuperuser; badge: () => securityChecks.attentionCount; prefetch: (ctx) => { if (ctx.isSuperuser) void securityChecks.ensureLoaded(); }

The admin id stays as it was, so ?tab=admin, the link of the open-registration warning, still opens the global settings (the warning shows to administrators only, as the tab does; for a regular user, ?tab=admin names a hidden tab and opens profile, the first visible one); lot A8b changed only its label and its icon, the group having taken the Shield, and removed the key settings.admin (Admin) from the catalogues. Five bodies are in lib/features/settings/tabs/, the Security tab's in lib/features/settings/security/ (SecurityTab). The Plugins tab's body, lib/features/plugin-settings/PluginSettingsTab.svelte (label pluginSettings.tab.label), the Backup tab's, lib/features/backup/BackupTab.svelte (label backup.tab), and the Email tab's, lib/features/email/EmailSettingsTab.svelte (label email.tab.label), live with their features: for the Plugins tab see Plugin Settings › The Interface, for the Email tab The Email Tab. The Plugins tab takes no props: every user sees it, and the catalogue the API returns already says which fields this user may change.

docs.title: Groups
docs.text:
SETTINGS_TAB_GROUPS, in the same module, holds the groups of the top bar (decision P13 b), each a SettingsTabGroup, {id, labelKey, icon, alignEnd?}. There is one today, administration: label settings.administration (Administration), icon Shield, alignEnd: true. Its members are admin, users, backup, email and security; profile, preferences, plugins and about belong to no group. A group's id is a ?tab= value and a test-id suffix too (settings-tab-administration): it is URL-safe, and no tab's id.

settingsBar(tabs, groups, ctx) gives the entries of the top bar, SettingsBarEntry[], as a new array, and leaves the lists it is given as they were: the tabs of visibleSettingsTabs(tabs, ctx), by order, each a {kind: 'tab', tab} entry, except the visible members of a group, gathered into one {kind: 'group', group, members} entry placed where its first visible member would be, members being its visible members by order. A group without a visible member has no entry, and a tab whose group names none of groups stays a tab entry. A regular user's bar is profile, preferences, plugins and about: every member of administration is an administrator's (since lot N69-2), so the group has no entry for them; an administrator's ends with administration and its five members.

docs.title: The page
docs.text:
The page is the runtime of the registry, written in Svelte 5 runes:

  • Top bar: settingsBar(SETTINGS_TABS, SETTINGS_TAB_GROUPS, ctx), handed to TabBar with the labels hidden on a phone (hideLabelOnMobile). A tab entry is drawn as its tab (settings-tab-{id}, its icon, $_(labelKey)); a group entry with the group's icon and label, and the test id settings-tab-{groupId}. An entry whose tab or group has alignEnd gets sm:ml-auto. The top bar selects the entry of the open tab: the tab itself, or the group of the open member.
  • Second bar: while the open tab is a member of a group with at least two visible members, a second TabBar, inside data-testid="settings-subtabs", lists those members, each with its own settings-tab-{id}, icon, label (hidden on a phone too) and badge, the open one selected. It takes the same props (hideLabelOnMobile, scrollable) and the same colour roles as the top bar. A group with one visible member gets no second bar: its entry opens that member directly, and the member has no settings-tab-{id} of its own. No context of today's registry makes such a group since lot N69-2 (a regular user sees no member of administration, an administrator all five), but the page still handles it, on a registry of the test's own (see the tests below).
  • Clicks (selectTop()): a tab entry opens its tab; a group entry opens the group's first visible member, unless one of its members is open already, which stays, its body not mounted again. A member of the second bar opens that member.
  • Both bars are scrollable: entries that do not fit the card (French or Spanish on a narrow screen) scroll sideways instead of being clipped by its overflow-hidden, the active one stays whole in view, and the sides that hide entries fade (see Scrollable tab bar).
  • Body: the active tab's component alone, with props(ctx) spread on it. The spread is live: when the auth store changes, the body on screen receives the new props. The heading shown on a phone names the active tab, a member and never its group: Global Settings, not Administration.
  • Addresses (lot B10): every tab has one, path, and every group too (/settings/admin). One route, settings/[...path], serves them all, /settings included. settingsPlaceOf(pathname, tabs, groups) reads an address back: the page, a tab, a group, or nothing the registry knows. An address opens its tab at the first render and whenever it changes (Back, Forward, a link); a group's address opens its first visible member. Choosing a tab writes its address with goto(path, {noScroll, keepFocus}), as a new entry of the history. /settings opens the first tab and keeps its address. An unknown address, or the address of a tab this user cannot see once the user is known, goes back to /settings (replaceState). Links never write an address by hand: settingsTabHref(id, query?) of settingsPaths.ts, a module that imports no tab body.
  • Active tab: always a tab, never a group. At /settings, the first visible tab, unless the ?tab= of 1.2 names a visible tab or a group; the address then becomes the tab's own (replaceState): a member's id opens that member inside its group (with the second bar when the group has two visible members or more), a group's id its first visible member (?tab=administration opens admin, for an administrator). The choice runs in $effect.pre, so the tab that ?tab= names is the first body mounted: the default body never mounts, not even for an instant. A ?tab= value is applied once: a later page update that keeps it does not take back the tab the user picked, while a new value, or the same one after a tab's address, is applied again. An unknown id, the id of a tab this user cannot see, or that of a group with no visible member, is ignored: a regular user's ?tab=admin or ?tab=administration opens profile, and the body of Global Settings never mounts for them. A ?tab= naming a tab that becomes visible later (the user is promoted while on the page) is applied when the tab appears, inside its group. If the active tab stops being visible, the first visible tab opens.
  • Badges: a tab entry shows its badge(ctx), a group entry the sum of its visible members', and TabBar draws none for 0. They are read while the bars are derived, so a badge follows the reactive state it reads: a count that arrives after the first render shows at once.
  • Prefetch: an $effect calls the prefetch(ctx) of every visible tab that has one, when the page mounts and again whenever the context changes (a promotion included, which prefetches the tab that has just appeared); never for a tab this context does not show. The calls run inside untrack(): a prefetch reads the state it fills (ensureLoaded() reads the security checks' status), and a tracked read would run the effect again each time that state moves — after a failure, a new request, in a loop. So nothing else prefetches again: not a change of tab, of group or of ?tab=, nor a change of the state a prefetch reads.

Adding a tab takes one entry in SETTINGS_TABS, plus the import of its body. The users entry, a tab only administrators see, in the administration group, is a complete example:

import {Users} from 'lucide-svelte';
import UsersTab from '$lib/features/settings/tabs/UsersTab.svelte';

export const SETTINGS_TABS: readonly SettingsTab[] = [
    // profile (10), preferences (20), plugins (25), about (30), admin (100, administration)
    // Administrators only: the accounts (decision D-A10) and every account link (lot UA3).
    {id: 'users', labelKey: 'settings.users', icon: Users, order: 110, component: UsersTab, visible: (ctx) => ctx.isSuperuser, group: 'administration'},
];
  • order: a free number between the neighbours. The orders leave gaps, so no other tab is renumbered; 110 puts users after Global Settings (100) in the group's second bar. A tab without a group and with an order between 30 and 100 lands after About, on the left; above 100, after the group's entry, which sits where its first member (100) would be, so on the right. Every order is unique.
  • visible: (ctx) => ctx.isSuperuser keeps the tab out of a regular user's bars altogether, and a ?tab= naming it is ignored for them. Leave visible out for a tab everyone sees.
  • group: 'administration' for a tab that looks after the instance: it has no button of its own in the top bar, and shows in the group's second bar. Leave it out for a tab of the top bar.
  • props: only when the body depends on the context, as admin does for canEdit. Since lot N69-2 only administrators see that tab, so canEdit is always true on screen: the read-only branch, canEdit: false, stays in GlobalSettingsTab, unreached from the interface, until a cleanup.
  • badge and prefetch: only for a tab whose button counts something, today security alone. badge reads a reactive count synchronously, 0 until there is one; prefetch starts what the count needs, does nothing for a context the tab is not for, and nothing again once loaded, as securityChecks.ensureLoaded() does.
  • alignEnd: one tab or one group carries it, today the administration group; no tab does, though the page still honours a tab's.
  • id and labelKey: the id is unique, made of lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starts with a letter, and is no group's id; the labelKey is a sentence in all four catalogues.
  • Tests: lib/features/settings/settingsTabs.test.ts pins the content of the registry through its TODAY table, so the new tab adds its row there in the same change, its id to the CONTEXTS and BARS lists of those who see it and, when it joins the group, to ADMINISTRATION, with a vi.mock of its body module like the others; the cases that list today's tabs by name follow it (users also has two cases of its own: STAB-01, hidden from a regular user, and STAB-02, order 110 after admin, both members of the group; admin has one, rewritten by lot N69-2: hidden from a regular user, shown to an administrator, its props still {canEdit: isSuperuser}). The same file checks the ids, the orders and the labels in the four catalogues, the group and what its tabs carry (STAB-03 to STAB-14: one group, its label, icon and members, no tab with alignEnd, security the only tab with a badge and a prefetch, the bar of each context; STAB-14, lot N69-2: no administration entry nor any of its members in a regular user's bar, the entry once in an administrator's, admin its first member), and settingsBar() on lists of its own (SBAR-01 to SBAR-05). routes/(app)/settings/page.tabs.test.ts tests the page on a registry of its own, with two groups (crew, and office, the stand-in for Administration as lot A8b had it, with one visible member for a regular user) and counts in a reactive box (SPAGE-01 to SPAGE-21: the top bar, the second bar and its clicks, ?tab= naming a member or a group, the badges and their sums, the prefetch at the start, again for a new context and never otherwise). SPAGE-22 to SPAGE-24 (lot N69-2) render the page on the real registry: a regular user's page with neither settings-tab-administration nor settings-tab-admin, Profile open; ?tab=admin and ?tab=administration opening Profile for a regular user, the Global Settings body never mounted, and Global Settings, with canEdit: true, inside its group for an administrator. The file loads the real settingsTabs module (importOriginal), which imports every body: the mocked module's SETTINGS_TABS and SETTINGS_TAB_GROUPS are getters, answering the real lists while a case sets mocks.registry.real and the synthetic ones otherwise, and each real body is a probe named by its module (mocks.realBodies). A new tab adds its body there, with its vi.mock (a store the registry imports gets a no-op stand-in, as securityChecks does). ./dev.py test front-utility core-unit runs settingsTabs.test.ts, ./dev.py test front-utility component-unit runs page.tabs.test.ts.

docs.title: 📐 SettingsLayout
docs.text:
The SettingsLayout component provides the structural shell for all settings tabs.

Features:

  • Two-Column Layout: Sidebar navigation on the left, content on the right.
  • Global Actions: "Save All", "Undo All", "Reset All" buttons in the header.
  • Lock Toggle: Optional lock button for admin settings (prevents accidental edits).
  • Responsive: Stacks vertically on mobile.

Props:

  • categories: Array of { id, icon, labelKey } for the sidebar.
  • selectedCategory: ID of the currently active category filter.
  • hasChanges: Boolean to show Save/Undo buttons.
  • hasNonDefaults: Boolean to show Reset button.
  • isLocked: Boolean state of the edit lock.

docs.title: 🎨 PreferencesTab
docs.text:
Manages user-specific settings (Language, Currency, Theme) and hosts the Onboarding category described below. Its categories are display (Language), currency (Default Currency), appearance (Theme) and onboarding, plus All Settings when none is selected.

Logic (lib/features/settings/tabs/PreferencesTab.svelte):

  1. Load: Fetches Global Defaults (/settings/global) and User Settings (/settings/user) in parallel.
  2. State Tracking:
    • originalValues: The values currently saved in the DB.
    • editedValues: The values currently in the form inputs.
    • globalDefaults: The system-wide default values — FALLBACK_DEFAULTS (en, EUR, auto) when /settings/global cannot be loaded.
  3. Computed States:
    • isModified: editedValues !== originalValues (Shows Save/Undo).
    • isNonDefault: originalValues !== globalDefaults (Shows Reset, but only while the field has no pending edit: SettingActions.svelte).
  4. Persistence: Saves to /settings/user via PUT, one field per request. Save sends that field; Save All sends the modified fields one after the other, then reports what was saved and what failed in a single toast (success, partial or error). Language and theme take effect only once their write succeeds (currentLanguage.set(), applyTheme()), and userSettings.setDirect() then writes the saved language, currency and theme into the store. Reset only copies the global default into editedValues: it still has to be saved.

The Default Currency (base_currency) is proposed when something new is created: BrokerForm.svelte uses it for the first initial balance, AssetModal.svelte for a new asset's currency and PacPlannerTool.svelte for a new plan's valuation currency. The Dashboard, the Brokers list and detail pages, and the risk panel of the Assets page start their display currency from the global default_currency ($globalSettings) instead.

docs.title: 🧭 OnboardingReplaySection
docs.text:
OnboardingReplaySection.svelte (in frontend/src/lib/features/onboarding/components/) is the Onboarding category of PreferencesTab ({id: 'onboarding', icon: Compass, labelKey: 'onboarding.settings.category'}). The tab renders it when that category is selected and in the All Settings view (no category selected). It lists every onboarding flow with its progress and lets the user replay any of them without changing that recorded progress. This section covers the Settings UI only; the mechanics behind it — when a guide is due, what a replay does once it runs, where its position is kept — are explained in Onboarding Guides.

What it lists. The section reads onboarding.progress?.flows, the per-user progress that the app bootstrap loads from GET /api/v1/settings/onboarding: one OnboardingProgressItem for each of the 15 flows of ONBOARDING_FLOW_VERSIONS (backend/app/services/accounts/onboarding_service.py; enum OnboardingFlow in backend/app/db/models.py). The section sorts them into collapsible groups; Setup and Core tour start open:

Group (onboarding.settings.groups.*) Flows setup welcome core intro_tour transactions transactions_page_guide, transaction_create_guide, transaction_bulk_guide, import_guide broker broker_page_guide, broker_guide, broker_detail_guide fx fx_page_guide, fx_guide, fx_detail_guide asset asset_page_guide, asset_guide, asset_detail_guide tools tools_page_guide

A group header counts its flows that are completed at the current version ({completed}/{total} guides completed). Each row shows the flow name (onboarding.flows.<flow>), its status (Pending, Completed or Skipped) and the Seen v{seen} · current v{current} label. Statuses are display-only: nothing in the section calls a complete or skip endpoint.

New version. When the version the user went through is older than the current one (update_available), the row adds the New version to view badge and its group no longer counts it as completed. Such a guide is due again and starts by itself at its next trigger.

Step-managed flows. The rows of transaction_bulk_guide (4 steps) and import_guide (9 steps) add a collapsible list of their steps, each with its status, under a {completed}/{total} counter in which a skipped step counts as done and a step with a newer version does not. The row's own status summarizes its steps.

Replay per flow. The row button depends on the flow:

  • welcome → Replay arms a Welcome replay (onboarding.startReplay) and opens /welcome. There, Continue saves the chosen language, currency and avatar through the regular PUT /api/v1/settings/user without touching the Welcome status, and Exit tour saves nothing.
  • intro_tour → Replay starts the tour at once, in replay mode, from its opening scene (onboardingGuide.startIntroReplay()), and opens /dashboard.
  • every other flow → Replay at next trigger only arms the replay (onboardingGuide.armReplay(flow); for Import and Bulk, with all their steps), and a toast says the guide is ready in this browser. The guide starts the next time its page, modal or wizard asks for it. While armed, the row reads Ready in this browser: {flow} starts at its next trigger. and the button becomes Cancel activation (onboarding.clearReplay).

Replay all arms every flow in list order — Welcome with onboarding.startReplay, the intro with onboardingGuide.prepareIntroReplay(), all the others with armReplay — then opens /welcome. If one of them cannot be armed (for example when localStorage is unavailable), the section clears the replays it already armed, then shows the error. Every button is disabled while an action runs. When the progress could not be loaded at all, the list is replaced by the error and a Retry button (appBootstrap.load(true)).

docs.title: 👤 ProfileTab
docs.text:
Manages user profile information:

  • Avatar: Editable via ImagePickerWrapper → AssetPickerModal → crop
  • Username and Email: editable once the edit lock is open, each with its own save and undo (PUT /api/v1/auth/profile)
  • The email's password (Changing the Email): while the tab is unlocked and the email is another address than the stored one, a password input appears under the email's hint (profile-email-password, autocomplete="current-password", placeholder settings.currentPassword), described by profile-email-password-hint (settings.emailPasswordHint). Both email Saves and profile-save-all stay disabled while it is empty; the username's Saves do not wait for it. The email's request is {email, current_password}, the username's never carries the password. The password is emptied whenever the email is back to the stored address, after a save included
  • Only the capitals changed (P18, A-25): «another address» is decided by sameEmail() of lib/features/auth/emailCase.ts, which folds A–Z only, like the server's index on lower(email) (user_service.email_fold). The stored address in other A–Z capitals is still a modification (the row stays marked, the Saves are on, the new form is saved), but no password input appears and the request is {email} alone, without a current_password key (the server refuses an empty one). Letters outside A–Z compare as written: émile@… → Émile@… asks for the password
  • Refusals: CURRENT_PASSWORD_REQUIRED, CURRENT_PASSWORD_INVALID and, since lot A8b (C11), TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS, the 429 of the failed sign-in limit, are worded by the tab (PASSWORD_REFUSALS: settings.currentPasswordRequired, settings.currentPasswordIncorrect, settings.tooManyPasswordAttempts, Too many wrong passwords: wait a few minutes and try again.) and published on profile-error as data-error-code. The typed email stays; the password is emptied after the first two, and kept after TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS, since it may be right and waiting is all there is to do. Since lot A-21a, PASSWORD_REFUSALS also holds USERNAME_INVALID, a new username holding @ (see Which Account an Identifier Names): auth.validation.usernameNoAt, the key of the registration card's own check, published as data-error-code like the others, never the server's sentence nor settings.updateFailed; the username goes back to the stored value. Any other refusal shows the server's detail when it is a sentence (Email already registered), settings.updateFailed for any other detail (another code, a 422 list), and puts the field back to the stored value. The banner clears after 5 seconds
  • Password change: opens PasswordChangeModal (features/settings/PasswordChangeModal.svelte): the current password, the new one with PasswordStrength under it, and the confirmation. The modal binds PasswordStrength's valid (bind:valid={passwordMeetsRules}) and keeps no copy of the password rules: password-change-submit stays disabled until the three fields are filled, the rules hold and the confirmation matches. A refusal with status 429 whose detail is {error_code: "TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS", …}, the failed sign-in limit, shows settings.tooManyPasswordAttempts (lot A8b, C11), and the three fields keep what was typed; a 429 with another code, with a sentence or with a proxy's page, and TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS on another status, go on to the cases below. A refusal whose detail is {error_code: "PASSWORD_TOO_WEAK", …} shows auth.validation.passwordTooWeak; the plain-string details of a wrong current password (incorrect) and of a new password equal to it (different) show settings.currentPasswordIncorrect and settings.passwordMustBeDifferent; anything else, the message trySave extracts, settings.passwordChangeFailed when it finds none. An object detail is never lower-cased as a string: before A6c that threw
  • Delete account: delete-account-button opens the AccountDeletionDialog in self mode, with testIdPrefix="profile-delete"; once the account is deleted, the tab calls auth.logout() and goes to /
  • Edit mode toggle to prevent accidental changes

Tests of the email's password: tabs/ProfileTab.test.ts (./dev.py test front-utility component-unit; since A8b also the limit's TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS through the row's Save and through profile-save-all: the key and its code on the banner, the new email and the typed password kept, and three other 429s worded as any other refusal), and the «A6e» block of frontend/e2e/settings.spec.ts (./dev.py test front-utility settings) on the lane's real backend, with a throwaway account and a second browser context signed in before the change, and signed out by it. The password change: PasswordChangeModal.test.ts, in the same component-unit action (what enables Save, what reaches the server, the refusals with PASSWORD_TOO_WEAK among them, the rules taken from PasswordStrength, and the limit's 429: the key, never the server's sentence, the fields kept and usable, no success and no toast).

docs.title: 🌍 GlobalSettingsTab (administrators only)
docs.text:
System-wide configuration with lock toggle:

  • Max file upload size
  • Registration mode: a select with three options, open, invite and disabled (settings.registrationModes.*: Open, By invitation, Closed)
  • Scheduler configuration and new-user defaults
  • Other app-wide settings

Only a superuser has this tab (lot N69-2, decision D4 a): its entry in the tab registry (admin, labelled Global Settings) has visible: (ctx) => ctx.isSuperuser, like every other member of the administration group, of which it is the first. A regular user has no group at all, and a ?tab=admin opens their profile (The page). The entry still passes canEdit through props: (ctx) => ({canEdit: ctx.isSuperuser}), so the tab always gets canEdit: true on screen; without canEdit it would show a read-only indicator (settings-readonly-indicator) instead of the lock toggle (settings-lock-toggle) and the bulk Save/Undo/Reset actions, a branch no longer reached from the interface and kept until a cleanup. Hiding the tab hides no value: the app still reads the global settings for every signed-in user, through GET /api/v1/settings/global (Settings System).

Space limit (lot B10). storage_limit_mb, in the Memory category, is a SettingNumber (default 0, no limit), named and explained as in Files › Advanced (storage.limit.label, storage.limit.hint, through the label and hint override maps). The hosting provider can fix it with LIBREFOLIO_STORAGE_LIMIT_MB; the tab learns it from the same answer as the space bar, limit_locked of GET /backup/instance/storage (getInstanceStorage): the field is then disabled even with the tab unlocked, its hint becomes storage.limit.locked, Reset All to Defaults skips it, and its card global-setting-storage_limit_mb carries data-locked="true" ("false" otherwise). Open the settings on a refusal of the limit links /settings/admin/global?setting=storage_limit_mb (STORAGE_LIMIT_SETTINGS_HREF): once the list is in, ?setting=<key> selects the row's category, brings the row into view and highlights it (data-highlighted="true"), once per value. The lock stays closed: the administrator opens it by hand (the developer's choice). A key the tab hides, or no row, changes nothing.

For the three display defaults (default_language, default_currency, default_theme) the tab reuses the same shared Setting* wrappers as the PreferencesTab, passing the embedded prop (see below) so they sit inside the tab's own cards without double separators.

Registration mode. registration_mode, in the Security category, is a SettingSelect (default invite, SETTING_DEFAULTS, as in GLOBAL_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS: Reset to Default and Reset All to Defaults propose invite, also on an upgraded instance that kept open). The server variable LIBREFOLIO_REGISTRATION can pin it (Registration Modes); the tab learns it from the instance configuration, instanceConfig.config.accounts.registration_locked:

  • Locked by the variable: the select shows the mode in force, instanceConfig.config.accounts.registration_mode, not the stored row; it is disabled even with the tab unlocked; its hint becomes settings.lockedByEnv with {variable: LIBREFOLIO_REGISTRATION} (Set on the server by LIBREFOLIO_REGISTRATION: change it there.); and Reset All to Defaults skips it. Its card, global-setting-registration_mode, carries data-locked="true" ("false" otherwise).
  • A save that meets the lock anyway — for example before the configuration arrived — gets 409 SETTING_LOCKED_BY_ENV; the tab shows settings.lockedByEnv with the variable of the answer.
  • After a save that includes registration_mode, alone or with Save All, the tab calls instanceConfig.load({force: true}), so the login page's Register here, the /invite page, the open-registration warning and the Security tab's finding of the same name, with its badge, follow the new mode on this page load.

docs.title: 🧹 CachePanel
docs.text: CachePanel.svelte shows the status of every named backend cache (the theine registry): name, current_size / maxsize, and a human-formatted TTL, refreshed on demand. It sits in the Memory category of the Global Settings tab, so only administrators see it since lot N69-2, although GET /api/v1/settings/cache/status still answers any authenticated user; the per-cache Clear and Clear all buttons appear only when the canEdit prop is set (it mirrors the Global-settings lock). Both clear actions pass through a danger confirmation modal — after a clear, the next fetch hits the providers again. Backend contract: Cache Registry & Admin.

docs.title: 👥 UsersTab
docs.text:
lib/features/settings/tabs/UsersTab.svelte, the registry's users entry: administrators only, no props. The accounts of the instance, every account link (lot UA3) and the places taken. User side: Users & Invitations; backend: Administrator API.

  • Load: on mount, GET /users and GET /users/account-links in parallel (list_accounts_api_v1_users_get, list_account_links_api_v1_users_account_links_get); the accounts and usage come from the first, the links from the second, split by their state: open, or closed (used, expired, revoked). The root, users-tab, carries data-busy ('true' while the lists load, at mount and after every action; aria-busy too). A failed load shows settings.usersTab.errors.load above the list, with an error toast.
  • Every action reloads: perform() runs the call, notifies its outcome, then calls load() whether it succeeded or not. The tab never updates a row by itself: it shows the backend's answer. The invitation and reset-link dialogs reload when they close (the new link is an open row), the deletion dialog after a deletion.
  • Header: users-usage with data-used and data-max (empty without a limit), drawn with settings.usersTab.usage ({used} / {max} accounts) or usageUnlimited. users-billing-link (target="_blank", rel="noopener noreferrer") only when usage.billing_url is set. The instance is full when max_users is set and used >= max_users: banner users-limit-banner (role="status"), with users-limit-billing-link when there is a billing URL.
  • Invite (users-invite-button) is disabled with data-disabled-reason: registration-disabled when instanceConfig.config.accounts.registration_mode is disabled, checked first as the backend does, else limit when the instance is full. With registration-disabled, users-invite-blocked says why: settings.usersTab.invite.blockedLocked, naming LIBREFOLIO_REGISTRATION, when registration_locked; settings.usersTab.invite.blocked otherwise.
  • Accounts (users-accounts): one UserRow per account, in the backend's order. isSelf compares the account with $currentUser.id; isOnlyActiveAdmin is true for the account that is the only one with is_superuser and is_active.
  • Account links (users-links): two AccountLinksTable, the open links (users-links-open) and, inside a FoldPanel folded by default (users-links-closed-fold, its title Closed links ({count})), the closed ones (users-links-closed).
  • Confirmations: one ConfirmModal, testId="users-confirm" (on its header; its buttons are confirm-modal-confirm and confirm-modal-cancel), for deactivate, cancel the setup link, promote, demote, sign out everywhere, restart the guides and revoke a link; danger for deactivate, cancel the setup link, demote and revoke. Title and message come from settings.usersTab.confirm.<kind>.*, the kind in camelCase (cancelSetup, signOut, revokeLink…), with {username}, or {type} and {target} for a link (its account, else its address, else settings.usersTab.links.anyone). Reactivate runs at once; the reset link and the deletion open their own dialogs.
  • Cancel the setup link (cancel-setup, lot A-43), for the initial administrator waiting for its setup: once confirmed, PATCH /users/{id} {is_active: false, cancel_setup: true}, which revokes its setup links (Cancelling the setup link). The row still reads Waiting for setup afterwards, so a success toast (settings.usersTab.toasts.setupCancelled, The setup link of {username} no longer works.) tells what changed. cancel_setup (lot A-51) makes the request a cancellation and nothing else, never the deactivation its is_active: false alone would be: when the administrator completed its setup after the list was loaded, the backend answers 409 SETUP_COMPLETED and changes nothing. The tab then shows settings.usersTab.errors.SETUP_COMPLETED in an error toast (This administrator completed its setup in the meantime: nothing was changed.), notifies accounts.action.failed with no success event, and reloads: the row shows the account active (A setup completed meanwhile).
Action Call Event on success Toast deactivate PATCH /users/{id} {is_active: false} accounts.user.deactivated — cancel the setup link PATCH /users/{id} {is_active: false, cancel_setup: true} accounts.user.setup-cancelled success reactivate PATCH /users/{id} {is_active: true} accounts.user.reactivated — promote PATCH /users/{id} {is_superuser: true} accounts.user.promoted — demote PATCH /users/{id} {is_superuser: false} accounts.user.demoted — sign out everywhere POST /users/{id}/sessions/revoke accounts.user.sessions-revoked success restart the guides POST /users/{id}/onboarding/reset, body null: every flow accounts.user.onboarding-reset success revoke a link DELETE /users/account-links/{link_id} accounts.link.revoked — invite InviteDialog: POST /users/invites accounts.invite.created — reset link ResetLinkDialog: POST /users/{id}/password-reset-link accounts.reset-link.created success delete AccountDeletionDialog: DELETE /users/{id} accounts.user.deleted success

App events. Every outcome goes through notify() (lib/stores/app/notify.svelte.ts), which keeps it in window.__lf.events, where the E2E reads it (frontend/e2e/fixtures/app-events.ts); the toast, when there is one, is a field of the same call.

Event detail accounts.user.deactivated, setup-cancelled, reactivated, promoted, demoted, sessions-revoked, onboarding-reset {user_id} accounts.link.revoked {link_id, purpose} accounts.invite.created {invite_id, grants_admin} accounts.reset-link.created {user_id} accounts.user.deleted {user_id, brokers_deleted, mode} accounts.address.checked {state, purpose}, without a toast (LinkShare) accounts.link.copied {purpose}, with a success toast (LinkShare) accounts.action.failed {action, code}, plus user_id, or link_id and purpose, when there is one, always with an error toast. action is load, deactivate, cancel-setup, reactivate, promote, demote, sign-out, restart-guides, revoke-link, invite, reset-link or delete; code comes from accountErrors.ts

docs.title: UserRow
docs.text:
lib/features/settings/users/UserRow.svelte. Props: account (AdminAccount, the GET /users item, with holds_place, pending_setup, pending_verification and avatar_url when they are sent: all four optional in users/types.ts), isSelf, isOnlyActiveAdmin, full, onAction(action, account).

  • The <li> is users-row, with data-user-id, data-username, data-active, data-admin, data-pending-setup, data-pending-verification, data-protected and data-self ("true" or "false"; data-pending-setup is "false" when the field is absent, the answer of an older server; data-pending-verification is the derived state of an account waiting for its email verification, described below, not the raw flag).
  • users-row-toggle, a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, shows the chevron, the account's avatar, the username, the badges (settings.usersTab.badges.you, admin, inactive, with the test id users-badge-inactive, protected, and the two of a waiting account below), the email and settings.usersTab.createdOn, and opens or closes the panel of actions under the row.
  • The avatar (lot N69-4, decision D8 a): a UserAvatar right after the chevron, given account.avatar_url ?? null, its root users-row-avatar with data-avatar="image" or "initial": an image uploaded to the app asked for as its 48×48 preview, an address elsewhere as it is, and the username's initial in a neutral circle for an account without one, avatar_url null or absent.
  • The own row (isSelf) has no action: users-self-hint, with a link to /settings/profile (settingsTabHref('profile')).
  • The buttons: users-action-deactivate for an active account or users-action-reactivate for an inactive one, users-action-cancel-setup in its place for an account with pending_setup; users-action-demote for an administrator or users-action-promote for a regular account; then users-action-reset-link, users-action-sign-out, users-action-restart-guides and users-action-delete.

  • An account waiting for its setup (pending_setup, the initial administrator whose setup link was never used, nor the account set up another way): the badge users-badge-pending-setup (settings.usersTab.badges.pendingSetup, Waiting for setup, in the tab's neutral style) in place of inactive; no users-action-reactivate, and so no limit reason on a full instance; under the buttons, users-pending-setup-hint (settings.usersTab.pendingSetupHint): the account activates through its setup link, and a lost link is replaced with dev.py user setup-link or by the hosting provider. The backend refuses its reactivation anyway, with 409 PENDING_SETUP (Account Errors). Since lot A-43:

    • users-action-cancel-setup (settings.usersTab.actions.cancelSetup, Cancel setup link, the Link2Off icon, the style of the row's other actions) stands where Reactivate would, and hands the account to onAction('cancel-setup', account): the tab confirms, then cancels (UsersTab). On a protected account it is turned off with the reason protected (cancelReason), shown under the buttons as for Deactivate: the backend refuses the cancellation with 409 ACCOUNT_PROTECTED;
    • users-action-demote is turned off with the reason pending-setup (settings.usersTab.reasons.pendingSetup): the account keeps its role until its setup, and the backend refuses its demotion with 409 PENDING_SETUP too;
    • users-action-delete stays enabled, without the demote-first reason: the backend deletes the waiting administrator directly (Deleting an Account).

    Its other buttons are those of any inactive account.

  • An account waiting for its email verification (pending_verification, lot E-7, the developer's decisions of 21/10/2026): the row derives pendingVerification = account.pending_verification === true && !account.is_active && !pendingSetup, so an active account that arrives with the flag is drawn as any active account, and the setup's wait wins over it. Then:

    • the badge users-badge-pending-verification (settings.usersTab.badges.pendingVerification, Waiting for verification, in the tab's neutral style) is drawn in place of inactive, whose users-badge-inactive is then absent; its title is the hover hint settings.usersTab.pendingVerificationHint. holds_place takes no part in it: the badge is the same for a live link and for one that has expired, and an older server that sends no flag leaves the row with Deactivated;
    • the opened panel shows users-pending-verification-hint, the same settings.usersTab.pendingVerificationHint, under the buttons (the setup's users-pending-setup-hint takes that place for pending_setup);
    • the buttons are those of any inactive account, users-action-reactivate included: the badge changes what the row says, not what it offers. On a full instance Reactivate is turned off with the limit reason unless holds_place, so a waiting account whose link has expired reads Waiting for verification with a Reactivate turned off.

A button the backend would certainly refuse is disabled, with data-disabled-reason; the first condition that holds gives the reason:

Button data-disabled-reason users-action-deactivate protected when account.protected; last-admin when the account is an administrator and isOnlyActiveAdmin users-action-reactivate limit when full, unless account.holds_place: an account waiting for its email verification with a live link already holds its place (Email Verification); pending_verification changes nothing here, so once the link has expired the reason comes back. Never drawn for an account with pending_setup users-action-cancel-setup protected when account.protected: the backend refuses the cancellation of a protected account (409 ACCOUNT_PROTECTED). Drawn only for an account with pending_setup users-action-demote protected when account.protected; pending-setup when the account has pending_setup; last-admin when the account is active and isOnlyActiveAdmin users-action-delete protected when account.protected; demote-first when the account is an administrator, active or not, unless it has pending_setup

Promote, the reset link, sign out everywhere and restart the guides are never disabled. Under the buttons, one line per distinct reason (settings.usersTab.reasons.*). The backend stays the authority: last-admin never shows in a live session, as whoever reads the tab is an active administrator and their own row has no actions, so the 409 LAST_ADMIN of the server covers what the row cannot see.

docs.title: AccountLinksTable
docs.text:
lib/features/settings/users/AccountLinksTable.svelte (lot UA3). Props: links (AccountLink[], the GET /users/account-links items, users/types.ts), variant (open or closed), testId, isLoading?, onRevoke?(link). A DataTable with its own ColumnVisibilityToggle: sorting, Excel-style column filters, column visibility, widths and order kept per table (storageKey settings.users.accountLinks.<variant>), pagination by 10; no selection. The root carries testId and data-count; each row data-row-id (the link's id).

Column Cell Filter Type AccountLinkTypeBadge: a neutral pill, one lucide icon per purpose (account-link-type, data-purpose), settings.usersTab.links.purpose.<purpose> enum of the five purposes For the account's username (→ new address for an email_change), else the address, else settings.usersTab.links.anyone; the Admin badge (account-link-admin) for an invitation that grants it text Created by created_by_username, — without one text Created, Expires date and time date range State AccountLinkStateCell (account-link-state, data-state): the state pill on the state roles (open info, used success, expired warning, revoked neutral), then, closed, its date (account-link-state-detail) and, used, settings.usersTab.links.usedBy enum of the variant's states

The open table's row menu has Revoke (account-link-revoke) on the rows whose revocable the backend set; the tab confirms it. The tables decide nothing: the state and revocable are the backend's.

docs.title: Invitations and Reset Links
docs.text:
• InviteDialog.svelte: props open, onClose, onCreated?(response). A ModalBase (testId="users-invite-dialog", trapFocus) whose form starts empty at every opening: users-invite-email (sent trimmed, and only when not blank), users-invite-admin (grants_admin), users-invite-create, users-invite-cancel. A success shows LinkShare with purpose="invite", the response's path and url, expiresAt from the invitation and context: {email}; users-invite-done calls onClose, then onCreated. A refusal stays on the form: users-invite-error, with data-error-code.
  • ResetLinkDialog.svelte: props open, account: {id, username}, onClose. It opens on its explanation (settings.usersTab.reset.message) with users-reset-create and users-reset-cancel; a success shows LinkShare with purpose="password_reset" and context: {username, userId}, closed by users-reset-close. A failure shows users-reset-error, with data-error-code.

docs.title: LinkShare
docs.text:
lib/features/settings/users/LinkShare.svelte: the panel both dialogs share a link through. Props: purpose (LinkPurpose; the dialogs pass invite or password_reset), path (the page with the token in the fragment, as the backend's token_path() builds it), url (LIBREFOLIO_PUBLIC_URL followed by path, or null), expiresAt, context? ({username?, email?, userId?}). The root is link-share, with data-purpose.

  • Address: link-share-address, editable, starts from initialBase(url, path, window.location.origin) (users/linkShare.ts): the part of url before path when url ends with it — the public address, with the path prefix of a reverse proxy — otherwise the browser's origin; trailing slashes removed either way.
  • Link: link-share-link, read-only, is composeLink(address, path): the normalized address followed by path, character for character. Not a URL resolution, which would drop a path prefix, and no re-encoding of the token.
  • Expiry: link-share-expires, with data-expires-at.
  • Check: link-share-probe, whose data-state is one of:
data-state When idle The address, once normalized, is the starting one: no check checking 500 ms after the last keystroke on a changed address, while checkAddress() runs match, mismatch, unverifiable The verdict of the check invalid normalizeBase() refuses the address: not an absolute http: or https: URL, or with credentials, a ? or a #. No check runs, and link-share-copy is disabled

A newer edit outruns an older check: each run takes a generation number, and the verdict of a stale one is dropped. Each verdict is notified as accounts.address.checked, without a toast.

checkAddress(base, {issueNonce, fetchImpl?, timeoutMs?}) (users/addressProbe.ts) never throws. The nonce comes from the Zodios client (issue_address_probe_api_v1_users_address_probe_post, POST /users/address-probe); then GET <base>/api/v1/auth/address-probe?nonce=… (probeUrl()) goes through a bare fetch — the global one, read at call time, or fetchImpl — called as a plain function, with {method: 'GET', credentials: 'omit', cache: 'no-store', referrerPolicy: 'no-referrer', signal} and nothing else: no headers, no body, no mode. It must stay a CORS simple request, as the backend's CORSMiddleware refuses every preflight. A 2xx with {match: true} is match, with {match: false} mismatch; anything else is unverifiable: the nonce refused, a network or CORS error, mixed content, a local-network permission denied, another status, a body that is not JSON or has no boolean match, or PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS (8 s) passed, when the request is aborted. The server's half: Address Probe.

  • Copy: link-share-copy writes the link with writeTextToClipboard() ($lib/utils/clipboard: the Clipboard API, then the legacy copy) and notifies accounts.link.copied with a success toast (settings.linkShare.copied). When neither transport works, the link input is focused and selected, for a copy by hand. The button is disabled only in invalid.
  • Extra actions: link-share-actions draws the registered actions, see below.

docs.title: Link-Share Actions Registry
docs.text:
lib/features/settings/users/linkShareActions.ts holds LINK_SHARE_ACTIONS: LinkShareAction[], with one entry since workstream E's lot E4, {id: 'send-by-email', component: SendLinkByEmail, visible: () => sendByEmailVisible()}: «Send by email», shown while email.links is true (Send by Email).
