An entry is {id, component, visible?}: component receives {link, purpose, context} (LinkShareActionProps), and visible({purpose, context}) filters it; without visible the action is always shown. visibleLinkShareActions(purpose, context) returns the visible ones in registry order, and LinkShare draws each in link-share-actions. Adding an action is one line in the list, as «Send by email» shows; the dialogs do not change:

// `MyAction` stands for your own component
export const LINK_SHARE_ACTIONS: LinkShareAction[] = [
    {id: 'my-action', component: MyAction, visible: ({purpose}) => purpose === 'invite'},
];

docs.title: Account Errors
docs.text:
lib/features/settings/users/accountErrors.ts turns a failed call into what the UI shows, for the tab, its dialogs and the deletion dialog. describeAccountError(error, action?) returns {code, key, params?, message?}; accountErrorText(error, $_) returns message when there is one, the translated key otherwise.

Answer code Shown detail.error_code among LAST_ADMIN, USER_LIMIT_REACHED, REGISTRATION_DISABLED, ACCOUNT_PROTECTED, SELF_DELETION, DEMOTE_FIRST, PENDING_SETUP, SETUP_COMPLETED (ACCOUNT_ERROR_CODES) that code settings.usersTab.errors.<code>, but for LAST_ADMIN on a deletion (next row); a detail.billing_url is passed as params.billingUrl. PENDING_SETUP is the 409 of a reactivation or, since lot A-43, a demotion of the initial administrator waiting for its setup: a list loaded earlier may still offer either. SETUP_COMPLETED (lot A-51) is the 409 of a cancellation of a setup link that the administrator spent since the list was loaded detail.error_code LAST_ADMIN on a deletion (action is 'delete', lot A-16) LAST_ADMIN settings.usersTab.errors.LAST_ADMIN_DELETION, which says to make another account an administrator first: on a deletion it can only be the 400 of DELETE /auth/users/me, the last active administrator deleting their own account, as another administrator's deletion answers 409 DEMOTE_FIRST. Without 'delete', the 409 LAST_ADMIN of a deactivation or a demotion keeps settings.usersTab.errors.LAST_ADMIN 404 NOT_FOUND settings.usersTab.errors.NOT_FOUND 422 INVALID_INPUT settings.usersTab.errors.INVALID_INPUT 500 of a deletion (action is 'delete') DELETION_FAILED settings.usersTab.errors.DELETION_FAILED: nothing was deleted 400 or 409 whose detail is a sentence null The server's sentence, as it is: a fallback for a refusal that carries no code. Every 400 and 409 of the calls these components make carries one today Anything else null settings.usersTab.errors.generic

docs.title: 🗑️ AccountDeletionDialog
docs.text:
lib/features/settings/AccountDeletionDialog.svelte: the one dialog for deleting an account, one's own from ProfileTab or another's from UsersTab. A ModalBase with trapFocus. The rule it shows and applies is the backend's: Deleting an Account.

Prop Role open Opens the dialog; every opening loads the preview again and clears the typed name mode 'self' or 'admin' account {id, username, is_active} testIdPrefix The prefix p of every test id: profile-delete in the Profile tab, users-delete in the Users tab onClose Closes the dialog: cancel, a close request of ModalBase, or once Deactivate is done onDeleted(result) After a deletion, with {user_id, brokers_deleted}, the number of brokers that went onDeactivate? Administrators only: deactivate the account instead mode="self" mode="admin" Preview GET /auth/users/me/deletion-preview GET /users/{id}/deletion-preview Deletion DELETE /auth/users/me DELETE /users/{id} Title and warning settings.deleteAccountConfirm, settings.deleteAccountWarning settings.accountDeletion.titleAdmin, settings.accountDeletion.warningAdmin After a deletion ProfileTab: auth.logout(), then / UsersTab: closes the dialog, reloads
  • Deactivate first: in admin mode, for an active account and with onDeactivate given, the dialog opens with Deactivate instead? and ${p}-deactivate, which awaits onDeactivate(), then closes. The Users tab passes its own deactivation (PATCH {is_active: false}, accounts.user.deactivated, reload).
  • Preview (${p}-preview; ${p}-dialog carries data-busy while it loads): ${p}-broker-deleted, with data-broker-id and data-transactions, for each broker that goes (or settings.accountDeletion.noBrokersDeleted); ${p}-broker-left, with data-broker-id and data-role (OWNER, EDITOR or VIEWER), for each broker where only the access goes; ${p}-unpaired, with data-count, when transfers_unpaired is above 0.
  • Confirmation: ${p}-confirm-input stays disabled until the preview is in; ${p}-confirm (settings.deleteAccountPermanently) is enabled only while the typed text equals the username exactly. ${p}-cancel closes. A failed preview shows settings.accountDeletion.previewFailed in ${p}-error, and the deletion stays out of reach.
  • Outcome: a success notifies accounts.user.deleted, with a success toast (settings.accountDeletion.deletedSelf, or deletedAdmin with {username, count}), then calls onDeleted; brokers_deleted is counted from the preview, as the deletion answers no numbers. A failure shows ${p}-error, with data-error-code, and notifies accounts.action.failed with an error toast. The last active administrator deleting their own account gets the 400 LAST_ADMIN (lot A-16), shown as settings.usersTab.errors.LAST_ADMIN_DELETION, You are the last active administrator: make another account an administrator before deleting yours., and the dialog stays open.

docs.title: 🧪 Users Tab and Account Deletion Tests
docs.text:
• ./dev.py test front-utility core-unit: users/linkShare.test.ts (initialBase, composeLink), users/addressProbe.test.ts (normalizeBase, probeUrl, and checkAddress: the request options key by key, every verdict, the deadline on fake timers, never the network), users/accountErrors.test.ts (every code of ACCOUNT_ERROR_CODES, PENDING_SETUP included, the answers read from the status, and each key a sentence in the four catalogues; AERR-13 and AERR-14, lot A-51: the 409 SETUP_COMPLETED worded by its key, never the server's sentence; AERR-15 to AERR-19, lot A-16: the 400 LAST_ADMIN of a deletion worded by LAST_ADMIN_DELETION, the 409 LAST_ADMIN of the other actions keeping LAST_ADMIN), and the users row of settingsTabs.test.ts.
  • ./dev.py test front-utility component-unit: tabs/UsersTab.test.ts (the tab against a mocked server that changes as the backend would; UTAB-55 to UTAB-60, lot A-43: the cancellation of a setup link confirmed as danger, its one PATCH, event and toast, a dismissed confirmation that sends nothing, a stale demotion's PENDING_SETUP, and the keys in the four catalogues; UTAB-61 and UTAB-62, lot A-51: the cancellation's body exactly {is_active: false, cancel_setup: true}, and a 409 SETUP_COMPLETED worded by its key, with no success, the row reloaded active), users/LinkShare.component.test.ts (not LinkShare.test.ts: linkShare.test.ts is in the same folder, and macOS volumes ignore case), users/InviteDialog.test.ts, users/ResetLinkDialog.test.ts, users/UserRow.pendingSetup.test.ts (the row of an account waiting for its setup: the badge, data-pending-setup, no Reactivate and no limit reason, the hint; since lot A-43, UPS-12 to UPS-23: users-action-cancel-setup in its place, turned off with protected on a protected account (UPS-23), users-action-demote off with pending-setup, users-action-delete enabled; every other row unchanged), users/UserRow.verification.test.ts (UVR-01 to UVR-03, lot E5b: Reactivate on a full instance usable with holds_place, off with limit without it; UVR-04 to UVR-11, lot E-7: the badge users-badge-pending-verification with its hover hint in place of users-badge-inactive, for a live link, an expired one and holds_place absent alike; data-pending-verification as the derived state; an inactive account without the flag keeping Deactivated; the hint in the opened panel, with Reactivate still offered, usable on a full instance only with a live link; pending_setup winning over the flag; an active account with the flag drawn with no badge), users/UserRow.avatar.test.ts (URA-01 to URA-04, lot N69-4: the avatar in the toggle, between the chevron and the username, an uploaded image asked for as its 48×48 preview, an address as it is, the initial without one, and the toggle still opening its panel), AccountDeletionDialog.test.ts (both modes; ADEL-28 and ADEL-29, lot A-16: a refused own deletion worded in the interface language, the 400 LAST_ADMIN as LAST_ADMIN_DELETION with the dialog left open, the 500 as DELETION_FAILED) and tabs/ProfileTab.test.ts.
  • ./dev.py test front-utility admin-users (frontend/e2e/settings/admin-users.spec.ts): the tab on the lane's real backend, e2e_test_admin acting on disposable accounts only. Only an administrator has the tab; the own row has no action; deactivate and reactivate, promote and demote; a reset link and an invitation, each token inspected live, the invitation then revoked; the address check (match on the lane's other loopback origin, through the real CORS path, unverifiable on a closed port, invalid for ftp://, mismatch from a stubbed stranger, back to idle); a deletion with its preview; sign out everywhere; the guides restarted. The deletion of one's own account through the Profile tab is ./dev.py test front-user account-deletion (frontend/e2e/brokers/account-deletion.spec.ts).

docs.title: 🛡️ SecurityTab
docs.text:
lib/features/settings/security/, the registry's security entry (lot A8b): administrators only, no props, the only tab with a badge and a prefetch. It lists the configuration checks that GET /api/v1/security/checks evaluates, and one check that only the browser can make, most severe first. Administrator side: «Security» in Global Settings.

File Role securityChecksApi.ts The seam over the generated client: fetchSecurityChecks() calls list_security_checks_api_v1_security_checks_get once and resolves to the items of the answer as they came, SecurityCheck[] ({check_id, severity, i18n_key, detail}, severity one of ok, info, warning, error); a refusal or a network error propagates securityFindings.ts Pure: what the tab lists, from the server's checks and from what only the browser knows securityChecks.svelte.ts The state: one read per page load, shared by the tab, the badges and, since lot N69b, the sidebar's dot SecurityTab.svelte The body

The findings. securityFindings(checks, browser), where browser is {registrationMode, registrationLocked, hostname}, returns {attention, passed}, two lists of SecurityFinding, {id, severity, messageKey, params, action?, source}; it changes neither of its inputs.

  • attention: every check that is not ok, its check_id as id, its i18n_key as messageKey, a copy of its detail as params, source: 'server'; sorted error → warning → info by a stable sort, so that within a severity the server's order holds.
  • The browser's own check: openRegistrationNoticeFor({isAdmin: true, ...browser}) (Open-Registration Warning), registration open reached through a host that isLocalHost() does not call local. Its notice becomes a warning with the notice's id (accounts.openRegistration), messageKey, params ({} today) and action, source: 'browser', and nothing else of it (no dismissible). Pushed after the server's findings, the stable sort puts it after the server's warnings and before the infos. With the mode pinned by LIBREFOLIO_REGISTRATION the notice is auth.notices.openRegistrationLocked, without an action. The finding holds whether or not the notice was closed: the tab does not read the instance notices.
  • passed: the ok checks, in the server's order, with the severity info and never an action; their message is the check's own ok sentence.
  • Actions, the in-app links where a setting of the app fixes the finding (SERVER_ACTIONS): email.smtp, email.smtp_encryption and email.links → settings.securityTab.openEmail (Open the Email tab), /settings/admin/email; platform.plugin_secrets → settings.securityTab.openPlugins (Open the plugin settings), /settings/plugins; the browser's finding → its notice's action, auth.notices.openRegistrationAction (Change who can sign up), /settings/admin/global. The other checks are fixed in the server's configuration: no link.
  • attentionCount(findings): the errors and the warnings of attention, the browser's included, never an info. It is the badge.
  • attentionSeverity(findings) (lot N69b): how serious what attentionCount counts is: 'error' when an attention finding is an error, wherever it sits in the list, else 'warning' when one is a warning, else null. An info never counts, so it is null exactly when attentionCount is 0. It changes nothing it reads. It is the colour of the sidebar's dot.

The state. createSecurityChecks({fetch?, browser?}) builds a store; securityChecks is the app's, created at import, asking nothing until it is told to. Its getters are reactive: status (idle, loading, ready or error), checks, answered (true once a read has succeeded), findings, attentionCount and attentionSeverity, which are securityFindings(checks, browser()), its count and its severity once answered; empty lists, 0 and null before.

  • ensureLoaded() reads once: nothing while a read is under way, whose promise concurrent calls share, nor once ready; again after a failure. There is no retry of its own.
  • reload() always reads, sharing a read under way. The last checks stay listed meanwhile, and after a failure, which only sets status to error.
  • The default browser() takes the registration from instanceConfig.config.accounts only once instanceConfig.loaded: before, the configuration in force is the default one, whose mode is open, and an invite-only instance would warn for nothing. The host is window.location.hostname. As findings is computed on each read, the browser's finding follows instanceConfig: a save of registration_mode in GlobalSettingsTab, which reloads it, adds or removes the finding, badge and dot included, without a new request.
  • The default fetch is fetchSecurityChecks().

The badge. The registry's security entry reads securityChecks.attentionCount as its badge, summed on the administration entry, and its prefetch calls securityChecks.ensureLoaded() for an administrator, nothing for a user. The page runs the prefetch when it opens, so the number shows before the tab is opened; the tab's own onMount calls ensureLoaded() too. Since lot N69b the sidebar's connection line has usually asked already, on the first page of the load (The sidebar's dot): the prefetch and the tab then share its read, or read nothing once it has succeeded. The store lives as long as the page load: leaving Settings and coming back reads nothing again (unless the last read failed), «check again» or a reload of the page does.

The body. SecurityTab.svelte, prop checks: the store to show, securityChecks unless a test hands its own. The root, security-tab, carries data-status (the store's status), and data-busy and aria-busy, true while a read runs.

  • Header: settings.securityTab.title (Security checks), settings.securityTab.description, and Check again (security-refresh, settings.securityTab.refresh), which calls reload(), disabled while a read runs, its icon spinning.
  • Before the first answer (idle or loading): security-loading, two pulsing placeholder rows.
  • A failed read: security-load-error, role="alert", settings.securityTab.loadError (The security checks could not be loaded.) with Try again (security-retry, reload()). After a failed «check again», the last findings stay listed under it.
  • The findings: one security-finding per attention finding, with data-check-id and data-severity: the severity's icon (AlertCircle, AlertTriangle, Info, hidden from screen readers), the severity in words for screen readers only (sr-only, settings.securityTab.severity.error, .warning, .info: Error, Warning, Information, then a colon), the message $_(messageKey, {values: params}), and the action as a link (security-finding-action).
  • The help of a check (FB-27): CheckHelp.svelte (features/instance/components/) on every finding and passed check, from checkGuides.json: a guide shows the «Guide» DocsLink (security-guide); a support check that has not passed shows «Contact support» (check-support, settings.securityTab.support), a link to the instance's LIBREFOLIO_SUPPORT_URL with the report of buildCheckReport() (code, severity, instance address, version, date); without a usable address, a line, check-support-missing (settings.securityTab.supportMissing), never a GitHub issue. See The Checks on Demand.
  • No finding: security-all-clear, settings.securityTab.allClear (Nothing needs your attention.). An info is a finding, so it is not all clear.
  • The passed checks: a closed <details>, security-passed, whose summary counts them (a neutral chip and settings.securityTab.passed, an ICU plural: 1 check passed, N checks passed), with one security-passed-check (data-check-id) per ok check.
  • Colours: roles only, after the state convention of STATUS_TONES (lib/theme/toneClasses.ts), written in the component: a tint per severity, bg-lf-X-soft text-lf-X-on-soft border-lf-X-line with X danger, warning or info (success for the all-clear), and a neutral chip, bg-lf-neutral text-lf-secondary, for the count of the passed checks.

Tests: ./dev.py test front-utility core-unit runs security/securityChecksApi.test.ts (one call of the generated client, its items as they came, an empty answer, a failure that propagates), security/securityFindings.test.ts (the order by severity and within one, the passed checks, which findings link where, the browser's finding against openRegistrationNoticeFor() for every mode, pin and host, the inputs left as they were, attentionCount; since lot N69b, attentionSeverity: an error wherever it sits among warnings, warnings with or without infos, null for infos only or for nothing, null exactly when attentionCount is 0 on what securityFindings lists, the browser's warning included, a frozen list left as it was) and security/securityChecks.test.ts (idle at creation, ensureLoaded() once and shared, reload() keeping the last checks, the failures, the findings following the browser's state, the reactive getters, the defaults: the generated client, instanceConfig and the page's host; since lot N69b, the getter attentionSeverity: null before the first answer, even after a failed read, then the most severe of each answer, a reactive read following reload() and the browser's state). ./dev.py test front-utility component-unit runs security/SecurityTab.test.ts (the store it is given, the placeholder, the findings and their words, the links, the all-clear, the passed checks, «check again», the failures, colour roles only, every key a message of the four catalogues).

docs.title: The sidebar's dot
docs.text:
Lot N69b (point 1 of N69; decisions D1 a, D2 a, D3 a) shows an administrator the tab's count from every page of the app shell: as a dot on the sidebar's connection line, lib/components/layout/ConnectionSecurityIndicator.svelte (plan 36), and, on a phone, on the menu button of Header.svelte. Both only read securityChecks and the auth store. Neither has a branch for the managed profile (D1 a): the dot is the same there.

  • Who sees it. isAdmin is $auth.user?.is_superuser === true. The line's count, attention, is securityChecks.attentionCount for an administrator and 0 for anyone else; its severity is securityChecks.attentionSeverity while attention > 0, none otherwise. The role is checked in the components, not in the store: securityChecks is not reset when the account changes (it has no registerClientSessionReset, as since lot A8b), so an administrator's answer stays in memory for the rest of the page load, and a member who signs in after them in the same tab is shown none of it.
  • One read per page load. An $effect of the line calls securityChecks.ensureLoaded() for an administrator, inside untrack(): ensureLoaded() reads the store's status and moves it, and a tracked call would run the effect again at each move — after a failure, a new request, in a loop. The page's prefetch is untracked for the same reason. The effect depends on isAdmin alone; the sidebar belongs to the app shell, on every page and on a phone too (off-screen until the menu opens); and ensureLoaded() reads nothing more once a read has succeeded: one read per page load, on its first page. A failed read is not retried by the line: the next page load retries it, and so do Settings (its prefetch and the tab's mount) and Try again. Anyone else never asks: no request to GET /api/v1/security/checks, which would answer them 403. The header never asks either: it reads what the line loaded.
  • The root, connection-security, publishes data-security-attention, the count (0 for anyone not an administrator, and until the answer), and data-security-severity, error, warning or none, beside data-level, data-reason and data-server-checked. Since lot A-62 it also publishes data-security-checks, where the checks stand: off for anyone not an administrator, pending for an administrator until the first answer, ready from the first answer on (while Check again reloads, and after a later reload failed, too), error when the first read failed and nothing has answered yet. The expression is !isAdmin ? 'off' : securityChecks.answered ? 'ready' : securityChecks.status === 'error' ? 'error' : 'pending'. Invisible to the user, it is there for the tests and the gallery to wait on the checks instead of guessing a delay.
  • The dot, connection-security-attention-dot: on the corner of the level's icon, inside the toggle (connection-security-toggle), with data-severity the severity and aria-hidden="true"; drawn while attention > 0, with the sidebar expanded or collapsed. A dot, not a number (D3 a): bg-lf-bar-danger for an error, bg-lf-bar-warning for warnings only, with a ring-2 ring-lf-bar in the bar's colour that cuts it out of the icon.
  • The name. Colour is not the only sign (WCAG 1.4.1): while attention > 0, the toggle's aria-label is «‹level label› — ‹attention text›», expanded and collapsed, and its title the same when collapsed. The attention text is $_('connectionSecurity.attention', {values: {count}}), an ICU plural in the four catalogues of the app subsystem (1 security warning, 2 security warnings: the errors are counted in it). Without attention the toggle is named as before: by the level label in aria-label and title when collapsed, by its visible label when expanded.
  • The link, connection-security-attention-link: in the details, after the reason and before the administrator's cookie line and the docs link, an <a href="/settings/admin/security"> whose text is the attention text after a ShieldAlert icon, with data-severity the severity and its border and icon in lf-bar-danger or lf-bar-warning. A click calls closeDetails() while the app navigates to the tab.
  • The menu button (D2 a). On a phone the sidebar, and the line with it, hide behind mobile-menu-toggle. Its dot, mobile-menu-security-dot, until N69b for an insecure connection alone (plan 36), is drawn while the connection is insecure or an administrator's attentionCount is above 0: one dot either way. Its data-severity is error when the connection is insecure or attentionSeverity is error, warning otherwise; bg-lf-danger or bg-lf-warning, with ring-2 ring-lf-header and aria-hidden="true". The button's aria-label starts with $_('nav.toggleMenu'), the translated «Toggle menu» (a key of the base catalogue since lot A-62; it was an English literal), followed by the insecure level's label when the connection is insecure and by the attention text with attention, each after « — ».

Tests: ./dev.py test front-utility component-unit runs lib/components/layout/ConnectionSecurityIndicator.test.ts and lib/components/layout/Header.test.ts (the latter also in onboarding-component-unit). Each file fakes the checks' store over a reactive box, one list of findings from which findings, attentionCount and attentionSeverity derive as in the real store, with ensureLoaded and reload spied and the answer landed by the case; and each gives connectionSecurity.attention an ICU message of its own, so that a name reads the key, the plural branch and the count, never a translation. N69b's describe closes Header.test.ts (A-62's nests inside it) and comes just before A-62's, the last, in ConnectionSecurityIndicator.test.ts:

  • the line, 6 cases: an administrator with warnings (2 and warning on the root, the dot in the toggle, the count in the name, the link after the reason, which closes the details); with an error among them (error on the root and the dot); with infos only (0 and none, no dot nor link, the name as before, expanded and collapsed); a member over a store holding an administrator's warnings (0 and none, no dot nor link, and no call of ensureLoaded(), reload() or the generated client); collapsed (the dot, and the singular in the name and the title); an administrator's line asking the store once from its mount and following the answer when it lands;
  • the header, 5 cases: an administrator with warnings, then with an error among them, on a secure connection (the dot and its severity, the count appended to the name, nothing for infos only); a member on an insecure connection (the plan-36 dot, now data-severity="error", nothing about the checks in the name); an administrator with warnings on an insecure connection (one dot, error; the name carries the level, then the count); a member over an administrator's warnings, then an administrator signed in on the same header, the control. The header never calls ensureLoaded() nor reload().

Lot A-62 adds the last describe of the indicator's file and one inside N69b's in the header's:

  • the line, «the checks signal on the root (A-62)», 10 cases: a member over a store that holds the answer, a failed first read or a read under way, and nobody signed in (off each time, and a member's line never asks the checks); an administrator before the answer (pending, the line's own request having moved the store to loading); an answer already there at mount (ready, an answer with nothing to look at included); pending then ready when the answer lands; ready kept during a Check again reload and after a later reload failed; a first read that failed (error, and no second request);
  • the header, «the burger's name starts with the translated toggle menu (A-62)», 4 cases: a member on a secure connection (the first part alone) and on an insecure one (then the level); an administrator with warnings, on a secure connection (then the count) and on an insecure one (the level, then the count, in that order). The describe gives nav.toggleMenu a marker of its own (⟦nav.toggleMenu⟧, through addMessages), so that the name must start with that key's text and not with a literal.

./dev.py test front-utility connection-security runs frontend/e2e/layout/connection-security.spec.ts on the desktop and the mobile projects. Its describe «An administrator: the security dot (N69-1)» runs under a loopback name, where the browser adds no open-registration finding of its own, and reads the root's two attributes, the dots and the link:

  • ADOT-E-01, the lane as it is: accounts.login_limit is a warning on every lane (dev.py server --test sets LIBREFOLIO_LOGIN_LIMIT=off), read first as a precondition. The page reads the checks once, and the line's count and severity are those of that very read (platform.client_address may differ from one server process to another), with, on a phone, the burger's dot. Its link opens Settings › Administration › Security and closes the details, and the tab lists as many errors and warnings without a second read;
  • ADOT-E-02, stubbed (page.route), one error and two warnings, an info and an ok besides: 3 and error, the dot expanded and, on desktop, collapsed, the burger's on a phone, the link;
  • ADOT-E-03, stubbed, every check ok: 0 and none once the Security tab has settled on the same answer, no dot on the line nor, on a phone, on the burger, no link;
  • ADOT-E-04, stubbed, one warning: 1 and warning, on the line and, on a phone, on the burger;
  • ADOT-E-05, a member: 0 and none, no dot, and no read of the checks through a sign-in, a page load and a navigation to Settings.

A stubbed case counts one read for its page load, answered by the stub.

docs.title: ℹ️ AboutTab
docs.text:
Read-only system information:

  • Version (from Git tag)
  • Backend/frontend info

Between the links (website, GitHub, license) and the system information sit two cards:

  • Support (about-support-card): SupportActions, whose Buy Me a Coffee link and «Or share» divider follow donationsVisible(), shown only once GET /system/instance has answered selfhosted (Instance configuration). The share buttons stay on every instance.
  • Legal notice (about-legal-card): the legal.title heading, then LegalNotice. It does not depend on the diagnostics: it shows, links included, when GET /system/info fails.

docs.title: The legal notice
docs.text:
lib/features/legal/ holds the legal notice of the instance (F09, workstream A; its places are decision D-A11): two components that read legal of instanceConfig, the {terms_url, privacy_url} of GET /system/instance (Public instance configuration).

Component Shows Used by LegalNotice.svelte (legal-notice) legal.disclaimer, then a row with Terms of service (legal-terms-link, legal.terms) and Privacy policy (legal-privacy-link, legal.privacy), each only while its address is set; no row without either AboutTab (about-legal-card); WelcomePage, under its card (Welcome) LegalLinks.svelte (legal-links) One line: legal.disclaimerShort, then the same two links, each after a ·. Prop tone: page (the default) or bar, the colours of the sidebar's bar AuthPageFrame (auth-legal-links), under the card of every sign-in page; Sidebar (sidebar-legal-links, tone="bar"), after the version while the sidebar is expanded
  • Both links open in a new tab, with rel="noopener noreferrer": the page they open gets no window.opener and no Referer.
  • Neither component loads the configuration: the page around it does (the (app) layout, AuthPageFrame). The default configuration has no legal, so until the answer the notice shows without links, and the links appear in place when it lands.
  • The keys legal.title, legal.disclaimer, legal.disclaimerShort, legal.terms and legal.privacy belong to the app i18n subsystem (frontend/src/lib/i18n/app/, prefix legal).
  • AI Export renders legal.title and legal.disclaimer too, without the components and without links, as the legal_notice section of every prompt (Exact Prompt Order): a change to either text changes every exported prompt.
  • Colour roles only, as everywhere: no palette class and no dark: variant, which the tests check in each place.
  • Tests: ./dev.py test front-utility component-unit runs LegalNotice.test.ts, LegalLinks.test.ts, AboutTab.legal.test.ts, AuthPageFrame.legal.test.ts and Sidebar.legal.test.ts; ./dev.py test front-utility onboarding-component-unit runs WelcomePage.legal.test.ts.

docs.title: 🔧 Field Components
docs.text:
Each setting type has a specialized component that handles its own UI and events.

  • SettingSelect: Generic dropdown (uses SimpleSelect).
  • SettingCurrency: Searchable currency selector (uses SearchSelect).
  • SettingTheme: Radio buttons for Light/Dark/Auto theme with visual preview.
  • SettingNumber: Numeric input with increment/decrement.
  • SettingToggle: Boolean toggle switch.

Common Props for Field Components:

  • value: Two-way bound value.
  • label: Field label.
  • hint: Helper text.
  • isModified: Highlights the field if changed.
  • isNonDefault: Shows a "Reset to Default" indicator.
  • isLocked: Disables input.

The three wrappers shared with the Global Settings tab — SettingSelect, SettingCurrency, SettingTheme — also accept embedded: when true, the row drops its own padding and bottom border so it can sit inside a parent card without a double separator. The standalone Preferences tab renders rows in a list and keeps the default; the Global Settings tab embeds the shared wrappers in its own per-setting cards and passes embedded.

docs.title: 💻 Usage Example
docs.text:
Both components take callback props (onsaveAll, onundoAll, onresetAll on the layout; onsave, onundo, onreset on a field), not component events:

<script lang="ts">
  import SettingsLayout from '$lib/features/settings/SettingsLayout.svelte';
  import SettingSelect from '$lib/features/settings/SettingSelect.svelte';

  let original = $state('option1');
  let value = $state('option1');
  let hasChanges = $derived(value !== original);

  function save() {
    // persist `value`, then:
    original = value;
  }
</script>

<SettingsLayout title="My Settings" {hasChanges} onsaveAll={save} onundoAll={() => (value = original)}>
  <SettingSelect
    bind:value
    label="Choose Option"
    options={[{value: 'option1', label: 'One'}]}
    isModified={hasChanges}
    onsave={save}
    onundo={() => (value = original)}
  />
</SettingsLayout>

docs.title: 📝 Transaction Form Modal
docs.text:
The Transaction Form Modal (TransactionFormModal.svelte, in frontend/src/lib/features/transactions/form/) creates, edits or displays one transaction — or one linked pair, shown as a single two-sided form. It adapts its fields to the selected transaction type, validates against the backend while the user types, and either hands the result back to the bulk workspace or commits it itself.

The modal owns the whole state — the draft, the validation, the handlers — and renders its sections through four components in frontend/src/lib/features/transactions/form/, which read that state as props, write back only what they bind, and call the modal's handlers:

Component Section TxFormBanners The inline banners: a failed commit, the validation result and its issues, the partner loading TxFormPairSection The two-sided form of a pair (FX, transfer of an asset, transfer of cash): the shared fields, then From and To TxFormSingleSection The one-row form: date, type, quantity and cash, asset, broker, and the cost basis of an adjustment TxFormOptionalSection The optional fields: linked event, tags, description, link id, pair partner

The header, the footer, the read-only footer and the stacked modals stay in the modal.

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture
docs.text:
The form works on a local copy of one row; nothing it holds is shared until the user presses the footer button.

mode Footer button Behaviour create Apply / Save Blank form, or pre-filled from items[0] (e.g. a staged row) edit Apply / Save Existing row; type and broker are locked unless unlockImmutable (then the type list is limited to the original type's swap group) view — Read-only; the pencil switches to edit through onSwitchToEdit, shown only when canEdit

commitOnSave decides where the result goes:

  • commitOnSave={false} — Apply. onPushDraft(payload) hands a create-shaped payload back to the caller, and the modal closes. TransactionBulkModal mounts the form this way (with unlockImmutable in edit mode), so every row created or edited in the workspace goes through it.
  • commitOnSave={true} (default) — Save. The form posts to POST /transactions/commit itself and reports onCommitted. The Transactions, broker-detail and dashboard pages mount the form in view mode only; on the Transactions page, the pencil reopens the row in the bulk workspace.

Closing the form with unsaved changes asks for confirmation (Discard Changes?).

docs.title: 🔀 Form State vs Staging State
docs.text:
It is important to keep the single-item form state apart from the workspace's staging state:

  • Form state — draft: FormDraft, plus dualTo: DualDraftTo for a pair, is local Svelte 5 $state inside the modal. It is rebuilt from items each time the modal opens (a new openKey forces a rebuild even when open never went back to false) and may be incomplete or invalid while the user types.
  • Staging state — on Apply, TransactionBulkModal writes the pushed payload into the row's DraftFields (applyFormPayload) and keeps the row as a PendingOp. The payload is signed, as a create is sent, while the workspace holds a value whose type rule demands a negative (a SELL's quantity, a BUY's cash) as its magnitude: applyFormPayload ends by bringing the quantity and the cash back to that convention (magnitudeForRule), so an untouched Apply leaves them as the row held them (W-B65). Read more in the Transaction Staging State guide.

docs.title: 🗄️ State Schema
docs.text: Which fields are shown, required or forbidden comes from the type rules that transactionTypeStore loads from GET /transactions/types (assetField, cashField, quantityMode, the quantity and cash sign rules, eventLinkable). Changing the type clears the values the new type forbids.

docs.title: 📋 Common Fields
docs.text:
FormDraft (declared, with DualDraftTo, in features/transactions/form/txFormTypes.ts):

Field Type Description type TransactionTypeCode Core discriminator (BUY, SELL, DIVIDEND, …) broker_id number 0 until chosen; pre-filled from forcedBroker (locked), defaultBrokerId, or the only broker the user can edit. Create new in the broker select opens a stacked BrokerModal (zIndex + 10) date string YYYY-MM-DD; today on a blank form cash {code, amount} \| null ISO 4217 code and decimal string, edited with CompactCashCell tags string[] Free tags, with suggestions from availableTags description string Free-text memo asset_event_id number \| null Linked asset event (Linked Event, AssetEventPicker), for the event-linkable types (DIVIDEND, INTEREST, ADJUSTMENT); the picker shows once an asset and a date are set (canShowAssetEvent). + New event in the picker (not in view mode) opens a stacked EventCreateMiniModal (zIndex + 10), which sends the new event with mode: "create". Its amount is handled as a decimal string: the suggestion (the form's cash) is prefilled whole (0.2345 stays 0.2345), blur pads it to two decimals at least and keeps the typed ones, the event is sent with that string, and past the 6 decimals an event value keeps (trailing zeros not counted, as the backend counts them) the field is aria-invalid, event-create-amount-digits-error (data-max="6", common.decimalPlacesExceeded) shows under it and the submit button (event-create-submit) is disabled. On EVENT_EXISTS it shows EventExistsPanel: Use this (writes nothing), Edit this for manual events only (the form then saves that event by its id, mode: "upsert"), Cancel. The field then holds the id the response names (results[0].event_ids[0]), or the id of the event chosen with Use this. Any refusal other than EVENT_EXISTS shows as one sentence in the modal's error banner (eventSaveErrorMessage(), lib/features/transactions/events/eventSaveError.ts); a 400 EVENT_TOO_MANY_DIGITS has its own, events.saveError.tooManyDigits, which names the first event at fault (date and type), how many more there are, and the three maxima of its params: decimal places, significant digits and digits before the decimal point (max_decimal_places, max_significant_digits, max_integer_digits) cost_basis_override {code, amount} \| null Manual cost basis (see WAC State) link_uuid string \| null Pairing UUID; shown read-only when set

docs.title: 📦 Asset Operations (BUY / SELL / TRANSFER)
docs.text:
Shown when the type's rules allow them:

Field Type Description asset_id number \| null Selected asset (AssetSelect); New asset opens a stacked AssetModal quantity string Exact decimal string, edited with ExactQuantityInput (built on ExactDecimalInput; at most 15 integer and 10 fraction digits); '0' when the type forbids a quantity

docs.title: 💱 Paired layouts and FX conversion
docs.text:
When the type requires a link (requiresPair, the backend's requires_link), the form switches to a two-sided layout chosen by the type's pairFormLayout: transfer_asset for TRANSFER, transfer_cash for CASH_TRANSFER and fx for FX_CONVERSION. Each side, From and To, has its own date. Swap sides (swapDualSides()) exchanges the two dates and, for the transfer layouts, the two brokers; for FX it exchanges the amounts instead (see below). The To side lives in dualTo:

interface DualDraftTo {
    broker_id: number;                                    // transfers: the receiving broker
    cash: {code: string; amount: string} | null;          // fx: the currency bought
    date: string;                                         // this leg's own date
    quantity?: string;                                    // transfer_asset: receiver quantity
    cost_basis_override?: {code: string; amount: string} | null; // transfer_asset: receiver cost basis
}

docs.title: 🧾 The two FX legs
docs.text:
An FX_CONVERSION exchanges one currency for another inside one broker: one leg spends a currency, the other receives a different one.

Part Fields Notes Shared type, broker_id One broker field for both legs. Outside view mode, effectiveDualTo always puts the To leg on the source broker, as the type's pair_field_constraints ask (broker_id equal, cash_currency different) From date, cash The currency sold and its amount (tx-form-cash-from) To dualTo.date, dualTo.cash The currency bought and its amount (tx-form-cash-to); its date may differ from the From date Shared tags, description Copied onto both legs

Both amounts are typed as magnitudes; the signs are applied when the payload is built. The swap arrow (tx-form-dual-swap) exchanges the amounts and the dates of the two legs and keeps the broker. Once both amounts are set in two different currencies, a badge (tx-form-fx-info) shows the implied rate (To ÷ From) and, in its tooltip, the market rate on the From date (lookupFxRate from fxStoreRegistry); ⚠️ marks a market rate carried over from an earlier day.

docs.title: ✅ Pair validation
docs.text:
• Different currencies — dualValidationError reports Currencies must be different (transactions.form.sameCurrencyError) and disables the footer button. Transfers check the reverse: their two brokers must differ (sameBrokerError).
  • Completeness — isFormComplete needs the From fields the type requires, a destination broker and a destination date and, for FX, a currency and a finite, non-zero amount on both legs. It gates the automatic validation, ⚡ Validate now and, in the bulk workspace, Apply.
  • Sign — the paired cash editors use the positive rule: a negative amount on either leg (cashSignResult, cashToSignViolation) disables the footer button.
  • Server — both legs are validated together in one POST /transactions/validate; the issues the two halves share are shown once (deduplicateIssues, by issue code).

docs.title: 📤 How the pair is submitted
docs.text:
collectDualCreates() calls buildDualCreatePayloads('fx', …) (lib/features/transactions/txPayloadHelpers.ts), which returns two FX_CONVERSION items:

Field From item To item broker_id source broker source broker date From date To date (the From date when empty) quantity '0' '0' cash sold currency, negative amount bought currency, positive amount link_uuid shared shared tags, description when set same as From

The signs are applied on the decimal strings (applySign), never through a float. The two items share one link_uuid: draft.link_uuid when it is set, otherwise a fresh generateUUID().

  • Apply (bulk workspace) — the pushed payload carries _dual: true and _items: [from, to] (with _partnerBrokerId, _partnerCash, _partnerDate). TransactionBulkModal turns it into a visible row plus a hidden partner op that points to it through pairedWith; both keep the shared link_uuid.
  • Save (standalone) — a new pair is sent as {creates: [from, to]}. An edited pair, once its partner is loaded, is sent as {updates: …}: collectDualUpdates() matches each leg to its original by the sign of its cash and keeps only the legs that changed (diffDualItem).

Opening an existing pair loads the partner (passed in items[1], or read with GET /transactions?ids=…), puts the spending leg on From, and merges diverging descriptions and tags of the two legs.

docs.title: ✅ Client-Side Validation
docs.text:
The form checks locally only what it can know without the ledger:

  • Required fields — isDraftReadyForValidation() (transactionTypeStore) needs a broker, the asset when the type requires one, a non-zero cash amount when cash is required and a non-zero quantity unless the type forbids it; the form also needs a date, and for a pair the destination side (Pair validation). Until then there is no automatic validation and ⚡ Validate now stays disabled.
  • Quantity — ExactQuantityInput checks the syntax, the 15 + 10 digit budget (the 15 integer digits, decision N63, and the 10 decimals the backend keeps for a quantity; zeros that do not change the value are not counted: 0.10000000000 has one decimal, 007 one integer digit) and the type's sign rule, and reports its validity (onvaliditychange); an invalid quantity disables the footer button. A fraction past those 10 decimals is also said under the field (tx-form-quantity-digits-error, common.decimalPlacesExceeded), and the value stays as typed.
  • Cash sign — for a type whose cash rule is negative the user types a magnitude and the payload builder negates it (applySignRules). An amount that still breaks the rule (computeSignHint) disables the footer button.
  • Hints — the single-layout cash editor always carries 💡 Total amount (not per share) (transactions.form.cashLabelTotal). The quantity and cash editors also show the hint of the type's sign rule (signHintText() → signHintKey() in lib/features/transactions/form/txFormFields.ts: must be > 0, enter positive — auto-negated on save, must be 0, must be ≠ 0). Negative quantity rules are auto-flipped like cash (effectiveQtyRule), so a SELL quantity is typed as a positive number.

Everything deeper — balances, pairing rules, access — belongs to the backend's Balance Validation. While the form is complete, every change schedules POST /transactions/validate (createValidateScheduler, debounced 500 ms by default). Inside the bulk workspace the request also carries the other staged rows (getBulkContext()), so the balance walk sees the whole batch; for a single-row layout the banner then keeps only this row's issues plus the global ones.

docs.title: 💰 WAC State
docs.text:
The cost-basis editor is WacPreviewSection (frontend/src/lib/features/transactions/wac/WacPreviewSection.svelte). The form shows it where a cost basis applies: on the receiving side of a paired TRANSFER, and on an ADJUSTMENT with a positive quantity (showCostBasisField in TransactionFormModal.svelte). An ADJUSTMENT taking units out has no value (N78-1), so the form shows no cost basis for it, and the bulk editor gives such a saved row no cbMode (TransactionBulkModal.svelte). BUY and SELL do not show it.

  • costBasisMode is 'auto' (the backend computes the weighted average cost) or 'manual' (the user's cost_basis_override). In Auto mode the item is sent with cost_basis_mode: 'auto' and, once wacCurrencyHint holds a currency (the user's pick, the first WAC result's, or the one in the row's sentinel), the hint {code, amount: '0'} as override.
  • In Auto mode the backend writes the WAC into cost_basis_override (TransactionService._compute_wac_for_auto_items() → compute_wac_iterative()): for the receiving side of a TRANSFER pair, the WAC of the partner's broker as of the partner's date, without the partner's outgoing leg; otherwise the WAC of the row's own broker as of the row's date, without the row. The batch's other Auto rows not yet costed are left out too, and the rows are costed in date order (W-B67; see Inline Batch Auto Modes). When that broker has no other row of the asset up to that date — the transfer's own outgoing leg aside — the WAC is 0, and the row is saved with a zero cost basis. That is by design (developer decision of 2026-10-09): the user corrects that transaction later if needed. Auto rows skip the required-cost-basis check (_auto_mode_indices()); split-linked adjustments and missing FX are covered in WAC & Cost Basis.
  • In Manual mode, a TRANSFER or ADJUSTMENT with a positive quantity and no cost_basis_override gets a costBasisRequired issue (validate_cost_basis()) when it is created, and when an update changes its type, quantity, cost basis or its asset event link. TransactionService._requires_cost_basis() reads which rows need one from TX_TYPE_METADATA, the table GET /transactions/types serves (cost_basis_required() in backend/app/schemas/transactions/type_metadata.py). Like any issue, it makes the batch committed=False, and POST /transactions/commit rolls the whole batch back: the row is not saved. A free acquisition is entered as 0.
  • Known mismatch: for an ADJUSTMENT with a positive quantity, not in Auto mode and with an empty manual field, the form shows transactions.costBasisOverride.warningAdjustment (tx-form-cost-basis-warning), which says the transaction cannot be saved without a cost basis. That holds for a create, not for an update that leaves the type, quantity, cost basis and asset event link alone: editing only the notes, tags or date of an older row stored without a cost basis gets no costBasisRequired, and the row stays without one.
  • For validation, upgradeAutoToDetail() turns 'auto' into 'auto-detail', so the response's wac_results carries the WAC with its qualifying transactions. Standalone, the form keeps that result in formWacResult; inside the bulk workspace it first reads the workspace's own result (getWacResult(editingTempId)).
  • A wacFxUnavailable issue comes with a link that opens FxSyncModal on the missing pairs and dates (handleSyncFx).

docs.title: 🏦 BrokerCard
docs.text: BrokerCard.svelte shows one accessible broker. The whole card is a link to its detail page (<a href="/brokers/{id}">).

docs.title: ⚡ Features
docs.text:
• Header — BrokerIcon (md), the role badge when user_role is set (👑 Owner, ✏️ Editor, 👁️ Viewer, named in its tooltip), the name, and a one-line description
  • Actions — Share (share), Edit (edit), Delete (delete) and, when portal_url is set, a button that opens the portal in a new tab (a greyed icon otherwise). Each button stops the click, so it never follows the card link. They show for every role: the server enforces the rules (edit: Owner or Editor; delete: Owner), and the list page opens the sharing modal read-only for a non-Owner
  • Figures — from summary: NAV (net_worth) and Gain/Loss (gain_loss in targetCurrency, with gain_loss_percent; red when negative), or — while summary is null
  • Cash Balances — one chip per currency of summary.cash_balances, largest first, or No cash positions
  • Footer — {n} asset(s) (assetCount) and {n} currency(ies) (the number of cash balances)
  • Closed accounts: a broker whose is_active is false (Account Active off) is dimmed (class:opacity-60). The portfolio figures still include it; the PAC allocator flags it with allocation.broker_inactive (portfolio_allocation_source.py)

Default null assetCount number The broker's rows in the report's summary.holdings. Default 0 targetCurrency string The page's Currency choice, used for the gain/loss amount. Default 'EUR'

docs.title: 📝 Broker Forms
docs.text: Form and input components for broker creation and editing.

docs.title: 📝 BrokerForm
docs.text: The create/edit form for a broker (BrokerForm.svelte), used inside BrokerModal. It dispatches submit with the trimmed values, and cancel; the modal makes the API calls.

docs.title: 📋 Fields
docs.text:
Field Component Required Description Name Text input (max 100) ✅ Broker display name; unique among all brokers of the instance Description Textarea (max 500) ❌ Optional description Default Import Plugin ImportPluginSelect ❌ BRIM parser proposed for this broker's files Portal URL URL input ❌ Broker website; its /favicon.ico is an icon fallback Icon ImagePickerWrapper (preset="broker-icon") ❌ Custom broker icon, previewed with BrokerIcon Opened at SingleDatePicker ❌ Account opening date, never in the future (allowFuture={false}); today for a new broker Active Toggle ❌ is_active, on by default Allow Overdraft Checkbox ❌ Allow a negative cash balance Allow Shorting Checkbox ❌ Allow a negative asset quantity Initial Balances Amount + CurrencySearchSelect rows ❌ Create mode only: opening cash per currency; the first row uses the user's base currency

In edit mode a cleared optional text field is sent as '', which clears it on the server; in create mode it is left out.

docs.title: ✅ Validation
docs.text:
Client side, the submit button stays disabled while a save is running or while:

  • Name is empty after trimming, or longer than 100 characters (isValid);
  • Initial balances repeat a currency (hasDuplicateCurrencies, with a warning under the rows).

Balance rows whose amount is zero or negative are dropped on submit. The form has no base-currency field: currencies appear only in the initial balance rows.

On the server, BrokerService.create_bulk() turns each remaining balance row into a DEPOSIT dated today (today_date(), not opened_at), written through execute_batch(creates_raw=…); a deposit refused by validation adds its issue to the broker's create errors. The raw row carries the amount in its short form, str(v), never expanded with format(v, "f"): the batch refuses a value past its column's limits (R13-SEC7-3). An amount whose exponent is outside ±100 never gets that far: the Currency of initial_balances refuses it, and POST /brokers answers 422 on initial_balances.<n>.amount and creates nothing (see Decimal Columns).

docs.title: Duplicate names
docs.text:
Broker names are unique across the instance (Broker.name is a unique column), so the server rejects a create whose name is taken. BrokerModal turns the backend's English message into a localized one (localizeDuplicateName), chosen by who owns the existing broker, and appends the recovery guidance:

Backend message Key (frontend/src/lib/i18n/brokers/en.json) English text You already have a broker named '<name>' brokers.duplicateNameOwn You already have a broker named "{name}". Broker '<name>' already exists (owned by '<owner>') brokers.duplicateNameOwned Broker "{name}" already exists (owned by "{owner}"). Broker with name '<name>' already exists, or the 409 A broker with that name already exists brokers.duplicateNameExists A broker named "{name}" already exists. appended to each of the above brokers.duplicateNameRecovery To resolve this, rename the existing broker or choose a different name for the broker you are adding.

The message fills the dialog's error banner. The 409 comes from a creation that lost a race on the unique name; it also raises an error toast. Any other error is shown as received. The error is reset whenever a new dialog opens, so it never carries over into the next create or edit.

docs.title: 🔔 Feedback
docs.text:
• Create — a success toast, Broker "{name}" created. (brokers.created), from BrokerModal once the new broker is merged into brokerStore.
  • Delete — a success toast, Broker "{name}" deleted. or Broker "{name}" and {count} transactions deleted. (brokers.deleted, brokers.deletedWithTransactions), from the broker list page once DELETE /brokers succeeds — see DeleteBrokerDialog.
  • Edit — the dialog closes without a toast.

docs.title: ✏️ BrokerModal
docs.text:
Modal wrapper (BrokerModal.svelte) around BrokerForm for creating or editing a broker. The broker list and detail pages, the Files page, the Import Wizard and the transaction form (to create a broker inline) all mount it.

  • Create — POST /brokers with a one-item list. On success the new broker is merged into brokerStore (mergeBrokers), a success toast reads Broker "{name}" created., then oncreated({id}) and onclose() run.
  • Edit — PATCH /brokers/{id} with the form values. On success the patched fields are merged into brokerStore, then onupdated({id}) and onclose() run; there is no toast.
  • Errors appear in the dialog's InfoBanner. When a create fails on a duplicate name, the message is localized and carries recovery guidance (Duplicate names). The error, the touched flag and the discard prompt are reset whenever a new dialog opens, and the answer to a request from an earlier dialog is ignored.
  • Closing with unsaved edits asks Discard Changes? (Continue Editing / Discard & Close); nothing closes while a save is running.

docs.title: 📋 Props
docs.text: Prop Type Description isOpen boolean Modal visibility mode 'create' \| 'edit' Defaults to 'create' brokerId number \| null Broker updated in edit mode initialData object Values pre-filled in the form (name, description, portal_url, icon_url, default_import_plugin, allow_cash_overdraft, allow_asset_shorting, is_active, opened_at) zIndex number Defaults to 50; raised when the modal is stacked over another one tourPreview boolean Non-writing preview: the form is inert, has no submit button, and the dialog closes without the discard prompt onclose, oncreated, onupdated callbacks oncreated and onupdated receive {id}

docs.title: 🤝 BrokerSharingModal
docs.text:
Sharing a broker with other users, with RBAC roles and ownership shares.

The sharing UI is one component, BrokerSharingPanel.svelte, mounted in two places:

Host Mounted as Read-only when Broker list (routes/(app)/brokers/+page.svelte) BrokerSharingModal: the panel inside ModalBase, opened from a broker card's share action the user is not the broker's OWNER; always for a discovery card (a broker the user has no access to) Broker detail, Info tab (routes/(app)/brokers/[id]/+page.svelte) the panel itself, without modal chrome the user is not the broker's OWNER

BrokerSharingModal adds only the title (Share Broker — {name}), the X button and the unsaved-changes prompt.

docs.title: 🧩 BrokerSharingPanel
docs.text: Prop Type Description brokerId number Broker whose access list is loaded; changing it reloads the list readOnly boolean Shows the list without any editing control onChanged () => void Called after a successful save or self-service action, so the host can reload onCancel () => void Optional. Renders Cancel next to Save and is called after a successful save. The modal passes its close handler; the Info tab passes nothing hasChanges boolean, $bindable true while the staged list differs from the loaded one

docs.title: ⚡ Features
docs.text:
• Ownership chart — a SemiDonutChart of the owners' shares with the Allocated and Available totals. When the owners' shares exceed 100% a warning banner appears; Save stays available and the server refuses the list.
  • Owners, Editors, Viewers — three columns, one chip per user with role and share.
  • Add user (the + under the chart) — the candidates come from GET /users/search (excluding users who already have access) and are picked with UserSearchSelect, built on SearchSelect. The endpoint matches the username only (ILIKE) and never returns e-mail addresses. The role defaults to Viewer; only an Owner gets a share, capped at what is still unallocated.
  • Edit and remove — a chip opens the role and share editor, which also removes the user after a confirmation. The last Owner can be neither removed nor demoted.
  • Your access — the user's own row offers Leave broker (Leave and delete broker for the last Owner) and, for an Editor, Switch to viewer. Both ask for confirmation and then act at once — they are not staged — and both stay available in read-only mode.

docs.title: 💾 Staged save, Reset and closing
docs.text:
Adding, editing and removing users only change the panel's local list; nothing is written before Save Configuration.

  • Save Configuration sends the whole list in one PUT /brokers/{id}/access, shares as 0–1 fractions. It is disabled while nothing changed, during a save, and until the current list has loaded: a failed load shows a blocking error with Retry instead of an empty, editable list. On success the saved list becomes the new baseline, onChanged runs, a toast reads Access configuration saved, and onCancel is called. A refused save is shown inline in the panel and keeps the draft.
  • Why a save is refused. BrokerService.bulk_update_access() rejects a list when the caller is not an Owner (403; superusers are exempt), and with 400 when no Owner would remain, when the shares add up to more than 1, when a user appears twice, or when a user does not exist. The schema (BRAccessBulkItem) also rejects a share above 0 on an Editor or a Viewer, and an empty list is a 422.
  • Reset (the ↺ button, shown only with unsaved changes) puts back the list as loaded.
  • After a save, the two hosts differ. The panel awaits a tick() before calling onCancel, so the bound hasChanges is already false: in the list-page modal a successful save closes the dialog without the discard prompt. The Info tab passes no onCancel, so the panel stays open and editable after saving.
  • Closing with unsaved changes. The modal asks Discard Changes? (Discard & Close) on X, Cancel, Escape or a backdrop click. The Info tab binds hasChanges but does not use it yet: switching tab unmounts the panel and drops unsaved changes without a prompt.
  • Read-only (non-owners): the chips are disabled, and there is no add button, Reset, Save or Cancel.

docs.title: 🌐 API Calls
docs.text:
• GET /brokers/{id}/access — load the current access list
  • PUT /brokers/{id}/access — replace it with the staged list
  • PATCH /brokers/{id}/access/me — switch the current user from Editor to Viewer
  • DELETE /brokers/{id}/access/me — leave the broker; when the last Owner leaves, the broker is deleted
  • GET /users/search — candidates for Add user

See Broker Sharing (User Guide) and Access Control (RBAC) for details.

docs.title: 📥 BrokerImportFilesModal
docs.text: Modal for the BRIM report files of one broker, opened from the broker detail page (Uploaded Reports in its Transactions tab). It stores and manages files; parsing them is the job of the Import Wizard.

docs.title: ⚡ Features
docs.text:
• Lists the broker's files in a FilesTable (type="brim", without the broker column), with preview (FilePreviewModal) and single or bulk delete; a bulk delete asks for confirmation.
  • Uploads through FileUploader (.csv, .xlsx, .xls, several at once). A pending file can be renamed before upload (FileEditModal). The files of one upload share a batch_id (generateUUID()), so a report-set plugin can read them as one report set. The upload stops at the first failing file and names it in the error banner.
  • Closing with files picked but not uploaded asks for confirmation (Pending Uploads).
  • The modal does not check the user's role: a Viewer also sees the upload area and the bulk delete, and the server refuses them with 403 (EDITOR or OWNER access required on the broker). The row's Delete comes from FilesTable, which hides it on a file whose can_delete is false, as for a Viewer (see FilesTable).
  • A link opens the Files page filtered on this broker (/files?tab=brim&broker=<id>).

docs.title: 🌐 API Calls
docs.text:
• GET /brokers/import/files?broker_ids=<id> — list the broker's files
  • POST /brokers/import/upload — upload one file (multipart: file, broker_id, batch_id)
  • DELETE /brokers/import/files/{file_id} — delete one file

For details on the BRIM plugin system, see Registry & Plugin System.

docs.title: 🗑️ DeleteBrokerDialog
docs.text:
A ModalBase dialog (DeleteBrokerDialog.svelte) driven by the broker list page (confirmDelete in routes/(app)/brokers/+page.svelte):

  • It first asks to confirm the deletion of the named broker. Delete dispatches confirm with {force: false}, and the page calls DELETE /brokers?ids=<id>&force=false.
  • When the broker still has transactions, the server refuses and the dialog switches to its blocked state (blocked, transactionCount): it says how many transactions the broker holds and offers Go to transactions (viewTransactions, which opens /transactions?broker_id=<id>) or Delete broker and transactions (confirm with {force: true}).
  • On success the page evicts the broker from brokerStore (invalidateBroker), closes the dialog, shows a success toast — Broker "{name}" deleted., or Broker "{name}" and {count} transactions deleted. after a force delete — and reloads the list. A failure ends in an error toast (Could not delete broker).

No cash-operation modal

Deposits and withdrawals have no dialog of their own: they are ordinary transactions. The broker detail page opens the bulk transaction workspace (TransactionBulkModal, intent {action: 'create'}) with the broker pre-selected through defaultBrokerId.

docs.title: 📄 Frontend Pages
docs.text: Status: Implemented (Feb 2026)

docs.title: 📖 Overview
docs.text: Application pages and routing structure. All authenticated routes are under (app)/. The build is a static SPA: SSR is off in the root +layout.ts (FastAPI serves the static files), and only the login page is prerendered; the other routes, the public link pages included, are served through the SPA fallback.

docs.title: 🔐 Login Page (/)
docs.text:
• Public access
  • LoginCard / RegisterCard / ForgotPasswordCard (card-style, not modals), inside AuthPageFrame
  • Register here only while the instance accepts anyone (registration_mode open), or while it has no account yet (first_account_open: the first account can be created in any mode)
  • Animated background with waves and chart lines
  • Redirect to dashboard after login
  • User preferences (language, theme) applied on login

docs.title: 🔗 Account Link Pages (/invite, /reset-password, /setup)
docs.text:
• Public access, not prerendered: the SPA fallback serves them
  • The token of the link travels in the fragment (#token=…) and leaves the address bar on load
  • /invite opens RegisterCard in invitation mode; /reset-password opens ResetPasswordCard; /setup, the setup link of the initial administrator, opens SetupCard; a link that cannot be used shows LinkStatusCard
  • /invite and /reset-password end on the login page, with a success message; /setup signs the administrator in and goes to /dashboard
  • Details: Account Link Pages

docs.title: 👋 Welcome (/welcome)
docs.text:
• First-run setup of the onboarding: language, base currency and avatar
  • Rendered by the (app) layout without the app shell (no sidebar or header)
  • The layout's gate sends the user here (/welcome?returnTo=<requested path>) while the Welcome flow is due or a Welcome replay is armed (appBootstrap.resolveDestination); afterwards the page continues to returnTo, or to /dashboard when the intro tour starts
  • Architecture: Onboarding Guides

docs.title: 📊 Dashboard (/dashboard)
docs.text:
• Portfolio view in four tabs: Overview (KpiSection, GrowthChart, AllocationPanel), Positions (PositionsPanel, with the FIFO LotsAnalysisPanel), Risk (RiskLevelsPanel) and Transactions (TransactionsTable)
  • Toolbar with the date range (DateRangePicker) and the display currency (CurrencySearchSelect)
  • DataQualityBanner above the tabs; its actions can open FxPairAddModal to add a missing FX pair
  • KPI row — KpiSection, also mounted on the broker detail Overview:
    • it reads PortfolioSummary: period_pnl and its rows period_unrealized_gain_loss_delta (tooltip rows period_unrealized_breakdown, in backend order), period_realized_gain_loss, period_income and period_fees_taxes (a positive magnitude, shown negated; the tooltip splits period_fees / period_taxes); simple_roi_percent, twrr_percent, mwrr_cumulative_percent, mwrr_annualized_percent; net_worth, total_gain_loss with total_gain_loss_percent (since inception), market_value, open_cost_basis, cash_total and net_deposited_capital (total_deposited / total_withdrawn, period only)
    • the start-of-period carets come from period_market_value_start, period_book_value_start and the first history point's cash_value; the Cash tooltip from the last history point's cash_from_contributed_capital / cash_from_generated_returns
    • the day-change lines read pnl_change_1d: the Total P&L's change from the calendar day before the valuation date (date_to, else today) to it, from the engine's daily states; null for a portfolio born on the valuation date. Card 1 shows it as «amount (share)», the share being pnl_change_1d_vs_nav_percent: a fraction of the day before's |nav_value|, with the change's sign, null on a zero base; its tooltip says «versus yesterday's portfolio value». Card 2 repeats nothing of it, and there is no share of the day before's total P&L (it exploded near zero; the field was removed on 07/11/2026). A null change drops Card 1's line, a null share its percentage; the line is not derived from history
    • the timing effect reads timing_effect_percent, the backend's mwrr_cumulative_percent − twrr_percent (null when either is missing), shown ×100 in pp: — with no label when null, labelled neutral below 0.05 pp; its colour intensity saturates at 3 pp
    • each card's help icon is a DocsLink to user/dashboard/kpi-cards/#card-1-period-pl, #card-2-returns and #card-3-net-worth: keep these explicit anchors in every language
  • Positions tab — PositionsPanel, also mounted on the broker detail Positions tab:
    • Portfolio / Period (modes holdings / performance) × Table / Map: ExposureTable, ExposureTreemap, ContributionTable with OtherPeriodEffectsTable, PerformanceChart; both toggles persist per user in localStorage (dashboard-positions-semantic, dashboard-positions-visual)
    • the table layouts (dashboard-holdings-v5, dashboard-performance-v2) are shared with the broker detail page; the Period view's Status filter is a hidden-by-default enum column of ContributionTable, not a panel toggle, and PerformanceChart shows an Open / Closed badge
    • positions_contribution is fetched apart, on demand: PositionsPanel asks for it the first time the Period view is shown; a cached copy shows at once and is refreshed when stale; a failed request is asked again at most three times, 2, 4 and 8 s later (Lazy sections after a failure)
    • ExposureTreemap's type and broker tooltips take their G/L and G/L % from summary.holding_groups, passed by PositionsPanel as holdingGroups (only holdings with a known value and G/L count): the group of the same (broker_id, asset_type), asset_type null for the whole broker. A group not sent, or sent without gain_loss, reads Unrealized P&L —; tile areas and NAV weights still add up the holdings' own current_value and nav_weight_percent
    • PerformanceChart computes no return: it shows the backend's fractions of |start_value|, rounded to 4 decimals and ×100 for display only — period_pnl_percent beside period_pnl (the bar label and the tooltip's Period P&L row), and period_unrealized_delta_percent, period_realized_gain_loss_percent, period_income_percent and period_fees_taxes_percent beside the tooltip's four component rows (period_fees_taxes_percent is positive, a cost, and shown negative). A null fraction shows no return
    • the lots panel opens from the Analyze Lots row action (⋮) or the right-click menu of every view — there is no plain-click trigger — and is mirrored in ?asset=<id>; LotsAnalysisPanel renders inline below, with a slide transition, and scrolls itself into view. Its broker_ids are the broker filter, or every owned broker with a share above 0%
    • architecture: Lots Analysis and the Lots Analysis Service

docs.title: 🏦 Brokers (/brokers)
docs.text:
• Grid of broker cards with icons (fallback chain)
  • Add/Edit broker via BrokerModal (extends ModalBase); the icon is picked in the form (ImagePickerWrapper → AssetPickerModal)
  • Sharing via BrokerSharingModal; brokers the user has no access to are listed apart as BrokerDiscoveryCards, whose sharing view is read-only
  • Delete via DeleteBrokerDialog, with a force option when the broker still has transactions

docs.title: 🔍 Broker Detail (/brokers/[id])
docs.text:
• Header with back button, icon and name; toolbar actions: edit (BrokerModal, owners and editors), share (opens the Info tab), refresh, and AI export
  • Tabs: Overview (KPIs, cash balances, growth chart, allocation), Positions (Analyze Lots, from the ⋮ menu or the right-click menu, opens the FIFO lots panel, mirrored in ?asset=<id>), Risk, Transactions and Info
  • Transactions tab: the broker's transactions, its report files (Uploaded Reports → BrokerImportFilesModal), a link to the Transactions page, and — for owners and editors — import and new transaction through the bulk workspace, with this broker pre-selected
  • Info tab: broker details and the embedded sharing panel (BrokerSharingPanel)

docs.title: 📝 Transactions (/transactions)
docs.text:
• Master ledger of all user transactions
  • Advanced filtering and pagination; filters are mirrored in the URL (filterState.ts)
  • A row opens read-only in the Form modal; adding, editing, cloning, deleting and importing go through the bulk workspace (TransactionBulkModal). After every saved operation the page clears its selection (Selection on the Transactions page)
  • Relink events (tx-reconcile-events-button) opens EventReconciliationModal: the dividends, interest and adjustments without an asset event, each with the event of the same day the server found; see Event Reconciliation

docs.title: 💼 Assets (/assets)
docs.text:
• Full list of tracked financial instruments
  • Interactive data tables with sorting and filtering

docs.title: 🔍 Asset Detail (/assets/[id])
docs.text:
• Live prices and historical charts (ECharts)
  • Technical signals and related events
  • Detailed performance metrics and history

docs.title: 💱 FX Rates (/fx)
docs.text:
• List of configured currency pairs and conversion rates
  • Direct route and chain management
  • Live data sync and technical signals

docs.title: 🔍 FX Pair Detail (/fx/[pair])
docs.text:
• [pair] is a slug such as EUR-USD: its order sets the display direction, while stores and API calls use the alphabetical (canonical) pair; an invalid slug redirects to /fx (+page.ts)
  • Rate summary (FxPriceSummary), full chart with signals and measurements (PriceChartFull, ChartSignalsSection, MeasurePanel), and the rate editor (FxDataEditorSection)

docs.title: 🧰 Tools (/tools, /tools/[tool_code])
docs.text:
• /tools mounts ToolsHub: the catalogue of computation tools read from GET /api/v1/tools/catalog, one card per tool with its compatibility label
  • /tools/[tool_code] mounts ToolHost, which resolves the tool's compiled renderer in lib/features/tools/registry.ts and mounts it; a tool without a compatible renderer is shown as unavailable. Today the registry holds one tool, the PAC allocator
  • Contract and frontend binding: Tool plugins

docs.title: 📁 Files (/files)
docs.text:
• Two tabs: Static Resources / Broker Reports (BRIM)
  • DataTable with sorting, filtering, pagination, URL-synced filters
  • Grid view toggle with image previews and search
  • Upload interface with:
    • Image files → ImageEditModal (crop, rotate, flip)
    • Non-image files → FileEditModal (rename)
  • Copy link, download, delete actions; delete only on the files the user may delete (can_delete)
  • Static Resources: a Visibility column (common or personal) and the switch between the two, see Scope of uploaded files
  • File thumbnails via ?img_preview= API

docs.title: ⚙️ Settings (/settings)
docs.text:
• Tabs from the tab registry (SETTINGS_TABS and SETTINGS_TAB_GROUPS, see Settings Components): Profile, Preferences, Plugins and About, then, for a superuser only, the Administration group on the right, whose tabs show in a second bar: Global Settings, Users, Backup, Email and Security (since lot N69-2 a regular user has none of them, so no group). Every tab has an address (lot B10): /settings/<tab> for Profile, Preferences, Plugins and About, /settings/admin/<tab> for the group (global, users, backup, email, security), and /settings/admin for its first tab. The route is settings/[...path]. An address opens its tab from the first render, choosing a tab writes its address, an unknown address or a hidden tab goes back to /settings, the first tab. The ?tab=<id> of 1.2 still opens its tab and is replaced by the tab's address. The Security tab's badge, summed on Administration, counts the security checks that need attention
  • ProfileTab: Avatar editing via AssetPickerModal, username and email editing, account deletion through AccountDeletionDialog
  • PreferencesTab: Language, currency, theme, and the Onboarding category (guide replays — see Settings Components)
  • GlobalSettingsTab: superusers only, behind an edit lock (see Settings Components); the values stay readable through the API by every signed-in user, whose app reads them
  • AboutTab: Version info (from Git tag), system info
  • UsersTab: superusers only — the accounts of the instance, each with its avatar, and the open invitations, with the invitation, reset-link and deletion dialogs (see Settings Components)
  • SecurityTab: superusers only — the configuration checks of the instance (GET /security/checks) and the browser's open-registration check, most severe first, with Check again and the passed checks folded below (see Settings Components)
  • PasswordChangeModal from profile
  • Mobile responsive with dropdown category selector

docs.title: 📦 Store Client System Overview
docs.text: Status: Implemented (Feb 2026)

docs.title: 📖 Introduction
docs.text:
LibreFolio relies on a robust and segmented store architecture. Given the complexity of tracking real-time asset prices, portfolio computations, global settings, and user navigation, the frontend uses a combination of Svelte Stores and Svelte 5 Runes ($state, $derived, $effect) located in src/lib/stores/.

The Store Client System is divided into 5 Macro-Categories, each with its own dedicated documentation page:

  1. App & UI State: Manages global UX elements (Authentication, Settings, Theme, Navigation, Toasts, Instance configuration and notices).
  2. Reference State: Stores dictionaries and basic CRUD entities (Brokers, Assets, Currencies) synced with the backend.
  3. Domain & Feature State: Heavy computational and business logic stores (Portfolio report cache, FX graph routing, Transaction ledger).
  4. Registries & Caches: Dynamic stores that spawn sub-stores per entity (Asset Prices, FX Rates, Image Previews).
  5. Core Infrastructure: Base classes and utility wrappers (EntityStore, EditBuffer, TimeSeriesStore) used to build the other stores.

docs.title: 🗺️ High-Level Architecture & UI Mapping
docs.text:
The following diagram illustrates how the major store categories interact with the Frontend UI Systems (Pages and generic components).

---
config:
  layout: elk
---
graph LR
    subgraph UI ["Frontend UI & Pages"]
        UI_Dash["Dashboard (/dashboard)"]
        UI_Port["Portfolio & Holdings"]
        UI_Set["Settings (/settings)"]
        UI_Trans["Transactions (/transactions)"]
        UI_FX["FX Rates (/fx)"]
        UI_Nav["Global Shell (Navbar/Toasts)"]
    end

    subgraph Stores ["Store Client System"]
        S_App["1. App & UI State"]
        S_Ref["2. Reference State"]
        S_Dom["3. Domain State"]
        S_Reg["4. Registries & Caches"]
        S_Core["5. Core Infra"]
    end

    S_Core -.->|extends| S_Ref
    S_Ref -->|provides entities| S_Dom

    S_App ===>|drives UX| UI_Nav
    S_App ===>|configured by| UI_Set

    S_Dom --->|powers| UI_Dash
    S_Dom --->|powers| UI_Port
    S_Dom --->|powers| UI_Trans
    S_Dom --->|powers| UI_FX

    S_Ref --->|populates dropdowns| UI_Trans
    S_Reg --->|rate series| UI_FX

The portfolio figures are not computed from live prices in the browser: the backend computes the portfolio report, and the Domain State keeps it as a session cache that refreshes in background — see Domain & Feature State.

docs.title: 🔄 Reactivity Paradigm
docs.text:
• Local State: Component-level reactivity is handled exclusively via Svelte 5 Runes ($state, $derived).
  • Global State: Cross-component data sharing is managed via exported Svelte stores (both classic .subscribe stores and new .svelte.ts reactive modules).
