None of them uses refreshVersion or requestPortfolioRefresh(): those are the user's Refresh, which spins the page's icon and says the page is busy. On the price and FX pages a store that a catch-up marked stale and that still holds points for the range (TimeSeriesStore.isStale) shows them at once and asks the server in background, with no loading state (rule D3; Registries & Caches).

docs.title: 🔁 Lazy sections after a failure
docs.text:
Two sections of the report are left out of the page's main request and asked apart: the P&L candles of the growth chart (includePnlCandles, the expensive OHLC work) and the contribution of the Period view. While its view is on screen without the section, an $effect of the panel — GrowthChart.svelte:981-985 or PositionsPanel.svelte:112-116, both in frontend/src/lib/features/dashboard/ — calls onRequestPnlCandles or onRequestContribution, which the page wires to its loader, loadPnlCandles() or loadContribution(), through pageBusy.join() (Page busy). Before Y-24, a failed report started that loop again at once: fetchReport() resolved null, the loader's finally set its loading flag back to false, and the effect, which had read the flag, asked again — an endless stream of full report requests. createLazyReportRetry() (frontend/src/lib/stores/portfolio/lazyReportRetry.svelte.ts) bounds it, one instance per section and per page:

  • Four requests at most per scope. The delays are LAZY_REPORT_RETRY_DELAYS_MS, [2_000, 4_000, 8_000], each counted from the failure before it: a scope may be asked again 2 s after its first failure, 4 s after the second, 8 s after the third, and after the fourth no more, until the scope changes or reset(). The scope is the string the page builds in reportScope(). One scope is recorded at a time: canAsk(scope) lets any other scope ask, a failure of another scope starts over, and succeeded() forgets.
  • A reactive read, no clock. canAsk reads a $state tick that moves only when a retry falls due and on reset(), so the effect that called the loader runs again by itself, and the page needs no timer of its own. No clock is read: only the timer says that a retry is due. reset() also cancels the pending timer; dispose() cancels it and wakes no reader afterwards.
  • The loader's side. Its guard reads canAsk(reportScope()) before the first await, which makes it a dependency of the panel's effect. An answer that lands after the scope changed is dropped, neither applied nor counted; otherwise the loader records failed() or succeeded() before its finally lets the loading flag go, so the effect that the flag wakes already sees the failure.
  • Dashboard (frontend/src/routes/(app)/dashboard/+page.svelte): candlesRetry and contributionRetry, disposed in onDestroy; the scope is the broker ids, start, end and currency of the request. loadContribution() checks it whoever calls it, loadAll() refreshing a stale cached contribution included. The Refresh, handleSync(), calls reset() on both.
  • Broker detail (frontend/src/routes/(app)/brokers/[id]/+page.svelte, legacy mode): the same two, disposed in onDestroy, with the broker id, dateFrom, dateTo and the currency as scope; handleRefresh() resets both. Before Y-24 the contribution looped there as on the Dashboard, but the failed candles were never asked again: pnlCandlesLoading is a plain let that nothing reactive reads, so nothing ran the chart's effect again. The retry's tick is what wakes it now.

The retry adds nothing on screen (an indicator and an error state for the candles are backlog Y-18). Its tests: frontend/src/lib/stores/portfolio/lazyReportRetry.svelte.test.ts (Vitest in jsdom, ./dev.py test front-portfolio store-unit) pins the schedule, the scope, succeeded, reset, dispose, an effect woken when a retry falls due, and that no clock is read; frontend/e2e/portfolio/lazy-report-retry.spec.ts (./dev.py test front-portfolio lazy-report-retry) drives Playwright's page clock while the section under test is answered 500: on both pages the candles and the contribution are asked four times at most, a retry that succeeds draws its candles, and a period change or the Refresh asks again.

docs.title: 🗃️ Reference State
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (Feb 2026)

The Reference State manages domain entities that act as "dictionaries" or master data. These entities are rarely mutated rapidly by the system itself but are created, updated, or deleted by the user (CRUD operations).

docs.title: 🗂️ Stores
docs.text:
All these stores are located in src/lib/stores/reference/ (with one exception).

Store API Endpoint Purpose brokerStore /brokers?include_inaccessible=true Brokers the user can see: the accessible ones with their user_role, plus the inaccessible ones with user_role: null. Lookups by id from any component (tables, selectors, badges) and role helpers (canEditBroker, getEditableBrokers). assetStore /assets/query All accessible financial instruments (Stocks, ETFs, Crypto, …), looked up by id. currencyStore /utilities/currencies ISO 4217 currencies with symbols and flags; reloaded when the language changes. suggestCurrency(value) asks /utilities/currencies/suggest what a stored value that is no ISO code stands for, once per value; a failure answers «no suggestion» and is asked again next time. countryStore /utilities/countries ISO 3166-1 countries (alpha-3 and alpha-2 codes, name, flag), looked up by alpha-3; reloaded when the language changes. sectorStore /utilities/sectors The standard financial sectors (GICS-based: Technology, Health Care, Financials, …) and their emoji. fxRoutesStore /fx/providers/routes The configured FX pairs and the currencies they reach — the two endpoints of each configured pair. Currency selectors with configuredOnly, the FX pair dialog and the risk panels use it to offer only what the user can actually convert. invalidateFxRoutes() forces a reload, e.g. after a pair is created. transactionTypeStore /transactions/types List of valid Tx Types (BUY, SELL, DIVIDEND) and their behavioral rules. (Located in transactions/)

docs.title: 📐 Architecture & Flow
docs.text:
brokerStore and assetStore are built on createEntityStore (documented in Core Infrastructure), the generic cache for user-scoped lists that modals create, edit and delete. The other stores are read-only module caches with the same shape: an idempotent ensure…Loaded() that shares the in-flight request, and, except for countries and sectors, a reactive version counter.

---
config:
  layout: elk
---
graph TD
    EntityStore["🛠️ createEntityStore (generic factory)"]
    API["🐍 Backend API (FastAPI)"]
    Modals["Create / edit / delete modals"]

    subgraph Reference_Stores ["Reference Stores"]
        B_Store["🏦 brokerStore"]
        A_Store["💼 assetStore"]
        C_Store["💶 currencyStore"]
        R_Store["💱 fxRoutesStore"]
        T_Store["📝 transactionTypeStore"]
    end

    subgraph UI_Components ["UI Components"]
        Dropdown["Forms & Dropdowns (AssetSelect, CurrencySearchSelect, TransactionTypeSearchSelect)"]
        Tables["DataTables (TransactionsTable, …)"]
    end

    EntityStore -. "builds" .-> B_Store
    EntityStore -. "builds" .-> A_Store

    API -->|"GET (load)"| B_Store
    API -->|"GET (load)"| A_Store
    API -->|"GET (read-only)"| C_Store
    API -->|"GET (read-only)"| R_Store
    API -->|"GET (read-only)"| T_Store

    Modals -->|"merge / invalidate"| B_Store
    Modals -->|"merge / invalidate"| A_Store

    B_Store -->|"Subscribe"| Dropdown
    A_Store -->|"Subscribe"| Dropdown
    C_Store -->|"Subscribe"| Dropdown
    R_Store -->|"Subscribe"| Dropdown
    T_Store -->|"Subscribe"| Dropdown

    B_Store -->|"Subscribe"| Tables
    A_Store -->|"Subscribe"| Tables

docs.title: 🔄 Reactivity & Caching
docs.text:
The stores are session caches; they never write to the backend themselves.

  1. Load once: ensureBrokersLoaded(), ensureAssetsLoaded(), ensureCurrenciesLoaded(language) and the other ensure…Loaded() functions fetch on the first call; later calls resolve at once or share the request in flight. refreshAllBrokers() / refreshAllAssets() discard the cache and fetch again.
  2. Reactivity: components subscribe to a version counter (brokerStoreVersion, assetStoreVersion, currencyStoreVersion, fxRoutesVersion, typesVersion) and read the data through plain getters (getBrokerInfo(id), getAssetInfo(id), …), which re-run when the counter moves.
  3. After a mutation: the modal that saved calls mergeBrokers / mergeAssets (a partial upsert that keeps the fields the patch does not carry) or evicts the entry with invalidateBroker / invalidateAfterMutation, which also marks the cache as not loaded so the next ensure…Loaded() fetches again. There is no optimistic update to roll back: the cache changes only after the server has answered.

docs.title: 🖼️ Broker icon hydration
docs.text:
A component that only has a partial broker ({id, name}) can ask for its icon fields with ensureBrokerIconFieldsLoaded(brokerId); BrokerIcon does it when given a brokerId and no icon field. The store calls GET /brokers/{id} and merges the answer, sharing a request already in flight for the same broker.

Since 1.2 each broker is asked at most once per cache generation: the first answer, success or error, settles the id (settledIconFieldIds), because a broker with no icon, portal URL or import plugin is a valid state, not missing data. Before this, every answer bumped the cache version, the icon effect ran again and found the fields still missing, and a page could request the same broker in a loop. invalidateBroker, refreshAllBrokers and the session reset release the settled ids, and an answer from an old session settles nothing.

docs.title: 🏭 Registries & Caches
docs.text:
Status: Implemented (Mar 2026) · asset price registry and image preview cache: Jun 2026 · stale after a price catch-up: Oct 2026 · reload of the open pages: Oct 2026 · bulk requests in batches: Oct 2026 · signal result cache: Oct 2026

The Registries & Caches category holds the client-side caches for data that the frontend loads in pieces and reuses across pages: the daily price series of each asset, the daily rate series of each FX pair, the backend signal results the detail pages already received, and the object URLs of image previews.

A registry is not a store itself: it is a module-level Map of many independent stores, one per key. It creates a store the first time its key is requested and returns that same instance on every later request.

docs.title: 🗂️ Stores
docs.text: Store Location Purpose assetPriceStoreRegistry assetPriceStoreRegistry.ts One TimeSeriesStore<AssetPricePoint> per asset and currency, keyed "{assetId}:{CURRENCY}" (e.g. "42:EUR"), holding the daily price points already loaded. Prices converted to another currency (target_currency) are cached apart from the native ones. reducedPriceCache reducedPriceCache.ts The series a card of the Assets grid draws, sampled by the backend for the card's plot (Z-29b): one entry per asset and range, with the step it was read at (resolution), the point on the fill's first day (derived.base) and the counts of days and weeks of the fill; and, apart, the comparison targets read for a card (sample_like), by card. It answers a width only if the step that width asks is the entry's own, so a resize that changes the step reads again from the backend. It marks everything stale on {kind: 'prices'}; invalidateAsset() drops what an asset's sync touched. It sits beside assetPriceStoreRegistry, which holds every day and is not touched. fxStoreRegistry fxStoreRegistry.ts One TimeSeriesStore<FxDataPoint> per currency pair, keyed by the pair slug in alphabetical order ("EUR-USD", see createPairSlug), holding the daily rates already loaded in that orientation. The FX list and the FX detail page share these stores. signalResultCache signalResultCache.ts The backend signal results of the asset and FX detail pages, kept under the exact request they answered and given back only while the price or rate stores they were computed from are unchanged: three singletons, assetChartAnswers, fxSignalAnswers and comparisonSeriesAnswers (N64, N64b). See Signal result cache. imagePreviewCache stores/files/imagePreviewCache.ts Plain Map from file ID to the object URL of the largest preview fetched for that file. LazyImage reuses it for the same or a smaller size instead of downloading the preview again; a larger size replaces the entry and revokes the old URL. Emptied, every URL revoked, when the signed-in account changes.

docs.title: 📐 Architecture & Flow (The Registry Pattern)
docs.text:
A chart shows a date range, and the user moves between ranges (another preset, a custom range) and between pages that show the same series. The stores outlive the page components, and each one remembers both the points it holds and the ranges already requested: a range that is already loaded is answered from memory, and only a range with gaps costs a price or rate request.

---
config:
  layout: elk
---
graph TD
    Page["📄 Page: assets list, asset detail, FX list, FX detail"]
    Bus["📣 portfolioMutation.ts: end of a price catch-up (notifyPricesCaughtUp)"]

    subgraph Registries ["🏭 Registries: module-level Maps"]
        AP["assetPriceStoreRegistry: 42:EUR, 42:USD, …"]
        FX["fxStoreRegistry: EUR-USD, CHF-EUR, …"]
    end

    Store["📈 TimeSeriesStore of the key: points by date, ranges fetched"]
    Gaps{"getMissingIntervals(start, end)"}
    Read["getRange(start, end).data"]
    API["🐍 POST /api/v1/assets/prices/query or POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/convert"]
    State["Page $state: chart, cards, table"]

    Page -->|"getAssetPriceStore(assetId, currency)"| AP
    Page -->|"getFxStore(slug)"| FX
    AP -->|"created on the first request, same instance afterwards"| Store
    FX -->|"created on the first request, same instance afterwards"| Store
    Bus -->|"kind: prices only, markStale() on every store"| Store
    Store --> Gaps
    Gaps -->|"no gap: read from memory"| Read
    Read --> State
    Gaps -->|"gaps"| API
    API -->|"answer"| State
    API -->|"merge(points), markFetched(start, end)"| Store

The portfolio figures do not come from these stores: the backend computes the portfolio report, and portfolioStore keeps it as a session cache — see Domain & Feature State.

docs.title: 🧠 How it Works
docs.text:
1. Getting a store: a page asks the registry for the store of its key: getAssetPriceStore(assetId, currency), which upper-cases the currency into the key, or getFxStore(slug) (getFxStoreByPair(base, quote) builds the slug first). The first request creates an empty TimeSeriesStore (stores/core/TimeSeriesStore.ts); every later request returns the same instance.
  2. Finding the gaps: store.getMissingIntervals(start, end) lists the date intervals of the range that hold no point and were never marked fetched; in a store a price catch-up made stale, the intervals not fetched since, points or not (step 5). With no gap, the page reads store.getRange(start, end).data instead of asking the backend for prices or rates (the asset detail page still asks for its events, and backend-computed signals are still requested), so narrowing or widening the range is instant once it is loaded.
  3. Fetching and merging: otherwise the data is requested, store.merge(points) upserts the answer by date, and store.markFetched(start, end) records the range as fetched (the asset pages do so only when the answer holds points). Asset prices are requested for the whole range, not gap by gap: each item of POST /api/v1/assets/prices/query carries one date_range. FX rates come from POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/convert, one item per gap, or one for the whole range when the request also asks for signals.
  4. Invalidating (explicit): after a sync or a refresh, invalidateAssetPriceStore(assetId) empties every currency store of the asset. The FX pages empty every FX store with invalidateAllFxStores() or one range of a pair with store.invalidateRange(start, end), and removeFxStore(slug) drops the store of a deleted pair.
  5. Going stale after a price catch-up: when a price catch-up on the server has updated something, notifyPricesCaughtUp() sends {kind: 'prices'} on the portfolio bus (stores/portfolio/portfolioMutation.ts, see Updating prices…). Each registry registers a listener when it is imported, under its own name (registerPortfolioMutationListener('assetPriceStoreRegistry', …), 'fxStoreRegistry'), and on that kind alone calls markStale() on every store it holds: kind: 'mutation' (among others the live-price poll writing today's candle, every 30 s on an asset's page) and kind: 'refresh' (the portfolio's Refresh) leave the stores alone. A stale store keeps its points — get, has, size, getRange and getAllSorted answer as before — and drops its fetched marks: getMissingIntervals(start, end) then returns the parts of the range that no markFetched made after the mark covers, even where the store holds points, so the next read of a range asks the server again, once; the fetches made after the mark add up. lookupFxRate takes a stale cached day for a miss: it asks the server for that day and marks it fetched, while lookupFxRateSync stays a pure cache read. invalidateAll() ends the stale state; invalidateRange() does not. Marking a store stale also renews its generation, so what was computed from its data misses too (Signal result cache). The mark ignores the points because the price and rate answers fill the days without a value backward (backward_fill_info): a loaded store holds a point for every day, so the days a catch-up filled are not gaps. And it is a mark rather than invalidateAll() because many reads are synchronous (getRange, getAllSorted, lookupFxRateSync): an emptied store would leave them blank, with nobody to reload them. The read-only getter store.isStale tells a page that the store was marked and not emptied since (it stays set until invalidateAll(); a fetch clears the gaps, not the flag). So the next visit of a price or FX page, or its next change of range, finds the gaps; when the store still holds points for the range (isStale and a non-empty getRange), the page puts them on screen at once and asks the server in background, with no loading state (rule D3, Y5-1); a store with no points for the range loads as on a first visit. A page already open during the catch-up reloads by itself, in silence: see Going stale, then reloading.
  6. Lifetime: nothing counts subscribers and nothing is evicted. TimeSeriesStore is a plain class, not a Svelte store: each page copies what it reads into its own $state. The stores stay in memory as long as the loaded app: a logout does not clear them, a page reload does. removeAssetPriceStore(assetId) exists for asset deletion, but nothing calls it.

ensureAssetPriceRangeLoaded(assetId, currency, start, end, {targetCurrency}) and ensureFxRangeLoaded(slug, start, end) wrap steps 2 and 3 in one call and return the cached points of the range; ensureFxRangeLoadedBulk does the same for several pairs in one request. They mark a range fetched even when the answer is empty or a 404, so it is not requested again; any other error (network, 5xx) leaves it unmarked, and the next call retries. ensureFxRangeLoaded loads the FX overlays of the FX detail page and the FX data of the asset pages; the other two are called only by their unit tests. The asset pages run steps 2 and 3 inline: the assets list sends POST /api/v1/assets/prices/query for every asset that misses prices or needs backend signals, in one request when they fit under the backend's caps, with a margin, and in batches otherwise (Bulk requests in batches), and the asset detail page asks for events and signals in the same request. On the FX side, loadFxRatesAndSignalsBulk loads the rates and signals of the FX list cards the same way, in one request or in batches, and lookupFxRate(base, quote, date) answers one day's rate for the transaction modals, reading the cache first (lookupFxRateSync).

docs.title: 🔔 Going stale, then reloading
docs.text:
Going stale is the other way to let go of a store: nothing is emptied, the store only says its fetched marks are out of date. Who marks it, and who asks again, after a price catch-up:

flowchart TD
    Bus["portfolio bus: kind prices"] -->|"markStale() on every store"| Store["TimeSeriesStore: points kept, fetched marks dropped, isStale true"]
    Bus -->|"after the dispatch (onPricesCaughtUp)"| Page["page on screen: assets list, asset page, FX list, FX pair page"]
    Page --> Gaps{"getMissingIntervals(start, end)"}
    Gaps -->|"no gap"| Memory["read from memory"]
    Gaps -->|"gaps, store isStale, points held"| Shown["points on screen at once, no loading state"]
    Gaps -->|"gaps, no points"| Load["loading state, as on a first visit"]
    Shown --> Ask["ask the server in background"]
    Load --> Ask
    Ask -->|"merge(points), markFetched(start, end)"| Store

The pages call onPricesCaughtUp() (Updating prices…), which runs their loader without force after the dispatch, once every store has been marked; the loader goes down the diagram above. The reduced cache of the Assets grid (reducedPriceCache) is marked stale by the same signal, and the grid reads it through the same reload.

docs.title: 🧮 Signal result cache
docs.text:
The detail pages keep their prices and rates in the stores above, but their backend signals (SMA, RSI…, the calendar rolling returns) used to be asked again at every change of mode, window, period or currency, even when nothing had changed. lib/stores/signalResultCache.ts (N64) keeps each answer under the exact request that produced it and gives it back only while the data it was computed from is the same.

  • Key: canonicalCacheKey(value) is the JSON text of a request body with the keys of every object sorted at every depth, so two bodies that differ only in the order of their properties are one key; arrays keep their order. There is no merge by intervals as for prices: a signal on [start, end] depends on its warm-up before start, so only the exact request matches.
  • Generations: the caller reads TimeSeriesStore.generation (Core Infrastructure) of the stores the answer is computed from when the request starts, and passes them to get(key, generations) and set(key, generations, value). A get hits only if the entry was stored over the same generations, same stores in the same order; any other generation is a miss and drops the entry.
  • Bounded and isolated: SignalResultCache<T> is an LRU of 32 entries (a hit becomes the most recent; a set past 32 drops the oldest), with clear() and size. Values are deep copies (structuredClone) both ways, so no caller can change what another one reads later. All three singletons are emptied when the signed-in account changes (registerClientSessionReset('signalResultCache', …), stores/app/clientSession.ts).
Singleton Page What it keeps Generations in the check Key assetChartAnswers Asset detail The answer of POST /api/v1/assets/prices/query without the prices (the price store holds them): events, backend signals and calendar returns, the comparison peers' included. assetChartAnswerForCache(answer) drops each item's prices. The price store of the asset and of each comparison peer, in the displayed currency. assetChartAnswerKey(body): the body, canonical, with each item's include_price left out, since the answer is the same whether the prices travel or come from the store. fxSignalAnswers FX detail The validated backend signal results (BackendSignalResult[]) of the pair's convert request. The pair's store. canonicalCacheKey(requestBody) of that request. comparisonSeriesAnswers Asset detail and FX detail The series of the assets the price-view comparisons draw, as loadComparisonAssetsData answered them (ComparisonAssetsLoadResult: prices, in the displayed currency, and events, per peer). The price store of each peer, in the displayed currency (the peer's own on the FX page): comparisonAnswerGenerations(ids, allAssets, targetCurrency), null (nothing is kept) when a peer is unknown to the page. comparisonAnswerKey(ids, range, targetCurrency): the distinct peer ids ascending, the range and the target currency.

A hit also needs the prices (or rates) of the range to be cached already: the asset page checks pricesFromCache and skips the cache on a forced load; the FX page checks that getMissingIntervals has no gap. On a hit the page applies the cached answer and asks nothing; on a miss it asks and, after applying the answer, writes it. Only answers the page could apply are written: signal results that parse, a calendar return that is not an error (the peers' too), never a failed request or an invalid answer.

docs.title: 🔒 Invalidation, by construction
docs.text:
No call is needed to invalidate an entry: it goes stale on its own. TimeSeriesStore.generation is a number renewed by invalidateAll(), invalidateRange() and markStale(), never by merge(), markFetched() or a read, so:

  • Refresh, a sync, an editor save, a currency change that empty or re-key a store, and a price catch-up ({kind: 'prices'} on the portfolio bus marks every store stale, step 5 above), all renew the generations of the affected stores: the next load with the same request misses, asks the server and stores the new answer. After a price catch-up the pages thus ask again, once, as they do for the prices.
  • Loading more points (a wider range, a gap filled) renews nothing: a signal answer on a range does not depend on days outside it.
  • A generation is never given twice in the app (a module-level counter), not even to a store made anew after removeAssetPriceStore().

The asset page adds an explicit clearAssetPageAnswers() (it empties assetChartAnswers and comparisonSeriesAnswers) where a kept answer may have been built from data the stores do not all show: handleRefresh() (Refresh asks everything again, the peers' calendar returns included), runSyncAsset() (a sync may change this asset, a comparison peer or a pair the converted prices use) and handleSyncPair() (the rates may have changed under a converted answer); both clear even when the sync's own response finds the page moved on. The FX page relies on the generation for its signals; for the comparison series it also empties comparisonSeriesAnswers in runSyncAsset().

The comparison series (N64b) come from the backend with the displayed currency applied, not from a store, so a peer's store generation shows only the invalidations that go through the store (an editor save of the peer, a price catch-up, a currency change); a sync of the peer or of a pair is the explicit clear above. maybeLoadComparison() of both pages keeps its fingerprint memo (comparisonAppliedFingerprint: the same request twice in a row) and, past it, asks comparisonSeriesAnswers.get(key, generations) unless the load is forced (a refresh, a sync): a period seen before comes back in the same tick, so lastComparisonLoadAskedServer stays false and no busy token opens. A miss loads, and comparisonAnswerIsCacheable(loaded) decides what is kept: an answer with a price the backend could not convert (_conversionFailed) is not.

docs.title: ⏳ Cache hits and the busy token
docs.text:
A load the cache answers shows no spinner and leaves the Refresh button still (Page busy). So on both detail pages the pageBusy token is taken only when a load asks the server:

  • loadChartData() and maybeLoadComparison() set lastChartLoadAskedServer and lastComparisonLoadAskedServer as soon as they know: true when a request goes out (or the load joins one in flight), false when the cache, the comparison memo or a price or rate store that already covers the range answers with no request.
  • trackChartLoad(), trackComparisonLoad() and trackChartAndComparison() start the load, read the flag right after the call, and wrap the load's promise in pageBusy.track() only if it is true. trackChartAndComparison() holds one token for the chart and the comparisons together if either asks.
  • The load must therefore decide before its first await: on the asset page const response = cachedAnswer ?? (await …) skips the await on a hit, so the whole load completes synchronously and the flag is already final when the caller reads it. A load that asks the server is wrapped as before.

docs.title: 📦 Bulk requests in batches
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/assets/prices/query and POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/convert refuse a request of more than 1,000 items or more than 1,000,000 item-days (422 bulk_too_many_items, bulk_too_many_days: see Bulk request limits), and the assets list and the FX list send one item per asset or pair. frontend/src/lib/api/bulkBatches.ts keeps their requests under both caps (Z-27):

  • Caps: BULK_MAX_ITEMS (1,000) mirrors the backend's MAX_BULK_ITEMS; BULK_ITEM_DAYS_BUDGET (800,000) is 80 % of its MAX_BULK_ITEM_DAYS, a margin (decision D1) because the web app only estimates the days: it sees neither an asset's first stored price nor a signal's real warm-up.
  • Estimate: bulkRangeDays(start, end, today) counts the days of a range cut as the backend cuts it, at tomorrow and 100 years back from its end (BULK_RANGE_SPAN_DAYS, 36,525); 0 when it is empty. Each caller adds what its items build beyond the range.
  • Plan: planBulkBatches() cuts the items, in order, into consecutive batches: an item joins the current batch unless that would pass either cap, and one whose estimate alone passes the budget gets a batch of its own. When everything fits there is one batch: the single request the lists sent before Z-27.
  • Groups (Z-29b): groupOf(item) names the group of an item; the members of a group are consecutive and never separated, by the plan or by the split after a bulk_too_many_days: a group's estimate is the sum of its items', and a batch of one group fails like a batch of one item. The Assets list groups a card's item with the items of its comparison targets, which name its key in sample_like.
  • Send: sendBulkBatches() sends the batches one after the other (D2: production runs one backend process). A batch refused with bulk_too_many_days is split by the refusal's own numbers into max(2, ceil(item_days / max_item_days) + 1) consecutive parts (never more parts than items), sent next, at most BULK_SPLIT_MAX_DEPTH (4) levels deep. Any other error, or a refused batch of one item or at the last level, stops the sending: the outcome keeps the answers already received, each with its batch, plus the error and the batch that failed.

The callers apply nothing until every batch has settled (D3):

  • Assets list: fetchPriceSeries() (routes/(app)/assets/+page.svelte) estimates an item (estimateEntryDays(), utils/reducedPriceQuery.ts) as its range's days, plus BULK_SIGNAL_MARGIN_DAYS (400) when it asks for backend signals, and nothing for a card's item that only gives its step to its targets (include_price: false, no signals). Each batch's raw answer goes through the worker pool (processPriceItemsInParallel()) before the next batch is sent. The assets left without an answer stay as a failed request leaves them: cached prices kept, signals untouched and reported as not updated, the error in the console. «All» resolves its start date only from a complete load.
  • FX list: loadFxRatesAndSignalsBulk() estimates an entry as its range's days, or twice that plus the same margin when it carries signals (its daily items, then its signal items with their warm-up). A signal_results[].request_index points into its own batch (batch.items[request_index]). The rates of the answered batches are merged and marked fetched; after a failure, a 404 also marks the failed batch's entries fetched, as before, and the error is re-thrown to the FX page.
  • Δ columns of both lists (X-R64): fetchAssetPeriodChanges() and fetchFxPeriodChanges() (lib/utils/periodChanges.ts) send one item per asset or pair, all up to the same as_of, through inBatches(), which calls sendBulkBatches(items, () => 0, send). No day estimate: POST /api/v1/assets/prices/period-changes and POST /api/v1/fx/currencies/period-changes have the item cap but no item-days budget, so only BULK_MAX_ITEMS cuts the batches, and no batch is ever split again, since neither answers bulk_too_many_days. The answers merge as if one request had answered, the periods taken from the first item that has any. Unlike the two callers above, which apply what the batches before a failure answered (the prices and signals of those assets, the rates of those pairs), these calls are all or nothing: a failed batch rejects the call with its own error, nothing after it is sent, and the answers of the batches before it are dropped. What stays on screen then follows the list's PeriodChangesLedger (X-R60: Assets, FX).
  • Live poll of the Assets list (X-R64): fetchCurrentPrices() (lib/services/livePriceService.ts) sends the poll's ids to POST /api/v1/assets/prices/current, which refuses more than 1,000 since R13-SEC9-1, through sendBulkBatches(ids, () => 0, send) as well: that endpoint has only the item cap. The results of every batch are mapped in order, as if one request had answered. All or nothing too: a failed batch rejects the call with its own error, as axios raised it, so that livePollFailure() still reads its Retry-After; nothing after it is sent, and the list keeps the prices of its previous poll. The batches answered before the failure have still written, though: each one persists today's candles and counts as a portfolio mutation (Still a write).

Since X-R64 the Δ columns of both lists and the Assets list's live poll no longer send one request each, outside the helper: past 1,000 items they are no longer refused for their length. And batching bounds each request, not the total. The cards of the Assets list no longer load a full daily history on «All»: each asks for the points its plot takes (Z-29b, Sampled Price Series); the FX list still does (backlog Z-29fx).

Since X-R58 a size refusal that still comes back (bulk_too_many_items, or a bulk_too_many_days on a batch of one item or at the last level) is said to the user: bulkRefusalMessage(error, t) (frontend/src/lib/api/bulkRefusal.ts) turns it into one sentence in the interface language, common.bulkRefusal.tooManyItems with the cap and the count, or common.bulkRefusal.tooManyDays with the cap only (for the FX conversions item_days is a lower bound) and a hint to choose a shorter period, which the Assets list (fetchPriceSeries(), when outcome.failed) and the FX list (the catches of fetchAllPairSeries() and fetchPairSeries()) show as an error toast, still logging it in the console; any other error gives null and is handled as before. loadFxRatesAndSignalsBulk() still re-throws on a failure, by choice, since a size refusal can only come from a mismatch between the web app's caps and the backend's: the rates of the batches answered before it stay merged and marked fetched, and their signals are lost.

docs.title: 📝 Transaction Staging State
docs.text: This document describes how LibreFolio manages the transient staging state of transactions in the frontend before they are committed in bulk to the database.

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture Overview
docs.text:
The staging state acts as a local in-memory sandbox where users can add, edit, clone, split, promote, and delete transactions. Rather than immediately saving changes, the operations are staged in the TransactionBulkModal as a list of operations.

The workspace is TransactionBulkModal.svelte. It owns the staging state, the validation and the commit, and renders its banners and its toolbar through TxBulkBanners and TxBulkToolbar (frontend/src/lib/features/transactions/bulk/), which read that state as props, write back only what they bind, and call the modal's handlers.

---
config:
  layout: elk
---
graph TD
    Store["📝 txStore (Master Ledger)"]
    BulkModal["🖥️ TransactionBulkModal<br/><small>Holds ops: PendingOp[]</small>"]
    FormModal["✏️ TransactionFormModal<br/><small>Edits op.fields: DraftFields</small>"]

    API_Val["⚡ POST /transactions/validate"]
    API_Com["💾 POST /transactions/commit"]

    Store -->|Zero-Copy Read| BulkModal
    BulkModal -->|Opens with op| FormModal
    FormModal -->|Returns edited fields| BulkModal

    BulkModal -->|Validates staged ops| API_Val
    API_Val -->|Highlights validation issues| BulkModal

    BulkModal -->|Commits batch| API_Com
    API_Com -->|Clears staging & refreshes| Store

docs.title: 🏷️ The PendingOp Tagged Union
docs.text: LibreFolio represents each staged row as a PendingOp. It is implemented as a TypeScript discriminated (tagged) union, declared with DraftFields in features/transactions/bulk/txBulkTypes.ts and held by TransactionBulkModal.svelte, that separates metadata from pure transaction data fields (DraftFields).

docs.title: State Schema
docs.text:
interface DraftFields {
    broker_id: number;
    asset_id: number | null;
    type: TransactionTypeCode;
    date: string;
    quantity: string;
    cash: { code: string; amount: string; } | null;
    tags: string[];
    description: string;
    asset_event_id: number | null;
    cost_basis_override: { code: string; amount: string; } | null;
    cost_basis_mode: 'auto' | 'manual' | null; // UI-only; null = not applicable to this type/side
}

type PendingOp = (
    | { op: 'create'; } // Brand new row
    | { op: 'edit'; txId: number; markedDelete: boolean; addedViaPicker?: boolean; } // Existing DB row
) & {
    tempId: string;
    createdSeq: number; // Keeps new rows of the same day in the order they were added
    fields: DraftFields;
    pairedWith?: string; // Set on the hidden partner op: the tempId of its visible row
    link_uuid?: string | null; // Shared pairing UUID for transfers & conversions
    inaccessible?: boolean; // Read-only marker for a partner on an inaccessible broker
    promoteFromType?: TransactionTypeCode | null; // Pre-promote type sent to the backend by a mixed promote
    _wacCache?: WacResultEntry | null; // Transient WAC result returned by validate
    wacCurrencyHint?: string | null; // WAC target currency; null = backend decides
    todos?: ImportTodo[]; // Import field todos (see below)
};

A linked pair is two ops: the visible row and a hidden partner whose pairedWith points to it.

quantity and cash.amount are decimal strings held in the workspace's sign convention: a value whose type rule demands a negative — a SELL's quantity; the cash of a BUY, a WITHDRAWAL, a FEE or a TAX — is held as its magnitude, and applySignRules() puts the sign back in every payload built for validate and commit (buildCreatePayload() and buildUpdateDiff(), in lib/features/transactions/txPayloadHelpers.ts). Every other value is held as given; under a nonzero rule, such as a TRANSFER leg's or an ADJUSTMENT's quantity, its sign is information. The conversion is magnitudeForRule(value, rule) (same file, W-B65): under the negative rule a negative value becomes its magnitude, its digits exact, trailing zeros dropped, never in exponent notation (-0.00000001 → 0.00000001, -0.020000 → 0.02); anything else comes back as given — a magnitude, a zero, a text that is no plain decimal, any value of another rule. It is idempotent, and the inverse of applySign() on the negative rule. A saved row, or a clone of one, is read in through it (fieldsFromTx), its cash exactly, no longer through Number; an imported row takes the same convention in txCreateItemToPendingOp, which still reads its cash, whatever the rule, through Number.

On Apply the Form pushes back a create-shaped payload, signed as a create is sent (buildCreatePayload(), or buildDualCreatePayloads() for a pair). applyFormPayload() copies it into the row's DraftFields, reads the signed quantity to derive cost_basis_mode, and as its last step brings the quantity and the cash back to the workspace's convention with magnitudeForRule(). Every Apply goes through it — a new row, an edited one, both halves of a pair — so an untouched Apply gives the quantity and the cash back as the row held them (W-B65). Before, the row kept the signed values: an untouched Apply on a one-satoshi SELL showed -0.00000001 in its cell, and closing the workspace asked to discard, though the row stayed original (see Derived Row Status below).

docs.title: 1. Zero-Copy Originals
docs.text: For edits (op: 'edit'), the staging state never stores a copy of the database row. The single source of truth is always the txStore. The original values are read live on-demand via txStoreGet(op.txId). This ensures that if the transaction is modified elsewhere, the staging state remains in sync without stale data risks.

docs.title: 2. Derived Row Status
docs.text:
Row status is calculated dynamically at runtime. It is never stored as an editable property. The helper function deriveStatus(op) computes it instantly based on Svelte reactivity:

Operation Mode Condition Derived Status Description op.op === 'create' Always new A newly appended transaction row op.op === 'edit' markedDelete === true delete Row marked to be removed op.op === 'edit' fields match txStoreGet(txId) original Unchanged row op.op === 'edit' fields differ from txStoreGet(txId) edited Row has local modifications

The comparison goes through collectUpdate() → buildUpdateDiff(), which signs the draft and the saved row alike (applySignRules()) and compares their decimals exactly (fieldEq()): a magnitude held for a negative rule matches the signed value saved, so the sign convention never shows in the status.

The close guard is stricter. Closing the workspace — ✕, Cancel, Escape or a click on the backdrop — goes through requestClose(), which first asks Discard Changes? when hasUnsavedChanges() finds that serializeOps(ops) differs from initialOpsKey, the key serializeOps() (lib/features/transactions/bulk/bulkDisplay.ts) took when the rows were seeded. The key is the JSON of every op, hidden partners included: its DraftFields as held (not through applySignRules()) and its other keys. It leaves out tempId and createdSeq, names pairedWith and link_uuid by the rows they point at, and sorts object keys, so a reset (resetRow, resetAll), which rebuilds the saved rows under new identities, reads no change. Unlike the status, it compares values as held: a signed value where the row held a magnitude is a change. And JSON.stringify keeps a key set to null but drops an absent one, so an Apply whose payload carries no WAC currency (_wac_currency_hint: null) deletes the op's wacCurrencyHint (patchRowFromForm, and the partner in patchDualRowFromForm) instead of writing null: both mean that the backend decides (opToTxFields() uses the hint only when it holds a currency), and a row starts without the key. Before W-B65 it wrote null, and every such Apply, even on a DEPOSIT, asked to discard.

docs.title: ✂️ Split & Promote Integration
docs.text:
The tagged union structure of PendingOp simplifies complex composite operations in Svelte:

  • Split (handleSplitRow) breaks a linked pair (TRANSFER, CASH_TRANSFER, FX_CONVERSION) into two independent rows; nothing is deleted.
  • A pair merged in the workspace and not saved yet — an entry of pendingPromotes, two saved rows or a saved and a new one — is not split: its merge is undone, whichever row the pair shows (undoPendingPromote, J-67). Each row takes its source type back (a saved row's from the store, txStoreGet(txId).type; a new row's promoteFromType) and its quantity and cash back in the workspace's sign convention (magnitudeForRule(), as fieldsFromTx reads them), the new row's link_uuid is cleared, both rows are visible, and the entry leaves pendingPromotes: the save sends neither the promote nor a split, where a mixed merge's save used to be refused (promoteRefNotFound). The description and the tags chosen for the merge stay. Two new rows merged are no such entry: they split as a new pair.
  • A saved pair is queued in pendingSplits as {id_a, id_b}; the backend splits it at commit. Meanwhile the partner op loses pairedWith and becomes a visible row next to its former main row.
  • A new pair is split locally: both ops lose their link and take the standalone types of SPLIT_TYPE_MAP (the client mirror of the backend's split rules, e.g. WITHDRAWAL and DEPOSIT for FX_CONVERSION).
  • Promote (executePromote) links two independent rows (e.g. a WITHDRAWAL and a DEPOSIT) into a pair of the matching type; both ops take the target type and collapse into one paired row, the receiving op becoming the hidden partner (collapseIntoPaired). Before the type changes, every branch below moves the sign into the values (applySignRules(), under each row's own type rule), so a WITHDRAWAL's cash, held as its magnitude, turns negative: the target is free-sign (CASH_TRANSFER, FX_CONVERSION), and collapseIntoPaired picks the row to show by the sign of its cash — the paying one, its cash negative, on the From: line of the pair's cells, the receiving one on To: (J-67; before, only a merge of two new rows did). For a merge with a saved row the save does not depend on it: a saved row is not sent as an update (resolveOps() skips the ids in pendingPromotes), and a new row is created under its source type (promoteFromType), whose rule signs it again — applySign() is idempotent.
  • Two saved rows are queued in pendingPromotes ({id_a, id_b}) for the backend.
  • Two new rows simply share a fresh link_uuid.
  • A mixed pair (one saved, one new) is queued as {id_a, link_uuid_b}, and the new row keeps its pre-promote type in promoteFromType, because the backend derives the target from the two source types.

e2e/transactions/tx-bulk-promote-split.spec.ts pins both (J-67): a saved WITHDRAWAL merged with a new DEPOSIT shows the withdrawal on From: (F1), its cash negative (F2); Split pair on a new WITHDRAWAL merged with a saved DEPOSIT, before the save, gives each row its type back, and the save creates the withdrawal alone, with no update and no promote (F3); G guards two new rows, merged, split and saved as two creates.

docs.title: 💡 Promote suggestions
docs.text:
The workspace looks for the two halves of a transfer or an exchange and offers to promote them (TransactionBulkModal.svelte, with the pure helpers of lib/features/transactions/bulk/promoteSuggest.ts):

  • The green banner (promote-suggest-banner) lists bannerSuggestions: pairs of standalone rows that are both in the workspace — two new rows, two saved rows, or a new row and a saved one (mixedPromotePairs). The two dates are at most Max Δ days apart (maxDeltaDays, 0–14), and findPromoteMatch finds a rule on the context buildPromoteCtx reads from the two rows: its broker, currency, asset and quantity constraints hold — the quantities exactly opposite for an asset transfer — and the target type accepts the rows' event links (eventA/eventB, each row's asset_event_id). No promote target accepts one, so a row linked to an asset event, such as an ADJUSTMENT linked to a split, is never offered. The two sides must also cancel exactly: a cash transfer's amounts (cashAmountsCancel), and an asset transfer's quantities of one asset (assetQuantitiesCancel, in promoteSuggest.ts). Both helpers give each value the sign its type implies, then compare the decimal strings exactly, as the backend compares Decimals: a relative tolerance of 1e-9 would let a one-cent difference through above about 10 million, a pair the backend refuses. It shows the first five pairs, and promotePairOrder (promoteHelpers.ts, J-66) tells which row of a pair pays: the one whose cash, signed by its type (buildSignedCash, its sign read exactly by exactDecimalSign, as cashAmountsCancel reads it), is negative — a WITHDRAWAL pays whether the workspace holds its cash as its magnitude (the sign convention above: fieldsFromTx, txCreateItemToPendingOp, and since W-B65 applyFormPayload()) or signed — and never a row without cash, or whose amount is no plain decimal. Five readers share that answer: the banner's order, the paying row first when the other one receives (swapped); the implied rate shown for an exchange, from that row to the other (from → to, to ÷ from in computeFxConversionInfo); the market rate it is compared with, fetched in the same direction on the paying row's date (the fxMarketCache effect); the left of Merge all (All left), the row the banner lists first (mergeAllSuggestions); and the Merge dialog, which shows that row first, its text first in the combined description it opens with (triggerPromoteFromSuggestion; executePromote still gets the rows in the suggestion's order) — all but the dialog used to read the stored amount, where a WITHDRAWAL held as its magnitude never paid and the pair could show backwards. executePromote asks findPromoteMatch again before it promotes, so its refusals hold for every promote of the workspace: Merge, Merge all, and the selection toolbar's promote button (selectedForPromote, promote-toolbar-confirm), which also asks cashAmountsCancel of a cash transfer and assetQuantitiesCancel of an asset transfer.
  • The 💡 button (tx-bulk-suggest-import, and the row action suggest) lists importableSuggestions: saved transactions that POST /transactions/promote-suggest proposes as the other half of a row, and that are not in the workspace yet. The search runs debounced on the standalone saved rows and on the new rows that have a type, a broker, a date and an amount or a quantity, asked about under a negative id (newRowSuggestId). It uses the banner's Max Δ days window: the slider's value (maxDeltaDays) goes as tolerance_days, and the backend searches each row's date ± that many days, so 0 means the same day only. A row dated at the calendar's edge (0001-01-01, 9999-12-31) gets its window cut there (shift_date(), W-B71) and simply finds nothing; it used to fail the whole search. The window is part of the search key, so moving the slider starts a new search, debounced like any other change. Each input also carries the row's asset_event_id (TXPromoteSuggestInput, where null or 0 means not linked): the backend skips, for a linked row, every rule whose target type refuses the link — today all of them, so the row gets an empty list — and never returns a saved row linked to an event as a candidate for such a rule, so the 💡 never offers a pair that an event link would keep from merging. The 💡 opens TransactionPickerModal on those candidates; once one is added, the banner offers the pair.
  • Merge (promote-suggest-link-<idx>) promotes one pair: executePromote at once, or PromoteMergeModal first, showing the two rows in the banner's order (promotePairOrder), when they differ in description or tags. Where the descriptions differ, the dialog counts the merged one under its textarea (promote-merge-desc-counter, data-state ok or over), in code points as Python's len() counts them (textLength() and TX_DESCRIPTION_MAX_LENGTH, 500, in promoteHelpers.ts). Past 500 — 500 itself fits — the textarea is aria-invalid, a message names the limit (promote-merge-desc-too-long) and Confirm promotion (promote-merge-confirm) is disabled: the backend would refuse the merged notes with string_too_long (W-B70).
  • Merge all (N) (promote-suggest-merge-all, when mergeAllPairs holds more than one pair) opens PromoteAllModal.svelte (promote-all-modal), which asks one PromoteAllStrategy for every pair, merge preselected at each opening: left (All left, the description and tags of the row the banner lists first), right (All right, those of the other row) or merge (Combine: mergeStrings of the two descriptions and mergeTagSets of the tags, PromoteMergeModal's default). mergeAllPairs is the banner's pairs in their order (all of them, not only the five shown), without any pair that shares a row with an earlier one: when two suggestions share a row, only the first is kept and the row is merged once. N, and the count the dialog shows, is mergeAllPairs.length: the pairs to merge, not the suggestions. mergeAllSuggestions then walks mergeAllPairs; it skips a pair whose rows no longer match a rule, or with a row already merged (isPaired), and passes executePromote what resolvePromoteAllFields(strategy, left, right) (promoteHelpers.ts) returns: {} when the two rows agree on description and tags, otherwise the chosen side's values or both combined. With merge, a pair whose combined description would pass 500 characters gets null instead: it is left unpromoted, for Merge and its dialog, and never saved with one side's notes only. After the walk, notify() counts those pairs in a warning toast (transactions.promote.mergeAllLeftTooLong) and the app event tx.bulk.promote-all.left-for-manual-merge, detail {pairs} (W-B70).
  • The save gate. requestCommit first counts the suggestions nobody looked at (unseenSuggestionCount): the 💡 candidates until the picker has been opened once (suggestPickerSeen), and the banner's pairs until a click lands anywhere in the banner (promoteBannerSeen, an onclickcapture). With any left, Save All opens Suggestions you have not looked at (tx-bulk-unseen-suggestions) instead of saving. Save anyway marks both as seen and goes on to the warnings gate (requestCommitPastSuggestions). Show the suggestions — and closing the dialog — opens the picker when it was never opened and has candidates, and otherwise marks the banner as seen and scrolls it into view. Both flags reset only when the workspace opens again.

PromoteAllModal.test.ts (Vitest, jsdom) pins the dialog: the three answers, Combine by default and again at every opening, and cancelling. e2e/transactions/tx-import-scalable-transfers.spec.ts runs the whole path on two Scalable exports: the banner's Merge (S1), the 💡 and a new + saved pair (S2), the save gate (S3) and Merge all (S4). The 500-character limit (W-B70) is pinned by promoteHelpers.test.ts (textLength(), resolvePromoteAllFields()), PromoteMergeModal.test.ts (the counter and the disabled confirmation) and e2e/transactions/tx-bulk-promote-cost-basis.spec.ts (PC7: Merge all merges the pair that fits and leaves the one past it, with the toast and the app event).

docs.title: 📤 Validation & Commit Pipeline
docs.text:
Staged operations undergo a two-phase validation before they are persisted:

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as User / UI
    participant BulkModal as TransactionBulkModal
    participant FormModal as TransactionFormModal
    participant Backend as Backend API

    %% Phase 1: Local & Staging Validation
    Note over User, FormModal: Phase 1: Editing & Local Validation
    User->>FormModal: Edit transaction fields
    FormModal->>FormModal: Local checks (required fields, exact quantity, sign rules)
    FormModal->>BulkModal: Push the row on Apply (onPushDraft)

    %% Phase 2: Server-Side Validation
    Note over BulkModal, Backend: Phase 2: Server-Side Validation
    BulkModal->>Backend: POST /transactions/validate (Staged Ops)
    Backend->>Backend: Run Access Checks & Balance Walk
    Backend-->>BulkModal: Return Validation Issues & WAC Previews
    BulkModal->>User: Display inline warnings & WAC indicators

    %% Phase 3: Commit Batch
    Note over User, Backend: Phase 3: Atomic Batch Commit
    User->>BulkModal: Click Save All
    BulkModal->>Backend: POST /transactions/commit (creates, updates, deletes, splits, promotes)
    Backend->>Backend: Access Check & execute_batch() inside DB Transaction
    Backend-->>BulkModal: Return Commit Result (Success)
    BulkModal->>BulkModal: onCommitted(response), then close
    BulkModal->>User: Host page reloads its data

docs.title: 1. Local Sanity Checks
docs.text: Before a row reaches the workspace, the single-row form checks what it can know locally: the fields its type requires, the exact quantity and the sign rules (see Client-Side Validation).

docs.title: 2. Server-Side Validation (/transactions/validate)
docs.text:
LibreFolio defers all deep ledger validation (such as checking if a sale results in a negative cash or asset balance) to the backend.

  • Auto-validation: while the workspace holds at most 50 operations (AUTO_VALIDATE_THRESHOLD, hidden partners included) and at least one row is ready for validation, every edit schedules a run, debounced by createValidateScheduler (500 ms by default); an idle run also fires after 60 s without changes.
  • Manual validation: above that threshold the automatic runs stop, and once more than 50 rows are visible the toolbar says so (Auto-validate is OFF … press ⚡️ Validate now before commit). The ⚡ Validate now button works at any size.
  • Import hand-over: the rows handed over by the Import Wizard (onImportBatch) are validated once right away, whatever their number (scheduler.trigger('manual')), so even a large import shows its issues without a click. Later edits follow the two rules above.

docs.title: 3. Batch Commit (/transactions/commit)
docs.text:
Save All passes two gates first (requestCommit): the suggestions nobody looked at, then the warning todos (below).

Then resolveOps() turns PendingOp[] into create, update and delete operations, and buildBatchPayload() assembles them, together with the queued splits and promotes, into a single atomic batch:

  • Creates: Array of brand-new transaction data (a pair contributes both legs).
  • Updates: Key-value diffs containing only modified fields vs the original txStore data.
  • Deletes: List of transaction IDs marked for deletion.
  • Splits / Promotes: the pairs queued in pendingSplits and pendingPromotes.

Empty lists are left out of the payload. When the server refuses the batch (committed: false), the workspace stays open with the issues; on success it calls onCommitted and closes.

docs.title: 🗺️ The WorkspaceIntent Pattern
docs.text:
To keep components decoupled and avoid passing large, stale arrays of transaction objects, LibreFolio uses a declarative routing pattern to open the bulk transaction workspace.

Instead of passing copies of data, the calling component (such as the transactions page or toolbar) sets a reactive intent property on the TransactionBulkModal:

export type WorkspaceIntent = 
  | { action: 'create'; }                      // Open empty grid to add new rows
  | { action: 'import'; }                      // Mount BRIM wizard to parse files
  | { action: 'edit'; txIds: number[]; }       // Edit specific existing rows
  | { action: 'delete'; txIds: number[]; }     // Pre-mark specific rows for deletion
  | { action: 'clone'; txIds: number[]; };     // Copy existing rows, keeping their dates

Upon receiving the intent, TransactionBulkModal resolves the actual row data directly from txStore (the Single Source of Truth) using the provided transaction IDs. This ensures the modal always operates on the most up-to-date ledger state.

docs.title: 📥 ImportTodo (BRIM Staging Integration)
docs.text:
When running a file import (action: 'import'), LibreFolio's backend BRIM parser plugins might accept a transaction but leave some fields incomplete if they cannot be computed automatically (e.g. cost basis on complex corporate mergers). These are returned to the frontend as a list of field_todos (BRIMFieldTodo schema).

On the frontend, these are loaded into the bulk modal grid as an array of ImportTodo objects (lib/features/transactions/txPayloadHelpers.ts) linked to the staging row:

export interface ImportTodo {
    field: string;                  // The field requiring manual input (e.g. 'cost_basis_override')
    severity: 'blocker' | 'warning'; // blocker = prevents saving; warning = to verify before saving
    reasonCode: string;             // Machine-readable code (e.g., 'stock_merger')
    message: string;                // Human-readable fallback message
    evidence?: BrimEvidence[];      // Source-data tables backing the todo (raw rows + plugin comment)
    context?: Record<string, unknown>; // Numbers behind the todo
}

docs.title: Validation & Resolution Lifecycle:
docs.text:
1. Highlighting: A row with a blocker todo gets the row-todo-blocker row class. Above the grid, two folded banners list the open todos: the blockers in red (each with its evidence tables) and the warnings (auto-derived fields to verify). Each entry shows the row number and the todo's message.
  2. Going to the row: clicking an entry calls jumpToTodoRow(), which pages the grid to that row and highlights it through DataTable.navigateToRowId() — the same mechanism as a validation issue. The highlight clears on the next row click or key press in the table. A todo of a hidden partner leads to its visible row (pairedWith); a row filtered out of the table gives a warning toast instead (The affected rows are hidden by the table filters.).
  3. Blocker Prevention: If any row has a todo with severity: 'blocker', the Save All button is disabled and its tooltip reads Complete all required fields before saving.
  4. Warnings gate: with warning todos left, Save All — once past the suggestions gate — opens Verify auto-derived fields?, listing them, with Save anyway and Review.
  5. Resolution: the user opens the row in the nested TransactionFormModal (double-click or the row action) and applies it. Applying re-checks the row's todos with remainingTodos() (lib/features/transactions/bulk/bulkTodos.ts): a todo is resolved when its field now holds a value. A missing cost basis has a second answer: Auto (WAC) mode, where the backend computes the cost. Applying the form with Auto selected clears the "enter the cost" todo (cost_basis_override) even when Auto was already the mode, because remainingTodos() looks only at the row's resulting cost_basis_mode. Once its last blocker is resolved, the row no longer holds Save All back.

docs.title: 🧹 Selection on the Transactions page
docs.text: The Transactions page (routes/(app)/transactions/+page.svelte) empties its selection — the table's checkboxes and the toolbar's selectedRows — with clearSelection() after every operation that ran: any save from the bulk workspace (add, edit, clone, delete, import) through handleBulkCommitted, and a successful link (promote) or unlink (split) of a pair. The rows the selection pointed at may have changed or disappeared. Cancelling — closing the workspace without saving, or dismissing a confirmation — keeps the selection. The Refresh button also clears it, together with the filters.

docs.title: 🧪 Test Walkthrough
docs.text:
This section guides you through the LibreFolio test suite. Understanding the tests is one of the best ways to understand the codebase.

Modular Test Runner Architecture

LibreFolio uses a modular test orchestrator package located in scripts/test_runner/ to manage, register, and isolate coverage for all backend and frontend test suites. For details on how the runner is structured and how to extend it, see the Test Runner Architecture documentation.

docs.title: 🚀 Running Tests
docs.text:
All tests are executed through dev.py:

# Run everything
./dev.py test all

# Run a single category
./dev.py test api all

# Run one action (here: backend/test_scripts/test_api/test_auth_api.py)
./dev.py test api auth

# Run only the tests whose name matches (pytest -k)
./dev.py test api auth test_register_success

# List available tests (without running them)
./dev.py test api all --list

Test names go only to the actions that take them, which ./dev.py test <category> --help marks [TEST_NAME]. all, db create, db populate and most Vitest unit actions (such as front-fx fx-unit) take none: a name after one of them stops the command with exit code 2 before it does anything, even with --list — after all, name the action instead (./dev.py test services <action> test_foo).

The action is required, --list included: all lists the whole category, an action name narrows the list to that action (on a backend category, to the first test file the action runs). On a backend category --list runs pytest --collect-only and prints the test names grouped by file and class; on a frontend category it prints the test.describe() and test() titles of the category's Playwright spec files (Vitest files are not listed).

docs.title: 🌐 Global Flags
docs.text:
Flag Description -q / --quiet Suppress the detailed test output. Without it, the output is verbose --coverage [py\|js\|all] Run with code coverage tracking. The language is optional and defaults to all --cov-clean-backend Together with --coverage, clean Python coverage from backend tests (htmlcov-backend/ + .coverage_data/backend) --cov-clean-backend-e2e Together with --coverage, clean Python coverage collected during E2E runs (htmlcov-backend-e2e/ + .coverage_data/frontend) --cov-clean-js Clean JS/Svelte coverage (coverage-js/). Manual utility only — a --coverage js run cleans it by itself --workers N\|auto Run isolation-safe backend units in parallel, for a whole category or suite only: naming one action, or filtering by test name (pytest -k, which only a named action takes), keeps them serial. The same number sets the Playwright workers, capped at half the logical cores. Default 1 — the serial path, unchanged. auto is half the cores --fail-fast Stop handing out work after the first red. The default runs everything and reports every failure --resume Continue from the last failure: skip the tests the run cache records as passed and run the rest (see Run cache and timing campaign below) --fresh-run Delete the run cache before starting, and open a new timing campaign. Without a category it only deletes the cache --run-status Print the run cache (per suite, the tests passed and where the last run stopped) and exit without running anything --log-file PATH Tee the full run output (build, pytest and Playwright output included) to PATH while still printing it. An existing file is overwritten --log-dir PATH One log file per test unit, plus shared-backend.log, the shared test backend's output for the whole run: when a backend start fails, the runner prints the last 30 lines that start wrote. Defaults to .testLog; --log-dir "" turns it off --no-consolidate Keep one invocation per action. By default a whole category or suite is grouped: one pytest invocation per backend category (db and external keep one per action) and, per frontend category, one vitest run plus one Playwright run per project selection (desktop only, or desktop and mobile), split into batches of 8 specs under JS coverage --no-shared-server Do not start the one test backend the run shares: each pytest process and each Playwright run that needs a server starts its own, and the --workers parallel pass keeps only the units that touch neither database nor server. Slower — an escape hatch --assume-scoped Experiment for the --workers parallel pass of backend categories: every pytest unit counts as parallel-safe, whatever isolation class the catalogue gives it, except the units with a written exclusive_because. No effect at one worker or with --no-shared-server. The reds are the work list, not a regression --test-port PORT / --port PORT Port of this run's test backend. Defaults to TEST_PORT, then 6041 — see Isolated Runtime Lanes --data-dir PATH Test data root of this run. Defaults to LIBREFOLIO_TEST_DATA_DIR, then backend/data/test — see Isolated Runtime Lanes --lane-setting NAME=VALUE A setting of this run's instance, repeatable: only LIBREFOLIO_PROFILE, LIBREFOLIO_FRAME_PROTECTION and LIBREFOLIO_CSP_REPORT_ONLY. None by default: the instance's defaults — see Lane Settings

Where the flags go

They belong to ./dev.py test, so they come before the category: ./dev.py test --workers 4 --coverage py services all.

--cov-clean-frontend is deprecated

It still works as an alias for --cov-clean-backend-e2e, but the old name was misleading: it never cleaned JavaScript coverage. It cleans the Python coverage collected while Playwright drives the backend.

JS coverage has no accumulate-or-clean choice to make. Its istanbul counters belong to the build that produced them — the statement maps follow that build's instrumented sources — so they cannot survive a frontend rebuild: kept across one, old counts would land on statements that have since moved. A run that collects JS coverage (--coverage js|all on a front-*, all-frontend or all suite) therefore always wipes frontend/coverage-js/ first. --cov-clean-js exists only to clean it outside a run.

Two axes, not one

--coverage selects which language is measured; the suite you run selects which tests drive it. See Coverage Model for the full picture — including why the report formerly called htmlcov-frontend/ actually measured Python.

Run cache and timing campaign

The serial suites and the consolidated passes record their outcomes in scripts/test_runner/.run_cache.json (gitignored): per suite, the tests that passed and the last one that failed. --resume skips the recorded passes, --run-status summarises the file, --fresh-run deletes it. A serial suite that passes in full drops its own entry; the consolidated passes keep theirs (consolidated:<category>) until the next --fresh-run. The --workers parallel pass neither reads nor writes the cache, so a --resume runs its units again.

A second gitignored file, scripts/test_runner/.campaign.json, times the campaign: the run that a --fresh-run opens and every run after it. Each run of a category or suite closes with a Timing section: this invocation's duration, the wall-clock time since the campaign opened (the gaps where fixes were written included) and, once the campaign holds several invocations, their count and summed machine time.

docs.title: 🛣️ Isolated Runtime Lanes
docs.text:
A test run owns one runtime lane: the port of the backend it starts and talks to, and the data directory that backend uses (sqlite/app.db, uploads, broker reports, logs). Runs that are active at the same time — one per worktree — must each have their own lane: never point two active runs at the same port or the same data directory.

Flag Environment variable Default Lane resource --test-port PORT / --port PORT TEST_PORT 6041 Port of the test backend --data-dir PATH LIBREFOLIO_TEST_DATA_DIR backend/data/test Root of the test data

A flag wins over the shell environment, which wins over the checkout's .env. A relative data path resolves against the root of the checkout that runs the command, so each worktree's default data directory is already its own. The port is machine-wide, so every worktree that runs tests at the same time needs a different one — on the command line, or as TEST_PORT in that worktree's .env. If you set LIBREFOLIO_TEST_DATA_DIR to an absolute path, give each worktree a different one as well.

A lane runs on the instance's defaults. Of the checkout's .env and of the shell it keeps only the ports, the production data directory, HOST, the log level, the version a release job froze and every LIBREFOLIO_TEST_* name (kept_in_a_test_lane() in scripts/cli_base.py); every other setting of the instance (secrets, profile, block, mail, accounts, plugins) is removed from its environment, and in test mode Settings does not read .env either. A test that needs a setting sets it itself — see Security → Test lanes and the instance's configuration.

# A second worktree, testing while another one uses the default lane (6041)
./dev.py test --test-port 6141 api all

The runner applies the lane before any setup, server start, or child process (configure_test_runtime in scripts/cli_base.py), and stops with an error when:

  • the port is outside 1–65535 or equals the production port (PORT, default 6040);
  • the data directory overlaps the production data directory (backend/data/prod, or LIBREFOLIO_DATA_DIR) in either direction, sits inside — or holds in its managed subdirectories — a directory marked as production data, or has a managed path that escapes it or aliases production data.

The resolved TEST_PORT and LIBREFOLIO_TEST_DATA_DIR are exported to every child process, together with a random lane identity (LIBREFOLIO_TEST_LANE_ID). A backend counts as ready only when /api/v1/system/test-lane-health echoes that identity in the X-LibreFolio-Test-Lane header, and the shared test server refuses to start on a port that another process already holds: it never reuses or terminates another lane's server. The contract is covered by ./dev.py test utils runtime-isolation.

docs.title: Lane Settings
docs.text:
A lane may set three settings of its own instance with --lane-setting NAME=VALUE: LIBREFOLIO_PROFILE, LIBREFOLIO_FRAME_PROTECTION and LIBREFOLIO_CSP_REPORT_ONLY (TEST_LANE_SETTABLE in scripts/cli_base.py). They are what a hosting provider's instance runs with, so the suite can meet the managed profile, its frame protection and its report-only content security policy for real. Nothing else can be set this way: never a secret, a port, a data directory or one of the runner's own names.

# The cloud smoke on a lane of its own, in the managed profile (on any lane, it runs only when named)
./dev.py test --test-port 6181 --data-dir /tmp/lane-h --lane-setting LIBREFOLIO_PROFILE=managed front-utility cloud-smoke

# Repeatable: the managed profile with its frame protection off
./dev.py test --lane-setting LIBREFOLIO_PROFILE=managed --lane-setting LIBREFOLIO_FRAME_PROTECTION=false front-utility auth
  • Checked first. One option per setting, before the category like every flag of ./dev.py test. parse_lane_settings() checks them before the environment is touched: each item NAME=VALUE, a name of the three, given once, with a value that is not empty and holds no ; and no line break. Anything else stops the run with an error that names the item. The value itself (selfhosted or managed, a boolean for the two switches) is checked by the instance, when it reads its settings.
  • Set after the cleanup, then handed down. configure_test_runtime() sets them once it has removed the developer's settings, and exports LIBREFOLIO_TEST_LANE_SETTINGS: the NAME=VALUE pairs sorted by name and joined by ;. That name is under the kept LIBREFOLIO_TEST_* prefix, so the variable travels down the lane's process tree (the runner, Playwright, dev.py server --test, uvicorn's workers), and each nested configure_test_runtime() sets the settings again after its own cleanup. Playwright's webServer (WEB_SERVER_ENV in frontend/playwright.config.ts) passes the variable on only when it is set.
  • From the command line only. A LIBREFOLIO_TEST_LANE_SETTINGS line in the checkout's .env stops the run, with or without --lane-setting and under pipenv run too, with an error that names --lane-setting and .env: a forgotten line would silently change every lane of the checkout. A run's children never read .env (PIPENV_DONT_LOAD_ENV=1, set by configure_test_runtime() and by Playwright's webServer), so they keep applying the settings they inherited.
  • Shown. The runner prints them in one info line: Test lane settings: LIBREFOLIO_PROFILE=managed.
  • A manual test server. ./dev.py server --test --lane-setting LIBREFOLIO_PROFILE=managed starts one with the same settings. Without --test, --lane-setting stops the command with exit code 1, before any build.

A managed lane is still a test lane: test mode is on, with its test-only providers and the test users, whose passwords are in frontend/e2e/fixtures/test-users.ts. The managed profile refuses test mode only outside a test lane, and the lane identity above makes every process of the run one: see Security → Configuration Checks. ./dev.py test utils runtime-isolation covers the lane settings too.

docs.title: 🔍 Provider Filter Flags (external, all, all-backend)
docs.text:
Flag Description --providers CODE [CODE ...] Only test these provider(s) --exclude-providers CODE [CODE ...] Exclude these provider(s) from testing 
# Skip yfinance when Yahoo Finance is down
./dev.py test external asset-providers --exclude-providers yfinance

# The same flags work with all and all-backend
./dev.py test all --exclude-providers yfinance
./dev.py test all-backend --providers ECB justetf

See available provider codes

Run ./dev.py test external -h to see all available provider codes (Asset, FX, BRIM), dynamically discovered from the source tree.

docs.title: 🖥️ Frontend Flags
docs.text: Frontend test categories support additional flags (--headed, --debug, --ui). See the Frontend Tests Overview for details.

docs.title: 📋 Test Categories
docs.text:
LibreFolio organizes tests into 16 categories — seven backend, nine frontend — grouped by layer:

Category Command What It Tests External ./dev.py test external all Provider integrations (FX, assets, BRIM) — no server needed Database ./dev.py test db all SQLite schema, migrations, constraints, persistence — no server needed Services ./dev.py test services all Business logic in the service layer Utils ./dev.py test utils all Helper functions and utility modules Schemas ./dev.py test schemas all Pydantic model validation API ./dev.py test api all FastAPI endpoints (auto-starts server) E2E ./dev.py test e2e all Backend end-to-end with API interaction Front-Utility ./dev.py test front-utility all Auth, settings, files, select, image crop, onboarding, layout, scheduler (Playwright) + core and component units (Vitest) Front-Broker ./dev.py test front-broker all Broker list, CRUD, detail page, deletion recovery (Playwright) + broker helpers (Vitest) Front-User ./dev.py test front-user all Multi-user isolation, broker sharing (Playwright) + auth and client-session stores (Vitest) Front-FX ./dev.py test front-fx all FX list, detail, add-pair, editor, CSV import, sync, bulk actions (Playwright) + EditBuffer, TimeSeriesStore, fxStoreRegistry (Vitest) Front-Asset ./dev.py test front-asset all Asset list, detail, modal, data editor, merge, classification (Playwright) + price store, chart aggregation (Vitest) Front-Transaction ./dev.py test front-transaction all Transaction modals, table, bulk operations, WAC, import wizard (Playwright) + payload and commit helpers (Vitest) Front-Portfolio ./dev.py test front-portfolio all Dashboard charts, banners, page cache, privacy masking, risk analysis (Playwright) + portfolio and risk stores (Vitest) Front-AI-Export ./dev.py test front-ai-export all AI Export panel, catalog, session memory, contracts (Playwright) + AI Export and signal units (Vitest) Front-Designer-Lab ./dev.py test front-designer-lab all Designer Lab: live preview in another tab, element picker, neutrality (Playwright) + Lab units (Vitest)
