docs.title: 🔧 Backend Categories
docs.text:
• External — Tests the provider plugins, without the backend server. The FX and asset provider tests call the real external APIs, so they need an internet connection; the BRIM import plugins are tested on the local sample files of backend/app/services/brim_providers/sample_reports/, with no network.
  • Database — Tests the database layer directly (schema validation, persistence, migrations). Uses an isolated test SQLite file.
  • Services — Tests the service layer business logic, often with mocked dependencies.
  • Utils — Tests utility modules and helper functions.
  • Schemas — Tests Pydantic model validation, serialization, and edge cases.
  • API — Integration tests for FastAPI endpoints. Automatically starts a test server if needed.
  • E2E — End-to-end backend tests with real API interaction and database state.

docs.title: 🎭 Frontend Categories (Playwright)
docs.text:
Every frontend category also runs Vitest unit files next to its Playwright specs. The categories without a walkthrough page list their actions with ./dev.py test <category> -h.

  • Front-Utility (./dev.py test front-utility all) — Tests UI components and app-wide flows: authentication, settings tabs, file upload and management, search selects, image cropping, the onboarding tour and guides, layout, and the scheduler settings.
  • Front-Broker (./dev.py test front-broker all) — Tests the Brokers module: broker list and CRUD, detail page, deletion recovery, creation feedback.
  • Front-User (./dev.py test front-user all) — Tests multi-user scenarios: data isolation between users, broker sharing with RBAC.
  • Front-FX (./dev.py test front-fx all) — Tests the FX module: pair list, detail chart, add-pair modal, data editor, CSV import, sync, bulk actions, and FX-specific API calls.
  • Front-Asset (./dev.py test front-asset all) — Tests the Asset module: asset list, detail page, create/edit modal, data editor, merge, classification.
  • Front-Transaction (./dev.py test front-transaction all) — Tests the Transactions module: bulk and form modals, transactions table, split and promote, WAC, import wizard.
  • Front-Portfolio (./dev.py test front-portfolio all) — Tests the Dashboard and the risk views: charts, data-quality banners, page cache, privacy masking, risk analysis.
  • Front-AI-Export (./dev.py test front-ai-export all) — Tests AI Export: panel, catalog, session memory, public contracts.
  • Front-Designer-Lab (./dev.py test front-designer-lab all) — Tests the debug-only Designer Lab: live preview in another tab, element picker, neutrality of the idle client.

Frontend tests require a running server

Before its Playwright specs, a frontend category builds the frontend when its sources changed (or when the build is not of the kind the run needs, instrumented for JS coverage or plain), and the test database is repopulated and the E2E users created, by the runner or by Playwright's globalSetup. The specs then run against a backend that also serves the build: the run's shared backend or, with --no-shared-server, the one Playwright starts itself. Use --headed to watch the browser in action.

docs.title: File Architecture
docs.text:
Coverage data is stored in SQLite databases and HTML reports:

LibreFolio/
├── .coveragerc                 # Coverage configuration (parallel=true, sigterm=true)
├── .coverage                   # Working copy — swapped in/out by scripts/test_runner/
├── .coverage_data/
│   ├── backend                 # Accumulated backend-only coverage DB
│   ├── frontend                # Python coverage of the last E2E coverage run
│   └── 00_archive/             # Earlier versions, compressed (scripts/test_runner/_archive.py)
│       ├── backend_20260416_093012.tar.xz
│       ├── backend_clean_20260416_095107.tar.xz
│       └── frontend_20260415_142033.tar.xz
├── htmlcov-backend/            # HTML report: Python, driven by backend tests
├── htmlcov-backend-e2e/        # HTML report: Python, driven by frontend E2E
├── htmlcov/                    # HTML report: Python, combined
└── frontend/coverage-js/       # JS/Svelte coverage (unit, e2e, combined)

An archive is named <label>_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>.tar.xz (.tar.bz2, .tar.gz or plain .tar when the Python build lacks lzma). The end of a coverage run archives the database it is about to overwrite (backend or frontend); --cov-clean-backend and --cov-clean-backend-e2e archive the database they remove (backend_clean, frontend_clean); and before a coverage run, a database that cannot be read or was recorded in the other measurement mode (statement instead of branch, or the reverse) is moved into the archive (backend_mode_change, frontend_mode_change, and root_mode_change for .coverage).

File Updated by Contains .coverage pytest-cov (working copy) Temporary — swapped in before pytest, swapped out after .coverage_data/backend run_command() finally block Accumulated backend-only coverage, grows with each backend test run .coverage_data/frontend _finalize_coverage() Server subprocess coverage from Playwright E2E htmlcov-backend/ _finalize_coverage() HTML report from .coverage_data/backend htmlcov-backend-e2e/ _finalize_coverage() HTML report from .coverage_data/frontend htmlcov/ _finalize_coverage() HTML report from merged backend + frontend frontend/coverage-js/ _finalize_js_coverage() JS/Svelte reports — see Coverage Model

docs.title: Full Run (clean baseline)
docs.text:
# Full test suite with coverage: first the language (all = Python + JS), then the suite (all)
./dev.py test --coverage all all

# Clean stale data before a fresh run
./dev.py test --coverage --cov-clean-backend --cov-clean-backend-e2e all

all is both a coverage language and a suite name, and --coverage takes the word after it as its language whenever that word is one. So name the language before the suite all (--coverage all all, --coverage py all): ./dev.py test --coverage all uses all as the language, is left without a suite and stops with test category required. Any other category can follow --coverage directly (./dev.py test --coverage services all).

docs.title: Incremental Runs (append to existing)
docs.text:
After a full run, you can run individual test files and the coverage accumulates in the existing .coverage database thanks to --cov-append:

# Run only specific tests — coverage is added to the existing DB
./dev.py test --coverage services static-uploads
./dev.py test --coverage services fx-core
./dev.py test --coverage utils day-count

# The HTML report (htmlcov-backend/) is regenerated after each run
# The .coverage_data/backend snapshot is updated automatically

Incremental coverage workflow

  1. Run ./dev.py test --coverage all all once to establish a baseline
  2. Write new tests
  3. Run only the new test file with --coverage — it appends to the existing DB
  4. Check the updated report with ./dev.py test coverage show backend

docs.title: Viewing Reports
docs.text:
./dev.py test coverage show backend    # open htmlcov-backend/
./dev.py test coverage show frontend   # open htmlcov-backend-e2e/
./dev.py test coverage show combined   # open htmlcov/ (merged)

./dev.py test coverage show js         # open frontend/coverage-js/combined/
./dev.py test coverage show js-unit    # open frontend/coverage-js/unit-combined/
./dev.py test coverage show js-e2e     # open frontend/coverage-js/e2e/

docs.title: Coverage Isolation
docs.text:
The .coveragerc uses parallel = true (required for frontend subprocess coverage). This causes coverage combine to pick up all .coverage.* files and delete them.

To keep backend and frontend coverage properly isolated, the test runner uses a swap-in/swap-out pattern with a dedicated .coverage_data/ folder:

Before pytest (run_command):
  .coverage_data/backend ──copy──▶ .coverage    (restore accumulated DB)

During pytest:
  pytest-cov runs with --cov-append → appends to .coverage
  parallel=true writes .coverage.HOST.PID, then combines → .coverage
  (.coverage_data/ folder is safe — combine only looks in root)

After pytest (finally block):
  .coverage ──copy──▶ .coverage_data/backend    (save accumulated DB)

After all tests (_finalize_coverage):
  .coverage_data/backend → htmlcov-backend/     (generate HTML report)
  .coverage_data/frontend → htmlcov-backend-e2e/
  merge both → htmlcov/                          (combined report)

Why .coverage_data/ instead of .coverage.backend?

With parallel = true, coverage combine picks up all files matching .coverage.* in the current directory. A file named .coverage.backend would be consumed and deleted. Files in a subdirectory are safe.

docs.title: Frontend Coverage Architecture
docs.text:
This section is about Python coverage driven by the E2E suite

For JS/Svelte coverage — the frontend's own code — see Coverage Model.

Backend coverage during Playwright E2E tests requires a precise signal chain so that coverage run receives SIGTERM (not SIGKILL) and can write .coverage.<pid> data.

4 required elements:

  1. gracefulShutdown in playwright.config.ts — sends SIGTERM instead of SIGKILL
  2. exec in the shell command — shell replaces itself with dev.py
  3. os.execvpe() in dev.py — replaces itself with pipenv run coverage run
  4. sigterm = true in .coveragerc — coverage catches SIGTERM and writes data
graph LR
    PW["Playwright<br/><small>gracefulShutdown<br/>sends SIGTERM</small>"]
    SH["/bin/sh<br/><small>exec (level 1)</small>"]
    DP["dev.py<br/><small>os.execvpe (level 2)</small>"]
    PP["pipenv<br/><small>os.execvpe (level 3)</small>"]
    CR["coverage run<br/><small>-m uvicorn</small>"]

    PW -->|SIGTERM| SH
    SH -->|"replaces itself"| DP
    DP -->|"replaces itself"| PP
    PP -->|"replaces itself"| CR

    style CR fill:#4caf50,color:#fff

All four steps share the same PID. When Playwright sends SIGTERM, it reaches coverage run directly. The .coveragerc option sigterm = true catches it and writes .coverage.<pid> before the process exits.

Without gracefulShutdown

By default, Playwright sends SIGKILL to terminate the webServer. SIGKILL cannot be caught or handled — the process is killed instantly and no coverage data is ever written. This is the most common cause of missing htmlcov-backend-e2e/.

Without exec at any level

If any level uses subprocess.run() instead of exec, SIGTERM only reaches the parent process. The child (coverage run) becomes an orphan and no coverage data is written.

The grace window must be wide enough

SIGTERM is only half the story: Playwright falls back to SIGKILL once the gracefulShutdown.timeout expires. Flushing the coverage data file takes real time, and the original 5 s was not always enough — when it wasn't, the run lost all backend coverage and reported only a terse No .coverage.* files found! at the end, which looks like a configuration problem rather than a race.

The timeout is therefore widened to 30 s whenever COVERAGE_BACKEND is set, and is 10 s otherwise: the server has its own shutdown budget (LIBREFOLIO_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, 8 s by default), and the window gives it that plus a margin. The runner's shared backend gets the same two windows (SHUTDOWN_GRACE_COVERAGE and SHUTDOWN_GRACE_PLAIN in scripts/test_runner/_server.py), so outside coverage its Shared backend ignored SIGTERM warning means that the server broke its own budget.

docs.title: 📡 API Endpoint Tests (api)
docs.text: These are integration tests that run against a live backend server. They verify the full request-response cycle.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: To ensure that the API endpoints are reachable, return the correct status codes, and produce the expected JSON responses.

docs.title: ✅ Prerequisites
docs.text:
Do not start a server. The runner starts one, once, and every module talks to it over API_BASE. A module that starts its own uvicorn takes port 6041 from everyone else and makes the whole category serial by construction. The only thing to check before a run is that the port is free: lsof -ti:6041 must come back empty.

That single shared backend is what lets the category run concurrently — and what makes the run test something the old design could not: whether the application actually holds up under concurrent requests. It has already answered twice, both times with a product defect rather than a test one (a cache that silently stopped caching, and a SQLite busy_timeout left at zero so a second writer failed instead of waiting).

The test database needs no preparation either. Several units (brim, uploads, …) sign in as the fixture users e2e_test_admin and e2e_test_user, which db populate seeds. A whole api run reseeds the database of its lane first; before one action run on its own (./dev.py test api brim), the runner checks that database and reseeds it only when those users are missing, saying so in one line. After a run that recreated the database empty (services, db create), there is no db populate --force to remember.

docs.title: ⛔ The semantics: verify, never assume
docs.text:
Modules share one database, and now share it at the same time. Three consequences, normative in .github/instructions/backend-testing.instructions.md:

  • Never identify data by position. response.json()[0] is a claim about everybody else's rows. Search the response for the id you created.
  • Never assert a count you did not create. len(items) == 4 breaks the moment a neighbour adds one; len([i for i in items if i["id"] == mine]) == 1 says what you mean.
  • Never reach a third party over the network. A test that calls the real ECB is testing today's weather. MOCKFX and MOCKFX_FAIL exist for this, and return fixed values — which lets the assertion be exact instead of "some number arrived".

A unit that genuinely cannot share the database declares exclusive_because= with the surface it mutates. There is currently one in the whole backend; see runner_architecture.md for what justifies a second.

docs.title: 🔑 Key Tests
docs.text:
• Auth: Login, token refresh, protected routes.
  • Assets CRUD: Create, read, update, delete assets via API (19 tests).
  • Assets Metadata: Classification params, sector/geo distributions (4 tests).
  • Assets Patch: Partial field updates including identifiers (8 tests).
  • Assets Provider: Provider assignment, probe with valid/invalid params, Scheduled Investment via API (16 tests).
  • Assets Prices: Bulk upsert, query with backward-fill, sync idempotency, events in response, bulk multi-asset sync (9 tests).
  • FX: Currency pair CRUD, conversion, sync, delete (25+ tests).
  • Brokers: CRUD, sharing, multi-user access control.
  • Transactions: Import and manage transactions.
  • Uploads: File upload and media management.
  • Settings: Global and user settings.
  • Utilities: Country codes, currency utils.
  • AI Export API: Runtime catalog, versioned snapshots, authorization, applicability, typed problems, and cross-domain request contracts.

docs.title: 🧠 AI Export Test Stack
docs.text:
AI Export spans API, service, probe, frontend unit, and live Playwright layers:

# Catalog, snapshots, authorization, typed API problems
./dev.py test api ai-export

# Backend components, datasets, analyses, sampling, runtime, and composition
./dev.py test services ai-export

# Strict request/response/catalog schemas
./dev.py test schemas ai-export

# Fast unit tests for probe helpers; does not run a real prompt probe
./dev.py test utils ai-export-probe-helpers

# Frontend runtime, renderer, clipboard, memory, and Signal unit tests
./dev.py test front-ai-export unit

# Focused live UI concerns
./dev.py test front-ai-export panel
./dev.py test front-ai-export catalog
./dev.py test front-ai-export memory
./dev.py test front-ai-export contract

# Compatibility alias for all four Playwright concerns
./dev.py test front-ai-export cutover

# Canonical frontend AI Export gate: unit + Playwright
./dev.py test front-ai-export all

# Ensure every remaining test file is registered
./dev.py test check-orphans

# Accumulate backend AI Export coverage
./dev.py test --cov-clean-backend --coverage services ai-export
./dev.py test --coverage schemas ai-export
./dev.py test --coverage api ai-export
./dev.py test --coverage utils ai-export-probe-helpers

docs.title: 🚀 Running
docs.text:
# All API tests
./dev.py test api all

# AI Export API only
./dev.py test api ai-export

docs.title: Coverage Model
docs.text:
LibreFolio measures coverage on two independent axes. Keeping them apart is the single most important thing to understand about the reports — most of the confusion around the older report names came from collapsing them into one.

Axis Question it answers Values Language Which code is being measured? py (Python backend) · js (JS/Svelte frontend) Suite Which tests are driving it? backend pytest · Playwright E2E · vitest unit

The two axes are orthogonal. A Playwright E2E run drives both languages at once: it exercises the frontend in the browser and the backend through HTTP.

graph LR
    BE["pytest<br/><small>backend suites</small>"]
    E2E["Playwright<br/><small>E2E suites</small>"]
    UNIT["vitest<br/><small>unit suites</small>"]

    PY[("Python<br/>coverage")]
    JS[("JS / Svelte<br/>coverage")]

    BE --> PY
    E2E --> PY
    E2E --> JS
    UNIT --> JS

    style PY fill:#3776ab,color:#fff
    style JS fill:#f0db4f,color:#000

docs.title: The six reports
docs.text:
Report Language Driven by Opened with htmlcov-backend/ Python backend pytest ./dev.py test coverage show backend htmlcov-backend-e2e/ Python Playwright E2E ./dev.py test coverage show frontend htmlcov/ Python both, merged ./dev.py test coverage show combined frontend/coverage-js/unit-combined/ JS/Svelte vitest ./dev.py test coverage show js-unit frontend/coverage-js/e2e/ JS/Svelte Playwright E2E ./dev.py test coverage show js-e2e frontend/coverage-js/combined/ JS/Svelte both, merged ./dev.py test coverage show js

Why htmlcov-backend-e2e/ and not htmlcov-frontend/

The folder used to be called htmlcov-frontend/, which suggested it measured frontend code. It never did: it measures Python, driven by the frontend's E2E suite. The HTML title was already correct ("Frontend E2E → Backend Coverage") — only the folder name lied. Frontend code coverage now lives under frontend/coverage-js/.

docs.title: The --coverage flag
docs.text:
./dev.py test --coverage all            # both languages (default when omitted)
./dev.py test --coverage py all         # Python only
./dev.py test --coverage js front-asset all

--coverage takes an optional language. When omitted it means all, so every pre-existing invocation keeps working unchanged:

./dev.py test --coverage api all        # still valid — 'api' is the suite, not a language

docs.title: all means "everything measurable in that suite"
docs.text:
Not "everything, always". Asking for something a suite cannot produce is an error, not an empty report:

Suite What all collects backend (api, db, services, schemas, utils, external) Python only Playwright E2E Python + JS vitest unit JS only

./dev.py server --coverage stays boolean

A server process can only ever measure Python. The flag is deliberately not generalised there, and the argv normaliser that makes --coverage api all work is scoped to the test sub-command so it cannot corrupt the Playwright webServer command line.

docs.title: How JS coverage is collected
docs.text:
vitest     ──(istanbul provider)────▶ unit/<time>-<pid>/coverage-final.json ──▶ unit-combined/ ─┐
                                                                                                ├──▶ combined/
Playwright ──(window.__coverage__)──▶ e2e-raw/worker-<slot>-<pid>.json     ──▶ e2e/           ─┘

Both levels speak istanbul, end to end; paths are relative to frontend/coverage-js/. While the tests run, each level only writes JSON files — one per vitest process, one per Playwright worker, holding the sum of that worker's tests — the same role .coverage.<pid> files play on the Python side before coverage combine. Across workers nothing is merged until the run is over: then _finalize_js_coverage() (scripts/test_runner/_coverage.py) calls frontend/scripts/js-coverage-report.js once per arrow on the right. The script merges its inputs with istanbul-lib-coverage — same file, same statement map, hit counts summed — and writes a coverage-final.json, an HTML report and a console summary. combined/ is built from the two level reports, and only when both exist; with a single level, that level's report is the final one.

The moving parts:

File Role frontend/vite.config.ts E2E level — vite-plugin-istanbul instruments the build when COVERAGE_INSTRUMENT=1 frontend/vitest.config.ts Unit level — vitest's istanbul provider (@vitest/coverage-istanbul), on when COVERAGE_JS=1 frontend/e2e/fixtures/playwright.ts The jsCoverage fixture — reads window.__coverage__ after every test frontend/e2e/fixtures/js-coverage-sink.ts The worker's running sum of those slices, written to one JSON per worker frontend/scripts/js-coverage-report.js Merges, remaps and filters its inputs into one report scripts/test_runner/_frontend_common.py _ensure_frontend_build() — builds the instrumented frontend, and checks that it is scripts/test_runner/_coverage.py Wipes frontend/coverage-js/ before the run, builds the three reports after it

Nothing survives from one run to the next: _clean_js_coverage_dirs() deletes the whole frontend/coverage-js/ at the start of every run that collects JS coverage. The counters belong to the build that produced them — istanbul's statement maps follow that build's instrumented sources — so data kept across a rebuild would add old counts onto statements that have since moved. A directory that still cannot be deleted after three attempts stops the run, rather than let it report stale data.

Why istanbul, and no monocart any more

Until August 2026 the E2E level read Chromium's V8 coverage of the bundles, and monocart-coverage-reports walked those ranges back through the sourcemaps to the .svelte and .ts files. But V8 reports an empty branch map for a Svelte template: on a component with a single {#if} exercised from both sides, V8 saw no branch where istanbul saw two. Every {#if}, {:else} and {#each} of the app was outside the count and only <script> blocks were measured — when the build switched to istanbul instrumentation, the branches counted on .svelte files went from 0 to 11 620. A build that carries its own counters also left monocart without a job, and monocart left the project.

docs.title: The Playwright fixture
docs.text:
frontend/e2e/fixtures/playwright.ts is a barrel: every spec imports test and expect from it instead of from @playwright/test. It adds an auto fixture, jsCoverage, that steps aside unless COVERAGE_JS=1. Even then there is nothing to start before the test — the instrumented build counts by itself — so the whole job happens in the teardown:

  1. read window.__coverage__ from every page of the test's browser context (a page that has already closed is skipped) — about 17 MB of JSON per test on the instrumented build;
  2. merge it into the worker's sum, an istanbul CoverageMap held by the worker-scoped fixture jsCoverageSink (e2e/fixtures/js-coverage-sink.ts), with the same istanbul-lib-coverage merge the report uses. No file is written per test.

window.__coverage__ is keyed by source file, not by bundle chunk, and holds the statement, branch and function maps of every module the page loaded. Its positions are those of the module as Vite transformed it; each entry carries the sourcemap back to the source (inputSourceMap), and the report script follows it — see detail 3 below.

The sum is written to one file per worker, frontend/coverage-js/e2e-raw/worker-<parallelIndex>-<pid>.json, every 20 tests that brought counters (FLUSH_EVERY_TESTS) and once more when the worker stops. Each write goes to a .tmp file renamed over the old one, so a kill mid-write leaves the previous sum whole — the report skips a file it cannot parse without saying so. Playwright stops a worker normally after a failed test and after its last one, and both run the final write; only a worker killed outright (out of memory, or force-killed) skips it, and loses at most the tests since its last write.

A new worker also absorbs the files of dead workers that held its parallelIndex before it: it merges them into its sum and deletes them once its own file, which now contains them, has been written. Under JS coverage the runner splits a category into Playwright runs of at most 8 specs (_JS_COVERAGE_CHUNK in scripts/test_runner/_consolidate.py), and Playwright replaces a worker after every failed test, so a full run starts a hundred or more worker processes; with absorption it still leaves about one file per parallel slot. A file whose pid is still alive is never touched. A worker killed in the instant between writing its file and deleting the absorbed ones would count those tests' hits twice — hit counts change, covered and total do not.

Until 8 November 2026 the fixture wrote one file per test instead, about 17 MB each and some 30 GB over a full run, all kept until the report. That design answered a real crash: the V8-era fixture kept every payload in memory — sources and sourcemaps included — and over the 25 spec files of a consolidated category, run in one worker, it reached 8 GB and took the worker down. An istanbul map does not grow that way. FileCoverage.merge replaces a file's hit counts and maps instead of appending a payload, and the bulk of a slice — the inputSourceMap, with the sources inside — is kept once per source file, from the first slice that loaded it. The map is bounded by the number of modules in the build, not by the number of tests: about one slice's size for the worker's whole life. Summing is associative, so the worker sums merged by the report give exactly the numbers the per-test files gave. _JS_COVERAGE_CHUNK was measured against the V8 accumulator, and stays as a bound on how long one worker lives.

When no page exposes window.__coverage__ and the build has no instrumentation sentinel, the fixture warns once per worker that nothing will be collected — the case of Playwright launched by hand against a plain build.

The collection has a time budget of its own

jsCoverage is registered with timeout: JS_COVERAGE_TIMEOUT_MS (120 s). A fixture without a timeout has its teardown charged to the slot Playwright gives the test's after-hooks — the test timeout again, 30 s, shared with every afterEach and every other teardown. Under load the collection overran it: in the full coverage run of 12 October 2026, 15 tests that pass in 11–19 s on their own went red after 40–49 s with Tearing down "jsCoverage" exceeded the test timeout of 30000ms. With a slot of its own the test keeps its whole budget, and a slow collection fails under its own name: Fixture "jsCoverage" timeout of 120000ms exceeded during teardown. 120 s is four times the 30 s it overran, and still short enough for a hung page.evaluate to fail instead of holding the worker. The option is set unconditionally: without COVERAGE_JS the teardown returns at once and the slot can never fire, so every run exercises the registration the coverage run relies on.

The unit level: one report per vitest process

vitest measures with its own istanbul provider (@vitest/coverage-istanbul, provider: 'istanbul' in frontend/vitest.config.ts), switched on by enabled: process.env.COVERAGE_JS === '1': the runner exports the variable once and every vitest it launches inherits it, so no command line carries --coverage. It measures src/**/*.{js,ts,svelte} minus the test files, __tests__/, __mocks__/ and app.d.ts, and writes a json report at the end of every process. A run launches vitest several times — once per frontend category, or once per action with --no-consolidate — and in a shared directory each process would delete the previous one's report, so each writes into its own coverage-js/unit/<time>-<pid>/. They are merged afterwards, like the E2E files.

docs.title: Four non-obvious details
docs.text:
1. The build must really be instrumented — and the runner checks. vite-plugin-istanbul installs itself only for vite serve unless told otherwise, so vite.config.ts sets forceBuildInstrument: true (and checkProd: false). Without it, vite build produces an ordinary bundle and the run measures nothing while still reporting success. _ensure_frontend_build() therefore does not trust the flag: it builds with COVERAGE_INSTRUMENT=1 and Node's heap raised to 8 GB — instrumenting all of src with sourcemaps does not fit the default — then looks for the __coverage__ global in the chunks under frontend/build/_app/immutable/ and stops the run when it is missing.

  2. The kind of build is recorded beside it. The frontend auto-build reuses any build whose sources have not changed, and timestamps cannot tell an instrumented build from a plain one. So a verified instrumented build gets a sentinel, frontend/build/.coverage-instrumented, and when the kind a run needs differs from what the sentinel says, the rebuild is forced — in both directions: a coverage run never measures a plain build, and a normal run never tests an instrumented one (the sentinel goes with it). Under COVERAGE_JS=1, playwright.config.ts also passes COVERAGE_INSTRUMENT=1 and the larger heap to its webServer, so a rebuild started by the test server reproduces the same kind instead of laying a plain bundle over the instrumented one. An instrumented build must never ship: scripts/docker/check_frontend_build.sh fails the image build when it finds the sentinel.

  3. Each level is remapped before the levels meet. vite-plugin-istanbul runs after the rest of the Vite pipeline (enforce: 'post'), so its counters are positioned in the transformed module: formatPercent.ts reported its first statement at line 2, inside the docblock. vitest's provider remaps before writing, and put the same statement at line 36, where it is. istanbul matches statements by position; two coordinate systems do not line up, so it appends instead of merging. js-coverage-report.js therefore merges each input on its own, follows the inputSourceMap its entries carry (a no-op for the unit level, already remapped), re-keys every file to its frontend-relative src/… path — the remapper returns absolute paths, the unit level relative ones, and two keys for one file merge into neither — and drops the followed map, so that a report can be fed back in. Only then do the levels meet. combined/ is built from the two level reports rather than from the raw data again: re-reading it would repeat minutes of sourcemap work.

    How this fails

    The broken report still generates, still lists every file, and still shows plausible percentages. The symptom is in the denominator: the first combined report counted 119 291 statements — exactly 83 527 + 35 764, the sum of its two levels — with every file both levels measured counted twice, and a percentage lower than the truth. If you change the merge, compare the totals the script prints: a combined statement total equal to unit + E2E means files are being appended, not merged.

  4. Only src/ carries counters. The plugin instruments src/**/* with the .js, .ts and .svelte extensions and always skips node_modules; vitest measures src/**/*.{js,ts,svelte} — by extension, because a bare src/** once had the provider instrument a .DS_Store, and the run died on a SyntaxError. Third-party code never gets counters, so there is nothing to tell apart afterwards. The report script still filters every input: only keys that normalise to src/… are kept, and test files, __tests__/, __mocks__/ and the generated API client src/lib/api/generated.ts are dropped — the client is crossed on every call, so it is covered by construction and would lift the percentage without anyone having tested anything.

docs.title: How Python coverage reaches spawned children
docs.text:
.coveragerc already declares concurrency = multiprocessing,thread,gevent, which lets a running tracer follow forked children (e.g. uvicorn --workers N). It does nothing for a spawned child — backend/app/services/risk/quant/spawn_worker.py starts a fresh interpreter that inherits the environment but no tracer, so the quant workers measured 0 % while being very much alive.

The fix is coverage.py's documented subprocess recipe, wired by the test runner:

  1. backend/test_scripts/_coverage_sitecustomize/sitecustomize.py calls coverage.process_startup() at interpreter startup.
  2. Whenever a run collects coverage, scripts/test_runner/_common.py (apply_subprocess_coverage_env) sets COVERAGE_PROCESS_START=<repo>/.coveragerc and prepends that directory to PYTHONPATH on every child it spawns (pytest workers, the shared backend, Playwright → its webServer). Python's site module then imports the sitecustomize in every interpreter of the process tree.
  3. Each child reads the repo .coveragerc (parallel = true), starts its own tracer, and writes .coverage.<host>.<pid>.<rand> next to the parent's data file — where the existing coverage combine steps already pick it up.

Three load-bearing details:

  • The guard is the feature. Outside a coverage run COVERAGE_PROCESS_START is unset and the module is a no-op — production interpreters pay nothing. When the variable is set, a failure to start coverage must crash the spawn bootstrap (surfacing as a test failure) instead of silently dropping data. coverage.process_startup() is itself idempotent, so coexisting with the a1_coverage.pth that coverage 7.14 installs in the virtualenv is safe.
  • Not every interpreter has coverage installed. Along the spawn/exec chain there are interpreters that never run measured code (the Homebrew Python hosting the pipenv launcher): a ModuleNotFoundError on import coverage is tolerated for exactly those.
  • The sitecustomize chain-execs the next one down sys.path. Python imports only ONE sitecustomize — the first found — so prepending ours shadows the interpreter's own. Homebrew Python ships one that rewrites sys.prefix from the Cellar path to the opt prefix and exposes /opt/homebrew/lib/pythonX.Y/site-packages; when it is shadowed, pipenv becomes unimportable and every pipenv run … child of the server/test flow dies at import. The file therefore finds and execs the next sitecustomize down the path — do not remove that block. The full post-mortem lives in the devWiki at LibreFolio_devWiki/wiki/problems/sitecustomize-shadows-homebrew-python.md.

docs.title: Reading the reports
docs.text:
Coverage is a map, not a grade

There are deliberately no blocking thresholds. Svelte 5 compiles templates into closures: the remap is reliable about "was this component reached" and much less so about "is line X covered".

On the defects actually found during beta testing, coverage would have flagged roughly half of them — the ones caused by code that never ran. It says nothing about code that runs and is simply wrong.

Running under coverage doubles as a slow-environment stress test

Python instrumentation slows the backend down enough to turn latent races into deterministic failures. A spec that passes without --coverage and fails with it is worth investigating: it has usually found a real timing bug, not a measurement artefact.

docs.title: Finding the gaps
docs.text:
An HTML report tells you the percentage. It does not tell you which untested code is worth a test. coverage-report does:

./dev.py test coverage-report --lang js --summary          # counts by category
./dev.py test coverage-report --lang js --category js_store   # the detail
./dev.py test coverage-report --lang js --priority high --json

Without --lang js the same command analyses the backend JSON, exactly as before — one analyser, two languages, identical filters and output modes.

The input is picked automatically: combined, then e2e, then unit-combined, whichever exists. Pass --input to point elsewhere.

Category Covers JS_FEATURE src/lib/features/ — AI export, import wizard, asset grouping JS_STORE src/lib/stores/ — shared client state JS_API src/lib/api/, src/lib/services/ JS_UTILITY src/lib/utils/, src/lib/features/risk/ — pure functions, the cheapest to test JS_CHART src/lib/charts/ — chart building and signal overlays SVELTE_UI .svelte component blocks JS_ROUTE src/routes/ — pages and layouts JS_ACTION src/lib/actions/ JS_I18N, JS_INFRA, JS_OTHER plumbing, workers, types

Two things to know about the JS numbers

Svelte components have no function names. The compiler turns markup into closures, so entries appear as block@142 — the line, which is what you need to find the code anyway. .ts files keep their real names, which is why the JS_UTILITY / JS_STORE sections are the most readable and the best place to start.

Statements are attributed by line range. istanbul does not record which statement belongs to which function, so a nested closure is counted both for itself and for its parent. Use the numbers to rank untested code by weight, not to quote a percentage.

docs.title: Cleaning
docs.text:
./dev.py test --coverage --cov-clean-backend --cov-clean-backend-e2e all

JS coverage directories are cleaned automatically at the start of every run that requests js or all, since the counters belong to one build: istanbul's statement maps follow that build's instrumented sources, so counts kept across a rebuild would land on statements that have since moved (see How JS coverage is collected).

docs.title: 🗄️ Database Layer Tests (db)
docs.text: These tests interact directly with the SQLite database file to verify its integrity and behavior. They do not require the backend server to be running.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: To ensure the database schema, constraints, and data persistence are working correctly.

docs.title: 🔑 Key Tests
docs.text:
• Schema Validation: Checks that all tables, columns, and constraints exist as defined in the SQLAlchemy models.
  • Data Integrity: Verifies that CHECK constraints (e.g., positive quantities) and foreign keys are enforced.
  • Persistence: Tests basic CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations on models like Asset, Transaction, etc.

docs.title: 🚀 Running
docs.text: ./dev.py test db all

docs.title: 🎯 End-to-End Tests (e2e)
docs.text: These tests verify the full application stack, from the frontend UI down to the database.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: To ensure that user flows (e.g., logging in, viewing the dashboard) work correctly in a real browser environment.

docs.title: ✅ Prerequisites
docs.text: None to arrange by hand: the runner starts the backend and the frontend build for you. The one thing to check is that port 6041 is free — lsof -ti:6041 must come back empty.

docs.title: 🔑 Key Tests
docs.text:
• Login Flow: Verifies that a user can log in and is redirected to the dashboard.
  • Dashboard: Verifies that the dashboard loads and displays data.

docs.title: 🚀 Running
docs.text:
./dev.py test front-transaction all      # one domain
./dev.py test all-frontend               # everything

docs.title: ⛔ The semantics: verify, never assume
docs.text: Every spec shares one database and one backend with every other spec, and increasingly shares them at the same time. A spec that assumes it is alone is not simpler — it is broken, and running one worker was only hiding it. The normative form of the rules lives in .github/instructions/frontend-testing.instructions.md; what follows is why they exist.

docs.title: Position
docs.text: Never .first() on an unfiltered locator, never .nth(0), never "the first row". Filter to something the spec itself created — a name carrying a timestamp — and if the table pages, walk the pages until you find it. .first() on an already-filtered locator is fine: it resolves to one element by construction.

docs.title: Count
docs.text: toHaveCount(4) is a claim about everyone else's data. toHaveCount(1) on a locator filtered to your own row is a claim about yours.

docs.title: Time
docs.text:
waitForTimeout() is forbidden. It is a bet on machine speed that concurrency loses, and it is the single largest source of dead time in the suite — 885 calls declaring 410 seconds of sleep per run when they were first counted.

Wait for the condition that matters, not for the clock:

// ✘ waits for the field to exist, not to be filled
await page.waitForTimeout(2000);
await expect(input).toBeVisible();

// ✔
await expect(input).not.toHaveValue('');

docs.title: And when there is nothing to wait for
docs.text:
That is the interesting case, and it is not a prompt to find a cleverer selector. If no observable signal says the operation finished, the user cannot tell either: the sleep is the symptom, the diagnosis is that a state of the system is invisible.

The fix serves both at once — publish the state the component already has:

<!-- the list loads in two waves: rows first, then prices per row -->
<div data-testid="assets-page" aria-busy={busy} data-busy={busy ? 'true' : 'false'}>

await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="assets-page"][data-busy="false"]');

The same contract exists for charts. ECharts emits finished when a render pass — animations included — completes, but nothing in the DOM says so. attachChartReady() (frontend/src/lib/utils/chartReady.ts) publishes it on the chart container: data-chart-ready flips to 'true' after the first render, and data-chart-renders counts completed passes so a re-render (new range, new series) can be awaited without a stale true letting the reader through too early.

On the spec side, expectChartCanvas(page, testId) (frontend/e2e/fixtures/charts.ts) asserts the container holds a rendered chart — container and <canvas> visible, non-zero CSS box and non-zero bitmap — with both size checks under expect.poll because ECharts attaches and sizes the canvas asynchronously after mount. Asserting the container alone stays green while ECharts never draws inside it; that is the exact regression shape this helper exists to catch.

A signal can exist and still be lying

ImageEditModal sets data-cropper-ready as soon as the cropper can paint — but the modal keeps discarding change events for another ~500 ms while it runs its own reset pass. Edits made in that window disappear, for the spec and for the user, who can then close the modal and lose them without a warning. The spec had answered with waitForTimeout(1500). The fix was to publish the state that actually decides (data-edit-ready), not to sleep longer.

When you write "extra settle time", "let it load", "wait for X to finish" in a comment, you have just named a state the product does not expose.

docs.title: 🧵 Parallelism: earned, not assumed
docs.text:
The suite runs fully parallel, and the unit of parallelism is the test, not the file: one worker interleaves tests from many spec files against one backend and one database. That was not the starting point — it was earned, category by category, by running each at four workers until it was green and fixing what came out.

./dev.py test --workers 4 front-fx all      # the runner decides E2E_WORKERS for Playwright
what means --workers N how many browsers. The backend follows: one uvicorn worker per two browsers, never fewer than one fullyParallel: true the default. Tests are distributed individually; a worker does not own a file test.describe.configure({mode: 'serial'}) this block opts out — and says why in a comment

The order that got us here still applies to any new area: first run it parallel, then read the reds, then fix them, and only then declare an exception. A declaration added without a run behind it is a guess with better syntax.

E2E_FORCE_PARALLEL is gone

It existed to override fullyParallel: false, which no longer exists. And it never could have overridden a mode: 'serial' block — Playwright gives the config no such knob. Re-testing an exception means commenting its declaration out, running the category, and deciding with the result in hand.

docs.title: What the reds actually turned out to be
docs.text:
Across every category promoted, not one red was a write conflict between two specs. They were all specs asking a question whose answer happened to be stable at one worker:

  • "is it on the first page?" asked as if it meant "does it exist?" — the tables paginate client-side over the whole dataset, so a neighbour's row changes the answer;
  • "has it finished?" asked with waitForTimeout — a bet on machine speed that four workers lose;
  • "did the write succeed?" asked as response.ok() — POST /transactions/commit answers 200 with a rolled-back batch when a business rule fails, and reports the ids the rows would have had. Check committed, and treat per-item status: "simulated" as "this row does not exist";
  • "is the row still gone?" asked by id — SQLite reuses the highest rowid the moment you delete it, so an id you freed is very likely already someone else's row. Assert absence on a marker you generated;
  • "do I still own this position?" asked by selling a fixture holding — SELL create → commit sold a quantity a neighbour had already consumed. A test that needs a precondition creates it: the batch now deposits, buys and sells in one commit;
  • "is this feature supported?" asked by looking for the section that a capability catalog gates — the section is absent while the catalog is in flight too, so the question silently became "has the fetch landed yet?". The panel now publishes data-catalog="pending|ready" and the test waits on that instead.

A conditional render driven by a fetch must publish that the fetch landed

This one is a product defect, not a test defect. Whenever {#if someCapability} depends on data that arrives asynchronously, absence has two meanings — "not supported" and "not loaded yet" — and nothing in the DOM separates them. Every observer, test or human, is then measuring network latency and calling it functionality. Publish the distinction (data-catalog, data-busy, a skeleton) and the ambiguity disappears for everyone.

docs.title: Cleanup is where interleaving bites hardest
docs.text: A fixture that deletes "everything created since I opened this file" was correct exactly while a worker owned the file from start to finish. It no longer does, so the same sentence now describes another worker's in-flight rows — and the repopulate path would wipe the database under three running tests. e2e/fixtures/playwright.ts therefore disables transaction hygiene above one worker, and any new cleanup must either do the same or delete only ids the test itself created.

docs.title: Staying serial is a legitimate answer — but it is the second-best one
docs.text:
multi-user.spec.ts shares two browser contexts across its tests. tx-brim-import.spec.ts parses the same two sample files in every test, and parsing rewrites the file's metadata JSON. Neither is fixable with a better timeout, and both say so in a comment above the declaration — the frontend twin of the backend catalogue's exclusive_because.

asset-event-delete.spec.ts was the third, and is the instructive one. Its first test deleted one of Apple's two unlinked mock events, so it worked exactly twice: on the third run the oldest row was a linked event, the API answered in_use, and the suite went red for a reason unrelated to any code change. Serialising the block hid the interference but not the expiry date. The test now creates the event it deletes, and the declaration is gone.

A test that consumes fixture data is a test with an expiry date. Declaring it serial buys time; making it create what it needs removes the problem.

docs.title: 🛡️ The CSP collector
docs.text: A managed instance sends a report-only Content-Security-Policy on the web app's pages: nothing is blocked, and the browser lists each violation in its console, where nobody reads it. Each one is something an enforced policy would block. The collector (lot H-43) turns them into reds: cspViolations, an automatic, test-scoped fixture of e2e/fixtures/playwright.ts, which every spec imports, records the violations of the test's pages and fails the test on any that the baseline does not know. Its pure logic is in e2e/fixtures/csp.ts (cspCollectorEnabled, isKnown, loadBaseline).

docs.title: 🧾 What it records
docs.text:
• Every page of the test's context. Before the test, the fixture adds to the test's browser context an init script, which listens for securitypolicyviolation on document in the capture phase, and a binding, __lfCspViolation, which the listener calls. Both belong to the context, so every page of it, its frames and every navigation are covered. The pages of a context the test creates itself (browser.newContext()) are not.
  • Each violation as the page saw it, with the URL of the page it came from: directive (the effective one), violatedDirective, blockedURI, sourceFile, lineNumber, columnNumber, sample, disposition (enforce or report), documentURI and page.
  • At teardown, one round trip through each open page lets a report still on its way land. When anything was recorded, the list is attached to the test as csp-violations (JSON). Then, while the option cspFailOnUnknown is on (the default), a violation the baseline does not know fails the test, one readable line each: directive, blocked URI, source file and line, page, disposition.
  • Readable by the test. A test that asks for the fixture gets cspViolations.list(), every violation so far, and cspViolations.unknown(), those the baseline does not know.

What there is to record depends on the lane:

  • Every lane, self-hosted or managed, sends the enforced policy on the web app's pages (web_app_policy() in backend/app/services/platform/security_headers.py, see Frame Protection and the Report-Only Policy), with the hashes of the build's inline scripts, so the app's own inline scripts report nothing. What the collector records there are violations with disposition enforce: what the browser really blocked.
  • Where LIBREFOLIO_CSP_REPORT_ONLY is on (the managed profile's default; a self-hosted lane can set it with --lane-setting, see Lane Settings), the pages also carry Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only with CSP_REPORT_ONLY_POLICY, the whole policy the app aims at. Its violations, disposition report, are what that stricter policy would block.
  • A spec may add a policy of its own (layout/page-policy.spec.ts, layout/csp-collector.spec.ts).

docs.title: 📒 The baseline
docs.text:
frontend/e2e/csp-baseline.json lists the violations already known, each entry with an id, a directive, the blocked resource, an optional sample, a reason and an owner. An entry knows a violation of its directive through three keys:

  • blockedURI: the violation's blocked URI, equal (inline, eval, an address);
  • blockedPath: the path of the blocked address, whole, whatever its origin and query, for an address the user typed. A blocked URI that is not an absolute URL (inline, eval) never matches it;
  • sample, optional: the violation's sample, equal. The policy has 'report-sample', so Chromium reports the first 40 characters of a blocked script or eval; an entry without sample knows the violation whatever its sample.

An entry has exactly one of blockedURI and blockedPath. The app's own inline scripts need no entry: the policy allows them by their hashes (lot H-52).

One entry today:

id Matches The violation, and who cures it cheetah-grid-global-probe script-src, eval, sample (function anonymous( ) { return this }) ( a line break) cheetah-grid's bundled webpack probe of the global object, new Function("return this")(), inside a try/catch that falls back to window: harmless under an enforced policy. Found by the first cloud smoke in the BRIM table preview (files.spec.ts). The sample is the source Chromium reports for new Function("return this"), and any other eval fails a test. Coverage builds are not concerned: istanbul reaches the global object through globalThis, not through new Function. Removed when cheetah-grid stops probing the global object with eval (an upgrade, or a bundler that rewrites the probe)

The address check of a link no longer needs an entry: it loads an image (GET /api/v1/auth/address-probe.png), and img-src is not enforced, see The Address Check Is an Image.

The baseline is a ratchet: an entry is added only by a recorded decision, with its reason and its owner, never to silence a red, and removed by the lot that cures it.

docs.title: 🔌 The kill switch
docs.text:
E2E_CSP_COLLECTOR=0 in the environment of a run turns the collector off for the whole run: no binding, nothing recorded, nothing failed. Give it to one run, on its command line:

E2E_CSP_COLLECTOR=0 ./dev.py test front-utility csp-collector   # the run where the kill-switch test runs

Never put it in .env.example: a lane's cleanup removes every variable that file documents, so the switch would no longer reach Playwright.

docs.title: 🚨 When the collector fails a test
docs.text:
1. Read the test's csp-violations attachment in the report: each violation with its directive, blocked URI, source file, line and page, and for a blocked script or eval its sample, the first 40 characters of the code.
  2. Fix the page. A real fix changes what the app does (a script moved to a file, a resource served from the app's own origin), and the violation is gone. An inline <script> in a page of the build is allowed by its hash, which the server computes when it starts: after a new build, restart the server. An inline event handler (onclick="…") is script-src-attr, which no hash covers: listen from the page's script instead, as frontend/static/offline.html does. The gate frontend/src/noInlineEventHandlers.gate.test.ts (Vitest) fails on any inline on…="…" attribute in the source, src/app.html included; icon fallbacks go through the attributes data-hide-on-error, data-fallback-text and data-fallbacks, handled by frontend/src/lib/features/security/imageErrorFallback.ts.
  3. Add a baseline entry only by a recorded decision: the violation understood, its reason written, its owner the lot that will cure it.
  4. test.use({cspFailOnUnknown: false}) belongs only to a test whose subject is the violations themselves, never to silence a red. Two specs use it today, each in a nested describe: the collector's own (e2e/layout/csp-collector.spec.ts), for its two tests that record an unknown violation without failing on it, and e2e/layout/page-policy.spec.ts, for its positive-control test, which raises three enforced violations on purpose (base-uri, object-src, form-action) and checks them itself. The collector still records and attaches what they raise.

The collector's own tests and the cloud smoke, the main specs on a managed lane, are actions of front-utility: see CSP Collector and Cloud Smoke.

docs.title: 🔍 When a spec fails
docs.text: Use the test-triage skill. Its first hypothesis is "was it the shape of the response?" — the data was there but elsewhere, the page held something else, the count differed. flaky is not a verdict.

docs.title: 🌐 External Services Tests (external)
docs.text: These tests verify integrations with external APIs and data sources. They do not require the backend server to be running, but they do require an internet connection (except BRIM, which uses local sample files).

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: To ensure that external providers (like Yahoo Finance, ECB, etc.) are reachable and returning data in the expected format.

docs.title: 🔑 Sub-commands
docs.text:
Sub-command What It Tests fx-providers Every registered FX provider: ECB, FED, BOE, SNB, MANUAL, and the MOCKFX test providers asset-providers Asset pricing providers: yfinance, JustETF, CSS Scraper, etc. justetf-multicurrency The JustETF provider in its four currencies (EUR, USD, CHF, GBP): current price, history, search, parameter validation brim-providers Broker Report Import Manager parsers (local sample files, no network) brim-danske-bank The Danske Bank report-set plugin: file roles, combining a set into one file, parsing it (local sample files, no network) brim-credit-agricole Crédit Agricole report-set plugin: roles, rule M, pairing, balances and holes, combining, parsing (local sample files, no network) brim-degiro The DEGIRO plugin: recognition, reading by position, types, FX pairs, numbers, messages, orders list (local sample files, no network) all All of the above

--providers and --exclude-providers (see Provider Filtering) filter fx-providers, asset-providers and brim-providers. justetf-multicurrency, brim-danske-bank, brim-credit-agricole and brim-degiro take no provider filter: all runs them in full whatever the filter says.

docs.title: 🚀 Running
docs.text:
# All external tests
./dev.py test external all

# Single sub-command
./dev.py test external fx-providers
./dev.py test external asset-providers
./dev.py test external brim-providers

# Quiet output (verbose is the default)
./dev.py test -q external asset-providers

# With coverage tracking
./dev.py test --coverage external all

docs.title: 🔍 Provider Filtering
docs.text: When an external service is down (e.g., Yahoo Finance outage), you can skip its tests without modifying code.

docs.title: Exclude specific providers
docs.text:
# Skip yfinance tests (Yahoo Finance is down)
./dev.py test external asset-providers --exclude-providers yfinance

# Skip multiple providers
./dev.py test external all --exclude-providers yfinance broker_coinbase

docs.title: Include only specific providers
docs.text:
# Only test JustETF
./dev.py test external asset-providers --providers justetf

# Only test ECB and FED
./dev.py test external fx-providers --providers ECB FED

docs.title: Works with all and all-backend too
docs.text:
# Run the full test suite but exclude yfinance
./dev.py test all --exclude-providers yfinance

# Run all backend tests, only test ECB for FX
./dev.py test all-backend --providers ECB justetf

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The --providers / --exclude-providers flags translate to pytest -k expressions:

Flag Pytest equivalent --providers yfinance justetf -k "yfinance or justetf" --exclude-providers yfinance -k "not yfinance"

Dynamic help

Run ./dev.py test external -h to see all available provider codes, discovered automatically from the source tree.

docs.title: Lightweight discovery
docs.text: Provider codes are discovered by regex-parsing the Python source files — the modules are never imported. This avoids heavy side-effects (TTL cache creation, logger initialisation, network client setup) and keeps ./dev.py test -h instant.

docs.title: 🔄 yfinance Retry Logic
docs.text:
The Yahoo Finance provider includes automatic retry with exponential backoff for transient network errors (API instability, timeouts).

Parameter Value Attempts At most 3 (_YF_MAX_RETRIES) Delays 1.5 s, then 3 s Transient keywords curl, connection, timeout, reset, 503, ssl, broken pipe, etc.

Wrapped operations: get_current_value, get_history_value, search, fetch_asset_metadata.

Non-transient errors (e.g., INVALID_IDENTIFIER_TYPE) are raised immediately without retry. So is a refusal for too many requests (YFRateLimitError, or «429», «too many requests», «rate limit» in the message): it leaves at once as AssetRateLimitedError (RATE_LIMITED), for the core to pause the provider (see Yahoo Finance Provider). These tests call the provider directly, not through the core's boundary: a refusal fails the test with that error, and no pause follows.

Thread safety

yfinance calls run in dedicated threads (via _run_provider_in_thread() in the core), so time.sleep() blocks only that thread without affecting the asyncio event loop.

docs.title: 💱 Front-FX Tests
docs.text: Frontend E2E and unit tests for the FX (Foreign Exchange) module.

docs.title: 🔍 What's Tested
docs.text:
The FX module has the most extensive frontend test coverage, with 7 Playwright spec files:

Test Suite Description FX List Currency pair list page, filtering, sync-all button FX Detail Detail page chart, data view, measure/signal panels Add Pair Add-pair modal, currency search, route selection Data Editor Inline rate editing, delete, date picker Sync Individual pair sync, provider fallback FX API Backend API integration (rates, routes, providers) FX Settings Chart settings, signal configuration, benchmarks

docs.title: 🚀 Running
docs.text:
# Run all front-fx tests
./dev.py test front-fx all

# List the units (actions), each with its description
./dev.py test front-fx --help

# List the Playwright tests of every unit, without running them (Vitest files are not listed)
./dev.py test front-fx all --list

# Run a specific test file
./dev.py test front-fx fx-detail

# Run with Playwright UI mode (interactive)
./dev.py test front-fx all --ui

docs.title: 📂 Test Location
docs.text:
frontend/e2e/
├── fx-list.spec.ts       # FX pair list page
├── fx-detail.spec.ts     # FX detail chart & data
├── fx-add-pair.spec.ts   # Add pair modal
├── fx-editor.spec.ts     # Data editor inline editing
├── fx-sync.spec.ts       # Sync operations
├── fx-api.spec.ts        # Backend API calls
└── fx-settings.spec.ts   # Chart settings & signals

docs.title: 🎭 Frontend Tests Overview (Playwright)
docs.text: LibreFolio's frontend tests use Playwright to drive a real browser and interact with the application exactly as a user would.

docs.title: 🧰 Tools & Framework
docs.text: Tool Role Playwright Browser automation engine (Chromium, headless by default) @playwright/test Test runner with test(), expect(), fixtures page Playwright's page fixture — represents a browser tab expect Assertion library with auto-retry and web-first semantics

docs.title: ⚙️ How Tests Work
docs.text:
Each test file (.spec.ts) contains scenarios that:

  1. Navigate to a URL (page.goto('/fx'))
  2. Interact with elements (page.click(), page.fill(), page.getByRole())
  3. Assert outcomes (expect(page.getByText('EUR/USD')).toBeVisible())

Playwright automatically waits for elements and retries assertions, making tests resilient to timing issues.

// Example: verify broker creation
test('create a new broker', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/brokers');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'New Broker' }).click();
    await page.getByLabel('Name').fill('My Broker');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' }).click();
    await expect(page.getByText('My Broker')).toBeVisible();
});

docs.title: 🤖 Automated Setup
docs.text:
When you run a frontend test category, everything the Playwright specs need is prepared for you (the category's Vitest files need none of it):

  • Builds the frontend, when needed — front build, which syncs the API client before building, runs only when there is no build yet, when the frontend sources, its static files, its configuration or the Tool codegen inputs changed since the last build (frontend/src/, and frontend/static/, which adapter-static copies into the build: sw.js, offline.html, the icons, the fonts; under both, the same rule: hidden files and folders, such as the macOS Finder's .DS_Store or the font cache's .cache_manifest.json, do not count, nor do *.test.* / *.spec.* files and the __tests__/ / __mocks__/ folders, which only the tests use), or when the existing build is not of the kind needed: instrumented for JS coverage or plain, and a debug build for dev.py server --test. The Tool codegen inputs, among them the .py files of backend/app/schemas/, backend/app/services/tools/ and backend/app/services/tool_plugins/, and the files of frontend/src/ and frontend/static/ that count (the generated translation catalogues aside), are also checked against the fingerprint of their listing that the last successful front build recorded in frontend/build/.tool-contract-inputs: an input added, removed or renamed counts even with an old date, while a .DS_Store, an editor's hidden file or a __pycache__/ next to them does not. For a build without that record (one made before the record existed, or by npm run build alone), the check reads the dates of the Tool codegen folders instead (for the frontend's files, only their own dates), which a .DS_Store or a __pycache__/ moves too: one rebuild too many at worst, after which the record exists. The runner checks before the specs, and for the shared test backend before starting it: dev.py server --test --build-only runs in the foreground (the frontend build, and the documentation site when it is missing or stale), outside the backend's startup timeout. With --no-shared-server, the server that Playwright's webServer starts makes that check itself, inside the webServer's startup wait.
  • Uses a test backend — dev.py server --test, serving the API and the built frontend on the run's test port. By default it is the shared backend the runner starts once for the whole invocation; with --no-shared-server, Playwright's webServer starts its own for each Playwright run. It runs with the popups that would interrupt the specs switched off: the donation prompt (LIBREFOLIO_DISABLE_DONATION_POPUP=1), since the specs sign in again and again with the same users, and the «What's new» window (LIBREFOLIO_DISABLE_WHATS_NEW=1, lot C-54), since the lanes' accounts predate it, so their GET /auth/me answers user.whats_new: null. Both switches are hidden: no .env.example line, no admin page. A spec that needs the window gives its own page a value instead, as layout/whats-new.spec.ts does (What's new). It always runs at DEBUG (dev.py server --test sets LIBREFOLIO_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG), so the lane publishes client_log_level: "debug" and the browser console gets a line for every failed API call, a 4xx included; no spec fails on a console line (The Browser Console).
  • Prepares the test data — repopulates the test database with mock data and creates the E2E users, in the runner or in Playwright's globalSetup.
  • Runs Playwright — executes the specs against the live application at http://localhost:<test port>: 6041 unless --test-port or TEST_PORT says otherwise.
  • Tears down — stops the backend it started: the shared one at the end of the invocation, Playwright's own at the end of its run.

Test isolation

The test backend works on the run's test data root: backend/data/test/ in the checkout unless --data-dir or LIBREFOLIO_TEST_DATA_DIR says otherwise, with the database in sqlite/app.db under it. The runner refuses a test data root that overlaps the production data, so your production data is never touched. See Isolated Runtime Lanes.

docs.title: 🏁 Flags
docs.text:
Every frontend test category — front-utility, front-broker, front-user, front-fx, front-asset, front-transaction, front-portfolio, front-ai-export, front-designer-lab — supports these flags. --headed, --debug, --ui and --list follow the category (./dev.py test front-fx all --headed); --coverage belongs to ./dev.py test and comes before it (./dev.py test --coverage js front-fx all).

Flag Effect When to Use --headed Opens a visible browser window instead of headless Watch the test flow visually, debug layout issues --debug Runs headed with the Playwright Inspector (PWDEBUG=1), which pauses the test so you can step through its actions Step through actions one by one, inspect selectors, set breakpoints --ui Opens Playwright UI Mode — a full interactive test runner Explore tests interactively, view timeline/trace, re-run selectively --list Lists the category's Playwright spec files and the test titles they declare, without running anything (all for the whole category, an action name for its specs only) Discover tests, verify naming, plan what to run --coverage [py\|js\|all] Tracks Python and/or JS coverage: the backend's Python while the E2E tests drive it, the frontend's JS in the browser and in the category's Vitest files py → htmlcov-backend-e2e/, js → frontend/coverage-js/ (e2e/, unit-combined/, and combined/ when both ran), all (default) → both

E2E runs are the only ones that measure both languages

A Playwright run exercises the frontend in the browser and the backend over HTTP, so it is the only suite where --coverage all produces two reports. See Coverage Model.

These Playwright tests cover fundamental UI components that are used across the entire application:

Test Suite Description Authentication Login, registration, logout, session persistence Account links The invitation and password-reset pages, /invite and /reset-password (auth-links) Settings Profile editing, preferences tabs, password change Users tab Settings → Administration → Users, for administrators: account actions, invitation and password-reset links with their address check, deletion after its preview (admin-users) Settings addresses Every Settings tab at its own address, /settings/<tab> and /settings/admin/<tab>; the ?tab= of 1.2 replaced by the address; «Open the settings» on a refusal of the space limit to the limit in Global Settings (settings-addresses) Plugins tab Settings → Plugins and Configure, as a member and as an administrator: the two personal search preferences, mockprov's settings through an asset's edit dialog, the search's «to configure» row and the 👑 legend (plugin-settings) Files File upload, file list, drag & drop, file deletion Select Components SearchSelect, SimpleSelect, currency pickers Image Crop ImageEditModal, crop presets, zoom, rotation, format export CSP collector The collector of Content-Security-Policy violations that every spec carries: its helpers and its baseline, synthetic documents under a report-only policy of their own, the sign-in page and the offline page under the managed profile's, with the hashes of the build's inline scripts (csp-collector) Cloud smoke Thirteen specs of the suite on a managed lane, desktop only, and on any lane only when named: the managed profile's frame protection and report-only policy for real, the collector failing on any violation its baseline does not know (cloud-smoke)

docs.title: 👥 Users Tab (admin-users)
docs.text:
settings/admin-users.spec.ts drives the Users tab of Settings › Administration on the lane's real backend. e2e_test_admin acts through the page, and only on what the test itself created: accounts it registers and invitation addresses of its own. After each test, red or green, every invitation still pending with one of those addresses is revoked, and every account still there deletes itself. Each action is checked on what the page publishes (data-* attributes and the app events of notify()), then read back on the server.

Case What it checks AUSR-E-01 An administrator has the tab, and it settles (data-busy="false"); a regular member has none, and ?tab=users opens Profile AUSR-E-02 The administrator's own row: data-self="true", a link to Profile, no action AUSR-E-03 Deactivate, confirmed, then reactivate AUSR-E-04 Promote, confirmed; Delete off (demote-first) while the account is an administrator; demote, confirmed AUSR-E-05 A password-reset link: issued from its dialog, shown with its expiry, its token live for that very account AUSR-E-06 An invitation with an e-mail: its link and live token, listed once Done, then revoked, confirmed, after which its token reads revoked AUSR-E-07 The address check of a link, once edited: match on the lane's other loopback origin (localhost for 127.0.0.1, or the reverse), through the real CORS path; unverifiable on a closed port; invalid for an ftp:// address, with the copy off; mismatch from a stubbed stranger, reached by simple GETs only; idle back on the prefilled address AUSR-E-08 A deletion: deactivating instead is offered, the preview lists the account's broker with its one transaction, only the username typed exactly enables the button; then the account and its broker are gone AUSR-E-09 Sign out everywhere, confirmed: the account's open session gets 401, and the account stays active AUSR-E-10 Restart the guides, confirmed: every guide the account had skipped is pending again

Prerequisites: the test users (e2e_test_admin an administrator, e2e_test_user a regular member), and on the lane registration_mode open and no user limit. The usage line, the limit banner, the billing link, the refusals with their error codes, and the copy itself are left to the Vitest component tests: see Users Tab and Account Deletion Tests. Run it alone with ./dev.py test front-utility admin-users.

docs.title: 🔗 Settings Addresses (settings-addresses)
docs.text:

Test What it checks Address and Back /settings/admin/backup opens Backup inside «Administration»; Users writes /settings/admin/users, Preferences /settings/preferences; Back returns to Users Unknown address /settings/nope-… becomes /settings, Profile open The address of 1.2 /settings?tab=email opens Email and becomes /settings/admin/email «Open the settings» A simulated 507 storage_limit_exceeded on an upload from Files offers the button; it opens /settings/admin/global?setting=storage_limit_mb, the limit's row highlighted and in view, the field read-only until the lock is opened by hand A member /settings/admin/users becomes /settings, Profile open, no «Administration»
