docs.title: 💡 Overview
docs.text: This page formally defines the mathematical model underlying LibreFolio's portfolio calculation engine. All other metric pages (NAV, Book Value, Period P&L, Yield on Cost, WAC, Deposited Capital) reference this page for their precise computation rules.

docs.title: 📐 1. Notation and Sets
docs.text: Symbol Meaning \(V(u)\) All brokers visible to user \(u\) \(S \subseteq V(u)\) Selected (filtered) broker scope \(A\) Set of assets with positions \(C^*\) Target currency \([t_0, t_1]\) Requested evaluation frame \(q(a,b,t)\) Quantity of asset \(a\) at broker \(b\) on date \(t\) \(p(a,t)\) Valuation price of asset \(a\) on date \(t\) \(\mathrm{fx}(c_1, c_2, t)\) Exchange rate from currency \(c_1\) to \(c_2\) on date \(t\)

docs.title: 📐 2. Valuation Price
docs.text:
\[ \operatorname{mark}(a,t)= \begin{cases} \text{MARKET}(a,t) & \text{same-day asset-system quote}\\ \operatorname{avg}(\text{TRADE}(a,t)) & \text{same-day BUY/SELL observations, or transfer cost estimates}\\ \text{last observation before }t & \text{carried forward (LOCF)}\\ \varnothing & \text{no observation on or before }t \end{cases} \]
  • The unified resolver is the single valuation brain: MARKET → TRADE_AVG → CARRIED → MISSING.
  • Market quotes and BUY/SELL trades are observations. An ADJUSTMENT never is, incoming or outgoing, with or without a cost basis: its cost basis is a cost, not what the asset was worth that day.
  • The cost of an incoming TRANSFER (its per-unit cost basis, in the cost basis's currency) is a TRADE observation, estimated, only while the asset has, on or before that day, no market quote and no other operation — no BUY or SELL, no ADJUSTMENT, no outgoing transfer; other incoming transfers do not stop it. It is carried forward until a real quote or trade replaces it, and never overrides one: a quoted security moved between brokers keeps its carried quote (Transfer cost as an estimate).
  • CARRIED is last-observation-carried-forward. It carries days_back staleness metadata.
  • estimated=True means TRADE-origin. A stale carried MARKET quote is stale, not estimated.
  • Marks stay in native currency; each consumer converts to \(C^*\) at valuation date \(t\).
  • Cost-basis FX remains pinned to the transaction date.
  • Cash stays in the currency it was recorded in, broker by broker, and is valued at the rate of \(t\) (§5); each cash movement is still booked, and each external cash flow enters the capital, at the rate of its own date.
  • WAC is never used as valuation price. A position whose asset has no mark at all (\(\varnothing\)) is counted at its cost basis instead, as a declared estimate, not a price (§3).

See Price Resolution for the resolver contract and data-quality semantics.

docs.title: 📐 3. Position State
docs.text:
A position \((a, b)\) is held on \(t\) when its quantity is above the dust threshold \(\varepsilon = 10^{-5}\) units: \(q(a,b,t) > \varepsilon\). For each position held:

\[ \mathrm{MV}(a,b,t) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{q(a,b,t)}{qbq(a)}\cdot \operatorname{mark}(a,t)\cdot \mathrm{fx}\bigl(\mathrm{ccy}_{mark}, C^*, t\bigr) & \operatorname{mark}(a,t) \neq \varnothing\\ \mathrm{CB}(a,b,t) & \operatorname{mark}(a,t) = \varnothing \text{ and the cost of } (a,b) \text{ is complete} \end{cases} \] \[ \mathrm{CB}(a,b,t) = q(a,b,t) \cdot w(a,b,t) \] \[ \mathrm{UGL}(a,b,t) = \mathrm{MV}(a,b,t) - \mathrm{CB}(a,b,t) \]

Where \(w(a,b,t)\) is the Weighted Average Cost for position \((a,b)\) at date \(t\), kept in \(C^*\) at historical rates (§4): the cost basis takes no exchange rate at \(t\), so for a foreign asset the exchange-rate effect is part of \(\mathrm{UGL}\).

The second case covers an asset with no observation yet — no quote, no BUY or SELL and no transfer cost estimate on or before \(t\), as for a holding received through adjustments, or through transfers without a cost basis. The position is valued at its cost basis, valuation source ESTIMATED_AT_COST: a declared estimate, not a price. It reports no unit price, it does not move with exchange rates, and its \(\mathrm{UGL}\) is zero, with neither a price effect nor an exchange-rate effect. The choice is made day by day, with no look-ahead: from the first observation on, the mark wins, even an old one carried forward. A position whose cost is incomplete (§4) has no market value on such a day (MISSING) and is left out of \(\mathrm{MV}(t)\). The valuation sources therefore rank MARKET_PRICE > LAST_TRADE_PRICE > ESTIMATED_AT_COST > MISSING (Price Resolution).

A quantity of \(\varepsilon\) units or fewer — the dust a sale of almost every unit can leave behind — is not held: it has no position state, so no market value, no cost basis, no allocation slice and no snapshot, and dust without a mark does not make the day incomplete. The same threshold decides which positions the Performance rows hold (§7), so the portfolio and its rows count the same positions; where the cost of the dust goes is in §7.

docs.title: 📐 4. WAC Iterative Update
docs.text:
Maintained per-position \((a,b)\) with pool state \((\hat{q}, \hat{c})\), the cost \(\hat{c}\) kept in \(C^*\):

Acquisition (qty \(> 0\), amount \(P\) paid in currency \(c\) on date \(d\)):

\[ \hat{q}_{\text{new}} = \hat{q} + q_{\text{tx}}, \quad \hat{c}_{\text{new}} = \hat{c} + P \cdot \mathrm{fx}(c, C^*, d), \quad w = \frac{\hat{c}_{\text{new}}}{\hat{q}_{\text{new}}} \]

\(P\) is the cash paid for a BUY, or the per-unit cost basis override times \(q_{\text{tx}}\) for a TRANSFER or ADJUSTMENT; \(\mathrm{fx}(C^*, C^*, d) = 1\). When no rate exists on or before \(d\), or the acquisition has no cost basis, the quantity enters and the cost does not: the position's cost is flagged incomplete instead of counting zero.

Reduction (qty \(< 0\)):

\[ w_{\text{pre}} = \frac{\hat{c}}{\hat{q}}, \quad \hat{q}_{\text{new}} = \hat{q} - |q_{\text{tx}}|, \quad \hat{c}_{\text{new}} = \hat{q}_{\text{new}} \cdot w_{\text{pre}} \]

Split (linked to a split event): \(\hat{q}\) changes, \(\hat{c}\) does not.

Ordering

Within the same date: additions processed before reductions. Ensures SELL reads the correct WAC including same-day BUYs.

docs.title: 📐 5. Portfolio Aggregation
docs.text:
\[ \mathrm{MV}(t) = \sum_{(a,b) \in S} \mathrm{MV}(a,b,t) \] \[ \mathrm{NAV}(t) = \mathrm{MV}(t) + \mathrm{Cash}(t) + \mathrm{InTransit}(t) \] \[ \mathrm{Book}(t) = \mathrm{OCB}(t) + \mathrm{Cash}(t) + \mathrm{InTransitBook}(t) \] \[ \mathrm{UGL}(t) = \mathrm{NAV}(t) - \mathrm{Book}(t) \]

\(\mathrm{MV}(t)\) and \(\mathrm{OCB}(t)\) run over the positions held on \(t\) (§3): dust, at or below the threshold, is in neither, so neither in NAV nor in Book.

\(\mathrm{Cash}(t)\) is each broker's cash, kept in the currencies it was recorded in and valued at the rate of \(t\):

\[ \mathrm{Cash}(t) = \sum_{b \in S} \sum_{c} N_{b,c}(t) \cdot \mathrm{fx}(c, C^*, t) \]

where \(N_{b,c}(t)\) is the balance of broker \(b\) in currency \(c\) after its movements dated on or before \(t\), scaled by the broker's ownership share, and \(\mathrm{fx}(c, C^*, t)\) is the latest rate on or before \(t\) (\(1\) for \(c = C^*\)). The same term is in NAV and in Book, so the exchange-rate effect on cash cancels in UGL: it is booked as an exchange result (§6) and belongs to the Total P&L.

docs.title: 🔀 Two Unrealized Figures
docs.text:
\(\mathrm{InTransit}(t)\) and \(\mathrm{InTransitBook}(t)\) hold the same cash in transit, and the securities travelling between two brokers of \(S\) at market value, \(\mathrm{MV}^{\mathrm{tr}}(t)\), in the first and at historical cost, \(\mathrm{CB}^{\mathrm{tr}}(t)\), in the second. Cash cancels, so with \(\mathrm{OCB}(t)\) the cost basis of the positions held (§3):

\[ \mathrm{UGL}(t) = \bigl[\mathrm{MV}(t) - \mathrm{OCB}(t)\bigr] + \bigl[\mathrm{MV}^{\mathrm{tr}}(t) - \mathrm{CB}^{\mathrm{tr}}(t)\bigr] \]

The engine reports two unrealized figures:

Figure Definition Where it shows Portfolio unrealized \(\mathrm{UGL}(t) = \mathrm{NAV}(t) - \mathrm{Book}(t)\), securities in transit included unrealized_gain_loss of the portfolio report's summary and history points (POST /portfolio/report) and of the AI Export portfolio and broker summaries; Book Value — Unrealized Period unrealized \(\mathrm{MV}(t) - \mathrm{OCB}(t)\) at each period boundary, positions held only period_unrealized_gain_loss_start, _end, _delta and their split by currency; the Dashboard's Unrealized change; the \(\Delta\mathrm{UGL}\) of Period P&L and the per-position rows of §7

They differ only by the securities in transit: on a day when none is travelling, they are equal. A security in transit on a period boundary is in NAV, so in the period P&L, but in no position's state: its part of the result is in the residual of §7, not in \(\Delta\mathrm{UGL}\).

docs.title: 🏦 The Whole Broker
docs.text:
Every amount of broker \(b\) — its quantities, cash and flows — counts at the broker's ownership share \(s_b\): an owner's share, \(1\) for an editor or a viewer. The whole-broker view, meant for the broker page, sets \(s_b = 1\) for every broker, as an editor sees it, whatever the user's share; the Dashboard keeps the owner's share. A broker worth 10 000 € owned at 30 % is 3 000 € on the Dashboard and 10 000 € whole; owned at 0 %, 0 € and 10 000 €.

For a single broker the ratios are the same in both views: every flow and every value is multiplied by the same constant \(s_b\), which cancels in TWRR, MWRR, simple ROI, the weights and the period percentages. Only the amounts change.

docs.title: 📐 6. Three-Pool Cash Model — Per-Broker \((K_b, R_b, W)\)
docs.text:
Three accumulator pools track cash provenance. \(K\) and \(R\) are maintained per-broker \(b\); \(W\) is global (exits the system entirely).

Pool Scope Meaning \(K_b\) Per-broker External capital still in broker \(b\) as cash \(R_b\) Per-broker Generated returns still in broker \(b\) as cash \(W\) Global Returns that left the system (hidden, restorable on re-deposit)

Key property

A BUY on broker \(b_1\) can only consume \(R_{b_1}\), never \(R_{b_2}\). Cash does not teleport between brokers — only explicit transfers move pool balances.

docs.title: 🔁 Update rules (per-transaction on broker \(b\), chronological)
docs.text:
Icon & Type Update Formulas Logic & Description DEPOSIT\(D > 0\) \(r = \min(D,\, W)\)\(R_b \mathrel{+}= r\)\(W \mathrel{-}= r\)\(K_b \mathrel{+}= D - r\) Restores previously withdrawn returns from the global tracker \(W\) first, then adds the remainder to capital \(K_b\). WITHDRAWAL\(X > 0\) \(k = \min(X,\, K_b)\)\(K_b \mathrel{-}= k\)\(\rho = \min(X - k,\, R_b)\)\(R_b \mathrel{-}= \rho\)\(W \mathrel{+}= \rho\) Consumes capital \(K_b\) first, then moves remaining returns \(\rho\) to the global tracker \(W\). DIVIDEND / INTEREST\(I > 0\) \(R_b \mathrel{+}= I\) Yields directly increase the returns pool \(R_b\). FEE / TAX\(F > 0\) \(R_b \mathrel{-}= F\)\(\text{if } R_b < 0\text{: } K_b \mathrel{+}= R_b,\; R_b = 0\) Consumes returns \(R_b\) first; if \(R_b\) becomes negative, it drains from capital \(K_b\). BUY\(B > 0\) \(\rho = \min(B,\, R_b)\)\(R_b \mathrel{-}= \rho\)\(K_b \mathrel{-}= (B - \rho)\) Consumes returns \(R_b\) first, then drains the rest from capital \(K_b\). SELL \(G = P - C\)\(K_b \mathrel{+}= C\)\(R_b \mathrel{+}= G\)\(\text{if } R_b < 0\text{: } K_b \mathrel{+}= R_b, \quad R_b = 0\) Cost basis $C = CASH TRANSFER / FX CONVERSION(Internal, \(s \to d\), \(X > 0\) leaves, \(Y > 0\) arrives) Departure Leg (\(s\)):\(\rho = \min(X,\, R_s)\)\(R_s \mathrel{-}= \rho\)\(\kappa = X - \rho\)\(K_s \mathrel{-}= \kappa\)Arrival Leg (\(d\)):\(K_d \mathrel{+}= \kappa\)\(R_d \mathrel{+}= \rho + (Y - X)\)\(\text{if } R_d < 0\text{: } K_d \mathrel{+}= R_d,\; R_d = 0\) The departure takes returns \(R_s\) first, then capital \(K_s\). The arrival brings back what the departure took from each pool. \(X\) and \(Y\) are in \(C^*\) at the rate of each leg's own date, each weighted by its broker's ownership share, so they can differ: a conversion's spread against the reference rate, the rate move while the cash travels, two brokers owned at different shares. Neither leg is an external flow, so the capital baseline does not move and Total P&L already counts the gap \(Y - X\): it is a result, booked like the exchange result on cash at rest — a gain to the returns, a loss out of the returns first and then of the capital, as a FEE. With \(Y = X\): \(K_d \mathrel{+}= \kappa\), \(R_d \mathrel{+}= \rho\).An FX CONVERSION has both legs at the same broker (\(s = d\)), in two currencies.The global tracker \(W\) is never touched (capital remains inside the system). CASH TRANSFER / FX CONVERSION(External or orphan leg on \(b\): \(Y > 0\) arrives, or \(X > 0\) leaves) Incoming (\(Y\)), as a DEPOSIT:\(r = \min(Y,\, W)\)\(R_b \mathrel{+}= r\)\(W \mathrel{-}= r\)\(K_b \mathrel{+}= Y - r\)Outgoing (\(X\)), as a WITHDRAWAL:\(k = \min(X,\, K_b)\)\(K_b \mathrel{-}= k\)\(\rho = \min(X - k,\, R_b)\)\(R_b \mathrel{-}= \rho\)\(W \mathrel{+}= \rho\) A leg whose other leg sits at a broker outside \(S\), or that has lost its pair — the link cleared, or the paired row gone — is an external flow: the capital baseline counts it at its amount, like a deposit or a withdrawal. Its pools move as that deposit or withdrawal would: an arrival first restores withdrawn returns \(W\) into \(R_b\), the rest is capital \(K_b\); a departure takes capital \(K_b\) first, then returns \(R_b\), which go to \(W\). Unlike an internal pair, this leg does touch \(W\), and it records or takes up no split.

For example, with \(C^* = \mathrm{EUR}\), a broker with \(K = 1000\), \(R = 300\) converts 650 EUR into 715 USD at a reference rate of 0.92 EUR per USD (\(Y = 657.80\)): afterwards \(K = 1000\) and \(R = 307.80\) — the capital still equals what was deposited, and the 7.80 spread is a result. Between brokers owned at different shares, \(A\) at 100 % sending 400 to \(B\) at 50 % gives \(X = 400\), \(Y = 200\): a loss of 200, out of the returns first.

Each departure records its split \((\rho, X)\) until its arrival takes it up, once. An arrival whose departure is unknown — no recorded split, or \(X = 0\) — goes entirely to \(K_d\). When both legs fall on the same day, the arrival is applied after that day's other movements, whatever their transaction ids, so it always finds its departure's split. A transfer or conversion whose other leg is outside \(S\), or that has lost its pair, is not internal and does not follow this rule: it moves the pools as a DEPOSIT or a WITHDRAWAL (the row above). In a view of broker \(B\) alone, \(650\) arriving from a broker \(A\) outside the view makes an empty \(B\) hold \(K_B = 650\), \(R_B = 0\); a \(B\) holding \(K_B = 100\), \(R_B = 100\) ends at \(K_B = 750\), \(R_B = 100\). If the \(B\) holding \(K_B = 100\), \(R_B = 100\) sends \(150\) out of the view instead, it keeps \(K_B = 0\), \(R_B = 50\), and \(W = 50\): the next inflow — a deposit or another leg from outside — restores those \(50\) into \(R_B\) first, and a later BUY spends \(R_B\) first, as usual. In the view of \(A\) and \(B\) together the same pair is internal and follows the rule above.

If departure and arrival dates differ, the transfer is in-transit: subtracted from \(s\) at departure day, added to \(d\) at arrival day. Between those dates, \(\sum K_b + \sum R_b < \mathrm{Cash}_{\text{like}}\) by the in-transit amount — the reconciliation below reads that cash with the pools' current mix until the arrival brings back the departure's split.

docs.title: 💱 Exchange Result on Foreign Cash
docs.text:
Each cash movement enters the broker's cash, and its pools, at the rate of its own date; the balance held afterwards follows the rate (§5). On every day \(t\) on which the rate of a foreign currency held as cash in \(S\) changes — its first known rate included — after that day's cash movements and before that day's transactions update the pools, each broker \(b\) holding foreign cash is revalued:

\[ \varepsilon_b(t) = \sum_{c} N_{b,c}(t) \cdot \mathrm{fx}(c, C^*, t) - \mathrm{Cash}^{\text{replay}}_b(t) \] \[ \mathrm{Cash}^{\text{replay}}_b \mathrel{+}= \varepsilon_b, \qquad R_b \mathrel{+}= \varepsilon_b, \qquad \text{if } R_b < 0\text{: } K_b \mathrel{+}= R_b,\; R_b = 0 \]

\(\mathrm{Cash}^{\text{replay}}_b(t)\) is the cash the replay carries for \(b\): its value at the previous revaluation plus every later movement at the rate of its own date. A gain goes to the returns; a loss consumes them first and then the capital, exactly like a FEE. The capital baseline does not move: an exchange result is a result, not a contribution, so it is in NAV, Total P&L, ROI, TWRR and MWRR, never in the deposited capital.

docs.title: 🧮 Aggregation for output
docs.text: \[ \mathrm{CashFromCapital}(t) = \sum_{b \in S} K_b(t) \] \[ \mathrm{CashFromReturns}(t) = \sum_{b \in S} R_b(t) \]

docs.title: ⚖️ Reconciliation invariant
docs.text:
\[ \mathrm{Cash}_{\text{like}}(t) \approx \sum_{b \in S} K_b(t) + \sum_{b \in S} R_b(t) \]

Both pools are first clamped at zero per broker. If the pools are not empty and the drift still exceeds \(0.01\), the summed pools are scaled to \(\mathrm{Cash}_{\text{like}}\), the cash plus the cash in transit — an aggregate scaling, not a per-broker one, each result floored at zero:

\[ \mathrm{CashFromCapital}(t) = \sum_{b \in S} K_b(t) \cdot \frac{\mathrm{Cash}_{\text{like}}(t)}{\sum_{b \in S} K_b(t) + \sum_{b \in S} R_b(t)}, \qquad \mathrm{CashFromReturns}(t) = \mathrm{Cash}_{\text{like}}(t) - \mathrm{CashFromCapital}(t) \]

Otherwise \(\mathrm{CashFromCapital}(t) = \min\bigl(\sum_b K_b(t),\, \mathrm{Cash}_{\text{like}}(t)\bigr)\) and \(\mathrm{CashFromReturns}\) is the rest, floored at zero. The exchange results on cash at rest are booked into the pools (above); the scaling absorbs two drifts:

  • Cash in transit. The departure has left the pools, while \(\mathrm{Cash}_{\text{like}}\) still counts the cash in transit — and the move of its exchange rate while it travels — so \(\sum K_b + \sum R_b < \mathrm{Cash}_{\text{like}}\). Until the arrival, the scale reads that cash with the pools' current mix. A broker with \(K = 1000\), \(R = 300\) sends \(650\) in \(C^*\) to an empty broker of \(S\): it keeps \(K = 650\), \(R = 0\), the scale is \(1300 / 650 = 2\), so \(\mathrm{CashFromCapital} = 1300\) and \(\mathrm{CashFromReturns} = 0\) during the transit. On arrival the split comes back: \(1000\) and \(300\).
  • Negative cash (overdraft). Both pools are clamped at zero per broker, so a broker whose cash goes below zero leaves pools that no longer sum to its cash — also on the following days, since the clamped values are kept.

docs.title: 📐 7. Period Contribution
docs.text:
For period \([t_0, t_1]\), per-position \((a,b)\):

\[ \Delta\mathrm{UGL}(a,b) = \mathrm{UGL}(a,b,t_1) - \mathrm{UGL}(a,b,t_0) + T(a,b) \] \[ \mathrm{PnL}(a,b) = \Delta\mathrm{UGL}(a,b) + \mathrm{Realized}(a,b) + \mathrm{Income}(a,b) - \mathrm{FeesTaxes}(a,b) \]

Contribution position set:

\[ \mathcal{P} = \text{positions with BUY/SELL/ADJUSTMENT/TRANSFER activity or boundary quantity} \]

\(\mathrm{UGL}(a,b,t)\) is the position state of §3 at the end of day \(t\), the one the portfolio aggregates (§5): the mark of §2 — a trade-derived mark restated through any later split —, the cost basis when the asset has no mark at all, the exchange rate of \(t\) itself. A position not held on \(t\) counts 0. A position held on \(t\) whose \(\mathrm{UGL}(a,b,t)\) is unknown — no rate, an incomplete cost — makes \(\Delta\mathrm{UGL}(a,b)\) unknown, never the known side minus zero. When every row is known, the rows add up to the portfolio's change, that of the positions held — the period unrealized of §5, securities in transit left out:

\[ \sum_{(a,b) \in \mathcal{P}} \Delta\mathrm{UGL}(a,b) = \Delta\mathrm{UGL} = \bigl[\mathrm{MV}(t_1) - \mathrm{OCB}(t_1)\bigr] - \bigl[\mathrm{MV}(t_0) - \mathrm{OCB}(t_0)\bigr] \]

The identity holds with dust too: a row and the portfolio state of §3 use the same threshold, so a position left with \(10^{-5}\) units or fewer is not held on either side — no value, no unrealized, in no row and not in \(\Delta\mathrm{UGL}\). Its cost leaves the open cost basis without being sold, so it is in neither \(\Delta\mathrm{UGL}\) nor Realized: it ends in the period's residual (below).

Internal transfers. \(T(a,b)\) splits the result of a security moved between two brokers of \(S\): each broker answers for its own stretch. For each linked TRANSFER of \(a\) from broker \(s\) to broker \(d\) that departs after \(t_0\) and arrives on or before \(t_1\), with \(V\) the value of the moved units on the arrival day (§3) and \(C\) the historical cost the sender's pool gave up for them (§4):

\[ T(a,s) \mathrel{+}= V - C, \qquad T(a,d) \mathrel{-}= V - C \]

The sender answers for the units until they arrive, transit included, the receiver from their arrival; the terms cancel, so the total is unchanged. A transfer already in transit at \(t_0\), still in transit at \(t_1\), or with \(V\) or \(C\) unknown adds nothing: the boundary values stand.

Example: 10 units moved from broker A to broker B

A holds 10 units bought at 80 (\(C = 800\)). The price is 100 at \(t_0\), 120 on the day they move to B (\(V = 1{,}200\)), 150 at \(t_1\):

\[ \Delta\mathrm{UGL}(a,A) = 0 - (1{,}000 - 800) + (1{,}200 - 800) = +200 \] \[ \Delta\mathrm{UGL}(a,B) = (1{,}500 - 800) - 0 - (1{,}200 - 800) = +300 \]

A answers for 100 → 120, B for 120 → 150: +500 in all, the portfolio's \(\Delta\mathrm{UGL}\) (\(700 - 200\)). Without \(T\), A would show −200 and B +700.

Portfolio-level period P&L also exposes a residual:

\[ \mathrm{Other} = \mathrm{PnL}_{period} - \Delta\mathrm{UGL} - \mathrm{Realized} - \mathrm{Income} + \mathrm{FeesTaxes} \]

Since UGL cannot contain the exchange result on cash (§5), Other splits into each broker's exchange result over the period and what remains:

\[ \mathrm{Other} = \sum_{b \in S} \mathrm{FXonCash}_b + \mathrm{Residual} \]

Unallocated fees/income without asset_id are grouped per broker as other period effects, and so is \(\mathrm{FXonCash}_b\): one row per broker holding foreign cash, shown when its result is not zero. See Period P&L — FX on Cash.

When every row is known, the rows and the other period effects together close \(\mathrm{PnL}_{period}\). Since the rows are valued as the portfolio is, the residual holds no valuation difference between them, only what no position holds: what travels between two brokers, the cost of a currency exchange, a disposal left out of Realized, the cost of dust.

Example: a sale that leaves 0.00001 units

10 units are bought at 100,000 before the period, and the price is 100,000 at \(t_0\): NAV is 1,000,000 and the unrealized 0. Inside the period, 9.99999 units are sold at 120,000 for 1,199,998.80: Realized is \(9.99999 \times 20{,}000 = 199{,}999.80\), and 0.00001 units are left; the price is 120,000 at \(t_1\) too, so they are worth 1.20 at a cost of 1.00. They are dust: they are in no row and not in NAV, so the row's and the portfolio's \(\Delta\mathrm{UGL}\) are both 0, and NAV at \(t_1\) is the cash of the sale. \(\mathrm{PnL}_{period} = 1{,}199{,}998.80 - 1{,}000{,}000 = 199{,}998.80\), and

\[ \mathrm{Other} = 199{,}998.80 - 0 - 199{,}999.80 = -1.00 \]

the cost of the dust. Valued in NAV, the dust would have put \(1.20 - 1.00 = 0.20\) into the portfolio's \(\Delta\mathrm{UGL}\) that no row had.

docs.title: 📐 8. Realized Gain/Loss
docs.text:
On a disposal of \(|q_s|\) units from position \((a,b)\) on date \(t\) — a SELL, or an outgoing ADJUSTMENT not linked to a split:

\[ C = |q_s| \cdot w_{\text{pre}}(a,b) \] \[ \mathrm{Realized} = P \cdot \mathrm{fx}(c_P, C^*, t) - C \]

\(P\) is what the units leave for, in its currency \(c_P\): a SELL's proceeds, in the currency of its cash; \(0\) for an outgoing ADJUSTMENT, which has no value whatever cost basis the row holds (Outgoing Adjustments), so it realizes \(-C\). \(w_{\text{pre}}\) is the WAC in \(C^*\) before the pool reduction (same value used by 3-pool SELL rule above): the units leave at their historical cost, with no conversion at \(t\), while \(P\) converts at \(t\). A disposal whose \(P\) cannot be converted, or drawn from a position whose cost is incomplete, is left out of Realized.

An outgoing ADJUSTMENT moves no cash, so no pool of §6 changes, and no capital either: the capital baseline does not move (Deposited Capital — Outgoing Adjustments).

docs.title: 📐 9. One Daily Replay
docs.text:
Range Date range Role Replay \([\min(t_{\mathrm{first}},\ t_0),\ t_1]\) Every day, with the same rules: cash, qty, WAC, pools, prices, FX, position and portfolio states Frame \([t_0,\ t_1]\) The days whose states are returned

There is one replay, from the first movement \(t_{\mathrm{first}}\) (or \(t_0\), when earlier) to \(t_1\). A movement dated before \(t_0\) follows the same rules as any other: it is converted at the rate of its own date and moves the WAC pools and the 3-pool K/R/W, and on every day the rate of a held foreign currency changes the cash is revalued and the exchange result enters the pools (§6). The states are returned from \(t_0\), so a day's state does not depend on the frame it is read in. A day on which no term of the model changes carries the previous day's state. A day changes it when it brings a movement, a change of a rate the day reads, a quote, a split, a transit boundary, a price turning stale or a rate turning stale; the first replayed day and the start of the frame are always computed.

When a price turns stale. A carried price is stale once its last observation \(o\) (a quote or a BUY/SELL trade) is more than \(\theta = 7\) days old. The flag of every day is computed as before, but the engine starts a new state on the first stale day, \(o+\theta+1\), only when the price is still carried then:

\[ \text{stale turn at } o+\theta+1 \iff \text{no observation of the asset falls in } (o,\ o+\theta+1] \]

A newer observation inside that stretch is a change of its own and renews the age of the price: with a Friday quote followed by a Monday quote, Friday + 8 days is not a turn, because the price in use then is Monday's and is not stale.

When a rate turns stale. A rate read to value the held securities (the currency of the asset and of its quotes against \(C^*\)) turns stale in the same way: when the stored row it comes from, dated \(r\), is more than \(\theta\) days old, the day \(r+\theta+1\) starts a new state, unless a newer row replaces it first. The state then carries the pair CCY/C* with the date \(r\) of its row, and the report lists it in data_quality.stale_fx_pairs as {pair, last_rate_date, stale_days} for the valuation day. The rate is still the last one known: staleness is a flag, not a different value.

docs.title: 🪜 Daily States as Steps
docs.text:
Between two days that change the state, every value of the report is identical. The portfolio report therefore does not return one point per calendar day: it returns one point per stretch without news, which holds from its date to its through, both included. The response carries range {start, end}, the window after clipping to the days that have a state.

{
  "range": {"start": "2026-10-23", "end": "2026-10-26"},
  "history": [
    {"date": "2026-10-23", "through": "2026-10-25", "nav_value": {"code": "EUR", "amount": "10450.00"}, "twrr": "0", "roi": "0.045000"},
    {"date": "2026-10-26", "through": "2026-10-26", "nav_value": {"code": "EUR", "amount": "10462.50"}, "twrr": "0.001196", "roi": "0.046250"}
  ],
  "mwrr_line": [
    {"date": "2026-10-23", "annualized": "0", "cumulative": "0"},
    {"date": "2026-10-25", "annualized": "0", "cumulative": "0"},
    {"date": "2026-10-26", "annualized": "0.156557", "cumulative": "0.001196"}
  ]
}

A fund held on Friday 23, Saturday 24, Sunday 25 and Monday 26 October, quoted on Friday and on Monday (the figures are illustrative, and the other fields of a point are left out). Saturday's NAV is the NAV of the step that contains it: \(\mathrm{NAV}(t)\) is read from the point with date \(\le t \le\) through, with a search by date and no calculation.

  • Which series. history, allocation_history.*, broker_pnl_history[].points and pnl_candles.points. The event series (income, cost, deposit, acquisition funding) are unchanged: one point per event.
  • Maximal steps. Two adjacent steps never carry identical values; the steps of a broker are maximal for its own P&L, not for the portfolio's.
  • Gaps. A day that no step covers has no value: a broker that starts mid-window, or a day without a P&L candle (a held asset could not be valued).
  • TWRR and ROI stay inside the steps. On a quiet day the TWRR factor is exactly 1 and the ROI does not change. The first point of the TWRR is pinned to 0, being period-relative. A step on which the NAV is zero or less carries no TWRR (null), under the same rule as the card (When No TWRR Is Shown); the chain keeps compounding through it, so the TWRR returns once the NAV is above zero again. The ROI's capital is the card's (The ROI of a Period).
  • MWRR moves every day, because time passes, and with several flows it has no closed form: it does not sit in the steps but in mwrr_line, a series of true values, each equal to the MWRR of the period ending that day, under the same rule as the card (no rate when the portfolio's value or the net invested capital is not positive). The line has a point at the date and at the through of every step; inside a step longer than 62 days it adds the last day of each calendar month strictly inside it, at most 24 per step, evenly spread. Its first point is pinned to 0.
  • Data quality follows the same idea: incomplete_nav_ranges, incomplete_book_value_ranges, incomplete_allocation_ranges and incomplete_valuation_ranges are lists of {start, end} with consecutive days merged. missing_fx_pairs[].dates holds only the dates of the movements, and missing_fx_pairs[].ranges the valuation days, merged. The older incomplete_*_dates lists are transitional.

docs.title: 📐 10. Performance Metrics (Layer 2)
docs.text:
Computed after daily states, as a separate pass:

Metric Formula Reference Total PnL \(\mathrm{NAV}(t) - \text{CapitalBaseline}(t)\) Deposited Capital Period PnL \(\mathrm{NAV}(t_1) - \mathrm{NAV}(t_0) - \text{ECF}_{[t_0,t_1]}\) Period P&L TWRR \(\prod_i (1 + r_i) - 1\) (sub-period chain) TWRR MWRR XIRR solving \(\sum \frac{CF_i}{(1+r)^{d_i/365}} = 0\) MWRR Simple ROI \((\mathrm{NAV} - \text{NetInvested}) / \text{NetInvested}\) ROI Net annualized return \((1+r_{\mathrm{net}})^{365/d}-1\), suppressed below 30 days Net Annualized Return Yield on Cost Trailing-365-day gross transaction income per eligible historical unit, divided by residual unit WAC at \(t_1\) Yield on Cost Timing Effect \(\text{MWRR}_{\text{cum}} - \text{TWRR}_{\text{cum}}\) Timing Effect

docs.title: 💡 What is it?
docs.text:
MWRR (also known as Internal Rate of Return) measures your personal performance as an investor. Unlike asset-only metrics, it accounts for both the performance of the underlying assets and the timing and size of your deposits and withdrawals.

To provide complete visibility, LibreFolio distinguishes between two forms of this metric: Annualized MWRR and Cumulative MWRR.

docs.title: 📈 Annualized MWRR
docs.text:
Annualized MWRR is the compound annual rate of return that makes the Net Present Value (NPV) of all cash flows equal to zero.

This compound rate is mathematically equivalent to the CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate) of your actual invested money, representing the smoothed annual growth rate required for the capital to grow to the final balance, accounting for all intermediate movements.

\[ 0 = \sum_{i=0}^{n} \frac{CF_i}{(1 + r)^{\frac{t_i}{365}}} \] 🧮 How the NPV Equation is Unfolded

Variable Descriptions:

  • \(r\) = Annualized MWRR (representing the CAGR of your actual money).
  • \(CF_i\) = Cash flow from the investor's perspective:
    • Negative cash flows (\(CF_i < 0\)): Capital committed to the portfolio (deposits, investments). This represents money leaving the investor's wallet.
    • Positive cash flows (\(CF_i > 0\)): Capital returned to the investor (withdrawals, dividends). This represents money returning to the wallet.
    • Final valuation (\(CF_n > 0\)): The final portfolio Net Asset Value (NAV) at the end of the period, treated as a positive inflow (a hypothetical liquidation where the entire portfolio is converted back to cash returning to the wallet).
  • \(t_i\) = Days elapsed since the start of the period (\(t_0 = 0\)).

Key Concepts:

  • It represents an annual velocity/rate of growth.
  • It is ideal for long-term comparisons (e.g., comparing your performance with an annual bank interest rate or CAGR).
  • Volatility Warning: On short periods (e.g., a few days or weeks), the annualized return can be highly volatile and display extreme percentages because the math extrapolates a small-window return to a full 365-day year.

LibreFolio builds MWRR cash flows from capital-baseline deltas, not cash-only deposit rows. Priced in-kind ADJUSTMENT/TRANSFER capital is therefore treated as contributed capital rather than as sudden investment performance. An outgoing ADJUSTMENT has no value: it returns nothing to the investor and is no cash flow (Deposited Capital — Outgoing Adjustments).

docs.title: 1. Intuitive Final Value Form
docs.text:
Imagine trying to project your final Net Asset Value (NAV) by growing each cash flow by a compound rate \(r\):

\[ NAV_{final} = CF_0 \times (1 + r)^{\frac{d_0}{365}} + CF_1 \times (1 + r)^{\frac{d_1}{365}} + \dots + CF_n \times (1 + r)^{\frac{d_n}{365}} \]

Where \(d_i\) represents the number of days each cash flow was invested during the period.

docs.title: 2. Discounting to Net Present Value (NPV = 0)
docs.text:
By dividing both sides of the equation by \((1 + r)^{\frac{\text{total days}}{365}}\), we shift all cash flows back to the start of the period (\(t_0\)). This gives us the standard Net Present Value equation where the sum of discounted cash flows equals zero:

\[ 0 = \sum_{i=0}^{n} \frac{CF_i}{(1 + r)^{\frac{t_i}{365}}} \]

Where \(t_i\) is the number of days from the start of the period to the date of cash flow \(i\).

docs.title: 3. Example of Unfolding Cash Flows
docs.text:
Let's see how cash flows populate for a portfolio over a 31-day period:

  • Day 0: Starting value of the portfolio is €1,000 (represented as a deposit/investment).
  • Day 15: You deposit €100.
  • Day 31: Final portfolio NAV is €1,150.

First, we construct the transaction table from the investor's perspective (money going into the portfolio is negative, money coming back is positive):

Step (\(i\)) Day (\(t_i\)) Event Wallet Cash Flow (\(CF_i\)) 0 0 Initial Balance -€1,000 (Outflow) 1 15 Deposit -€100 (Outflow) 2 31 Hypothetical Liquidation (NAV) +€1,150 (Inflow)

Now, we splay/unfold these transactions into the NPV summation:

\[ 0 = -1000 + \frac{-100}{(1+r)^{\frac{15}{365}}} + \frac{1150}{(1+r)^{\frac{31}{365}}} \]

The mathematical solver iteratively searches for the value of \(r\) (Annualized MWRR) that makes the right side of this equation equal to 0.

docs.title: 4. Cumulative Chart Anchor
docs.text:
This sign convention ensures that on the very first day (\(t_0\)), the initial deposit (\(CF_0 = -1000\)) and the hypothetical liquidation (\(CF_1 = +1000\)) cancel each other out:

\[ 0 = -1000 + 1000 = 0\% \]

This anchors the start of the Cumulative MWRR chart at exactly 0%.

docs.title: 📊 Cumulative MWRR
docs.text:
Cumulative MWRR represents the total equivalent return over the selected period, obtained by compounding the annualized rate for the actual duration of that window.

Direct Formula (without roots, uses \(r\) directly):

\[ \text{MWRR}_{\text{cumulative}} = (1 + r)^{\frac{\text{days}}{365}} - 1 \]

Daily Rate Formula (with root):

\[ \text{MWRR}_{\text{cumulative}} = (1 + r_d)^{\text{days}} - 1 \quad \text{where} \quad r_d = \sqrt[365]{1 + r} - 1 \]

Both formulas are mathematically equivalent. However, computationally, the direct formula using \(r\) (without roots) is preferred once the annualized rate \(r\) is found, as direct exponentiation is simpler and more efficient for the software to calculate.

Variable Descriptions:

  • \(\text{days}\) = The actual number of calendar days in the selected time window.

Key Concepts:

  • It represents the total distance covered over the period.
  • It starts at 0% and grows along the timeline, making it the correct metric for serial chart visualization.
  • Not a simple HPR: While it represents cumulative return, it is a money-weighted cumulative return. It should not be confused with the simple Holding Period Return (ROI), which ignores cash flow timing.

docs.title: 🔢 10-Year Numerical Example
docs.text:
Let's look at a 10-year scenario to see how timing impacts performance and how these metrics convert:

  • Year 0: You deposit €10,000.
  • Year 5: You deposit another €90,000.
  • Year 10: Your final Net Asset Value (NAV) is €200,000.

docs.title: 📉 Simple ROI Comparison
docs.text:
The simple ROI is calculated purely on total net contributions:

\[ ROI = \frac{200,000 - 100,000}{100,000} = +100\% \]

docs.title: ⏱️ MWRR Timing Effect
docs.text:
If the bulk of your capital (€90,000) was deposited in Year 5, right before a massive multi-year market recovery, your money worked very efficiently. Because the larger sum was exposed to the high-growth years, your Annualized MWRR would be much higher than the market's TWRR.

Using a mathematical NPV solver for this specific scenario: * Annualized MWRR (\(r\)) is exactly 13.02%.

docs.title: 🔁 Converting to Cumulative MWRR
docs.text:
By compounding this 13.02% annualized return over the 10-year period:

\[ \text{MWRR}_{\text{cumulative}} = (1 + 0.130227)^{10} - 1 \approx +240.14\% \]

docs.title: 💡 What does +240.14% mean?
docs.text:
• It does not mean that your total €100,000 contributions grew to €340,140.
  • It means that a theoretical euro, invested at the very beginning of the 10-year period and left untouched, would have grown to €3.40, achieving a total return of 240.14% by growing at the same average compound speed as your actual cash flows.

docs.title: 🖥️ UI Integration & Dashboard Usage
docs.text: LibreFolio displays these performance metrics across the dashboard:

docs.title: 📊 Percent Chart (%)
docs.text: Plotted series use Cumulative MWRR, Cumulative TWRR, and Simple ROI. This allows direct, side-by-side visual comparison as all three series start at 0% and represent total progress over the selected timeframe.

docs.title: 📐 The MWRR Line Is Made of True Points
docs.text: Unlike TWRR and ROI, the MWRR changes even on a day on which nothing happens: time passes, and with several flows there is no closed form that extends it from one day to the next. In the portfolio report it is therefore not stored in the daily steps of the history but in its own series, mwrr_line, whose points are true values: each is the MWRR of the period ending on its day, solved on that day, annualized and cumulative, with the same rule as the cards (see below). The line has a point at the start and at the end of every step of the history, plus one at the end of each calendar month inside the steps longer than 62 days (at most 24 per step); its first point is 0. Nothing between two points is estimated or stored: the chart joins them.

docs.title: 🧾 KPI Cards
docs.text:
• Simple ROI (Primary metric for absolute return).
  • Cumulative TWRR (Strategy/allocation performance indicator).
  • Cumulative MWRR (Primary personal timing indicator).
  • Annualized MWRR (Shown as a secondary/comparative metric to understand the compound yearly rate).

docs.title: 🚫 When No MWRR Is Shown
docs.text:
The KPI cards and the MWRR line of the chart follow the same rule on every day of the period. A day has an MWRR only when:

  • the portfolio's value on that day is above zero, and
  • the period still holds net invested capital on that day: the value it opened with, plus the deposits, minus the withdrawals made up to that day (the capital flows described above), is above zero.

Otherwise there is no rate: the card shows —, and the line has a gap (a point without a value). After net withdrawals, the gap starts on the day they take the net invested capital to zero or below, and lasts until new deposits bring it back above zero. The cards always show the line's last point, so a card without MWRR goes with a line that ends in a gap. A day also has no MWRR when no rate solves the cash-flow equation: LibreFolio never shows a rate that does not solve it.

Analyzing the Performance Difference

To interpret the difference between Cumulative MWRR and Cumulative TWRR, refer to the Timing Effect page.

docs.title: 💡 What is NAV?
docs.text: Net Asset Value (NAV) is the total market valuation of your portfolio at a point in time \(t\). It answers: "How much is the portfolio worth right now?"

docs.title: 🧮 Formula
docs.text:
\[ \boxed{\mathrm{NAV}(t) = \mathrm{MV}(t) + \mathrm{Cash}(t) + \mathrm{InTransit}(t)} \]

Where:

\[ \mathrm{MV}(t)= \sum_{(a,b)\in S} \frac{q(a,b,t)}{qbq(a)} \cdot \operatorname{mark}(a,t) \cdot \mathrm{fx}(\mathrm{ccy}_{mark}, C^*, t) \]

and the cash of each broker, kept in the currencies it was recorded in and valued at the rate of \(t\):

\[ \mathrm{Cash}(t) = \sum_{b \in S} \sum_{c} N_{b,c}(t) \cdot \mathrm{fx}(c, C^*, t) \]

with \(N_{b,c}(t)\) the balance broker \(b\) holds in currency \(c\) on \(t\), scaled by the broker's ownership share, and \(\mathrm{fx}(c, C^*, t)\) the latest rate on or before \(t\) (\(1\) for \(c = C^*\)). Cash held in another currency therefore moves NAV when its exchange rate moves.

A position whose asset has no mark yet — no quote, no BUY or SELL and no transfer cost estimate on or before \(t\) — enters \(\mathrm{MV}(t)\) at its cost basis \(\mathrm{CB}(a,b,t)\) instead when that cost is complete, and is left out of NAV otherwise.

🔗 See Portfolio Engine — §3 Position State and §5 Aggregation for full derivation.

docs.title: 🔗 Unified Price Resolver
docs.text:
The mark \(\operatorname{mark}(a,t)\) comes from the unified resolver:

  1. MARKET — same-day asset-system quote.
  2. TRADE_AVG — average same-day BUY/SELL observation, or the cost of an incoming transfer for an asset with nothing else yet (estimate).
  3. CARRIED — last observation before \(t\), carried forward (LOCF).
  4. MISSING — no observation on or before \(t\).

An ADJUSTMENT is never an observation, with or without a cost basis: it records a cost, not a price. An incoming transfer's cost counts only as an estimate, only while the asset has no quote and no other operation on or before that day.

Marks remain in native currency until valuation, and so do cash balances, each in the currency it was recorded in; FX conversion happens at \(t\). WAC is never a price: only a position with no mark at all is counted at its cost basis, a declared estimate (ESTIMATED_AT_COST) that keeps the exchange rates of its acquisition dates. See Price Resolution.

docs.title: 📝 Example
docs.text: Component Amount Market Value of Assets €32,759 Cash Balance €631 In-Transit €0 \[ \mathrm{NAV} = 32\,759 + 631 + 0 = 33\,390 \text{ EUR} \]

docs.title: ⚖️ Key Distinctions
docs.text:
• NAV vs Book Value: NAV = market value; Book = acquisition cost. Difference = unrealized gains.
  • NAV vs Period PnL: NAV = snapshot; Period PnL = flow-adjusted change over time.

docs.title: ⚠️ Data Quality
docs.text:
Valuation Source Confidence MARKET_PRICE Full — real quote, exact or carried LAST_TRADE_PRICE Partial — trade-origin resolver mark ESTIMATED_AT_COST Estimate — no price at all: the cost basis, with no unrealized gain or loss MISSING None — no price and an incomplete cost: excluded from NAV

estimated=True only applies to TRADE-origin marks. A stale carried MARKET quote is stale but not estimated.

For an asset with a price provider, the Dashboard warns as of the valuation date: a trade-origin valuation, once the asset has had no market quote for more than the 14-day grace period — counted from the transfer's arrival for an asset never quoted, bought or sold, valued at a transfer's cost —, raises the “valued at their last transaction price” warning, and a valuation at cost, more than 14 days after the asset's first acquisition, raises the “valued at cost” warning. An asset without a provider raises neither: its trades, or its cost, are its intended value.

docs.title: 💡 Purpose
docs.text:
LibreFolio reports annualized return only when the observed window is long enough to make compounding meaningful. The shared conversion is:

\[ \boxed{r_{\mathrm{ann}} = (1+r_{\mathrm{cum}})^{365/d}-1} \]

where \(d\) is calendar days. It is the inverse of:

\[ r_{\mathrm{cum}}=(1+r_{\mathrm{ann}})^{d/365}-1 \]

The implementation returns None when:

  • \(r_{\mathrm{cum}} \leq -1\)
  • \(d < 30\)
  • the computation overflows

Thirty-day guard

A one-week return annualized to 365 days can explode into meaningless percentages. LibreFolio therefore suppresses annualization below 30 days and displays an empty value instead of a mathematically correct but misleading CAGR.

docs.title: 🧾 Holdings View
docs.text:
For an open holding in “Your positions” / portfolio summary:

\[ r_{\mathrm{net}} = \frac{ \mathrm{MarketComponent} + \mathrm{Income} - \mathrm{FeesTaxes} }{ \mathrm{CostBasis} } \]

where:

\[ \mathrm{MarketComponent} = \begin{cases} \mathrm{CurrentValue}-\mathrm{CostBasis}, & \text{market value exists}\\ 0, & \text{price-less / valued at cost} \end{cases} \]

Annualization window:

\[ d = t_{\mathrm{report}} - t_{\mathrm{first\ lot\ affecting}} \]

Lot-affecting transaction types are:

\[ \{\text{BUY},\ \text{SELL},\ \text{ADJUSTMENT},\ \text{TRANSFER}\} \]

This includes in-kind successions, broker transfers, and adjustment-seeded positions. Old BUY/SELL-only discovery would miss those holdings.

docs.title: 🪟 Period View
docs.text:
For per-asset period contribution:

\[ \mathrm{PnL}_{period} = \Delta \mathrm{UGL} + \mathrm{Realized} + \mathrm{Income} - \mathrm{FeesTaxes} \]

The displayed period percentage remains:

\[ r_{\mathrm{period}} = \frac{\mathrm{PnL}_{period}}{|\mathrm{StartValue}|} \]

when StartValue is non-zero. Annualization can fall back to end cost basis for assets opened mid-period:

\[ \mathrm{ann\_base}= \begin{cases} |\mathrm{StartValue}|, & |\mathrm{StartValue}|>0\\ \mathrm{CostBasis}_{end} + \sum_a \left(V_a - C_a\right), & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

The sum is over the transfers from another broker of the scope the position received in the period, each counted as in Positions Closed in the Period: what their units gained before they arrived, value on arrival less the historical cost moved (MF-A9). The position's result counts those units from their value on arrival, its end cost at their historical cost, so the base adds the same amount. It applies only while no unit has left the position in the period, before the arrival or after it: once units left it, a transfer carries no quantity to tell which part of the sum left with them, and the sum is dropped — the end cost alone is the base, as for any position opened mid-period that sold part of what it bought.

Window start is clamped to the oldest FIFO lot still open at period end:

\[ t_{\mathrm{start}}=\max(t_{\mathrm{from}},\ t_{\mathrm{oldest\ open\ lot}}) \]

Lots are counted at each broker: a transfer opens a lot dated at its arrival at the receiving broker. A stock split rescales the open lots and keeps their dates, so it never shortens the window. The oldest lots that together hold \(10^{-5}\) units or fewer — the residual a sale leaves — are set aside, as a closed position counts such a residual as closed: a residual left years ago does not pull the window start back to its date, and a position holding nothing more than that residual has no open lot (MF-A7). The quantities are the engine's, at the owner's share of the broker: on a broker held at 50 %, a residual of \(0.000012\) units is \(0.000006\) for the owner, dust for the window as for the row (MF-A10).

Then:

\[ r_{\mathrm{ann}} = \operatorname{annualize}\left(\frac{\mathrm{PnL}_{period}}{\mathrm{ann\_base}},\ t_{\mathrm{end}}-t_{\mathrm{start}}\right) \]

docs.title: 🔚 Positions Closed in the Period
docs.text:
A position is closed when its quantity at \(t_{\mathrm{end}}\), at the owner's share of the broker, is at or below the dust threshold of \(10^{-5}\) units, so a residual left by redemptions in tranches counts as closed. It has no end cost, and a start value says nothing about a holding sold a few weeks in. Its annualized return uses the capital it deployed and the time it was held inside the period:

\[ \mathrm{CostOut} = \sum_{s\,\in\,(t_{\mathrm{from}},\ t_{\mathrm{end}}]} C_s \;+\; \sum_{m\,\in\,(t_{\mathrm{from}},\ t_{\mathrm{end}}]} C_m \;+\; \sum_{a\,\in\,(t_{\mathrm{from}},\ t_{\mathrm{end}}]} \left(V_a - C_a\right) \] \[ t_{\mathrm{start}} = \max(t_{\mathrm{from}},\ t_{\mathrm{first\ opening}}), \qquad t_{\mathrm{close}} = \text{last day its quantity fell to the dust threshold or below} \] \[ r_{\mathrm{ann}} = \operatorname{annualize}\left(\frac{\mathrm{PnL}_{period}}{\mathrm{CostOut}},\ t_{\mathrm{close}}-t_{\mathrm{start}}\right) \]
  • \(C_s\) is the historical cost, in \(C^*\), of each disposal the period's Realized counts — a SELL, or an outgoing ADJUSTMENT not linked to a split (Portfolio Engine — §8). A disposal left out of Realized adds no cost.
  • \(C_m\) is the historical cost each transfer to another broker of the scope moved out, when the row counts that transfer's tract: it left after \(t_{\mathrm{from}}\), arrived by \(t_{\mathrm{end}}\), and both its value on arrival and the cost moved are known (Period P&L, developer decision P22). The row's result carries what those units did until they arrived (the tract adjustment), so their cost belongs in the base.
  • \(V_a - C_a\) is, for each such transfer the position received, what its units gained before they arrived: their value on arrival less the historical cost moved with them. The row's result starts those units at \(V_a\) (the tract adjustment takes back \(V_a - C_a\)), while \(C_s\) and \(C_m\) carry their historical cost, so the base adds the same amount and counts them at their value on arrival too (MF-A8). So \(\mathrm{CostOut}\) is not only historical cost: for the units the position received, the base holds their value on arrival.
  • \(t_{\mathrm{first\ opening}}\) is the position's first acquisition at that broker: a transfer opens it on its arrival there, a split never does. It is the first one ever, not the last lot's, so days at zero between two closes inside the period stay in the window.
  • The numerator is the row's whole \(\mathrm{PnL}_{period}\): for a position held at \(t_{\mathrm{from}}\), its \(\Delta\mathrm{UGL}\) gives back the unrealized gain/loss it started with.
  • The displayed period percentage keeps \(|\mathrm{StartValue}|\) as base: only the annualized value changes base and window.

When this gives no value, two cases follow:

  • Fewer than 30 days held in the period, \(t_{\mathrm{close}} - t_{\mathrm{start}} < 30\): the row has no annualized return (—), whatever else made the base unusable. The rule above would annualize over \(t_{\mathrm{from}} \to t_{\mathrm{end}}\), as if ten days held had lasted the whole period (MF-A3).
  • Otherwise the row keeps the rule above. That happens when units left the position in any other way — a transfer outside the scope, or still in transit at \(t_{\mathrm{end}}\), a transfer or a disposal whose value or cost is unknown — since the row's result would then hold more than its base covers; and with a return of \(-100\%\) or worse. The rule above is: \(|\mathrm{StartValue}|\) over \(t_{\mathrm{from}} \to t_{\mathrm{end}}\), and no value for a position opened in the period.
Example: a position sold 90 days into a one-year period

At \(t_{\mathrm{from}}\) the position is worth 1,100 for a cost of 1,000. All of it is sold 90 days later for 1,250:

\[ \mathrm{PnL}_{period} = (0 - 100) + (1{,}250 - 1{,}000) = +150 \] \[ r_{\mathrm{ann}} = \operatorname{annualize}\left(\frac{150}{1{,}000},\ 90\right) = 1.15^{365/90} - 1 \approx +76.3\% \]

The unrealized +100 it started with comes back out of \(\Delta\mathrm{UGL}\), Realized adds +250. The period percentage stays \(150 / 1{,}100 = 13.64\%\); annualized over the whole year on the start value, as an open position would be, the same +150 would read 13.64% as well.

Example: half sold, half moved to another broker

At \(t_{\mathrm{from}}\) the position holds 10 units, worth 1,100 for a cost of 1,000. Five are sold for 625; five move to another broker of the scope and are worth 600 when they arrive:

\[ \mathrm{PnL}_{period} = \underbrace{(0 - 100)}_{\Delta\mathrm{UGL}} + \underbrace{(625 - 500)}_{\text{Realized}} + \underbrace{(600 - 500)}_{\text{tract}} = +125 \] \[ \mathrm{CostOut} = 500 + 500 = 1{,}000, \qquad \frac{125}{1{,}000} = 12.5\% \]

The cost of the sold units alone would read \(125 / 500 = 25\%\): the moved units' result in the numerator, without their cost in the base (MF-A5).

The broker that received the five units and later sold them for 660 reads the mirror: its result is \((660 - 500) - (600 - 500) = +60\), and its base \(500 + (600 - 500) = 600\), so \(60 / 600 = 10\%\) — the units count from their value on arrival, in the result and in the base alike (MF-A8).

docs.title: 🧬 FIFO Lots
docs.text:
FIFO lot annualized return is net of allocated income, fees, and taxes:

\[ \mathrm{NetTotalPnL}_i = \mathrm{MarketPnL}_i + \mathrm{RealizedPnL}_i + \mathrm{Income}_i - \mathrm{Fees}_i - \mathrm{Taxes}_i \] \[ \mathrm{NetTotalReturn}_i = \frac{\mathrm{NetTotalPnL}_i}{\mathrm{OpeningValue}_i} \]

The annualized value uses net_total_return, not gross total_return:

\[ r_{\mathrm{ann},i} = \operatorname{annualize} \left( \mathrm{NetTotalReturn}_i,\ t_{\mathrm{lot\ end}}-t_{\mathrm{opening}} \right) \]

where \(t_{\mathrm{lot\ end}}\) is the closing date for fully closed lots, otherwise the analysis end date.

docs.title: 💡 What is Period PnL?
docs.text: The absolute monetary gain or loss generated by your portfolio within \([t_0, t_1]\), adjusted for external cash flows.

docs.title: 🧮 Formula
docs.text:
\[ \boxed{\mathrm{PnL}_{\text{period}} = \mathrm{NAV}(t_1)-\mathrm{NAV}(t_0)-\Delta \mathrm{CapitalBaseline}_{[t_0,t_1]}} \]

The baseline delta comes from cumulative_external_cash_flow, so it includes cash flows and priced in-kind ADJUSTMENT/TRANSFER capital. An outgoing ADJUSTMENT has no value and takes nothing out (Deposited Capital — Outgoing Adjustments).

docs.title: 🧮 Decomposition
docs.text:
\[ \mathrm{PnL}_{\text{period}} = \Delta\mathrm{UGL} + \mathrm{Realized} + \mathrm{Income} - \mathrm{FeesTaxes} + \mathrm{Other} \] Component Definition \(\Delta\mathrm{UGL}\) Change in unrealized gain/loss over the period: market value − open cost basis of the positions held at each boundary, securities in transit left out (the period unrealized) — for assets priced in another currency, including the exchange-rate effect on their historical cost Realized Sum of (proceeds − historical cost of the units given up) for the SELLs in period and the outgoing ADJUSTMENTs not linked to a split, whose proceeds are zero; proceeds are converted at the transaction's date (Portfolio Engine — §8) Income DIVIDEND + INTEREST in period FeesTaxes FEE + TAX in period Other What closes the identity: the exchange result on cash held in another currency (FX on cash), the gain securities accrued outside the view before crossing its boundary (transfers at market value), plus a residual

Other is computed as:

\[ \mathrm{Other} = \mathrm{PnL}_{\text{period}} - \Delta\mathrm{UGL} - \mathrm{Realized} - \mathrm{Income} + \mathrm{FeesTaxes} \]

Because the cost basis keeps its historical exchange rates (see Book Value), the effect of exchange rates on foreign assets is part of \(\Delta\mathrm{UGL}\), not of Other. Cash held in another currency is different: NAV and Book both value it at each day's rate, so its exchange-rate effect cancels in the unrealized gain/loss and is not in \(\Delta\mathrm{UGL}\). It is the first part of Other, the FX on cash of each broker \(b\), which the Period view shows per broker. The second part, the transfers at market value, is shown per broker too:

\[ \mathrm{Other} = \sum_{b \in S} \mathrm{FXonCash}_b + \sum_{b \in S} \mathrm{TMV}_b + \mathrm{Residual} \]

The residual holds what neither the four components, the exchange result on cash nor the transfers at market value can see:

  • the exchange-rate move of cash while it travels between two brokers: in transit, it belongs to no broker's balance;
  • the cost of a currency exchange, at one broker or across two: −1,000 USD worth €920 at the day's rate, exchanged into +€900, gives −€20, which is neither a fee nor a sale;
  • the value of assets travelling between two brokers on a boundary day;
  • a sale left out of Realized because its proceeds could not be converted, or a sale or an outgoing ADJUSTMENT left out because its position's cost is incomplete.
  • the cost of dust: a sale that leaves \(10^{-5}\) units or fewer in a position takes what is left out of the open cost basis without selling it, so its cost is in neither \(\Delta\mathrm{UGL}\) nor Realized — 0.00001 units bought at 100,000 leave −1.00 here (§7).

docs.title: 💵 FX on Cash
docs.text:
For each broker \(b\) holding cash in a currency other than \(C^*\), over the period \((t_0, t_1]\), \(t_0\) being the opening state:

\[ \mathrm{FXonCash}_b = \sum_{c \neq C^*} \Bigl[N_{b,c}(t_1)\,\mathrm{fx}(c, C^*, t_1) - N_{b,c}(t_0)\,\mathrm{fx}(c, C^*, t_0)\Bigr] - \sum_{\substack{m \in (t_0, t_1] \\ \mathrm{ccy}(m) \neq C^*}} s_m \cdot \mathrm{amount}_m \cdot \mathrm{fx}(\mathrm{ccy}(m), C^*, d_m) \]

\(N_{b,c}(t)\) is the balance \(b\) holds in currency \(c\) on \(t\), scaled by the broker's share, and \(\mathrm{fx}\) the latest rate on or before the day. The second sum runs over \(b\)'s movements in a foreign currency dated in the period: each amount, scaled by the share \(s_m\), at the rate of its own date \(d_m\). The first term is the change in value of the foreign cash, the second what the movements brought in or took out: the difference is what the exchange rates did to the cash the broker held. It equals the exchange results the engine books on the period's rate-change days (Portfolio Engine — §6). Cash in \(C^*\) has none.

Example: dollars at a broker on a euro dashboard

A broker holds 1,000 USD for the whole period while the rate goes from 0.90 to 0.92 EUR per USD:

\[ \mathrm{FXonCash} = 1{,}000 \times 0.92 - 1{,}000 \times 0.90 = +20 \text{ EUR} \]

With a deposit of 500 USD in the middle of the period at 0.91, and 0.92 at the end:

\[ \mathrm{FXonCash} = 1{,}500 \times 0.92 - 1{,}000 \times 0.90 - 500 \times 0.91 = 1{,}380 - 900 - 455 = +25 \text{ EUR} \]

The deposit entered the capital at €455; the +€25 is what the dollars gained against the euro while the broker held them.

docs.title: 🔀 Transfers at Market Value
docs.text:
In a view that selects only some brokers, a TRANSFER leg whose other side is outside the view — securities sent to a broker that is not selected, received from one, or a transfer with no counterpart — is in-kind capital at its market value on its date, while the position's cost moves with it (Deposited Capital). The gain the units accrued at the other broker is therefore in neither \(\Delta\mathrm{UGL}\) nor Realized, and used to end up in the residual. It is the second part of Other. For each broker \(b\) of the view, over the legs \(\ell\) dated in \((t_0, t_1]\):

\[ \mathrm{TMV}_b = \sum_{\ell \in (t_0, t_1]} \bigl(\mathrm{Cost}_\ell - \mathrm{Capital}_\ell\bigr) \]

\(\mathrm{Capital}_\ell\) is the market value the leg adds to the capital (positive when received, negative when sent) and \(\mathrm{Cost}_\ell\) the cost it moves in the position (same sign), both in \(C^*\) at the broker's share. For units with market value \(\mathrm{MV}\) and cost \(C\):

Leg \(\mathrm{Capital}\) \(\mathrm{Cost}\) Contribution Sent out of the view \(-\mathrm{MV}\) \(-C\) \(+(\mathrm{MV} - C)\) Received from outside the view \(+\mathrm{MV}\) \(+C\) \(-(\mathrm{MV} - C)\)

The sender's view takes the gain the units made while it held them as a result of its own; the receiver's view starts from the value they arrive with, so what they gained before is not its result and is taken out. A figure below the rounding threshold is not shown, and the residual drops by the amount shown. With both brokers selected nothing changes: the pair is internal, and the units only split the result between the two rows (see the internal transfer under Per-Asset Contribution below).

Example: units bought at one broker and sent to another

10 units bought at 50 each (cost €500) on broker A are sent to broker B when worth €800.

  • View on A only: the units leave at €800 of capital and take €500 of cost with them: \(\mathrm{TMV}_A = -500 + 800 = +300\) EUR.
  • View on B only: the units arrive at €800 of capital with €500 of cost: \(\mathrm{TMV}_B = 500 - 800 = -300\) EUR.
  • View on A and B: no such row.

docs.title: 💱 Unrealized Change by Currency
docs.text:
\(\Delta\mathrm{UGL}\) is split by the currency \(A\) the assets are priced in. For the positions in currency \(A\) on day \(t\), let

Symbol Meaning \(\mathrm{MV}_A(t)\) Their market value in \(C^*\), at the day's price and rate \(\mathrm{Cost}^{A}_A(t)\) Their historical cost in \(A\) \(\mathrm{Cost}^{*}_A(t)\) Their historical cost in \(C^*\) \(r_A(t) = \mathrm{fx}(A, C^*, t)\) The day's exchange rate

Each acquisition's cost in \(A\) comes from its cost in \(C^*\) at the acquisition date, \(c^{A} = c^{*} \cdot \mathrm{fx}(C^*, A, d)\) (or the amount paid, when paid in \(A\)). The unrealized gain/loss then splits exactly into an asset effect and an exchange-rate effect:

\[ E^{\text{asset}}_A(t) = \mathrm{MV}_A(t) - \mathrm{Cost}^{A}_A(t)\, r_A(t) \] \[ E^{\text{fx}}_A(t) = \mathrm{Cost}^{A}_A(t)\, r_A(t) - \mathrm{Cost}^{*}_A(t) \] \[ E^{\text{asset}}_A(t) + E^{\text{fx}}_A(t) = \mathrm{MV}_A(t) - \mathrm{Cost}^{*}_A(t) = \mathrm{UGL}_A(t) \]

For a mark quoted in \(A\), \(\mathrm{MV}_A(t) = \frac{q}{qbq} \cdot \mathrm{mark}_A(t) \cdot r_A(t)\), so the asset effect is the assets' own change in their currency, translated at the day's rate: \(E^{\text{asset}}_A(t) = \bigl(\frac{q}{qbq} \cdot \mathrm{mark}_A(t) - \mathrm{Cost}^{A}_A(t)\bigr)\, r_A(t)\). The exchange-rate effect is zero on the day of each purchase. For \(A = C^*\), \(r = 1\) and \(\mathrm{Cost}^{A} = \mathrm{Cost}^{*}\): the exchange-rate effect vanishes, and assets already in the report currency have an asset effect only.

A position in a currency \(A \neq C^*\) that cannot be split on day \(t\) — no market value, no rate \(r_A(t)\), or a cost incomplete in either currency — adds its whole \(\mathrm{MV} - \mathrm{Cost}^{*}\) (with \(\mathrm{MV} = 0\) when it has no market value) to an unsplit part \(E^{\text{unsplit}}_A(t)\) instead. Positions in \(C^*\) always count in the asset effect. A position valued at its cost because its asset has no mark at all (Portfolio Engine — §3) has \(\mathrm{MV} = \mathrm{Cost}^{*}\) and adds to no part: splitting it would invent an asset effect and an exchange-rate effect of opposite sign.

The period rows are the changes between the period's two boundary states — the last state on or before \(t_0\) (zero if there is none) and the state at \(t_1\) —, the same two states as \(\Delta\mathrm{UGL}\):

\[ \Delta E^{k}_A = E^{k}_A(t_1) - E^{k}_A(t_0), \qquad k \in \{\text{asset}, \text{fx}, \text{unsplit}\} \] \[ \sum_{A}\ \sum_{k} \Delta E^{k}_A = \Delta\mathrm{UGL} \quad \text{exactly} \] Example: a US ETF on a euro dashboard

10 units bought for €400 when they were worth 500 USD, so \(\mathrm{Cost}^{*} = 400\) EUR and \(\mathrm{Cost}^{A} = 500\) USD.

Day Value in USD \(r_{USD}\) MV in EUR \(E^{\text{asset}}\) \(E^{\text{fx}}\) \(\mathrm{UGL}\) \(t_0\) 520 USD 0.78 405.60 \((520-500) \times 0.78 = 15.60\) \(500 \times 0.78 - 400 = -10.00\) 5.60 \(t_1\) 550 USD 0.75 412.50 \((550-500) \times 0.75 = 37.50\) \(500 \times 0.75 - 400 = -25.00\) 12.50 \[ \Delta E^{\text{asset}} = +21.90, \qquad \Delta E^{\text{fx}} = -15.00, \qquad \Delta\mathrm{UGL} = +6.90 \text{ EUR} \]

The ETF gained in dollars (+€21.90), the dollar lost ground against the euro (−€15.00): together, the +€6.90 of the period's unrealized change.

docs.title: 🎯 Per-Asset Contribution
docs.text:
For each position \((a,b)\):

\[ \mathrm{PnL}(a,b) = \Delta\mathrm{UGL}(a,b) + \mathrm{Realized}(a,b) + \mathrm{Income}(a,b) - \mathrm{FeesTaxes}(a,b) \]

The position set includes all activity in the period:

\[ \mathcal{P} = \text{positions with BUY/SELL/ADJUSTMENT/TRANSFER activity or boundary quantity} \]

A position's start and end values are the portfolio's own valuation of it at the end of \(t_0\) and of \(t_1\), the two states of \(\Delta\mathrm{UGL}\) (Portfolio Engine — §3):

  • its mark (§2): a market quote, or else a BUY/SELL price — or, for an asset with nothing else yet, the cost of an incoming transfer as an estimate —, a trade price being restated through any later split;
  • its cost basis, for a holding whose asset has no mark at all (ESTIMATED_AT_COST);
  • converted at the exchange rate of the boundary day itself.

The rows therefore add up to the portfolio: when every row is known, \(\sum_{(a,b)} \Delta\mathrm{UGL}(a,b) = \Delta\mathrm{UGL}\), and the rows plus the other period effects — unallocated income and costs, FX on cash, transfers at market value, the residual — close \(\mathrm{PnL}_{\text{period}}\). Other holds no valuation difference. A position left with \(10^{-5}\) units or fewer — dust — is held neither by a row nor by the portfolio, so it changes nothing in the identity (§3); its cost is in the residual (above).

  • Internal transfer. A security moved between two of your brokers inside the period splits its result: the sending broker's row answers for the units until they arrive, the receiving broker's from their arrival, and the total is unchanged. A transfer already in transit at \(t_0\), or still in transit at \(t_1\), keeps the plain boundary values (§7).
  • Unknown values. A position held at a boundary whose unrealized gain/loss is unknown there — a missing exchange rate, an incomplete cost — has an unknown \(\Delta\mathrm{UGL}(a,b)\), never the known side minus zero.

Annualized period return clamps its window start to the later of the requested start and the oldest open lot date. It uses \(|\mathrm{StartValue}|\) as annualization base, falling back to end cost basis for positions opened mid-period. See Net Annualized Return.

A position closed in the period — nothing left at \(t_1\) — annualizes differently: on the historical cost of the units that left it in the period — sold, or moved to another broker of the scope — over the time it was held inside it, from the later of \(t_0\) and its first opening to the day its last units left. Its period percentage keeps \(|\mathrm{StartValue}|\) as base. See Net Annualized Return — Positions Closed in the Period.

🔗 See Portfolio Engine — §7 Period Contribution for details.

docs.title: 📝 Example
docs.text:
• NAV at \(t_0\): €27,000
  • Capital baseline increase in period: €1,000
  • NAV at \(t_1\): €33,000
\[ \mathrm{PnL} = 33\,000 - 27\,000 - 1\,000 = +5\,000 \text{ EUR} \]
