docs.title: ➕ Create & Edit Assets
docs.text: Add an instrument you hold or follow, connect it to a price provider and keep its details right.

docs.title: 🚀 Create an asset
docs.text:
From the Assets pageFrom a broker import
  1. On the Assets page, click + Add Asset.
  2. In Search Online, type a name, ticker or ISIN and pick a result: LibreFolio fills in the form, connects that provider and checks its data. No result? Fill in the form yourself, and report the search with Let us know.
  3. Check the fields below, then click Create Asset.
  1. In the import wizard's Resolve Assets section, choose Create new asset in the security's selector.
  2. The form opens with the report's codes and names. If the report has no name, Name starts with the ISIN (or the ticker).
  3. Click one of the Suggestions under Search Online to look the security up, or fill in the form yourself. Then click Create Asset.

If the result you pick has the same name as one of your assets, LibreFolio offers to use that asset instead; Use it and add the key also saves the report's codes on it.

Check these fields before saving:

  • Name: required and unique; a warning appears if another asset already uses it.
  • Type: see Choose the asset type.
  • Units per single price: how many units one price refers to, usually 1, and 100 for most bonds. Picking a Search Online result sets it, as it sets the name: to the provider's suggestion if it makes one, with a note under the field saying why (Yahoo Finance suggests 100 for a London line quoted in pence, for example), otherwise to 100 for a Bond and 1 for any other type. It does so in Edit Asset too, over the saved value, which changes only when you save. Typing in the field removes the note. Choosing the Type yourself leaves the field as it is; for a Bond, a hint reminds you that bonds are usually quoted per 100.
  • Currency: the currency the prices are quoted in. For a fund listed in euros that is EUR, even when the fund is denominated in another currency.

After saving from the Assets page, the confirmation links to the new asset. If the asset has a provider, its price history starts downloading right away.

docs.title: 🔎 Search Online results
docs.text:
Search Online asks the providers all at once and sorts their results as they arrive: premium sources first (those your instance vouches for, such as licensed data), then community ones, each group by priority. None of the providers that come with LibreFolio is premium, and all have the same priority: the results appear as the providers answer, unless your administrator changes the order.

When the search included a premium source, the list has two parts:

  • Premium: the premium sources' results, or No results from the premium sources.
  • Non-premium sources (community) · N results, closed. Opening it first shows a warning: these are third-party sources, LibreFolio does not vouch for their prices or data, and choosing one applies to this asset only. The section is closed again the next time you open the form.

docs.title: 📨 Can't find it? Let us know
docs.text:
Once a search has finished, whatever it found, even after an error or a timeout, the list offers Can't find it? Let us know (between the two parts, when there are two), as long as the app knows where to send the report. The report goes to whoever supports your instance. If the list has closed, click in the search box to bring it back; emptying the box forgets the search.

Where the link leads depends on your instance's support address; its tooltip tells you which:

Support address What Let us know does An email address Your email app opens a message with the subject and the details filled in A web page The page opens in a new tab with the subject and the details in its address, so a support form can fill itself in. The details are copied too, ready to paste there; a message confirms the copy, or says it failed None (the default), on a self-hosted instance A new GitHub issue opens in a new tab, filled in. It is public: review it before you submit it

The link is missing, even with a support address, when the app could not read your instance's configuration; reloading the page tries again.

The details are in English: the text you searched; each provider asked and its outcome (how many results, no answer, or an error, with its code when it has one; never the error's message); the identifiers already in the form, and its currency and type unless they are still the defaults of a new, blank form (your base currency and Stock); your LibreFolio version, the instance profile and the language of the app. When you edit an asset, the details therefore include the asset's own identifiers (ISIN, ticker…), its currency and its type, as the form shows them. They never include who you are, an email address, your instance's address or any portfolio data. You send the report yourself, from your own device: it never goes through the LibreFolio server.

docs.title: 🗂️ Choose the asset type
docs.text:
The Type field opens a searchable menu of asset types. ETF and Crowdfunding are families: open one to see its generic member first (ETF, Crowdfund), then specific ones such as Equity ETF or Real estate crowdfunding. Type a few letters to search both levels, by name or code (for example etf_bond).

Search Online usually sets a general type such as ETF. If you know what the fund holds, refine it, for example to Equity ETF: its badge and icon then show what it holds. A later check against the provider's data keeps your choice.

docs.title: 🔌 Connect a price provider
docs.text:
Picking a Search Online result connects its provider for you. To set one up by hand, expand Provider Assignment (untick No Provider first if it is ticked):

  1. Choose the Provider, then enter the Identifier, its Identifier Type and any settings the provider asks for.
  2. Click Test Configuration: LibreFolio fetches a Current Price and a few days of History. ⚠️ means the provider does not offer that data or has none right now (CSS Scraper has no history, for example); the test still passes. ❌ is an error: check the identifier and the settings. When History answers, ⚠️ included, a note recalls that the test reads only the last few days: a new asset gets its whole price history when it is created.

⚠️ Paused for too many requests until … means the provider has refused LibreFolio's requests because there were too many: LibreFolio leaves it alone until the time shown, in your local time, with the date when the pause ends another day. Your settings may well be right, so the test still passes. When the end of the pause is not known, you see Too many requests: try again later. Meanwhile, the Assets list and the asset page keep showing the last saved price.

An asset has at most one provider; tick No Provider if you will enter its prices yourself. See Providers for what each one offers.

docs.title: ⚖️ Check the provider's data
docs.text:
LibreFolio compares the provider's details with your form after you pick a Search Online result, and when you click Ask Provider: at the top of Asset Details for everything, next to Identifiers or in a distribution editor for that part only. It needs a provider and an identifier.

  • Empty fields are filled in, and the provider's extra codes join Other identifiers.
  • Provider has no data for: … names a missing sector or geographic breakdown; All data matches provider means there is nothing to review.
  • Anything that differs opens the Provider Data Comparison dialog.

Each row of the dialog shows your Current Value next to the Provider Value, and starts ticked:

  1. Untick the rows where you want to keep your value (Select All and Deselect All help).
  2. On an identifier row, choose the main code; the other is kept under Other identifiers (see Edit identifiers). The provider's code is proposed, as it is normally the quoted one.
  3. Click Apply Selected, which counts the rows you take (for example Apply Selected (2/3)), or Cancel to change nothing.

The accepted values only fill in the form: they are stored when you save the asset.

  • Your refined type is kept. Borsa Italiana, for example, reports every ETFplus instrument as plain ETF: if you chose Equity ETF, that counts as agreeing and no row appears (the same goes for Crowdfunding). A type more specific than yours is still offered.
  • Each question is asked once. When a search result brings a different ISIN (or other code) from the one in the form, LibreFolio first asks which is the main one, and the comparison does not ask again.
  • Units per single price is proposed, never filled in. A check of everything (after a search pick, or with Ask Provider at the top of Asset Details) compares it with the provider's suggestion or, without one, with 100 for a bond and 1 for any other type (the type the provider proposes, if it proposes another). A difference is a ticked row under Asset Details, with a note giving the reason: the provider's suggestion, or that bonds are usually quoted per 100 (a row proposing the usual 1 has none). Untick it to keep your value. If a check comes back without the provider's suggestion (it took too long, for example), the one it gave earlier for the same provider and identifier, in the search result or an earlier check, still counts: LibreFolio does not propose to undo it.

docs.title: 🛠️ Edit an asset
docs.text: On the asset's detail page, click Edit (✏️), change what you need in the Edit Asset form, and click Save Changes.

docs.title: 💱 Changing the currency
docs.text:
A new Currency is always allowed, but prices and events are stored in the currency they were quoted in, so the old ones cannot stay next to the new ones. Changing the currency deletes some of what is stored for the asset, and keeps the rest:

Stored for the asset After the change Its price history Deleted Its dividends, interest and other events, the ones you entered and the ones the provider generated Deleted Your transactions Always kept. The ones linked to a deleted event stay, but lose that link Its splits Kept, and so are the transactions linked to them: the adjustments of a split keep their link and their cost

Splits are a ratio, not an amount of money, so they mean the same in any currency.

Before anything is saved, the form asks the server what would go. If the answer cannot be read, the form shows the error and saves nothing. If nothing would go (the asset has no prices, events or linked transactions yet), the change is simply saved. If something would, one Change asset currency dialog lists it:

  • the price points that will be deleted, with the period they cover;
  • the manual events and the events generated by the provider that will be deleted;
  • the transactions that lose their link to a deleted event (the transactions themselves are kept);
  • the split events that stay, with the transactions linked to them.

Nothing is deleted until you click Delete & change currency; Cancel leaves the asset as it was. The dialog also lets you download a backup of the prices and of the events (CSV or JSON) first, when there are some.

After the change, if the asset has a provider and it had prices, they are downloaded again from the provider, from the oldest date you had, in the new currency. Without a provider, you import the prices again yourself. The transactions that lost the link to an event can be linked again in one go: see Relink events.

Changing or removing the provider has its own rules, below.

docs.title: 🔄 Changing or removing the provider
docs.text:
Some changes of provider throw away data LibreFolio had stored. Before saving, the form asks the server what would go, and if something would, it shows one confirmation that gives the numbers. Nothing is deleted until you confirm; Cancel leaves the asset as it was.

What you change What is deleted New settings for a Scheduled Investment plan All the asset's prices, and the events the plan generated: they are generated again from the new settings Another provider, when the asset was on a Scheduled Investment plan The same: all the prices and the events the plan generated; the new provider then supplies the history No Provider The events the provider generated (its dividends, splits or coupons). The prices you already have are kept Another online provider, or new settings for an online one (Yahoo Finance, justETF…); a first provider for an asset that had none Nothing, and no question is asked

For example, switching from a plan to Yahoo Finance asks:

The history of this asset was generated by Scheduled Investment. Switching to Yahoo Finance deletes 1,240 price points and 6 events generated by the provider. 3 transactions lose their link to a deleted event (the transactions themselves are kept). […] Manual events are kept. This cannot be undone. Continue?

What the dialog means:

  • Price points and events are counted as stored right now. The prices include any you entered yourself, when a plan's settings or provider change; with No Provider they stay.
  • Transactions are never deleted. A transaction you recorded against a deleted event, such as a dividend or a coupon, stays in your portfolio but loses its link: its Linked Event field is empty. The dialog counts all such transactions, including any on brokers you cannot see, and does not name them.
  • Events you added yourself stay, with their links.
  • If nothing would be lost, or the count could not be obtained, the form saves without a dialog.

⚠️ One case is refused. If a split the provider generated has linked adjustments without a purchase cost, the change or removal is not made: with the split gone, those units would count as bought at an unknown price. The form shows the message instead of the dialog, names the split by its date, and the rest of your edit is saved. Give those adjustments a purchase cost, then change the provider again.

docs.title: 🏷️ Edit identifiers
docs.text:
One security can have several codes. LibreFolio keeps one asset with all of them, under More Info in the asset form:

  • Identifiers: the main codes, one per type (ISIN, ticker…). Add identifier adds a row and Ask Provider fetches them.
  • Other identifiers: any extra code or broker label. Type one and press Enter, comma, semicolon or Tab. These codes are searchable and help recognise the asset on later imports.

Keep the quoted code as the main ISIN

A price is the value of the last trade, so only a tradeable code has a price. Put that code in ISIN and everything else in Other identifiers, or no provider can price the asset.

docs.title: 🏛️ Italian retail government bonds (BTP Valore, BTP Più, BTP Italia)
docs.text:
These bonds are subscribed under one ISIN and traded under another:

Phase Code What it does Subscription at issue the "CUM" ISIN Entitles you to the loyalty premium if you hold to maturity. Not tradeable, so no provider quotes it Secondary market a different ISIN Freely traded and quoted: this is the one with a price

To sell before maturity, the bond is converted to the market code. Keep both codes on one asset:

  1. Put the market ISIN in ISIN.
  2. Put the CUM ISIN in Other identifiers.
  3. Record the loyalty premium, when it is paid, as an Interest transaction on that asset. This works after maturity too: a deactivated asset stays selectable.

When an import brings the CUM code for an asset that holds the market one, LibreFolio asks which code should lead and keeps the other under Other identifiers.

docs.title: 🗺️ Set sector and country distributions
docs.text:
Providers fill in the sector and geographic breakdowns when they can; for other assets, set them yourself. They feed the dashboard's allocation charts and the AI Export.

In the asset form, expand More Info: under Classification, Sector Distribution and Geographic Distribution list one row per sector or country, with its weight in percent.

  • Add sector / Add country adds a row: pick the entry, then type its weight.
  • The Total turns green at 100%, amber when something is missing, red when you go over.
  • Balance to 100%, a row action, moves the whole gap into that row. Balance selected rows shares it among the selected rows, in proportion to their weights.
  • Remove deletes a row, Ask Provider fetches the provider's breakdown, and Import CSV loads one from a file.

docs.title: 📥 Import a distribution from CSV
docs.text:
Import CSV expects a name,weight header, then one row per country or sector, with weights in percent:

name,weight
USA,60
Italy,40
  • Names must match exactly, ignoring letter case and surrounding spaces. Countries: an ISO code (IT, ITA) or the name in your language. Sectors: the sector key (such as Government Bonds) or the name in your language.
  • Weights go from 0 to 100 and must total 100 (within 0.005 points); each name appears once.
  • The import is all-or-nothing: one bad row blocks it. When it succeeds, it replaces the whole distribution.

Decimal commas

The separator, , or ;, is read from the header. With ,, the row Italy,12,5 is silently read as 12. Use ; throughout (name;weight, then Italy;12,5), quote the value (Italy,"12,5"), or write Italy,12.5.

docs.title: 🧲 Merge duplicate assets
docs.text:
If the same instrument ended up as two assets, each holds part of its history. To fold one into the other:

  1. On the Assets page, use Merge with… on the asset that should disappear: the button on its card, or the right-click menu in the table.
  2. Choose the asset to keep (inactive ones too) and click Continue. On a day both have a price, the kept asset's price wins; so does its price provider, if it has one.
  3. Read What moves: the exact counts of transactions, prices and events. Where both assets have a different code of the same type, choose the one that leads.
  4. Click Merge and delete. The first asset is deleted; this cannot be undone.

No identifier is lost: each code of the deleted asset fills an empty field of the kept one or joins its Other identifiers. Identical events are merged.

During an import, when two of your assets carry a security's ISIN, its Resolve Assets card says Two stored assets match this security and offers Merge. Matching names alone never trigger it.

docs.title: 💼 Assets
docs.text: Assets are the instruments you hold or follow: stocks, ETFs, bonds, crypto, or a savings account with scheduled interest. The Assets page lists them all, each with a small price chart, and opens the detail page of any of them.

docs.title: 📌 What is an asset?
docs.text:
Each asset has:

  • a name and identifiers — ISIN, ticker or other codes;
  • a type — stock, ETF, bond, crypto, commodity… (asset types);
  • a currency — the one its prices are quoted in;
  • a price provider, optional — it downloads the current price and the history for you (Providers);
  • a sector and country breakdown, optional;
  • events — dividends, splits, interest… (Asset events).

Assets are shared by everyone on this LibreFolio: your transactions decide which ones are yours.

docs.title: 📋 Browse the list
docs.text:
Open Assets in the sidebar, then:

  • Pick a layout — the two buttons next to Add Asset switch between cards with a small chart (Grid view) and a sortable table (Table view). Your choice is remembered in this browser.
  • Pick the period — the date range sets the period of the card charts and of the change they show. When a card's chart groups the days into weeks or months because the plot is too narrow for so many days, a small Weekly or Monthly badge at its top left says so, like on the detail page's chart. In the table, the Δ columns give the change over one day and over each period, from 1W to 5Y, that fits in the range.
  • Filter — type in Search assets... to filter by name, and pick one or more currencies and types in the two menus; the ✕ clears the search and both menus.
  • Show archived assets — the list starts with Active assets only: switch on Inactive to add the archived ones, or switch off Active to see only those.

Click a card or a row to open the asset's detail page. There, the ‹ › arrows step through the assets in the order this list shows them, filters and sort included.

📉 Abs, % or Rolling Return on the cards — grid view only

The switch in the toolbar has three options: the chart-line icon, the same as on the cards, for the absolute prices (its tooltip says Show absolute), % (the change over the period) and the calendar icon for Rolling Return. Your choice applies to every card, its chart and its change, and it is remembered in this browser, for your user, with the chart settings.

The view button on a card goes to the next view, % → Rolling Return → Abs → %, and shows the view it will go to. A card keeps its own choice, even after you reload, until you change the toolbar again: that resets every card to the toolbar's view.

In Rolling Return, a card draws the asset's rolling return, the same calendar-window return as the Rolling Return mode of the asset detail page, and over it the rolling returns of the asset comparisons saved on that card. The other indicators stay saved, only hidden in this view. The price and the change at the top of the card do not change. If the asset has less history than the window, the card shows a short message instead of the chart.

The window is chosen in Chart Settings: 1W, 1M, 3M, 1Y or a custom one. Until you choose one, it is automatic: the largest preset that fits the period shown in the list, so a 3-month range uses 3M and a range of one year or more uses 1Y.

The asset's detail page opens in the view of its card, and with the card's Rolling Return window. A view chosen there becomes the card's.

⚙️ The look of the card charts

Settings in the toolbar sets the look and the overlays of every asset chart at once, and applying it replaces each asset's own settings, detail pages included. The ⚙️ on a card changes that card only. See Chart Settings.

docs.title: 🗂️ Your assets, other users' assets, watched
docs.text:
Both layouts split the list into up to three panels, each with its count; an empty panel is not shown.

Panel What it holds Your assets Assets held now in a broker you own Other users' assets Assets held now only by other users — in brokers you do not own Watched Assets held by no one now — never bought or already sold, kept on the radar

What counts is the position today: when you sell your whole position, the asset moves to Other users' assets if someone else still holds it, and to Watched otherwise. Brokers shared with you as Editor or Viewer count as other users' brokers, and a position closed down to a negligible leftover counts as not held.

In the table view each panel is a table with its own pages; resizing, moving or hiding a column applies to all three.

docs.title: 🔄 Keep prices up to date
docs.text:
• Sync All opens a window where Start Sync downloads the latest prices of every asset that has a provider; Reload All reloads the list from what LibreFolio has stored. Hover over Settings, Sync All or Reload All for half a second to read what the button does. When the period already holds stored prices for some of the assets, the window says so before you start: the sync replaces them with the provider's values, your manual edits included. On the Correlation tab they become Sync selection, which also downloads the exchange rates that convert the selected assets, and Reload All, which recomputes every analysis.
  • Live prices — while the date range ends today, prices refresh by themselves: every minute on this page, every 30 seconds on an asset's page. A price turns green when it went up since the previous refresh, red when it went down; when the market is closed you see the last close, uncoloured. To spare the server and the price providers, refreshing pauses while the browser tab is in the background, and after two minutes without using the page: then a small Updates paused label shows at the top of the page. There is nothing to click: as soon as you come back to the tab, move the mouse or press a key, prices refresh again on their own.
  • In the background, the server refreshes prices on a schedule your administrator sets (Market Data Scheduler). The Dashboard shows the stored prices.

docs.title: 🖱️ Act on one asset
docs.text:
Each card has its own buttons; in the table, the ⋮ at the end of a row, or a right-click, opens the same actions:

  • Sync — downloads the asset's prices for the selected period. It needs a provider, and the table also blocks it for an archived asset.
  • Reload — reloads its prices from what LibreFolio has stored.
  • Merge with… — folds a duplicate into another asset, which keeps everything (Create & Edit).
  • Delete — removes an asset that no transaction uses, with its provider, prices and events (dividends, splits…).

In the table, tick several rows to Sync, Reload or Delete them together.

🗑️ When an asset cannot be deleted

An asset is not deleted while any transaction uses it, even one in a broker you cannot see. The result shows how many transactions use it, with a Transactions link filtered to that asset. That page shows only the brokers you can access, so it may list fewer transactions than the count.

When the list already counts transactions for the asset, its confirmation opens straight on that result, with no Delete button: there is nothing to confirm. Otherwise the result appears after you confirm, and LibreFolio still checks before deleting.

docs.text: Create an asset, connect it to a price provider and keep its details right.

docs.title: 🧪 Correlation Tab
docs.text: Compare a selection of assets side by side — correlation matrix, losses, risk against return, and historical replay, in percentages only.

docs.title: 📊 Asset Detail Page
docs.text: The price chart with its signals, measures and events, the data editor, and the classification.

docs.title: 🔌 Providers
docs.text: Automatic prices from Yahoo Finance, justETF, Borsa Italiana, the CSS Scraper, or the Scheduled Investment engine.

docs.title: 📈 Interactive Chart
docs.text:
The chart is the heart of the asset page: the price history, or how much the price moved over a rolling window. Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, and hover a point for its values.

Last updated: 2026-10-22

docs.title: 🔀 Prices or Rolling Return
docs.text:
The two buttons above the chart choose what it draws:

  • Prices — the price history, with the asset's events as markers.
  • Rolling Return — for every date, the price change over a window you choose (below).

The page opens in the view this asset's card has on the Assets page: Abs or % open Prices in that view, Rolling Return opens Rolling Return. Change the mode here, or Abs and % under Prices, and that becomes the asset's view: its card and your next visit open in it. It is remembered in this browser, for your user, with the chart settings; the list's switch resets every card, and so every detail page, to its view.

docs.title: 🗓️ Rolling Return Window
docs.text:
This view answers how much has the price moved over the window, at every date? Each point compares that day's close with the close exactly \(N\) calendar days earlier:

\[ R(d) = \frac{P(d)}{P(d-N)} - 1 \]

where \(P\) is the last close known on that day, in the chart's currency → Rolling return over calendar days.

Pick \(N\) with the Window control next to the two buttons:

  • 1W, 1M, 3M, 1Y — 7, 30, 90 and 365 days.
  • Custom — a whole number with W, M or Y, counted as 7, 30 and 365 days: 3M is 90 days.
  • ? opens this section of the manual.

The window may be longer than the dates on screen: LibreFolio reads the older prices it needs. It is the same as on the asset's card: the one chosen for this asset or, until you choose one, an automatic one, the largest preset that fits the dates on screen (about 3 months use 3M, a year or more 1Y, under a week 1W). A window you pick here is kept for this asset, in this browser.

How to read it:

  • Above zero, the price is higher than \(N\) days before; below zero, lower.
  • Hover a point: ↩ gives the date it is compared with; 📅 and 💱 give the dates of the price and of the exchange rates actually used, when one of them is older.
  • Asset comparisons turn into rolling returns too, with the same window and currency.
  • Price only: dividends, interest and your transactions are not included.
🧩 Gaps and short lines — when the history is incomplete

A point stays empty, never estimated, when either of its two prices is missing or not positive. Each line starts on the first date it can be computed, so a recent asset or a missing exchange rate shortens only its own line, and a later missing price leaves a gap. When only part of the range can be computed, a note under the chart says so; when nothing can, a message replaces the chart.

docs.title: 📅 Date range
docs.text:
The date range in the page toolbar sets the dates on screen: 1W, 1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y, 2Y, YTD, All, or Custom, a number of days, weeks, months or years back from today; click a date to pick the two ends on a calendar. The two ends must be different days: the day you click first cannot be clicked again, and a typed date equal to the other end turns red. With spare room on the bar, more presets appear (3Y, 5Y, 10Y, WTD, MTD, QTD). The range you pick follows you to the Dashboard, broker, asset and FX pages of the same browser tab.

On a long range the chart may group the days into weeks or months to stay readable: a Weekly or Monthly badge at its top left says so.

docs.title: 💱 Convert to another currency
docs.text:
Convert to, next to the price, shows the chart in another currency, with a dashed 💱 line for the price in the asset's own currency. The menu lists the currencies your FX pairs can reach; Create forex… at its bottom adds a missing pair. Rolling returns are computed in the chosen currency too.

💱 When an exchange rate is missing

A banner above the chart names the pair, with a shortcut to create it or to open it. The page's Sync downloads the rates of the pairs that exist; it never creates one.

docs.title: 📊 Line or candles, Abs or %
docs.text:
In Prices mode, the buttons at the top left of the chart switch:

  • between a line and candlesticks, which need the open, high and low prices;
  • between Abs, the prices, and %, the change since the first day of the range.

docs.title: 🧰 Tools on the chart
docs.text:
The three buttons at the top right of the chart:

  • 📏 Add measurement — compare two points: see Measures. Prices and Rolling Return keep separate measures.
  • ✏️ Edit Prices & Events — opens the Data Editor, in Prices mode only.
  • ⚙️ Aesthetics — Area Fill, Baseline Colors (green above the starting value, or above zero in %, red below), Grid Lines, Stale Gradient (fades the points whose price or exchange rate is carried over from an earlier day) and Y-Axis Scale (Auto, Include 0 or Custom limits). Candlesticks turn off Area Fill, Baseline Colors and Stale Gradient.

These settings and your signals are remembered for this asset, in this browser. To change them for every asset at once, use Settings on the Assets page: see Chart Settings.

docs.title: 🗂️ Classification
docs.text: The Classification panel shows the asset's sector and geographic distribution, when this data has been configured for the asset (manually or fetched from a provider).

docs.title: 📊 Sector Distribution
docs.text: A pie chart showing the breakdown by industry sector (e.g., Technology 35%, Healthcare 20%, Finance 15%...). This is especially useful for ETFs and diversified funds to understand the underlying sector allocation.

docs.title: World Map
docs.text: An interactive world map with countries colored by allocation weight. Hover over a country to see its percentage.

docs.title: Country Breakdown
docs.text: A pie chart showing the percentage breakdown by country or region (e.g., United States 60%, Europe 25%, Asia 15%...).

docs.title: 🛠️ How to Use
docs.text:
1. Click the Classification toggle button in the toolbar area
  2. The panel expands below the chart showing sector and geographic data
  3. Hover over pie chart slices or map regions for details

docs.title: ⚙️ Configuring Classification
docs.text:
Classification data can be set in two ways:

  1. Provider metadata: Some providers (Yahoo Finance, justETF) fetch sector and geographic data automatically during sync
  2. Manual entry: Edit the asset (✏️) and fill in the sector/geographic distributions using the Distribution Editor

docs.title: 🔗 Related
docs.text:

  • 🔌 Providers — Providers that fetch classification metadata

docs.title: ✏️ Data Editor
docs.text: The Data Editor lets you fix and complete an asset's data by hand: its daily prices and its events, such as dividends. Use it to correct a wrong price from a provider, add the history of an asset without one, fill a gap, or record an event the provider missed.

docs.title: 🛠️ Edit prices and events
docs.text:
1. In Prices mode, click ✏️ Edit Prices & Events at the top right of the chart. The editor opens below the chart, with a Prices and an Events tab.
  2. Change what you need:
    • Add Row adds a row on a free date: change the date if needed, then fill in the values.
    • Click a cell to edit it.
    • Delete, in a row's ⋮ menu, marks the row for deletion, and Undo brings it back. Tick several rows to delete them together.
    • Import CSV loads many rows at once (below).
  3. Click Save (n), where n counts your changes, or Cancel to drop them. Both close the editor and bring the other panels back; so does ✕, without saving.

Until you save, new and changed prices show on the chart as a purple line. A price saved outside the dates on screen widens them to include it.

docs.title: 💰 Prices tab
docs.text:
• Close is required and must be above 0; Open, High, Low and Volume are optional, 0 or more, and the eraser in a cell clears its value. LibreFolio keeps no negative price: a row with one, which only an imported file can bring, is not saved and counts as skipped.
  • Prices are in the asset's currency, shown beside the tabs (Prices in USD).
  • Stale rows are days without a price of their own, filled with the last known one. When there are some, a ⚠️ count and a switch appear: turn it on to hide them.
  • A price the server refuses is named. If it refuses some of your prices, such as a close above the row's High or below its Low, it saves the others. A warning then names up to five refused dates, each with its reason, and counts the rest; it stays for 20 seconds, so you can note them and enter them again. If it refuses the whole save, for example because a date is after tomorrow, nothing is saved: the message says why, and the editor stays open with your changes.

docs.title: 📅 Events tab
docs.text:
Each row has a Type (Dividend, Interest, Split, Price Adjustment or Maturity), an Amount in the asset's currency (per share for a dividend, the ratio for a split) and optional Notes. See Asset Events for what each type does.

  • Events from a provider are read-only: an edit would be overwritten at its next sync. You can delete one, but the provider adds it back at its next sync; to remove it for good, change the asset's provider settings.
  • Editing one of your events changes that event, its Type included: no second event is added. A transaction linked to it stays linked and is read according to the new type: an Adjustment linked to a split, for example, no longer counts as a split once the event is a Price Adjustment.
  • Your event changes are saved all together, or not at all. Deletions, edits and new rows go in one step, deletions first. If anything is refused, no event change is stored, deletions included: Failed to save: … tells you why, in your language, and your changes stay in the editor for you to fix. Price changes from the same save are stored all the same, since prices are saved first.

A save is refused, with a message that names the event at fault, when:

  • an event is in another currency than the asset's: this comes from a CSV line, which keeps the currency it was written in (below);
  • an event's new Type is the one another of your events has on that date: swapping the types of two events in one save works, and so does deleting that other event in the same save;
  • you delete an event a transaction is linked to: the message names the event and how many transactions use it. Remove the link from those transactions first. Before LibreFolio 1.3, the rest of the save went through and that deletion was skipped with a warning;
  • you change the Type of a split whose linked adjustments have no purchase cost: without the split, those units would count as bought at an unknown price. The message counts those adjustments, including any at a broker you cannot see; give them a purchase cost first, then change the Type;
  • a Type is not one of the five: this too comes from a CSV line.

docs.title: 📥 Import from CSV
docs.text:
Import CSV opens a window where you drop a file or paste its text, and each row is checked before you import it. The first line must name the columns, in any order.

PricesEvents 
date;currency;close;open;high;low;volume
2024-01-15;USD;145.50;144.00;146.20;143.80;1500000
2024-01-16;USD;146.10;;;;

date, currency and close are required: write the asset's currency.

date;currency;type;amount;notes
2024-03-15;USD;DIVIDEND;1.25;Q1 payout
2024-06-01;;SPLIT;2;2:1 split

date, type and amount are required. type is one of DIVIDEND, INTEREST, SPLIT, PRICE_ADJUSTMENT and MATURITY_SETTLEMENT: any other value is refused when you save.

value is accepted in place of amount, so an events file exported by LibreFolio (the backup offered when you change an asset's currency) imports back, its other columns ignored. Mind two limits:

  • One event per date and type: rows sharing both a date and a type are all left out as duplicates; a dividend and a split on the same day import together.
  • Rows marked PROVIDER: when the asset has a provider, they are left out and the editor tells you how many; sync the asset to load them. When the asset has no provider, they are added as your own events.

In that file, a note that starts with =, +, - or @ has an apostrophe in front of it, so that a spreadsheet shows it as text instead of running it as a formula: the import removes that apostrophe, and the note comes back as it was.

  • Dates are YYYY-MM-DD, and decimals can use . or ,.
  • Columns are separated by ; or ,; with ,, write decimals with ..
  • Other columns are ignored, so a price file exported by LibreFolio imports as it is.
  • The currency column is never converted. On a price line it is not checked either: the price is stored in the asset's currency as it is. An event line keeps its currency, and one in another currency than the asset's is refused when you save; an empty one takes the asset's. So before importing a backup taken before a currency change, convert its amounts and write the asset's new currency.
  • A price line updates the price of its date; an event line updates your event with the same date and type. A line that matches only a provider's event is left out, since an import never changes those; the others are added. Nothing is stored until you click Save.

docs.title: 🖱️ Jump from the chart
docs.text: With the editor open, double-click a point of the chart (or long-press it on a phone) to jump to that date: to the Events tab when the date has an event, to Prices otherwise.

docs.title: 📅 Asset Events
docs.text: Asset events are things that happen to the asset itself, for everyone who holds it: a dividend, a split, an interest payment. They are not your transactions, which record what happens in your portfolio.

docs.title: 📊 Event types
docs.text:
Each type, with what it does to the price and its theory page:

  • 💰 Dividend (DIVIDEND) — cash paid out by a stock or an ETF; the price drops by about that amount on the ex-date → 📖
  • 📈 Interest (INTEREST) — interest paid by a bond, a loan or a deposit; the value drops by the amount paid → 📖
  • ✂️ Split (SPLIT) — the units are split; their number changes, not the total value → 📖
  • 📊 Price Adjustment (PRICE_ADJUSTMENT) — a value change without cash, up or down: a write-down, a haircut, a re-rating → 📖
  • 🏁 Maturity Settlement (MATURITY_SETTLEMENT) — the asset reaches maturity and pays back its capital; its value stops changing → 📖

The codes in brackets are the ones a CSV import expects.

docs.title: 📈 Events on the chart
docs.text:
In Prices mode, events appear as markers on the price chart, each type with its own shape: a triangle for a dividend, a diamond for interest, a square for a price adjustment, a rounded square for maturity, an arrow for a split. Hover a marker for its date, type, amount and notes.

  • In another currency, the amount is converted, with the original amount below it; an event that cannot be converted is hidden.
  • Compared assets show their events too, in the colour of their line.

docs.title: ⚙️ Where events come from
docs.text:
• From a provider, at each sync: dividends and splits from Yahoo Finance, dividends from justETF, and from Scheduled Investment the interest payouts and final maturity settlement of Generate Coupon, plus the events listed in its schedule (Add Event in the asset form).
  • From you: in the Events tab of the Data Editor, one by one or from a CSV file, or with + New event in the Linked Event field of a transaction (below).

A sync refreshes the provider's events and never touches yours. A provider's event is read-only in the editor, and deleting it lasts only until the provider sends it again: to change a Scheduled Investment's events, edit its schedule. Removing the provider (No Provider in the asset form) deletes its events, and is refused while a transaction is linked to one of them.

docs.title: ✨ New event from a transaction
docs.text:
+ New event, in the Linked Event field of a dividend, an interest or an adjustment, creates an event for the transaction's asset and links it to the transaction. It never overwrites an event: if the asset already has one of that type on that date, entered by hand or from a data provider, nothing is saved and the window shows what is there under This event already exists. For each event: its type, date, amount and notes, where it comes from and how many transactions are linked to it. Then choose:

  • Use this — links that event to the transaction, and changes nothing else.
  • Edit this — only for an event entered by hand: the window becomes Edit event for …, filled with that event's values. Change what you need and click Save: that same event is updated, for the transactions already linked to it too, and this transaction is linked to it.
  • Cancel — back to the form, with what you typed (the Cancel at the bottom closes the window).

An event from a data provider offers only Use this, with a note: the provider updates its own events. There is no way to add a second event of the same type on the same date from here. In the Data Editor, instead, a new row or a CSV line on the date and type of one of your events updates that event.

After Edit this, the Linked Event field shows the event with its new values.

docs.title: 🧮 Events in a Scheduled Investment
docs.text:
For a Scheduled Investment, events are part of the price itself:

\[ P(d) = V_0 + I(d) - \sum \text{Interest} + \sum \text{Price adjustments} \]

with \(V_0\) the initial value and \(I(d)\) the interest accrued so far. For a market-priced asset, events only explain moves in the price, such as the drop on an ex-dividend date; they do not change the prices the provider sends.

docs.title: 🔍 Asset Detail Page
docs.text:
Click an asset on the Assets page to open its own page: its price history, the tools to analyse it, and the data behind it.

The page has two tabs: Overview, described below, and Risk & Scenarios.

Beta

The Risk & Scenarios tab is still in beta: it opens with the notice Risk Analysis is in beta. and is not covered by this documentation yet.

docs.title: 🧭 What the Overview shows
docs.text: From top to bottom:

docs.title: 📊 Signals
docs.text: Draw any of the 22 technical indicators, another asset or currency pair, or a reference curve over the chart.

docs.title: 📈 Interactive Chart
docs.text: The price history, or the Rolling Return over a window you choose (1W, 1M, 3M, 1Y or a custom length). Zoom, pan, and convert it to another currency.

docs.title: ✏️ Data Editor
docs.text: Add, fix or delete prices and events, one by one or from a CSV file.

docs.title: 📐 Measures
docs.text: Click two points of the chart to read the change between them.

docs.title: 🗂️ Classification
docs.text: The sector and country breakdown, in the Metadata & Classification panel.

docs.title: 📅 Events
docs.text: Dividends, splits, interest and other asset events, drawn as markers on the chart.

docs.title: 🔧 Header and toolbar
docs.text:
• ← goes back to the list, or to the page you came from, in one step, even after browsing with the arrows.
  • The asset — a dot (green active, red archived), its name, type and currency, a Transactions (N) link when it has any, its provider (or ✏️ Manual), and a link to its web page: the one you set on the asset, or else the provider's.
  • ‹ n/N › — the previous or next asset, keeping the same dates (see the panel below).
  • Date range and Convert to — the period and the currency of the chart.
  • AI Export — copies the asset's data for an AI assistant (Asset AI Export).
  • Edit (✏️) — opens the asset form (Create & Edit).
  • Sync (🔄) — downloads the latest prices, with those of the compared assets and the exchange rates the chart needs; it reads Recalculate for a Scheduled Investment. Not available for an asset without a provider or an archived one.
  • Reload (↻) — reloads the page's data from what LibreFolio has stored.
🧭 Which order the ‹ › arrows follow
  • Opened from the Assets page: the list as you left it — its search, filters, grid or table view and, in the table, its sort and column filters.
  • Opened any other way (a link or bookmark, a reload, the Dashboard, Transactions…), or for an asset that list does not show: every asset in the Assets page's default order, archived ones only when the asset you opened is archived.
  • The counter (for example 3/12) shows where you are. The arrows stop at both ends and disappear when there is only one asset to browse.

docs.title: 📐 Measures
docs.text: The Measure tool answers how much did it change between these two days? Pick two points on the chart and read the change of the asset, and of the lines drawn with it, between them.

docs.title: 🛠️ Take a measure
docs.text:
1. Click 📏 Add measurement at the top right of the chart: the Measures panel opens below it, and over the chart the pointer becomes a crosshair.
  2. Click the start point on the chart: a dashed line follows the pointer from it. Then click the end point, on another day.
  3. The new measure opens with its table, and the chart draws it in its own colour.

A measure needs two different days. Back over the start's day, the dashed line disappears and the pointer shows the not allowed sign (🚫): a second click there does nothing, and the start stays picked.

+ Add measurement in the panel's header measures the whole chart instead, from its first to its last point: handy on a phone. Each measure's header holds its colour and 🗑️ to remove it; expand the measure to change its dates, again two different days.

Measures are not saved: reloading the page empties the panel. Prices and Rolling Return keep separate measures.

docs.title: 💵 In Prices mode
docs.text:
The table has a row for the asset (a second one in its own currency when the chart is converted) and one for each line drawn on the price axis, such as a comparison asset or a moving average. Next to the Start and End values:

  • Δ Abs — the difference \(V_{end} - V_{start}\), in the line's unit.
  • Δ % — the change \(\frac{V_{end} - V_{start}}{V_{start}}\), or — when the line starts at 0 → Returns & Growth Rates
  • Δ%/yr — the same change as a yearly rate over the \(d\) calendar days between the points, \((1 + \Delta\%)^{365/d} - 1\), from 30 days on: — on a shorter span, without a Δ %, or when the line ends on the other side of zero → Returns & Growth Rates

The measure's summary line adds the number of days.

docs.title: 📈 In Rolling Return mode
docs.text:
The values are already returns, so the table compares them:

  • Start, End — the rolling return on each of the two dates.
  • Δ pp — End minus Start, in percentage points → Rolling return over calendar days
  • Days — the calendar days between the two points.

docs.title: 📊 Signals
docs.text: Signals are lines drawn over the price chart: technical indicators that LibreFolio computes from the stored prices, another asset or a currency pair to compare with, and reference curves such as a steady growth. Use them to read trend, momentum, volatility and risk at a glance.

docs.title: 🛠️ Add a signal
docs.text:
1. Open the Signals panel above the chart.
  2. Pick a signal from one of its three menus: Technical Indicators, Data Comparison or Synthetic Benchmarks. In the indicators menu, type to search by name, description or the data an indicator uses.
  3. Set its parameters on the card that appears; the chart follows.
  4. Drag a card by its handle (arrows on a phone) to change the order, or remove it with 🗑️.

Each line of a card, and each zone of indicators such as RSI, has its own colour and line style. Your signals are remembered for this asset, in this browser.

docs.title: 📉 Technical indicators
docs.text: 22 indicators, grouped by what they measure. Each name links to its theory page; the ? on a card opens the same page.

docs.title: 📈 Trend
docs.text:
• SMA — simple average of the closing prices
  • EMA — average that weighs recent prices more
  • KAMA — average that adapts to market noise
  • ADX — trend strength, with +DI and −DI for its direction
  • Aroon — how recent the latest highs and lows are

docs.title: ⚡ Momentum
docs.text:
• RSI — buying and selling pressure, with overbought and oversold zones
  • MACD — momentum between two moving averages, with a signal line and a histogram
  • PPO — the same momentum, in percent
  • ROC — speed of the price change
  • Stochastic RSI — where RSI sits within its recent range
  • CCI — distance from the average price

docs.title: 🌊 Volatility
docs.text:
• Bollinger Bands — a band around a moving average that widens with volatility
  • ATR — volatility in price units
  • NATR — volatility in percent of the price
  • Donchian Channels — the highest high and the lowest low of the period

docs.title: 📊 Volume
docs.text:
• OBV — pressure of the volume behind price moves
  • MFI — volume-weighted momentum

docs.title: ⚠️ Risk
docs.text:
• Underwater Drawdown — how far the price is below its running peak (full history)
  • Rolling Return — price-only return against the close a chosen number of calendar days earlier, the same measure as the chart's Rolling Return mode
  • Rolling Volatility — annualized volatility over a sliding window
  • Rolling Sharpe Ratio — excess return per unit of volatility over a sliding window
  • Rolling Beta — how strongly the asset follows a comparison asset you pick

Periods count sessions, the days the asset was quoted: an SMA 200 covers 200 sessions, about 290 calendar days (why). The Window of Rolling Volatility, Rolling Sharpe Ratio and Rolling Beta counts observations: one return for each day the asset was quoted — for Rolling Beta, for each day either of the two assets was quoted, the other counting at its last price. The Window of Rolling Return counts calendar days, as in the chart's Rolling Return mode.

Not every indicator can run on every asset

ADX, Aroon, ATR, NATR, CCI, Donchian Channels and MFI need high and low prices; OBV and MFI need the volume. Without them, the card tells you which data is missing.

docs.title: 📉 Drawdown over the full history
docs.text: The Underwater Drawdown card has a Full history checkbox, on by default: the drop is measured from the highest price of the asset's whole history, even years before the dates on screen. Untick it for a quicker view, measured from the highest price within the dates on screen.

docs.title: 💱 Compare with an asset or a currency pair
docs.text:
The Data Comparison menu adds:

  • Asset Comparison — another asset on the same chart, such as a stock against its index ETF. In % view both lines start at 0 %. The asset is picked in the same panel as the risk comparison's: a search box, Type and Currency filters, the benchmarks listed first, one click to choose. The chart's own asset is greyed out; one that another comparison already uses carries a warning mark but can still be chosen.
  • FX Pair — the rate of one of your currency pairs.

With All selected, the chart starts on the older of the two series. If the compared asset has prices from 1985 and the chart's own asset from 2010, the chart is drawn from 1985, the chart's own line empty until 2010, and the From date shows 1985. In % view each line starts at 0 % on its own first price. If the compared asset starts later than the chart's own, the chart stays as it was and the comparison line begins on its own first day. The other signals (indicators and synthetic benchmarks) follow the chart's own days, so they are empty before its first day.

Sync (🔄) on an Asset Comparison card downloads that asset's prices for the chart's dates, together with the exchange rates that convert it, for pairs that exist. When the pair is missing, an amber ⚠️ on the card creates it; when its rates are missing, an amber 🔄 syncs them.

In Rolling Return mode only Asset Comparison stays: each compared asset becomes a rolling return, with the same window and currency. The other signals are hidden, not deleted, and come back in Prices mode.

docs.title: 📐 Synthetic benchmarks
docs.text:
Reference curves drawn from their parameters alone, with no market data:

  • Linear Growth — \(y(t) = y_0\,(1 + r\,t)\)
  • Compound Growth — \(y(t) = y_0\,(1 + r)^t\)
  • Sine Wave — \(y(t) = A \sin(2\pi t / T) + y_0\)

docs.title: 🩺 Read a signal card
docs.text:
• A spinner turns while the signal is computed.
  • 📈 N is the number of price points loaded.
  • A grey ℹ — computed, with a small caveat: a short gap or a nearly complete warm-up. Hover the icon for the details.
  • An amber ⚠ — computed, with a caveat worth a look: larger gaps, an incomplete warm-up, or data that starts after the first date on screen. The card turns amber too.
  • A red ⚠ — not computed: a missing price field, too little history for the parameters, no data at all, or a calculation error. The card turns red.
🧩 Patchy price history — when a signal is partial

ADX, Aroon, ATR, NATR, CCI, Donchian Channels, MFI and OBV can run on a patchy history: they use the most recent stretch without gaps that is long enough, and the tooltip names that stretch and how many points were left out. The other indicators need a history without gaps, and explain why they cannot run rather than draw a misleading line. A weekend or a market holiday is not a gap.

docs.title: 🇮🇹 Borsa Italiana
docs.text: Borsa Italiana is the Milan stock exchange, run by Euronext. This provider reads prices, price history and instrument details from its public website — no account or API key needed.

docs.title: 🔍 What It Offers
docs.text:
• Current price: the last market price. For a mutual fund, its NAV — only when it is dated today.
  • History: daily open, high, low, close and volume. Mutual funds have no past series: each NAV is saved at its own date, so the history grows from the day you add the fund.
  • Search: by name or ISIN. Each instrument appears twice, 🇮🇹 and 🇬🇧 — or only in your preferred language: the flag sets the language of its name and description. Indices are left out, as you cannot buy them. No result? LibreFolio also looks for a matching Borsa Italiana page on the web, unless your administrator has turned this off.
  • Details: name, type, currency, a sector and a description (market, issuer, maturity, coupon); the ticker for stocks; for funds, the ISIN, the fund's features and its costs.

It covers what Borsa Italiana lists — Italian stocks, ETFs and ETCs (ETFplus), bonds (MOT, ExtraMOT, EuroTLX) and closed-end funds (MIV) — plus mutual funds and SICAVs.

docs.title: 💱 Currency and Type
docs.text:
• Currency is the one Borsa Italiana quotes the prices in: EUR for ETFs and ETCs on ETFplus, even when the fund itself is denominated in USD; USD for a bond traded in dollars on EuroTLX. If LibreFolio cannot read it, it leaves your currency as it is — check it before saving.
  • Type: ETFs, ETCs and ETNs all arrive as plain ETF. If you know what the fund holds, refine it (for example Equity ETF or Commodity ETF): a later check against the provider's data keeps your choice.
  • Bonds get the sector Government Bonds or Corporate Bonds (supranational issuers: Financials) and, when the issuer is recognised, its country — United States of America becomes USA.

docs.title: ✏️ Set It Up
docs.text:
Search Online fills in everything. To set the provider up by hand, open the asset with Edit (✏️) — or + Add Asset for a new one — and expand Provider Assignment:

  1. Choose Borsa Italiana as Provider.
  2. Type the instrument's ISIN, for example IT0003128367 (ENEL). Every instrument page on borsaitaliana.it shows it.
  3. Pick the Language: 🇬🇧 English or 🇮🇹 Italiano.
  4. Click Test Configuration, then save.

Search Online also fills in the other three settings; set them by hand only in these cases.

🧾 Fund internal code — for a mutual fund or SICAV

Mutual funds are priced by Borsa Italiana's own fund code, not by the ISIN. Find the fund on borsaitaliana.it and copy the code from its page address: in …/borsa/fondi/dettaglio/2FADB602822.html the code is 2FADB602822. Leave the field empty for anything else.

🧭 Market MIC and Platform — when the instrument page does not open

Some markets must be named explicitly. Open the instrument on borsaitaliana.it: the code after the ISIN in the page address is the Market MIC — in …/scheda/US912810TU25-ETLX.html it is ETLX. Platform is needed only on EuroTLX, where it is TLX.

Market Market MIC Platform MTA (Italian stocks) MTAA — MOT (bonds) MOTX — ExtraMOT (bonds) XMOT — ETFplus (ETFs, ETCs) ETFP — MIV (closed-end funds) MIVX — EuroTLX (bonds) ETLX TLX

For example, the US Treasury bond US912810TU25 on EuroTLX works once Market MIC is ETLX and Platform is TLX; its prices are in USD.

docs.title: 🌐 Your Preferred Language
docs.text:
Always pick the same language in search? Choose it once as Preferred language, under Borsa Italiana in Settings › Plugins, or with Configure next to the provider in the asset dialog. Your searches then show each instrument once, 🇮🇹 Italian or 🇬🇧 English. Both languages, the default, shows both, Italian first. The website is searched the same way whatever you choose.

It is a personal setting: it changes only your own searches, never a price or an asset you already have, and the Language of an asset you set up by hand stays yours to pick. See Plugin Settings.

docs.title: 🧾 Mutual Funds and NAV
docs.text:
A fund's NAV is published once a day, with a delay. LibreFolio saves each NAV at the date it refers to, never as today's price: until the next one arrives, the fund is valued at the latest known price — that NAV, or your own trade if it is more recent.

The fund code is kept under Other identifiers; the real ISIN stays the main identifier when the fund's page shows it.

docs.title: ⚠️ Limits
docs.text:
• LibreFolio spaces out its requests to the website, so syncing many Borsa Italiana assets can take a few minutes.
  • A market LibreFolio cannot read yet gives an error asking you to report the ISIN on GitHub.

docs.title: CSS Scraper
docs.text: The CSS Scraper reads an asset's price from any public web page, using a CSS selector that points at the number. Use it when no other provider covers the instrument. In the Provider list it is called CSS Web Scraper.

docs.title: 🔍 What It Offers
docs.text:
• ✅ Current price: read from the page at every sync, in the currency you choose.
  • ❌ History: none. Each sync saves the day's price, so the history grows from the day you start.
  • ❌ Search and details: none — you enter the page address and the settings yourself.

docs.title: 1️⃣ Copy the Price's CSS Selector
docs.text:
The selector tells LibreFolio which element of the page holds the price.

ChromeFirefox
  1. Open the page and right-click the price.
  2. Choose Inspect (or press F12): DevTools highlights the price element.
  3. Right-click the highlighted element, then Copy → Copy selector.
  1. Open the page and right-click the price.
  2. Choose Inspect (or press F12): the Inspector highlights the price element.
  3. Right-click the highlighted element, then Copy → CSS Selector.

docs.title: 2️⃣ Fill In the Provider Settings
docs.text:
In Provider Assignment, choose CSS Web Scraper and paste the page address into URL. The settings appear under their technical names:

Setting Required What to enter current_css_selector ✅ The selector you copied, e.g. .summary-value strong currency ✅ The currency of the price, e.g. EUR decimal_format — us for 1,234.56 (the default) or eu for 1.234,56 timeout — Seconds to wait for the page (default 30) user_agent — How LibreFolio introduces itself to the site (default LibreFolio/1.0)

docs.title: 3️⃣ Test It
docs.text:
Click Test Configuration: Current Price must show the number you see on the page. The ⚠️ on History is expected, as this provider has none.

A BTP on Borsa Italiana

  • URL: https://www.borsaitaliana.it/borsa/obbligazioni/mot/btp/scheda/IT0005634800.html?lang=en
  • current_css_selector: .summary-value strong
  • currency: EUR
  • decimal_format: us — the English page shows 100.39. The Italian page (lang=it) shows 100,39, so there use eu.

For instruments listed on Borsa Italiana, the Borsa Italiana provider also brings their history.

docs.title: 🛠️ Troubleshooting
docs.text: What you see What to do Price element not found The page layout may have changed: copy the selector again. Failed to parse price Check decimal_format. The element must hold just the number: spaces, €, $, £, ¥ and % are ignored, letters such as EUR are not. HTTP error or Request failed Check the URL; raise timeout for a slow site. Error 403 means the site refuses automated visits. Paused for too many requests until … The site refused because LibreFolio visited it too often: LibreFolio leaves it alone until then. Your other sites are not affected. A wrong number The selector matches another element (LibreFolio uses the first match): make it more specific.

docs.title: ⚠️ Limits
docs.text:
• LibreFolio reads the page as the site sends it, without running its scripts: a price filled in by JavaScript cannot be read, nor can pages behind a login.
  • When the site changes its layout, the selector may stop matching: test again and copy a new one.

docs.title: 🔌 Providers
docs.text:
A provider keeps an asset's prices up to date for you: today's price, its history and, for some, details such as the type or the sector. Each asset has at most one provider: pick a Search Online result to connect it, or set it up yourself in Provider Assignment — see Create & Edit.

Yahoo Finance Stocks, ETFs, funds and crypto from exchanges worldwide. justETF European ETFs comparison, prices, and asset structures. Borsa Italiana Italian stocks, bonds, ETFs and funds, in Italian or English. CSS Scraper Web page selector scraper for custom bond prices or exotics. Scheduled Investment Fixed-income assets calculating value via interest rate schedules. Request New Plugin Your price provider is missing? Request a new plugin or contribute code!

docs.title: 📊 Provider Comparison
docs.text:
Provider Current price History Search Details Identifier Best for Yahoo Finance ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Ticker (AAPL, VWCE.DE) or ISIN Stocks, ETFs, funds and crypto worldwide justETF ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ISIN (IE00B4L5Y983) European ETFs, priced in EUR, USD, CHF or GBP Borsa Italiana ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ISIN (IT0003128367) Instruments listed in Milan, Italian mutual funds CSS Scraper ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ Page URL A price shown on any public web page Scheduled Investment ✅ ✅ ❌ ❌ None — created for you Deposits, loans and bonds valued by their interest

Details are the type, currency, description and similar data that LibreFolio offers to fill in for you. Some providers also record asset events: dividends (Yahoo Finance, justETF), splits (Yahoo Finance), interest payouts and maturity (Scheduled Investment).

docs.title: 🎯 Choosing a Provider
docs.text:
• Stocks, ETFs or crypto on any exchange → Yahoo Finance.
  • A European ETF, or ETF prices in USD, CHF or GBP → justETF.
  • Stocks, bonds, ETFs or funds traded in Milan, and Italian mutual funds → Borsa Italiana.
  • A price that only a web page shows → CSS Scraper.
  • A savings account, term deposit, P2P loan or bond followed by its interest → Scheduled Investment.
  • Nothing fits? Tick No Provider and enter the prices yourself in the Data Editor.

docs.title: justETF
docs.text: justETF prices European ETFs by their ISIN, in euros, US dollars, Swiss francs or British pounds. It also brings each fund's description and its country and sector breakdowns.

docs.title: 🔍 What It Offers
docs.text:
• Current price: in EUR, the live price from the gettex exchange; when there is none — and always in USD, CHF and GBP — the latest daily price.
  • History: daily closing prices in the currency you choose.
  • Dividends: the distributions shown in the fund's chart become dividend events.
  • Search: by name, ticker, WKN or ISIN, among the ETFs listed on justETF.
  • Details: a description with the TER and the distribution policy, the country and sector breakdowns, the ISIN and the ticker.

docs.title: ✏️ Set It Up
docs.text:
Search Online sets it up for you. By hand, in Provider Assignment:

  1. Choose JustETF as Provider.
  2. Type the fund's ISIN, for example IE00B4L5Y983 (iShares Core MSCI World).
  3. In currency, pick EUR (the default), USD, CHF or GBP: every price of the asset is stored in that currency.

docs.title: 💱 Pick the Currency in Search
docs.text:
Each ETF appears four times in the results, once per currency: 🇪🇺 EUR, 🇺🇸 USD, 🇨🇭 CHF and 🇬🇧 GBP — unless you chose a preferred currency. 👑 marks the fund's own currency, the one its NAV is computed in — not necessarily the one you trade in. A line at the bottom of the results says so whenever a result shows 👑.

justETF converts the USD, CHF and GBP prices with its own exchange rates. Is your reporting currency another one? Pick any of the four: LibreFolio converts with its own exchange rates.

docs.title: ⭐ Your Preferred Currency
docs.text:
Always pick the same currency? Choose it once as Preferred currency, under JustETF in Settings › Plugins, or with Configure next to the provider in the asset dialog. Your searches then show each ETF once, in that currency, with 👑 only on the funds computed in it. All currencies, the default, shows all four.

It is a personal setting: it changes only your own searches, never a price or an asset you already have. See Plugin Settings.

docs.title: ⚠️ Limits
docs.text:
• ISIN only: for a ticker, use Yahoo Finance.
  • Only the EUR price is live.
  • LibreFolio reads justETF's website: a change on their side can stop the prices until LibreFolio is updated.

docs.title: Scheduled Investment
docs.text: The Scheduled Investment provider calculates an asset's value from its interest schedule instead of reading a market price. Use it for savings accounts, term deposits, P2P or crowdfunding loans, and bonds you follow by their accrued interest. In the Provider list it is called Scheduled Investment Calculator.

docs.title: 🔍 What It Offers
docs.text:
• ✅ Current price and history, calculated from your schedule: no website is queried, and the same schedule always gives the same values.
  • ✅ Events: with Generate Coupon, interest payouts and a final maturity settlement, plus the events you add yourself.
  • ❌ Search and details: not applicable. There is no identifier to type either: LibreFolio creates one for you.

docs.title: 📋 Interest Schedule Editor
docs.text:
Choosing the provider in Provider Assignment opens the Interest Schedule editor. Start with the settings for the whole schedule:

  • Initial Value and Currency: the amount invested, or the face value — e.g. 10,000 EUR.
  • Interest Type: Simple or Compound — see How the value is calculated.
  • Day Count: how the days of a year are counted — ACT/365, ACT/360, ACT/ACT or 30/360. See Day count conventions.

Then add the periods with Add First Period, and Add Period for the next ones:

Column What to enter Period Start and end date, both included Rate % The annual rate as a percentage: 5.00 means 5% a year Frequency How often interest matures: Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Semiannual or Annual Generate Coupon Tick it to pay the accrued interest out at each maturity date

Periods must follow one another, with no gaps or overlaps. Split cuts a period in two; select neighbouring periods and click Merge to join them.

Limits of a schedule

Every period must lie between 1 January 1900 and 31 December 2200, and the whole schedule may span at most 100 years, with at most 1,200 periods. The grace days of late interest are at most 100 years too (36,525 days). A schedule outside these limits is refused: Test Configuration, and the price calculation (Recalculate on the asset page), report invalid parameters.

docs.title: ⚡ Late Interest
docs.text:
For a loan repaid late, turn on ⚡ Late Interest below the periods: the asset keeps growing after the last period ends. A late row appears with its own Rate %, Frequency and Generate Coupon. Click its period to set the grace days, and choose Simple or Compound (the default) next to the switch.

  • During the grace days, interest keeps accruing at the last period's rate.
  • After them, the late rate applies.

docs.title: 📅 Asset Events
docs.text:
Add one-off events with Add Event: a Date, a Type, a Value and optional Notes. Each event counts from its date onwards.

Type Effect on the value Interest An interest payout you received: the value drops by that amount Price Adjustment A write-down (negative) or a write-up (positive) Maturity Settlement The asset reaches maturity and pays back its capital; its value stops changing. Generate Coupon adds one on the last maturity date

docs.title: 🧮 How the Value Is Calculated
docs.text:
LibreFolio walks the schedule day by day. On day \(d\) the value is

\[ V(d) = V_0 + I(d) - \sum \text{Interest events} + \sum \text{Price adjustments} \]

where \(V_0\) is the Initial Value, \(I(d)\) the interest accrued so far, and the sums cover the events up to day \(d\). Each day adds interest at the period's annual rate \(r\) over \(\Delta t\), one day's share of the year under the Day Count (for example \(1/365\) with ACT/365):

  • Simple — interest on the initial value only: \(\Delta I = V_0 \, r \, \Delta t\)
  • Compound — interest on the interest already accrued too: \(\Delta I = (V_0 + I) \, r \, \Delta t\)

With Generate Coupon, at each maturity date the gain \(V(d) - V_0\), when positive, is paid out as an interest event: the value starts again from \(V_0\), and \(I\) and the sums restart from zero.

  • Before the first period, the value is the Initial Value.
  • After the last period, it stays at its final amount, unless late interest is on. With Generate Coupon on the last period and no late interest, the last coupon is paid on the end date and a maturity settlement event closes the asset at the value left after it: the Initial Value.
  • The chart gets a point on each Frequency date: choose Daily for a smooth line.
🧮 A €10,000 loan at 5%, with a coupon every month

Simple interest, ACT/365, one period starting on 1 January, Frequency Monthly, Generate Coupon ticked. The first maturity date is 1 February, 31 days later: the loan has earned about €42.47 (\(10\,000 \times 0.05 \times 31/365\)). That amount is paid out as an interest event, and the value goes back to €10,000 to grow again in February.

docs.title: Yahoo Finance
docs.text: Yahoo Finance covers stocks, ETFs, funds, indices and crypto from exchanges worldwide, and you can search it by name or ticker.

docs.title: 🔍 What It Offers
docs.text:
• Current price: the latest price Yahoo reports for the ticker — on some exchanges it is delayed.
  • History: daily open, high, low, close and volume, as far back as Yahoo goes. The closes are saved as the exchange gives them, without the adjustment for the dividends paid since (a split is already in Yahoo's closes, and is recorded as an event).
  • Dividends and splits: recorded as asset events. For a London line quoted in pence, the dividend is saved in pounds (1.95 pence is 0.0195 GBP).
  • Search: by name or ticker.
  • Details: type, currency, description, sector, ticker and, when Yahoo has it, the ISIN.
  • Fund details: for an ETF or a fund, the sector breakdown (a stock gets its single sector), the fund's own description when Yahoo has no business summary for it, and at the end of the description the expense ratio (TER: 0.03%) and the issuer (Issuer: Vanguard). Yahoo does not give every fund its expense ratio — Vanguard FTSE All-World (VWCE.DE) has none — and then that part is left out. The country breakdown comes only from justETF.

docs.title: ✏️ Set It Up
docs.text:
Search Online sets it up for you. By hand, in Provider Assignment, choose Yahoo Finance, set Identifier Type to TICKER and type the ticker as Identifier. There is nothing else to fill in.

Asset Ticker Apple Inc. AAPL Vanguard FTSE All-World (Xetra) VWCE.DE iShares Core S&P 500 (Milan) CSSPX.MI Bitcoin in US dollars BTC-USD

Outside the US, add the exchange suffix to the ticker: .DE for Xetra, .MI for Milan, .AS for Amsterdam.

Many London lines (suffix .L) are quoted in pence, which Yahoo reports as the currency GBp. LibreFolio stores the currency as GBP and the prices as Yahoo gives them, in pence, so such an asset needs Units per single price at 100, or its value comes out 100 times too high. When Yahoo reports GBp, picking the line in Search Online sets 100, with a note under the field, and Ask Provider proposes it if the field says otherwise (Check the provider's data).

docs.title: ⚠️ Limits
docs.text:
• ISIN also works as Identifier Type, but only when Yahoo can match it to a ticker: prefer the ticker.
  • Data saved before this behaviour stay as they were. If you have a Yahoo asset whose closes were saved earlier, they still carry the dividend adjustment of the day they were read, and the dividends of a pence line are still in pence. Nothing rewrites them on its own: run the full Sync of the asset again (the dialog warns before it overwrites) and the history is read afresh. This does not change the split behaviour below.
  • Known limitation: splits. After a stock split Yahoo rewrites the past closes (and dividends) to the new number of shares. For Apple's 4:1 split of 31 August 2020, the close of 28 August 2020 is given as 124.81 instead of the 499 it really was. So the value of a position on the days before a split can come out divided by the split ratio (10 shares × 124.81 = 1,248 instead of 4,990), and the return jumps on the day of the split. A correction is planned after 1.3.
  • Yahoo may throttle frequent requests: LibreFolio then pauses it for a while and keeps showing the last saved prices. Some tickers have missing days.
