docs.title: 📥 Broker Transactions
docs.text:
The Transactions tab of a broker lists its transactions, newest first, for the date range chosen in the toolbar. To see the whole history, choose All there.

Above the list you find Uploaded Reports, View in Transactions and the column picker. Owners and Editors also get Import, Add Transaction and, once you tick rows, the bar to edit, clone or delete them. A Viewer sees the table, the uploaded reports and View in Transactions.

docs.title: ➕ Add a transaction
docs.text:
1. Click Add Transaction. The transaction workspace opens on a New transaction form, with this broker already selected.
  2. Pick the Type and fill in the required fields — see Transaction Form.
  3. Click Apply to place the row in the workspace, then Save All to write it.

Nothing is saved before Save All: until then you can add more rows, change them or cancel (see The bulk workspace).

docs.title: 🔎 Open, edit or delete transactions
docs.text:
• Double-click a row to open it read-only.
  • Owners and Editors can edit, clone or delete rows here: use the actions of a row, or tick rows and use the bar above the table.
  • View in Transactions opens the Transactions page, filtered on this broker, on the period of the toolbar and on the column filters you set here.

docs.title: 🧙 Import a statement
docs.text:
Import opens the workspace together with the Import Wizard (BRIM, the Broker Report Import Module). The wizard reads the files exported by your broker, lets you check every row, and hands the result to the workspace: nothing is written until Save All.

  • 📥 Import from Broker — supported brokers and formats.
  • 🧙 How to Import Transactions — the wizard, step by step.

The same wizard opens from Import on the Transactions page.

🧩 Your broker is not supported yet — what you can do
  • Request a plugin: open a plugin request on GitHub and attach an anonymised sample of the broker's export.
  • Write a plugin: the BRIM Plugin Guide explains the plugin contract, and Contribute the workflow.
  • If imported rows keep looking wrong, the wizard's Corrections step links to GitHub so you can report a possible importer bug.

docs.title: 🗂️ Uploaded reports
docs.text:
Uploaded Reports opens the report files stored for this broker:

  • Upload CSV or Excel files: they are assigned to this broker and listed in the wizard's Select Files step. Files you upload together form one set — this is how banks that split an account across several exports, such as Danske Bank, are imported.
  • Preview or Delete a file. Deleting a report never deletes the transactions imported from it.
  • Check each file's Status and Report set badges — see Report sets.
  • Manage all files opens the Files & Uploads page, filtered on this broker.

Uploading and deleting reports needs Owner or Editor access to the broker.

The reports an older version of LibreFolio stored without a broker are not in this list: the person who uploaded them and the administrators find them on the Files & Uploads page.

docs.title: 🏦 Brokers
docs.text:
A broker is one of your accounts — at a brokerage, a bank or an exchange: the place where your investments and your cash live. Every transaction and every uploaded report belongs to a broker, so you need at least one before you start.

The Brokers page shows one card per broker, with its value (NAV) in the currency chosen in Currency at the top of the page. Click a card to open the broker.

Gain/Loss is the NAV minus the capital that went into the broker: your deposits minus withdrawals, plus the cost of securities you brought in without cash, plus what you moved in from your other brokers minus what you moved out, each move valued on the day it arrived. So moving money or securities between two of your brokers is not a gain on one card and a loss on the other, and while a transfer is on its way, its value stays on the sending broker's card. Cash held in another currency is valued at the latest exchange rate, so what the rate does to it counts in Gain/Loss, not in the capital. The percentage in brackets is the gain over that capital: it shows 0.00% when that capital is zero or less, for example when the broker has sent out more than it received. → Internal transfers

Shared brokers show your share on the card

On a broker you co-own, the values on its card are scaled by your ownership share: a 50% Owner sees half of the account. Editors and Viewers see the full amounts. The broker's own page shows the whole account to everyone — see The broker page is the Dashboard on one broker. See Broker Sharing.

docs.title: ➕ Create a broker
docs.text:
1. Open Brokers from the sidebar and click Add Broker.

  2. Type a Name — the only required field — and set the options you need.

  3. Click Create: the broker appears in your list, ready for transactions and reports.

⚙️ The optional fields — what each one does
  • Description — your own notes.
  • Default Import Plugin — the importer that the Import Wizard proposes for this broker's files.
  • Portal URL — the broker's website, opened from the broker page. The broker's icon is, in this order: your Custom Icon URL; the icon of the Default Import Plugin, when that importer is made for this broker; the website's icon; the icon of a generic importer such as the Generic CSV; otherwise a briefcase.
  • Account Opened and Account Active — when the account was opened, and whether it is still open. A closed broker shows dimmed in the list.
  • Trading Options — Allow Leveraged Buying and Allow Short Selling, explained in Trading options.
  • Initial Balances (only when creating) — your starting cash. LibreFolio records one Deposit per currency, dated today: if the money was there earlier, change the date of those deposits on the Transactions page.
🏷️ “A broker named … already exists” — when it appears

Broker names are unique on the whole server, across all its users. Choose a different name, or rename the existing broker if it is yours.

Brokers of other users that you cannot open are listed under Other Existing Brokers. Their share button shows who has access, so you know whom to ask: every signed-in user of this LibreFolio can see it, for any broker.

docs.title: ✏️ Edit or delete a broker
docs.text:
• Edit — the pencil on the broker card, or Edit in the broker's toolbar. Owners and Editors can edit a broker.
  • Delete — the bin on the broker card. Only an Owner can delete a broker. If it still holds transactions, LibreFolio says how many and offers Go to transactions or Delete broker and transactions, which deletes them as well. Assets it transferred to another broker, a shared one included, stay there as an opening position at their transfer cost, starting on the transfer date: that broker's gain then also counts what they gained before the transfer. Assets another broker transferred to it leave that broker as an adjustment that takes the units out: it has no value, so the units only leave the quantity and their cost counts as a realized loss there (Outgoing Adjustments). Cash transfers with another broker become a deposit or a withdrawal there.

docs.title: 🗂️ Inside a broker
docs.text:
A broker's card opens its page on the Overview tab:

At the top, the header shows the broker's name, its icon and, as a badge, your role and your ownership share. The toolbar below applies to every tab:

  • the date range and the Currency of the figures, with the same list as on the Dashboard, Create forex included;
  • Edit (Owners and Editors) and Share Broker, which opens the Info tab;
  • AI Export, which copies a ready-made prompt about this broker to your clipboard — see Broker AI Export;
  • Refresh, which recalculates the page on demand.

Below it, five tabs:

  1. Overview — how the account is doing (below).
  2. Positions — what you hold at this broker (below).
  3. Risk — the Dashboard's risk analysis, limited to this broker (see Dashboard Risk Tab).
  4. Transactions — the broker's ledger, manual entries, imports and uploaded reports (see Broker Transactions).
  5. Info — account details, trading options and sharing (see Configuration & Info).

docs.title: 🧭 The broker page is the Dashboard on one broker
docs.text:
A broker's page is the Dashboard with that broker already chosen, plus the broker's own Info tab. The controls, the tabs and their panels work as described in the Dashboard pages; there is no broker filter, because the page is one broker.

What is the same as on the Dashboard:

  • Period, currency and buttons. The date range, the Currency menu, AI Export and Refresh are the Dashboard's. When you have not used the page for two minutes, the Refresh button shows a pause icon and a greyer tone, and its tooltip says the updates are paused: click it to update the prices again (see Live prices on the Assets page).
  • Cash balances follow the period. They show the cash at the end of the period you picked.
  • Lots. Analyze Lots opens the lot detail below the list; the browser's Back button closes it. See all → opens the Assets page on the same period.
  • Data-quality banner. Old prices and missing or old exchange rates are reported here too, with the same Sync prices and Sync rates buttons (Data Quality Banner). Every role sees them, a Viewer included: they update shared prices and exchange rates, not the broker.

What is different:

  • The whole broker. Every amount on the page, Risk included, is the broker's whole amount (100%), also when you own less than 100% of it. The badge in the header shows your role and share. The Dashboard filtered on the same broker shows your share of it.
  • Transactions follow the period. The Transactions tab lists the transactions of the date range chosen in the toolbar, and View in Transactions opens the Transactions page with the same period. Import, Add Transaction, Edit, Clone, Delete and the selection bar are for Owners and Editors; a Viewer sees the table, the import history and View in Transactions.

docs.title: 📈 Overview tab
docs.text:
The Overview answers "how is this account doing?" with the same blocks as the Dashboard Overview, limited to this broker:

  • KPI cards — Period P&L, Returns and Net Worth (KPI Cards).
  • Cash Balances — the cash held here at the end of the period, per currency.
  • Growth chart — the Abs, % and P&L views, with P&L as Line, Candles or Income (Portfolio Growth Chart, P&L mode). The view you pick is shared with the Dashboard.
  • Allocation — by type, sector and geography (Allocation Panel).

Coming back to a broker you already opened shows its last figures at once, refreshed in the background if something changed (Coming back and refreshing). Refresh recalculates on demand, the Risk tab and the lots panel included.

docs.title: 🔍 Positions tab
docs.text:
The Positions tab lists what you hold at this broker, in the same panel as the Dashboard Positions:

  • Portfolio shows your holdings (quantity, value, weight); Period shows each position's gains and losses over the selected dates. Both come as a Table or a Map.
  • The YOC column is each holding's Yield on Cost at this broker.
  • Analyze Lots opens the FIFO Lots Analysis panel below the list: find it in a row's ⋮ menu, or right-click the asset in the table or the map.

docs.title: 📑 In this section
docs.text:
• 📥 Broker Transactions — add transactions to this broker, import statements and manage its uploaded reports.
  • ⚙️ Configuration & Info — account details, trading options and the sharing panel.
  • 🧠 Broker AI Export — what a broker export contains, and the analyses you can ask an AI for.
  • 🤝 Broker Sharing — roles (Owner, Editor, Viewer) and ownership shares.

The Brokers page, the Add Broker form and the broker page each have a short contextual guide: replay them from Settings → Preferences → Onboarding and guides.

docs.title: ⚙️ Broker Configuration & Info
docs.text: The Info tab of a broker shows the account's details on the left and who can access it on the right.

docs.title: 📋 Account details
docs.text:
The Details card lists:

  • Account Active — ✓ Active, or ✗ Closed for an account you no longer use. A closed broker keeps its history in your charts.
  • Account Opened — when you opened the account, if you set it.
  • Allow Leveraged Buying and Allow Short Selling — the two trading options, explained below.
  • Created in System — when the broker was added to LibreFolio.

To change them, click Edit in the broker's toolbar (Owners and Editors).

docs.title: 🛡️ Trading options
docs.text:
Both options are off for a new broker, and LibreFolio then guards you against impossible balances:

  • with Allow Leveraged Buying off, a save is refused if it would leave the cash of a currency below zero;
  • with Allow Short Selling off, a save is refused if it would leave the quantity of an asset below zero.

Turn an option on for a margin account, or to record short sales.

📅 How balances are checked — when a save is refused

For each currency \(c\) and each asset \(i\) of the broker, LibreFolio looks at the balance at the end of every day \(d\), after all of that day's transactions:

\[ C_c(d) = \sum_{\text{date}_t \le d} a_t \ge 0 \qquad\qquad Q_i(d) = \sum_{\text{date}_t \le d} q_t \ge 0 \]

Here \(a_t\) is the cash amount of each transaction \(t\) in currency \(c\), and \(q_t\) the quantity of each transaction of asset \(i\). Money in and out on the same day nets out, but a deposit made later does not fix a day that already closed below zero.

A refused save shows in the workspace under This configuration causes data inconsistencies, with the currency or asset, the date, and links to the workspace rows involved.

docs.title: 🤝 Share the broker
docs.text:
The right column holds the Share Broker panel; Share Broker in the toolbar brings you here too. Only an Owner can change it: everyone else sees it read-only.

To give someone access:

  1. Click + (Add User) under the ownership chart and find the person by username.
  2. Choose the Role — Viewer by default, Editor or Owner — and, for an Owner, the Ownership %. Then click Add User.
  3. Click Save Configuration: nothing changes before you do.

Save before you switch tab: on the Info tab, unsaved changes are dropped without asking.

Under Your access you can also Leave broker, or Switch to viewer if you are an Editor. Roles and ownership shares are explained in Broker Sharing.

docs.title: 🔗 Related
docs.text:
• 🧠 Broker AI Export — AI Export sits in the broker's toolbar and works from every tab.
  • 🏦 Brokers — creating a broker and its optional fields.

docs.title: 🤝 Broker Sharing
docs.text: Share a broker with the people who need it — a partner, a family member, an advisor or an accountant. Each person gets a role, which decides what they can do, and each Owner an ownership share, which decides how much of the account counts as theirs.

docs.title: ➕ Share a broker
docs.text:
Open the sharing panel with the share button on the broker's card, or with Share Broker in the broker's toolbar (it opens the Info tab). Only an Owner can change it; everyone else sees it read-only.

  1. Click + (Add User) and find the person by username.
  2. Choose the Role and, for an Owner, the Ownership %. Then click Add User.
  3. Click Save Configuration. Nothing changes before you do: until then, ↺ Reset puts the list back as it was.
✏️ Change or remove someone — and when a save is refused

Click a person's chip to change their Role or Ownership %, or to Remove Access; click Confirm, then Save Configuration.

A save is refused if it would leave the broker without an Owner — so the last Owner can be neither removed nor demoted — or if the shares add up to more than 100% (the panel warns Total ownership exceeds 100%).

Unsaved changes: the dialog opened from the broker list asks before closing, but on the Info tab, switching to another tab drops them.

docs.title: 🛡️ What each role can do
docs.text:
What you can do Viewer Editor Owner See the broker, its transactions, reports and charts ✅ ✅ ✅ Add, edit and import transactions; upload and delete report files ❌ ✅ ✅ Edit the broker's settings ❌ ✅ ✅ Manage who has access ❌ ❌ ✅ Delete the broker ❌ ❌ ✅
  • 👁️ Viewer — read-only, for an accountant or relatives who only need to look.
  • ✏️ Editor — does the day-to-day work, but cannot share or delete the broker.
  • 👑 Owner — full control; a broker can have several Owners.

docs.title: 📊 Ownership share
docs.text:
Each Owner has a share from 0% to 100%: the part of the account that is theirs. Viewers and Editors always have 0%. The shares can add up to less than 100% — for example when a co-owner does not use LibreFolio — but never more; the panel shows the Allocated and Available totals as you edit.

The share decides what counts in your figures:

  • The Dashboard counts only the brokers you own with a share above 0%, and scales their amounts by your share: with 50%, you see half of the broker's value, income and P&L.
  • The Dashboard's Risk tab covers the same brokers: the ones you own with a share above 0% (see Risk Tab).
  • Brokers where you are a Viewer or an Editor, or that you own with 0%, are not on your Dashboard. Their own page shows them, and it shows the whole broker (100%) to every role, an Owner with a smaller share included.

docs.title: 💡 Common setups
docs.text: Who Setup What they see Spouse or partner Two Owners, 50% each Each of you sees half of the account on your own Dashboard Co-owner without a LibreFolio account You as Owner, 50% Your half; the other 50% stays unallocated Financial advisor or accountant Viewer The whole broker on its page, nothing on their Dashboard Family member who records operations Editor Adds and imports transactions, but cannot share or delete the broker

docs.title: 🚪 Leave a broker or step down
docs.text:
You never need an Owner to leave. Under Your access in the sharing panel, after a confirmation:

  • Leave broker removes your access at once, and the broker disappears from your lists;
  • Switch to viewer (Editors only) gives up editing; an Owner can make you an Editor again.

Last Owner: leaving deletes the broker

If you are the only Owner left, the button becomes Leave and delete broker: leaving permanently deletes the broker together with all its transactions and imported report files. This cannot be undone. To keep the broker, make another user an Owner first, then leave.

Deleting your account follows the same rule — see Profile.

To get access to someone else's broker, ask one of its Owners. The brokers you cannot open are listed under Other Existing Brokers on the Brokers page, and their share button shows who has access. Every signed-in user of this LibreFolio can see who has access to any broker, so the people who share an instance can find each other.

docs.title: 📊 Charts
docs.text: Below the KPI cards, the Portfolio Growth chart and the Asset Allocation panel show where your portfolio has been and what it is made of. Both follow the Dashboard's time range and broker filter, and a broker's page shows them for that broker alone.

docs.title: 📈 Portfolio Growth Chart
docs.text:
The growth chart shows how your portfolio evolved over the selected period: the Abs / % / P&L toggle in its top-right corner switches between absolute values, rates of return, and the money actually earned.

On a long period the chart groups the days to stay readable: into weeks, then months, and, for a history of many decades, years. A Weekly, Monthly or Yearly badge at the top left of the chart says which. When nothing is grouped, there is no badge.

docs.title: 〰️ How the lines are drawn
docs.text:
Every chart joins its points in one of three shapes: Segments (the default, a straight line between two points), Steps (each value holds until the next one) or Smooth curve (a soft line that never goes above or below the two neighbouring points, so it draws no value that never existed). You pick the shape on the first page of the welcome tour and later in Settings → Preferences; it is kept with your account and applies to every chart, in every browser you sign in from, until you give one chart its own shape. Until you pick one it follows the administrator's default. On the asset and FX detail pages the chart settings also have a Line shape row, to give that one chart its own shape. The shape changes only how the points are joined: a day's value in the tooltip is always the one the report holds for that day. Where a chart shows weeks or months, the points are not steps, so Steps draws segments there.

The chart remembers your last view, P&L sub-view included, in this browser and for each user, and shares it with the broker pages. It starts on Abs. Without rate-of-return data, % is greyed out and the chart shows Abs, but keeps your choice: % comes back as soon as there is data to draw — after you change the period or the broker, or the next time you open the chart — unless you pick another view in the meantime.

Hide amounts (the eye button in the top bar) turns every amount on the axis and in the tooltips into •••; signs, currencies, lines, and colours stay. See Privacy mode.

docs.title: 💶 Abs — absolute values
docs.text:
Element Color Meaning Area — Purchase Cost Blue What the positions you hold cost you (average cost × quantity) Area — Returns Emerald Returns held as cash (dividends, interest, realized gains not yet reinvested, exchange-rate gains on cash you hold in another currency) Area — Capital Grey-green Deposits not yet invested, held as cash Line — Net Asset Value Dark green solid Total portfolio value at current market prices Line — Deposited Capital Grey dashed Net external capital contributed over time

The gap between the two lines is your Total P&L: every gain ever made (unrealized, realized, interest, dividends, and exchange-rate gains or losses on cash held in another currency) minus fees and taxes. The tooltip shows both lines, the Total P&L in green or red, and the breakdown: Assets at Cost (the blue area, assets moving between your brokers included), Returns, and Capital.

Assets valued at their purchase price, such as P2P loans with no live market price, keep NAV close to Purchase Cost, so the gap can be thin: read Total P&L in the tooltip.

Money from a broker outside the view. On a broker's page, or with the broker filter on, money received from a broker outside the view is Capital, as a deposit would be — or Returns again, if it brings back returns you withdrew earlier. Money sent to a broker outside the view leaves Capital first, then Returns, as a withdrawal does. The same goes for the half of a transfer whose other half was deleted or unlinked, in every view.

🔗 Theory: Deposited Capital & Total P&L · Cash Decomposition

docs.title: 📉 % — rate of return
docs.text:
Each line is the return accumulated since the start of the selected period:

Series What it shows MWRR cumulative Your personal money-weighted return including deposit timing TWRR Pure asset strategy return, ignoring when you deposited ROI Raw return on net invested capital

The gap between MWRR and TWRR is the Timing Effect. The MWRR line has a gap on the days that have no MWRR — a value of zero or less, or net withdrawals that leave no invested capital — by the same rule as the MWRR cards (MWRR). The TWRR line has a gap on the days your portfolio is worth zero or less, for example after you sold everything and withdrew the cash, by the same rule as the TWRR card; after new deposits it picks up again from where it stood (When No TWRR Is Shown). The ROI line has no gap. When the last day of the period has none, the Data Quality banner says MWRR cannot be calculated for this period.

docs.title: 💰 P&L — the money you made
docs.text:
P&L plots your Total P&L (NAV minus deposited capital): how much money the portfolio has actually made since inception. Zooming in does not restart the count at zero.

A second toggle, at the top-left of the plot, picks how to draw it (icons only on a narrow chart):

View What it draws The question it answers Line Accumulated P&L as a single line How has my result moved over time? Candles One candle per period, from a day to a year How wide was the swing inside each period? Income Bars of the cash that actually moved Where did the money come from, and what did it cost me?

docs.title: Line — accumulated P&L
docs.text:
• The line is green above zero and red below.
  • A dashed grey line marks the P&L of the first day in view: the gap to it is what you gained or lost since the left edge.

Broker lines. With two or more brokers in scope, each broker gets a dashed line and a tooltip row with its share of the total; the shares add up to the total every day. A broker's line is the P&L made while the value was at that broker: moving money or securities between two of your brokers is neither a gain nor a loss, so no line jumps when a transfer arrives.

  • In transit — until the transfer arrives, the value and its price or exchange-rate moves stay with the broker it left.
  • Different ownership shares — when the two brokers have different ownership shares, the receiving line keeps a step on the arrival day: the same step the total shows.
  • No value on the arrival day — if an exchange rate is missing, or the security has no price yet and no cost was recorded on its arrival, the jump stays: nothing is guessed. A security with no price at all moves at the cost the receiving broker records for it, the value LibreFolio gives it there; if part of what that broker paid for the asset was already unknown, its own line takes the gap.
  • Brokers outside the view — on a broker's page, or with the broker filter on, securities sent to or received from a broker outside the view count as capital at their market value on that day — at their cost if they have no price at all — not as a gain or a loss; money counts as a deposit or a withdrawal. When the other broker of a transfer is deleted, the half left behind is no longer a transfer: securities become an adjustment, counted as capital at their cost rather than their market value, and money a deposit or a withdrawal (see Edit or delete a broker). Only securities sent whose average cost needs a missing exchange rate stay a transfer, counted at market value.

With one broker, or on a broker's page, only the total is drawn.

🔗 Theory: Internal transfers in the broker lines

docs.title: Candles — the swing inside the period
docs.text:
Each period of the width you pick becomes a candle made of P&L values, not prices. Its close is exactly the Total P&L that Line shows for that day.

Highs and lows are hypothetical

A candle's top and bottom add up each asset's own daily high and low, which were not reached at the same moment: that portfolio state may never have existed, as the caption under the chart says (Synthetic — cross-asset high/low are hypothetical and non-simultaneous). Read them as how far the portfolio could have swung.

Also expect:

  • No volume — a portfolio's P&L has no traded volume.
  • Thin bodies, long wicks — open and close are usually close while the summed range is wide.
  • Gaps — a day on which a held asset could not be valued has no candle rather than a guessed one.

The tooltip gives the period, Open, Close, High, and Low, plus a row per broker when two or more are in scope.

docs.title: Income — the cash that actually moved
docs.text:
Income leaves valuations aside and plots your real cash flows. Each bar is the sum of its period's flows, in up to three columns:

Column Bars What it represents Income and costs Dividend · Interest above zero, Fees & taxes below it What the portfolio paid you, and what the activity cost you Deposits Deposit Fresh money you put in (withdrawals are not drawn) Purchases Purchase Cost, in two zones: New capital at the bottom, Reinvested on top What you spent on buys, split by where the money came from

How to read it:

  • New capital or reinvested. A purchase first spends the returns already held as cash at that broker (Reinvested, green as in Abs); the rest is New capital (blue). Money moved to or from a broker outside the view changes that cash as a deposit or a withdrawal would, as in Abs above. Sales are never drawn.
  • Signs are kept. A negative correction on a past dividend shrinks the dividend bar; fees and taxes stay below zero.
  • It matches the KPIs. For the same dates and brokers, Dividend and Interest add up exactly to the Dividends & interest row of the Period P&L card.
  • One legend entry. Both purchase zones are named Purchase Cost: one click hides both, and the Abs area of the same name too.
  • Missing exchange rates. An amount that cannot be converted on its date is left out, not counted as zero; the Data Quality banner reports it.

The purchase bars are not the Purchase Cost KPI

The bars are a flow: what you spent on buys in each period. The Purchase Cost row of the Net Worth card is a level: what the positions you still hold cost you on the end date. Sales and earlier purchases count in the KPI but have no bar.

docs.title: Candle width — 1D to 1Y
docs.text:
In Candles and Income, the buttons in the top-right corner of the plot, from 1D to 1Y, set how much time one candle, or one group of bars, covers. The chart still shows the whole range, and zooming never changes the width.

  • Calendar periods. 1W runs from Monday to Sunday, 1M is a calendar month, 3M a quarter, 6M a half-year, 1Y a year; 3D and 2W are fixed blocks of days.
  • Axis labels. Each label names the start of its period, even one the range covers only in part; months and years appear only where they change, and crowded labels tilt or thin out.
  • Only widths that fit the chart and the range are offered; Income starts at 1W.
  • Where it starts. Candles take the finest width available; Income opens on 1M, or the nearest width available, each time you enter it. Reloading the page resets the width.
  • Partial periods are faded. A period the range starts partway through, or a last one cut short by a range ending in the past, is drawn faded, and its tooltip says Partial: N of M days. Otherwise, the period in progress is drawn whole, with In progress: N of M days.

docs.title: 🥧 Allocation Panel
docs.text: The Asset Allocation panel shows how your portfolio is split, today and over time. Pick a dimension with the By Type, By Sector, Geographic and By Asset tabs, and a view with the two buttons in the top-right corner: the pie for Now, the area chart for History.

docs.title: 🗂️ Three dimensions
docs.text: Tab What it shows By Type What each holding is — its asset type, such as Stock, ETF, Bond, Fund, or Crypto — plus Liquidity for your cash. Subtypes count with their family, such as an Equity ETF with your other ETFs. By Sector Industry sector: 💻 Technology, 🏦 Financials, 💊 Health Care, etc. Geographic Where your assets are invested, country by country, according to each asset's geographic distribution By Asset How much each single asset weighs: one slice per asset, with Liquidity for your cash. See By Asset.

docs.title: 🕰️ Now and History
docs.text:
• Now — the allocation on the last day of the selected range: a donut for By Type and By Sector, a world map for Geographic. Hover a slice or a country for its percentage and amount; by type, the tooltip also shows the asset type as a badge (Liquidity, your cash, has none). By type, the donut can have two rings.
  • History — a 100% stacked area chart of how the allocation shifted over time, handy to see rebalancing. By type, each family is one area; hovering a date lists its subtypes, such as Generic ETF and Equity ETF.

The panel remembers the view and the tab in this browser, for each user, and shares them with the broker pages.

docs.title: 🧩 By Asset
docs.text:
Which single assets weigh most? By Asset splits the portfolio asset by asset instead of by category.

  • Now — a pie with the weight of every asset on the last day of the selected range. Each slice shows its asset's icon — its own, or its type's when it has none or it cannot be loaded; the cash shows the Liquidity one. There is no legend: hover a slice to read the asset type, as a badge, then the name, the share and the amount.
  • History — how the distribution by asset changed over time. Closed positions are included, so an asset you sold still shows in the days you held it.
  • Colours follow the weight today: the heaviest asset gets the first colour, then the others by weight, then the closed assets, the most recently closed first. The pie, the history and the lines of Return of the positions use the same colour for the same asset.

docs.title: 🍩 Two rings by type
docs.text:
As soon as you hold an asset with a subtype, such as an Equity ETF or Real estate crowdfunding, the Now donut of By Type draws two rings:

  • Inner ring — one slice per family, with its icon where it fits: all your ETFs (generic ETF and every subtype) together, Crowdfund with Real estate crowdfunding, and every other type, Liquidity included, on its own. These are the families the asset Type menu groups together.
  • Outer ring — thinner and set apart, it splits each family that holds a subtype into its members, in shades of the family's colour, captioned where there is room. The generic member reads Generic ETF or Generic Crowdfund.
  • Hover a slice for its share and amount; on the outer ring, a last line starting with ↳ gives the whole family's share.
  • The legend lists families only: clicking one hides its slices on both rings.

With no subtype at all, the donut keeps a single ring.

docs.title: 💵 Cash as Liquidity
docs.text: Your cash is the Liquidity slice of By Type, By Sector and By Asset; the Geographic map leaves it out, as cash belongs to no country. With the broker filter on, the panel shows only the selected brokers' assets and cash.

docs.title: ➖ Negative cash
docs.text:
Each slice's percentage is its amount divided by the sum of all the slices, cash included, so negative cash changes the shares:

  • Cash below zero, assets above it — for example €1,500 of stocks with cash at −€500 on an overdraft: the slices add up to €1,000, so Liquidity reads −50% and the stocks 150%. The percentages still add up to 100%.
  • Nothing left to share — when the slices add up to zero or less, no slice has a percentage: €500 of stocks bought on an overdraft of −€500, or a portfolio you emptied, whose only slice is Liquidity at zero. Each slice shows — instead of a percentage and keeps its amount, and the chart has nothing to draw and says so. In History, a day on which the slices add up to zero or less has no percentages either.
  • A tiny leftover of 0.00001 units or fewer, which a sale of almost every unit can leave, is not a holding: it has no slice.

⬅️ Back to Dashboard Overview

docs.title: 📊 Dashboard
docs.text: The Dashboard is your portfolio's command center — a single screen that tells you what your portfolio is worth, how it's performing, and where your money is allocated.

docs.title: 🗂️ Tabbed Layout
docs.text:
The Dashboard interface is organized into four primary tabs, allowing you to switch between different levels of detail:

  1. Overview (default): Key metrics, cash balances, and visual charts of your portfolio.
  2. Positions & Analysis: Open holdings, weights, and detailed tax lot (FIFO) analysis.
  3. Risk: The Portfolio risk panel, which answers four questions about your portfolio's risk.
  4. Transactions: The operations in the selected date range and broker scope, as a paginated, read-only list — double-click a row to open its detail viewer. See Transactions for the full guide.

docs.title: 📈 Overview Tab
docs.text:
The Overview tab is the default landing page. It is structured into the following sections:

Section Description KPI Cards Summary of Net Worth, Period P&L, and rate-of-return metrics. Cash Balances Liquid balances grouped by currency across the active broker scope. Growth Chart Portfolio value over time in three views: absolute values (Abs), rates of return (%), and the money actually earned (P&L). Allocation Panel Donut and historical stacked charts grouped by Type, Sector, and Geography.

docs.title: 🪙 Cash Balances
docs.text:
Directly below the KPI cards, the Cash Balances panel displays your total liquid cash aggregated by currency. For example, if you hold USD in broker A and EUR in broker B, both balances will be displayed side-by-side.

When you apply a broker filter, the cash balances automatically update to reflect only the cash held within the selected brokers.

docs.title: 🛡️ Risk Tab
docs.text: The Risk tab holds the Portfolio risk panel, which answers four questions about your portfolio's risk: How much can it hurt?, Am I as diversified as I think?, Am I being paid for this risk? and What if…? It always covers your whole portfolio — every broker you own with a share above 0% — and follows the dashboard date range and target currency, but not the broker filter: when a filter is on, a subtitle says so. See Risk Tab for the blocks and the tools they show.

docs.title: 🎛️ Date Range, Filters & AI Export
docs.text:
At the top right of the dashboard, you have several controls to customize your view:

  • Time range — presets from 1W to All, or a custom range via the date picker.
  • Broker filter — filters the metrics to one or more specific brokers; the Risk tab always covers every broker you own, and a subtitle says so when a filter is on.
  • Target currency — converts all assets and cash balances dynamically into a single selected currency for aggregate viewing. The list offers your default currency and the currencies of your configured FX pairs — both ends of each pair. A currency that a chain route only passes through is not offered: syncing a chain stores only the rate of its own pair, so LibreFolio has no rates to convert into that currency. To make a currency available, give it a pair of its own: pick Create forex… at the bottom of the list, or tick Also create intermediate pairs when you add a pair through a chain route.
  • AI Export () — opens a clipboard export. Choose Data Snapshot for factual data only, or an analysis task that automatically includes its instructions and response contract, then select the detail level (Compact, Standard, or Full). The backend snapshot follows the active broker filter, date range, and target currency; LibreFolio does not contact an AI service. See Portfolio AI Export or the AI Export overview.

The time range, the broker filter and the target currency stay as you set them for the rest of your session in this browser tab — a page reload keeps them too — and reset when you log out. The time range is shared with the other pages that have one (the Assets and FX pages, their detail pages, and each broker's page), so a change made there shows up here as well. Next to AI Export, the Refresh button () recalculates everything on demand: see Coming back and refreshing.

Scope matters

When you filter to a single broker, cash transfers to other brokers become external flows for that scope. This affects Deposited Capital and P&L calculations.

Sharing affects these numbers

The dashboard counts only the brokers you own with a share above 0%, and every amount from them is scaled by your ownership share: an Owner with a 50% share sees half of that broker's value, income, and P&L counted in the totals. Brokers where you are an Editor or a Viewer — who always carry a 0% share by rule — are left out, like those you own with a 0% share: they are missing from the totals, from the broker filter, from the Positions tab (Period view and lots panel included), from the Risk tab and from the Transactions tab. You see them on their own broker page, which counts the broker whole for every role. See Broker Sharing for details.

A broker's page is this same Dashboard on one broker, with that broker's own Info tab: see The broker page is the Dashboard on one broker.

docs.title: 🔄 Coming back and refreshing
docs.text:
Come back to the Dashboard — from the sidebar, or with the ← back button of an asset page — and it shows at once what it showed when you left: the KPI cards, the charts, the Positions tab with its Period view and FIFO Lots Analysis panel, and the Risk tab. There are no loading placeholders, and the KPI figures appear at their value instead of counting up from zero. If you changed the time range on another page in the meantime, the Dashboard opens on that range instead.

  • If nothing changed in the meantime, that is all: LibreFolio recalculates nothing.
  • If something changed — for example a transaction; prices, rates or events entered by hand or brought in by a sync; an asset edited or merged; a change to one of your brokers or to your access to it; or the live price that an asset page checks while it is open — the old figures stay on screen while LibreFolio recalculates in the background, then the numbers move to the new values. A price or rate sync that brought nothing new is not a change.

The Refresh button recalculates everything, even when nothing changed: the figures, the Period view, the lots panel and the Risk tab. What you see stays on screen meanwhile.

If a recalculation fails, the figures already on screen stay and a message tells you so. On the Risk tab, this holds only for figures of the period and currency you are viewing: if you switch to a period or a currency the tab has no figures for yet and the calculation fails, it shows Risk data could not be loaded. in place of its levels, rather than the figures of your previous choice.

docs.title: 🌡️ Data Quality Banner
docs.text:
If any prices or FX rates are missing on the end date, a banner appears at the top explaining which assets could not be valued.

Assets without a price provider (entered manually, such as real-estate crowdfunding projects) are valued at the price of their latest purchase or sale, unless you enter a more recent price yourself — this is intentional and does not generate a warning. An asset that does have a price provider but still has no market price on the end date, more than two weeks after you first bought it, is valued meanwhile at the price of its latest purchase or sale too, and the banner lists it: a bond bought at issue, before its first quote, for example.

An adjustment records what the units cost, never a price. A transfer does too, with one exception: for an asset that has nothing else yet — no market price, no purchase or sale, no adjustment, no earlier departure — the cost you gave an incoming transfer counts as its price, an estimate, until a real price or trade replaces it. Such an asset is valued at that cost converted at each day's exchange rate, so its value moves with the rate, and the banner treats it like an asset valued at its latest purchase or sale: for an asset with a price provider, it is listed more than two weeks after the transfer arrived, if it still has no market price. A quoted asset moved between your brokers keeps its market price. An asset you hold with no price at all — no market price, no purchase or sale and no such transfer, such as one you received through an adjustment — is valued at what it cost you, when that cost is known, with no unrealized gain or loss. For a manual asset this is intentional and generates no warning; for an asset with a price provider, from more than two weeks after you first acquired it, the banner lists it as valued at cost until it gets a price.

The banner also warns you when an asset you hold has a price provider but its latest price is more than a week old on the end date: click Sync prices to fetch the missing prices, and the warning goes away once they are up to date. Manual assets are never flagged this way, since there is nothing to sync.

The same goes for old exchange rates. When the portfolio is valued on the end date with an exchange rate whose latest stored rate is more than a week old, one warning row lists the affected currency pairs, with one Sync rates button for all of them. If the sync succeeds but the provider has no newer rate yet, an alert says so — The provider has no newer rates for USD → EUR yet: try again later — instead of a plain success message; try again later, and the row goes away once a newer rate is stored.

It also lists the assets with a missing purchase cost: a transfer or an adjustment that brought units in without a cost basis. LibreFolio cannot know what those units cost, so it counts them at zero in your purchase cost and shows that position's average cost and unrealized P&L as unavailable (—). To fix it, find that transfer or adjustment among your transactions and give it its cost basis.

It also warns you about currency codes that are not ISO codes: a number or a name, such as 978 or EURO, that an earlier version of LibreFolio saved as you typed it. LibreFolio now saves only codes such as EUR, so amounts in such a value cannot be converted, and a row that holds it cannot be saved again after an edit until its code is corrected. The warning names the value and the code it stands for (978 is EUR), and lists no exchange rate to add for it, since none would help. When the value is your own default currency, it tells you to choose it again in Settings › Preferences. Your administrator can list every such value with ./dev.py db currencies (CLI Admin Tools, «Currency Codes That Are Not ISO Codes»).

It also notes, without asking you to fix anything, the transfers between brokers you own at different shares: each side counts at its own broker's share, so what leaves one broker and what reaches the other differ, and LibreFolio counts that difference as a gain or loss.

Exchange rates are checked for every transaction up to the end date — each purchase, sale and cash movement is converted at the rate of its own date — and, to value what you hold, on each day of the period on screen: your securities, and also the cash you keep in another currency, valued every day at that day's rate. When a configured FX pair with a provider has no rate for some of those dates, the banner lists it with the span of the missing dates. LibreFolio converts an amount with the latest rate on or before its date, however old, so these dates come before the pair's first stored rate — often well before the period on screen, because every past transaction counts towards totals such as your Total P&L and your purchase cost. Click Sync rates to fill them:

  • LibreFolio downloads that span of dates with one extra week on each side (never beyond today), whatever period the dashboard is showing. The extra week covers weekends and bank holidays, when providers publish nothing: such a day at the edge of the span then takes the rate of the previous working day.
  • Once the download is over, the dashboard refreshes and a message reports the result for each pair.
  • If the download goes through but the same pairs are still flagged, the provider has no rates for the dates still missing — typically because they come before the start of its history. The message then turns into a warning that says so: enter those rates by hand in the pair's Data Editor.

Pairs with manual rates only (no provider) get a warning of their own: its View FX button opens the page of the first pair it lists, where you add the rates yourself.

Fill a pair's whole history at once

Open the FX page, choose the All range and click Sync All: LibreFolio downloads everything the providers publish for your pairs, up to today. A pair you add with a provider does this by itself — see Adding a Currency Pair.

docs.title: 💰 KPI Cards
docs.text:
The three cards at the top of the Dashboard answer three questions at a glance: what did I earn in this period, how well did my money work, and what is my portfolio worth. They follow the time range and the broker filter at the top of the page, and a broker's page shows the same cards for that broker alone. The ? icon in a card's corner opens its section below.

  • 📉 Card 1 — Period P&L — the money your investments made in the period
  • 📈 Card 2 — Returns — your returns in percent, and what your timing did to them
  • 💰 Card 3 — Net Worth — what you own, and your gain since the start

Shared brokers count for your share

The Dashboard adds up the brokers you own with a share above 0%, each in proportion to that share: a 50% owner sees half of the broker's value and P&L. Brokers where you are an Editor or a Viewer are not counted here; their own page shows them, with their full amounts. See Broker Sharing.

docs.title: 📉 Card 1 — Period P&L
docs.text:
How much money did your investments make in the selected period? The Period P&L card answers, leaving out the money you moved in or out yourself.

Metrics shown

  • Period P&L — the big number: \(\text{NAV}_{\text{end}} - \text{NAV}_{\text{start}} - \text{Net flows}\), the net flows being the capital you moved in or out → Period P&L
  • The line under it — for example -1,141 € (-1.95%): how much your Total P&L moved since yesterday, and that change as a percentage of yesterday's portfolio value (panel below)
  • Unrealized change — how the unrealized gain or loss of your holdings moved over the period, exchange-rate effect included → Period PnL
  • Sales — the realized gain or loss of the period's sales, against the average cost of the units sold. An adjustment that removes units has no value: it counts here as a sale for nothing, a loss of what those units cost (see Outgoing Adjustments) → Weighted Average Cost
  • Dividends & interest — dividends, coupons and P2P interest received → Dividend & Interest
  • Fees & taxes — commissions and taxes recorded as transactions; hover the row for the split → Fee & Tax

How to read it

  • Green is a gain, red a loss — and a deposit or a withdrawal is neither.
  • The four rows explain the big number. What they cannot see goes to the Period view: what the exchange rates did to cash you hold in another currency appears there as FX on cash, a row for each broker whose cash the rates moved. When you look at only some of your brokers, securities moved to or from a broker outside your selection count at their market value on the day: the gain they made at the other broker appears as Transfers at market value, a row for each broker involved (how it works). The rest — such as assets moving between two of your brokers on the first or last day — is the Other / reconciliation residual.
  • The longest bar is the row that moved your result the most.
📏 The line under the big number — how it is computed

It is the change of your Total P&L — your gain or loss since the start — from yesterday to today, today being the end date of the period. The percentage compares it with yesterday's net worth — the value of the whole portfolio — taken without its sign:

\[ \Delta = \text{Total P}\&\text{L}_{\text{today}} - \text{Total P}\&\text{L}_{\text{yesterday}} \qquad \text{percentage} = \frac{\Delta}{\left|\text{Net Worth}_{\text{yesterday}}\right|} \times 100 \]
  • Sign and colour follow the change, even while the Total P&L is a loss: from -558.10 € to -466.79 € on a net worth of 10,000 €, the line reads +91.31 € (+0.91%). The base is the portfolio, not the Total P&L: close to zero a Total P&L would turn the same change into a huge percentage that says nothing.
  • It is missing only when the period ends on your portfolio's first day, as there is no day before to compare with; the percentage is left out when yesterday's net worth is exactly zero, and a day without change shows 0.00%. On a Monday the line covers the whole weekend, since a day without a market keeps the last trading day's prices.

docs.title: 💱 Unrealized change by currency
docs.text:
Hover Unrealized change to split it by the currency your assets are priced in — here with euro as display currency:

Row What it shows 📈 Assets in USD What your dollar assets did in dollars — their own price change — counted at the day's exchange rate 💱 USD → EUR rate What the exchange rate did to what you paid for them ❔ USD, not split Only when, on the first or last day, some of those assets had no rate or an incomplete purchase cost: their change, in one piece

There is a 📈 row for every currency, euro included, and a 💱 row for every currency other than your display currency; together the rows add up exactly to the Unrealized change. On a day an asset is valued at what it cost you, because it has no price at all, it has no unrealized gain or loss and adds nothing to any row.

A US ETF on a euro dashboard

During the period you bought 10 units for €400, when they were worth 500 USD. At the end of the period they are worth 550 USD, and 1 USD = €0.75. The tooltip shows:

  • 📈 Assets in USD: (550 − 500) × 0.75 = +€37.50 — your ETF gained 10% in dollars;
  • 💱 USD → EUR rate: 500 × 0.75 − 400 = −€25.00 — the dollar lost value against the euro;
  • together, the Unrealized change: 550 × 0.75 − 400 = +€12.50.

🔗 Theory: Unrealized change by currency — the formulas behind each row

docs.title: 📈 Card 2 — Returns
docs.text:
How well did your money work, whatever the size of your portfolio? The Returns card answers in percentages, and its big number tells you whether your timing helped.

Metrics shown

  • Timing effect — the big number, in percentage points (pp): \(\text{MWRR}_{\text{cumulative}} - \text{TWRR}\) → Timing Effect
  • ROI — the period's gain against the capital invested: what the portfolio was worth when the period began, plus the deposits and minus the withdrawals made since. When the range starts before your first transaction, your first deposit counts as capital too, so the ROI is the same as over your whole history → Simple ROI
  • TWRR — how your asset choices performed, whatever the timing of your deposits → TWRR
  • MWRR cumulative and MWRR annualized — your personal return, deposit timing included, over the period and as a yearly rate → MWRR

How to read it

  • Favorable timing (green): you tended to deposit before prices rose. Unfavorable timing (red): you tended to deposit at the peaks. Close to zero it reads Neutral timing, neither green nor red.
  • TWRR judges the strategy, MWRR your personal result — as for a fund manager and an investor.
  • The four rows cover the whole period.
  • — means no value: a return LibreFolio cannot compute for the period shows — instead of a number. TWRR and MWRR show — when your portfolio is worth zero or less at the end of the period, for example after you sold everything and withdrew the cash (When No TWRR Is Shown, MWRR). The timing effect needs both TWRR and MWRR: when one is missing it shows a grey —, with no timing label. The ROI is never —: without capital invested in the period it reads 0.00%.

docs.title: 💰 Card 3 — Net Worth
docs.text:
What is your portfolio worth at the end of the period, and what has it gained since you started? The Net Worth card answers, cash included.

Metrics shown

  • Net Worth — the big number: securities at market value, plus cash, plus anything in transit between your brokers → NAV / Net Worth
  • The line under it — for example -1,141 € (-1.95%): how much your Total P&L moved since yesterday, and that change as a percentage of yesterday's portfolio value (panel below)
  • Market Value — what the assets you hold are worth at market prices → NAV / Net Worth
  • Purchase Cost — what the positions you still hold cost you, each purchase at its own date's exchange rate → Book Value
  • Cash — the cash at your brokers; hover it to split the capital you deposited from the returns you made → Cash pools
  • Deposited Capital (Period) — deposits minus withdrawals in the period, green to the right and red to the left; hover it for the totals → Deposited Capital
\[ \text{Total P}\&\text{L} = \text{Net Worth} - \text{Capital put in since the start} \]

That capital is every deposit minus every withdrawal, plus the purchase cost of securities you brought in without cash, such as an opening position; the ROI in brackets divides the Total P&L by it.

How to read it

  • End date or period? The big number and the first three rows are values on the end date; Deposited Capital (Period) counts only the movements between start and end.
  • The small caret on a bar marks its value at the start of the period (hover it); Market Value turns red when it ends below it.
  • Net Worth includes cash, unlike the "securities value" of a bank statement.
  • The Total P&L is not a daily change: for today's pulse, see the small line on Card 1.

docs.title: 🔍 Positions & Analysis
docs.text:
The Positions tab shows what you hold, what each position earned in the period and, one click away, the FIFO lots behind any position. Each broker's page has the same tab for that broker alone, with the same table settings.

  • 📋 Holdings — what you own on the end date
  • 📈 Period — what each position earned in the period
  • 🔬 FIFO Lots Analysis — the lots behind one position

docs.title: 🎛️ Choosing a view
docs.text:
• Portfolio / Period switches between what you own and what each position earned; Table / Map (the two icons) between a table and a chart.
  • The eye icon (in Table) shows, hides or reorders the columns; Reset layout restores them. See all → opens the Assets page.
  • To dig into a position, open its ⋮ menu in a table, or right-click it in any view: Analyze Lots opens the FIFO Lots Analysis below the positions (on the Dashboard as on a broker's page), View Asset the asset's page.

LibreFolio remembers your choices.

docs.title: 📋 Holdings — what you own
docs.text:
What do you own on the end date, and how is each position doing? Portfolio lists one row per asset and broker, the largest value first. At the bottom, in italics, come the positions you sold out inside the period: they have no value, weight or yield, but you can tick them to draw their line in the chart, and they have the usual row actions.

Columns shown

Column What it shows Asset The asset, with its type icon Δ1 / Δ1% Today's move of the unrealized P&L at today's quantity, in money and in % of yesterday's value Unrealized P&L / P&L % Current value minus what the open position cost, in money and in % of that cost → Book Value Annualized Yearly compound return since the first transaction, income and fees included → Net Annualized Return YOC The last year's dividends and interest per unit, against its average price → Yield on Cost Value / Weight What the position is worth, and its share of your Net Worth, cash included Qty Shares, units or coins held Price (hidden) The unit price used: the market price, or the price of your last purchase or sale when there is no quote; — for an asset valued at what it cost you, which has no price at all → Price Resolution Avg. Cost (hidden) Average purchase price per unit, each purchase at its own date's exchange rate → Weighted Average Cost Oldest open lot (hidden) Opening date of the oldest lot still open at this broker; a stock split keeps the dates Brokers The broker holding the position

How to read it

  • Weight counts cash, so the rows add up to less than 100% when you hold cash.
  • Weight shows — when your Net Worth is zero or below, for example when you have borrowed more cash than your holdings are worth: a share of it would mean nothing.
  • Avg. Cost keeps each purchase's exchange rate, while Value uses the end date's: the Unrealized P&L includes what the rate did since.
  • Δ1 compares two prices at two exchange rates: today's price, the one the position is valued at, at today's rate, against the last market price up to yesterday at yesterday's rate. For an asset quoted in another currency whose price did not move, Δ1 is only what the exchange rate did in one day, and 0 when the rate did not move either.
  • In the Map, tiles are grouped by broker and asset type; size is the value, colour the P&L %. Scroll to zoom, drag to move, and Reset zoom (↺) shows everything again.
➖ Empty cells — when a value is missing
  • — in Unrealized P&L, P&L % or Avg. Cost: part of what you paid is unknown — an exchange rate missing on a purchase date, or a transfer or adjustment without a cost basis —, or, for Unrealized P&L and P&L % only, the price cannot be converted because the end date's exchange rate is missing. The Data Quality banner names what to fix.
  • — in Price, with an Unrealized P&L of 0: the asset has no price at all — no market price and no purchase or sale, as when you received it through an adjustment or a transfer — so its Value is what it cost you.
  • Δ1 and Δ1% need a market price today and one on or before yesterday; on your portfolio's first day there is no day before, so they stay empty. Annualized needs a position old enough for a yearly rate to mean anything.

docs.title: 📉 Return of the positions
docs.text:
Which of your positions did better than the portfolio, and which worse? On the Dashboard, the Table view of both Portfolio and Period puts a tick box on every row and, under the table, a Return of the positions chart. It sits beside the allocation by asset — the pie of today and the history area, with two buttons — at about 3/5 and 2/5 of the row, like the Growth chart and the Allocation of the Overview. The Map view has no chart.

  • Nothing ticked: the chart shows the portfolio line only. Tick a row, in either table, to add a line for that position, and tick more to compare them.
  • The legend under the title has one button per line, named by the asset's name (a name too long for its button scrolls by itself): click it to turn the line off and on. A flag marks a position that closed, and a warning mark one with a missing price or exchange rate, whose line leaves those days out.
  • Abs / % / Rolling switch the view; the buttons are on the chart, top right, drawn as the Assets list draws them: the line chart icon for Abs, % for the percent, the calendar with arrows icon for Rolling (hover a button to read its name). Abs is the position's profit or loss in money, from the start of the period. % is its return in base 100: every line starts at 100 on the first day of the period, so 112 means +12%. Rolling is described below. LibreFolio remembers the view.
  • Colours are the asset's: a line wears the colour its asset has in the allocation pie and history beside it, whatever you tick and in whatever order. When two brokers hold the same asset, their lines share the colour and differ by pattern: the first is solid, the other dashed (then dotted, then dash-dotted).
  • The box that follows the cursor lists every drawn line on that day; a name too long for the box scrolls by itself.
  • A closed position's line ends on the day it closed; hover the legend button for the date.
  • Up to 50 positions can be drawn at once.

Rolling — comparing assets with each other. For every ticked position, the line shows the percent the asset's price moved over a window that rolls along the period, so assets bought on different days can be compared on the same footing. The window is the largest of 1 week, 1 month, 3 months and 1 year that fits the period, until you choose another one: the Window row above the chart offers those four and Custom, a duration of your own in weeks, months or years. Your choice stays while you change the period, and goes back to the automatic window when you leave the page. It is per asset: two brokers holding the same asset share one line. There is no portfolio line in this view, since the portfolio has no price.

📐 Why the portfolio line can differ from the positions

The portfolio line is the return the Dashboard measures, the time-weighted return, not the profit of your positions on the capital they employed. The two can therefore differ, even when every position is ticked; a sentence under the chart says so. On the days your portfolio is worth zero or less there is no time-weighted return, so the portfolio line has a gap in % (When No TWRR Is Shown).

docs.title: 💸 Yield on Cost (YOC)
docs.text:
How much income does each unit pay you, compared with what it cost? YOC compares the dividends and interest each unit received over the last 365 days with its average purchase price.

How to read it

  • One value per asset and broker, over the year that ends on the end date: moving the start date does not change it.
  • Gross, not after tax: separate tax and fee transactions are not subtracted.
  • Hover a value for the income per unit, the period and the exchange rates used — each payment at its own date's rate.
  • 0.00% means income recorded at zero, or corrections that exactly cancel it; a plain - means no income in the last year.

🔗 Theory: Yield on Cost — the exact rules, and how YOC differs from dividend yield or CAGR

🚦 A dash with an ⓘ icon — when YOC is unavailable

LibreFolio shows no partial YOC. When an input fails, hover the amber ⓘ for the reason: less than a year of history at this broker and no income yet, a payment with no units held the day before, a purchase, sale, transfer or split history that does not add up, a missing exchange rate, or an unknown average price. Once that is fixed, YOC is computed again. A dash also appears when corrections recorded in the last year — older negative dividend or interest rows — add up to more than the income itself: the ⓘ then reads Corrections exceed the income of the last year.

docs.title: 📈 Period — what each position earned
docs.text:
Which positions made or lost money in the period, and how? Period lists every position of the period, open or closed since, the biggest movers first. LibreFolio computes it the first time you open it, so it can take a moment.

Metrics shown

  • Period P&L, split as on the Period P&L card into Unrealized change, Sales, Dividends & interest and Costs → Period P&L
  • Annualized — the period result as a yearly rate, over the time the position was held in the period; — for a position closed in the period after fewer than 30 days held in it, too short for a yearly rate to mean anything → Net Annualized Return
  • Δ1 / Δ1% for open positions and, hidden by default, Start Value, End Value, Oldest open lot and Status
  • Other Period Effects — what belongs to no position: Unallocated income and Unallocated costs, recorded without an asset; FX on cash, what the exchange rates did in the period to cash you hold in another currency, with a row only for a broker whose cash they moved; Transfers at market value, when you look at only some of your brokers, the gain that securities moved to or from a broker outside your selection made before crossing the boundary, one row per broker (Transfers at market value); and the Other / reconciliation residual, what is left — a currency exchanged at a cost, the exchange-rate move of cash on its way between two of your brokers, securities on their way between them on the first or last day of the period, a sale left out of Sales because a rate or a purchase cost is missing, or the purchase cost of a tiny leftover — 0.00001 units or fewer, which a sale of almost every unit can leave and which does not count as a holding → FX on cash

How to read it

  • Closed positions are in italics, or carry a Closed badge in the chart; to list one kind only, show Status and filter it.
  • In the Map, gains stack right of zero and losses left, the net result closing the row; each percentage compares with the position's start value.
  • A position's Period P&L can differ from its lifetime gain: only the period counts.
  • Start Value and End Value are worked out as the Value in Portfolio — same prices, an asset with no price at what it cost you, each day's exchange rate — so the rows plus the Other Period Effects add up to the Period P&L card. A — in Unrealized change means a value could not be computed, such as a missing exchange rate or purchase cost: it is not a zero.
  • Securities moved between two of your brokers during the period split their result: the sending broker's row keeps what they did until they arrived, the receiving broker's what they did after; the total does not change.
🙈 Hide amounts — what the chart still shows

With Hide amounts on (the eye button in the top bar), the chart's amounts and axis turn into •••, as in +€•••. Signs, currencies, percentages, bar lengths and colours stay, so you still see who gained or lost, and how much compared with the others. See Privacy mode.

docs.title: 🔬 FIFO Lots Analysis
docs.text:
Which purchases make up a position, where are they held, and how has each one done? The FIFO Lots Analysis answers lot by lot: each purchase opens a lot, and each sale closes the oldest open lots first — First-In, First-Out.

Choose Analyze Lots on a position and the panel opens, for the brokers of the page: your broker filter on the Dashboard, the broker itself on its own page. On the Dashboard, as on a broker's page, it opens below the positions: the positions table and the return chart stay on screen. View Asset (↗) opens the asset; ✕ closes the panel, and so does the browser's back button.

How the blocks work together

  • One selection: click bubbles, bars or table rows to pick lots; with none picked, every visible lot counts. Open / Closed, on the timeline, filters every block.
  • Double-click to jump: from a chart marker to the lots of that transaction, from a timeline bar to its table row, and back.
  • Full broker amounts: on a broker you co-own, your share is not applied here, unlike the KPI cards and Holdings.

🔗 Theory: FIFO Engine · FIFO Lot Analysis · FIFO matching · Taxation

docs.title: 💹 1. Avg. Cost / Market Price
docs.text:
How does the price compare with what you paid, and where does each lot stand?

Metrics shown

  • Market Price — dashed where LibreFolio estimates it from your last trade → Valuation Price Chain
  • Avg. Cost — one line per broker, and a dashed Combined line when the asset sits at several → Weighted Average Cost
  • Bubbles — one per long lot, at its total return, among the markers of your transactions and payments → FIFO Lot Analysis

How to read it

  • Abs / % shows prices or their change from the first point; Auto / From 0 sets where the axis starts.
  • Bubble colour is the opening broker, its size the lot's quantity (Abs) or its opening value (%); a dashed border means valued at cost.
  • A gap in an Avg. Cost line is a day whose average cost is unknown: no wrong average is drawn.
  • The Market Price line covers the whole period, days without an open lot included: after you sell everything, it runs on to the end date.

docs.title: 🕒 2. Lot Life & Custody
docs.text:
When was each lot open, and which broker held it?

Metrics shown

  • Bars — one per lot, coloured by the broker holding it and as thick as the quantity held; dashed violet while in transit, with a lane per broker after a transfer → FIFO Engine

How to read it

  • Open / Closed keeps only open lots, only closed ones, or both.
  • A thinner bar lost part of its quantity, for example to a partial sale.
  • Click a bar to select its lot, double-click it to find its row in the table.
  • The markers on a bar are the lot's events: ▲ purchase, ▼ sale, ◆ transfer, + adjustment in, × adjustment out and │ split. Hover a marker, tap it or reach it with the keyboard to see what happened, the date, the quantity (hidden as ••• in privacy mode) and the broker: a transfer between your brokers reads From and To, one with a broker outside the panel names only the broker you are looking at, and a point where several events fall on the same day lists them all. Click or double-click a marker as you would its bar.

docs.title: 📋 3. Lots Table
docs.text:
Every lot with its figures, following the panel's filter and selection.

Metrics shown

  • Opening Date, Total P&L, Total return, Annualized, Current Value, Open Quantity and Custody, with a Totals row → FIFO Lot Analysis
  • Income when a lot received some, and Fees, Taxes, Net P&L and Net return when a lot bears costs → Costs & Net Metrics

How to read it

  • Click a row to select it, double-click to find it in the timeline; the row colour is the opening broker.
  • The ⋮ menu offers View lot detail, Go to lot in Gantt, Go to opening transaction and Copy lot identifier — a stable reference, handy for support.
  • More columns, such as Opening Value, wait behind the eye icon.

docs.title: 💰 4. Value / Return Comparison
docs.text:
What are the selected lots worth, and what have they earned since opening? With none selected, the chart covers every visible lot.

Metrics shown

  • Value — Residual value, Sale proceeds and Cumulative income stacked up to the Comprehensive value, against the Opening value → FIFO Lot Analysis
  • Return — the result since opening, in money (Abs) or percent (%): an Aggregate return, plus a line per lot when you compare several

How to read it

  • Comprehensive value above Opening value: the lots gained, sales and income included.
  • A dashed line in Value means a lot's current value is estimated at cost: its asset has no price at all — no market price, no purchase or sale, and no transfer whose cost counts as its price up to the end date.
  • A flat start: until the asset's first price — market price, purchase or sale, or the cost of a transfer that brought it in before anything else — a lot, for example one you received through an adjustment, is valued at what it cost you, with no gain or loss. A day whose price has no exchange rate is left out instead.

docs.title: 🧾 5. Lot Detail
docs.text:
The whole story of one lot. Open it with View lot detail (⋮) or by clicking its Custody cell.

Metrics shown

  • Summary — opening and current value, proceeds, FIFO P&L, Total P&L, Total return, and Cash yield when the lot received income → FIFO Lot Analysis
  • Net breakdown — the total P&L minus the fees and taxes allocated to the lot → Costs & Net Metrics
  • Current Custody and History — where the lot is now, and every event since its opening. A transfer between two of your brokers reads as two rows, A → In transit and In transit → B, even when the units leave and arrive on the same day

How to read it

  • Quantities are the broker's full holdings, as the ⓘ beside them says.
  • A transfer with a broker outside the panel counts as units coming in or going out. Units received open a new lot on the day they arrive, at the cost the transfer carries. Units sent close their lots on the day they leave, at that day's market price, so the gain they made at this broker counts as realized here. The lot's History labels these moves TRANSFER+ and TRANSFER-, and the charts mark them as transfers — ◆ on Lot Life & Custody, Transfer In and Transfer Out on the markers of Avg. Cost / Market Price — without naming the other broker. To follow the original lots through the move, open the panel with both brokers (no broker filter on the Dashboard). A transfer still on its way on the panel's last day shows its units as in transit.
  • Go to transaction opens the transaction of the History row you picked — by default, the opening one.
⚠️ When the panel warns you
  • A folded banner lists what is missing — a rate, a price, a purchase cost — with a chip per affected lot that finds its bubble. Fix it as for the Data Quality banner. The folded banner also lists income and costs that no lot could take — a dividend paid after every lot was sold, for example — each with its own amount and date.
  • A red message means the quantities or transfers of some of the asset's transactions do not add up, so its lots cannot be rebuilt. It lists each transaction to fix with its day, its broker, what is wrong and a Go to transaction button. Meanwhile the panel hides the lots, their timeline and the comparison, and the first chart keeps only its Avg. Cost lines and the Market Price. Fix those transactions and the lots come back.
  • Valued at cost: on the days before the asset's first price — no market price, no purchase or sale, no transfer whose cost counts as its price — its lots are valued at what they cost, with no market gain or loss, and the banner names those days. With no price at all up to the end date, the lot's bubble has a dashed border.
