docs.title: 🛡️ Risk Tab
docs.text:
The Risk tab of the Dashboard shows how risky your portfolio is, through four plain questions — from what really happened to what could happen. It sits between Positions & Analysis and Transactions, and every broker's page has the same tab for that broker alone.

Each block below follows one pattern: what it answers, a screenshot, its tools and how to read them.

  • 📉 How Much Can It Hurt? — the losses your portfolio actually went through
  • 🧩 Am I as Diversified as I Think? — which holdings carry the risk, and which move together
  • ⚖️ Am I Being Paid for This Risk? — return against risk, holding by holding and against a benchmark
  • 🔮 What If…? — a past crisis, a shock you choose, or a simulation
  • 🚩 Notices and Missing Data — what the data lacked, and what to do about it

docs.title: 📉 How Much Can It Hurt?
docs.text:
How much could you lose, and how bad has it already been? Every figure here is something your portfolio really went through in the period; deposits and withdrawals do not count as gains or losses.

Tools shown

  • A bad day, Thirty bad days — your average loss on the worst 5% of days, or of 30-day stretches → Conditional Value at Risk
  • VaR threshold — on Distribution of daily returns: the daily loss that only the worst 5% of days went beyond; a dashed line marks it on the chart, and hovering a bar tells how many days fell in it and whether it lies beyond the threshold; the wheel or two fingers zoom into the chart, and with many bars a slider appears under it → Value at Risk
  • The worst day — under A bad day: the single worst day of the period, and when it was → Worst Realization
  • The worst 30 days — under Thirty bad days: the worst 30-day stretch the portfolio really went through, and when it was. Thirty bad days itself is an average of the worst 5%, which no single stretch ever printed
  • The worst fall — the deepest drop from a high to a later low, when it began and ended, and how long it lasted → Max Drawdown
  • Drawdown at risk — how far below its peak the portfolio stood, its worst 5% of days aside → Drawdown at Risk
  • Average beyond the threshold — how far below its peak it stood, on average, on those worst days → Conditional Drawdown at Risk
  • Below the peak, today — how far below its last high the portfolio stands today → Current Drawdown
  • Ulcer index — under The worst fall, beside Drawdown at risk: how deep and how long the falls were; lower is calmer → Ulcer Index

How to read it

  • Different horizons: the cards go from a day to a month to the worst fall, so never add them up.
  • The amount beside each percentage is that loss applied to your net worth.
  • Every card has the same shape: a title and a subtitle, the percentage with its amount, then detail rows with the name on the left and the figure on the right. A date is written the way your language writes it.
  • Below the peak, today appears only while your portfolio is below its last high.
  • The ? and ⓘ icons next to a figure open its theory page.

docs.title: 🧩 Am I as Diversified as I Think?
docs.text:
Owning many holdings is not the same as being diversified. This block shows which holdings really carry your risk, and which move together so closely that they are the same bet.

Tools shown

  • How many independent bets do I really hold? — the effective number of positions: how evenly your money is spread; above the count of positions, the excess comes from the part that is not covered (cash and holdings without prices) → Concentration
  • Did spreading the money achieve anything? — how much your holdings cushion each other: 1 means no benefit, higher means more, up to about √N for N positions → Concentration
  • How much of me is not measured here? — cash, plus holdings without usable prices → Data Quality
  • Weight and risk contribution — each holding's share of your money, and of your risk → Risk Contribution
  • Which of these are the same bet? — how closely each pair of holdings moves together → Correlation

How to read it

  • A long red bar to the right marks a holding that carries more of your risk than its weight suggests; when one stands out, the sentence under the title names it.
  • In the matrix, blue pairs move together, so holding both adds little; red pairs move in opposite directions and cushion each other.
  • Hover a square for its value in words. The lists The most alike and The ones that offset pick out the pairs worth a look.

docs.title: ⚖️ Am I Being Paid for This Risk?
docs.text:
Risk is worth taking only if it pays. This block sets the return of your portfolio and of each holding against its swings — in a table and in a chart — and, if you choose one, against a benchmark.

Tools shown

  • Volatility — how much the returns swing over a year → Volatility
  • Ann. return — the average return, scaled to a year → Observed Annualization
  • Sortino — the return earned for each unit of downward swings → Sortino Ratio
  • Sharpe — the return earned for each unit of swings, up or down → Sharpe Ratio
  • Beta — how much a holding moves when the benchmark moves → Beta & Active Return
  • Correlation — how closely a holding moves with the benchmark → Correlation
  • Compared with and the dashed line — your benchmark, and the line between better and worse paid → Benchmark Selection

How to read it

  • Choose a benchmark in Compared with — a tracker of a broad world index is the most meaningful. It applies to every Risk page, and adds the Beta and Correlation columns.
  • Above the dashed line, a dot was better paid for its risk than the benchmark — or, with no benchmark, than your portfolio.
  • Click a column title to sort the table, or a row to find its dot in the chart.
  • The Portfolio row replays today's holdings, at today's weights, over the period — the title says on the current composition — so it is not the history of your trades. Returns come from prices only, without dividends or coupons for now.

docs.title: 🔮 What If…?
docs.text:
What would a past crisis, or a shock you imagine, do to the portfolio you hold today — and what could lie ahead? The block starts closed: click its title to open it.

Tools shown

  • Historical replay — a real past period, applied to your portfolio as it is today → Historical Replay
  • Hypothetical shock — a fall or a rise you assume for each asset class, sector or region → Hypothetical Shock
  • Simulation — a range of possible futures, built from your own history → Simulation Modes

How to read it

  • Add a tool with the Add: buttons; its × closes it and drops its result. The tools you leave open come back next time, in this browser.
  • Historical replay: pick a crisis in Preset, or your own Period, then Run replay. Holdings with no prices for that period are left out, and a button may offer a period in which they all have prices.
  • Hypothetical shock: click a scenario, such as Equity crash, to run it; Show the shock per bucket lets you change its assumptions.
  • Simulation: pick a mode — Reshuffled history is recommended — and a horizon, in days or as years, months and days (2y3m5d), then Simulate. Read the cone as a range of possibilities, not a forecast.

The simulation is still in beta

Its outcome depends heavily on how much history the period holds compared with the horizon — see Why the Simulation Is Still in Beta.

docs.title: 🚩 Notices and Missing Data
docs.text:
A risk figure is only as good as the prices behind it. When data is missing or old, the tab says so, and what that changed.

Tools shown

  • Data quality — missing or old prices and rates, and the holdings they leave out → Data Quality

How to read it

  • The banner at the top lists missing or old prices and exchange rates: fix them with its buttons, or with Sync at the top right.
  • A currency pair with no exchange-rate route gets its own button in the banner, one per pair (tooltip Add FX pair): it opens the Add New Currency Pair window right there, already filled in with that pair, and the tab recalculates by itself once the pair is saved and its rates are downloaded → Adding a Currency Pair
  • The notice above the blocks says which results are partial, and why.
  • A banner inside a block names a figure that could not be computed, with the reason.
  • A dash (—) means a figure could not be measured: it never means zero.
  • To try again, press Refresh, or run the What If…? tool again.

docs.title: 🔎 Good to Know
docs.text:
• The Dashboard's tab covers your whole portfolio — every broker you own with a share above 0% — over the Dashboard's date range and currency. It ignores the broker filter: a subtitle says so, and the amounts under the percentages are hidden while a filter is on.
  • On a broker's page, the tab shows the same blocks for that broker alone.
  • Changing the period or the currency recalculates every block and clears the What If…? results: run them again.
  • Calculation details, folded at the bottom of each block, shows how much data the figures rest on.

docs.title: 🔗 Related
docs.text:
• 🧪 Correlation Tab — the same questions, asked of a selection of assets you choose
  • 📚 Risk Metrics — the theory behind every figure; each block's book icon opens it
  • 📊 Dashboard — the other tabs, the date range, the currency and the broker filter
  • 🏦 Brokers — each broker's page, with its own Risk tab
  • 🛠️ Technical details — for developers: how this tab works inside

docs.title: 📁 Files & Uploads
docs.text:
The Files page keeps everything uploaded to LibreFolio, in two tabs:

  • Static Resources — avatars, broker icons and other images or documents, each one shared with every user or personal to whoever uploaded it;
  • Broker Reports — the statement files you import transactions from, visible only to the people with access to their broker.

Administrators also see a third tab, Backups, and a bar with the space the instance takes.

docs.title: 🖼️ Static resources
docs.text:
Here you find the users' avatars, the brokers' icons and the images and documents uploaded by users: the shared ones, which everyone with a LibreFolio account can see, and your personal ones, which only you and the administrators can see (see Shared or personal).

  • Switch between list and grid view: the grid previews images.
  • In the list, right-click a file for Preview, Copy Link, Download or Delete. You can delete only the files you uploaded, so Delete appears only on them; an administrator can delete any. Tick several files to delete them together: the files of other users stay in place, and a notice tells you so.
  • Preview shows a PDF in a read-only viewer: you can read it, search it and copy its text, but not edit, annotate or print it; to keep the file, use Download. A password-protected PDF asks for its password, which stays in your browser: it is never sent to the server or saved, and it is gone once the preview closes.

docs.title: ⬆️ Upload a file
docs.text:
1. Click Upload, then drop files on the area or click it to browse.
  2. Before uploading, you can click ✏️ Edit on an image to crop it with the Image Crop tool, then confirm with Crop; on any other file, ✏️ Rename changes its name. Restore original puts a file back as you picked it.
  3. Click Upload. The files are personal: only you and the administrators see them, until you share them.

docs.title: 👥 Shared or personal
docs.text:
Every static resource is Shared or Personal, as its badge in the Visibility column of the list shows:

  • Shared — every signed-in user can see it;
  • Personal — only the person who uploaded it and the administrators can see it. The other users do not find it in their list, and cannot open, preview or download it.

A file you upload is:

  • personal when you upload it from this page;
  • shared when you upload it from an image picker (your profile picture, in Profile or on the Welcome page; a broker icon; an asset icon), because the other users see the picture where you use it.

Files uploaded with an older version of LibreFolio are shared if they are images, personal otherwise.

You can change the visibility of the files you uploaded; an administrator, of any file:

  • in the list, right-click the file: a personal file offers Share with everyone, a shared one Make personal;
  • in the grid, use the same switch on the file's card: 👥 shares it, 🔒 makes it personal.

Sharing is immediate. Make personal asks you to confirm first: the other users lose the file, also where it shows as an icon or a photo.

The Visibility filter, in the column header, keeps only the shared or only the personal files. Like the Uploaded by filter, it also applies to the grid view and is saved in the page address.

An image picker's Existing tab lists the shared images and your own personal ones, even for an administrator. Picking one of your personal images there makes it shared, and a notice tells you so: the other users can then see it where you used it.

docs.title: 📊 Broker Reports
docs.text:
These are the statements exported by your brokers, waiting to be imported or already imported. You see the reports of every broker you can access, as Owner, Editor or Viewer. The reports an older version of LibreFolio stored without a broker appear only here: to the administrators, and to the person who uploaded them when LibreFolio recorded who did.

The Status column tells you where each file stands:

  • Uploaded — stored, not analysed yet;
  • Parsed — the Import Wizard read it successfully;
  • Failed — the analysis failed; the file stays here so you can check it or report it.

docs.title: 📤 Upload a broker report
docs.text:
1. On Broker Reports, click Upload and pick CSV or Excel files.
  2. In Assign Brokers, choose the broker of each file, or one for all with Assign all to. Create new adds a broker on the spot; if you can edit only one broker, it is already chosen.
  3. Click Upload. The files are stored, but nothing is imported yet.

To import them, open the Import Wizard (Transactions → Import): its Select Files step lists the reports you have uploaded.

The broker you choose only decides which account receives the transactions. The importer recognises the file format by itself, and one import plugin can read the exports of several brokers.

docs.title: ⚙️ Manage reports
docs.text: Right-click a report for Preview, Download or Delete, or tick several to delete them together. Delete appears only on the reports you may delete, and deleting several leaves the others in place, with a notice. Deleting a report never deletes the transactions already imported from it.

docs.title: 🧩 Report sets
docs.text:
Some banks split one account across several exports: Danske Bank, for example, needs a securities export and a cash statement. The exports of such a bank that you upload together form a report set, and LibreFolio imports them as one, through a combined file it builds from them. The Report set column tells you where each file stands (the same column appears in a broker's Uploaded Reports):

Badge Meaning Set of ‹date› The file belongs to the set uploaded on that date, together with the other exports of the set. Incomplete The set still lacks a required export: hover the badge to see which one. Add it from the set's card in the Import Wizard, with Upload the missing file. Combined The file LibreFolio built from the exports of a set — the one the import actually reads. Hover the badge to see the files it was built from, and which of them have been deleted since. Used in a combined file This export went into a combined file of its set. To re-combine The importer has changed since the combined file was built: analysing the set again rebuilds it.

You can preview, download and delete these files like any other report. Deleting one export of a set leaves its combined file in place, but to import the set again you first need to upload that export into it again.

docs.title: 👤 Who uploaded each file
docs.text:
Both tabs show who uploaded each file in the Uploaded by column, with the person's avatar and name:

  • click the column header to sort by uploader;
  • open its filter to keep only the files of one or more people: tick them in the list, or search them by name;
  • a file whose uploader was not recorded shows Uploader not recorded.

The filter also applies to the grid view of Static Resources. It is saved in the page address, so a bookmark or a shared link opens with the same filter.

docs.title: 🛠️ For Administrators
docs.text: Only administrators see what follows; other users find neither on the page.

docs.title: 📊 The space used
docs.text: Above the tabs, a bar shows how much room the instance takes, split into the database, the uploaded files, the broker reports, the backups and the other LibreFolio files. With no limit set it is drawn against the disk, with the other files of the disk in grey; with a limit, against that limit. Under the bar, in the closed Advanced panel, you set LibreFolio total space (MB), 0 for no limit; the same field is in the Global Settings of an administrator. Past the limit the bar warns you, and LibreFolio refuses a new file or report that would add to it, saying how much to raise the total space to; nothing is deleted. The bar reads again with Refresh. How to read it, and what sets the limit: The Space Bar.

docs.title: 🗃️ The Backups tab
docs.text: The Backups tab lists the backups LibreFolio keeps on the server, with their date, origin, type and size. For each one you can Download or Delete it. The same list is in Settings › Administration › Backup, where you also set the automatic clean-up: see Backups Kept on the Server.

docs.title: 🔒 Access and limits
docs.text:
• 🌐 Static resources — every signed-in user can see the shared ones; a personal file, only the person who uploaded it and the administrators (see Shared or personal). Deleting a file and changing its visibility belong to whoever uploaded it, and to an administrator.
  • 🔐 Broker reports — only the users with access to the broker can see them; uploading and deleting need Owner or Editor access. An administrator can see and delete every report.
  • 📏 Size — up to the limit the administrator sets in Global Settings: 10 MB unless changed.
  • 🚫 File types — programs and scripts (such as .exe, .sh or .py files) are refused as static resources; broker reports must be CSV or Excel files.

Where the files live on the server is described in Filesystem Structure.

docs.title: ➕ Adding a Currency Pair
docs.text:
A pair tells LibreFolio where the rate between two currencies comes from: a central bank provider, a chain of providers, or rates you enter yourself.

Click Add Pair on the FX page. The same window opens from the Dashboard, from an asset page and from the FX step of the PAC allocator.

docs.title: 🧭 Add a pair step by step
💱 Step 1: Pick the two currencies
docs.text: In Add New Currency Pair, choose the Base Currency and the Quote Currency. Each list hides the currencies already paired with the other one, so a pair cannot be added twice.

docs.title: 🛤️ Step 2: Choose a route
docs.text:
Click Add conversion route to see every way the providers can produce this rate:

  • 🔗 Direct conversion (1 step) — one provider publishes the pair;
  • 🔀 Chain conversion — steps through other currencies, grouped by number of steps;
  • 🚫 Not usable — providers that cannot reach this pair.

Filter with the search box (provider, currency or country), then click a route to add it.

🛟 Backup routes — when you add more than one

LibreFolio uses route #1 first and tries #2 if it fails during a sync, and so on. Drag the routes to reorder them; 🗑️ removes one, and ⚠️ shows a note from its provider.

🔀 Also create intermediate pairs — when you pick a chain route

Tick Also create intermediate pairs to save each step as a pair of its own. You can then sync each step separately and convert into the intermediate currency too: a chain stores only the rate of its own pair.

✏️ No route — manual rates only

You can save without a route, then enter the rates yourself in the pair's Data Editor.

docs.title: 💾 Step 3: Save
docs.text:
Click Save Configuration; the window closes right away.

  • With a provider, LibreFolio downloads the pair's whole history up to today, whatever period the page shows, intermediate pairs included. A message reports the result, in green only if everything worked.
  • Without a provider, a message confirms that the pair was created.

Click the pair's name in the message to open its page.

docs.title: 🛤️ Direct and chain routes
docs.text:
A direct route uses one provider that publishes both currencies, such as the ECB for EUR 🇪🇺 / USD 🇺🇸. When no central bank publishes the pair, a chain route multiplies the rates of its steps. RON 🇷🇴 / USD 🇺🇸, for example, goes RON → EUR → USD, both steps from the ECB, which publishes EUR/RON and EUR/USD:

\[ r_{\text{RON}\to\text{USD}} = r_{\text{RON}\to\text{EUR}} \times r_{\text{EUR}\to\text{USD}} \]
  • A chain has a rate only on the days when every step has one.
  • If one step fails during a sync, the whole chain fails: shorter chains are more reliable.
  • A chain rate can differ slightly from a direct market quote.

docs.title: 🔗 Related
docs.text:
• 🔄 Synchronization — Download rates again later
  • 🔌 Provider Config — Change a pair's routes after creating it
  • 🧑‍💻 For developers: FX Configuration & Routing and FX Chain Algorithm

docs.title: ⚙️ Chart Settings
docs.text: The Chart Settings window changes how charts look and which overlays they draw. It serves both the FX list and the Assets list, and each list keeps its own settings: changing the FX charts never touches the asset charts.

docs.title: 🔓 Open chart settings
docs.text:
• 🌐 For all charts — click Settings (⚙️) in the list toolbar. The window is titled Chart Settings. Applying it replaces the custom settings of every chart in the list, detail pages included, and the window warns you about it.
  • 🎯 For one chart — click ⚙️ on a card. The window is titled Chart Settings (Local), and its settings apply to that chart only.

Detail pages use inline panels

On a pair detail page (and on an asset detail page), ⚙️ on the chart opens the same appearance settings in a panel, and the Signals panel above the chart holds the overlays. They are the same settings as the card's local ones.

docs.title: 👀 Preview before you apply
docs.text:
The window shows a preview chart with a view selector. It is the chart's saved view, and Apply saves it: Abs, % or Rolling Return. It is the same chart as on the pair and asset detail pages, only taller than a card's chart: a line (no candlesticks), without the toolbar, event markers or measure tool, and you can zoom it with the mouse wheel like on the detail page. It draws with the look and the axis ranges you are editing, and a comparison signal shows its asset's icon and type in the tooltip. Your charts change only when you click Apply; Cancel asks before discarding your changes.

  • 🌐 For all charts, the preview draws a demo curve. The server computes the indicators on it, so they look exactly as they will on your real charts.
  • 🎯 For one chart, the preview uses that chart's real data. Indicators show the last applied settings until you click Apply, and a banner reminds you of it.

A signal looks the same in the preview as on the card, so what you see here is what the card draws after Apply.

docs.title: 🔁 Rolling Return view
docs.text: On Rolling Return the preview draws the rolling return of the rate or of the asset, with the rolling returns of its comparisons. For one chart it uses the card's real data and, on an FX chart, the FX pairs compared on it; for all charts it draws a demo curve. Two more controls choose the window: 1W, 1M, 3M, 1Y or a custom amount. Until you choose one, the window is automatic: the largest preset that fits the period shown in the list. The Signals list shows only the comparisons this view draws, with another FX pair on an FX chart and with another asset on an asset chart; technical indicators and benchmarks stay saved but are hidden until you switch the preview back to Abs or %.

docs.title: 🎨 Appearance
docs.text: Setting What it does Baseline Colors Green above, red below the start of the period, with a dashed baseline. It applies to the cards in the lists, the detail pages and the preview Area Fill Gradient under the line Grid Lines Horizontal dashed grid Stale Gradient Fades the days without a new value, which repeat an earlier one

docs.title: 📏 Axis ranges
docs.text:
Y-Axis Scale has one row for each axis on the chart: the main axis (the rate, or the percentage in % view) and one for each indicator scale, such as the RSI axis. Indicators that share a scale share a row.

  • Auto fits the data on that axis.
  • Include 0 fits the data and also shows zero.
  • Custom uses the Min and Max you type.

The Abs and % views keep separate ranges: switch the preview to % to set the percentage one.

docs.title: 📈 Overlay signals
docs.text:
Add overlays from three dropdowns, the same as in the detail page's Signals panel:

  • 🧮 Technical Indicators — 10 indicators work on FX rates (asset charts offer more), grouped by family with a search box. The math is in Technical Indicators — Financial Theory.
  • ↔️ Data Comparison — another FX pair or an asset on the same chart. On an FX card the line of an asset is its price in the asset's own currency, with no conversion, exactly as the pair detail page draws it: read it in the % view, where it starts at its own first value like the rate. In Abs it sits on the rate's axis. The list loads the daily prices of the compared assets once for all cards, and asks nothing when no card compares an asset. In the window opened for all charts a comparison with an asset is not drawn, because the demo curve has no real asset to compare with (as in the Assets list). An asset is picked in the same panel as the risk comparison's: a search box, Type and Currency filters, each row showing the asset's icon, name, type and currency, and the benchmarks listed first; one click chooses and closes. The chart's own asset is greyed out, and one that another comparison already uses carries a warning mark but can still be chosen.
  • 📐 Synthetic Benchmarks — reference curves built from parameters alone, not market data: Linear, Compound and Sine Wave.

Each signal becomes a card with its parameters, a 📖 link to its theory page and, once computed, a diagnostics icon.

docs.title: 💾 Where settings are saved
docs.text:
• Chart settings are saved in this browser, for your user, separately for the FX and asset lists. A chart's own settings sit on top of its list's settings.
  • They are not stored on the server: another browser or device starts from the defaults, and clearing this site's browser data resets them.
  • The selected period is not a chart setting: the pages of the same browser tab share it.

docs.title: 💱 FX Rates (Currency Exchange)
docs.text: LibreFolio converts your amounts between currencies with the rates kept here. Each currency pair downloads its rates from a central bank (ECB, FED, BOE or SNB), or holds rates you enter yourself.

docs.title: 📋 The FX list page
docs.text:
Open FX Rates from the sidebar to see your currency pairs:

Each pair shows its flags (e.g. 🇪🇺 EUR → 🇺🇸 USD), its latest rate, the change over the selected period and a mini chart. When the chart groups the rates by week or month because the plot is too narrow for so many days, a Weekly or Monthly badge at its top left says so, like on the detail page. A ✏️ Manual badge marks pairs without a provider. Click a pair to open its detail page.

docs.title: 🔀 Cards or table
docs.text:
• The view toggle next to Add Pair switches between cards and table; LibreFolio remembers your choice.
  • In the table, the Δ columns show the change over the last day, over the period and, on long periods, over 1W to 5Y. Columns adds hidden ones, such as each pair's Providers.
  • Select rows to act on several pairs at once, or right-click a row.

docs.title: 🔍 Filter by currency
docs.text: Pick a currency in Filter currency to list only its pairs, and a Second currency to narrow the list to one pair; ✕ clears both.

docs.title: 🧰 Page and pair actions
docs.text:
• The period picker at the top sets the range of every chart and change; in card view, the chart-line icon (tooltip Show absolute), % and the calendar icon (Rolling Return) show all cards as rates, as % change or as rolling return. The list opens on Abs; once you choose a view, it is remembered for you in this browser.
  • A card's view button cycles % → Rolling Return → Abs and shows the view it goes to. The card keeps its own choice across reloads until you change the toolbar, which resets every card. On Rolling Return a card draws the rolling return of the rate the way the card shows the pair (flipped with ⇄: the return of the flipped rate), and over it the rolling returns of the FX pairs compared on that card. The rate and its change at the top stay as they are, and with too little history the card shows a short message instead of the chart. The window is the one set in Chart Settings.
  • A card draws the comparisons saved in its Chart Settings, with another FX pair or with an asset. The line of an asset is its price in the asset's own currency, so compare it in the % view; the prices load once for all the cards that compare an asset.
  • Sync All downloads new rates (Synchronization); Reload All reads the stored ones again. Settings sets the look of every card (Chart Settings). Hover over any of the three for half a second to read what it does.
  • On a card, ⇄ flips the direction shown (USD → EUR instead of EUR → USD); the buttons at the bottom open its own chart settings, Sync or Reload it, or delete it.

Deleting a pair deletes its rates

Deleting a pair removes its provider settings and all its stored rates, once you confirm.

docs.title: 🔮 What's next?
docs.text:
• ➕ Adding a Pair — Create a pair with a direct or chain route
  • 🔄 Synchronization — Download rates, by hand or on a schedule
  • 📊 Pair Detail Page — Chart, signals, measures, rate editor and providers
  • ⚙️ Chart Settings — Chart look and overlay signals
  • 🔌 Providers — The central banks LibreFolio reads (ECB, FED, BOE, SNB)

docs.title: 🔄 FX Synchronization
docs.text: Pairs with a provider get their rates from official central bank sources. LibreFolio downloads them when you add a pair, whenever you ask, and — if your administrator turned it on — on a schedule.

docs.title: 🔄 Sync all pairs
docs.text:
1. On the FX page, choose the period in the date picker. Pick All for the whole history.
  2. Click Sync All. The Sync FX Rates window lists every pair with a provider: pairs with manual rates only have nothing to download.
  3. Click Start Sync.

docs.title: 📊 Reading the results
docs.text:
• Each row shows a pair, the provider that answered, ↓ the rates downloaded and Δ the rates that were new or changed.
  • An amber row means the provider sent no rates for the period; a red row means the sync failed. Hover the message to read it in full, and click the row's ↻ button to try that pair again.
  • The summary at the bottom shows how many pairs synced and the totals. Retry N failed runs every failed pair again.
  • A long history can need more time: if the window reports Request timed out, raise its Timeout, then click Retry N failed.

docs.title: 🎯 Sync one pair
docs.text:
• On the FX page, the Sync button of a pair's card, or of a table row, downloads that pair's rates for the selected period. A message reports the result.
  • On the pair's detail page, Sync opens the sync window for the pair and for any pair or asset you compare it with on the chart.

Sync is greyed out for pairs with manual rates only.

docs.title: ⚠️ What a sync changes
docs.text:
• Dates of the period that are already stored take the provider's value; missing dates are added. Before you start, the window warns when the period already holds stored rates, and for how many of its pairs.
  • Dates outside the period are left untouched.
  • If a pair's first route fails, LibreFolio tries the next one: see Provider Config.

The provider has the last word

A sync overwrites the rates you edited by hand within its period. To keep your own rates, use a pair without a provider (manual rates only).

🕰️ Older history missing — when a pair's chart starts later than expected

A pair you add with a provider downloads its whole history by itself. If an older pair's chart starts later than the provider's history, set the period on the FX page to All and click Sync All once: LibreFolio downloads everything the providers publish, up to today.

docs.title: 🕐 Automatic sync
docs.text: When your administrator turns on the background scheduler, LibreFolio refreshes the recent rates of every pair with a provider on its own, at the times they choose: see Market Data Scheduler.

docs.title: 🔗 Related
docs.text:
• ➕ Adding a Pair — Direct and chain routes
  • 🔌 FX Providers — The central banks LibreFolio reads rates from
  • ⚙️ Provider Config — Routes, priorities and fallbacks of a pair
  • 🧑‍💻 For developers: FX Configuration & Routing

docs.title: 📉 Interactive Chart
docs.text: The heart of the pair detail page: the pair's rate history over the selected period.

docs.title: 🔀 Abs or % view
docs.text:
Switch with Abs / % in the chart's top-left corner; the page opens in % view.

  • 📊 % — the change since the first day of the period. Overlays start from 0 % too, so their moves compare at a glance.
  • 📈 Abs — the rate itself, e.g. 1 EUR = 1.0845 USD.

docs.title: 🔍 Zoom, pan and period
docs.text:
Action Desktop Mobile Zoom Mouse wheel Pinch Pan Click and drag Drag with two fingers (one finger scrolls the page)
  • Period: the presets 1W to 2Y, YTD and All, or Custom (a number of days, weeks, months or years back from today); click the dates to pick them on a calendar. The two ends must be different days: the day you click first cannot be clicked again, and a typed date equal to the other end turns red. More presets appear when the toolbar has room. The pages of the same browser tab share the period.
  • On a long period the chart groups the rates by week or month and shows a Weekly or Monthly badge: zoom in for daily rates.
  • On a narrow screen the axis shows fewer, shorter dates; the first and the last always stay.
📅 History shorter than the period — when the chart starts later

A banner shows the date the data is available from. Sync may fetch older rates, if the provider publishes them; otherwise enter them in the Data Editor.

docs.title: 💬 Tooltip
docs.text:
Hover the chart, or touch it on mobile, to see:

  • 📅 the date (or the week or month, when the chart groups the rates);
  • 💱 the rate and the value of each overlay;
  • 📊 the change since the start of the period: Δ and % in Abs view, % in % view;
  • ⚠️ Stale: N day(s) old on days without a new rate, such as weekends and bank holidays.

docs.title: 🔁 Rolling Return
docs.text:
Two buttons above the chart choose what it draws: Prices (the rate history, as above) and Rolling Return.

In Rolling Return every point answers how much has the rate moved over the last N days? It compares that day's rate with the rate N calendar days earlier. Example: on EUR → USD with the 3M window (90 days), if the rate is 1.0845 today and was 1.0500 ninety days ago, the point reads +3.3 %. Above zero the first currency bought more of the second than N days before; below zero, less.

  • 🗓️ Window — next to the two buttons: 1W, 1M, 3M, 1Y, or Custom (a whole number of weeks, months or years). Until you pick one, the window is automatic: the largest preset that fits the period on screen. The window may be longer than the period: LibreFolio reads the older rates it needs. The ? button opens the same explanation given for assets, and the Chart Settings preview draws this view too.
  • 💱 Compare with another pair — add an FX Pair in the Signals panel: each compared pair draws its own rolling return, with the same window. In this mode the panel offers only these comparisons; your other signals stay saved and come back with Prices.
  • 🔄 Direction — the return follows the direction the page shows, EUR → USD or USD → EUR.
  • 📏 ✏️ Measure and Edit Rates are hidden: they work on the rates, so they belong to Prices.
  • 💾 Remembered — the mode and the window are saved with this pair's chart settings, in this browser. The pair's card in the FX list shares them: a card in Rolling Return opens the page in it, and the page opens again in the mode you left it in. Going back to Prices is immediate.

Changing the period, the window, the direction or the compared pairs, or clicking Refresh, computes the return again, and a spinner shows until the answer arrives. If no return can be computed, the chart shows the reason instead of a curve.

docs.title: 🧰 Chart buttons
docs.text:
• 📏 Measure — see Measures. Prices only.
  • ✏️ Edit Rates — see Data Editor. Prices only.
  • ⚙️ Aesthetics — colours, fill, grid and axis ranges, as in Chart Settings.
  • 📊 The Signals panel above the chart — see Signals.

docs.title: 🔗 Related
docs.text:
• ⚙️ Chart Settings — Chart look and overlay signals
  • 📈 Signals — Technical indicators on the chart

docs.title: ✏️ Data Editor & CSV Import
docs.text: The Data Editor lets you add, change and delete a pair's stored rates one by one, or load many at once from a CSV file. Nothing is saved until you click Save.

docs.title: 📝 Open the editor
docs.text:
Click ✏️ (Edit Rates) on the chart. The editor opens below the chart, and the other panels fold away while you edit.

It lists the rates of the selected period with their Date, Rate and Status (Original, Edited, Deleted or New).

  • A date marked ⚠️ and a number of days has no rate of its own (a weekend or a bank holiday) and repeats the previous one. The ⚠️ switch at the top hides these days.
  • Double-click a point on the chart (long-press on mobile) to jump to its date in the editor.

docs.title: ➕ Add a rate
docs.text: Click Add Row: a row appears on the day after the last one, never later than today. Change its date with the date picker if needed, then type the rate.

docs.title: ✏️ Edit a rate
docs.text: Click a rate and type the new value.

docs.title: 🗑️ Delete rates
docs.text: Click 🗑️ on a row, or select rows and click the bin at the top. Undo brings a row back until you save.

docs.title: 💾 Save your changes
docs.text:
Your changes show on the chart as a purple Preview line. Save (N) writes them all; Cancel drops them. A rate must be greater than zero: a zero, negative or empty one is skipped. A rate the database cannot keep — more than 14 digits before the decimal point, or below 0.0000000001 — is refused when you save and is not stored. The limit applies to the rate as stored: LibreFolio keeps each pair in alphabetical order, so on the USD/EUR page it applies to 1 ÷ the rate you type.

If the server refuses some of your rates, such as a rate too large or too small to store, it saves the others. A warning then names up to five refused dates, each with its reason, and counts the rest; it stays for 20 seconds, so you can note them and enter them again. If it refuses the whole save, for example because a date is after tomorrow, or because none of the rates can be stored, nothing is saved: the message says why, and the editor stays open with your changes.

Synced data overwrites manual edits

A later sync of the same dates replaces your values with the provider's. For full manual control, use a pair without a provider — see Provider Config.

docs.title: 🔓 Open the import window
docs.text:
1. In the editor, click Import CSV.
  2. In Import CSV Data, drop a .csv or .txt file, or paste the text into the box.
  3. Check the direction at the top, then click Import (N).

The rows join the editor: review them, then click Save.

docs.title: 📄 File format
docs.text:
Two columns, with a header row that sets the direction:

date;EUR>USD
2024-01-02;1.1045
2024-01-03;1.0982
2024-01-04;1.0911
Rule Details Separator Semicolon (;) Header date and the direction, e.g. EUR>USD Dates YYYY-MM-DD Rates Positive numbers; . or , as decimal mark, optional _ for thousands (1_000.50)

docs.title: ↔️ Direction
docs.text:
• EUR>USD means 1 EUR = X USD; EUR<USD is the other way round, 1 USD = X EUR.
  • The header must name this pair's two currencies, in either order.
  • The bar at the top shows how the rates are read (Rates interpreted as: 1 EUR = X USD); ⇄ flips it and rewrites the header.
  • A file in the opposite direction to the page is inverted for you: each rate \(r\) becomes \(1/r\).
📋 Examples — the same rates written in both directions 
date;EUR>USD
2024-01-02;1.1045
2024-01-03;1.0982

date;USD>EUR
2024-01-02;0.9053
2024-01-03;0.9106

On the EUR/USD page both files give the same rates: 0.9053 becomes \(1/0.9053 \approx 1.1046\).

docs.title: ⚠️ Common errors
docs.text:
The import window marks each wrong line; only the valid lines are imported.

Message Cause Fix Header currencies don't match Other currencies in the header, e.g. GBP>JPY on the EUR/USD page Use this pair's currencies Expected header or Missing required columns No header row, or a column is missing Start with a line such as date;EUR>USD Invalid date format The date is not YYYY-MM-DD Fix the date Invalid number The rate is not a number Fix the value Duplicate date The same date appears twice Keep one line per date 🔀 How imported rows merge — when the editor already has some of the dates
  • A date already in the editor takes the imported rate (Edited); a new date is added (New). Dates missing from the file stay as they are.
  • Dates outside the selected period are saved too, replacing any rate stored on those days; after saving, the period widens to show them.

docs.title: 🔍 Pair Detail Page
docs.text: Click a pair in the FX list to open its page: a large chart of its rates, with tools to analyse, edit and configure the pair.

docs.title: 🗺️ The page at a glance
docs.text:
• Header — ⇄ swaps the pair's direction and the list card follows (with unsaved changes in the rate editor, LibreFolio asks first); ← goes back to the list.
  • Toolbar — the period, the latest rate with its change, and the AI Export, Providers, Sync and Reload buttons. Reload reads the stored rates again; Sync downloads new ones, see Synchronization.
  • Below — the folded Signals panel, the chart, then the folded Measures panel.

docs.title: 📈 Interactive Chart
docs.text: The rate history, with zoom, pan, an Abs / % view and period presets.

docs.title: 📊 Signals
docs.text: Indicators, comparisons and benchmark curves drawn on the chart; nine indicators work on FX rates.

docs.title: 📐 Measures
docs.text: The change, the change in % and the yearly rate between two points of the chart.

docs.title: ✏️ Data Editor
docs.text: Add, edit or delete single rates, or import many at once from a CSV file.

docs.title: ⚙️ Provider Config
docs.text: Providers changes where the rates come from: the provider, backup routes and chains.

docs.title: 🧠 AI Export
docs.text: AI Export prepares a snapshot of the pair, or an FX Pair Analysis or FX Exposure Impact request, to paste into an AI assistant. FX Exposure Impact counts only the cash and the positions held directly in the pair's currencies: it does not look inside funds. See FX AI Export.

docs.title: 🔗 Related
docs.text:
• ⚙️ Chart Settings — Chart look and overlay signals
  • 📋 FX Overview — Back to the FX list page

docs.title: 📐 Measures
docs.text: The Measures panel tells you how the rate moved between two points of the chart: the change, the change in % and the yearly rate.

docs.title: 📏 Step 1: Turn on measure mode
docs.text: Click 📏 (Add measurement) at the top right of the chart. The Measures panel below the chart opens and reads Active — click chart; over the chart the pointer becomes a crosshair.

docs.title: 📍 Step 2: Click the start point
docs.text: A hint shows the date and rate you picked; a dashed line follows the pointer. A measurement needs two different days: back over the start's day, the line disappears and the pointer shows the not allowed sign (🚫), and a second click there does nothing.

docs.title: 🏁 Step 3: Click the end point
docs.text:
Click a point on another day. The measurement is added and measure mode turns off. The two dates are put in order for you.

➕ The whole period in one click — handy on a phone

The + button on the Measures bar measures the selected period from its first rate to its last, without clicking on the chart.

docs.title: 📊 Read a measurement
docs.text:
Each measurement is a card showing its dates, the change in % and the number of calendar days; you can also set its line's colour and style. Expand it to change the dates, again two different days, and to see Start, End, Δ Abs, Δ % and Δ%/yr for the pair and for each overlay on the same axis.

Δ%/yr is the yearly rate (CAGR), with \(d\) the calendar days between the two dates:

\[ \Delta\%_{yr} = \left(\frac{P_{end}}{P_{start}}\right)^{365/d} - 1 \]

It appears from 30 days on: a shorter span shows —, as everywhere in LibreFolio. A line that starts at 0 shows — for Δ % and Δ%/yr.

See Returns & Growth Rates — Financial Theory for log returns and compounding.

docs.title: 🔁 Several measurements
docs.text: Each new measurement is added next to the others, in its own colour; 🗑️ removes one. They stay until you leave the page.

docs.title: 💡 Tips
docs.text:
• 🔍 Zoom in before clicking, to hit the exact points.
  • 📰 Compare the move before and after an event, such as a central bank announcement.
  • ⚠️ Δ%/yr waits for 30 days because compounding inflates short moves: 1 % in 7 days would read as about 68 % a year.

docs.title: 🔌 Provider Configuration
docs.text: Each currency pair gets its rates from one or more routes: a central bank that quotes the pair directly, or a chain of conversions. Here you see and change the routes of the pair you are viewing.

docs.title: 🔓 How to Access
docs.text: On the pair's detail page, click Providers (🔧) in the toolbar, next to Sync. The Edit Pair Providers window opens.

docs.title: 📋 What You See
docs.text:
Under Conversion Routes, each row is a route, in priority order:

  • the currencies, with the provider of each step between them — hover a provider's icon for its name and description;
  • the priority badge: #1 is used first;
  • ⚠️ when a provider has a data warning, such as the SNB's monthly rates;
  • 🗑️ to remove the route.

docs.title: 🔧 Changing Providers
docs.text:
1. Click Add conversion route and pick a route under Direct conversion (1 step) or Chain conversion. Type in the search box to filter by provider, currency or country.
  2. Drag the rows to set their priority (on a phone, use the up and down arrows).
  3. Click Save Configuration: the next sync uses the new routes.
🔗 Also create intermediate pairs — when you pick a chain route

Tick it to save each step of the chain as a pair of its own, with its provider, so that you can sync and view it on its own.

✍️ No route left — when you remove them all

The pair becomes manual: Sync is disabled, and you enter the rates yourself in the Data Editor.

docs.title: 🔢 Priority & Fallback
docs.text: A sync tries the routes from the top. If one fails — for example, its central bank does not answer — it moves on to the next; the pair fails only when every route does. With EUR/USD set to #1 ECB and #2 FED, a sync that cannot reach the ECB uses the FED rate instead.

docs.title: 📚 Related
docs.text:
• ➕ Adding a Pair — Full route discovery (direct + chain routes)
  • 🔄 Synchronization — How sync uses the configured providers
  • 🔌 FX Providers — User guide and details on each provider (ECB, FED, BOE, SNB)
  • 🧮 For developers: FX Chain Algorithm — How chain routes are found and calculated

docs.title: 📈 Signals
docs.text: The Signals panel draws technical indicators, comparison series and benchmark curves on the FX chart. LibreFolio computes the indicators from the pair's stored rates.

docs.title: 🛠️ Add a signal
docs.text:
1. Click the Signals bar above the chart to unfold the panel.
  2. Pick a signal from one of the three dropdowns: Technical Indicators, Data Comparison or Synthetic Benchmarks.
  3. Adjust its parameters on its card: the chart follows.
  4. Drag the cards to reorder them; 🗑️ removes one.

The signals you add are kept with this pair's chart settings.

In the chart's Rolling Return mode the panel offers only the FX Pair comparisons, each drawing its own rolling return; your other signals stay saved and return with Prices.

docs.title: 🧮 Technical indicators — 9 for FX
docs.text:
Nine indicators work on FX rates. Follow the links below, or click 📖 on a card, for the math behind each one.

Family Indicators 📈 Trend (3) EMA · SMA · KAMA ⚡ Momentum (5) RSI · MACD · ROC · Stochastic RSI · PPO 🌊 Volatility (1) Bollinger Bands 🤔 Why only 9? — the other indicators need more than a daily rate

FX rates have one value per day, with no high, low or volume. The other indicators need those fields, or measure portfolio-style risk, so they are available on asset charts only. The full list is in Technical Indicators — Financial Theory.

docs.title: 🔍 Finding an indicator
docs.text:
The Technical Indicators dropdown is a tree grouped by family (trend, momentum, volatility), with a search box on top: type to filter every family at once. The arrow keys and Enter work too.

Screenshot coming: the grouped indicator tree open on the FX Signals panel.

docs.title: 💱 Data comparison
docs.text:
• 💱 FX Pair — another of your pairs, e.g. GBP/USD next to EUR/USD. In the list, 👑 marks this page's pair and 📌 a pair already used by another signal.
  • ↔️ Asset Comparison — an asset's price next to the rate, picked in the same panel as the risk comparison's (search, Type and Currency filters, benchmarks first). One already used by another comparison carries a warning mark but can still be chosen.

A comparison card has buttons to sync the compared pair or asset and to open its page. In % view both curves start at 0 %, so their moves compare directly.

docs.title: 📐 Synthetic benchmarks
docs.text: Reference curves built from parameters alone, with no market data: Linear Growth, Compound Growth and Sine Wave.

docs.title: 🎛️ Read a signal card
docs.text:
• 📖 opens the indicator's theory page; hover a parameter for help.
  • A badge counts the data points loaded for the signal.
  • A spinner turns while the signal is computed. Then an icon may report a problem — hover it for the details:
    • grey ℹ️ — a small caveat;
    • amber ⚠️ — computed with caveats, such as gaps, a short warm-up or data that starts after the period;
    • red ⚠️ — not computed, for example because the history is too short.

If a card reports missing data, syncing the pair usually fills the gap.

docs.title: 📚 Deep dive: financial theory
docs.text:
Each indicator's formula, its signal-processing view (EMA as an IIR filter, SMA as an FIR filter) and how to read its crossovers:

Technical Indicators — Financial Theory

docs.title: Bank of England (BOE)
docs.text: The Bank of England (BOE) provider offers daily reference exchange rates quoted against the British Pound Sterling (GBP). It serves as an excellent reference for Sterling-denominated portfolios.

docs.title: 📊 Capabilities
docs.text:
• ✅ Current Price: Reference rate updated daily
  • ✅ History: Deep historical coverage
  • ❌ Search: No asset search (FX rates only)

docs.title: 🔧 Specifications
docs.text:
• Base Currency: GBP 🇬🇧
  • Update Frequency: Daily on UK business days
  • API Key: Not required (retrieved from the BOE Statistical Database)

docs.title: 💰 Supported Currencies
docs.text:
The Bank of England supports approximately 15 major currencies, including:

  • Major: USD 🇺🇸, EUR 🇪🇺, JPY 🇯🇵, CHF 🇨🇭, CAD 🇨🇦, AUD 🇦🇺, NZD 🇳🇿
  • Other: SEK 🇸🇪, NOK 🇳🇴, DKK 🇩🇰, CNY 🇨🇳, HKD 🇭🇰, SGD 🇸🇬, ZAR 🇿🇦, INR 🇮🇳

docs.title: 📝 Important Notes
docs.text:
• Quotes format: Rates are expressed as the amount of foreign currency per 1 GBP (e.g., 1 GBP = 1.25 USD). LibreFolio automatically normalizes this representation behind the scenes.
  • Holidays: The BOE does not publish rates on UK bank holidays or weekends.

docs.title: European Central Bank (ECB)
docs.text: The European Central Bank (ECB) is the primary reference rate provider for European portfolios. It publishes daily reference rates for the euro against about 30 currencies.

docs.title: 📊 Capabilities
docs.text:
• ✅ Current Price: Reference rate updated once daily
  • ✅ History: Historical rates available back to 1999
  • ❌ Search: No asset search (FX rates only)

docs.title: 🔧 Specifications
docs.text:
• Base Currency: EUR 🇪🇺
  • Update Frequency: Monday to Friday (excluding ECB holidays), around 16:00 CET
  • API Key: Not required (public endpoint)

docs.title: 💰 Supported Currencies
docs.text:
The ECB publishes a rate every business day for about 30 currencies, including:

  • Major: USD 🇺🇸, GBP 🇬🇧, JPY 🇯🇵, CHF 🇨🇭, CAD 🇨🇦, AUD 🇦🇺, NZD 🇳🇿
  • European/Regional: SEK 🇸🇪, NOK 🇳🇴, DKK 🇩🇰, ISK 🇮🇸, PLN 🇵🇱, CZK 🇨🇿, HUF 🇭🇺, RON 🇷🇴, TRY 🇹🇷
  • Global / Emerging: CNY 🇨🇳, HKD 🇭🇰, SGD 🇸🇬, KRW 🇰🇷, INR 🇮🇳, BRL 🇧🇷, MXN 🇲🇽, ZAR 🇿🇦

Currencies the ECB no longer publishes, such as the Bulgarian lev (BGN, replaced by the euro in 2026), the Croatian kuna (HRK) or the Russian rouble (RUB), keep their past rates: a sync still downloads their history, and no new rates arrive.

docs.title: 📝 Important Notes
docs.text:
• Quotes format: Rates are expressed as the amount of foreign currency per 1 EUR (e.g., 1 EUR = 1.08 USD). LibreFolio automatically normalizes this rate depending on your portfolio base currency.
  • No Weekend Data: The ECB does not publish rates on Saturdays, Sundays, or official ECB holidays (e.g., Good Friday, Easter Monday, Christmas). LibreFolio will retain the last available business day rate for weekend valuations.

docs.title: Federal Reserve (FED)
docs.text: The Federal Reserve (FRED) provider retrieves exchange rate data from the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) database. It is the ideal primary or fallback source for portfolios centered around the US Dollar.

docs.title: 📊 Capabilities
docs.text:
• ✅ Current Price: Reference rate updated daily
  • ✅ History: Deep historical rates (depends on the currency series)
  • ❌ Search: No asset search (FX rates only)

docs.title: 🔧 Specifications
docs.text:
• Base Currency: USD 🇺🇸
  • Update Frequency: Daily on US business days
  • API Key: Not required (retrieved via public CSV download)

docs.title: 💰 Supported Currencies
docs.text:
FRED provides rates for approximately 20 major currencies, including:

  • G10 Currencies: EUR 🇪🇺, GBP 🇬🇧, JPY 🇯🇵, CAD 🇨🇦, CHF 🇨🇭, AUD 🇦🇺, NZD 🇳🇿, SEK 🇸🇪, NOK 🇳🇴, DKK 🇩🇰
  • Emerging & Regional: CNY 🇨🇳, HKD 🇭🇰, SGD 🇸🇬, KRW 🇰🇷, INR 🇮🇳, BRL 🇧🇷, MXN 🇲🇽, ZAR 🇿🇦, TWD 🇹🇼, THB 🇹🇭

docs.title: 📝 Important Notes
docs.text:
• Quotes format: FRED quotes some currencies as "USD per unit of foreign currency" (e.g., EUR, GBP) and others as "foreign currency per USD" (e.g., JPY, CAD). LibreFolio automatically inverts and normalizes these rates to guarantee consistency in your database.
  • Holidays: No rates are published on US federal holidays (such as Thanksgiving, Independence Day, etc.) or weekends.

docs.title: 🔌 FX Providers
docs.text:
LibreFolio downloads exchange rates from central banks — free, and without an API key. A currency pair can have several sources in priority order: if the first one fails during a sync, the next one takes over.

European Central Bank (ECB) Daily reference exchange rates from the ECB, base currency EUR. Federal Reserve (FED) FRED database exchange rates, base currency USD. Bank of England (BOE) Daily reference rates from the BOE, base currency GBP. Swiss National Bank (SNB) Stable monthly average Swiss Franc rates from the SNB, base currency CHF. Request New Plugin Your exchange rate source is missing? Request a new plugin or contribute code!

docs.title: 📊 Provider Comparison
docs.text:
Each central bank quotes other currencies against its own, the base currency.

Provider Base Currency Update Frequency Good for ECB (European Central Bank) EUR 🇪🇺 Daily, around 16:00 CET on ECB working days Euro pairs and the main world currencies FED (Federal Reserve FRED) USD 🇺🇸 Daily, on US business days US-dollar pairs BOE (Bank of England) GBP 🇬🇧 Daily, on UK business days Sterling pairs SNB (Swiss National Bank) CHF 🇨🇭 Monthly averages, one value per month Swiss-franc pairs, when a monthly rate is enough

docs.title: 🎯 How Routing & Fallback Works
docs.text:
1. 🛤️ Direct route: one central bank quotes the pair — e.g. EUR/USD from the ECB.
  2. 🔀 Chain route: no bank quotes the pair, so LibreFolio combines steps — e.g. RON/USD as RON → EUR → USD, both steps from the ECB. A chain gets a rate only on days when every step has one.
  3. 🔄 Fallback: with several routes, a sync tries them in priority order and uses the first one that works.
  4. ✍️ Manual: no route for your pair? Save it without a provider and enter the rates yourself in the Data Editor.

You choose the routes when you add a pair, and change them later with the pair's Providers button.

SNB: one rate per month

The SNB publishes monthly averages, dated the 1st of each month. A pair that uses it gets one rate per month, and a chain through the SNB has rates only on those days.

docs.title: 🔗 Related
docs.text: • 🛠️ For developers: FX Providers — APIs, series and quotation formats

docs.title: Swiss National Bank (SNB)
docs.text:
The Swiss National Bank (SNB) provider publishes monthly average exchange rates for the Swiss Franc (CHF), fetched from the public SNB Data Portal. It is a stable and authoritative source for CHF-based assets.

Monthly data only — no daily rates

The SNB does not offer a daily-rate dataset: each value is the average of a calendar month, stored on the 1st of that month. In conversion chains a rate is computed only on dates where all involved providers have data, so chaining through SNB yields one point per month. If you need day-by-day CHF rates, use another provider (e.g. ECB or FED) for the pair.

docs.title: 📊 Capabilities
docs.text:
• ✅ Current Price: Latest available monthly average
  • ✅ History: Historical monthly averages
  • ❌ Search: No asset search (FX rates only)

docs.title: 🔧 Specifications
docs.text:
• Base Currency: CHF 🇨🇭
  • Update Frequency: Monthly — new averages are published around the 2nd business day of the following month
  • API Key: Not required (public SNB Data Portal API)

docs.title: 💰 Supported Currencies
docs.text:
The SNB covers about 25 currencies against CHF; LibreFolio loads the exact list dynamically from the SNB Data Portal. It includes:

  • Major: USD 🇺🇸, EUR 🇪🇺, GBP 🇬🇧, JPY 🇯🇵, CNY 🇨🇳
  • Global: CAD 🇨🇦, AUD 🇦🇺, and other world currencies

docs.title: 📝 Important Notes
docs.text:
• Multi-Unit Currency Quotation: The SNB quotes some currencies per 100 units instead of 1 unit (e.g. 100 JPY = x CHF). LibreFolio automatically detects and normalizes these rates to per-unit values to ensure your transactions are calculated correctly.
  • One point per month: rates are dated the 1st of each month. Conversions on dates between two monthly points use the most recent available rate (backward-fill).

docs.title: ✂️ Image Crop Tool
docs.text: Frame, rotate and resize a picture before LibreFolio stores it.

docs.title: 🎯 When Does It Appear?
docs.text:
• 👤 Profile picture — in Profile or on the Welcome page: in the image picker, choose Upload and pick an image.
  • 🏦 Broker icon and 📈 asset icon — the same picker, from the broker or the asset form.
  • 📂 Files page — add images to the upload list, then click the ✏️ Edit button of an image.

docs.title: ✂️ Frame the Picture
docs.text:
• 📏 Drag a corner or a side of the crop area to resize it, its inside to move it, the outside to move the picture. The crop area always stays inside the picture.
  • 🔍 Zoom with the mouse wheel or + / − — the crop area tightens (or widens) first, then the picture zooms — or pinch on a touch screen.
  • 🔄 Rotate 15° at a time with ↺ / ↻, and 🪞 flip with ↔ / ↕.
  • 👁️ The eye button on the left toggles a round preview: how the picture looks in a circle, like your avatar in the sidebar.
  • 🔁 Reset All (top right) undoes the crop, zoom, rotation and flip.

docs.title: 📐 Presets
docs.text:
Preset Output size Shape Avatar 200 × 200 px Square, round preview on Icon 64 × 64 px Square, round preview on Custom Same as the crop area Free, or a ratio of your choice: 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, 3:4

Profile pictures open with Avatar, broker icons with Icon and Files-page images with Custom; asset icons are cut square at 256 × 256 px. You can switch preset at any time.

docs.title: ⚙️ Output Settings
docs.text:
• 🎨 Format — .png (lossless, keeps transparency), .jpg (smaller, no transparency) or .webp (best compression), next to the file name, which you can also change. A .jpg or .webp picture keeps its format; anything else starts as .png.
  • 📊 Quality (.jpg and .webp only) — − / + in steps of 10%, from 10% to 100%: lower quality means a smaller file.
  • 📐 Output — width × height in pixels, set by the preset but editable. The two stay in proportion with the crop area, and you can't set them larger than it; Scale sets both at once.

docs.title: ✅ Confirm or Cancel
docs.text:
• Crop & Upload saves the picture and uses it. The picture is shared: every user can see it, as your avatar or as the icon you chose. On the Files page, Crop puts it in the upload list instead (Restore original ↺ brings the original back), and Upload sends the list: those files are personal (see Shared or personal).
  • Cancel or ✕ closes the tool — after asking, if you have unsaved changes (Discard & Close). From the image picker, you go back to the picker.
📄 Non-image files — on the Files page

A PDF, a CSV or any other non-image file has no crop step: its ✏️ button opens a simple Rename dialog instead.

docs.title: 🔗 Related
docs.text: • 🛠️ File Upload & Media Components — How the tool is built (for developers)

docs.title: ℹ️ About
docs.text:
The About tab shows:

  • Current LibreFolio version
  • License (AGPL-3.0)
  • Links to the GitHub repository and documentation
  • A Support LibreFolio card with the coffee link and the share buttons — see Support LibreFolio below
  • A Legal notice card — see Legal Notice below
  • A system information grid (Python version, operating system, deployment mode — Docker or local — browser, viewport, theme and language) with a copy-for-issue button that packs these details into a ready-to-paste bug report
  • The installed plugins: collapsible lists of the asset price providers, FX rate providers, broker import plugins, and signal indicators detected at startup, followed by Plugin diagnostics

docs.title: ❤️ Support LibreFolio
docs.text:
The Support LibreFolio card offers two ways to help the project:

  • Buy Me a Coffee opens the project's Buy Me a Coffee page in a new tab. The same link is in the page header (the coffee icon, with its label on wider screens), in the Help & Support menu, and at the top of the sign-in pages.
  • Below Or share, one button per social network: X, Reddit, Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok.

A share button opens a Share on … dialog with a Suggested message written for that network, in the language of the interface. Whatever the language, every message ends with the same five hashtags: #LibreFolio #OpenSource #SelfHosted #PortfolioTracker #PersonalFinance.

Copy and go copies the message, followed by the link to the project's public website, and opens the social network in a new tab: LibreFolio stays open in its own tab. Each network accepts a different amount of prepared content, and the dialog explains what to expect before you click:

Network What opens X A new post with the message and the project link already filled in. Reddit A new text post, with the Suggested title as its title and the message as its body. If Reddit leaves the body empty, paste the text you just copied. Facebook A post with the link preview only: paste the copied text into the post's message. Instagram Instagram itself, which cannot prepare a post from a link: choose Create (+), select a photo or video, then paste the copied caption. TikTok TikTok's upload page (sign in if asked): select your video, then paste the copied caption.

If the text cannot be copied, the dialog says so and asks you to allow clipboard access. If the browser blocks the new tab, the dialog says that the text is copied but the site could not be opened, and asks you to allow pop-ups. LibreFolio never publishes anything for you: the post is yours to review and publish on the social network.

docs.title: ☕ The donation popup
docs.text: Every now and then, right after you sign in, LibreFolio reminds you that you can support the project, with the same coffee link and share buttons.

docs.title: ⚖️ Legal Notice
docs.text:
The Legal notice card holds a short disclaimer: LibreFolio helps you follow your investments, and it is not financial advice. If your instance has them, the card also links its Terms of service and Privacy policy: each opens in a new tab.

You find the same notice under the card of the Welcome page. A shorter version, on one line with the same links, sits under the card of every sign-in page and at the foot of the sidebar, below the version number, while the sidebar is expanded. Every text you copy with AI Export carries the notice too, near its end and without the links.

docs.title: 🧩 Plugin Diagnostics
docs.text:
The Plugin diagnostics collapsible reports the health of the four plugin registries — Asset (price providers), FX (rate providers), BRIM (broker importers), and Signals (indicators) — and, below them, of the Tools.

Each registry is either marked All loaded (green) or lists the plugins that failed to import (red), with the file name and the underlying error. If a provider, importer, or indicator you expected is missing from the rest of the application, this panel tells you why — a plugin that fails to load at startup is simply not registered.

docs.title: 🧰 Tools and Tool diagnostics
docs.text:
Below the registries, the Tools panel lists the catalogue of Tools. It is read-only — no calculation, probe, or repair is run — and it loads only when you open Plugin diagnostics; Reload reads it again. For each tool you see its name and description, a Documentation link, its code and Version: <contract_version>, and whether a compatible interface is included in the frontend you are running. The implementation version is not shown here, and the Backend/API · UI version pair appears only on the cards of the Tools page and in the header of an open tool.

Open Tool diagnostics to load a snapshot of the server process that answered:

  • the Snapshot scope and the API process identifier;
  • the Execution pool snapshot: whether the pool is available, the active, queued, pending, completed, and failed jobs, and the degraded lanes;
  • the Tools loaded in this API process, each with its name, code, and contract version, and any Discovery failures;
  • the Effective platform limits, in a collapsible of their own.

The snapshot describes one server process, not the whole instance, and does not update by itself: reload it to read it again.

docs.title: 📜 Changelog Modal
docs.text:
The in-app changelog modal shows the changelog bundled with LibreFolio, in your interface language. You can reach it from two places:

  • the version number at the bottom of the sidebar (any page), and
  • the version label right below the title of this About page (Settings → About).

Each release is shown in your language when its translation is available; a release not translated yet appears in English, marked with a small Not translated yet label.

  • One foldable panel per release — only the most recent release starts open; sections and sub-sections fold too.
  • A version index of chips across the top: clicking a version unfolds it and scrolls straight to it.
  • A search box that descends into the folds: matching sections auto-open, and the clickable result chips jump to the exact spot.
  • Expand-all / collapse-all buttons, and a link to the changelog file on GitHub.

docs.title: 🔄 Checking for updates
docs.text:
The modal header also has a Check for updates button. It asks the server which version is running, reads the latest stable release from GitHub again (instead of reusing the result that the automatic check keeps for an hour), and compares the two. A newer release counts only once its Docker image is available on the registry, so a release whose build is still in progress is not offered yet — see Update Notifications.

A check started here always tells you how it went:

  • If LibreFolio is up to date, a confirmation toast appears, with the version detected online.
  • If GitHub has no stable release, or a newer release's Docker image is not available yet, a warning says so.
  • If the check fails — for example when GitHub or the registry cannot be reached — an error asks you to try again. A failed check never reports that you are up to date.
  • If a newer release exists and you are an admin, the New version available modal opens at once, on top of the changelog: current and latest versions side by side, with How to update (the updating guide) and Release notes on GitHub. You can dismiss it with Remind me later (you will be reminded at the next login) or Skip this version (the automatic check never prompts again for that release; a check started here still shows it). Admins are also probed automatically at login — see Update Notifications for the admin-side flow.
  • If a newer release exists and you are not an admin, the Update available — contact an administrator dialog lists the instance administrators — with e-mail addresses when available, each with a mailto link and a copy button — so you know whom to ask for the upgrade. Non-admins are never probed automatically.

docs.title: ✨ What's new after an update
docs.text:
When LibreFolio has been updated since your last visit, the next time you open it a What's new in LibreFolio window shows what changed: the part of the changelog for each version released since the last one you saw. If your account is older than this window, it shows the part of the version now running.

  • Each part is in your interface language when its translation is ready; otherwise it is in English, marked Not translated yet, as in the changelog.
  • Full changelog opens the complete changelog on GitHub, in a new tab.
  • Got it closes the window, and so do Esc and a click outside it. It does not come back until the next update. If LibreFolio cannot record that you closed it, for example because the connection dropped, the window shows again the next time you open LibreFolio.
  • It waits until no guide and no other window is open, and comes before the donation popup and the update notice.
  • A new account never sees it: it starts with the version it was created on.

docs.text:

  • 👤 Profile — Username, email, avatar, password
  • 🎛️ User Preferences — Language, base currency, and theme
  • 🛡️ Global Settings — Administrator options and scheduler

docs.title: ⚙️ Settings
docs.text:
LibreFolio's Settings panel lets you personalise the application and, if you are an administrator, manage global configuration.

Everyone has four tabs; administrators also have the Administration group, which gathers the tabs of the instance:

  • 👤 Profile — Username, email, avatar, password, and account deletion.
  • 🎛️ Preferences — Language, base currency, and theme.
  • 🧩 Plugins — What the price and exchange-rate sources ask for: your own search preferences, and the instance's settings, which only administrators change.
  • ℹ️ About — License info, version numbers, installed plugins, and the in-app changelog.
  • 🗂️ Administration — The tabs of the instance, for administrators only, on the right of the bar on a wide screen:
    • ⚙️ Global Settings — Instance-wide configuration, which applies to every user.
    • 👥 Users — The accounts of the instance, invitations and password-reset links.
    • 💾 Backup — The data of the whole instance in one archive, to download.
    • ✉️ Email — Whether LibreFolio can send emails, and a test email.
    • 🛡️ Security — How the instance is configured, with what needs attention first: see «Security» in Global Settings.

docs.title: 🗂️ The Administration Group
docs.text:
Only administrators have this group. Click Administration to open its first tab, Global Settings: a second row of tabs then shows under the first one, with Global Settings, Users, Backup, Email and Security. Clicking Administration again while one of them is open keeps you on it.

  • 👤 Not an administrator? You have no Administration: your tabs end with About, and a link to one of the administration tabs opens your Profile instead. The instance's settings still apply to you: your administrator changes them.
  • 🔢 A number on Security, repeated on Administration, counts what the security checks of the instance ask an administrator to look at.
  • 🔗 Each tab has its own address, which you can bookmark or share: /settings/profile, /settings/preferences, /settings/plugins, /settings/about and, for administrators, /settings/admin/global, /settings/admin/users and the other tabs of the group. The address follows the tab you open, and Back returns to the tab before. An address the app does not know opens the first tab.
  • 📱 On a phone, the tabs show their icons only, and the title above them names the open tab.

docs.title: ↔️ When the Tabs Do Not Fit
docs.text: In a narrow window, or in a language with longer names such as French or Spanish, a row of tabs can be wider than the panel. The row then scrolls sideways, and fades out on each side where more tabs are hidden. When you open a tab, resize the window or change the language, the row scrolls so that the open tab shows whole.

docs.text:
