  • 👥 Multi-User & Sharing — Invite collaborators and manage access

docs.title: 🧩 Plugin Settings
docs.text:
The Plugins tab holds what the price and exchange-rate sources ask for: the API key of a paid data source, a region, or a preference of your own. Open Settings (gear icon in the sidebar), then the Plugins tab, after Preferences (on a phone, the tab with the puzzle-piece icon). Every user has it; what you can change there depends on whose setting it is. The book icon at its top opens this page.

Only the plugins that ask for something are listed, under Prices for the price providers and Exchange rates for the exchange-rate providers, each heading after its family's icon (a column chart for prices, coins for exchange rates); a heading with no such plugin is left out. Of the plugins shipped with LibreFolio, two have a setting today, a personal search preference each: JustETF and Borsa Italiana (see Search Preferences). A plugin added to your installation may ask for more. The tab also has a Tools group, for the Tools that have settings of their own; none of them does yet, so you will not see it today. When no plugin asks for anything, the tab says No installed plugin asks for settings.

docs.title: 🧾 One Plugin, One Form
docs.text:
Each plugin has a form of its own: its icon and name (a puzzle piece when the plugin has no icon), a badge that says whether it can work, then its settings. Each setting shows its name, a red * when it is required, whose it is — Personal or Whole instance — and what it does.

  • Change what you need, then click Save at the bottom of that plugin's form: each plugin is saved on its own. Discard drops the changes you have not saved.
  • Save keeps all the changes of the plugin, or none of them: when one is refused, nothing is saved, and the setting at fault says why.
  • Before you save, LibreFolio checks what you typed against the plugin's rules — a number, a whole number, a minimum or a maximum, a length, one of the options — and says under the setting what is wrong, such as At least 8 characters. Save stays disabled until it is fixed.
  • A saved change shows in the setting itself, with no message. A plugin whose settings you cannot change has no buttons.
💬 When a save does not go through Message What happened Nothing was saved: check the settings below. A setting was refused. Under it: The value is not valid for this setting., Only an administrator can change this setting., A server variable sets it: it cannot be changed here. or This setting no longer exists: reload the page. These settings changed meanwhile: they have been reloaded, save again. Someone saved the same settings at the same moment: nothing of yours was saved. Check the values shown, then save again. Secrets cannot be saved: this instance's key cannot be used (see the configuration checks). Nothing was saved: a secret cannot be encrypted. An administrator finds the cause in the startup checks. The settings could not be saved. No answer from the server: try again.

docs.title: 👥 Personal and Whole-Instance Settings
docs.text:
Next to its name, each setting says whose it is:

Personal Whole instance Its value Your own: every user has theirs One for everybody on this LibreFolio Who changes it You An administrator Who sees it You alone: not even an administrator Everybody; the users who are not administrators see it read-only, with Only an administrator can change it. Of a secret, they see only whether it is set What it changes What LibreFolio does for you alone: your searches, and the provider checks of the asset dialog, such as Test Configuration Everything the plugin does, prices and exchange rates included

Prices, price histories and exchange rates are shared by everybody, so they never depend on one user's choice: for them, a personal setting always takes the plugin's default.

🛡️ For administrators

You change the whole-instance settings here, like everybody else changes their personal ones. A whole-instance setting can also be given by the server's configuration instead: see Set by the Server, and Plugin Settings in the administrators' manual for the variables.

docs.title: 🔐 Secrets
docs.text:
Some settings are secrets, such as an API key. A secret is write-only:

  • Type it, then Save. What you typed is sent once, then dropped from the page: from then on the setting shows only Set on with the date and time it was saved, never the secret itself — not even to you. The field is marked as a new password, so the browser does not fill it in with one of your saved passwords.
  • Replace opens the field for a new value; Cancel keeps the saved one.
  • Clear deletes the secret when you click Save (It will be deleted when you save.); Undo keeps it.

Users who are not administrators see a whole-instance secret as Set on … (Set when the server sets it) or Not set, and nothing else. LibreFolio keeps a saved secret encrypted: see Saved Secrets and the Instance Key.

docs.title: 🔒 Set by the Server
docs.text:
An administrator can also give a whole-instance setting through the server's configuration, with an environment variable. The setting then shows its value read-only, a secret only as Set, with Set by the server: nobody can change it here, not even an administrator. Administrators also see the name of the variable, Set by the server variable followed by it.

To change such a setting, an administrator changes the variable and restarts LibreFolio: see A Variable Locks the Setting.

docs.title: ↩️ Back to the Default
docs.text: Once you have saved a value of your own in a setting you can change, Use the default appears under it. It deletes the saved value when you click Save, and the setting goes back to the plugin's default: The saved value will be deleted when you save: the default applies., with Undo. Emptying a text field that shows a saved value does the same. A secret has no default: Clear deletes it (Secrets).

docs.title: ⚠️ When a Setting Has a Problem
docs.text: The setting says What happened What to do The server variable … is invalid: the plugin stays unconfigured until it is fixed. The variable that sets it holds a value the setting refuses, or names a file that cannot be read. LibreFolio never falls back to a saved value or to the default. Administrators see the variable's name An administrator fixes the variable and restarts LibreFolio The saved value is no longer valid: the default applies. The plugin no longer accepts the value saved earlier, after an update for example Choose a value again and save it, or leave it: the default applies meanwhile Saved, but this instance's key cannot read it. If an administrator can put the old key back, that comes first; otherwise enter it again. A saved secret can no longer be read, because the instance's encryption key has changed. LibreFolio keeps it, but never uses it If an administrator can still put the old instance key back, that comes first: a secret saved under the new key would become unreadable once the old key is back (see Saved Secrets and the Instance Key). Otherwise, type the secret again and save it; for a whole-instance secret, an administrator does

docs.title: 🚦 Configured or To Configure
docs.text:
The badge next to each plugin's name says whether it can work:

  • Configured: every required setting has a value LibreFolio can use.
  • To configure: a required setting has no usable value — never set, or a secret that can no longer be read — or a server variable that sets one of its settings is invalid.

LibreFolio does not call a plugin that is To configure: its prices or exchange rates are not updated, a search says that it must be configured, and Test Configuration fails with ❌ This provider must be configured before use. The plugins shipped with LibreFolio need no setting to work: JustETF and Borsa Italiana are always Configured.

docs.title: 🛠️ Configure, From an Asset
docs.text:
You do not have to leave an asset to change its provider's settings: Configure opens the same form as this tab, for that one price provider, over the dialog you are in.

  • In the asset dialog (+ Add Asset, or Edit on an asset), under Provider Assignment: when the chosen provider has settings, Configure sits next to its help link — on a phone, its icon alone. When the provider cannot work yet, To configure shows there too. After a save the badge follows, and the asset you are editing is left as it was.
  • In Search Online: when a provider must be configured before it can search, the list of results starts with a line … must be configured before it can search, naming the provider, and its own Configure button. Once you save, the search runs again. So a provider that could not search is never mistaken for one that found nothing.

docs.title: 🔎 Search Preferences: JustETF and Borsa Italiana
docs.text:
Both are Personal settings, and both show everything until you choose otherwise. They only choose which rows your own searches list: no price changes, and neither does an asset you already have. No instrument disappears either: each one exists in every currency or language, so a preference only keeps one of its rows.

Plugin Setting Choices What it changes in Search Online JustETF Preferred currency All currencies (the default), 🇪🇺 EUR, 🇺🇸 USD, 🇨🇭 CHF, 🇬🇧 GBP With a currency, each fund appears once, in that currency. With All currencies, each fund appears four times, once per currency Borsa Italiana Preferred language Both languages (the default), 🇮🇹 Italian, 🇬🇧 English With a language, each instrument appears once, in that language: the one its name and details come in. With Both languages, Italian first, then English. Borsa Italiana's website is searched the same way whatever you choose

Set them here, under JustETF and Borsa Italiana, or with Configure in the asset dialog while that provider is chosen.

docs.title: 👑 The Crown in JustETF Results
docs.text:
👑 marks a fund's own currency, the one its NAV is computed in — not necessarily the one you trade in. Whenever a result shows it, a line at the bottom of the list says so: 👑 the fund's own currency. With a preferred currency, 👑 appears only on the funds computed in that currency: with 🇪🇺 EUR, a fund computed in US dollars shows 🇪🇺 alone.

How the currency of a justETF asset works: Pick the Currency in Search.

docs.title: 🎛️ User Preferences
docs.text:
The Preferences tab controls how the app looks and behaves for you — changes apply only to your account. Your identity (username, email, avatar, password) lives in the Profile tab instead.

Setting Category Description Language 🌍 Display Interface language — 🇬🇧 English, 🇮🇹 Italiano, 🇫🇷 Français, 🇪🇸 Español. Applies as soon as you save it, and also decides how numbers and dates are written Default Currency 💰 Currency Your own base currency. The Dashboard, the Brokers page and each broker's page, and the Correlation tab of the Assets page open in it, and the AI Export of a currency pair uses it too; a currency you pick on the Dashboard stays for the session. It is also proposed when you create something new — an asset, a new broker's first cash balance, a PAC plan. This menu lists every currency Theme 🎨 Appearance ☀️ Light / 🌙 Dark / 🖥️ Auto (follows your operating system). Kept with your account, so it follows you to every browser and device. Until you choose one, it follows the administrator's default and a Global badge shows beside it; the ↺ button beside a theme you chose goes back to that default, like any change once you Save it. The sun/moon button in the header still switches only this browser

🌍 Numbers and dates follow the interface language

Amounts, percentages and dates are written the way the interface language writes them: for example 14.788,01 and 12 ott 2026 in Italian, 14 788,01 and 12 oct. 2026 in French, 14.788,01 and 12 oct 2026 in Spanish. Your browser adds only its region, and only when it uses the same language: in English, a browser set to US English writes 14,788.01 and Oct 12, 2026, and a browser in another language gets the British format, 14,788.01 and 12 Oct 2026.

Line shape of the charts

Preferences also holds the Line shape of every chart — segments, steps or a smooth curve. It is kept with your account and applies once you Save it, like the other fields. Until you pick one it follows the administrator's default (a Global badge shows beside it); ↺ goes back to that default once saved. How the shapes look: Dashboard charts.

Pick a category in the sidebar — on a phone, in the Category menu — to show only its settings; All Settings shows everything.

Currency menus on the Dashboard and asset pages

The currency menus of the Dashboard and of an asset page are shorter than Default Currency: they offer only the currencies of your FX pairs, and Create forex… at the bottom of the list adds a missing pair. See Dashboard.

docs.title: 💾 Saving, Undo, Reset
docs.text:
Each field keeps its own state:

  • Change a field and it shows Save and Undo; the header offers Save All and Undo All for every changed field.
  • When a saved value differs from the instance default (set by your administrator in Global Settings), an orange Reset to Default button appears: it puts the default back in the field, ready to save. Reset All to Defaults does it for every field.

docs.title: 🧭 Onboarding and guides
docs.text:
The Onboarding category lists every guide, grouped by where it appears. Each one shows its status — Pending, Completed or Skipped — and the version you have seen. New version to view means updated content is waiting: the guide starts again the next time you reach it.

Group Guides Setup Welcome setup Core tour Quick tour Transactions Transactions overview, Add transaction guide, Bulk workspace overview, Import guide Brokers Brokers overview, Broker guide, Broker details guide FX FX overview, FX guide, FX pair details guide Assets Assets overview, Asset guide, Asset details guide Tools Tools page

docs.title: 🔁 Replay a guide
docs.text:
• Welcome setup and Quick tour — Replay starts them at once.
  • Any other guide — Replay at next trigger gets it ready: it starts the next time you open its page, form, wizard or workspace. Cancel activation takes it back.
  • Replay all gets every guide ready and opens the Welcome page first.

A replay never changes the saved status, and guides never click or save for you. One exception: in a Welcome replay, Continue saves the language, currency and picture you chose (Exit tour leaves without saving).

🧩 Import guide and Bulk workspace overview — guides with steps

Expand the row of either guide to see each step with its own status. An optional Import step (Unify assets, Corrections, Duplicates, Align with the bank) stays Pending until an import first needs it.

In these two guides, ✕ skips only the current step: the next one starts when the wizard or the workspace reaches it. In a replay, ✕ removes the step from the replay without changing its saved status.

💾 Where a replay is kept — this browser only

A replay is kept in this browser, for your account: a half-finished one survives a reload, closing the browser, or logging out and back in. It is not shared with other accounts, browsers or devices. It ends when you finish or exit it, cancel it here, or an update brings a newer version of the guide — and then it closes in your other open tabs too.

If the guide list cannot be loaded, this section shows its own Retry button.

docs.title: 🙈 Privacy mode
docs.text:
Privacy mode hides how much you own while someone else can see your screen — a colleague walking past, a shared screen, a projector. It is not a field of this tab: it is the eye button in the page header, at the top right next to the theme and language buttons.

  • Hide amounts — amounts are visible; click to hide them.
  • Show amounts — privacy mode is on; click to show the amounts again.

The change applies at once to the page you are on, without a reload, and privacy mode stays on as you move between pages and after a reload, until you switch it off. Not to be confused with the eye icon of a table toolbar, which shows or hides table columns.

docs.title: 🔒 What is hidden
docs.text:
Privacy mode replaces the number of an amount with •••. The currency always stays, and so does the sign, so a gain still reads as a gain and a loss as a loss:

Normally With privacy mode 1,234.56 € 🇪🇺 EUR ••• € 🇪🇺 EUR -1,234.56 € 🇪🇺 EUR -••• € 🇪🇺 EUR €1,234.56 or 1234,56 € €••• or ••• € — (no value) —

••• is always the same three dots — even the K or M of a shortened figure goes — so it never gives away the order of magnitude. It covers:

  • Dashboard, Brokers and the risk panels — their amounts: the KPI cards, Cash Balances, the Allocation tooltips, the broker cards and the broker detail page.
  • Positions and FIFO Lots Analysis — every amount except the prices per unit, in the tables, the Lot Detail modal and the charts, and the quantities you hold (the Holdings Qty column, the lot quantities). A partly closed lot shows its open share, for example ••• (60%).
  • Transactions — the cash amount of every transaction.
  • PAC allocator — every amount and quantity of the result, and the purchase limits of a route.

docs.title: 👀 What stays visible
docs.text:
Numbers that do not tell how much you own stay readable, so you can keep working:

  • the currency of every hidden amount, percentages (returns, weights, allocation shares, yield on cost) and FX rates;
  • prices per unit — market prices, the Price and Avg. Cost columns of Positions, the prices of lots and the price lines of the WAC / Market Price chart;
  • counts, dates and names, and asset events such as a dividend or a split, which describe the asset rather than your portfolio;
  • the quantities in the Transactions list — a deliberate choice, even though a quantity times the public price hints at the size of a trade;
  • the numbers inside edit fields, for example while you add or edit a transaction: a field you cannot read is a field you cannot edit.

docs.title: 🌐 Where the setting is kept
docs.text:
Privacy mode belongs to this browser, not to your account: it is about the screen someone may be looking at.

  • It is off until you turn it on. Logging out or switching account leaves it as it is, and it does not follow you to another browser or device.
  • Other LibreFolio tabs already open in this browser pick up the change when you reload them.
  • If the browser blocks site storage, privacy mode still works in this tab, but may be off again after a reload.

What privacy mode does not cover

  • AI Export copies the real figures to the clipboard even while privacy mode is on. Review the text before you share it.
  • Downloads and exported files contain the real figures.
  • It hides what is drawn on the screen. The figures still reach your browser, so it is not protection against someone who can use your device or its developer tools.
  • Some figures can still be worked out: the sign tells a gain from a loss, and when you hold a single unit of an asset, its visible price is its value.

docs.title: 👤 Profile
docs.text: The Profile tab manages your identity in LibreFolio — who you are and how you log in. Display choices (language, currency, theme) live in Preferences instead; instance-wide options live in Settings › Administration › Global Settings.

docs.title: 🔒 Edit Lock
docs.text:
The tab opens locked: fields are read-only until you click the ✏️ pencil button in the header. This prevents accidental edits. If you lock the tab again while changes are unsaved, a confirmation dialog asks whether to discard them.

While unlocked, every modified field shows its own save / undo buttons, and the header offers save all and undo all for bulk actions.

docs.title: 🖼️ Avatar
docs.text:
Hover your avatar (while unlocked) and click the 📷 camera overlay to open the image picker: choose an existing image from the Files library, a shared one or one of your own, or upload a new one. Uploads pass through the Image Crop tool with the avatar preset (square crop, circular preview).

The avatar is saved immediately and is used across the app wherever your identity is shown — sidebar, broker sharing, and collaborator lists. Administrators also see it in Settings › Administration › Users, next to your username.

Since the other users see your avatar, its picture is shared: an image you upload here is stored shared, and one of your personal images becomes shared when you pick it, with a notice (see Shared or personal).

Also settable from the Welcome page

Brand-new accounts can pick the same picture once, during the first-login Welcome setup — it's the same picker, just reached from a different screen. Skipping that step leaves your initials as the avatar; you can always add or change a picture later from here.

docs.title: ✏️ Username, Email, Account Created
docs.text:
• Username and Email are editable (unlocked tab required). Changes apply to your login credentials straight away. Changing the email also asks for your current password: see Changing Your Email below.
  • Account Created is a read-only field showing your registration date.

docs.title: 📧 Changing Your Email
docs.text:
As soon as the email in the field is another address than your current one, a Current Password field appears right under the email field, with a reminder: To change your email, enter your current password. Your other devices will be signed out. The email's save button, and save all, stay disabled until you type it.

  • Wrong password: the tab says Current password is incorrect. Your new email stays in its field and only the password is emptied: type it again, then save.
  • Wrong password, again and again: wrong passwords here and failed sign-ins with your username count together. After 10 in 15 minutes, the change is refused even with the right password, and so is signing in with your username, for up to 15 minutes. The tab then says Too many wrong passwords: wait a few minutes and try again., and keeps both your new email and the password you typed: save again once the wait is over.
  • Email refused for another reason, for example because another account already uses it, as its email or as its username, even with other capitals: the tab shows the reason, and your current email comes back.
  • Email saved: you stay signed in on this device. Every other device signed in to your account is signed out, and needs to sign in again. Any password-reset link sent to you before the change stops working, even one still waiting in your old mailbox.
  • An email to each address: when your instance can send emails, LibreFolio writes to the address you had before, to tell you of the change, and to your new address, to confirm that it is now your account's. The first shows nothing of the new address and says what to do if you did not make the change; the second shows nothing of the old one. If one does not arrive, check the spam folder too.
  • Only the capitals changed, such as Anna@example.com for anna@example.com: it is still your address, so the tab asks for no password, you save it straight away, no device is signed out and it stays verified. Only the letters A to Z are matched this way, accented letters are not: Émile@example.com and émile@example.com are two different addresses.

Changing only your username asks for no password and signs no device out. The new username cannot contain @, because when you log in, LibreFolio reads anything with an @ as an email address: the tab says The username cannot contain @: to sign in, you can always use your email address., and your current username comes back. Spaces, accented letters and signs such as ., _, - or + are fine.

Why your password

Your email address is how your account can be recovered: a password-reset link sent there lets whoever reads it choose a new password. Without this check, someone with a moment inside your open session (a computer left unlocked, a stolen session cookie) could put their own address on your account, and keep the account for good. Without your password, they cannot change the address.

docs.title: 🔑 Change Password
docs.text:
The Change Password button (always available, no unlock needed) opens a modal requiring:

  1. Your current password (for verification)
  2. A new password that meets every rule of the checklist under the field: at least 8 characters, an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number and a special character — and it must differ from the current one
  3. Confirmation of the new password

The checklist follows what you type, and the server applies exactly the same rules. Letters and digits of any alphabet count: É is an uppercase letter, é a lowercase one. A special character is anything that is neither a letter, a number nor a space, such as !, _ or €. If the server still refuses the new password, the modal says Password does not meet security requirements, and the checklist shows which rules are missing.

Wrong current passwords and failed sign-ins with your username count together, as for the email: after 10 in 15 minutes, the change is refused even with the right current password, and so is signing in with your username, for up to 15 minutes. The modal then says Too many wrong passwords: wait a few minutes and try again., and keeps what you typed in its three fields: try again once the wait is over.

After confirmation, your session remains active — you do not need to log in again. Every other device signed in to your account is signed out. Any password-reset link sent to you before the change stops working.

docs.title: 🗑️ Delete Account
docs.text:
The Delete Account button permanently removes your account and its settings. Its dialog first shows what your deletion would take with it, then asks you to type your username. Delete Permanently acts at once: you are logged out and returned to the login page.

Your brokers follow the same rule as leaving a shared broker, and the dialog lists them before you confirm:

  • Deleted, with all their transactions and files: the brokers you are the only Owner of, each with its number of transactions. Their imported report files go too, and they disappear also for the users you shared them with. Without any, the dialog says No broker is deleted.;
  • Shared brokers that stay (only the access goes): every other broker you can open, with your role on it. It stays for its other users: only your access is removed;
  • a warning when transactions on other brokers are halves of transfers with the brokers that go: they stay, without their other half. A received transfer becomes an adjustment at its cost, and a transfer sent to one of those brokers an adjustment that takes the assets out of the broker that sent them, without a value: their cost counts as a realized loss there (see Edit or delete a broker).

If the dialog cannot load that list, it does not let you delete: close it and try again. If the deletion fails for a technical reason, nothing is deleted.

Irreversible

Deleting your account cannot be undone. If you are the only active administrator of the instance, the deletion is refused: first make another account an administrator, from the Users tab.

docs.title: 🔗 Related
docs.text:
• 🎛️ User Preferences — Language, base currency, and theme
  • ⚙️ Settings Overview — General settings summary
  • ℹ️ About — Version info, plugins, and changelog
  • 🛡️ Global Settings — Instance-wide options (admin)

docs.title: 🧰 Tools
docs.text:
A Tool is a standalone calculation: you supply the data for one operation, and it returns a result or a structured error. It is not an instruction to modify your portfolio.

The Tool platform is stable and still being refined. The catalogue currently offers exactly one tool:

Tool What it does PAC allocator Plans which purchases bring an allocation as close as possible to its target, using the cash and contributions available now.

Its card opens a guided planner. Its own page explains how to use it and what the calculation engine behind it does.

A second tool was withdrawn

The catalogue previously offered a Portfolio Rebalancer next to the PAC allocator. Both were prototypes and both were removed. Only the PAC allocator has been rebuilt so far, so a bookmark to the Rebalancer's documentation page no longer resolves.

docs.title: 🖱️ Opening a tool
docs.text:
Open Tools from the sidebar to see the catalogue as a grid of cards. For a ready tool, the entire card is clickable, not just its title or an icon; an arrow indicator marks it as open-able. A tool whose interface is missing has neither, and states its situation on the card instead.

Both the catalogue and an open tool show:

  • a Documentation action linking to that tool's page, with a label that appears next to the icon on wider screens and collapses to an icon-only control on narrow screens;
  • a Reload action that reloads the catalogue (from the hub) or the current tool's interface (from an open tool), with the same responsive icon-only behavior; reloading an open tool first asks for confirmation (Reload tool?), because it replaces the interface and discards its current draft;
  • the tool's compatibility pair, Backend/API <contract_version> · UI <ui.version>, with no separate build or implementation number shown alongside it.

When some catalogue entries or interfaces are unavailable, the hub says how many and points to Settings → About → Plugin diagnostics.

docs.title: ℹ️ Good to know
docs.text:
• A tool never changes your portfolio. It records no transactions, places no orders, and saves nothing to your portfolio: acting on its result is up to you.
  • Server busy, or a time limit reached? You get no result, and that says nothing about your figures: wait a moment, then try again.
  • A tool is missing or cannot be opened? Look in Settings → About → Plugin diagnostics: its Tools panel says, tool by tool, whether it is available and, if not, why. See About.

docs.title: 🧮 PAC allocator
docs.text:
The PAC allocator answers one question:

With the money available for this contribution cycle, which purchases bring my allocation as close as possible to its target?

Open Tools from the sidebar and click the PAC allocator card: it opens a guided planner. You describe a scenario step by step, press Calculate plan, and get a purchase plan to evaluate. It is a simulation: nothing is bought and no order is sent to a Broker.

docs.title: 🗺️ Using the planner
docs.text: The planner guides you through these steps, in order. The FX step appears only when the scenario needs exchange rates.

docs.title: 🎬 Scenario
docs.text:
You plan a new investment, a "pure PAC": the calculation starts from an empty portfolio, so what you already hold is not counted, and it splits the cash you choose among the Assets, as close as possible to the target weights.

Here you set the Valuation currency, in which amounts are compared and summarized. At first it is the Default Currency of your preferences. Money stays in its own currency: every exchange needed appears in the plan.

The reference date is always today: the planner sets it again before every copy from LibreFolio and before every calculation.

docs.title: 💰 Liquidity
docs.text:
Where does the money come from? You can combine several sources:

  • From your Brokers: cash already on your Brokers in LibreFolio. You choose how much of it to use.
  • New contribution: new money you add, such as the PAC instalment.
  • External account: a balance on an account not registered in LibreFolio, for example at your bank. You declare how much is there and how much to use. Nothing is bought from an external account: its money is sent to a Broker.

The Broker that receives a contribution or an external account's money is chosen in the Brokers step. Each amount stays in its own currency.

docs.title: 🏦 Brokers
docs.text:
Add the Brokers where the plan may buy: Choose existing Broker copies one of yours, and Manual Broker adds one by hand. Either way they are scenario data: the Broker itself is never changed. Fees and order modes are not recorded in LibreFolio, which is why you set them here.

For each currency you buy in, set:

  • The order mode: By number of units or By amount.

  • The Increment \(\Delta\): every proposed order is a whole multiple of it. With \(q\) the size of an order, in units or as an amount:

    \[ q = k\,\Delta, \qquad k = 0, 1, 2, \dots \]

    By number of units, \(\Delta\) is a whole number: \(\Delta = 1\) means whole units only. By amount, \(\Delta\) is the smallest amount you can enter, such as \(\Delta = 0.01\), and the units you get can be fractions of a unit.

  • The Purchase fee: a Fixed part \(f\) plus a Percentage \(r\) of the order amount \(A\), price margin included. The Minimum \(f_{\min}\) and the Maximum \(f_{\max}\) limit the percentage part only, and an empty Maximum sets no upper limit:

    \[ \text{fee} = f + \min\big(\max(r\,A,\ f_{\min}),\ f_{\max}\big) \]

    The fee is charged on every order, and no order means no fee. It is paid from your liquidity and is not invested. For example, with \(r = 0.19\%\), \(f_{\min} = 1.50\), \(f_{\max} = 18\) and no fixed part, an order of \(500\) pays \(1.50\), one of \(2{,}000\) pays \(3.80\), and one of \(20{,}000\) pays \(18\).

Each Broker also has two settings of its own:

  • Usable liquidity: the money the plan may use to buy there, that is the Broker's own cash plus the contributions and other accounts you allow. All of them are allowed at first: you can exclude a source, cap how much of it is used there, and give it a Priority (\(0\) = preferred).
  • Currency conversion: You convert before buying or The Broker converts when you buy. Both convert at the rate of the FX step minus the spread, so the calculation is the same either way: only the way the plan shows the conversion changes.

Not supported yet: a tax regime, losses, and sell fees for a Broker.

docs.title: 💼 Assets
docs.text:
Add the Assets the plan may buy, in any mix:

  • search the Assets registered in LibreFolio;
  • add Your Assets: those with an open position today in your Brokers, added as rows only, without quantities;
  • add a Manual Asset.

Each price is either:

  • Auto: the latest price stored in LibreFolio, read again just before the calculation. No data provider is called.
  • Manual: your own price, used as typed and never read again.

A missing price stays in the draft: the calculation asks for it.

The composition by country, sector, and type, copied from the Asset or typed, feeds only the exposure maps and bars of the result, not the calculation.

docs.title: 🔀 Routing
docs.text:
For each Broker, choose which Assets it may buy: Allow all, Exclude all, or click each one.

Then, only where you need them, set limits on each route. They are measured like that Broker's orders, in units or as an amount. With \(q\) the purchase of the Asset on that Broker:

  • Minimum purchase \(q_{\min}\): if the plan buys there, it buys at least this much, so \(q = 0\) or \(q \ge q_{\min}\).
  • Required purchase \(q_{\text{req}}\): bought whatever happens, \(q \ge q_{\text{req}}\). If the resources are not enough, the plan becomes impossible.
  • Maximum purchase \(q_{\max}\): the most the plan may buy there, \(q \le q_{\max}\).

Two more settings shape how the plan buys there:

  • Priority (\(0\) = preferred): it only breaks ties between plans equally close to the target.
  • Price margin \(m\): each purchase is counted at \(p\,(1 + m)\) instead of the price \(p\) of one unit, to cover a price that rises before the order. A margin of \(0.5\%\) on a price of \(100\) counts \(100.50\). The difference is a reserve, not invested. By amount, an order of \(A\) buys \(A / \big(p\,(1 + m)\big)\) units.

Empty fields restrict nothing.

docs.title: ⚖️ Targets
docs.text:
Here you split the money you invest now among the Assets: one target \(w_i\) per Asset, in percent, decimals allowed. To calculate, the targets must add up to exactly \(100\%\):

\[ \sum_i w_i = 100\% \]

Two actions help you get there:

  • Balance all rescales every target, keeping their ratios:

    \[ w_i' = \frac{w_i}{\sum_j w_j} \cdot 100\% \]

    If they are all \(0\), every Asset gets an equal part. Rounding keeps the total at exactly \(100\%\). To change only some rows, Balance to 100% on a row gives that Asset what is missing, or takes away the excess, and Balance the selected rows to 100% rescales only the rows you tick.

  • Copy current distribution reads how much each of these Assets weighs today in the Brokers you tick, counting only these Assets and not cash. With \(H_i\) the market value of Asset \(i\) held there today — what it cost you, for an Asset with no price at all, whose Valuation reads valued at cost · no price:

    \[ w_i = \frac{H_i}{\sum_j H_j} \cdot 100\% \]

    The weights are rounded to \(0.01\) percentage points and still add up to exactly \(100\%\), and an Asset you entered by hand gets \(0\). These are weights only, a base to edit and not advice: you see them before using them, and a target you changed is not overwritten without your confirmation.

docs.title: 💱 FX (only when needed)
docs.text:
This step appears only when the scenario needs exchange rates. It holds one rate \(x\) per currency pair in play, each Auto or Manual:

  • Auto: the latest valid rate stored in LibreFolio, read when the step opens and again just before the calculation. No data provider is called. A stored rate the planner cannot use (0 or infinite, which an older version could save) is skipped for the previous valid one, with a warning that names the pair, the day skipped and the day used: correct that day in the pair's Edit Rates; until then the results may be slightly approximate.
  • Manual: your own rate.

It also holds one Conversion spread \(s\): a percentage of every converted amount, kept as a margin for a change in the official rate or for Broker fees. Converting an amount \(D\) at the rate \(x\) (units received for each unit converted) gives

\[ D \cdot x\,(1 - s) \]

instead of \(D \cdot x\). Valuation, which compares and sums amounts in the valuation currency, uses the official rate \(x\) without spread; conversions use the rate with the spread, \(x\,(1 - s)\).

The rates must also agree with each other, so that no conversion creates value: with cash in CHF, an Asset in USD and valuation in EUR, for example, one CHF converted into USD after the spread may not be worth more in EUR than one CHF,

\[ x_{\text{CHF} \to \text{USD}}\,(1 - s)\,x_{\text{USD} \to \text{EUR}} \le x_{\text{CHF} \to \text{EUR}} \]

and the same holds for every conversion the plan may need between two currencies other than the valuation currency. Otherwise the calculation does not start and the outcome is Input not valid (see Reading the result): the cause can be a Manual rate or Auto rates from different days or sources, so align the rates or set a Conversion spread that covers the difference. Only a gap small enough to come from storing rates with ten decimals is tolerated: the conversion then uses the rate through the valuation currency when that is lower,

\[ \min\left(x_{\text{CHF} \to \text{USD}}\,(1 - s),\; \frac{x_{\text{CHF} \to \text{EUR}}}{x_{\text{USD} \to \text{EUR}}}\right) \]

so it still creates no value. When the rates agree, this rate is the usual \(x\,(1 - s)\). Your rates are not changed: each conversion of the plan shows the rate it starts from as spot and the rate it uses as effective.

Every amount the plan books is rounded once, on its exact final value, to the smallest unit of its currency (the cent for EUR or USD), and always against the plan: amounts it receives (what a conversion delivers) are rounded down, amounts it pays (the cost of an order and its fee) are rounded up. So rounding never improves a plan, splitting a conversion into smaller ones gains nothing, and the rounding part of Not invested is never negative. The Rounding column of Balances per Broker and currency shows how much of each row comes from rounding: ≈ marks a figure shown rounded, as when the exact difference has no finite decimal form (for example after converting USD → EUR at \(1/1.085\)), and a difference below the smallest unit keeps the digits it needs, such as ≈ −0.0022 rather than ≈ −0.00.

When LibreFolio has no rate for a pair, the step offers Add the pair or Download the rates: each opens the matching window of the FX page, and nothing is added or downloaded until you confirm there.

Not supported yet: a different exchange rate or spread per Broker, a safety margin on the rate, a conversion fee on top of the spread, and conversions in more than one step (for example EUR → USD → CHF).

docs.title: 🧠 Strategy
docs.text:
The strategy is Proportional: purchases only, it sells nothing.

Among all the purchase plans that respect your settings, it picks the best one with a cascade of criteria, each deciding only among the plans still tied on the ones above it:

  1. Closeness to the targets (L2 distance): the smallest distance

    \[ D = \sum_i \big(V_i - w_i\,R\big)^2 \]

    where \(V_i\) is the value of Asset \(i\) after the plan, \(w_i\) its target, and \(R\) the Base of the targets: the cash you chose that can reach a Broker where it can buy (in a PAC nothing is already invested). So \(w_i\,R\) is the ideal value of Asset \(i\). Values are in the valuation currency, at the quote price, without fees or price margin. Squaring makes big gaps weigh more, and \(D\) is measured in squared money, for example EUR².

  2. Uninvested money: the least money left out of the Assets, \(R - \sum_i V_i\).

  3. Broker and source priority: the smallest sum of the Priority numbers of the orders and cash sources the plan uses.

  4. Explicit costs (fees, spread, margin): the lowest total of fees, conversion spread, and price margin, in the valuation currency.

  5. Number of orders: the fewest orders.

A fixed order of Assets and Brokers settles any final tie, so a search that completes always gives the same plan for the same data; a search stopped by a time or node limit can give a different plan on a slower or busier machine.

docs.title: ✅ Review
docs.text: A last check before the calculation. It lists the complete copy that will be sent (the backend receives this copy, and only this), flags the fields still to complete, and offers Calculate plan.

docs.title: 📋 Copied or typed values
docs.text:
The planner works without any registered Broker or Asset: everything can be typed. When you would rather start from your LibreFolio data, you copy it with an explicit action: Choose existing Broker, From your Brokers, the Asset search or Your Assets, and Copy current distribution. In the FX step, an Auto rate is read from LibreFolio as soon as the step opens.

Each value shows where it came from (Copied, Manual, or Modified), and a copy also shows its date. A copy does not follow its source while you edit, and a copy you modified can be restored.

When you press Calculate plan, the planner first reads again from LibreFolio the prices, rates, and balances you copied and have not changed. Values you typed or changed stay as they are. If that read fails, nothing is calculated: you can Try again, or Calculate with the copied data to use the earlier copies.

docs.title: ⏳ While it calculates
docs.text:
While the request is active, the planner shows Calculation in progress and the configuration is locked. Stop waiting stops only the wait: the server may finish anyway, and that answer is discarded.

If you change the draft after a result, a Result not up to date banner appears: the previous values can still be consulted, but they no longer describe the current draft. From the banner, Back to Review returns to the last step, and Discard the previous result removes the old result and takes you there too.

docs.title: 📊 Reading the result
docs.text:
A calculated plan opens with a header: the scenario date, the valuation currency, and the draft revision, then a row of badges. Each badge explains itself when you point at it, tap it, or focus it. A plan also shows its L2 distance from the targets (the \(D\) of the Strategy step), how much is Not invested, and how many notes the calculation left; the notes are listed just below, under Notes on the calculation. Edit configuration takes you back to the Review step, and Calculate new plan runs the calculation again.

A calculation ends with one of these outcomes:

Outcome What it means Plan available A plan that respects every constraint. A second badge says what it is worth. Proven optimal: the solver proved, within its small calculation margin (which grows with the amounts), that no better plan exists, objective by objective in the order of the Strategy step, and the exact check of the plan matches its numbers. Optimality not proven: the solver reached its time or node limit, or its own numbers do not match the exact check of the plan; it is then the best plan found, but it is not proven to be the best. No operation With the cash you chose, no purchase meets the constraints: the plan is to do nothing. No order, no currency exchange, and no funding. Infeasible with these constraints Marked Infeasibility proven: no combination meets every hard constraint together. The constraints involved are listed (each Required purchase, and the liquidity that can reach the Brokers), each with a link to the step where you can change it. The planner does not choose which one to relax, and no partial plan is shown as valid. No plan within the limits The solver found no plan before reaching its limit. This is not a proof that none exists. A lighter search helps: fewer Assets or routes, a lower Maximum purchase, or a larger Increment. More data needed Something is missing. Your draft is intact, and no Asset is removed silently: add the missing fact or remove the Asset yourself. Input not valid Some of the data are not valid. Scenario not supported Not an error in your data: the tool does not handle this case yet.

Every plan shown has been checked again in exact decimal arithmetic, independently of the solver: that is the Verified in Decimal badge. A last badge tells how the search ended: Completed (the solver ended its search by itself), Time limit, or Node limit. When a plan was found but the search stopped at a limit, a notice adds that a better plan may exist; the result stays complete and can be consulted. If rounding to the smallest unit of a currency leaves a Broker slightly short, a notice says how much more cash that Broker needs to execute the plan.

The last three outcomes mean that the calculation could not start on your data: nothing is calculated, and the problems found are listed, with a link to the step concerned when there is one. Details adds the backend code of each problem.

Platform errors, such as a timeout, a full queue, or a crashed worker, are not financial conclusions about your scenario: your draft stays intact, so try again later. If the tool is unavailable, see Settings → About → Plugin diagnostics.

docs.title: 🗂️ How a plan is laid out
docs.text:
Below the outcome, a plan is laid out in this order:

  1. Key figures: the plan in a few numbers, Base of the targets, Invested after, Not invested, Cash chosen, Costs, and Orders, each with a ? that explains it and, below the value, the parts it is made of. Beside them, the Calculation box shows how long the optimizer worked, the time it was allowed for each objective, and how many objectives it closed.
  2. Allocation per Asset: for each Asset, its target share next to its share after the plan, with its ideal value \(w_i\,R\), its value after the plan \(V_i\), the gap from the ideal \(V_i - w_i\,R\), and the value bought.
  3. Operational plan: the steps to follow, in order. First the cash (Available cash, Transfer, Deposit), then the currency exchanges you make yourself, then one table of orders per Broker, with the Instruction to enter at the Broker, the Price, the Order amount, and the Fee. A conversion that the Broker makes by itself when you buy has no number: it appears above that Broker's orders as an Automatic conversion. This section is shown only when the plan has something to do.
  4. Exposures – ideal vs actual: maps and bars by country, type, and sector, built from the compositions of the Assets. The charts do not change the plan.
  5. Balances per Broker and currency: how each cash balance moves, and what is left.
  6. Proof and solver: how the outcome was established. The outcome, proof, and stop badges, the exact value of each objective, the solver stages, and the backend timings.

Allocation per Asset and Operational plan start open; the other sections open on request, and Expand all / Collapse all opens or closes them together. Without a plan (Infeasible with these constraints or No plan within the limits), Proof and solver is the only section, and the key figures show only the Calculation box.

Click an order, or its Detail button, to open its detail: the instruction, the economic quantity, the prices used (source price, mid price, and charge price with the price margin), the cash debit and the fee, the conversions that pay for it, and the priority, limit, and minimums of its route. Show provenance lists where each value came from, Copied or Manual, with the date and time of the copy or of your entry.

Proof and timings, at the top of the result, opens Proof and solver and scrolls to it.

Every figure comes from the backend accounting; the interface adds nothing up. With privacy mode on (see User preferences), the result hides what would tell how much you own: every amount (key figures, values, balances, order amounts, fees and costs, and the objective and solver values measured in money, the L2 distance included), every quantity, and the purchase limits of a route (Minimum purchase, Required purchase, Maximum purchase). The amounts in the problems listed when a calculation could not start are hidden too. Market prices, exchange rates, percentages (targets, shares, exposure weights, spreads, and margins), increments, priorities, counts, and dates stay visible, because they say nothing about how much you own.

docs.title: 🧮 What the calculation engine does
docs.text:
The engine behind this tool plans purchases. Given a set of Assets with their prices, the Brokers and buy routes that can be used to reach them, the cash and contributions available, and one target weight per Asset, it searches for the combination of purchases whose resulting allocation sits as close as possible to those targets.

Three properties are worth knowing, because they shape what the planner can promise:

  • It buys in each Broker's increments. Whole units or amounts, always in multiples of the increment you set: increments, fees, and the currencies involved are part of the problem it solves, not a rounding step applied afterwards.
  • Its published numbers come from exact arithmetic. Every candidate plan is re-checked exactly before anything is shown. A plan that fails that check is never published.
  • It never passes off an unproven plan as optimal. A plan stopped by a time or node limit is shown as the best one found and marked Optimality not proven. So is a plan whose exact check does not match the solver's own numbers, even when the search ended by itself. When no plan is found, it says so instead of guessing. With amounts of around ten billion units of a currency or more, the solver's calculations can lose precision: the tool may then stop with an error, or mark the plan Optimality not proven.

A completed calculation therefore reports one of the small set of honest outcomes listed in Reading the result.

The engine plans purchases only. It does not plan sales.

docs.title: 🎯 How its target is meant to be read
docs.text:
The PAC allocator distributes the liquidity available now — existing cash plus new contributions. Its targets describe how that money should be allocated; they do not describe the final mix of a portfolio you already hold.

The calculation does not take the positions you already hold as an input at all, so changing them cannot change what this tool plans. Copy current distribution only turns them into target weights for you to edit, and those weights do not follow later changes.

docs.title: 🚫 What this tool never does
docs.text:
The planner and the calculation behind it stay within the Tools platform contract:

  • it does not place orders, execute trades, or contact a Broker;
  • it does not write to your Assets, Brokers, or transactions;
  • it does not read your portfolio by itself: the calculation receives only the scenario sent from Review, and the planner reads your LibreFolio data only when you copy something or open the FX step (for its Auto rates), then again just before a calculation for the copied values you have not changed;
  • its result is a plan to evaluate, not advice and not an instruction.

docs.title: 🔒 Your financial data
docs.text:
The calculation runs on the scenario submitted with the request. It is not handed a live portfolio, a database connection, or your signed-in session, and it produces nothing that is stored.

Your draft lives only in the open page: it is saved neither on the server nor in the browser. Leaving the planner, or reloading or closing the tab, with a draft in progress asks you to confirm first. Signing out or switching account discards the draft without asking.

As always, avoid pasting real portfolio values, Broker exports, or account identifiers into examples or support messages.

docs.title: 📝 Transaction Form
docs.text: The transaction form adds or edits one transaction — or one linked pair — in the bulk workspace. It also shows a transaction read-only when you double-click it in a list. Only the fields that the chosen type needs appear.

docs.title: ✍️ Fill in the form
docs.text:
1. Pick the Type, then the Broker if it is not set already.
  2. Fill in the Required section: the Date, the Asset and its quantity when the type has one, and the cash amount.
  3. Open Optional for Tags, a Description or, on dividends, interest and adjustments, a Linked Event.
  4. Click Apply to place the row in the workspace; Save All in the workspace writes it.

A few rules keep entries quick:

  • Amounts are totals — the amount you save is the total paid or received, never the price per share (Total amount (not per share)). On a purchase or a sale you can write either one: the total, or the unit price (the buttons next to the field say which), and the form works out the other — see Total or unit price.
  • Type positive numbers — the form adds the minus sign where money or units go out: a purchase's payment, a sale's units, a withdrawal, a fee, a tax. Only an Adjustment quantity takes a sign: positive adds units, negative removes them.
  • Checks as you go — once the required fields are filled, the form checks the entry against your ledger and the other workspace rows, and lists any problem at the top. The form also spots some mistakes by itself: a date it cannot read, or one in the future, stays on screen in red, and the previous date is not used in its place; a quantity or amount with the wrong sign or format, such as a negative quantity on a purchase, turns red; and a warning at the top flags a transfer with the same broker on both sides, or an exchange with the same currency. Until you fix them, nothing is checked, valid does not appear and Apply stays disabled. ⚡ Validate now finds them all at once — see Validate now. Transaction dates can go back as far as the year 1 and up to tomorrow, but the form itself stops at today. A date before 1900 is almost always a typo, so the form warns you with an amber banner and Apply stays disabled until you press Yes, the date is right; change the date and it asks again, and once confirmed the date is saved like any other. A date after tomorrow is refused with a message such as Date: Not after 2026-10-18, when today is 17 October 2026.
  • Missing broker or asset? — Create new in the broker list, or New asset in the asset list, creates it without leaving the form.
  • Missing event? — + New event in the Linked Event field creates the asset's event and links it. If the asset already has an event of that type on that date, nothing is saved: the window shows that event, to use it, or to edit it if you entered it by hand, and never overwrites it (New event from a transaction).
💰 Cost basis of incoming units — for Adjustments and Asset Transfers

When an Adjustment adds units, or on the receiving side of an Asset Transfer, the form asks what those units cost:

  • Auto — LibreFolio computes it as a Weighted Average Cost; press ⚡ Validate now to see it.
  • Manual — you type it.

An Adjustment that removes units asks for no cost: it has no value. The units only leave the quantity, and what they cost counts as a realized loss. To record a sale, use a Sell.

In Auto, the average is taken at the sending broker of a transfer, or at the adjustment's own broker. If that broker holds none of the asset on the day the units leave it or come in, or only units whose cost is unknown, there is nothing to average: Auto is refused and nothing is saved — choose Manual and type what those units cost you (0 for a gift). In Manual, the field cannot stay empty: LibreFolio flags the row and saves nothing until you fill it in or switch to Auto; a negative cost is refused the same way — type 0 or more. Editing a saved transaction is no exception: if you empty its cost in Manual, the save is refused, because the transaction needs a cost basis — choose Auto or type a value. Type 0 for the new shares of a stock split. For a gift, instead of 0, you can type what the donor paid for those units: that keeps the weighted average cost, and the gain you may be taxed on, closer to the real ones. Units entered at a cost of 0 count as free, not as unknown: a later Auto average at their broker counts them at 0. If an exchange rate is missing, the Sync FX rates link fetches it.

docs.title: 🧮 Total or unit price
docs.text:
On a Buy or a Sell (and on any other single type that has both a quantity and a cash amount), the label of the cash field has two small buttons, Total and Unit price. The form stays a single amount and its currency: the buttons only say how to read the number you typed in that field.

  • Total (the default) — the number is the amount paid or received. Under the field the form shows the unit price it works out: = 83.40 per unit.
  • Unit price — the number is the price of one unit. Under the field the form shows the total it works out: = 1,000.80 in total.

Switching the buttons keeps the number you wrote and reads it the other way. What is saved is always the total: with Unit price on, the total shown under the field is the one that goes into the transaction. When you open a saved transaction the field shows the total, with the buttons on Total.

The calculation is made by the form itself, at once, on the exact digits you typed (no rounding errors from floating-point numbers). It uses the same price convention as the rest of the app: the quantity is divided by the asset's price per N units and multiplied by the price, so a bond quoted per 100 works the way its quote is read (= 98.55 per 100 units). The result is rounded to what is stored: amounts keep 6 decimals and unit prices 12. Ties round to the even digit (half-even). A value that is too long is flagged in red, as usual. The unit price is in the same currency as the amount. The asset and the quantity must be filled in; without them nothing is worked out and the field shows its usual hint (what to enter).

Example

You bought 12 shares at 83.40. Press Unit price, type 83.40 in the cash field, and under it you read = 1,000.80 in total. Your broker actually charged 1,000.90: press Total, type 1,000.90, and under it you read = 83.408333333333 per unit. The amount saved is 1,000.90.

When you open a saved transaction just to look at it, you see the total and, under it, the unit price worked out from the total and the quantity. The buttons only appear while you can edit.

The types without a quantity or without an amount, transfers and exchanges have no buttons. The bulk editor grid does not have them yet.

docs.title: ⚡ Validate now
docs.text:
⚡ Validate now is always clickable, even on a form you have only just opened. Press it whenever you want to know what is still missing or wrong. It works the same for a single transaction, a transfer pair and a currency exchange.

When you press it, it looks at the form in two steps, before anything leaves your computer:

  1. Required fields — the date, the broker, the asset and its quantity when the type has one, and the cash amount. For a pair it also checks the other side: the receiving broker and the second date, and for a currency exchange both amounts and both currencies.
  2. What you typed — a date that cannot be read, a quantity or amount that is not a valid number or has too many digits, a wrong sign, or the same currency or the same broker on both sides.

Every wrong cell turns red at once:

  • a missing required value gets a red outline;
  • a badly written one is red on the field itself.

The focus jumps to the first wrong cell, counting from the top, and a small counter next to the button says how many fields need fixing. While anything is wrong, nothing is sent to the server. Each mark disappears as soon as you fix its field.

When every field is correct, the button asks the server, as it always did, and shows valid or the issues the server finds in your ledger and in the other workspace rows.

Example

You leave the quantity empty and type abc as the date. Press ⚡ Validate now: both cells turn red, the focus lands on the date, the counter reads 2 fields need fixing, and nothing is sent. Fix the date and its mark goes away; fill in the quantity and the counter clears, and the next press asks the server.

docs.title: 🏷️ Transaction types
docs.text: The Financial Theory guide explains each type in depth.

docs.title: 🧾 Single transactions
docs.text: Type What it records Theory Buy Units of an asset bought, and the total paid 📖 Read Sell Units of an asset sold, and the total received 📖 Read Dividend Cash paid by an asset you hold 📖 Read Interest Interest received, with or without an asset 📖 Read Deposit Cash you put into the broker 📖 Read Withdrawal Cash you take out of the broker 📖 Read Fee A commission or another cost, optionally tied to an asset 📖 Read Tax A tax paid, optionally tied to an asset 📖 Read Adjustment Units added or removed without cash: a split, a gift, a position opened elsewhere 📖 Read

docs.title: 🔗 Paired transactions
docs.text:
A paired operation is recorded as two linked transactions, which the form shows as one, with a From and a To side. Each side has its own date, and the Swap sides arrow turns the direction around. In a currency exchange the two dates usually match: they differ when the broker credits the new currency on another day.

Type What it records Theory Asset Transfer Units of one asset moved between two of your brokers 📖 Read Cash Transfer Cash moved between two of your brokers, in one currency 📖 Read Currency Exchange One currency converted into another, inside one broker 📖 Read

A transfer needs two different brokers, an exchange two different currencies. Two single rows can also be linked into a pair later, and a pair split back — see Link or unlink a pair.

docs.title: 💸 Transactions
docs.text:
Transactions are every movement in your portfolio: purchases, sales, dividends, fees, transfers, and cash in or out. LibreFolio computes your positions, performance and costs from them, so a complete ledger keeps every figure right.

The Transactions page lists the transactions of all the brokers you can access, newest first. Each broker also shows its own in its Transactions tab.

docs.title: 🔎 Find and open a transaction
docs.text:
• Sort — click a column header.
  • Filter — open the filter of a column (date, type, asset, broker, tags, description…). In the date filter, type a date in From only to see the transactions from that day on, or in To only for those up to that day; the two ends of a range must be different days. Your filters are kept in the page address, so a bookmark reopens the same view.
  • Open — double-click a row to see it read-only; the pencil switches to editing.
  • Unit price — a column next to the amount shows the price per unit a trade implies (the amount divided by the quantity, per the asset's quote base); it is read-only and empty for a row without a quantity and an amount, and for the legs of a linked pair. Hide it from the column menu if you do not need it. The bulk editor has the same column.

Without filters or sorting, the two rows of a linked pair (a transfer or a currency exchange) stay next to each other, and the link icon jumps to the partner row.

docs.title: ➕ Add or import transactions
docs.text:
• Add Transaction opens the bulk workspace on a New transaction form: fill it in (Transaction Form), click Apply, then Save All.
  • Import opens the workspace with the Import Wizard, which reads the files exported by your broker — see Import from Broker.

docs.title: ✏️ Edit, clone or delete transactions
docs.text:
• One row — right-click it, or use its row actions: View, Edit, Clone, Split pair or Delete. You only see the actions your role on that broker allows.
  • Several rows — tick them, then choose Edit, Clone or Delete in the selection bar. Edit and Delete leave out the rows of brokers where you are only a Viewer.

Each of these opens the bulk workspace, and nothing changes before Save All. Editing or deleting one side of a linked pair brings its partner along.

Clone keeps the original date: it is how you re-record a historical row, for example under another type.

docs.title: 🔗 Link or unlink a pair
docs.text:
Some operations are two linked transactions — see Paired transactions.

  • Link — tick two single rows that belong together and click 🔗 Promote pair. Two Adjustments become an Asset Transfer; a Withdrawal and a Deposit become a Currency Exchange (same broker, two currencies) or a Cash Transfer (two brokers, same currency and amount). If the rows have a different description or different tags, you choose what to keep; each row keeps its own date. A description holds at most 500 characters: the dialog counts them and keeps Confirm promotion disabled until the description fits.
  • Unlink — Split pair on a linked row turns it back into two single rows. An Asset Transfer becomes two Adjustments: the receiving one keeps its cost, and the sending one takes the units out without a value: on its broker they only leave the quantity, and their cost counts as a realized loss (see Outgoing Adjustments).

Both ask for confirmation, then save at once, without the workspace.

docs.title: 🔁 Relink events
docs.text:
A dividend, an interest payment or an adjustment can be linked to the asset's event (the dividend the provider announced, a split…). The link is lost when changing an asset's currency deletes the events it pointed to, and a dividend you booked before its event was downloaded never had one. Relink events, in the toolbar above the table, finds those transactions and proposes the event to link.

The window lists your dividends, interest and adjustments that have an asset and no event, on the brokers where you are at least an Editor, newest first. Each row shows the asset, the date, the type and what was found:

What you see Meaning What you can do One event that day Exactly one event of the same asset, on the same day, of the matching type Link the row No event that day The asset has no such event on that day Nothing here: add the event, or link another one in the transaction N events that day More than one candidate Nothing here: LibreFolio never guesses. Choose the right one in the transaction

Link every row with one event links all the rows of the first kind at once, in a single save: if any is refused, none is linked. Nothing is linked unless you click.

The event must be on the same date

A candidate is proposed only if it is on the same day as the transaction. It must be the same asset too, and of the matching type: a dividend with a dividend, an interest payment with an interest event, an adjustment with a price adjustment or a split.

For example, you booked a dividend on 12 March. An event of the same asset dated 12 March is proposed. An event dated 10 March is not, even though it is the only one nearby: the row shows No event that day.

This is what happens when your broker credited the dividend a few days after the event. Open the transaction and pick the event yourself in Linked Event (Transaction Form).

docs.title: 🧰 The bulk workspace
docs.text:
The workspace is a grid of draft rows — marked new, edit or del — where you prepare changes before writing them:

  • Add Row, Import and Reset All sit above the grid. Ticking rows adds Reset selected, Delete selected and, for a matching pair, 🔗 Promote pair.
  • Rows are checked as you work: problems appear at the top under Validation errors were found, and a click takes you to the row. With many rows, automatic checking pauses — press ⚡ Validate now before saving.
  • When two rows look like the two halves of one transfer or exchange, a green banner offers to Merge them — two new rows, two saved ones, or one of each. When it proposes more than one pair, Merge all (N) merges them in one go. Where the two rows of a pair have a different description or different tags, one choice applies to every pair: All left keeps the description and tags of the first row, as the banner lists it; All right, those of the second row; Combine, the default, keeps both descriptions and the tags of both rows. A description holds at most 500 characters, as on any transaction: with Combine, a pair whose two descriptions together would go past it is not merged, and a message says how many pairs were left — merge them one by one with Merge, where you can shorten the description.
  • When the other half is already saved but not in the workspace — a transfer whose first side you imported last month, say — the 💡 button, above the grid and in the row's menu, offers to add it: once it is in, the banner offers the pair.
  • Save All writes everything at once. If there are merge suggestions you have not looked at — the 💡 never opened, the green banner never clicked — it asks first (Suggestions you have not looked at): Show the suggestions opens the 💡 list, or brings the banner into view; Save anyway goes on. Once you have looked, it does not ask again until you close the workspace. Cancel closes the workspace, asking first if you have unsaved changes.
🚦 Banners after an import — when they appear

After an import, banners above the grid list what to check before Save All:

  • red — rows the importer did not fully understand: Save All stays disabled until you complete them;
  • amber — auto-derived fields to verify: Save All first asks you to Review them or Save anyway;
  • amber, dates — rows dated before 1 January 1900, listed one by one (click a line to go to the row): Save All asks once for all of them (Yes, the dates are right). A date that early is usually a typo; once confirmed it is saved like any other.
  • amber — rows that may be stock splits (Revolut and Trading212 imports): link a Split event to each, or create it from the banner; see Revolut.

Click a banner to unfold its list, then an entry: the grid turns to that row's page and highlights it. Balance problems list the rows that cause them (Workspace rows: …), and a click opens the first one in the current sort order. If your column filters hide the row, a message tells you so.

After a save, a Promote pair or a Split pair, the Transactions page clears its selection, since those rows may have changed; closing or cancelling keeps it. If a Promote pair or a Split pair is refused, nothing changes: an error message says why, and the confirmation stays open.

docs.title: 🧭 Contextual guides
docs.text:
The Transactions page, the Add Transaction form, the bulk workspace and the Import Wizard each have a short guide. A guide starts only when its screen is ready and never edits a draft or presses a button for you; in the workspace it shows one notice at a time, closed with Got it.

Replay any guide from Settings → Preferences → Onboarding and guides.

docs.title: 📥 How to Export
docs.text:
To export your transaction statement from Coinbase:

  1. Log in to your Coinbase account.
  2. Click on your profile picture in the top-right corner, then select Taxes or Statements.
  3. Under the Reports section, locate Transaction History.
  4. Click Generate Report, select CSV as the file type, and choose the desired date range.
  5. Once the report is ready, download the CSV file to your computer.

docs.title: ⚠️ Common Pitfalls
docs.text:
Incorrect Report Type

Make sure you download the Transaction History report. Other reports (like Tax Statements, Balance Summaries, or specific Asset Ledger reports) are structured differently and will not be parsed correctly.

USD/EUR Conversions

The Coinbase parser processes crypto trades, buys, sells, and fees. Ensure your account display currency matches your main LibreFolio portfolio currency to avoid FX discrepancies.

docs.title: 📝 Notes
docs.text:
• Supports buys, sells, conversions, sends, receives, staking rewards, and fee assessments.
  • Supports major fiat base currencies (USD, EUR, GBP).
